## Model spec

A model is one JSON object (ModelSpec.to_dict(); api.save / api.load) made of the dataclasses below. Unknown keys, missing required keys, a wrong list / dict / text type and another version fail on load; everything else is reported by validation (check) as issues at node paths.

### Spec dataclasses

#### `ModelSpec` - the model file (root object)

- `title` (str; default "Untitled"): Free-text name of the model, shown in reports and the GUI.
- `description` (str; default ""): Free text (may span lines) on what the model shows and how to read its results; shown in the GUI (model node, Examples menu tooltip), never used by build or run.
- `version` (int; default 2): Spec format version 2; version 1 files (2D only, no size_z / geometry z params) load unchanged and are saved as version 2; other versions are rejected on load.
- `parameters` (list; default []): Named scalar parameters (ParameterSpec); every numeric value may be an expression of them.
- `domain` (DomainSpec; default {"size_x": 4e-06, "size_y": 4e-06, "size_z": null, "coordinates": "cartesian", "radius_min": 0, "angle_min": 0, "angle_wrap": "none"}): Size of the physical domain (DomainSpec), whose lower-left corner is the origin, and its in-plane grid (Cartesian, or polar / spherical about the origin).
- `geometry` (list; default []): Geometry objects (GeometrySpec): domain objects, points and lines, in m.
- `selections` (list; default []): Named entity lists (SelectionSpec), usable wherever entities are selected.
- `materials` (list; default []): Material assignments (MaterialSpec); list order and background materials decide overlapping cells (see materials).
- `physics` (list; default []): Physics instances (PhysicsSpec) of registered physics types, each with its features.
- `couplings` (list; default []): Couplings (CouplingSpec) that feed a field of one physics into a source slot of another.
- `meshes` (list; default [{"name": "mesh", "kind": "tensor", "mode": "uniform", "dx": 2e-08, "max_ratio": null, "wavelength_min": null, "points_per_wavelength": null, "refinements": [], "outer_dx": null, "outer_ratio": null, "axes": [], "h_min": null, "curvature_factor": 0.3, "mesher": "builtin", "sweep_axis": "none", "pml_layers": 8, "mirror_x": false, "mirror_y": false, "size_points": [], "face_sizes": []}]): Named meshes (MeshSpec, at least one, unique names; the first is the default): tensor (uniform, nonuniform or auto cells plus refinements), triangles (2D) or tetrahedra (3D). Each physics runs on one (PhysicsSpec.mesh); see mesh. A legacy "mesh" object (one MeshSpec) loads as [that mesh]; ModelSpec(mesh=...) and spec.mesh in scripts mean meshes[0].
- `solvers` (list; default []): Solver nodes (SolverSpec), each a solver type with its settings, used by the physics roles that name it in PhysicsSpec.solvers; [] = every physics on Automatic (the default solver of each role). A node no physics uses is a warning.
- `solver_defaults` (SolverDefaultsSpec; default {"backend": "auto", "precision": "auto", "subpixel_smoothing": false, "conformal_boundaries": false, "memory_check": "error"}): Model-wide solver choices (SolverDefaultsSpec).
- `study` (StudySpec; default {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {}, "stored_fields": [], "sweep": null, "stored_cuts": [], "adaptation": null, "estimation": null, "solved_physics": []}): What to compute (StudySpec): study type, its settings, stored fields and an optional sweep.
- `derived_values` (list; default []): Scalars evaluated at the end of the run (DerivedValueSpec), reported in summary.json derived (with derived_reference / derived_error when they have a reference).
- `analytic_curves` (list; default []): Analytic curves (AnalyticCurveSpec) the GUI draws dashed over a simulated curve (a feature result, the sweep plot or a line profile); figures=True draws them into the feature result figures and adds figures/curve_<name>.png per line curve and figures/<key>_vs_<x_column or row>.png per table target. They do not change the run.
- `derived_curves` (list; default []): Curves (DerivedCurveSpec) computed after the run from 1D feature results, e.g. several spectra on one plot, a sum or ratio of results or a result scaled to physical units; shown in the GUI Derived curves tab, in summary.json derived_curves and with figures=True in figures/derived_<plot>.png. They do not change the run.

#### `ParameterSpec` - items of ModelSpec.parameters

- `name` (str; required): Identifier; not a reserved expression name (function, constant, x, y, z, t, value) nor a physics field name.
- `expression` (float | int | str; required): Number or expression of other parameters and constants, e.g. "550*nm"; it must evaluate to a finite number.
- `description` (str; default ""): Free text, e.g. the meaning and unit.

#### `DomainSpec` - ModelSpec.domain

- `size_x` (float | int | str; default 4e-06): Width of the physical domain in m (> 0), x from 0 to size_x. On a uniform mesh the meshed window (Domain.physical_extent) is ceil(size_x / dx) cells wide, so it can be one cell larger than requested; EM PML cells are added outside. Polar / spherical coordinates: the radial depth in m, r from radius_min to radius_min + size_x (exact: dr = size_x / ceil(size_x / dx)).
- `size_y` (float | int | str | None; default 4e-06): Height of the physical domain in m (> 0), y from 0 to size_y; as for size_x, the meshed window can be one cell taller than requested on a uniform mesh. Polar / spherical coordinates: the angle span in rad (polar <= 2 pi; spherical angle_min + size_y <= pi). null = a 1D model (symmetry 2.20), invariant in both other directions: coordinates cartesian = a slab along x from 0 to size_x (totals per m^2), polar = a cylinder, r from radius_min to radius_min + size_x (per m of length; geometry planar), spherical = a sphere (whole shells; geometry axisymmetric); size_z, angle_min and angle_wrap stay unset. Only types whose dimensions include 1 run (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics). The model is drawn on the x axis of the plane (x = the slab coordinate or r, y = 0): objects select the cells whose centres (x, 0) they hold (rectangles across y = 0, circles about the origin for shells), points sit on y = 0, line curves run along y = 0; outer faces x_lo / x_hi only (x_lo at r = 0: the centre, no area). Mesh: uniform at dx, or graded by a mesh axis x entry (no axis y, object refinements or auto mode). Fields are the (nx, 1) cells along x; the Automatic linear solver is banded on both backends.
- `size_z` (float | int | str | None; default null): null (default) = a 2D model; a length in m (> 0) makes the model 3D, z from 0 to size_z: the xy layout is extruded over each object's z0..z1 interval (layer stack), the outer faces gain z_lo / z_hi and only physics types whose dimensions include 3 are allowed. z cells follow the mesh: uniform at dx, or graded by the refinements' z extents (see mesh mode).
- `coordinates` (str; default "cartesian"): cartesian (default) | polar | spherical: the in-plane grid of a 2D model. polar = (r, phi) cells, the drawing at x = r cos phi, y = r sin phi about the origin (planar per unit z, every physics with geometry 'planar'); spherical = (r, theta) cells of the meridional half plane, x = r sin theta the distance to the rotation axis y, y = r cos theta (every physics with geometry 'axisymmetric', whole shells). Circles about the origin, annuli, spheres, shells and cones (theta = const) are conformal; other shapes staircase on the cell centres. Outer faces: x_lo / x_hi = the inner / outer arc (r = radius_min, the origin when 0: no area), y_lo / y_hi = the rays at angle_min / angle_min + size_y (spherical theta = 0 / pi: the axis, no area); insulated by default (a full 2 pi disk keeps a cut at y_lo / y_hi unless angle_wrap joins them). Only physics types whose coordinate_grids include polar may run (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics; 3D: heat); k_xx / k_yy (sigma_dc_*, eps_dc_*) are the radial / angular components there and *_xy is refused; object perimeter flux features (heat_flux, convection, current_density, surface_charge on objects) weight each exposed cell face by its metric area (2D; refused in 3D sectors and 1D models); solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries applies on 2D polar / spherical grids too (heat, potential). Mesh: uniform at dx radially and dx along the outer arc (angle cells = ceil(size_y r_max / dx)); nonuniform: mesh axis 'x' bands / edges / segments (in r - radius_min) grade the radius, axis 'y' edges / segments (rad) set the angle cells; object refinements, mode 'auto' and EM PML are refused. Fields come as a containing-cell image over the sector's box (NaN outside); the _x / _y field components are the radial / angular ones; derived values integrate over the exact sector areas / shell volumes. With size_y null the same three values pick a 1D slab / cylinder / sphere (see size_y). polar with size_z set = a 3D cylindrical (r, phi, z) sector (symmetry 2.21; heat only): the same (r, phi) plane at every height, z along the axis (uniform at dx, or graded by a mesh axis z entry), z_lo / z_hi the end faces; geometry z params apply as in Cartesian 3D (prisms along z, spheres, boxes; masks on the drawing-plane centres per cross-section); k_zz is axial. Fields are z cuts only (plane x / y, stored x / y cuts and 3D segment line curves are refused), each shown as the polar window; derived values integrate over the volumes r_c dr dphi dz; Session.volume gives (r, phi, z) centres.
- `radius_min` (float | int | str; default 0): Polar / spherical coordinates: r of the x_lo face in m (>= 0; 0 = the origin is in the domain, a face without area). Ignored (warning) on a Cartesian grid.
- `angle_min` (float | int | str; default 0): Polar coordinates: phi of the y_lo face in rad (from +x toward +y); spherical: theta of the y_lo face from the +y rotation axis (>= 0). Ignored (warning) on a Cartesian grid.
- `angle_wrap` (str; default "none"): Polar coordinates only: none (default) | periodic | antiperiodic. periodic joins the y_hi ray to the y_lo ray (u continues across): a full 2 pi annulus or disk without a cut, or one C_N sector of size_y = 2 pi / N of a structure with N-fold rotational symmetry whose sources and conditions share it (warning when 2 pi / size_y is not whole). antiperiodic = u changes sign across the wrap, the angular Bloch phase pi of a C_N sector: needs an even N = 2 pi / size_y (error otherwise): the response to sources that alternate in sign from sector to sector; other Bloch phases are complex and not available. y_lo / y_hi are then no boundary: features may not select them (error). The wrap is exact in the finite-volume operator (the face between the last and first angle cells), anchoring counts loops through it (an antiperiodic loop anchors on its own).

#### `GeometrySpec` - items of ModelSpec.geometry

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among geometry objects and selections (one namespace); not x_lo, x_hi, y_lo, y_hi, z_lo, z_hi, all.
- `kind` (str; required): Geometry kind: rectangle, rounded_rectangle, circle, ellipse, polygon, point, line, union, intersection, difference, array, box, cylinder_z, sphere (see geometry).
- `params` (dict; default {}): Values of the kind params by name (numbers or parameter expressions, lengths in m); missing keys take the defaults.

#### `SelectionSpec` - items of ModelSpec.selections

- `name` (str; required): Identifier in the namespace shared with geometry objects.
- `kind` (str; required): Entity kind of the selection: domain | boundary | point | line | interface.
- `entities` (list; default []): Entity names: geometry objects, other selections of the same kind, outer faces (boundary) or all (domain). interface: domain objects (their outlines; composites: the outline of the result).
- `side` (str; default ""): Kind 'interface' only: 'inside' | 'outside' = the side of the outline its fields are read from; '' for the other kinds. An interface selection (2D models, polar / spherical domains too; not 3D) is the outline of each listed object in the drawing plane, sampled every half finest cell (outline parts on the window edge skipped); each sample reads its side 1.5 and 2.5 local cells deep along the outward normal, each a weighted least-squares plane (in the drawing plane, through the cell centres) through the side cells of a 4 x 4 block whose 8 neighbours lie on that side too (so no cell-centre average mixes the materials), extrapolated linearly onto the outline (exact for fields linear on the side; error ~1.9 (k_n h)^2 for a wave of normal wavenumber k_n; a side thinner than ~4 cells gives no samples; on a polar window the block does not reach across an angle_wrap seam). Derived values reduce such samples (see DerivedValueSpec.selection) and line curves read them (see AnalyticCurveSpec.interface): one-sided normal components (D_n continuity: E_n jumps by eps_2 / eps_1), tangential ones continuous.

#### `MaterialSpec` - items of ModelSpec.materials

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among materials.
- `library` (str | None; default null): Library material name (see materials), or null / "" for none.
- `properties` (dict; default {}): Material properties of the present physics types {name: number or expression}, overriding the library values (see materials).
- `dispersion` (list | None; default null): EM dispersion poles [{"model": "drude" | "lorentz" | "nk_fit", ...}], plus at most one {"model": "crystal", ...} entry (piezoelectric crystal data, not a pole); null, [] and a list: see materials.
- `selection` (list; default []): Domain entities the material covers (all = a background material, PML included: see materials); an empty list assigns it nowhere (warning).

#### `PhysicsSpec` - items of ModelSpec.physics

- `name` (str; required): Instance name (identifier) used in field names <name>_<field>, stored fields <name>.<component> and couplings; usually the default instance name of the type.
- `type` (str; required): Registered physics type name (see the physics type sections).
- `settings` (dict; default {}): Values of the physics type settings by name; missing keys take the defaults.
- `features` (list; default []): Features (FeatureSpec) of this physics: sources, probes, monitors, boundary and domain conditions.
- `every` (int; default 1): Stride in runner ticks (int >= 1): the physics steps on every n-th tick over n * dt_sync, dt_sync being the smallest dt_limit of all physics (EM: its Courant step). EM must use 1; heat coupled to EM typically a few hundred.
- `solvers` (dict; default {}): Solver role (stepper, linear, shifted, eigen) -> SolverSpec name; a missing role = Automatic. The roles of each physics type and their Automatic types: see solvers. A misfit (role, operator, precision) is an error; a role the study does not use is a warning.
- `mesh` (str; default ""): Name of the MeshSpec this physics runs on; "" = the first mesh (ModelSpec.meshes[0]). Physics on different meshes exchange data only through couplings whose type transfers across meshes (see mesh).

#### `FeatureSpec` - items of PhysicsSpec.features

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique within its physics; its result key is <physics>.<feature>.
- `type` (str; required): Feature type of the physics type (see its Feature sections).
- `selection` (list; default []): Entities of the selection kind of the feature type (domain, boundary, point or line entities).
- `params` (dict; default {}): Values of the feature type params by name; missing keys take the defaults.
- `enabled` (bool; default true): false leaves the feature out of validation and build; it stays in the model.

#### `CouplingSpec` - items of ModelSpec.couplings

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among couplings.
- `type` (str; required): Registered coupling type name (see the coupling type sections).
- `source` (str; required): Name of the physics instance whose field is read.
- `target` (str; required): Name of the physics instance whose source slot is written; two enabled couplings writing the same target slot are an error.
- `every` (int | None; default null): Transfer stride in runner ticks (int >= 1); null = the larger every of the source and target physics.
- `params` (dict; default {}): Values of the coupling type params by name; missing keys take the defaults.
- `enabled` (bool; default true): false leaves the coupling out of validation and build.

#### `MeshSpec` - items of ModelSpec.meshes

- `name` (str; default "mesh"): Identifier, unique among meshes; PhysicsSpec.mesh names it; issues of the mesh sit at node ["mesh", name].
- `kind` (str; default "tensor"): Mesh kind (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `mode` (str; default "uniform"): Mesh mode (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `dx` (float | int | str; default 2e-08): Cell size (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `max_ratio` (float | int | str | None; default null): Maximum growth ratio (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `wavelength_min` (float | int | str | None; default null): Shortest wavelength (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `points_per_wavelength` (float | int | str | None; default null): Points per wavelength (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `refinements` (list; default []): Local refinements (RefinementSpec), used in nonuniform and auto modes (triangles / gmsh tetrahedra: maximum element sizes in / along / at the object, gmsh tetrahedra also along its edges or at its surface only (where); builtin tetrahedra: tensor bands, per-axis sizes included).
- `outer_dx` (float | int | str | None; default null): Outer cell size (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `outer_ratio` (float | int | str | None; default null): Outer growth ratio (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `axes` (list; default []): Per-axis options (MeshAxisSpec, at most one per axis), used in nonuniform and auto modes (tensor meshes and builtin tetrahedra).
- `h_min` (float | int | str | None; default null): Minimum element size (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `curvature_factor` (float | int | str; default 0.3): Curvature factor (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `mesher` (str; default "builtin"): Mesher (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `sweep_axis` (str; default "none"): Swept layers (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `pml_layers` (int | str; default 8): Absorbing layers (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `mirror_x` (bool; default false): Mirror-symmetric in x (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `mirror_y` (bool; default false): Mirror-symmetric in y (see mesh: Mesh settings).
- `size_points` (list; default []): Element-size sources in m: [x, y, h] on triangles, [x, y, z, h] on tetrahedra (h > 0, mesher gmsh only: refused with builtin tetrahedra), each growing by max_ratio with the distance like an object size; adaptive mesh refinement writes them into adapted triangle meshes (convergence report adapted_meshes). [] = none.
- `face_sizes` (list; default []): Tetrahedra only: element sizes near plane faces (MeshFaceSizeSpec), every mode; gmsh: a size field over the face rectangle; builtin: a band [c - distance, c + distance] across the whole face plane (the plane an element face). [] = none.

#### `RefinementSpec` - items of MeshSpec.refinements

- `object` (str; required): Geometry object whose region is refined (domain object, line or point).
- `dx` (float | int | str; required): Target cell size in m in that region; it applies only when finer than the base size.
- `margin` (float | int | str | None; default null): Distance in m around the object that is refined too (3D: along z as well); null = 3 * the axis cell size.
- `dx_x` (float | int | str | None; default null): Cell size in m along x only (anisotropic refinement); null = dx. A value >= the base size leaves x unrefined, e.g. for a waveguide crossing the domain along x.
- `dx_y` (float | int | str | None; default null): Cell size in m along y only; null = dx (see dx_x).
- `dx_z` (float | int | str | None; default null): Cell size in m along z only (3D models); null = dx (see dx_x). dx_x / dx_y / dx_z: tensor meshes and builtin tetrahedra only.
- `automatic` (bool; default false): true = filled in from the auto-mode sizes (the GUI writes it when a mesh leaves auto mode, with dx = the auto base size); auto mode ignores such refinements and computes its own, so switching back to auto recalculates them. Default false.
- `where` (str; default "inside"): Where dx applies: 'inside' (default) = in the object; 'edges' = along the edges of its primitives (box 12 edges, z cylinder 2 rims, composite: every input, hole rims included; the physics' edge sizes path); 'surface' = at its surface only, dx + (max_ratio - 1) x |distance to the surface| on both sides (composites: the composite surface, a hole's inside stays coarse). 'edges' / 'surface': tetrahedron meshes with mesher gmsh only (validation error elsewhere); spheres have no edges, and objects gmsh gets no solid of (ellipses, polygons, x / y circles, tapers) get no size field (a warning).

#### `MeshAxisSpec` - items of MeshSpec.axes

- `axis` (str; required): 'x', 'y' or 'z' (z only in 3D models).
- `max_ratio` (float | int | str | None; default null): Maximum growth ratio of this axis (> 1; also its PML ramp); null = the mesh max_ratio.
- `bands` (list; default []): Coordinate bands (MeshBandSpec) refined along this axis only, without a geometry object.
- `edges` (list; default []): Custom cell edges in m (numbers or parameter expressions), increasing within [0, size]; 0 and the size are added when missing. They replace the graded cells of this axis (refinements and bands are then ignored along it); give edges or segments, not both.
- `segments` (list; default []): Custom cells as consecutive pieces (MeshSegmentSpec) from 0 to the axis size; they replace the graded cells of this axis like edges.

#### `MeshBandSpec` - items of MeshAxisSpec.bands

- `lo` (float | int | str; required): Band start in m along the axis.
- `hi` (float | int | str; required): Band end in m (> lo).
- `dx` (float | int | str; required): Cell size in m inside the band; applies only when finer than the base size (graded ramps outside, as for refinements).

#### `MeshSegmentSpec` - items of MeshAxisSpec.segments

- `cells` (float | int | str; required): Number of cells of the piece (whole number >= 1).
- `end` (float | int | str | None; default null): End of the piece in m (it starts at the previous end, the first at 0); null = the axis end (last piece only).
- `profile` (str; default "uniform"): 'uniform' (equal cells), 'geometric' (constant growth from the start, last / first cell = ratio; < 1 shrinks toward the end) or 'tanh' (two-sided clustering toward both ends of a gap, centre / end cell = ratio >= 1).
- `ratio` (float | int | str; default 1): Size ratio of the profile (see profile); 1 = uniform.

#### `MeshFaceSizeSpec` - items of MeshSpec.face_sizes

- `entity` (str; required): Outer face ('x_lo' ... 'z_hi') or a domain object (its bounding-box faces, clipped to the window).
- `size` (float | int | str; required): Element size in m at the face (> 0); applies only below dx, floored at h_min.
- `face` (str; default ""): Objects: one bounding-box face ('x_lo' ... 'z_hi'), '' = all six; outer faces: ''.
- `distance` (float | int | str; default 0): Half-thickness in m (>= 0) of the band held at size; beyond it the size grows by max_ratio up to dx.

#### `SolverSpec` - items of ModelSpec.solvers

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among solvers; PhysicsSpec.solvers refers to it.
- `type` (str; required): Registered solver type: pcg, line_block, sparse_direct, arpack_shift_invert, explicit_kernels (see solvers: roles, settings and which physics use them).
- `settings` (dict; default {}): Values of the solver type settings by name (see solvers); missing keys take the defaults.

#### `SolverDefaultsSpec` - ModelSpec.solver_defaults

- `backend` (str; default "auto"): auto (default) | gpu | cpu: where the run computes (api check / run backend=, CLI --backend override it); auto = gpu when cupy is installed, else cpu. cpu needs every physics type to list it in its backends (the Backends line of each physics type; else a validation error per physics) and every solver to fit it (pcg, line_block, sparse_direct without cusolver_qr, arpack_shift_invert do; explicit_kernels does not); on cpu the device memory estimate counts against the host RAM.
- `precision` (str; default "auto"): auto (default) | single | double | mixed | half_storage: model-wide solver precision. auto = each solver's own default (pcg double, explicit_kernels single, ...). Otherwise every role solver whose type and role offer that precision takes it, unless its solver node sets a precision of its own (the per-solver override): Automatic roles and nodes without a precision setting. Solvers that do not offer it keep their default (a validation info names them), e.g. double makes pcg and the time steppers double while sparse_direct / arpack_shift_invert / banded are double anyway; mixed reaches only pcg nodes and Automatic pcg of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics and magnetostatics, and line_block nodes. A node with pcg preconditioner multigrid and no precision of its own fails with mixed (set the node precision). check.json / summary.json solvers record the precision each role resolved to.
- `subpixel_smoothing` (bool; default false): false (default) | true: anisotropic permittivity averaging at material interfaces (Kottke / Farjadpour). Fill fraction and normal of every E_z cell / E_x and E_y face whose volume two materials share come once at build from 64 x 4 and 4 x 64 sample rasters per cell of the drawn material regions (each location takes the one whose fine axis is nearer its normal); the averaging (E_z and the field component along an interface: mean eps; across it: the harmonic mean, the diagonal of the inverse tensor) is reapplied to the current eps of two neighbouring cells of those materials after every change, so thermo-optic and other eps couplings keep working. Honoured by em_fdtd_ez / _hz, em_fdfd_ez / _hz, em_modes (E_x / E_y faces with the in-plane normal, E_z cells the area mean) and em_fdtd_3d outside an optimization study (incl. their mode ports); every other physics ignores it (validation info). em_fdtd_3d: the in-plane geometry per run of z cells sharing one cross-section (vertical walls: exact for z prisms; tapers and spheres are smoothed per layer, staircased along z) plus horizontal interfaces (prism tops / bottoms) sampled at 16 heights per half cell; the averaged face eps are re-quantised into a uint16 face index (2 bytes per cell). Only the background eps is averaged: sigma_e, mu_r and Drude / Lorentz poles keep their cell membership, and expression-defined eps jumps inside one material stay staircased. Restores second order on curved E_z interfaces; on slanted H_z interfaces it is better than staircasing, not second order.
- `conformal_boundaries` (bool; default false): false (default) | true: curved walls at their drawn position instead of staircased to the cells, located once at build from the drawn geometry (bisection along the cell links and faces). em_fdtd_ez / _hz pec_domain: E_z puts E_z = 0 at the exact wall distance along each H link to a PEC cell; H_z (Dey-Mittra) updates H_z of each cut cell from the free lengths of its faces and its free area, and only faces wholly inside the metal are PEC. Each corrected cell is limited so its update stays within the stability limit of the unchanged time step (the smallest cut never sets dt; a very small cut is then partly staircased). em_fdtd_ez / _hz dispersive materials (Drude / Lorentz poles): each pole current is weighted by the share of its control area inside the drawn material (E_z: the cell, exact for E tangential to the interface; H_z: the dual cell of each E_x / E_y face) instead of 0 / 1, the Courant check with those shares; the background eps keeps the cell mask (subpixel_smoothing averages it). em_fdfd_ez / _hz pec_domain: the same E_z wall distances (t >= 0.02) and H_z free face lengths, the H_z free area (>= 0.02 of the cell) entering the k0^2 mu term, so the operator stays reciprocal; no time-step limit. Mode ports, sources and the FDFD poles keep the cell mask. laminar_flow: interpolated (Bouzidi, linear) bounce-back on the links from fluid to solid cells, with the wall where the solid material is drawn (a material counts as solid when most of its cells have viscosity 0); outer faces keep their face rules. heat, electric_currents, electrostatics (cut cells): held regions (temperature / voltage on object perimeters, fixed_temperature_domain, terminal) put their value on the drawn outline: the free neighbour conducts c A / (t d) to it, t d its distance from the free centre along the link (t >= 0.02, Shortley-Weller), instead of the half cell 2 c A / w; walls of non-conducting materials (a material counts as closed when most of its cells conduct neither) get fractional face apertures and merged cut-cell volumes (>= 0.02), re-located whenever an assembly's conducting cells change (k(T), sigma(T)); perimeter heat_flux / current_density / surface_charge feed their value times each cut cell's chord of the drawn outline into the object cell owning it, convection loses h L / (1 + h delta / k_n) there (delta the owner centre's distance to the chord). em_modes pec_domain (Dey-Mittra on the projected Yee cell): E_z = 0 at the wall distance along each centre link into the metal, H_z from the free lengths of its E_x / E_y edges over the free area of its dual cell (fractions >= 0.02). em_fdtd_3d pec_domain (3D models, Dey-Mittra): every H face between four cell centres the drawn surface cuts takes the free lengths of its four E edges over its free area, floored so its update row stays within its uncut row at the time step (heuristic 3D Courant floor; E faces between two metal cells stay pinned). 2D Cartesian models only otherwise; heat / potential also (r, z) and polar / spherical domains (the cut fractions along the logical (r, angle) links / faces / cells, outline chords in the local (dr, r d_angle) frame; links across an angle_wrap seam stay staircased); every other physics ignores it (validation info). Features thinner than 1/16 of a cell face, or that no cell centre sees, stay invisible.
- `memory_check` (str; default "error"): error (default) | warning: what a memory estimate over the budget does (the GPU estimate at its peak, cuDSS factors outside the pool included, against the GPU budget; the host estimate against the available RAM; also per sweep value and per mesh refinement level). error refuses the model before the build (a triangle / tetrahedron mesh is built first when the estimate from its sizes is over: the judgement is on the built element count; the issue is reported at the mesh with the largest part); warning builds and runs it anyway with a validation warning, for a model whose estimate is known to be high (the cuDSS factor size depends on the fill of cuDSS's reordering, which the estimate can only model). The runtime guards stay: the GPU pool limit raises OutOfMemoryError, and each cuDSS plan checks cuDSS's own memory estimate against the free device memory before it factorises (an Automatic sparse_direct back end then falls back to SuperLU, an explicit cudss node raises); MUMPS / PARDISO factors (the host direct back ends / factorizations) check their own estimate after the analysis against 80 % of the available RAM (an explicit node raises).

#### `StudySpec` - ModelSpec.study

- `type` (str; default "time_dependent"): Registered study type name (see the study type sections).
- `settings` (dict; default {}): Values of the study type params by name; missing keys take the defaults.
- `stored_fields` (list; default []): Output fields stored in snapshots, as 'physics.component' (e.g. 'em.ez'); [] = the primary field of each physics (FDFD: <field>_re and <field>_im, so |field|^2 can be rebuilt).
- `sweep` (SweepSpec | None; default null): Optional parameter sweep (SweepSpec): one build and run per value; null = no sweep.
- `stored_cuts` (list; default []): 3D models only: extra cut planes [axis 'x' | 'y' | 'z', position in m (number or parameter expression)] each snapshot stores besides the mid-height z cut (the window cell containing the position; same stored fields, resolution rules and 1 GB limit), e.g. [["y", 1e-6]] for an xz side cut; saved run directories keep them. Read with Results.snapshot_field(index, name, plane=(axis, position) or the cut's index); summary.json stored_cuts lists the planes (cell-centre positions). [] = none.
- `adaptation` (AdaptationSpec | None; default null): Optional mesh refinement levels (AdaptationSpec, S7.7): the study is rebuilt and rerun on refined meshes until a derived value converges; null = the model meshes as they are. Only study types that support it (validation), no sweep or parity sectors.
- `estimation` (EstimationSpec | None; default null): Optional parameter estimation (EstimationSpec; industry-standard parameter estimation): the study is rebuilt and rerun per evaluation with the estimated parameters set, until the weighted misfit of measured derived values and curves is least; then one run at the best point stays live (summary estimation). null = one run. Any study type; no sweep or adaptation (validation); parity_sectors run every sector per evaluation (combined values fitted). A geometry parameter remeshes per evaluation (element meshes are reused while unchanged), which adds finite-difference noise: keep diff_step large or use nelder_mead.
- `solved_physics` (list; default []): Physics names the study solves itself (the industry-standard physics per study step), e.g. ['membrane']; the others run first as stationary background physics (also those of a type the study could solve), so couplings from them into the listed physics are allowed. [] = every physics whose solver has the study's solve. Only frequency_domain, mode_analysis, eigenfrequency, frequency_response and optomechanics (validation error elsewhere).

#### `SweepSpec` - StudySpec.sweep (or null)

- `parameter` (str; required): Name of the parameter that takes each value.
- `values` (list; default []): spacing 'list': numbers (or parameter expressions) the parameter takes, run in list order (kept but unused for the other spacings).
- `keep_fields` (bool; default false): true: keep the snapshots of every sweep value (summary sweep snapshot_times / snapshot_labels per value, results.npz sweep_snapshot/..., Results.sweep_field), not only those of the last value; past 1 GB in total only each value's final snapshot is kept (a warning). false (default): earlier values keep their derived values and results only.
- `spacing` (str; default "list"): 'list' (default: the values), 'linear' (count evenly spaced points from lower to upper) or 'log' (count geometrically spaced points; lower and upper non-zero, same sign).
- `lower` (float | int | str | None; default null): spacing 'linear' / 'log': first value (number or parameter expression); may exceed upper (a descending sweep).
- `upper` (float | int | str | None; default null): spacing 'linear' / 'log': last value (number or parameter expression).
- `count` (int; default 5): spacing 'linear' / 'log': number of values including both end points (1 = lower only).
- `reuse_build` (bool; default false): true: build once and run every value on that build: the swept parameter (and the parameters depending on it) may reach only feature values that follow a reused build (solid_mechanics on triangles / solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra: body_force, boundary_load, segment_load, displacement and prescribed_displacement_domain values of parameters only, no x / y / z), derived values, analytic / derived curves and study settings; any other use (geometry, mesh, materials, physics / solver / coupling settings, stored cuts) is a validation error, as are the time_dependent and optimization studies and parity_sectors. Each value then re-sets those loads and reruns the study from the previous state (nonlinear solids start Newton from it; summary sweep builds = 1). A model with a physics that cannot rerun (any other type) is rebuilt per value (an info line). false (default): one build per value.

#### `AdaptationSpec` - StudySpec.adaptation (or null)

- `target` (str; required): Derived value (DerivedValueSpec.name) whose relative change between levels stops the refinement (required).
- `method` (str; default "adaptive"): 'adaptive' (error indicator marks where to refine) or 'uniform' (every size of the meshes x growth^(-1/2) per level: a mesh-convergence sequence).
- `tolerance` (float | int; default 0.001): Converged when |v_k - v_k-1| <= tolerance |v_k| (> 0).
- `max_levels` (int; default 2): Largest number of refinement levels after the model meshes (integer >= 1); reaching it unconverged is a warning.
- `growth` (float | int; default 1.7): Cell / element count growth per level (> 1).
- `meshes` (list; default []): Mesh names refined ([] = every mesh the physics use).
- `max_cells` (int | None; default null): Stop before a level whose cell / element count would exceed this (null = no cap; the memory budget always applies).
- `anisotropic` (bool; default true): Tensor meshes: refine x and y bands separately by the indicator part that dominates (true) or both axes alike.
- `keep_levels` (bool; default false): true: keep every level's snapshots, not only the last level's.

#### `EstimationSpec` - StudySpec.estimation (or null)

- `parameters` (list; default []): Estimated model parameters (EstimatedParameterSpec, >= 1); each evaluation sets them as numbers, parameters depending on them follow.
- `targets` (list; default []): Measured derived values (EstimationTargetSpec); residual (model - value) / sigma.
- `curves` (list; default []): Measured curves (EstimationCurveSpec); residual per point (model interpolated onto x - y) / sigma.
- `method` (str; default "least_squares"): 'least_squares' (scipy least_squares TRF within the bounds, finite-difference Jacobian: n + 1 runs per step; standard errors from J^T J) or 'nelder_mead' (bounded simplex, no derivatives: for noisy misfits, e.g. a remeshed geometry parameter; no standard errors).
- `max_evaluations` (int; default 50): Largest number of study runs of the search (integer >= 1; the final run at the best point is extra); reaching it ends the search at the best point so far.
- `diff_step` (float | int; default 0.01): least_squares: finite-difference step relative to each parameter scale (> 0; default 1e-2: far above solver / mesh noise).
- `tolerance` (float | int; default 1e-06): Stop when the cost and the step change by less than this (relative; nelder_mead: absolute in the scaled parameters and the cost) (> 0).

#### `EstimatedParameterSpec` - items of EstimationSpec.parameters

- `name` (str; required): Model parameter name (ParameterSpec.name).
- `initial` (float | int | str | None; default null): Start value (number or expression of the base parameters); null = the parameter's own value. Must lie strictly between lower and upper; |initial| (else upper - lower, else 1) is the parameter scale of the search.
- `lower` (float | int | str | None; default null): Lower bound (number or expression); null = unbounded.
- `upper` (float | int | str | None; default null): Upper bound (number or expression); null = unbounded.

#### `EstimationTargetSpec` - items of EstimationSpec.targets

- `derived` (str; required): Derived value (DerivedValueSpec.name) compared with the measured value (parity sectors: the combined value).
- `value` (float | int | str; required): Measured value (number or expression of the base parameters).
- `sigma` (float | int | str | None; default null): Measurement uncertainty (> 0, same unit); null = |value| (a relative misfit; 1 when value is 0). Standard errors are absolute only when every target and curve gives sigma, else scaled by the reduced chi-square.

#### `EstimationCurveSpec` - items of EstimationSpec.curves

- `source` (str; required): Model curve: 'physics.feature:sample' of a 1D feature result (its abscissa, as a derived curve input) or a derived curve name (DerivedCurveSpec.name).
- `x` (list; default []): Measured abscissa values (numbers in the source abscissa unit), inside the model curve's range (the run fails otherwise).
- `y` (list; default []): Measured values, one per x.
- `sigma` (float | int | str | list | None; default null): Uncertainty: one number or expression (> 0), a list with one value per point, or null = the RMS of y.

#### `DerivedValueSpec` - items of ModelSpec.derived_values

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among derived values; its key in summary.json derived.
- `expression` (str; required): source null: expression of parameters, x, y (3D models: z), t and output fields (<physics>_<field>, or <field> when one physics alone provides it); over an interface selection also normal_x, normal_y, tangent_x, tangent_y (outward unit normal of the object outline, tangent = the normal turned +90 deg; on a polar / spherical domain their radial / angular components, as the fields _x / _y there; they shadow parameters), e.g. "em_ex_re*normal_x + em_ey_re*normal_y". Operation 'expression' (source null, an industry-standard global evaluation): one number of parameters, scalar outputs, t and the derived values listed before this one, no fields, x, y, z or selection, e.g. c_eff = "sqrt(N_int / rho_int)" of two integrals listed above; evaluated in float64 in list order like every derived value. With a source: expression of the result sample names and parameters, evaluated per sample, e.g. "power" or "1 - fraction_positive" (see Derived values). Both may use the names of the derived values listed before this one (their values; NaN when they failed): resonator figures of merit, e.g. W_E = integral of eps0_const*em_eps_r*em_e_intensity/4 (time-averaged stored electric energy of a phasor field, J/m in 2D), V = mode_volume of em_eps_r*em_e_intensity, n_eff = sqrt(eps_int / e2_int) of two integrals (operation expression), Purcell factor F = 3/(4*pi**2)*(lam/n)**3*Q/V in 3D, (Q/(pi**2*V))*(lam/n)**2 for an out-of-plane (E_z) line emitter in 2D (twice that in-plane, H_z family), with lam and Q from a resonance_table source (operation at, at = the row); first-order shift of a small inclusion of polarisability alpha [F m^2; 2D: F] at a point: d_omega/omega = -alpha*E2_at/(2*eps0_const*eps_int) with E2_at = |E|^2 at the point (operation at) and eps_int = integral of eps_r*|E|^2 (Clausius-Mossotti sphere: alpha = 4*pi*eps0_const*eps_b*a**3*(eps_s - eps_b)/(eps_s + 2*eps_b); 2D rod along z with E_z: alpha = eps0_const*(eps_s - eps_b)*area; in-plane E: 2*eps0_const*eps_b*area*(eps_s - eps_b)/(eps_s + eps_b)).
- `selection` (list; default []): Domain entities to reduce over; [] = the whole physical window; or exactly one 'interface' selection: its one-sided outline samples (see SelectionSpec.side; operations mean, max, min, integral: mean / integral weighted by outline length, integral per unit z length, axisymmetric times 2 pi r). Must be [] with a source and for operation 'expression'.
- `operation` (str; default "mean"): mean | max | min | integral | last | at | argmax | fwhm | polyfit | exp_fit | lorentz_fit | two_exp_fit | two_wave_fit | richardson | multi_lorentz_fit | pole_fit | mode_volume | expression. Over fields (mean, max, min, integral, mode_volume, at): mean is area-weighted, integral is the sum of value * cell area (per unit z length; with a physics set to geometry 'axisymmetric' both use the ring volume 2 pi r * cell area), mode_volume = integral / (maximum over the selection, or the value at point) [m^3; 2D: m^2, the area of a per-length mode], at = the value in the cell containing point; integral and mode_volume count each mirror face the selection reaches twice (the unfolded structure), and max / min (also the mode_volume maximum) include the mirror image there (each field with its mirror parity, x / y / z reflected). expression (source null, selection [], no point): the expression itself, one number of parameters, scalar outputs, t and earlier derived values (see expression). Over a source (the finite samples inside window): mean, max, min, integral = trapezoid over the abscissa (from the window edges, interpolated), argmax = abscissa of the maximum (parabola through it and its neighbours), fwhm = full width where the largest peak falls to half its maximum on both sides (linear crossings; baseline 0: subtract one in the expression), polyfit / exp_fit / lorentz_fit / two_exp_fit / two_wave_fit / richardson / multi_lorentz_fit / pole_fit = the quantity fit of a least-squares fit (see fit), last = the last sample in result order (the final time of a timeseries), at = linear interpolation at the abscissa value at. far_field angles wrap around (at, window, a peak at 0 rad; argmax in [0, 2 pi) without a window).
- `source` (str | None; default null): null = fields over the selection (operation 'expression': no fields, the other values); 'physics.feature' = the 1D result of that enabled feature (kinds timeseries, flux_spectrum, far_field, xy, table), reduced over its samples; the name of a derived curve = that curve (sample names: the curve name and x), e.g. a reduction or fit of a gradient / cumtrapz of results. Evaluated with the other derived values at the end of each run, so a sweep reports it per value.
- `at` (float | int | str | None; default null): Operation 'at' over a source only (fields: point): abscissa value of the source result, number or parameter expression in the abscissa unit (wavelength in m for a flux_spectrum, t in s for a timeseries, x in the x unit of an xy result, the 0-based row of a table); outside the sampled range the value is NaN plus a warning.
- `reference` (float | int | str | None; default null): Optional analytic value (number or expression of parameters only, in the unit of the derived value); summary.json derived_reference and derived_error = |value - reference| / |reference| (|value - reference| for a zero reference); the GUI shows both beside the value and dashes it over the sweep plot.
- `tolerance` (float | int | None; default null): Optional number >= 0 or null: largest accepted derived_error (relative, absolute for a zero reference; a sweep: at every value). Used only by selftest --examples, which fails the example above it; null = reported, never failed.
- `window` (list; default []): Source only: [lo, hi] (numbers or parameter expressions in the abscissa unit, e.g. ["1540*nm", "1560*nm"]) limiting the samples every operation but last / at reduces; [] = every sample. No finite sample inside gives NaN plus a warning. far_field: angles in rad, a window may cross 0 (e.g. [-0.3, 0.3]), at most 2 pi wide.
- `wavelength` (float | int | str | None; default null): far_field sources only: wavelength [m] (number or parameter expression) of the pattern reduced, the recorded one nearest to it; null = the first. Derived curve inputs of a far_field result use the first.
- `fit` (str; default ""): Fit operations only: the fitted quantity. polyfit: 'c0' .. 'c<degree>' (coefficient of x**k, in the abscissa unit); exp_fit (y = amplitude exp(rate x), log-linear least squares weighted by |y|, samples of one sign): amplitude, rate, decay (decay = -1 / rate, the e-folding length or time); lorentz_fit (y = offset + amplitude / (1 + (2 (x - center) / fwhm)**2), least squares, a peak or a dip; window it around one line): center, fwhm, amplitude, offset, q (q = |center| / fwhm, the quality factor of a line versus frequency or wavelength); two_exp_fit (y = amplitude_start exp(-kappa (x - x_first)) + amplitude_end exp(kappa (x - x_last)), kappa > 0, amplitudes at the outermost samples; an evanescent field between two ends): kappa, decay_length, amplitude_start, amplitude_end, r_squared (decay_length = 1 / kappa); two_wave_fit (complex y = A_f exp(-j beta x) + A_b exp(+j beta x), beta > 0; the expression is one bare '<name>_re' series, paired at run time with '<name>_im' of the same result and x samples; A_f travels toward +x in the exp(+j omega t) convention, phases at x = 0): beta, wavelength, forward_abs, forward_phase, backward_abs, backward_phase, reflection_abs, r_squared (reflection_abs = |A_b| / |A_f|); richardson (y = extrapolated + coefficient x**order, x > 0: a step size or cell count; samples monotone): extrapolated, order, coefficient, error_estimate, relative_error_estimate (order > 0 converges as x -> 0, order < 0 as x -> infinity; error_estimate = |y - extrapolated| of the sample nearest the limit). Peak fits (degree = number of lines K, quantities generated per line k = 1 .. K numbered by ascending position, then the shared ones; spacing = least-squares slope of the line positions vs k, degree >= 2 only): multi_lorentz_fit (y = offset + sum_k amplitude_k / (1 + (2 (x - center_k) / fwhm_k)**2), joint least squares seeded from the K most prominent maxima, or minima for dips): center_<k>, fwhm_<k>, amplitude_<k>, q_<k>, offset, spacing, r_squared (q_k = |center_k| / fwhm_k); pole_fit (complex y = sum_k r_k / (x - nu_k) + d0 + d1 x, vector fitting by pole relocation; the expression is one bare '<name>_re' series as for two_wave_fit; x is usually frequency, a nearby line outside the window is absorbed by d0 + d1 x only roughly: window around the K lines): frequency_<k>, q_<k>, fwhm_<k>, residue_abs_<k>, spacing, r_squared (frequency_k = Re nu_k, fwhm_k = 2 |Im nu_k|, q_k = |Re nu_k| / (2 |Im nu_k|), residue_abs_k = |r_k|; either sign convention of Im nu). A fitted line outside the samples is an error (lower the degree or move the window).
- `degree` (int; default 1): Operation 'polyfit': polynomial degree 0 .. 10 (default 1); multi_lorentz_fit / pole_fit: number of lines (peaks / poles) 1 .. 10.
- `point` (str; default ""): Field operations only: point object of 'at' (required: the value in the window cell containing it) and of 'mode_volume' (the field-at-point definition: integral / the value there; '' = integral / maximum over the selection).

#### `AnalyticCurveSpec` - items of ModelSpec.analytic_curves

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among analytic curves.
- `target` (str; required): Simulated curve to draw over: 'physics.feature' of an enabled feature with a timeseries, flux_spectrum, far_field, xy, table result, 'sweep' (the Sweep tab: versus the swept parameter) or 'line' (a profile of field along line).
- `expression` (str; required): Expression of parameters and the target variable: wavelength [m] (flux_spectrum, xy versus wavelength), t [s] (timeseries; iteration = the 1-based sample index when every sample shares one t, e.g. stationary iterations), frequency [Hz] (timeseries with series 'fft'), x (xy, in its x unit; table: the x_column value in its unit, or the 0-based row), angle [rad from +x] and wavelength [m] of the shown frequency (far_field, normalised to its peak like the simulated pattern), the swept parameter (sweep: every parameter is re-evaluated per point), x, y [m], z [m, the cut height or the 3D segment point; 3D models only] and s [m from the line start] (line). Variables shadow parameters of the same name.
- `series` (str; default ""): Simulated quantity the curve belongs to (drawn in its colour): an xy series name, a table column name, 'ratio' for the Spectra ratio-to-reference plot of a flux_spectrum / wavelength xy target, 'fft' for the probe FFT plot of a timeseries (|FFT| * dt as the Probes tab plots it, in the value unit times s), for sweep the derived value name, 'physics.feature' of a timeseries (its final value) or a '<column>_<k>' series of a per-value table (band k: the k-th smallest value, as Results.sweep_xy); '' = drawn with every quantity of the target.
- `line` (list; default []): Target 'line' only: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in m (numbers or parameter expressions), two distinct points; the Line profile tab plots field along it with the curve. 3D models also take the 3D segment [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1] (any direction, e.g. along z or oblique): sampled from the final state of the whole volume (containing cells or trilinear, see sampling; no mirror unfolding; live Results only), so plane stays null; every snapshot also stores the profile of each 3D segment line curve, so snapshot works with it (also from a saved run).
- `field` (str; default ""): Target 'line' only: output field 'physics.component' (e.g. 'heat.T') sampled along the line from the final state (or the snapshot), each sample reading the cell containing it (on a cell edge: the upper cell, as a probe there).
- `x_column` (str; default ""): 'table' targets only: numeric column used as the abscissa x of the curve and the plot (rows sorted by it); '' = the 0-based row index. series names the plotted column.
- `plane` (float | int | str | None; default null): Target 'line' in 3D models only: height z [m] (number or parameter expression) of the horizontal cut the line [x0, y0, x1, y1] lies in; null = the GUI cut-plane choice (when a z cut), headless the mid-height cut. Not with snapshot (snapshots hold the mid-height cut) or a 3D segment line (side planes: give a 3D segment).
- `snapshot` (int | str | None; default null): Target 'line' only: sample field from a stored snapshot instead of the final state: an index into Results.snapshots() (int, negative from the end) or a snapshot label, whole or its text before ':' (e.g. 'mode 2', 'resonance 1', 'iteration 3', 'lambda = 1550 nm'), else that text without its mirror parity tag ('mode 2' for 'mode 2 [x_lo symmetric]'; it must match one snapshot); null = the final state. field must be a stored field (a 3D segment line: any field, its profile is stored with each snapshot of the run).
- `tolerance` (float | int | None; default null): Optional number >= 0 or null: largest accepted summary.json curve_error max (max |simulated - analytic| / ptp(analytic) at the simulated samples, so an absolute temperature is judged against its rise; target sweep: relative per swept value; a feature target in a sweep: at every value). Used only by selftest --examples, which fails the example above it or when the curve cannot be compared; null = reported, never failed.
- `interface` (str; default ""): Target 'line' in 2D models only: name of an 'interface' selection; '' = the containing cells. Each line sample (two per finest cell) then reads the selection's side along the outward normal of the nearest outline sample of its objects and extrapolates onto the sample itself (see SelectionSpec.side), and the curve is compared at the sample positions; draw the line along the outline (e.g. a slot-waveguide sidewall). field is one component, or with projection the x component of an in-plane vector. Polar / spherical domains: live Results read the (r, angle) cells (field(native=True)), saved ones and snapshots the image over the sector box (first order at the outline).
- `sampling` (str; default "nearest"): Target 'line' with a 3D segment line only: 'nearest' (default; each sample reads its containing cell and curve_error compares at those cell centres) or 'trilinear' (each sample interpolated between the 8 surrounding cell centres, constant in the outer half cells; curve_error compares at the sample points, so a smooth field along an oblique segment shows no staircase). Other lines: 'nearest' (validation error otherwise).
- `projection` (str; default ""): With interface only: '' (field as it is) | normal | tangential: field names the x component of an in-plane vector (e.g. em.ex_re, its y component em.ey_re, found by turning its axis letter x into y: E_x -> E_y), both read one-sided and projected on the nearest outline normal (normal) or the tangent = normal turned +90 deg (tangential); on a polar / spherical domain the components are radial / angular and projected as such. A snapshot curve needs both stored.

#### `DerivedCurveSpec` - items of ModelSpec.derived_curves

- `name` (str; required): Identifier, unique among derived curves; its key in summary.json derived_curves.
- `expression` (str; required): Expression of the input aliases (arrays on the curve abscissa, or numbers for scalar samples), x (the abscissa, in its unit) and parameters, evaluated per abscissa point, e.g. "eta*S*P_top/(h_const*c_const/lambda0)". Aliases shadow parameters of the same name. Besides the expression functions it may call (here only): gradient(y): dy/dx along the curve abscissa x (second-order differences, also at the ends), over the finite samples of y (NaN ones stay NaN); cumtrapz(y): running trapezoid integral of y over x, 0 at the first finite sample; NaN samples (outside an interpolated input's range) are skipped and stay NaN, so it integrates over the overlap.
- `inputs` (dict; default {}): {alias: 'physics.feature:sample'}: an identifier (not a reserved name) per input, the sample a sample name of that enabled 1D feature result as for derived values (xy series, table column, timeseries values, flux power, or a numeric scalar such as variance). The first array input sets the abscissa (sorted); later ones are interpolated linearly onto it (NaN outside their range) and must share its abscissa label and unit.
- `plot` (str; default ""): Plot the curve is drawn in, shared with the other curves naming it (an identifier; '' = a plot of its own named after the curve); figures/derived_<plot>.png. Curves of different unit go to separate panels of the plot.
- `label` (str; default ""): Legend text; '' (or a label already used in the plot) = the curve name.
- `unit` (str; default ""): Unit of the values, free text ('' = none); panels group by it.
- `log_x` (bool; default false): Logarithmic abscissa; the first drawn curve of a plot sets it for the plot.
- `log_y` (bool; default false): Logarithmic value axis; the first drawn curve of a plot sets it for the plot.
- `reference` (float | int | str | None; default null): Optional analytic curve: number or expression of x (the curve abscissa) and parameters, drawn as series '<series> reference' in the plot; summary.json derived_curves <name> curve_error {max, rms, n_points} = |curve - reference| / ptp(reference) on the curve abscissa (as AnalyticCurveSpec.tolerance) and y_reference.
- `tolerance` (float | int | None; default null): Optional number >= 0 or null: largest accepted curve_error max against the reference. Used only by selftest --examples, which fails the example above it or when the curve fails; null = reported, never failed.

### Param kinds

- `float`: a number or an expression string (see expressions)
- `int`: a whole number, or an expression of parameters that evaluates to one
- `bool`: true or false
- `choice`: one of the listed choices (text)
- `str`: text
- `expression`: expression text kept as written and evaluated at run time (its help names the allowed names)
- `ref`: the name of a model node of the given kind (material, geometry object, physics or parameter); null or "" = none where optional
- `float_list`: a list of numbers or parameter expressions
- `points`: a list of [x, y] pairs of numbers or parameter expressions, in m
- `names`: a list of node names (of the given kind)
- `table`: a list of rows, each a list of one number or parameter expression per column, in the column order and units listed with the param (range bounds apply to every entry)

### Names

- Node names (parameters, geometry objects, selections, materials, physics, features, couplings, meshes, derived values, analytic and derived curves) are Python identifiers (letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit), unique within their kind; feature names are unique within their physics.
- Geometry objects and selections share one namespace and may not use the reserved entity names x_lo, x_hi, y_lo, y_hi, z_lo, z_hi, all.
- Parameter names may not be reserved expression names (functions, constants, x, y, z, t, value) or physics field names (see expressions).

### Entities and selections

- Selection kinds: domain | boundary | point | line | interface. An entity list (MaterialSpec.selection, FeatureSpec.selection, DerivedValueSpec.selection, SelectionSpec.entities) holds geometry object names, named selections of the same kind (expanded recursively) and reserved entity names.
- Domain entities: domain objects and all (the whole domain; build masks include the PML ring). Boundary entities: the outer faces x_lo (left), x_hi (right), y_lo (bottom), y_hi (top) and domain objects, meaning their perimeter cells inside the object (the window edge is no perimeter). Point and line entities: point and line objects.
- 3D models (DomainSpec.size_z set) add the outer faces z_lo (lower z face) and z_hi (upper z face); the 2D domain kinds become prisms over their z0 / z1 params (null = full height), points and lines sit at their z param (null = mid-height), and box, cylinder_z and sphere are 3D-only kinds. Results stay 2D: fields are cut planes (the mid-height z cut unless an x / y / z plane is chosen).
- Objects consumed as inputs of a composite (union, intersection, difference, array) cannot be selected on their own.

### Values

- Numeric fields and float / int params take a number or an expression string of parameters, e.g. "2*r_disk + 50*nm" (see expressions); params marked "may use x, y", "may use physics fields" or "may use t" may use those names too.
- Settings and params dicts (PhysicsSpec.settings, FeatureSpec.params, CouplingSpec.params, StudySpec.settings, GeometrySpec.params) hold values by param name: a missing key takes the param default, an unknown key is an error.
- A param is checked only while it is visible (visible when ...); an invisible param whose value fails keeps its default.
- Validation checks ranges of values that evaluate over the parameters. Material properties using x, y, z are range-checked on their cells at build time; those using physics fields at every update (for fields of an FDTD or transient physics at update 1, 2, 4, 8, ... and every 100th, so a run fails late, and a range left after the last such check is not reported), naming the material, property and the range found. Other expressions of x, y, z are checked for finite values only.

### Physics, couplings and study

- Snapshots (StudySpec.stored_fields): time_dependent at the output interval plus the final state, stationary the final state, frequency_domain one per wavelength (labelled "lambda = <nm> nm"), mode_analysis one per mode (labelled "mode <k>: n_eff = <value>"), eigenfrequency one per resonance (labelled "resonance <k>: lambda = <nm> nm, Q = <value>"). A snapshot holds the native window cells (graded included, x_centers / y_centers set) up to 250,000 cells; a larger window is nearest-cell resampled on square pixels of max(finest cell, sqrt(window area / 250,000)) (native_shape = the window cells, x_centers None), which can skip features finer than a pixel. 3D models: the mid-height z cut, plus each StudySpec.stored_cuts plane (opt-in).
- A physics type lists the studies it supports; a study with a background study (the "Background study" line of its entry, e.g. frequency_domain: stationary) also accepts the physics that support only that one and solves them first as background physics. Heat is solved as a steady state in every study except time_dependent.
- StudySpec.sweep {"parameter": name, "values": [...]} builds and runs the model once per value with the parameter set to it ({"spacing": "linear" | "log", "lower", "upper", "count"} for a range instead); summary.json sweep holds the derived values and feature result digests per value.
- Physics type entries: "Default study" is the study the GUI applies when the physics is the first one. State fields are the solver state: expressions name them <physics>_<field>, or <field> when one physics alone provides it; field_transfer source_field. Output fields are what Results.field, study stored_fields (<physics>.<field>) and derived values read; the primary one is stored when stored_fields is []. Scalar outputs are numbers after a run; derived-value expressions name them <physics>_<name>.
- Source slots (physics type entries) are the coupling targets (CouplingSpec.target; field_transfer target_slot), with unit and meaning; a slot takes one overwriting coupling, or several additive ones whose contributions are summed (see the coupling types).
- Feature entries: "Result kind `<kind>`" means Results.result(physics name, feature name) returns a dict with the keys listed under Result kinds (topic results; a feature topic lists them inline). "Requires a uniform mesh": nonuniform and auto modes fall back to a uniform grid at the finest target (see mesh).

### Derived values

- A derived value that fails for any reason, including running out of GPU memory, becomes NaN plus a warning (summary.json warnings); the run itself is not failed by it.
- DerivedValueSpec.source 'physics.feature' reduces a 1D result (timeseries, flux_spectrum, far_field, xy, table) instead of fields. Its sample names (they shadow parameters): every numeric scalar and every numeric array with one entry per sample of the result dict by key (timeseries t, values; flux_spectrum wavelength, frequency, power, power_per_cw (FDTD only); xy x and extras such as wavelength, n_eff), plus the xy series by name and the numeric table columns by name (one sample per row, abscissa row = 0, 1, ...). xy series and table column names are known only at run time: a missing one gives NaN plus a warning. far_field: the pattern at one wavelength (DerivedValueSpec.wavelength): angle [rad], power, power_norm (power over its peak), power_per_cw (when the result has it), and that wavelength and frequency as numbers.
- Far-field examples: beam direction {"name": "theta_peak", "source": "em.ff", "expression": "power", "operation": "argmax"}, beam width {"name": "theta_fwhm", "source": "em.ff", "expression": "power", "operation": "fwhm"}, value at an angle {"name": "p_up", "source": "em.ff", "expression": "power_norm", "operation": "at", "at": "pi/2"}; a line width {"name": "Q_line", "source": "em.trans", "expression": "power", "operation": "lorentz_fit", "fit": "q", "window": ["1545*nm", "1555*nm"]}.
- A sample name may equal an expression function name (e.g. the xy series abs of an FDFD probe): written without "(" it is the sample ("abs**2"), with "(" the function ("abs(phase)"); one expression may not use the same name both ways. Analytic curve series match series names as plain text, so any name works there.
- Example: {"name": "T_1550", "source": "em.trans", "expression": "power", "operation": "at", "at": "1550*nm", "reference": "T_film"}.

### Analytic curves

- ModelSpec.analytic_curves never change the run: they are drawn over the results and compared with them (summary.json curve_error; with a tolerance, selftest --examples fails the model above it). The GUI evaluates them with numpy on its own thread over the parameters of the last built session (a sweep: its last value) on 501 points spanning the sampled range (timeseries: the own sample times when there are 501 to 20000, else 501 or 20000 points, so a ring-down does not alias; fft: the FFT frequency bins; sweep: 201 points over the swept values) and draws them dashed in the colour of the simulated curve they belong to; a failing curve is reported in the Results panel message line.
- Sweep tab: each numeric column of a per-value table result is offered as bands vs the swept parameter ('<column>_<k>', sorted per value as Results.sweep_xy); the per-value result overlays also draw the curves targeting that result, evaluated at each swept value. Curves & tables: a table result is also plotted versus a chosen numeric column (x_column of its curves). Headless figures (figures=True) draw feature curves except series 'ratio' and 'fft' (no FFT figure; a flux spectrum only series '' and 'power', its one panel), a table's curves into figures/<key>_vs_<x_column or row>.png and line curves into figures/curve_<name>.png.
- Examples: {"name": "T_fp", "target": "em.trans", "expression": "1 / (1 + F*sin(2*pi*n_f*d_f/wavelength)**2)", "series": "ratio"}; {"name": "T_line", "target": "line", "expression": "T0 + q*s*(L - s)/(2*k_s)", "line": [0, "H/2", "L", "H/2"], "field": "heat.T"}; {"name": "R_sweep", "target": "sweep", "expression": "R0*(1 + alpha*w)", "series": "R"}; {"name": "ring", "target": "em.probe", "expression": "A*exp(-pi*f0*t/Q)*cos(2*pi*f0*t)"}; {"name": "ring_fft", "target": "em.probe", "expression": "A/(2*sqrt((2*pi*(frequency - f0))**2 + (pi*f0/Q)**2))", "series": "fft"}; {"name": "band_2", "target": "sweep", "expression": "c0*k_b/(2*pi*n_eff)", "series": "frequency_2"}; {"name": "Q_fit", "target": "em.res", "expression": "Q0", "x_column": "frequency", "series": "Q"}; {"name": "mode_2", "target": "line", "expression": "A*sin(2*pi*s/L)", "line": [0, "H/2", "L", "H/2"], "field": "em.ez", "snapshot": "resonance 2"}; {"name": "T_top", "target": "line", "expression": "T0", "line": [0, 0, "L", 0], "field": "heat.T", "plane": "h_top"}.

### Derived curves

- ModelSpec.derived_curves are evaluated with numpy after the run (GUI: on its own thread, re-evaluated when edited, no rerun) over the final feature results and the parameters of the last built session (a sweep: its last value). A failing curve (missing result or sample, other abscissa, expression error) is left out of its plot and reported: GUI message line, summary.json derived_curves {name: {plot, error}}.
- Example (heterodyne signal over shot noise, P_LO cancels: eta S / (h nu), S scaled from 1 V/m to a beam power): {"name": "snr_trn", "inputs": {"S": "heat.top_x:psd"}, "expression": "eta*S*E0sq/(h_const*c_const/lambda0)", "plot": "snr", "label": "TRN", "unit": "1", "log_x": true, "log_y": true} with E0sq a parameter.
- Calculus example (a capacitance dQ/dV from an xy result whose x is a voltage and whose series Q is a charge, against a constant): {"name": "C_V", "inputs": {"Q": "<physics>.<feature>:Q"}, "expression": "gradient(Q)", "unit": "F/m", "reference": "eps_ox*eps0_const/t_ox", "tolerance": 0.05}; a derived value with source "C_V" (expression "C_V") then reduces or fits the curve like a 1D result.

### Validation issues

- Levels: error, warning, info; errors block build and run. A build error becomes one issue at the node path of the failing build step.
- Node paths: ["parameters"] (each message names the parameter), ["geometry", name] (the domain size at ["geometry"]), ["selection", name], ["material", name], ["physics", name], ["feature", physics, feature], ["coupling", name], ["mesh"], ["study"], ["derived", name], ["curve", name], ["model"] (invalid file content and failures not tied to one node).
- Reports add node, the label of the path: [] -> model, ["mesh"] -> mesh, ["feature", "em", "source"] -> feature em/source.

## Expressions

Numeric values are numbers or expression strings, evaluated by a safe evaluator. Which names an expression may use depends on where it sits (Names available where).

### Syntax

- Arithmetic: + - * / // % ** and unary + -; ** is the power (^ is not allowed).
- Comparisons < <= > >= == != give 1 (true) or 0 (false), e.g. "(x > 1*um) * 2"; chained comparisons (a < b < c), and / or / not and if / else are not allowed: use where, min and max.
- Integer literals become floats (1/2 = 0.5). Only numbers, names and calls of the functions below with positional arguments are allowed (no attributes, indexing, strings or keywords). A function name without "(" is an ordinary name, which only a result sample name can supply (see Derived values).
- At most 2000 characters. Results must be real: a complex result (e.g. (-8)**(1/3)) is an error, and a value outside a function domain (log(-1)) gives nan, which fails where a finite number is needed.
- With numbers and parameters only an expression gives one float; with x, y, z or fields it is evaluated per cell.

### Functions

- abs(x): absolute value [1 argument]
- acos(x): inverse cosine in rad, for x in [-1, 1] [1 argument]
- asin(x): inverse sine in rad, for x in [-1, 1] [1 argument]
- atan(x): inverse tangent in rad, in (-pi/2, pi/2) [1 argument]
- atan2(y, x): angle of the point (x, y) in rad, in [-pi, pi], counter-clockwise from +x [2 arguments]
- ceil(x): smallest whole number >= x (a float) [1 argument]
- cos(x): cosine of an angle x in rad [1 argument]
- cosh(x): hyperbolic cosine [1 argument]
- erf(x): error function (2/sqrt(pi)) * integral of exp(-u**2) from 0 to x, in (-1, 1) [1 argument]
- erfc(x): complementary error function 1 - erf(x), accurate where erf(x) is close to 1 [1 argument]
- exp(x): e to the power x [1 argument]
- floor(x): largest whole number <= x (a float) [1 argument]
- hypot(a, b): sqrt(a**2 + b**2) without intermediate overflow [2 arguments]
- i0(x): modified Bessel function of the first kind I_0 (overflows to inf above x ~ 700) [1 argument]
- i1(x): modified Bessel function of the first kind I_1 (overflows to inf above x ~ 700) [1 argument]
- j0(x): Bessel function of the first kind J_0 (real x) [1 argument]
- j1(x): Bessel function of the first kind J_1 (real x) [1 argument]
- k0(x): modified Bessel function of the second kind K_0, for x > 0 (inf at 0, nan below) [1 argument]
- k1(x): modified Bessel function of the second kind K_1, for x > 0 (inf at 0, nan below) [1 argument]
- log(x): natural logarithm, for x > 0 [1 argument]
- log10(x): base-10 logarithm, for x > 0 [1 argument]
- max(a, b, ...): element-wise maximum of 2 or more arguments [at least 2 arguments]
- min(a, b, ...): element-wise minimum of 2 or more arguments [at least 2 arguments]
- pow(a, b): a to the power b, same as a**b [2 arguments]
- sign(x): -1, 0 or 1 by the sign of x [1 argument]
- sin(x): sine of an angle x in rad [1 argument]
- sinh(x): hyperbolic sine [1 argument]
- sqrt(x): square root, for x >= 0 [1 argument]
- tan(x): tangent of an angle x in rad [1 argument]
- tanh(x): hyperbolic tangent [1 argument]
- where(condition, a, b): element-wise a where condition is true (non-zero), else b; both a and b are evaluated everywhere [3 arguments]
- y0(x): Bessel function of the second kind Y_0, for x > 0 (-inf at 0, nan below) [1 argument]
- y1(x): Bessel function of the second kind Y_1, for x > 0 (-inf at 0, nan below) [1 argument]

### Constants

- `pi` = 3.14159: ratio of circumference to diameter of a circle
- `c_const` = 2.99792e+08: speed of light in vacuum [m/s]
- `eps0_const` = 8.85419e-12: vacuum permittivity [F/m]
- `mu0_const` = 1.25664e-06: vacuum permeability [H/m]
- `h_const` = 6.62607e-34: Planck constant [J s]
- `hbar_const` = 1.05457e-34: reduced Planck constant [J s]
- `e_const` = 1.60218e-19: elementary charge [C]
- `kB_const` = 1.38065e-23: Boltzmann constant [J/K]
- `NA_const` = 6.02214e+23: Avogadro constant [1/mol]
- `nm` = 1e-09: length unit 1e-9 (m)
- `um` = 1e-06: length unit 1e-6 (m)
- `mm` = 0.001: length unit 1e-3 (m)
- `cm` = 0.01: length unit 1e-2 (m)
- `fs` = 1e-15: time unit 1e-15 (s)
- `ps` = 1e-12: time unit 1e-12 (s)
- `ns` = 1e-09: time unit 1e-9 (s)
- `us` = 1e-06: time unit 1e-6 (s)
- `ms` = 0.001: time unit 1e-3 (s)
- `THz` = 1e+12: frequency unit 1e12 (Hz)
- `GHz` = 1e+09: frequency unit 1e9 (Hz)
- `MHz` = 1e+06: frequency unit 1e6 (Hz)
- `kHz` = 1000: frequency unit 1e3 (Hz)

### Reserved names

Not usable as parameter names: GHz, MHz, NA_const, THz, abs, acos, asin, atan, atan2, c_const, ceil, cm, cos, cosh, e_const, eps0_const, erf, erfc, exp, floor, fs, h_const, hbar_const, hypot, i0, i1, j0, j1, k0, k1, kB_const, kHz, log, log10, max, min, mm, ms, mu0_const, nm, ns, pi, pow, ps, sign, sin, sinh, sqrt, t, tan, tanh, um, us, value, where, x, y, y0, y1, z. Time and coordinates: t, x, y, z; value is the source field in coupling expressions.

### Names available where

- ParameterSpec.expression: numbers, constants and other parameters in any order (unknown names and cycles are errors).
- Domain size, geometry params, mesh values, refinement dx / margin, sweep values, dispersion pole values and every param without "may use x, y": parameters only.
- Physics settings, feature params and material properties marked "may use x, y": also x and y, the cell centres in m (EM PML cells take the nearest window centre), and in 3D models the height z [m] (z in a 2D model is a validation error). 3D materials using z are written one z cell plane at a time, feature values using z cover the bounding box of their selection.
- Params marked "may use physics fields" (material properties): also the state fields of the physics in the model as <physics>_<field>, or <field> when one physics alone provides it (e.g. T with one heat physics); such a property is rewritten right after each step of the physics it reads (the one with the largest every), so physics stepping on later ticks see it, but only when one of them solved or stepped since the last rewrite (a quasi-static physics that did not re-solve rewrites nothing), and once more after the final solves of a time-dependent run (a stationary study iterates it; a frequency_domain study allows only fields of its background physics). They may also use the time t [s] (with or without fields and x, y): a property using t is rewritten at the start of every runner step (before the steps of that tick, t = the step start time; t = 0 in every other study).
- Feature params marked "may use t": also the time t [s] with parameters only (no x, y, z: a value changing in time is uniform in space), re-evaluated at the start of every runner step of the physics (t = its step start time; an implicit step, e.g. transient heat, sees the start value, a first-order lag); t = 0 at the build and in every other study.
- Coupling params of kind expression (field_transfer expression): value (the source field), x, y (3D: z) and parameters; no other field names and no t.
- Derived values: parameters, x, y (3D: z), t (the final time), the output fields as <physics>_<field> or a unique <field> and the scalar outputs of a physics (its type's Scalar outputs, e.g. em_modes n_eff_1) as <physics>_<name> only (a number after the run; a name the solver did not report gives NaN plus a warning); with a source the sample names of that result (a derived curve source: the curve name and x) instead (see Derived values). Derived value at / reference / window / wavelength: parameters only.
- Analytic curves: parameters and the variables of their target (AnalyticCurveSpec.expression).
- Derived curves: parameters, their input aliases and x, plus the calls gradient / cumtrapz (DerivedCurveSpec.expression); reference: parameters and x.
- A parameter may not have the name of a physics state or output field or scalar output (validation error).
