## Geometry

ModelSpec.geometry objects are named shapes in m; selections, materials, features and mesh refinements refer to them by name.

- Geometry kinds by entity kind: domain: rectangle, rounded_rectangle, circle, ellipse, polygon, union, intersection, difference, array, box, cylinder_z, sphere; point: point; line: line.
- Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain: x from 0 to size_x (to the right), y from 0 to size_y (up); EM PML cells lie outside.
- Masks test cell centres: rectangles and polygons are half-open [x0, x1) x [y0, y1), circles and ellipses are closed; rounded rectangles are half-open along their straight sides, closed on their corner arcs; a point or line end exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell.
- Validation's material preview uses float64 cell centres over (0, size_x, 0, size_y) while the build tests float32 cell centres clamped into the window, so cells exactly on a boundary can differ: avoid material edges exactly on cell centres.
- Composite inputs (union, intersection, difference, array) are consumed: they can no longer be selected on their own and may feed only one composite.
- An array repeats its base object on an nx x ny (x nz) grid of copies moved by multiples of pitch_x / pitch_y / pitch_z, the base being the first copy: one GeometrySpec for thousands of holes or pillars. It acts as one domain object (a union of its copies) in selections, materials, features and refinements; meshes follow every copy's outline. Copies are internal shapes named '<array>[i,j]' (never selectable); overlapping copies get a validation warning.

### Geometry kind `rectangle` - Rectangle

Axis-aligned rectangle (domain object) between two opposite corners. Rectangle corners may be given in any order. Shape inclusion tests cell centres: rectangles are half-open [x0, x1) x [y0, y1) (corners sorted), so a centre exactly on x0 / y0 is inside and one on x1 / y1 is outside. In 3D models it is extruded along 'axis' (z by default) between z0 and z1, optionally with tilted side walls (sidewall_angle). Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `rectangle`; entity kind domain; composite: no

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `x0` (float; unit m; default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, x
  x of one corner, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain; the corners may be given in any order.
- `y0` (float; unit m; default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, y
  y of the same corner as x0, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `x1` (float; unit m; default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, x
  x of the opposite corner; cell centres with min(x0, x1) <= x < max(x0, x1) are inside (half-open).
- `y1` (float; unit m; default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, y
  y of the opposite corner; cell centres with min(y0, y1) <= y < max(y0, y1) are inside (half-open).
- `z0` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Extrusion start
  Lower end of the extrusion along its axis (z, or x / y with axis x / y) in m; null = from the bottom of the domain (full height, PML included; axis z only). Cell centres with min(z0, z1) <= coordinate < max(z0, z1) are inside (half-open). Only for 3D models (domain size_z set); it must stay null in a 2D model.
- `z1` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Extrusion end
  Upper end of the extrusion along its axis in m; null = to the top of the domain (axis z only). Only for 3D models (domain size_z set); it must stay null in a 2D model.
- `axis` (choice; default "z"; choices z | x | y) - Extrusion axis
  Axis the 2D shape is extruded along. 'z' (default): the shape lies in the x-y plane. 'x' / 'y': its coordinates (x, y) are the model's (y, z) / (x, z), the ellipse angle turns from the first toward the second, and z0 / z1 are its ends along x / y, which must then both be set (beyond the domain to run into the PML): a circle with axis 'x' is a cylinder along x (holes through a slab, rods, wires). Faces parallel to the mesh axes become snap nodes on refined meshes; curved faces are staircased. 3D models only; it must stay 'z' in a 2D model.
- `sidewall_angle` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Sidewall angle
  Tilt of the side walls from the extrusion axis in degrees, -90 < angle < 90 (0 = straight walls). The shape as given sits at min(z0, z1) and is offset inward by (s - min(z0, z1)) tan(angle) up to the other end, s the coordinate along the axis: positive angles narrow it toward z1 (etched ridges, tapered holes, waveguide tapers along x / y), negative ones widen it (undercuts; V-grooves as a widening hole subtracted from the substrate). Rectangles shrink on every side, circles become cones, ellipses elliptic frusta (both semi-axes shrink by the same offset), polygons are offset per vertex (mitred; simple polygons only). Needs both z0 and z1; an offset that collapses or self-intersects the shape is an error. The slanted walls are staircased by the cells (one 2D raster per z cell); along x / y each cross-section is a polygon sampled in 256 steps along the axis (tapered rectangles exact, curved and polygon walls within a fraction of a step). 3D models only; it must stay 0 in a 2D model.

### Geometry kind `rounded_rectangle` - Rounded rectangle

Axis-aligned rectangle (domain object) between two opposite corners with its four corners rounded to quarter circles of radius r (0 <= r <= half the shorter side; the same as a union of two rectangles and four circles). Shape inclusion tests cell centres: half-open like rectangles along the straight sides ([x0, x1) x [y0, y1), corners sorted), closed like circles on the rounded corners. Triangle meshes follow the corner arcs exactly (P2 curved edges); tetrahedron meshes (gmsh) export an untapered z prism as two boxes and four z cylinders, other axes and tapers are tagged per element. In 3D models it is extruded along 'axis' (z by default) between z0 and z1, optionally with tilted side walls (sidewall_angle). Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `rounded_rectangle`; entity kind domain; composite: no

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `x0` (float; unit m; default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, x
  x of one corner of the enclosing rectangle, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain; the corners may be given in any order.
- `y0` (float; unit m; default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, y
  y of the same corner as x0, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `x1` (float; unit m; default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, x
  x of the opposite corner of the enclosing rectangle.
- `y1` (float; unit m; default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, y
  y of the opposite corner of the enclosing rectangle.
- `r` (float; unit m; default 1e-07; range [0, inf)) - Corner radius
  Radius of the four quarter-circle corners in m, 0 <= r <= half the shorter side (0 = a plain rectangle; half the shorter side = a stadium; half of both sides of a square = a circle).
- `z0` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Extrusion start
  Lower end of the extrusion along its axis (z, or x / y with axis x / y) in m; null = from the bottom of the domain (full height, PML included; axis z only). Cell centres with min(z0, z1) <= coordinate < max(z0, z1) are inside (half-open). Only for 3D models (domain size_z set); it must stay null in a 2D model.
- `z1` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Extrusion end
  Upper end of the extrusion along its axis in m; null = to the top of the domain (axis z only). Only for 3D models (domain size_z set); it must stay null in a 2D model.
- `axis` (choice; default "z"; choices z | x | y) - Extrusion axis
  Axis the 2D shape is extruded along. 'z' (default): the shape lies in the x-y plane. 'x' / 'y': its coordinates (x, y) are the model's (y, z) / (x, z), the ellipse angle turns from the first toward the second, and z0 / z1 are its ends along x / y, which must then both be set (beyond the domain to run into the PML): a circle with axis 'x' is a cylinder along x (holes through a slab, rods, wires). Faces parallel to the mesh axes become snap nodes on refined meshes; curved faces are staircased. 3D models only; it must stay 'z' in a 2D model.
- `sidewall_angle` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Sidewall angle
  Tilt of the side walls from the extrusion axis in degrees, -90 < angle < 90 (0 = straight walls). The shape as given sits at min(z0, z1) and is offset inward by (s - min(z0, z1)) tan(angle) up to the other end, s the coordinate along the axis: positive angles narrow it toward z1 (etched ridges, tapered holes, waveguide tapers along x / y), negative ones widen it (undercuts; V-grooves as a widening hole subtracted from the substrate). Rectangles shrink on every side, circles become cones, ellipses elliptic frusta (both semi-axes shrink by the same offset), polygons are offset per vertex (mitred; simple polygons only). Needs both z0 and z1; an offset that collapses or self-intersects the shape is an error. The slanted walls are staircased by the cells (one 2D raster per z cell); along x / y each cross-section is a polygon sampled in 256 steps along the axis (tapered rectangles exact, curved and polygon walls within a fraction of a step). 3D models only; it must stay 0 in a 2D model.

### Geometry kind `circle` - Circle

Circle (domain object) of radius r around (cx, cy). Shape inclusion tests cell centres: circles are closed, so a centre exactly on the circle is inside. In 3D models it is extruded along 'axis' (z by default) between z0 and z1, optionally with tilted side walls (sidewall_angle). Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `circle`; entity kind domain; composite: no

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `cx` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - Centre x
  x of the centre, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `cy` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - Centre y
  y of the centre, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `r` (float; unit m; default 5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Radius
  Radius (> 0); a cell centre exactly on the circle is inside (closed test).
- `z0` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Extrusion start

### Geometry kind `ellipse` - Ellipse

Ellipse (domain object) with semi-axes a and b about (cx, cy). The ellipse angle is in degrees, counter-clockwise from +x. Shape inclusion tests cell centres: ellipses are closed, so a centre exactly on the ellipse is inside. In 3D models it is extruded along 'axis' (z by default) between z0 and z1, optionally with tilted side walls (sidewall_angle). Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- `cy` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - Centre y
  y of the centre, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `a` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - First semi-axis
  Semi-axis along the local x axis, which the rotation turns away from +x (> 0).
- `b` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Second semi-axis
  Semi-axis along the local y axis (> 0).
- `angle` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Rotation

### Geometry kind `polygon` - Polygon

Polygon (domain object) through its vertices. Polygons are implicitly closed, use the even-odd fill rule and need at least 3 points, not all on one line. Shape inclusion tests cell centres: polygons are half-open like rectangles, so a centre exactly on a left / bottom edge is inside and one on a right / top edge is outside. In 3D models it is extruded along 'axis' (z by default) between z0 and z1, optionally with tilted side walls (sidewall_angle). Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `polygon`; entity kind domain; composite: no

### Geometry kind `point` - Point

Zero-area point entity for sources, probes and monitors (point source, field probe, temperature probe). A coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell. Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `point`; entity kind point; composite: no

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `x` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - x
  x of the point, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain; on a cell edge it goes to the upper cell.
- `y` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - y
  y of the point, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain; on a cell edge it goes to the upper cell.
- `z` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - z
  Height (z) of the point / the plane holding the line, in m; null = mid-height size_z / 2; on a cell edge it goes to the upper cell. Only for 3D models (domain size_z set); it must stay null in a 2D model.

### Geometry kind `line` - Line segment

Zero-area line segment for sources, probes and monitors (line source, gaussian beam, flux monitor); lines used by EM features must be horizontal or vertical. A coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell. Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `line`; entity kind line; composite: no

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `x0` (float; unit m; default 1e-06) - Start x
  x of the start point, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `y0` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - Start y
  y of the start point, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `x1` (float; unit m; default 3e-06) - End x
  x of the end point; x1 = x0 makes a vertical line (EM line features need a horizontal or vertical line).
- `y1` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - End y
  y of the end point; y1 = y0 makes a horizontal line. An end exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell.
- `z` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - z
  Height (z) of the point / the plane holding the line, in m; null = mid-height size_z / 2; on a cell edge it goes to the upper cell. Only for 3D models (domain size_z set); it must stay null in a 2D model.

### Geometry kind `union` - Union

Union of domain objects: a cell centre inside any input is inside. Composites (union / intersection / difference / array) consume their inputs, which can no longer be selected on their own and may feed only one composite. Inputs are domain objects, composites included.

- GeometrySpec.kind `union`; entity kind domain; composite: yes

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `inputs` (names: geometry names; default []) - Input objects
  Domain objects combined by this operation (at least one); each input is consumed: it can no longer be selected on its own and may feed only one composite.

### Geometry kind `intersection` - Intersection

Intersection of domain objects: a cell centre must be inside every input. Composites (union / intersection / difference / array) consume their inputs, which can no longer be selected on their own and may feed only one composite. Inputs are domain objects, composites included.

- GeometrySpec.kind `intersection`; entity kind domain; composite: yes

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `inputs` (names: geometry names; default []) - Input objects
  Domain objects combined by this operation (at least one); each input is consumed: it can no longer be selected on its own and may feed only one composite.

### Geometry kind `difference` - Difference

The base object minus the subtracted objects: a cell centre inside the base and outside every subtracted object is inside. Composites (union / intersection / difference / array) consume their inputs, which can no longer be selected on their own and may feed only one composite. Inputs are domain objects, composites included.

- GeometrySpec.kind `difference`; entity kind domain; composite: yes

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `base` (ref: geometry name; required) - Base object
  Domain object the others are subtracted from; it is consumed: it can no longer be selected on its own and may feed only one composite.
- `subtract` (names: geometry names; default []) - Objects to subtract
  Domain objects removed from the base (may be empty); each is consumed: it can no longer be selected on its own and may feed only one composite.

### Geometry kind `array` - Array

Rectangular array (the industry-standard array operation) of nx x ny (x nz in 3D) copies of the base object: copy (i, j, k) is the base moved by (i pitch_x, j pitch_y, k pitch_z), copy (0, 0, 0) is the base itself; a cell centre inside any copy is inside (a union of the copies). The array is one domain object: materials, features, selections and mesh refinements naming it act on every copy; meshes follow every copy's outline (triangles: curved edges on circles, ellipses and rounded-rectangle arcs; tetrahedra (gmsh): the solids of each copy). Composite bases are copied whole (a hole with a ring cut out, nested arrays). At most 200000 copies. Composites (union / intersection / difference / array) consume their inputs, which can no longer be selected on their own and may feed only one composite. Inputs are domain objects, composites included. Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `array`; entity kind domain; composite: yes

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `base` (ref: geometry name; required) - Base object
  Domain object repeated by the array (a primitive or a composite); it is the first copy, at its own position, and is consumed: it can no longer be selected on its own and may feed only one composite.
- `nx` (int; unit 1; default 2; range [1, inf)) - Copies along x
  Number of copies along x (>= 1), the base included.
- `ny` (int; unit 1; default 2; range [1, inf)) - Copies along y
  Number of copies along y (>= 1), the base included.
- `pitch_x` (float; unit m; default 1e-06; range (0, inf)) - Pitch x
  Displacement between neighbouring copies along x in m (> 0): copy (i, j) is the base moved by (i pitch_x, j pitch_y). Copies whose bounding boxes overlap get a validation warning (overlapping copies merge into one region).
- `pitch_y` (float; unit m; default 1e-06; range (0, inf)) - Pitch y
  Displacement between neighbouring copies along y in m (> 0).
- `nz` (int; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Copies along z
  Number of copies along z (>= 1, the base included); above 1 it needs pitch_z. Only for 3D models (domain size_z set); it must stay null in a 2D model. In 2D models it must stay 1.
- `pitch_z` (float; unit m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Pitch z
  Displacement between neighbouring copies along z in m (> 0); needed when nz > 1. A base with an open z end (z0 / z1 null) reaches the domain top / bottom in every copy, so such copies overlap. Only for 3D models (domain size_z set); it must stay null in a 2D model.

### Geometry kind `box` - Box

Axis-aligned box (3D domain object) between two opposite corners, half-open on every axis like rectangles; the same as a rectangle with z0 / z1. 3D models only. Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `box`; entity kind domain; composite: no

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `x0` (float; unit m; default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, x
  x of one corner, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain; corners in any order.
- `y0` (float; unit m; default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, y
  y of the same corner as x0.
- `z0` (float; unit m; default 1.5e-06) - Corner 1, z
  z of the same corner as x0.
- `x1` (float; unit m; default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, x
  x of the opposite corner.
- `y1` (float; unit m; default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, y
  y of the opposite corner.
- `z1` (float; unit m; default 2.5e-06) - Corner 2, z
  z of the opposite corner; cell centres with min <= coordinate < max on each axis are inside (half-open).

### Geometry kind `cylinder_z` - Cylinder (z axis)

Cylinder with its axis along z (3D domain object): a circle extruded from z0 to z1 (a circle with axis 'x' / 'y' gives a cylinder along x / y, sidewall_angle a cone). 3D models only. Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `cylinder_z`; entity kind domain; composite: no

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `cx` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - Centre x
  x of the axis, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `cy` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - Centre y
  y of the axis, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `r` (float; unit m; default 5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Radius
  Radius (> 0); closed test like circles.
- `z0` (float; unit m; default 1.5e-06) - Bottom z
  One end of the cylinder along z (ends in any order; half-open in z).
- `z1` (float; unit m; default 2.5e-06) - Top z
  The other end along z.

### Geometry kind `sphere` - Sphere

Sphere (3D domain object) of radius r around (cx, cy, cz); closed test like circles. The 2D canvas draws its cross-section at the shown layer. 3D models only. Coordinates are physical, in m, with the origin at the lower-left corner of the physical domain (the PML lies outside).

- GeometrySpec.kind `sphere`; entity kind domain; composite: no

Params (GeometrySpec.params):
- `cx` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - Centre x
  x of the centre, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `cy` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - Centre y
  y of the centre, measured from the lower-left corner of the physical domain.
- `cz` (float; unit m; default 2e-06) - Centre z
  z of the centre, measured from the bottom of the physical domain.
- `r` (float; unit m; default 5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Radius
  Radius (> 0); a cell centre exactly on the sphere is inside (closed test).

## Materials

Materials assign properties to domain entities: a library material, explicit properties of the present physics types and EM dispersion poles.

- MaterialSpec.library takes a library material name below; properties override its values (a null property keeps the library value); dispersion null inherits the library poles, [] removes them, a list replaces them.
- Materials apply in list order and later materials win overlapping cells (whole cells). A material whose selection contains all is a background material: it fills only the cells no other material covers, wherever it sits in the list (of several background materials the later wins). Cells under no material keep the type defaults: vacuum for EM, k = 0 (no conduction) for heat, sigma_dc = 0 (insulator) for electric_currents, eps_dc = 1 (vacuum) for electrostatics.
- Only the material properties of the physics types present in a model are written, and only those the merged material sets; each physics type section lists its material properties with units and help. A property of kind table (e.g. magnetostatics bh_curve) is one constant table per material, written to no array: its physics reads it per material region.
- eps_r is isotropic; eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz are components written after it (a component wins): the E_z types (em_fdtd_ez, em_fdfd_ez) see eps_zz (their eps_r array), the H_z types (em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz) see eps_xx and eps_yy, em_modes sees all three; each type lists its own vocabulary.
- Library optical values (eps_r, sigma_e) are for 1.55 um; an entry without dispersion poles has the same index at every wavelength. Thermal data use the model property names (cp = specific heat). Electrical data (sigma_dc, eps_dc) are static values for electric_currents / electrostatics, distinct from the optical sigma_e / eps_r.
- Dispersion poles are dicts {"model": "drude" | "lorentz", ...} with the params below (EM only); for a Drude material that sets no permittivity property for an array (eps_r or that component) the first Drude eps_inf is the background permittivity of that array.
- An {"model": "nk_fit", ...} entry (one per material; library materials with tabulated n, k only: their description names the data set) is replaced by eps_inf (>= 1) + an optional Drude pole + Lorentz poles fitted to the table over [wavelength_start, wavelength_stop] (bounded least squares, all pole values >= 0: passive); the library optical values are then dropped, eps_inf is the Drude eps_inf or, without a Drude pole, eps_r. Validation reports the fit (max |eps error| relative to |eps|, loss error relative to |Im eps| + 0.03 |eps|) as info, as a warning above 2 % / 10 % or when the study band leaves the fit range. FDTD steps the fitted poles; the FDFD, em_modes and slab-mode ports use their exact chi(omega).
- A {"model": "crystal", "crystal": <name>, "euler_deg": [phi, theta, psi], "plane": "sagittal"} entry (one per material; crystals aluminum_nitride, gallium_arsenide, lithium_niobate, quartz, zinc_oxide) is no pole: it is removed from the list and sets the rotated crystal data in model axes, c11, c12, c22, c66 (c16 / c26 when non-zero), rho, piezo_e11 .. piezo_e26 and the clamped eps_dc_xx / _yy / _xy; with optical data (not every crystal) also photoelastic_p11 / _p12 (+ the elastic_waves tensor entries photoelastic_p16 .. _p66 when the cut is not isotropic in them; row 6 = xy, the eps_xy of em_fdfd_hz) and the clamped Pockels tensor pockels_r11 .. _r62 when non-zero (precedence: library < crystal < explicit properties, also beside nk_fit). The optical index itself is not set (eps_r / eps_xx / eps_yy stay the material values). euler_deg are plain numbers in degrees, SAW convention: passive Rz(psi) Rx(theta) Rz(phi), rows X1' = propagation, X3' = surface normal (YZ = 0, 90, 90); sagittal = model (x, y, z) = (X1', X3', -X2'). Only the anti-plane couplings are dropped (validation reports the sagittal values as info and warns when they are not negligible), and the off-diagonal photoelastic / Pockels index change (the acousto-optic and Pockels couplings warn). A 3D model needs "plane": "full" (2D models 'sagittal', the default; validation errors otherwise): model (x, y, z) = (X1', X2', X3'), the surface normal along z, and the entry sets all 21 c11 .. c66 (Voigt 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy), the 18 piezo_e11 .. piezo_e36, eps_dc_xx / _yy / _zz / _yz / _xz / _xy and rho (no optical entries).

### Library materials

#### Library material `air`

Air at room temperature with vacuum optics. Heat conducts through it only: there is no convection inside the gas, so model convective cooling with a convection boundary feature instead. An insulator (no sigma_dc).

- Properties: {"eps_r": 1, "k": 0.026, "rho": 1.225, "cp": 1005, "dndT": 0, "alpha": 0, "eps_dc": 1}
- Dispersion poles: none

#### Library material `aluminum`

Aluminium (library name aluminum) for EM, heat and electric currents (room temperature). The effective Drude pole is fitted to Rakic 1998 at 1.55 um: eps -244 - 49.6j (Rakic about -243 - 49j). It folds the 1.5 eV (0.83 um) interband band into the pole, so it is a near-IR fit only: in the visible / UV it is wrong (a broadband free-electron pole, Ordal omega_p 2.24e16, gamma 1.22e14, gives -335 - 34j at 1.55 um instead). For other bands use an nk_fit dispersion entry on its table (Rakic 1995 evaporated films, 207-1771 nm; a Lorentz pole takes the 800 nm interband band).

#### Library material `gold`

Gold for EM, heat and electric currents (room temperature). The Drude pole is a fit to Johnson & Christy 1972 valid about 0.6-2 um: eps about -116 - 10.6j at 1.55 um (Johnson & Christy about -114 - 11j; evaporated films in Olmon 2012 have |Im eps| about 7, single crystals about 4). The far-IR / DC damping (about 4e13 rad/s) would underestimate the near-IR loss 2-3x. No interband absorption, so least accurate below about 550 nm (|Im eps| up to ~5x low). Resolve the field decay into the metal (about 25 nm) with several cells. Its table (Johnson & Christy 1972, 188-1937 nm) serves an nk_fit dispersion entry, whose Lorentz poles add the interband absorption.

- Properties: {"k": 317, "rho": 19300, "cp": 129, "dndT": 0, "alpha": 1.42e-05, "youngs_modulus": 7.9e+10, "poisson_ratio": 0.42, "sigma_dc": 4.1e+07}

#### Library material `gst_225_amorphous`

Ge2Sb2Te5 phase-change alloy, amorphous (as deposited). Optical data at 1.55 um only, absorption as sigma_e (exact there, sigma_e = 2 n k omega eps0); non-dispersive. Thermal data: room-temperature conductivity of the phase (Lyeo et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 89, 151904 (2006)), density (Njoroge et al., J. Vac. Sci. Technol. A 20, 230 (2002)), a typical specific heat; no latent heat, no temperature dependence. For switching give its domains a phase_change_medium feature (its defaults are these optical constants plus the crystalline ones and the crystallisation kinetics). GST-225 data: n, k at 1.55 um as used for sputtered films in integrated photonics (e.g. Rios et al., Nat. Photonics 9, 725 (2015); film dependent by ~10 %); crystallisation onset ~150 C and activation energy 2.24 eV from Friedrich et al., J. Appl. Phys. 87, 4130 (2000); melting point 616 C from Yamada et al., J. Appl. Phys. 69, 2849 (1991). The Avrami exponent 2.5 is typical of nucleation-dominated GST (2-4 reported); the cap of 50 ns above 650 K is an illustrative calibration (100 s at the 150 C onset with 2.24 eV, tens of ns in laser / electrical SET pulses): fit both to the device.

- Properties: {"eps_r": 15.5216, "sigma_e": 3815.5, "k": 0.19, "rho": 5870, "cp": 210}
- Dispersion poles: none

X-cut lithium niobate film at 1.55 um and room temperature in top view, optic axis (crystal z) along model x: eps_xx = n_e^2 is seen by E_x (em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz, em_modes), eps_r = n_o^2 by E_y and E_z. Lossless and non-dispersive. dndT_xx is dn_e/dT, dndT_yy = dndT_zz dn_o/dT (approximate); k and alpha are a-axis values, alpha_xx the c-axis expansion along x, both the free crystal (a film bonded to Si follows the substrate: set alpha and alpha_xx; an alpha override alone keeps the library alpha_xx). eps_dc_xx = eps_c and eps_dc = eps_a are clamped values (eps^S, as for RF / electro-optic electrodes). Pockels coefficients for an applied field along the optic axis (electrostatics_em_pockels with field_component 'x'): r_xx = r33 (n_e, E_x of the H_z types), r = r13 on r_yy and r_zz (n_o), both clamped (r^S, consistent with the clamped eps_dc; the unclamped r13 / r33 of a free crystal at low frequency are 10 / 32.2 pm/V). An applied field along y acts through r22 / r51 terms, not modelled (keep field_component 'x').

#### Library material `lithium_niobate_z_cut`

Z-cut lithium niobate film at 1.55 um and room temperature, optic axis z (out of plane): eps_zz = n_e^2 (n_e = 2.138) is seen by E_z (em_fdtd_ez, em_fdfd_ez), and the isotropic xy plane has eps_r = n_o^2 (n_o = 2.211), seen by E_x / E_y (em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz). No Pockels coefficients: an in-plane applied field of a z-cut film acts through r22 with opposite signs on n_xx and n_yy, which the diagonal r_xx / r_yy / r_zz of electrostatics_em_pockels cannot express.

#### Library material `silicon`

Crystalline silicon at 1.55 um and room temperature (n = 3.476), lossless and non-dispersive, so every wavelength sees n = 3.476 (real silicon absorbs below about 1.1 um). An nk_fit dispersion entry gives dispersive, absorbing silicon instead (table: Green 2008, intrinsic, 300 K, 250-1450 nm, band-to-band absorption only). Intrinsic: no sigma_dc (doped silicon sets its own, e.g. 1e4 S/m). Thermal conductivity: the common engineering value, below the ~148 W/(m K) of pure bulk silicon at 300 K (doped silicon, thin device layers and higher temperatures run lower). Elastic data: an isotropic average of the cubic crystal (E is 130 GPa along <100>, 169 GPa along <110>). Drift-diffusion data: 300 K, mobilities of lightly doped silicon (no doping or field dependence).

### Dispersion pole models (MaterialSpec.dispersion items)

#### Pole model `drude`

- `omega_p` (float; unit rad/s; default 1.37e+16; range [0, inf)) - Plasma frequency
  Plasma angular frequency of the Drude current dJ/dt + gamma J = eps0 omega_p^2 E (on every E component the polarisation carries: E_z, or E_x and E_y), in rad/s (not Hz); gold ~1.37e16, aluminium ~2.24e16 rad/s (library aluminum: 1.94e16, a 1.55 um fit). em_fdtd_ez and em_fdtd_hz both step the current with a leap-frog (J on the half time steps), accurate to O((omega dt)^2) but stable only where eps_inf * mu_r >= courant_factor^2 + mu_r (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 (square cells; the build checks every cell and names the largest stable courant_factor). That bites for eps_inf ~1 metals: omega_p 2.24e16 needs dx <= 5.4 nm at courant_factor 0.99 (courant_factor <= 0.967 at 10 nm); otherwise the mesh only has to resolve the skin depth of the metal (a few tens of nm for noble metals in the visible). em_fdfd_ez and em_fdfd_hz add the exact susceptibility chi(omega) of every pole at the solve wavelength (no time stepping).
- `gamma` (float; unit rad/s; default 1.02e+14; range [0, inf)) - Damping rate
  Collision rate of the Drude current in rad/s; it sets the metal loss. Optical (visible / near-IR) values: gold ~1.0e14 (the far-IR / DC value ~4e13 gives 2-3x too little near-IR loss), silver ~2.7e13 rad/s.
- `eps_inf` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - High-frequency permittivity
  Background permittivity of the Drude material, used for a permittivity array only when the material sets no permittivity property that owns it (an explicit eps_r or component such as eps_zz / eps_xx wins; only the first Drude pole counts); empty = 1. Gold ~9.8, silver ~3.7.

#### Pole model `lorentz`

- `delta_eps` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [0, inf)) - Oscillator strength
  Oscillator strength of d2P/dt2 + gamma dP/dt + omega_0^2 P = eps0 delta_eps omega_0^2 E (on every E component the polarisation carries): the static permittivity is the background + delta_eps, the background being eps_r or the component that owns the array (as eps_inf).
- `omega_0` (float; unit rad/s; default 3e+15; range [0, inf)) - Resonance frequency
  Resonance angular frequency in rad/s (not Hz); its vacuum wavelength is 2 pi C0 / omega_0 (3e15 rad/s = 628 nm).
- `gamma` (float; unit rad/s; default 1e+14; range [0, inf)) - Damping rate
  Damping rate of the Lorentz oscillator in rad/s, the full width of the resonance in omega; smaller values give a sharper, less lossy resonance.

#### Pole model `nk_fit`

- `n_lorentz` (int; default 2; range [0, 6]) - Number of resonances
  Lorentz poles of the fit (0-6); a Drude pole is added when Re eps < 0 somewhere in the fit range (metals). Each pole adds 1-2 float32 arrays on its bounding box in the FDTD; poles whose contribution stays below 1e-6 of |eps| are dropped. 2 suits a visible / near-IR octave.
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Fit from wavelength
  Shortest vacuum wavelength of the fit range, a plain number (no parameter expressions: the fit runs once per material at validation and build). Set the range to the study band: the frequency_domain wavelengths, the FDFD / em_modes wavelength, or the FDTD source spectra and monitor ranges (validation warns when they leave it). It must lie inside the library table.
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Fit to wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the fit range (> wavelength_start), a plain number. A narrower range fits more accurately with fewer poles.

## Mesh

ModelSpec.meshes sets the cell sizes, one MeshSpec per mesh; each physics runs on one (PhysicsSpec.mesh, "" = the first). check.json reports the resulting grids (cells, dx range, dt, PML cells) before any GPU work.

- Per-physics meshes (S7.2): every mesh spans the same domain; its padding (PML, mirror ghosts) and auto sizes come from the physics on it only. One mesh is required for: all EM physics (family em), physics joined by a coupling whose type does not transfer across meshes, a feature naming another physics, and every physics of a thermal_noise, optomechanics or nonlinear_frequency_domain study (validation errors). Cross-mesh couplings interpolate fields (linear between cell centres, edge-extended into padding) and move densities conservatively (overlap averages: window totals kept); a state-dependent material property reads the fields of a physics on another mesh interpolated. A mesh no physics uses is a warning and is not built. Fields and feature results live on their physics' own mesh (FieldData / saved fields name it); a derived value is evaluated on the mesh of the first physics (model order) its expression names, the fields of the others interpolated onto it (validate lists them as info).
- Mesh kind triangles (S7.5, 2D Cartesian models): free triangles following curved boundaries for the physics, features and solvers that declare them (the Mesh kinds line of each type: drift_diffusion, electric_currents, electrostatics, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical, em_fdfd_ez, em_fdfd_hz, em_modes, heat, magnetic_fields_ac, magnetostatics, membrane, pressure_acoustics, solid_mechanics; some only in one study, validation names the limits). Sizes as an industry-standard free triangular mesher: dx = maximum element size, max_ratio = maximum growth rate (null: 1.3), refinements = maximum sizes in / along / at their objects, h_min (null: dx / 100), curvature_factor 0.3 along circle and ellipse edges; auto: the wavelength rule with points_per_wavelength (null: 5), else the physics-controlled rule; the absorbing ring has pml_layers structured layers over the PML cells x dx.
- Mesh kind tetrahedra (3D Cartesian models): tetrahedra for electric_currents, electrostatics, em_fdfd_3d, heat, magnetostatics_3d, pressure_acoustics, solid_mechanics_3d (em_fdfd_3d: its eigenfrequency study, Nedelec edge elements by the discretization setting). Sizes as triangles; mesher 'gmsh' follows spheres, boxes, z cylinders and z-prism circles / rectangles (any axis for rectangles), composite inputs and array copies included, other objects are tagged per element; 'builtin' splits the bricks of a rectilinear grid into 6 tetrahedra (no slivers at any aspect ratio), equal cells <= dx, or graded by the tensor rules (refinements with per-axis sizes, axes, face_sizes as bands) with flat object faces as element faces; curved objects are a staircase. sweep_axis 'z' (either mesher) meshes the x-y footprint with triangles and stacks them in z layers graded by the z tensor rules (object top / bottom faces are layer planes), each prism split into 3 tetrahedra: thin plates and films with a few layers across. The PML is a shell of pml_cells x dx outside every cpml face meshed like the window. Fields are sampled on a uniform lattice over the window (cut planes, profiles, volumes); derived values of fields reduce degree-4 quadrature points of the window (or selected) elements (not yet: interface selections, max / min over mirror images, fields of physics on other meshes).
- No physics boundary configuration -> no PML. EM CPML cells (pml_cells per cpml face; each PML cell is dx wide on a uniform grid; on a graded one they grow by max_ratio per cell from the window edge cell up to the base size) are added outside the domain, so the physical domain keeps its size and the grid grows.
- Several physics may define the boundary configuration when they agree (equal face types, CPML and Bloch settings); different ones are a validation error. E_z and H_z pec / pmc walls are half a cell apart (E_z pec at the outermost cell centre, H_z pec on its inner face); symmetric / antisymmetric mirror planes (E mirror-even / odd, PMC / PEC planes) coincide.
- A uniform mesh has ceil(size / dx) cells per axis, so the meshed window (Domain.physical_extent) can be one cell larger than size_x / size_y.
- nonuniform and auto fall back to a uniform grid when no refinement is finer than the base size, or at the finest target when an enabled feature requires a uniform mesh (laminar_flow.wall, laminar_flow.slip_wall, laminar_flow.inlet_velocity, laminar_flow.pressure, laminar_flow.periodic); the note in check.json mesh says why.
- Refinements apply in nonuniform and auto modes only (uniform mode ignores them): each refines the columns and rows spanned by a geometry object plus its margin to its dx; rectangle edges inside the domain become cell edges (no staircase), so a gap between two such edges narrower than dx (but >= 0.25 dx) gets cells of its width, which can set the time step; auto mode adds one refinement per material object by its refractive index. dx_x / dx_y / dx_z refine only some axes (anisotropic); MeshSpec.axes adds a per-axis max_ratio, coordinate bands and custom edges or uniform / geometric / tanh segments (they replace that axis, PML padding as usual); outer_dx grows the cells beyond the refined core. The RefinementSpec and MeshAxisSpec fields are listed under spec.
- Time step with EM: dt = courant_factor * dx / (c * sqrt(2)) on a uniform mesh (3D models: c * sqrt(3), the 3D limit; on a graded mesh the limit of the finest cells); the merged courant factor is the smallest declared (default 0.99). check.json study shows dt_estimate and n_steps.
- Limits: 400,000,000 cells and 50,000 cells per axis, PML cells included; a larger mesh fails before any meshing.

### Mesh settings (MeshSpec fields)

- `kind` (choice; default "tensor"; choices tensor | triangles | tetrahedra) - Mesh kind
  tensor: rectilinear cells (uniform or graded rows and columns; every physics type); triangles: a conforming triangle mesh for finite elements (2D Cartesian models only); tetrahedra: a tetrahedron mesh for finite elements (3D Cartesian models only; mesher 'gmsh' conforms to boxes, spheres, z cylinders and z-prism rectangles / circles, composite inputs included, other objects are tagged per element; 'builtin' = a Kuhn split of the bricks of a rectilinear grid graded like a tensor mesh, see mesher). Physics, features and solvers declare the kinds they run on, validation refuses the others. On triangles / gmsh tetrahedra dx is the maximum element size, max_ratio the maximum element growth rate, refinements the maximum sizes in or along their objects (margin and dx_x / dx_y / dx_z unused; gmsh tetrahedra also along the edges or at the surface only: RefinementSpec.where), axes and outer_dx / outer_ratio do not apply; builtin tetrahedra take the tensor rules (refinements with margin and dx_x / dx_y / dx_z, axes, outer_dx / outer_ratio; no size_points); h_min, curvature_factor and mesher apply to triangles / tetrahedra only, pml_layers and mirror_x / mirror_y to triangles only (a tetrahedron PML shell is meshed like the window), face_sizes to tetrahedra only; size_points are [x, y, h] on triangles, [x, y, z, h] on gmsh tetrahedra.
- `mode` (choice; default "uniform"; choices uniform | nonuniform | auto) - Mesh mode
  uniform: one cell size dx; nonuniform: base size dx plus the mesh refinements, graded by max_ratio; auto with an EM physics (family em) on this mesh or wavelength_min set: cell size wavelength_min / (points_per_wavelength * n) in each material, n = |sqrt(eps * mu_r)| at wavelength_min, largest over the permittivity arrays the mesh's physics types use, eps = the array background (a component such as eps_zz over eps_r, else the Drude eps_inf) - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) + the dispersion poles at that wavelength (a metal is meshed by its skin depth: gold |n| ~11 at 1.55 um), plus the refinements; auto without either (physics-controlled, S7.8): base size = the longest domain side / 50, every domain object the mesh's physics use (material selections setting one of their properties, their feature selections) refined to its smallest bounding-box side / 4, plus the refinements; with laminar_flow on the mesh a uniform grid at the smallest such side / 16 (lattice Boltzmann). auto raises for a permittivity, sigma_e, mu_r or pole value it uses that depends on x, y, z or a field (use nonuniform there). Graded meshes are rectilinear (one width per grid column and per row): a refinement refines every column and row its object plus margin spans, across the whole domain, so a waveguide crossing the domain refines that whole axis unless the refinement sets per-axis sizes (dx_x / dx_y / dx_z; a value >= the base size leaves that axis unrefined); the grading ramps lie outside the refined bands. MeshSpec.axes adds per-axis options: max_ratio, coordinate bands, and custom edges or segments (uniform / geometric / tanh) that replace the graded cells of that axis. In 3D models z is graded the same way: a refinement refines the z layers of its object's z extent plus margin (points / lines at their z, unset z = the whole height; an open prism end reaches the domain edge), set z0 / z1 faces of prisms are exact cell edges, and z cells away from refinements take the base size. nonuniform and auto fall back to a uniform grid when no refinement is finer than the base size, or (at the finest size) when a feature needs a uniform mesh (FDFD plane wave, laminar flow faces).
- `dx` (float; unit m; default 2e-08; range (0, inf)) - Cell size
  Cell size of a uniform mesh, or the base (coarsest) size of a nonuniform one; typically lambda / (20 n) for EM, n the largest refractive index. The grid is limited to 400e6 cells and 50,000 cells per axis, counting the PML cells that are added outside the domain; a uniform mesh rounds size_x / size_y up to whole cells, so the meshed window can be one cell larger. Validation previews materials on float64 centres while the build tests float32 clamped cell centres, so a material edge exactly on a cell centre can differ: avoid placing edges exactly on cell centres.
- `max_ratio` (float; unit 1; range (1, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto) or kind in (triangles, tetrahedra)) - Maximum growth ratio
  Largest size ratio of neighbouring cells on a graded mesh, or the maximum element growth rate of a triangle mesh (> 1); typically 1.1-1.3. Smaller ratios grade more smoothly (less numerical reflection) but need more cells. null = the kind default: 1.15 (tensor), 1.3 (triangles, the industry-standard default).
- `wavelength_min` (float; unit m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto)) - Shortest wavelength
  Shortest vacuum wavelength to resolve in auto mode. The auto cell size in a material of index n is wavelength_min / (points_per_wavelength * n). Empty (null): the shortest wavelength over the physics: FDFD and em_modes the shortest solved one (a frequency_domain study: its shortest wavelength, else the wavelength setting), FDTD the shortest significant source wavelength (gaussian lambda / (1 + bandwidth), ricker lambda / 2) of the physics on this mesh; a model error when an EM physics is on the mesh but none gives one (without EM physics auto mode takes the physics-controlled rule). A parameter sweep that changes that wavelength re-meshes per value. Set it to keep one mesh, to mesh finer, or for a wavelength the physics do not know (e.g. one generated inside the model).
- `points_per_wavelength` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto)) - Points per wavelength
  Cells (triangles: elements) per wavelength inside each material in auto mode; typically 15-30 on tensor meshes. Too few cells give numerical dispersion (phase errors that grow with the propagation distance). null = the kind default: 20 (tensor), 5 (triangles: the industry-standard five quadratic elements per wavelength).
- `outer_dx` (float; unit m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto)) - Outer cell size
  Outer grading (graded meshes; null = off): outside the refined core of each axis (the span of every refinement and band on that axis, margins included) cells grow geometrically from the base size by outer_ratio per cell up to outer_dx, so a domain ~1e3 x the structure costs a few dozen cells per side (quasi-static far fields: steady heat, electrostatics, low-frequency thermal noise). An axis without refinements is not outer graded; outer_dx <= the base size does nothing. Independent of the PML ramp (PML cells still grade toward the base size). Jacobi-PCG iterations grow with the grading: sparse direct solvers suit it better.
- `outer_ratio` (float; unit 1; range (1, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when mode in (nonuniform, auto)) - Outer growth ratio
  Cell growth per cell of the outer grading (> 1; null = the axis' max_ratio); 1.2-1.5 is typical for quasi-static fields.
- `h_min` (float; unit m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when kind in (triangles, tetrahedra)) - Minimum element size
  Triangles / tetrahedra: smallest element size (> 0, <= the maximum size); null = the maximum size (dx, or the auto size) / 100.
- `curvature_factor` (float; unit 1; default 0.3; range (0, inf); visible when kind in (triangles, tetrahedra)) - Curvature factor
  Triangles / tetrahedra: element size along circle / ellipse / sphere / cylinder boundaries <= curvature_factor x the local radius of curvature (0.3 = the industry-standard default).
- `mesher` (choice; default "builtin"; choices builtin | gmsh; visible when kind in (triangles, tetrahedra)) - Mesher
  Triangles: 'builtin' = open_sol's conforming Delaunay refinement (numpy / scipy, deterministic); tetrahedra: 'builtin' = the bricks of a rectilinear grid split into 6 tetrahedra each (Kuhn orthoschemes: every dihedral angle <= 90 deg, no slivers at any brick aspect ratio; periodic sides match). Uniform mode, or nothing finer than dx: equal cells <= dx per axis. Else the grid is graded like a nonuniform tensor mesh at base dx: refinements (and auto ones) with margin and dx_x / dx_y / dx_z, axes (bands, edges, segments, max_ratio), outer_dx / outer_ratio, face_sizes as bands [c - distance, c + distance] across their face plane, and every flat face of a domain object (box, rectangle prism sides, set prism ends) snapped as an element face. The PML shell takes cells of dx. Curved objects are tagged per element (a staircase); size_points are refused (mesher gmsh), h_min and a physics' edge sizes are unused (a warning). Example, a slender clamped string: refinement {string, dx 0.5 um, dx_y = dx_z = 50 nm} plus face_sizes x_lo / x_hi 50 nm. 'gmsh' = the gmsh program run as an external process (OPEN_SOL_GMSH or the PATH; never linked), a validation error when it is not found.
- `sweep_axis` (choice; default "none"; choices none | z; visible when kind in (tetrahedra)) - Swept layers
  Tetrahedra only (experiment plan D5). 'none' = the 3D mesher of mesher. 'z' = swept prism layers: the xy footprint meshed by the triangle mesher of mesher (builtin / gmsh 2D; dx = maximum element size, refinement dx in / along their objects' footprints over the whole height, h_min, curvature_factor, max_ratio growth; a physics' edge sizes refine along the objects' outlines), extruded through the z layers of the tensor planner (as builtin tetrahedra along z: refinements (dx_z, else dx) with margins, a z MeshAxisSpec, face_sizes on z_lo / z_hi faces as bands, outer_dx; every set z face of a domain object snapped as a layer plane; the PML shell in cells of dx) and each prism split into 3 tetrahedra by the minimum-vertex rule (conforming; periodic sides matched; about 3 x triangles x layers elements). Conforming: boxes, z cylinders, untapered z prisms and untapered x / y rectangles; spheres, other x / y prisms and tapers are tagged per element (a warning). The x / y PML ring has pml_layers structured layers. Refused: size_points, x / y axes options, dx_x / dx_y unlike dx, face sizes on x / y faces, where edges / surface.
- `pml_layers` (int; unit 1; default 8; range [1, inf); visible when kind in (triangles) or sweep_axis in (z)) - Absorbing layers
  Triangles (and swept tetrahedra, sweep_axis z: the x / y sides): structured element layers across each PML ring side (thickness = the PML cells of the physics x the maximum element size, the tensor CPML stretch profile).
- `mirror_x` (bool; default false; visible when kind in (triangles)) - Mirror-symmetric in x
  Triangles: mesh the half window x <= size_x / 2 (it conforms to the geometry and its mirror image), then mirror it about x = size_x / 2 (nodes on the line shared, the PML ring mirrored too), so the mesh and every operator on it are exactly mirror symmetric: an even drive gives no odd response beyond rounding (parity selection rules). The size field is the smaller of the sizes at a point and at its image. Needs equal absorbing rings on x_lo and x_hi (else the mesh estimate fails); a warning names material objects that are not mirror symmetric (the mesh still conforms to them; sources and probes are not checked). Default false.
- `mirror_y` (bool; default false; visible when kind in (triangles)) - Mirror-symmetric in y
  Triangles: as mirror_x about y = size_y / 2 (equal absorbing rings on y_lo and y_hi); with mirror_x the quarter window is meshed and mirrored twice. Default false.

## Solvers

A physics hands its numerical jobs (roles) to solvers: ModelSpec.solvers holds solver nodes (SolverSpec: name, type, settings), PhysicsSpec.solvers {role: node name} assigns them; a role left out is Automatic (the role's default type at its default settings; SolverDefaultsSpec.precision, when not auto, replaces the precision of every solver that offers it and sets none). check.json solvers shows what every role resolves to, summary.json solvers what ran (type, node, backend, precision, settings, counters): Automatic depends on the machine (backend auto, sparse_direct back_end auto), so the record is the reference for comparing runs.

- Roles: stepper (Time stepping); linear (Linear systems); shifted (Frequency sweeps); eigen (Eigenvalues). A role is used only in the studies listed for it (all studies when none are listed); an assignment in another study is a warning and ignored.
- Validation: an unknown node or role is an error at the physics; a node of the wrong role, operator class, backend, grid kind or precision (solver_misfit) is an error naming the fitting choices; a node no physics uses is a warning at the node; the node settings are checked like physics settings.
- Feature precisions: a feature whose entry lists "Stepper precisions ... only" (e.g. resonance_monitor, the em_fdtd_3d plane wave and mode ports) works only when the stepper role of its physics resolves to one of them; an enabled one is a validation error at the feature otherwise (e.g. with half_storage).
- Solver knobs are never physics settings: e.g. the CG precision / tolerance / max_iterations of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics, solid_mechanics and solid_mechanics_3d are the settings of a pcg node assigned as their linear solver ({"name": "cg", "type": "pcg", "settings": {"tolerance": 1e-12}} in solvers, {"linear": "cg"} in the physics solvers).
- One node may serve several physics; the build creates one runtime per (physics, role).
- Opt-in roles: line_block fills the linear role of em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz only (its shifted role: heat thermal noise, em_fdfd_bor, em_modes); a line_block node assigned as the linear solver of any other physics is a misfit.
- sparse_direct back_end auto: a role's auto_back_end_by_grid {grid kind: back end} (pressure_acoustics on triangles / tetrahedra, membrane on triangles: cudss_mixed) replaces it on the gpu backend when nvmath-python is installed, for Automatic and for nodes that leave back_end auto; else auto is host SuperLU (scipy_splu).
- sparse_direct back_end / arpack_shift_invert factorization mumps, mumps_mixed, pardiso, pardiso_mixed: the optional multicore host direct solvers MUMPS (python-mumps) and Intel MKL PARDISO (pydiso, x86-64 only) on both backends, opt-in like cudss (only roles whose line under Roles by physics type lists them; elsewhere a misfit) and never chosen by auto; without the package a node is a validation error. The host SuperLU size rules apply, each factor checks the library's own memory estimate after its analysis against 80 % of the available RAM, and a refusal raises (no fallback).

### Solver types

#### Solver type `arpack_shift_invert` - Shift-invert eigensolver

Eigenpairs nearest a target: host SuperLU (or, factorization cudss, GPU cuDSS; auto: cuDSS for the vibration modes of finite element solids on the GPU; mumps / pardiso: the optional multicore host MUMPS / Intel MKL PARDISO) factorisation of the operator shifted to the target and ARPACK (scipy eigs, largest |theta| of the shifted inverse) in double precision. Used by em_modes (cross-section modes near the effective-index guess) and by em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz in an eigenfrequency study (resonances nearest the wavelength setting). solid_mechanics (eigenfrequency, optomechanics: plane-strain or 2.5D guided vibration modes) uses symmetric shift-invert Lanczos (scipy eigsh) on a real SuperLU factor of K - sigma M. solid_mechanics_3d (eigenfrequency) uses it without a factor: symmetric Lanczos (scipy eigsh) on K^-1 M at 0, each K^-1 one PCG solve of its 'linear' solver on the device. The ARPACK basis stays on the host and SuperLU runs the same on both backends (cudss: GPU backend only); on triangle and tetrahedron meshes (FEM) the same factorisation of the assembled element matrices.

- SolverSpec.type `arpack_shift_invert`; roles eigen; operators spd, complex_symmetric, general; backends gpu, cpu; precisions double; grids tensor, triangles, tetrahedra

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Eigenvalue tolerance
  Relative accuracy ARPACK asks of each eigenvalue (scipy eigs tol); 0 = machine precision (default). solid_mechanics_3d (inexact PCG inner solves) raises it to at least 1e3 x its linear CG tolerance.
- `subspace_size` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Subspace size
  Arnoldi vectors ARPACK keeps (scipy eigs ncv), raised to the eigenpairs wanted + 2; 0 = scipy's default max(2 k + 1, 20) for k wanted eigenpairs. A larger basis converges in fewer operator applications but holds that many complex128 vectors of the system size on the host.
- `factorization` (choice; default "auto"; choices auto | superlu | cudss | cudss_mixed | mumps | mumps_mixed | pardiso | pardiso_mixed) - Shift-invert factorisation
  LU of the shifted operator. auto: superlu, except on the gpu backend with nvmath-python installed for the vibration modes of solid_mechanics on triangle meshes (cudss) and of solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra (cudss_mixed; brick meshes have no factor), where a cuDSS refusal (a zero pivot, missed accuracy or too little GPU memory) switches that solver to superlu for the rest of the run with a warning (up to 2e6 unknowns; the run summary records the resolved value and eigen_auto_fallbacks). superlu: scipy SuperLU on the host (host memory, both backends). cudss (GPU backend, needs nvmath-python with cuDSS): NVIDIA's sparse direct solver factorises on the device in double precision with its own nested-dissection ordering (LDL^T where the operator is complex symmetric after a diagonal scaling: em_fdfd_3d, 2D em_fdfd without Bloch phase, solid_mechanics); the factor lives in GPU memory outside the cupy pool (refused when cuDSS's own estimate exceeds 80 % of the free device memory, and the host SuperLU size rule of the FDFD eigen solves no longer applies); ARPACK still runs on the host, so each operator application moves one vector to the device and back. A probe solve checks the factor and turns on cuDSS iterative refinement when its residual misses 1e-10. cudss_mixed (em_fdfd_3d, em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical, em_modes on triangle meshes, solid_mechanics and solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra): the diagonally equilibrated operator factorised in single precision (complex64 / float32: about 10x faster to factorise on GPUs with slow double arithmetic, half the GPU memory, solves ~2x cheaper). The resonance solves of the frequency-domain optics types and em_modes correct every ARPACK solve by one float64 residual step (~3e-8), stop ARPACK at ~1e-6 and re-evaluate each eigenvalue by the float64 Rayleigh quotient of its vector, accurate to ~1e-14 because the scaled operator is complex symmetric (with a Bloch phase it is not: full float64 refinement per solve instead); the solid_mechanics pencils refine every solve to 1e-12. mumps / pardiso (every eigen role, both backends, never chosen by auto; needs python-mumps / pydiso): the shifted operator factorised on the host by MUMPS or Intel MKL PARDISO (x86-64 only), multicore, with the cudss equilibration and LDL^T where the operator is (complex) symmetric after the diagonal scaling, else LU; inertia counts of target / band searches come from the library's LDL^T pivots (a counting SuperLU when pivots were perturbed or the pencil is Hermitian); the host SuperLU size rules apply, plus the library's own memory estimate after its analysis against 80 % of the available RAM; a refusal raises (no fallback). mumps_mixed / pardiso_mixed (only where cudss_mixed is offered): a single-precision host factor, the solves refined and polished as for cudss_mixed; a first factor whose probe misses is refactorised in double for the rest of the run. Ignored by solid_mechanics_3d on brick meshes (no factor).

#### Solver type `banded` - Banded direct solver (1D)

Direct solve of 1D models (domain size_y null: a line of cells, symmetry plan 2.20): the operator of a window one cell across is banded (tridiagonal for heat, electric_currents, electrostatics), so one host banded Cholesky (scipy.linalg cholesky_banded, double precision) per assembly gives exact solves at a cost linear in the cells; on the GPU backend the operator, rhs and solution move to the host per factorisation / solve. The Automatic linear solver of these types in a 1D model on both backends; refused in 2D / 3D models (a node there is an error).

- SolverSpec.type `banded`; roles linear; operators spd; backends gpu, cpu; precisions double; grids line

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
none

#### Solver type `explicit_kernels` - Explicit time stepping

The fused GPU kernels of an explicit time-stepping engine (em_fdtd_ez / em_fdtd_hz / em_fdtd_3d, elastic_waves, laminar_flow): single precision (float32 fields and arithmetic), double (float64 fields and arithmetic; em_fdtd_ez / em_fdtd_hz, kernels compiled per precision) or half_storage (fp16 fields in memory, float32 arithmetic; em_fdtd_3d, elastic_waves and transient laminar_flow). On the CPU backend (every stepper type) the same steps run as numpy twins of the kernels, or numba-compiled twins of the per-step field updates (Yee updates, em_fdtd_3d CPML / ohmic loss, the elastic_waves velocity / stress updates, the lattice step) when numba is installed (environment variable OPEN_SOL_CPU_KERNELS=numpy keeps numpy); single or double there, several times slower than a GPU: small 2D models and tests.

- SolverSpec.type `explicit_kernels`; roles stepper; operators spd, complex_symmetric, general; backends gpu, cpu; precisions single, double, half_storage; grids tensor

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `precision` (choice; default "single"; choices single | double | half_storage) - Solver precision
  single: float32 fields and arithmetic (every engine). double (em_fdtd_ez / em_fdtd_hz, both backends): float64 fields, coefficients, CPML, pole and source arrays and arithmetic, about 2x the field memory and time; for long or high-Q ring-downs, where float32 rounding of the coefficients (~1e-7 of the mode frequency) accumulates into a visible phase drift; materials, coupling slots, absorbed power, probe traces and the box DFT spectra stay float32 / complex64; refused with nonlinear_medium and gain_medium. half_storage (em_fdtd_3d, elastic_waves, laminar_flow transient only): the fields / lattice populations are stored as fp16 and computed in float32 registers, about half the field memory and up to ~1.5-2x faster on bandwidth-bound grids; fp16 has an 11-bit mantissa, so results carry a ~1e-3 relative noise floor (-60 dB): flux spectra with deep nulls, harmonic inversion / Q values and steady states are refused or unusable (features that need single say so in validation), decaying tails below ~1e-7 of the peak flush to zero.

#### Solver type `line_block` - Line-block direct solver

Batched block-tridiagonal direct solver for families K + sum s_i M_i + sum t_j N_j of structured 2D systems (M_i diagonal, N_j sparse with the same line coupling as K): unknowns ordered line by line, per shift a block Thomas factorisation (cost lines x b^3, b = unknowns across a line), many shifts per batch, equilibrated and refined against the double-precision operator; on the GPU (cupy) or the CPU backend (numpy, the same array code, chunks sized by the available RAM). Users (role shifted): heat thermal noise spectra (K + j omega C + q^2 A per frequency and axial wavenumber) and em_fdfd_bor (every driven system and shift-invert operator, the orders of an azimuthal_orders list as shifts m, m^2 of K0 + m K1 + m^2 K2; a kept factor serves the Arnoldi iterations; frequency_domain wavelengths of one order in batches of whole operators) and em_modes (the shift-invert operators of the mode solves: omega and, with group_index, omega (1 +- 1e-3), and in a frequency_domain study the next wavelengths, in batches of whole operators). Role linear (em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz only; Automatic stays sparse_direct): one block factor of the Helmholtz operator per wavelength and material state, reused for every source and as the shift-invert factor of the eigenfrequency study; frequency_domain wavelengths in batches of whole operators; the periodic axis (if any) lies inside the blocks, two periodic axes are refused; adjoint (transposed) solves of the optimization study and rejected solves use a host SuperLU of the same operator instead. A batch holds at most 8 operators and what 60 % of the free memory holds. A rejected solve is re-solved by the physics' host SuperLU. On the CPU backend it is slower than the Automatic host SuperLU (each solve 7-15 x slower on 1e4-4e4 unknown complex 2D operators, double and mixed alike, at about the same factorisation time): there it only serves comparisons with the GPU runs.

- SolverSpec.type `line_block`; roles shifted, linear; operators spd, complex_symmetric, general; backends gpu, cpu; precisions mixed, double; grids tensor

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `precision` (choice; default "mixed"; choices mixed | double) - Solver precision
  mixed: block factorisation and sweeps in complex64, refined against the complex128 operator to a relative residual of 1e-09; a shift still above 1e-06 is re-solved by the physics' reference solver (counted as rejected_shifts, or rejected_factor_solves for kept factors: em_fdfd_* linear, em_fdfd_bor, em_modes). double: complex128 throughout (slower on consumer GPUs, rarely rejected; indefinite Helmholtz systems near a resonance may need it).

#### Solver type `pcg` - Iterative linear solver

Preconditioned conjugate gradients for symmetric positive definite systems (the linear role of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics, solid_mechanics, solid_mechanics_3d): Jacobi or the physics' block-Jacobi preconditioner, or algebraic multigrid (the scalar diffusion types), warm-started from the previous solve; on the GPU (fused cupy kernels) or the CPU backend (numpy / scipy, the same iteration); double, single or mixed (float32 CG passes refined against the float64 residual) precision. Automatic is pcg with the defaults below, except the preconditioner: multigrid for the scalar diffusion types (jacobi at mixed precision; on triangle and tetrahedron meshes Automatic is sparse_direct, pcg is opt-in there; solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra solves with sparse_direct only); to change precision, tolerance, max_iterations or the preconditioner add a pcg solver node and assign it (physics solvers {"linear": "<node name>"}).

- SolverSpec.type `pcg`; roles linear; operators spd; backends gpu, cpu; precisions double, single, mixed; grids tensor, triangles, tetrahedra

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `precision` (choice; default "double"; choices double | single | mixed) - Solver precision
  Arithmetic of the CG vectors and operator (the physics stores its fields as float32 either way). single saves solver memory but CG stalls near a relative residual of 1e-06: use tolerance >= 1e-06 with it (validation warns). mixed (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics: Jacobi on the assembled operator): the system is assembled in float64, each CG pass runs in float32 (vectors and a float32 copy of the operator values, ~1.5-2x faster per iteration) and reduces the float64 residual by up to 0.0001, then the residual is refreshed in float64 and corrected again, so any tolerance double reaches is reached (each pass restarts CG: up to ~1.5x the iterations of double; +~30 B per cell for the float32 copies). solid_mechanics_3d: float32 copies of the element Lame pair and the block-Jacobi inverses drive a float32 matrix-free product, which on GPUs with slow float64 arithmetic (most consumer cards) is several times cheaper than the float64 one (the stiffness product is compute bound). Not for 2D solid_mechanics (block preconditioner on the assembled operator).
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-08; range (0, inf)) - Solver tolerance
  CG stopping criterion, a relative residual norm: in a steady solve relative to ||b|| (the sources and boundary drive); in an implicit time step relative to the initial residual of the step (its change from the previous step, never below ~16 machine epsilons of ||b||). 1e-8 suits double; single cannot get below ~1e-06. Outputs that follow the solution linearly (terminal currents and charges, q_joule, reactions, stresses, B and H) carry a relative error of the order of the condition number times the tolerance: use 1e-12 for exact-identity checks; an iron part (mu_dc >> 1) raises the magnetostatics condition number by about its permeability, so use 1e-10 or below for flux-concentration ratios.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Solver iteration limit
  CG iteration limit per solve; 0 = auto: max(5000, 20 x the cells along the longest window axis), twice the ~10 x those cells Jacobi-PCG needs from a cold start (fewer when warm-started from the previous solve); solid_mechanics doubles the auto value (block-Jacobi PCG on the elastic operator needs about twice the iterations, more for poisson_ratio near 0.5). A solve that hits the limit keeps its unconverged (biased) result, and the first one per run is logged as a warning; validation warns when an explicit value is below 10 x the longest window axis (not with a heat out_of_plane_convection on every cell, which converges much faster).
- `preconditioner` (choice; default "jacobi"; choices jacobi | multigrid) - Preconditioner
  CG preconditioner. jacobi: the inverse diagonal (solid_mechanics: its 2x2 / 3x3 block diagonal), cheap per iteration, but the iterations grow with the cells along the longest window axis (~10 per cell) and with mesh grading, cell aspect ratio and coefficient contrast (outer grading to large cells, 1e3x conductivity ratios: up to ~1e5 iterations). multigrid (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics; precision single or double): a smoothed-aggregation algebraic multigrid V(1,1)-cycle (l1-Jacobi smoothing) built from the assembled operator, coarsening along strong couplings (threshold 0.1), so graded and stretched cells semi-coarsen; typically 10-40 iterations whatever the mesh size, each costing ~4-6 Jacobi iterations; the hierarchy takes ~150 B per cell (double) on the device, every assembly rebuilds its coarse operators and a change of the sparsity (held cells, empty rows) re-runs the aggregation, one host pass over the operator. Best for steady solves on large or strongly graded meshes; for implicit time steps the warm-started Jacobi is often cheaper. Automatic (no node) of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics and magnetostatics on the gpu backend is pcg with multigrid (jacobi when solver_defaults.precision is mixed); a pcg node without this setting uses jacobi.

#### Solver type `sparse_direct` - Sparse direct solver

Sparse direct factorisation, double precision (complex128): host SuperLU (scipy) or GPU sparse QR (back_end). Role linear: the Helmholtz systems of em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz / em_fdfd_nonlinear (one factorisation per wavelength and material state, reused for every source; after a small operator change GMRES on the earlier factor first), every Newton step of drift_diffusion and the eddy-current system of magnetic_fields_ac (host only); also the linear role of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics and magnetostatics (their Automatic on the CPU backend: one real float64 host SuperLU per assembly, exact solves; scipy_splu only), and the Automatic linear solver of the diffusion and elastic types on triangle meshes and of heat on tetrahedra (FEM, both backends). Role shifted: one host SuperLU per shift K + s M, the reference of the thermal noise spectra. Iterative solvers are not offered for these (they stall on the indefinite Helmholtz matrix). On the CPU backend: SuperLU on scipy operators, numpy solutions. back_end cudss / cudss_mixed (GPU cuDSS, kept device factor, plan reused across re-assemblies) only where the physics offers it (the diffusion and elastic linear roles, em_fdfd_ez / _hz, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical, drift_diffusion). back_end mumps / mumps_mixed / pardiso / pardiso_mixed (the optional host MUMPS / Intel MKL PARDISO, multicore, both backends, never chosen by auto) likewise only where the physics offers them.

- SolverSpec.type `sparse_direct`; roles linear, shifted; operators spd, complex_symmetric, general; backends gpu, cpu; precisions double; grids tensor, triangles, tetrahedra

Params (SolverSpec.settings):
- `back_end` (choice; default "auto"; choices auto | scipy_splu | cusolver_qr | cudss | cudss_mixed | mumps | mumps_mixed | pardiso | pardiso_mixed) - Back end
  Where the sparse factorisation runs (role linear). scipy_splu: SuperLU on the host (needs scipy; the matrix moves to the host, where its L + U factors stay), one factorisation reused for every right-hand side, practical up to ~1e6 unknowns (warning above, refused above 2e6). cusolver_qr: sparse QR on the GPU (cupy only), one factorisation per solve, for small models (~1e5 unknowns on a square grid): its workspace, estimated as 64 B * nx * ny * the cell count of the narrower axis (doubled by a periodic wrap of the other axis), lies outside the GPU memory budget, so validation warns above 512 MiB and refuses above 2 GiB, and the solver also refuses a workspace over half the free GPU memory (overrunning the GPU freezes the display). auto: scipy_splu when scipy is installed, else cusolver_qr; on the cpu backend always scipy_splu (cusolver_qr is an error there); on the gpu backend with nvmath-python installed, the frequency-response linear solves of pressure_acoustics (triangle and tetrahedron meshes) and membrane (triangle meshes) take cudss_mixed instead, solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra cudss_mixed, and cudss: em_fdfd_ez / _hz (tensor and triangle meshes), em_fdfd_bor / em_fdfd_conical and drift_diffusion (tensor meshes; drift_diffusion also triangles), solid_mechanics on triangles and the heat / electric_currents / electrostatics / magnetostatics types on triangle and tetrahedron meshes (the run summary records the resolved back end); when cuDSS refuses such an operator (a zero pivot, missed accuracy or too little GPU memory) that solver switches to scipy_splu for the rest of the run with a warning (up to 2e6 unknowns). The shifted role (thermal noise) and magnetic_fields_ac always factorise on the host. cudss (GPU backend, needs nvmath-python with cuDSS; only where the physics offers it: heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics, solid_mechanics and solid_mechanics_3d, em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical and drift_diffusion (real LU of every Newton Jacobian) linear solves): NVIDIA's sparse direct solver factorises on the GPU in double precision (real symmetric positive definite systems by Cholesky, LDL^T if that fails; its own nested-dissection ordering) and keeps the factor in GPU memory outside the cupy pool (refused when cuDSS's own estimate after planning exceeds 80 % of the free device memory; the host SuperLU size rules do not apply); a re-assembly with the same sparsity pattern (new material values, Newton / saturation iterations) refactorises without the host planning step; solves stay on the GPU. A probe solve checks each factor (cuDSS refinement when its residual misses 1e-10). cudss_mixed: the diagonally equilibrated operator factorised in single precision (float32 / complex64: on GPUs with slow double arithmetic ~10x faster to factorise, half the factor memory), every solve refined by float64 residual steps to 1e-12 (~3-4 single solves per solve); refused at the first factor when single precision cannot reach that (very high contrast: use cudss). mumps / mumps_mixed / pardiso / pardiso_mixed (both backends, never chosen by auto; only where the physics offers them: the linear solves of heat, electric_currents, electrostatics, magnetostatics(_3d), solid_mechanics(_3d), pressure_acoustics, membrane, em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical, drift_diffusion and em_fdfd_nonlinear, the shifted role of heat thermal noise, and mumps / pardiso for magnetic_fields_ac): a multicore sparse direct factor on the host by MUMPS (python-mumps) or Intel MKL PARDISO (pydiso, x86-64 only), after the diagonal equilibration of cuDSS: LDL^T for (complex) symmetric operators (the symmetrised D A of the FDFD types; the real symmetric positive definite systems: PARDISO Cholesky, LDL^T if that fails, MUMPS LDL^T), LU otherwise; transposed (adjoint) solves, GMRES on an earlier factor and inertia counts work as with scipy_splu. The scipy_splu size rules apply (uncalibrated for these libraries), plus a check of the library's own memory estimate after its analysis against 80 % of the available RAM; a probe solve checks each factor (float64 GMRES refinement on the factor when its residual misses 1e-10); a refusal raises (no fallback). mumps_mixed / pardiso_mixed: the equilibrated operator factorised in single precision (float32 / complex64, about half the factor memory), every solve refined by float64 GMRES to 1e-12 as cudss_mixed; a first factor whose probe misses is refactorised in double for the rest of the run. Threads: the library defaults (OMP_NUM_THREADS for MUMPS, MKL_NUM_THREADS for PARDISO; with numba or a threaded BLAS in the same process set them to share the cores). Optional packages, a validation error without them: MUMPS: conda install -c conda-forge python-mumps (pip install python-mumps builds against an installed MUMPS); PARDISO: pip install pydiso (Linux / Windows x86-64 wheels, pulls MKL) or conda install -c conda-forge pydiso; x86-64 only.

## Shared help texts

Long texts (param help, feature and type descriptions) that occur more than once in the physics, coupling and study sections below; each occurrence reads "Help: shared `<key>`", key = its first owner: <physics>.<param>, <physics>.<feature>, <physics>.<feature>.<param>, <coupling or study type>.<param> or a type name.

#### `elastic_waves.rho`

Mass density, shared by every physics that reads it (heat: heat capacity rho*cp; laminar_flow, elastic_waves and pressure_acoustics: inertia). Unset = 0: elastic_waves treats a cell without density and stiffness as vacuum (a traction-free surface around it; a face between two such cells does not move). Typical: water 998, silica 2200, silicon 2329, aluminium 2700, gold 19300.
