#### `elastic_waves.sound_speed`

Longitudinal (compressional, P) wave speed: c11 = c22 = rho sound_speed^2 unless the c_ij entries are set. A fluid sets only this one. Set (> 0), the speeds replace any youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio of the cell (library solids carry those; their speeds follow from rho). Typical: air 343, water 1480, silica 5960, aluminium 6420, silicon ~8430 (isotropic average). pressure_acoustics: the speed of sound c of the fluid.

#### `elastic_waves.youngs_modulus`

Young's modulus E of an isotropic linear-elastic solid. solid_mechanics: unset = 0 = void, cells without stiffness carry no stress and their displacement is not solved (air, a liquid, a cladding left out of the mechanics); every solid region needs a support. elastic_waves: the moduli c11 = c22 = lambda + 2 mu, c12 = lambda, c66 = mu of cells without a sound_speed (a set sound_speed / shear_speed wins, set c_ij entries win over both). Typical: silica 7.3e10, silicon 1.65e11 (isotropic average; 1.3e11 along <100>, 1.69e11 along <110>), gold 7.9e10, aluminium 7.0e10. May depend on x, y and state fields such as heat_T (a stationary study then iterates).

#### `elastic_waves.poisson_ratio`

Poisson ratio nu of an isotropic solid, -1 < nu < 0.5 (unset = 0), used with youngs_modulus. Plane strain (eps_zz = 0) makes the in-plane response stiffer by 1 / (1 - nu^2) and sigma_zz = nu (sigma_xx + sigma_yy) - E alpha_zz dT. solid_mechanics: bilinear elements lock (grow too stiff) as nu approaches 0.5, results above ~0.45 overestimate the stiffness (validation warns). Typical: silica 0.17, silicon 0.22, gold 0.42, aluminium 0.35.

#### `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p11`

Strain-optic (photoelastic) coefficient p11 of an isotropic or cubic material (crystal axes along x, y, z): Delta(1/n^2)_ii = p11 e_ii + p12 (e_jj + e_kk) of the elastic strain, read only by solid_em_strain_optic, acoustics_em_acousto_optic and the solid_mechanics optomechanical_coupling (with photoelastic_p44 for shear there; acoustics_em_acousto_optic into em_fdfd_hz uses (p11 - p12) / 2 for the eps_xy shear term). Unset = 0. Typical: silica 0.121, silicon -0.094. With the elastic_waves tensor entries (photoelastic_p16 .. _p66, e.g. from a crystal entry, which also sets p11 / p12 as the model-axis row xx) it is p_11 of that row: Delta(1/n^2)_xx = p11 S_xx + p12 S_yy + p16 2 S_xy; solid_em_strain_optic keeps the isotropic reading, the optomechanical_coupling overlap reads the crystal entry's full rotated p tensor instead (unless the material sets a photoelastic_* itself).

#### `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p12`

Strain-optic coefficient p12 (strain across the field direction; see photoelastic_p11). Unset = 0. Typical: silica 0.270, silicon 0.017. With the elastic_waves tensor entries it is p_12 of the model-axis row xx (Delta(1/n^2)_xx per S_yy) and the fallback of the unset p21 / p31 / p32.

#### `elastic_waves.force_source.waveform`

ricker: Ricker wavelet with its spectrum peaking at frequency, value 1 at t0 = 4 / frequency (broadband, up to ~2.5 f: 3 % of the spectral peak there, 1 % at 2.76 f); gaussian: sin carrier at frequency under a gaussian envelope of relative bandwidth (t0 = 4.5 / (pi bandwidth frequency)); cw: sin(2 pi f t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f, steady after ~15 periods.

#### `elastic_waves.force_source.frequency`

Centre (gaussian, cw) or peak (ricker) frequency; the mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per shortest wavelength, the slowest speed (shear in solids) over the highest significant frequency (gaussian f (1 + bandwidth), ricker 2.5 f; validation warns).

#### `electric_currents.azimuthal_order`

Azimuthal order m >= 0 of an axisymmetric (r, z) solve (symmetry 2.14). 0: rotationally symmetric. m >= 1: the order-m part u_m(r, z) cos(m phi) of a load on the body of revolution (m = 1: a uniform transverse field, V = -E0 r cos(phi)); the operator gains c_xx m^2 / r^2 per cell volume (r_c the cell-centre radius; the radial coefficient _xx is also taken along phi), which makes u_m vanish on the axis and anchors every cell with c_xx > 0 (no other anchor needed). Every field, source density, boundary, held and initial value is then the amplitude of cos(m phi) (heat: T - T0 is the amplitude, T0 drops out), field components are the in-plane r / z amplitudes (the phi part is not output), and ring totals carry pi instead of 2 pi (the phi integral of cos^2): held currents / charges, scalar outputs and field 'integral' derived values are cos(m phi) moments (e.g. the integral of rho cos(m phi) dV), a point source P is the order-m part of a point source P at phi = 0 (its Fourier sum over m: the m = 0 ring of total P plus every order with the same P), and a dissipation density (q_joule) is twice its phi mean, so its integral is the total power. Needs geometry 'axisymmetric' on a Cartesian domain; every physics of the model with this setting shares one m (derived values weight rings by one angle); couplings of an order-m physics warn (products such as Joule heating are no single order). solid_mechanics: the mode amplitudes U_r, U_z ~ cos(m phi), U_phi ~ sin(m phi) (see its description).

#### `electric_currents.discretization`

Lagrange order of the unknown on a triangle or tetrahedron mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles / tetrahedra; ignored on tensor meshes): quadratic (P2, the industry-standard default) or linear (P1). On triangles elements with an edge on a circle / ellipse are mapped isoparametrically with quadratic elements (geometry shape order = the element order), straight with linear ones; tetrahedra are always straight (affine).

#### `electric_currents.potential_probe`

Potential (V) of the cell containing the point (time-dependent study: one sample per re-solve plus one at the end of the run, V holding its value in between; electrostatics with a voltage waveform: one per step at its end time; stationary study and the background stage of a frequency-domain study: one per fixed-point iteration, all at t = 0).

#### `electrostatics.voltage.waveform`

Time dependence of the held voltage, V(t) = voltage s(t) (the elastic_waves source waveforms): none = constant; ricker = Ricker wavelet peaking at frequency, value 1 at t0 = 4 / frequency; gaussian = sin carrier at frequency under a gaussian envelope of relative bandwidth (t0 = 4.5 / (pi bandwidth frequency)); cw = sin(2 pi f t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f, steady after ~15 periods. Solved by superposition: one static solve per distinct waveform (its features at their voltage, every other voltage, source and charge 0) plus one of the constant part, after every operator change; each step then writes V, E, D = V_dc + sum s_w(t + dt) V_w at the end time of the step (exact: the solve is linear), and charge_<feature> / the table follow the same sum. Time-dependent study only (stationary: s(0) ~ 0, validation warns); not with an electrolyte (validation error). In 2D an interdigital transducer is two terminals with the same waveform and opposite voltages.

#### `em_eme.pml_cells`

CPML cells added outside every cpml face, so the physical domain keeps its size and the grid grows. Each PML cell is dx wide on a uniform grid; on a graded one they grow by max_ratio per cell from the window edge cell up to the base size (a layer next to a refined edge is thinner). 10-20 typical; thicker layers absorb grazing and long-wavelength waves better.

#### `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`

Peak CPML conductivity as a multiple of the vacuum optimum (m + 1) / (150 pi d) S/m, with m = pml_order and d the PML cell width; 1 is a good default, 0.5-2 when tuning reflections. A wave of index n attenuates n times faster, so where a cladding of index n crosses the PML the optimum is ~1/n (e.g. ~0.7 for silica, ~0.3 for silicon).

#### `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`

Peak complex-frequency shift alpha of the CPML stretch kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0), largest at the inner edge of the layer; 0 = plain kappa-stretched CPML. It acts only where alpha is comparable to omega eps0 (~1.1e4 S/m at 1550 nm, ~0.06 S/m at 1 GHz), damping evanescent and low-frequency waves; below ~100 S/m it does nothing in the optical range.

#### `em_eme.eps_xx`

x component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the only one E_x sees without an off-diagonal eps_xy (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells); overrides eps_r for E_x. Anisotropic crystals, e.g. x-cut lithium niobate at 1.55 um (optic axis along x): eps_xx 4.571 = n_e^2 with eps_r 4.889 = n_o^2 for the other components.

#### `em_eme.eps_yy`

y component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the only one E_y sees without an off-diagonal eps_xy (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells); overrides eps_r for E_y. For a uniaxial crystal with its optic axis along y set eps_yy = n_e^2.

#### `em_eme.sigma_e`

Ohmic loss in S/m on every E component, default 0. The mode solves use the complex permittivity at omega: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus every Drude / Lorentz pole chi(omega).

#### `em_eme.eme_ports.input_mode`

1-based rank of the incident mode among the port modes of the input face (the mode solver ranking: 1 = largest Re n_eff, the PML modes of a cpml face listed after all others, so mode k is the k-th mode the mode ports would find). It must carry power (a propagating mode), else the power fractions are NaN with a run-log warning.

#### `em_eme.eme_length_sweep`

Cheap length scan of the last solve: the sections whose centre lies in [start, stop] are re-propagated with their lengths times each stretch factor and the S-matrix re-cascaded from the kept interfaces (no mode solve; a taper staircase is stretched step by step, so it stays the same taper, longer). Result 'xy' versus the stretched length [m] of the range (in factor order): series transmission_<k> (k = 1 .. n_port_modes of eme_ports), transmission and reflection power fractions of the excitation, as the scalar outputs; extras stretch_factors, wavelength, n_sections_stretched. Keeps the interface S-matrices of every solve (4 N^2 complex per section).

#### `em_eme.eme_length_sweep.stretch_factors`

Factors applied to the lengths of the sections in the range, one re-cascade each (no new mode solve: the modes and interfaces of the solve are reused), e.g. 0.5 .. 4 for a taper length scan.

#### `em_eme.eme_periodic`

Periodic block (gratings, Bragg mirrors, band edges): the sections whose centre lies in [start, stop] are one period, drawn once and repeated n_periods times. The unit cell S-matrix (the junction from its last to its first section, then its sections) is raised to the power n_periods - 1 by repeated Redheffer star products and inserted after the drawn period, so the port results, scalars and length sweep see the whole periodic device (at least one section must follow the range when n_periods > 1); the field plot shows the first period, the sections after it carry the field leaving the last period. Bloch modes: the eigenvectors of the unit cell, fields one period on = lam times the fields (lam = exp(-j K period)), from the generalised eigenproblem of its S-matrix. Result 'table' (forward modes: |lam| < 1, or on the unit circle with net forward power; least attenuated first): bloch_mode, n_bloch = Re K / k0 (unfolded to the Brillouin zone nearest the length-weighted mean Re n_eff of mode 1 over the cell), n_bloch_imag = Im K / k0 (< 0: decaying, a stop band when the dominant mode decays without loss), multiplier_abs = |lam| per period, phase_per_period_deg = Re K period [deg, in (-180, 180]], dominant_mode = the cell mode carrying most of the Bloch mode. Extras wavelength, period [m], n_periods, first_section / last_section (1-based section table rows). At most one per physics.

#### `em_eme.eme_periodic.n_periods`

Periods of the device: the drawn unit cell stands for n_periods copies in a row (its S-matrix raised to that power by repeated star products, cost log2(n_periods)); the sections after the range follow the last period, so the hi port plane is (n_periods - 1) periods beyond the window face. 1 = only the Bloch analysis.

#### `em_eme.adjoint_objective.quantity`

Power fraction of the excitation (eme_ports, else mode 1 from lo) this term measures, as the scalar outputs: transmission_mode = into port mode mode_number of the output face (transmission_<k>), reflection_mode = back into port mode mode_number of the input face, transmission / reflection = summed over every mode of that face. J = the sum of weight * quantity over the enabled adjoint_objective features.

#### `em_eme.adjoint_objective.mode_number`

1-based port mode of transmission_mode / reflection_mode (the eme_ports ranking: 1 = largest Re n_eff, PML modes last); at most n_modes when n_modes > 0.

#### `em_eme.design_region.eps_min`

Relative permittivity of a design cell at density 0 (the void or cladding material, e.g. silica 2.085 at 1.55 um); a cell holds eps = eps_min + rho_bar (eps_max - eps_min) of its filtered, projected density rho_bar. em_fdfd_ez writes eps_r, em_fdfd_hz eps_xx and eps_yy.

#### `em_eme.design_region.eps_max`

Relative permittivity of a design cell at density 1 (the solid material, e.g. silicon 12.08 at 1.55 um). sigma_e, poles and mu_r of the design cells stay those of the material painted there and are not optimised: paint a lossless, non-dispersive material.

#### `em_eme.design_region.initial_density`

Density rho of every design cell before the first iteration (also the fixed design outside an optimization study). 0.5 (grey) leaves the optimiser free in both directions; 0 or 1 starts from the void or solid design.

#### `em_eme.design_region.filter_radius`

Radius R of the conic density filter rho_tilde_a = sum_b w_ab A_b rho_b / sum_b w_ab A_b, w_ab = max(0, R - |c_a - c_b|) over the design cells (A_b cell area, c cell centre): it sets the smallest feature (~R) and suppresses checkerboards. 0 = no filter. Use >= 2 cells; typical 50-150 nm. Host memory grows as cells x (R / dx)^2.

#### `em_eme.design_region.projection_beta`

Steepness beta of the tanh projection rho_bar = (tanh(beta eta) + tanh(beta (rho_tilde - eta))) / (tanh(beta eta) + tanh(beta (1 - eta))) that pushes the filtered density toward 0 or 1; 0 = no projection (rho_bar = rho_tilde). Larger beta gives a more binary design (the grayness series shows the remaining grey) but a stiffer problem with more local optima; typical 0-8, or 8-32 as the final value of the optimization study continuation_stages (earlier stages use a smaller beta).

#### `em_eme.design_region.projection_eta`

Threshold eta of the tanh projection (unused at projection_beta 0): filtered densities above it move toward 1, below it toward 0; 0.5 is neutral, lower erodes less (dilated design).

#### `em_fdfd_3d.eps_r`

Real relative permittivity (>= 1), n^2 of a lossless dielectric, seen by every E component unless eps_xx / eps_yy / eps_zz override one (it is stored in the eps_r array, which holds eps_zz). Each E face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically, re-quantised into a uint16 face index). May depend on x, y, z and on physics fields. em_fdtd_3d stores materials as a uint16 index of distinct (eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz, sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m) combinations: values that vary continuously (x, y expressions, thermo-optic or other field dependence) are re-quantised to at most 65534 levels per array (bins, member mean; the max deviation is logged, e.g. ~1e-5 in eps over a range of 1), refreshed at every material change. For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.eps_zz`

z component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the only one E_z sees; overrides eps_r for E_z. Diagonal anisotropy only (crystal axes along x, y, z). Setting any of eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz (or dndT_xx / _yy / _zz) on any material allocates the eps_xx and eps_yy arrays (8 B per cell; otherwise E_x and E_y read eps_r) and makes heat_em_thermo_optic write all three components.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.eps_xx`

x component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the only one E_x sees; overrides eps_r for E_x, e.g. a uniaxial crystal with its optic axis along x: eps_xx = n_e^2, eps_r = n_o^2. Setting any of eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz (or dndT_xx / _yy / _zz) on any material allocates the eps_xx and eps_yy arrays (8 B per cell; otherwise E_x and E_y read eps_r) and makes heat_em_thermo_optic write all three components.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.eps_yy`

y component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the only one E_y sees. Setting any of eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz (or dndT_xx / _yy / _zz) on any material allocates the eps_xx and eps_yy arrays (8 B per cell; otherwise E_x and E_y read eps_r) and makes heat_em_thermo_optic write all three components.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.sigma_e`

Ohmic loss J = sigma_e E in S/m, default 0 (isotropic, face mean like eps_r); model metals with a Drude pole. Counted in absorbed_power / em_heat_joule.

#### `em_fdfd_3d.sigma_m`

Magnetic conductivity in Ohm/m (semi-implicit, each H edge takes its lower cell), default 0; sigma_m = sigma_e mu0 / eps0 matches the impedance of free space. Not counted in absorbed_power. Setting it on any material allocates its array (4 B per cell).

#### `em_fdfd_3d.resonance_table.min_region_fraction`

Resonances whose region_energy_fraction (share of the |field|^2 dA weights inside the selected region) is below this are dropped by the eigen-solve (counted in the study log; ARPACK widens like for PML modes when too few remain). 0 keeps every resonance and only adds the column; needs a domain selection when > 0. Typical 0.5 to keep the modes concentrated in a cavity and drop those of an attached guide or cladding.

#### `em_fdfd_bor.bc_x_lo`

Faces of the (r, z) half plane; x_lo is always the symmetry axis r = 0 (bc_x_lo = axis, no other choice). Every wall sits on the outer grid edge (the window edge of a face without cpml): pec = tangential E 0 there, pmc = tangential H 0 there; cpml adds pml_cells absorbing cells outside the face (complex coordinate stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0) with the FDTD grading of the pml_* settings; on r_hi the stretched radius enters every metric factor, the cylindrical PML) and ends in a pmc edge beyond them. A pec / pmc z_lo face is the antisymmetric / symmetric mirror plane of a structure symmetric about z = 0 (the equatorial plane of a disk or sphere): pmc keeps the modes whose E_r, E_phi are even about it (quasi-TE whispering-gallery modes of a disk), pec those whose E_z is even (quasi-TM); it halves the unknowns. No periodic faces.

#### `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.power`

Power P [W] of the launched mode through the port (ring weights 2 pi: the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave; its cos(m phi) standing-wave half carries P / 2 for m != 0); fields scale with sqrt(P).

#### `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.mode_number`

Guided mode launched: 1 = the highest Re n_eff at this azimuthal order (e.g. HE11 of a fibre at m = 1, TE11 of a metal pipe), 2 the next; the result table lists the modes found.

#### `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.direction`

Launch toward +z ('positive': total field on the line row and above, only what comes back below) or -z ('negative': total field on the line row and below).

#### `em_fdfd_conical.point_source.component`

Current direction: 'z' sits on the E_z point (cell centre); 'x' / 'y' are split half on each of the two faces of the cell along that axis (the E_x / E_y points, by their dual areas; the lo face of the first cell of a periodic axis is its wrapped last face with the Bloch phase). Every direction is modulated as exp(-j k_z z) along the invariant direction.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.bc_x_lo`

cpml absorbs outgoing waves in pml_cells extra cells added outside the domain. In the frequency domain the CPML is the complex coordinate stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0) with the FDTD grading of the pml_* settings. periodic must be set on both faces of the axis and wraps the field with the meshed window as period (uniform mesh: the size rounded up to whole cells) and no phase step (k = 0 along that axis, e.g. normal incidence); the em_fdtd_*, em_fdfd_* and em_modes types add a Bloch phase with bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear per input harmonic_channel; em_eme / em_eme_3d: k = 0 only). Mirror planes, on any face: symmetric = E mirror-even (a PMC mirror plane), antisymmetric = E mirror-odd (a PEC mirror plane), on the domain edge itself: one ghost cell is added outside it (the width of the edge cell, its material copied from it) to hold the mirror image, so draw the structure about the edge (x = 0 for x_lo); heat, potential and the other physics of the model have their faces on the same plane. The same plane and parity hold for the ez and hz types, so one setting imposes the same symmetry on both. A source half a cell from the plane (in the outermost domain cell) is mirrored with it. Results count the unfolded structure: a flux line reaching a mirror face and a derived integral whose selection reaches one are doubled per such face (result extra mirror_factor; integrands assumed mirror-even, e.g. powers and losses), far fields add the image contour (a box touching the plane drops its face there; at most one mirror per axis), Results.field(unfold=True) and the GUI show the mirrored field; mode-port powers, source powers and the probes stay those of the drawn part. pec and pmc walls of the two polarisations are half a cell apart (E_z pec and H_z pmc at the centre of the outermost domain cell, E_z pmc and H_z pec on its inner face), so a cavity simulated in both polarisations differs in width by one cell. The outermost cell of a wall face (the ghost cell of a mirror face) takes the row of the matching FDTD type (em_fdtd_ez / em_fdtd_hz): E_z pec and H_z pmc 0; E_z pmc / symmetric and H_z pec / antisymmetric a copy of the neighbour (no flux through the inner face); E_z antisymmetric and H_z symmetric the negated copy. A source in that cell, or an H_z face current on the inner face of a copied row, radiates nothing. A mirror plane through a symmetric guide halves the unknowns of the direct solve.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength lambda0 of the solve in a stationary study (omega = 2 pi C0 / lambda0). In a medium of index n the wave is lambda0 / n long, so the mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / |n| and, in a lossy material or metal, >= 2 (better 4) per skin depth lambda0 / (2 pi |Im n|); validation checks both with the complex eps(omega) (sigma_e and poles included) at every solved wavelength. A frequency_domain study solves its own wavelengths and ignores this setting (validation info when it is not the default); an eigenfrequency study (and the optical solve of an optomechanics study) searches the resonances nearest it (the target); a parameter sweep over it repeats a coupled stationary solve (e.g. with heat) per wavelength, cold per value, while a frequency_domain study with a coupling reading this physics (em_heat_joule) solves that coupled fixed point per study wavelength, continued from the previous one. Typical 0.4e-6 to 2e-6 m.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.discretization`

Element order on a triangles mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles; tensor meshes ignore it and use the Yee cell). The out-of-plane field (E_z / H_z) on Lagrange elements of this degree (quadratic default: error ~h^4 in k^2, elements with a curved edge mapped isoparametrically, so round objects follow the drawn outline; linear: cheaper, ~h^2), one unknown per node (+ one per edge when quadratic), materials one value per element (H_z sees the full in-plane tensor with eps_xy), a cpml face gets a ring of mesh pml_layers element layers with the stretch of the pml_* settings and a pec outer side. E_z: pec / antisymmetric faces and pec_domain elements hold E_z = 0, pmc / symmetric faces are natural; H_z: pmc / symmetric faces hold H_z = 0, pec / antisymmetric faces and pec_domain outlines are natural (no staircase). Driven solves (stationary, frequency_domain, time_dependent) factor the complex symmetric operator once per wavelength and material state with host SuperLU (the linear role; cusolver_qr is not used here; back_end cudss / cudss_mixed: a cuDSS LDL^T on the GPU, the analysis reused); eigenfrequency uses the eigen role (host SuperLU, or cudss / cudss_mixed: a cuDSS LDL^T on the GPU). On triangles only point_source, field_probe (the in-plane components from the field gradient in the containing element), pec_domain and resonance_table work; the other features, periodic / Bloch faces and the optimization / optomechanics / thermal_noise studies are validation errors.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.bloch_kx`

Bloch wave vector along x in rad/m, used only when bc_x_lo and bc_x_hi are periodic: the solution is the Bloch wave F(x + L) = F(x) exp(-j kx L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t), so kx > 0 for a wave travelling toward +x); kx and kx + 2 pi / L are the same state. 0 = plain periodic. The phase sits on the wrap entries of the operator: same unknowns and solve cost as k = 0. Every source is repeated in each period image with that phase. Line sources and gaussian beams carry exp(-j k.r) along the line (r = cell centres from the grid lo corner, as em_fdtd_*), so a line spanning the period launches an oblique plane wave at sin(theta) = kx / (n k0) from its normal (k0 = 2 pi / vacuum wavelength); the calibrated amplitude holds at normal incidence: at angle theta an E_z sheet radiates amplitude / cos(theta), an in-plane sheet |E| = amplitude. A plane_wave_tfsf with bloch_ky != 0 becomes the oblique plane wave exp(-j (k_x x + ky y)), k_x from the discrete dispersion of the background (amplitude = E_z, or the in-plane |E|; ky at or beyond the background wavenumber is refused: evanescent; graded y cells are refused, graded x cells are fine); with bloch_kx it stays a +x wave repeated per period image. Mode sources, mode monitors and mode-power objectives on a line spanning a whole Bloch period are refused (the port mode would need the phase); port lines across the Bloch axis, or shorter than the period, are fine. Every result (absorbed power and em_heat_joule, probes, flux, far field, adjoint gradients) is that of the Bloch wave at +k. Band diagrams: an eigenfrequency study swept over k gives the band frequencies per k (template fdfd_band_diagram). Typical: kx = k0 sin(theta) of the incidence angle in vacuum, e.g. an expression 2*pi/lambda0*sin(theta).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.bloch_ky`

Bloch wave vector along y in rad/m, used only when bc_y_lo and bc_y_hi are periodic: the solution is the Bloch wave F(x + L) = F(x) exp(-j ky L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t), so ky > 0 for a wave travelling toward +y); ky and ky + 2 pi / L are the same state. 0 = plain periodic. The phase sits on the wrap entries of the operator: same unknowns and solve cost as k = 0. Every source is repeated in each period image with that phase. Line sources and gaussian beams carry exp(-j k.r) along the line (r = cell centres from the grid lo corner, as em_fdtd_*), so a line spanning the period launches an oblique plane wave at sin(theta) = ky / (n k0) from its normal (k0 = 2 pi / vacuum wavelength); the calibrated amplitude holds at normal incidence: at angle theta an E_z sheet radiates amplitude / cos(theta), an in-plane sheet |E| = amplitude. A plane_wave_tfsf with bloch_ky != 0 becomes the oblique plane wave exp(-j (k_x x + ky y)), k_x from the discrete dispersion of the background (amplitude = E_z, or the in-plane |E|; ky at or beyond the background wavenumber is refused: evanescent; graded y cells are refused, graded x cells are fine); with bloch_kx it stays a +x wave repeated per period image. Mode sources, mode monitors and mode-power objectives on a line spanning a whole Bloch period are refused (the port mode would need the phase); port lines across the Bloch axis, or shorter than the period, are fine. Every result (absorbed power and em_heat_joule, probes, flux, far field, adjoint gradients) is that of the Bloch wave at +k. Band diagrams: an eigenfrequency study swept over k gives the band frequencies per k (template fdfd_band_diagram). Typical: ky = k0 sin(theta) of the incidence angle in vacuum, e.g. an expression 2*pi/lambda0*sin(theta).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.eps_zz`

Out-of-plane relative permittivity, the only component E_z sees; overrides eps_r for this physics (a component wins over eps_r). Anisotropic crystals: eps_r for the in-plane components and eps_zz, e.g. z-cut lithium niobate eps_r 4.889, eps_zz 4.571 at 1.55 um; an eps_r override then does not change E_z (set eps_zz).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

Phase of the source phasor in degrees: the source varies as A cos(omega t + phase), the real part of A e^{j phase} e^{j omega t} (time convention exp(+j omega t)), so 0 = cos carrier and -90 = the sin carrier of the FDTD sources (the steady state of a cw FDTD source is the FDFD solution with phase -90). With a single source the phase only rotates every phasor (field and probe phases), not |E| or the flux.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam`

Line source with the profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line, radiating a beam of peak E_z = amplitude V/m to each side in the local medium (vertical line: along +x and -x; horizontal: along +y and -y); the waist lies on the line. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.waist`

1/e half-width of the field profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line; the waist lies on the line and the beam diverges from there. Typical 1-5 wavelengths; keep the line several waists long so the profile is not truncated (validation warns above 1e-2 of the peak at an end that stops inside the domain; an end on a cpml edge continues through the PML). The amplitude at the waist is paraxial: on axis the field is about amplitude (1 + 1/(k waist)^2) for E_z and (1 - 1/(k waist)^2) for H_z types, k = 2 pi n / lambda0 (+-2.5% at waist = lambda0 / n).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.center`

Position of the beam axis along the line: x for a horizontal line, y for a vertical one; empty = the midpoint of the line. It must lie on the line (validation warns otherwise): off it only the tail of the profile is launched.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`

1-based index of the mode in descending order of Re(n_eff) among the propagating modes (the industry-standard numbering; the ranking key is Re(k^2) of the transverse eigenvalue, so evanescent modes, Re(k^2) < 0, come after every propagating one whatever their Re(n_eff)): 1 = the fundamental, most strongly guided mode, 2 the next, ...; both parities count, so in a symmetric slab mode 1 is even and mode 2 odd; modes localised in the PML of a line that continues through it are discarded and not counted. The build fails when the line has fewer modes and warns when the selected one is not guided (Re(n_eff) not above the index of a span-end cell at a cpml or metal end: a cladding or radiation mode) or carries no forward power (an evanescent or backward mode). The source result table lists the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.direction`

positive launches the mode toward +x for a vertical line (x = const) and toward +y for a horizontal one, negative toward -x / -y (as the em_fdtd mode sources). The total field starts at the line cells and continues downstream; nothing is launched upstream, at every solved wavelength.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.power`

Time-averaged power per unit z length carried by the launched mode, 1/2 Re of the integral of (E x H*).n over the line (the industry-standard 2D port input power); the launched mode amplitude is sqrt(power) e^{j phase} on the line cells. Fields scale with sqrt(power) and are linear, so 1 W/m is the usual choice (a peak |E| of order 1e4 V/m in a 0.3 um silicon slab).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet`

Zero-thickness conducting sheet (2D material: graphene, a TMD monolayer in its linear response, a metal film much thinner than a cell) on an axis-aligned line: the tangential E drives the surface current K = sigma_s E_t [A/m], the normal E does not conduct. E_z (em_fdfd_ez): E_z of the line cells is tangential to any line, the delta enters the operator diagonal as -j omega mu0 sigma_s / w (w = the line-cell width across the line), exact for the 3-point stencil. H_z (em_fdfd_hz): the tangential E is E_x (horizontal line) or E_y (vertical line) on the hi face of the line cells (as an H_z line source), whose face permittivity gains -j sigma_s / (omega eps0 w) with w the face spacing; the line may not lie in the last grid cell before a non-periodic outer face. A sheet in vacuum at normal incidence transmits |1 / (1 + eta0 sigma_s / 2)|^2 (exactly 1 / |1 + omega mu0 sigma_s w / (2 sin(k w))|^2 on the grid, k the discrete wavenumber). Loss 1/2 Re sigma_s |E_t|^2 per unit area of sheet is added to absorbed_power (q_abs) of the line cells as a density over the line-cell width, so q_abs integrates to the sheet loss and em_heat_joule heats those cells. The sheet enters only the operator: line-source and TFSF calibrations, mode-port solves and the material maps do not see it (keep source lines, port lines and the TFSF outline off it; enclose it in the TFSF box as a scatterer). A span end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML (as a line source: a domain-wide sheet has no end). Several sheets on one line add. In an eigenfrequency study sigma_s stays at its value at the target wavelength (first-order error away from it). The line covers the cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) along it. No result (absorbed_power and the monitors show its effect).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.model`

Sheet conductivity sigma_s(omega): 'constant' = sigma_real + j sigma_imag at every solved wavelength; 'graphene_kubo' = the Kubo formula of monolayer graphene (intraband Drude e^2 tau (mu + 2 kT ln(1 + e^{-mu / kT})) / (pi hbar^2 (1 + j omega tau)) plus the interband term with temperature smearing, sigma_0 = e^2 / (4 hbar) = 6.085e-5 S above the 2 |E_F| absorption edge; no spatial dispersion, no magnetic field), evaluated per solved wavelength.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.sigma_real`

Re sigma_s [S] (> 0 absorbs; 0 lossless). The universal optical conductivity of graphene is 6.085e-5 S (the default; 2.3 % absorption in vacuum); a metal film of thickness d << skin depth has sigma_s ~ sigma_bulk d.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.sigma_imag`

Im sigma_s [S] in the exp(+j omega t) convention of the FDFD: < 0 inductive (free carriers, Drude 1 / (1 + j omega tau)), > 0 capacitive. Kubo literature written in exp(-i omega t) has the opposite sign.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.fermi_energy`

Chemical potential E_F of graphene relative to the Dirac point [eV] (sign irrelevant, |E_F| enters); gated or doped graphene 0.1-0.6 eV, n = (E_F / (hbar v_F))^2 / pi carriers per m^2 (v_F ~ 1e6 m/s). Interband absorption sets in at hbar omega = 2 |E_F| (wavelength 1.24e-6 / (2 |E_F| / eV) m).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.scattering_time`

Carrier relaxation time tau [s] of the intraband (Drude) term: 1e-14 - 1e-12 s (CVD graphene ~1e-13 s; mobility mu_e = e tau v_F^2 / |E_F|). The interband term is taken without broadening.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.effective_index`

Effective-index method (2.5D): at build time the guided slab mode mode_number of the vertical stack layer_indices / layer_thicknesses is solved at wavelength (the A3 slab-mode solver on a 1D grid of ~wavelength / (100 n_max) cells, claddings deepened until the tails decay) and eps_r = n_eff^2 is written on the selected cells, replacing the material background permittivity there (later features win on overlaps; the material's sigma_e and dispersion poles stay; a state-dependent permittivity expression of a material overwrites it). Approximate: vertical leakage, the n_eff dispersion away from wavelength and the vertical mode mismatch at stack boundaries are ignored. Validation reports n_eff (info); thermo-optic couplings take n_eff as their reference index n0.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.effective_index.layer_indices`

Real refractive indices of the vertical stack, bottom to top: substrate (semi-infinite), one or more films, cover (semi-infinite); at least 3 entries. Losses are not modelled (real indices only).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.effective_index.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength of the slab-mode solve. n_eff is computed once at this wavelength and used at every frequency (FDTD pulses, frequency_domain sweeps), so keep the band narrow around it.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.effective_index.slab_polarization`

'te': slab mode with E parallel to the layers, the vertical-stack partner of the in-plane-E top-view types em_fdtd_hz / em_fdfd_hz; 'tm': E mostly normal to the layers (H parallel), the partner of em_fdtd_ez / em_fdfd_ez. Default here: 'tm' (validation notes a mismatch).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium`

Phase-change medium (e.g. GST-225, the defaults) on the selected cells: a per-cell crystallinity X in [0, 1] (output field crystallinity) sets eps(X) by the mixing rule of the amorphous and crystalline (n - j k)^2, written as eps_r = Re eps and sigma_e = -Im eps omega eps0 (omega of wavelength) over the material there (later features win on overlaps; dispersion poles of the material stay; a state-dependent permittivity expression of a material overwrites it). X follows the heat temperature history only through heat_em_phase_change (time_dependent study, transient heat): after each heat step theta += k(T) dt with T the end-of-step temperature, X = 1 - exp(-theta^n) (JMAK with the additivity rule), k(T) = exp(-Ea / kB (1/T - 1/T_fast)) / tau_min between crystallization_temperature and fast_crystallization_temperature, 1 / tau_min from there to the melting point, 0 below the onset; T >= melting_temperature melts the cell (theta = 0, X = 0), and whether it recrystallises while cooling follows from the same rate (a fast quench stays amorphous). Each update rewrites the arrays on the bounding box of the selection and calls materials_changed (FDTD: coefficients rebuilt, sources recalibrated; FDFD: re-solved at its next step). Not modelled: latent heat, the liquid optical constants, thermal properties following X (heat uses the material, e.g. gst_225_amorphous), nucleation statistics. Result: timeseries of the mean X over the selected cells at every update (t = heat time). Linear at optical time scales, so it works in every study (frequency_domain, FDFD, Bloch k) as a static medium at initial_crystallinity. Time scales: GST crystallises in tens of ns, ~1e9 FDTD steps; switching runs use em_fdfd_* + transient heat in a time_dependent study (the FDFD re-solves after every heat step). GST-225 data: n, k at 1.55 um as used for sputtered films in integrated photonics (e.g. Rios et al., Nat. Photonics 9, 725 (2015); film dependent by ~10 %); crystallisation onset ~150 C and activation energy 2.24 eV from Friedrich et al., J. Appl. Phys. 87, 4130 (2000); melting point 616 C from Yamada et al., J. Appl. Phys. 69, 2849 (1991). The Avrami exponent 2.5 is typical of nucleation-dominated GST (2-4 reported); the cap of 50 ns above 650 K is an illustrative calibration (100 s at the 150 C onset with 2.24 eV, tens of ns in laser / electrical SET pulses): fit both to the device.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.n_amorphous`

Refractive index n of the amorphous phase at wavelength (eps = (n - j k)^2, exp(+j omega t)); default GST-225 at 1.55 um (library material gst_225_amorphous).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.k_amorphous`

Extinction coefficient k of the amorphous phase at wavelength (eps = (n - j k)^2, exp(+j omega t)); default GST-225 at 1.55 um (library material gst_225_amorphous).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.n_crystalline`

Refractive index n of the crystalline phase at wavelength (eps = (n - j k)^2, exp(+j omega t)); default GST-225 at 1.55 um (library material gst_225_crystalline).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.k_crystalline`

Extinction coefficient k of the crystalline phase at wavelength (eps = (n - j k)^2, exp(+j omega t)); default GST-225 at 1.55 um (library material gst_225_crystalline).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength of n and k: the absorption enters as sigma_e = -Im(eps) omega eps0 at this omega, exact there (FDTD pulses see sigma_e / (omega eps0) away from it); validation notes a source / solved wavelength more than 1 % off.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.mixing`

Permittivity of crystallinity X: 'lorentz_lorenz' (eps - 1) / (eps + 2) = (1 - X) (eps_a - 1) / (eps_a + 2) + X (eps_c - 1) / (eps_c + 2) (complex), or 'linear' eps = (1 - X) eps_a + X eps_c.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.initial_crystallinity`

Crystallinity X at t = 0 on every selected cell (theta = (-ln(1 - X))^(1/n)); without an enabled heat_em_phase_change into this physics (time_dependent study) X stays here, which also gives a static, partially crystalline medium for any study.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.fast_crystallization_temperature`

T_fast [K]: the rate is capped at 1 / min_crystallization_time from T_fast up to the melting point (the Arrhenius law would otherwise give picosecond crystallisation near melting, so no melt-quench could stay amorphous). Illustrative GST-225 value 650 K.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.min_crystallization_time`

tau_min [s]: JMAK rate k = 1 / tau_min between fast_crystallization_temperature and the melting point; a melt-quench crossing that range in much less than tau_min stays amorphous (with the defaults a 1e11 K/s quench keeps X < 0.01, a 1e8 K/s one recrystallises fully). Illustrative GST-225 value 50 ns (tens of ns in SET pulses).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.activation_energy`

Ea [eV] of the Arrhenius rate k(T) = exp(-Ea / kB (1/T - 1/T_fast)) / tau_min between the onset and T_fast. GST-225 2.24 eV (Friedrich et al. 2000); with the default cap it gives ~100 s at the 423 K onset.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.avrami_exponent`

JMAK exponent n: X = 1 - exp(-theta^n), theta = integral of k(T) dt (the additivity rule, exact for isothermal steps of any length); 2-4 for GST (2.5 default).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium.melting_temperature`

T_melt [K]: a cell at T >= T_melt is molten: theta = 0, X = 0 (optically amorphous; the liquid optical constants and the latent heat are not modelled). GST-225 889 K (616 C, Yamada et al. 1991).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.field_probe`

Phasor of one field component in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell) at every solved wavelength. The face components (ez hx / hy, hz ex / ey) come from neighbouring cells, so keep them off a plane_wave_tfsf outline and a mode_source interface face, where the solved field jumps between total and scattered field (validation warns). Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength (x in m, ascending; one point per solved wavelength, so a stationary study gives one, and a wavelength solved again keeps its latest solve): series abs = |phasor| in the unit of the component and phase = its argument in rad (exp(+j omega t): the field is abs cos(omega t + phase)); y_label the component label (e.g. E_z); extras frequency (Hz), wavelength (m), component (e.g. ez) and unit.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`

1-based index of the mode in descending order of Re(n_eff) among the propagating modes (the industry-standard numbering; the ranking key is Re(k^2) of the transverse eigenvalue, so evanescent modes, Re(k^2) < 0, come after every propagating one whatever their Re(n_eff)): 1 = the fundamental, most strongly guided mode, 2 the next, ...; both parities count, so in a symmetric slab mode 1 is even and mode 2 odd; modes localised in the PML of a line that continues through it are discarded and not counted. The build fails when the line has fewer modes and warns when the selected one is not guided (Re(n_eff) not above the index of a span-end cell at a cpml or metal end: a cladding or radiation mode) or carries no forward power (an evanescent or backward mode). It picks the mode at the first solved wavelength (solve order: the frequency_domain wavelengths list, else wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; a stationary study solves one); every later wavelength follows the same mode by its overlap with the previous solve, so it keeps its identity where two modes cross in n_eff.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective`

Objective term for the adjoint sensitivity: a flux_monitor or mode_monitor quantity on an axis-aligned line times weight. Every solve records the quantity; the output field eps_sensitivity is dJ/d eps_r per unit area [W/m^3] of J = sum of weight * quantity over the enabled objectives, from one extra sparse solve with the transposed operator on the forward factorisation (no new factorisation with scipy_splu), computed when the field is read (snapshot, derived value). A small permittivity change d eps in a region R changes J by the integral of eps_sensitivity * d eps over R; for em_fdfd_hz it is the sum of the eps_xx and eps_yy terms (an isotropic change, an off-diagonal eps_xy held fixed), and its output field eps_xy_sensitivity is dJ/d eps_xy per unit area from the same solve (zero where the solve drops eps_xy: PEC cells, the outer two rows of a wall or mirror face). For em_fdfd_hz the face fields an objective reads and the right-hand side of dipole and line source face currents are differentiated with the face permittivity; line source calibrations, port modes and a mode monitor's mode are held fixed, so the gradient is exact only in cells off every line source, port and mode monitor line and off the cells beyond their hi faces (they depend on the permittivity there too); sigma_e, poles and mu_r are not differentiated. An optimization study maximises J, summed over every physics, by varying the densities of the design_region features. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength: series value (the quantity, W/m) and weighted (weight * value, W/m); extras frequency, wavelength, quantity and weight. Keep the line off a TFSF outline and a mode_source interface face, as for the monitors. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.quantity`

Monitor quantity of this objective term, in W/m: flux = the time-averaged Poynting power through the line (as flux_monitor, > 0 toward +x / +y); mode_power_positive / mode_power_negative = |a|^2 of mode mode_number travelling toward +normal / -normal (as mode_monitor power_positive / power_negative). The objective J is the sum of weight * quantity over every enabled adjoint_objective of the physics.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.mode_number`

1-based index of the mode in descending order of Re(n_eff) among the propagating modes (the industry-standard numbering; the ranking key is Re(k^2) of the transverse eigenvalue, so evanescent modes, Re(k^2) < 0, come after every propagating one whatever their Re(n_eff)): 1 = the fundamental, most strongly guided mode, 2 the next, ...; both parities count, so in a symmetric slab mode 1 is even and mode 2 odd; modes localised in the PML of a line that continues through it are discarded and not counted. The build fails when the line has fewer modes and warns when the selected one is not guided (Re(n_eff) not above the index of a span-end cell at a cpml or metal end: a cladding or radiation mode) or carries no forward power (an evanescent or backward mode). Used by the mode_power quantities only; picked at the first solved wavelength and followed by overlap, as mode_monitor.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.weight`

Factor of this term in J = sum of weight * quantity: 1 to maximise the quantity, -1 to minimise it (the gradient points to increasing J), 0 to record the quantity without contributing.

#### `em_fdfd_ez.design_region`

Density design region on the selected domains (window cells only): each cell carries a density rho in [0, 1], filtered by a conic filter of filter_radius and projected by a tanh of projection_beta / projection_eta to rho_bar, and gets eps = eps_min + rho_bar (eps_max - eps_min) in its permittivity arrays (em_fdfd_ez: eps_r; em_fdfd_hz: eps_xx and eps_yy, an isotropic change), overwriting the material permittivity there (sigma_e, poles and mu_r stay the material's). The optimization study varies rho to maximise the adjoint_objective sum J; any other study solves the initial_density design. Design regions of one physics must not share cells. Keep the region off every source, port and objective line and the cells beyond their hi faces (the adjoint gradient is not exact there). Output field design_density = rho_bar (0 outside every design region). Result 'xy' versus iteration (0 = initial design, one point per accepted L-BFGS-B iteration): series objective (J of the whole model, W/m) and grayness (mean 4 rho_bar (1 - rho_bar) of this region, 0 = binary); extras n_cells, eps_min, eps_max, mean_density and final_grayness of the current design, and note (non-empty outside an optimization study, whose result is one point: iteration 0 with objective NaN).

#### `em_fdfd_ez.resonance_table`

Resonances of the last eigenfrequency study solve, nearest the target (the wavelength setting) first. Result 'table', one row per resonance: resonance_number (1-based rank by |omega - omega_target|), wavelength = 2 pi C0 / Re(omega) in m, frequency = Re(omega) / (2 pi) and frequency_imag = Im(omega) / (2 pi) in Hz (exp(+j omega t): > 0 decays), q_factor = Re(omega) / (2 Im(omega)) (inf when |Im omega| < 1e-12 Re omega: lossless and closed; negative = a growing, non-physical solution, usually a PML artefact), pml_fraction (share of the out-of-plane |field|^2 dA in PML cells: resonances above 0.5 are dropped, and above ~1e-2 the PML shapes the resonance: widen the cladding); extras target_wavelength (m) and selected_resonance. Accurate only near the target (see the eigenfrequency study). For Q versus a parameter add a derived value with source '<physics>.<this feature>', expression q_factor, operation at and at = 0 (the resonance nearest the target). Optional domain selection = a region: the table then ends with the column region_energy_fraction (share of the same |field|^2 dA weights in the selected cells, on triangles in the dofs of the selected elements, so a dof on the region outline counts fully), and resonances below min_region_fraction are dropped from the solve like PML modes (the table rows, snapshots and resonance numbers all skip them; a cavity mode passes, a mode living in an attached guide or in another part of the domain does not). One region per physics (one resonance_table with a selection).

#### `em_fdfd_hz.point_source.orientation`

Direction of the dipole current in degrees counter-clockwise from +x: 0 drives only the E_x faces, 90 only the E_y faces. It radiates most broadside (perpendicular to it) and nothing along it.

#### `em_fdfd_hz.effective_index`

Effective-index method (2.5D): at build time the guided slab mode mode_number of the vertical stack layer_indices / layer_thicknesses is solved at wavelength (the A3 slab-mode solver on a 1D grid of ~wavelength / (100 n_max) cells, claddings deepened until the tails decay) and eps_xx / eps_yy = n_eff^2 is written on the selected cells, replacing the material background permittivity there (later features win on overlaps; the material's sigma_e and dispersion poles stay; a state-dependent permittivity expression of a material overwrites it). Approximate: vertical leakage, the n_eff dispersion away from wavelength and the vertical mode mismatch at stack boundaries are ignored. Validation reports n_eff (info); thermo-optic couplings take n_eff as their reference index n0.

#### `em_fdfd_hz.effective_index.slab_polarization`

'te': slab mode with E parallel to the layers, the vertical-stack partner of the in-plane-E top-view types em_fdtd_hz / em_fdfd_hz; 'tm': E mostly normal to the layers (H parallel), the partner of em_fdtd_ez / em_fdfd_ez. Default here: 'te' (validation notes a mismatch).

#### `em_fdfd_hz.phase_change_medium`

Phase-change medium (e.g. GST-225, the defaults) on the selected cells: a per-cell crystallinity X in [0, 1] (output field crystallinity) sets eps(X) by the mixing rule of the amorphous and crystalline (n - j k)^2, written as eps_xx / eps_yy = Re eps and sigma_e = -Im eps omega eps0 (omega of wavelength) over the material there (later features win on overlaps; dispersion poles of the material stay; a state-dependent permittivity expression of a material overwrites it). X follows the heat temperature history only through heat_em_phase_change (time_dependent study, transient heat): after each heat step theta += k(T) dt with T the end-of-step temperature, X = 1 - exp(-theta^n) (JMAK with the additivity rule), k(T) = exp(-Ea / kB (1/T - 1/T_fast)) / tau_min between crystallization_temperature and fast_crystallization_temperature, 1 / tau_min from there to the melting point, 0 below the onset; T >= melting_temperature melts the cell (theta = 0, X = 0), and whether it recrystallises while cooling follows from the same rate (a fast quench stays amorphous). Each update rewrites the arrays on the bounding box of the selection and calls materials_changed (FDTD: coefficients rebuilt, sources recalibrated; FDFD: re-solved at its next step). Not modelled: latent heat, the liquid optical constants, thermal properties following X (heat uses the material, e.g. gst_225_amorphous), nucleation statistics. Result: timeseries of the mean X over the selected cells at every update (t = heat time). Linear at optical time scales, so it works in every study (frequency_domain, FDFD, Bloch k) as a static medium at initial_crystallinity. Time scales: GST crystallises in tens of ns, ~1e9 FDTD steps; switching runs use em_fdfd_* + transient heat in a time_dependent study (the FDFD re-solves after every heat step). GST-225 data: n, k at 1.55 um as used for sputtered films in integrated photonics (e.g. Rios et al., Nat. Photonics 9, 725 (2015); film dependent by ~10 %); crystallisation onset ~150 C and activation energy 2.24 eV from Friedrich et al., J. Appl. Phys. 87, 4130 (2000); melting point 616 C from Yamada et al., J. Appl. Phys. 69, 2849 (1991). The Avrami exponent 2.5 is typical of nucleation-dominated GST (2-4 reported); the cap of 50 ns above 650 K is an illustrative calibration (100 s at the 150 C onset with 2.24 eV, tens of ns in laser / electrical SET pulses): fit both to the device.

#### `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.orientation`

Crystal axes in model axes: z_cut = crystal x, y, z along model x, y, z (c axis out of plane, so E_z channels see d33); x_cut = crystal x, y, z along model y, z, x (c axis along model x); y_cut = crystal x, y, z along model z, x, y (c axis along model y); euler = Rz(euler_alpha) Rx(euler_beta) Rz(euler_gamma) (z-x-z, degrees; column a of the rotation = crystal axis a in model coordinates).

#### `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`

Name of the harmonic_channel (its feature name) this feature acts on; a polarization both channel splits into <name>_ez and <name>_hz: name one of those. The channel polarisation picks the E_z (em_fdfd_ez) or H_z (em_fdfd_hz) form of the feature; params of the other form are ignored (validation warns).

#### `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`

gaussian: sin carrier of f0 = C0 / wavelength under exp(-((t - t0) / tau)^2), tau = 1 / (pi * bandwidth * f0), centred at t0 = 4.5 tau, so it lasts about 9 / (pi * bandwidth * f0) (550 nm, bandwidth 0.5: ~10 fs). The amplitude / current is the envelope peak: the carrier is 0 at t0, so the source peaks lower (~0.87 at bandwidth 0.5, ~0.66 at 1). cw: sin(2 pi f0 t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f0, steady after ~15 periods. ricker: Ricker wavelet whose spectrum peaks at f0, delayed by 4 / f0 (broadband, up to ~2.5 f0: 3 % of the spectral peak there, 1 % at 2.76 f0).

#### `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength lambda0 = C0 / f0 of the carrier (ricker: of the spectral peak); in a medium of index n the wave is lambda0 / n long. In m, not nm: typical 400e-9 to 1600e-9 m (validation warns below 1e-9 m or above 100 domain diagonals); the mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / n at the highest source frequency.

#### `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`

Spectral width / f0 of the gaussian pulse, amplitude spectrum exp(-((f - f0) / (bandwidth * f0))^2): 0.78 of the peak at f0 * (1 +- bandwidth / 2), 1/e at f0 * (1 +- bandwidth) (power FWHM about 1.18 * bandwidth * f0); the mesh check and auto mesh resolve f0 * (1 + bandwidth). 0.2-1 typical; a wider band gives a shorter pulse but needs a finer mesh.

#### `em_fdtd_3d.field_probe.component`

Raw Yee sample of the cell containing the point: E_x / E_y / E_z on its +x / +y / +z face, H_x / H_y / H_z on its (+y +z) / (+x +z) / (+x +y) edge; H samples are dt/2 older than the recorded time.

#### `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.wavelength_min`

Shortest vacuum wavelength of the analysed band (its highest frequency C0 / wavelength_min). Keep the band inside the source spectrum; a narrower band gives a coarser decimation and a faster, better conditioned fit.

#### `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.start_time`

Start t_s of the analysed window [s]; empty = the end 2 t0 of the latest gaussian / ricker source pulse (0 with only cw sources). The fit assumes a free ring-down, so a start inside a pulse adds spurious poles; the amplitudes and phases refer to t_s.

#### `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`

Shortest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum. Keep the range inside the source spectrum (gaussian: lambda0 / (1 + bandwidth / 2) to lambda0 / (1 - bandwidth / 2), e.g. 440e-9 to 733e-9 m for 550 nm and bandwidth 0.5); outside it the source spectrum falls off and normalised results get noisy. Validation warns for wavelengths where every enabled source spectrum is below 1e-2 of its peak (gaussian beyond f0 (1 +- 2.15 bandwidth), ricker outside 0.06-2.76 f0, cw anywhere but within 1 / duration of f0).

#### `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.n_wavelengths`

Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. 50-200 give a smooth spectrum; the work per time step grows with the count.

#### `em_fdtd_bor.bc_x_lo`

Faces of the (r, z) half plane; x_lo is always the symmetry axis r = 0 (bc_x_lo = axis, no other choice). Every wall sits on the outer grid edge, as in em_fdfd_bor: pec = tangential E 0 there, pmc = tangential H 0 there; cpml adds pml_cells absorbing cells outside the face, ending in a pmc edge beyond them. On the z faces a convolutional PML (kappa, sigma, alpha graded as the 2D FDTD) on the d/dz terms of the curl; on r_hi a cylindrical PML: the complex radius stretch of em_fdfd_bor (kappa, sigma graded the same way, alpha = 0) in the radial derivatives and in the radius of the ring metric (the 1 / r and r terms), stepped by recursive convolutions, so it absorbs as well close to the axis and at large azimuthal order as far out (pml_alpha_max acts on the z faces only). A pec / pmc z_lo face is the antisymmetric / symmetric mirror plane of a structure symmetric about z = 0 (pmc keeps E_r, E_phi even about it, pec E_z). No periodic or mirror faces.

#### `em_fdtd_bor.resonance_monitor`

Resonance finder (harmonic inversion, like Harminv / the matrix-pencil method): records one component in the cell containing each selected point (1 to 16 points) every step; when the result is read (CPU, about a second per point) the traces from the analysis start t_s on are mixed down to the band centre, low-pass filtered (Kaiser FIR, 100 dB), decimated to a sample rate of about 8 band half-widths (in Hz) and fitted by sums of damped sinusoids a exp(-gamma (t - t_s)) cos(omega (t - t_s) + phi). Several points share one joint fit (the same poles, each trace scaled to unit peak, amplitudes per point), so a mode on a nodal line of one point is still found through the others. Result 'table', one row per resonance inside the band, strongest (largest a) first, with the eigenfrequency resonance_table names: resonance_number (1, 2, ... in that order), wavelength [m, vacuum C0 / frequency], frequency = omega / (2 pi) [Hz], frequency_imag = gamma / (2 pi) [Hz] (Im of the complex frequency, exp(+j omega t): > 0 decays; the amplitude decay rate is gamma = 2 pi frequency_imag), q_factor = omega / (2 gamma) (inf when it does not decay), amplitude a [unit of the component] and phase phi [rad] at t_s at the point where the resonance is largest, error = |difference of the complex pole -gamma + j omega between two pencil sizes| / omega (a noise / resolution estimate). Poles with error above 0.01, resonances below 0.0001 of the strongest at every point and poles growing by more than 2x over the window are dropped. Extras: component, unit, dt [s], start_time t_s and end_time [s] of the analysed window, sample_interval [steps], n_samples (at most 2000: the earliest decimated samples), model_order, wavelength_min, wavelength_max, note ('' or why no resonance was found), points (the point names in selection order), point_amplitudes / point_phases (per row, one value per point). Q far above pi f T_window is resolved as long as the ring-down stays above the float32 noise (~1e-7 of the signal). A mode with zero amplitude at every point is missed: select points off the nodal lines (with one point) or points that no mode of interest has as common node; a cw source drives an undamped line at its own wavelength. A coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_kx`

Bloch wave vector along x in rad/m, used only when bc_x_lo and bc_x_hi are periodic: the fields repeat with the phase exp(-j kx L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t), so kx > 0 for a wave travelling toward +x); kx and kx + 2 pi / L are the same state. 0 = plain periodic. Any k != 0 steps a second (imaginary) field set: field memory and time per step double. Line sources and gaussian beams carry exp(-j k.r) along the line, so a line along x launches an oblique plane wave at sin(theta) = kx / (n k0) from its normal (k0 = 2 pi / vacuum wavelength): at a fixed kx the angle changes with frequency across a pulse, and frequencies below c kx / n are evanescent. The calibrated amplitude holds at normal incidence: at angle theta an E_z sheet radiates amplitude / cos(theta), an in-plane sheet |E| = amplitude. Point, plane-wave box and mode sources drive only the real field set (every period image repeats them with the Bloch phase: good for band diagrams, where a point source and a resonance monitor per swept k give the bands). DFT-based monitors (flux, field map, far field, mode monitor) accumulate F_re + j F_im, i.e. the response at +k for every positive frequency; probes, field plots, expressions and couplings read the real set only. Absorbed power (track_absorption, q_accum, em_heat_joule) is refused. Typical: kx = k0 sin(theta) of the incidence angle in vacuum, e.g. an expression 2*pi/lambda0*sin(theta) swept over theta.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_ky`

Bloch wave vector along y in rad/m, used only when bc_y_lo and bc_y_hi are periodic: the fields repeat with the phase exp(-j ky L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t), so ky > 0 for a wave travelling toward +y); ky and ky + 2 pi / L are the same state. 0 = plain periodic. Any k != 0 steps a second (imaginary) field set: field memory and time per step double. Line sources and gaussian beams carry exp(-j k.r) along the line, so a line along y launches an oblique plane wave at sin(theta) = ky / (n k0) from its normal (k0 = 2 pi / vacuum wavelength): at a fixed ky the angle changes with frequency across a pulse, and frequencies below c ky / n are evanescent. The calibrated amplitude holds at normal incidence: at angle theta an E_z sheet radiates amplitude / cos(theta), an in-plane sheet |E| = amplitude. Point, plane-wave box and mode sources drive only the real field set (every period image repeats them with the Bloch phase: good for band diagrams, where a point source and a resonance monitor per swept k give the bands). DFT-based monitors (flux, field map, far field, mode monitor) accumulate F_re + j F_im, i.e. the response at +k for every positive frequency; probes, field plots, expressions and couplings read the real set only. Absorbed power (track_absorption, q_accum, em_heat_joule) is refused. Typical: ky = k0 sin(theta) of the incidence angle in vacuum, e.g. an expression 2*pi/lambda0*sin(theta) swept over theta.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.direction`

positive launches the mode toward +x for a vertical line (x = const) and toward +y for a horizontal one, negative toward -x / -y. The total field starts at the line cells and continues downstream; nothing is launched upstream at the source wavelength, and the backward leakage grows toward the band edges of a gaussian pulse.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.waveform`

gaussian: sin carrier of f0 = C0 / wavelength under exp(-((t - t0) / tau)^2), tau = 1 / (pi * bandwidth * f0), centred at t0 = 4.5 tau, so it lasts about 9 / (pi * bandwidth * f0) (550 nm, bandwidth 0.5: ~10 fs). The amplitude / current is the envelope peak: the carrier is 0 at t0, so the source peaks lower (~0.87 at bandwidth 0.5, ~0.66 at 1). cw: sin(2 pi f0 t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f0, steady after ~15 periods. The complex mode profile is driven by the carrier and its quadrature (cos) partner, so ricker is not offered.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength lambda0 = C0 / f0 of the carrier and the only wavelength at which the mode is solved (profile, n_eff, impedance): the launch is exact and one-sided there. Typical 1.31e-6 or 1.55e-6 m in silicon photonics; the mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / n at the highest source frequency.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.bandwidth`

Spectral width / f0 of the gaussian pulse, amplitude spectrum exp(-((f - f0) / (bandwidth * f0))^2): 0.78 of the peak at f0 * (1 +- bandwidth / 2), 1/e at f0 * (1 +- bandwidth); the mesh check and auto mesh resolve f0 * (1 + bandwidth). The mode is solved at f0 only, so the backward leakage and the launch into radiation grow toward the band edges as the guide disperses; 0.1-0.3 typical for waveguides (a narrower band lasts longer, about 9 / (pi * bandwidth * f0)). Above 0.6 the build warns: the cos quadrature partner (not an exact Hilbert partner) then biases fraction_* / phase_* toward the lower band edge and adds a DC part.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.power`

Power per unit z length carried by the launched mode, 1/2 Re of the integral of (E x H*).n over the line (the industry-standard 2D port input power): cw = the time-averaged power once the ramp has settled, gaussian = the cycle-averaged power at the envelope peak. Fields scale with sqrt(power) and are linear, so 1 W/m is the usual choice (a peak |E| of order 1e4 V/m in a 0.3 um silicon slab).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.n2`

Kerr coefficient: dn = n2 I with I = n0 c eps0 |E|^2 / 2 the cycle-mean intensity; stepped as the instantaneous chi3 = (4/3) n0^2 eps0 c n2 [m^2/V^2] (D = eps0 (eps + chi3 E^2) E), so a cw field also drives its third harmonic. Silicon ~6e-18, Si3N4 ~2.5e-19, silica ~2.6e-20 m^2/W at 1.55 um; negative = self-defocusing. Keep chi3 E^2 << eps (the implicit update assumes a monotonic D(E)).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.tpa_beta`

Two-photon absorption: dI/dz = -beta I^2 for a plane wave, stepped as the conductivity sigma = (2/3) beta (n0 c eps0)^2 E^2 (its cycle mean gives beta I^2 for a pure cosine). Silicon ~8e-12 m/W (0.8 cm/GW) at 1.55 um, GaAs ~3e-10. Its power counts as absorbed power (q_accum, em_heat_joule) and, with free-carrier parameters, generates carriers.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.carrier_lifetime`

Recombination time tau of dN/dt = beta I^2 / (2 hbar omega) - N / tau (generation = the instantaneous TPA power / (2 hbar omega), stepped with an implicit Euler step in float64). Must be > 0 when fca_cross_section or fcd_coefficient is set; silicon ~0.5-3 ns. Carriers build up over about tau, so a pulse train shorter than tau sees only part of the steady density.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fca_cross_section`

Free-carrier absorption alpha = sigma N (power loss per length), stepped as the conductivity sigma N n0 eps0 c. Silicon ~1.45e-21 m^2 at 1.55 um (scales ~lambda^2). Its power counts as absorbed power.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fcd_coefficient`

Free-carrier dispersion dn = -k N (k >= 0), stepped as delta eps = -2 n0 k N (first order) in the implicit update. Silicon ~1.35e-27 m^3 at 1.55 um, a common linearisation of the Soref-Bennett electron + hole terms (the hole term is sublinear, so k depends on the density range).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.pump_wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength of the TPA photons: each absorbed pair of photons (energy 2 hbar omega, omega = 2 pi c / pump_wavelength) creates one carrier pair. Set it to the source centre wavelength (validation notes a mismatch); unused without free-carrier parameters.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.d_eff`

Instantaneous second-order response P = eps0 chi2 E^2 with chi2 = 2 d_eff (not scaled by n0), stepped implicitly with the Kerr term: a cw field E = Re(E1 exp(j omega t)) drives P(2 omega) = eps0 d_eff E1^2 (the SHG phasor of em_fdfd_nonlinear) and the DC rectification eps0 d_eff |E1|^2. One scalar per field component, no tensor: E_z types take P_z = eps0 chi2 E_z^2 (d33 of a crystal with its c axis along z), H_z types P_x = eps0 chi2 E_x^2 and P_y = eps0 chi2 E_y^2 (no cross terms). LN d33 ~2.5e-11, GaAs d14 ~1.2e-10 m/V; keep |chi2 E| << eps. Use em_fdfd_nonlinear for crystal tensors; this term is for pulsed time-domain cross-checks.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.poling`

Domain sign of chi2 per cell, an expression of x, y and parameters: values >= 0 keep d_eff, < 0 invert it (Kerr, TPA and carriers are unchanged). Periodic poling: sign(sin(2 * pi * x / Lambda)) with Lambda = lambda / (2 |n(2 omega) - n(omega)|); H_z face values average the two cells, so a domain wall on a cell edge gives 0 on the face between them. 1 = unpoled.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.wavelength`

Vacuum wavelength lambda_a of the lasing transition 2 -> 1: the polarisation obeys d2P/dt2 + gamma dP/dt + omega_a^2 P = kappa (N1 - N2) E, omega_a = 2 pi c / lambda_a.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.linewidth`

Full width gamma of the Lorentzian gain line in angular frequency (rad/s, not Hz; FWHM in wavelength ~ lambda_a^2 gamma / (2 pi c)). The peak gain scales as 1 / gamma.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.density`

Total density N0 + N1 + N2 + N3 of the active centres [1/m^3] (conserved). Peak small-signal power gain ~ k0 delta_eps omega_a / (gamma n0) per metre with delta_eps = kappa (N2 - N1) / (eps0 omega_a^2) (validation reports it).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.pump_rate`

Pump rate W_p of N0 -> N3 per ground-state atom [1/s]. Steady small-signal inversion N2 - N1 = W_p (tau_21 - tau_10) N, N = density / (1 + W_p (tau_32 + tau_21 + tau_10)); it builds up over ~tau_21 (often ns = millions of steps), so short runs start from initial_upper_fraction instead. Explicit rate step: W_p dt must stay << 1.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.tau_21`

Lifetime of the upper lasing level [s], also taken as the radiative lifetime in kappa = 6 pi eps0 c^3 / (omega_a^2 tau_21) (Chang and Taflove 2004): a longer tau_21 means a weaker coupling per atom but a larger steady inversion.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.initial_upper_fraction`

Fraction of density in level 2 at t = 0 (the rest in level 0): an initial inversion N2 - N1 = fraction x density, e.g. for runs much shorter than tau_21. 0 = all in the ground level.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`

1-based index of the mode in descending order of Re(n_eff) among the propagating modes (the industry-standard numbering; the ranking key is Re(k^2) of the transverse eigenvalue, so evanescent modes, Re(k^2) < 0, come after every propagating one whatever their Re(n_eff)): 1 = the fundamental, most strongly guided mode, 2 the next, ...; both parities count, so in a symmetric slab mode 1 is even and mode 2 odd; modes localised in the PML of a line that continues through it are discarded and not counted. The build fails when the line has fewer modes and warns when the selected one is not guided (Re(n_eff) not above the index of a span-end cell at a cpml or metal end: a cladding or radiation mode) or carries no forward power (an evanescent or backward mode). It picks the mode at the middle monitor wavelength; at the other wavelengths the same mode is followed by its overlap with the neighbouring wavelength, so it keeps its identity where two modes cross in n_eff (a build warning lists wavelengths where that overlap stays below 0.9 or the followed mode is no longer guided, e.g. past a cutoff).

#### `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.n_wavelengths`

Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. Each wavelength costs one 1D mode solve at build and two complex spectra per line cell (little GPU memory) plus work per time step; 11-41 typical.

#### `em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor.downsample`

Stride s in cells along x and y: the monitor records cells x_start + min(s, box cells) // 2 + k s (likewise in y), point samples at those cell centres (the hz in-plane E is still the face mean onto each sampled centre), no averaging over the s x s block; memory and work per step drop by ~s^2. x_centers / y_centers of the result are the sampled centres and shape the recorded counts; extent stays the whole box. 1 = every cell. Features smaller than s cells alias.

#### `heat.convection.h`

Heat lost per unit area and kelvin of T - T_ext; h = 0 removes no heat and does not anchor a steady solve. Typical: still air 5-25, forced air 10-200, water 500-10000.

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.illumination_physics`

Name of the em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz physics whose solution is the incident field: it solves the cross-section (xy, light along z uniform: normal incidence in the cross-section plane, k_z = 0) as a background physics of the thermal_noise study, at the wavelength of mode_physics and with its boundary settings. em_fdfd_ez = E along the waveguide (E_z), em_fdfd_hz = E in the cross-section (E_x, E_y). With a mirror face the illumination has the collected mode's parity (validation info).

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.mode_physics`

Name of the em_modes physics (same model, straight waveguide) whose modes give the weighting; the thermal_noise study solves it first. A mirror face lies on the window edge (its em ghost cell is outside the window), where an insulated heat face is the matching even mirror (the whole mirrored cross-section counts). The outermost cells of its pec / pmc faces are ghosts outside the wall plane (weighting 0) that keep the heat condition of that face (e.g. a temperature sink), on the window edge one cell outside the em wall plane.

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.incident_selection`

Incident mode of a mode_pair weighting: collected = the collected mode itself (backscatter / phase noise of each collected mode), te / tm = the fundamental quasi-TE / quasi-TM mode (the highest-ranked mode with te_fraction > 0.5 / <= 0.5), number = incident_mode.

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_selection`

Collected (detected) mode(s): te / tm = the fundamental quasi-TE (E_x dominant) / quasi-TM mode, i.e. the highest-ranked mode (largest Re n_eff) with te_fraction > 0.5 / <= 0.5 (run error when the solve found none: raise n_modes; a mirror face keeps one family only); te_and_tm = both in one run, each its own spectrum (series psd_te*, psd_tm*, extras with suffix _te / _tm; one set of factorisations per mode, as their beta differ); number = collected_mode. The resolved mode number, n_eff and te_fraction are in the result (collected_mode, collected_n_eff, collected_te_fraction).

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_direction`

Travel direction of the collected light: backward = backscattering (q0 = beta_inc + beta_coll), forward = forward scattering (q0 = |beta_inc - beta_coll|, 0 for the same mode); illumination: q0 = beta_coll either way (only the sign of the E_z cross term differs).

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.axial_profile`

Envelope g(z) of the weighting along z. uniform: g = 1 over interaction_length L, S = L S_2D(q0) (asymptotic in L: exact once L >> 1/q0 and the thermal diffusion length sqrt(D / omega); at q0 = 0 and low f the finite-L integral is the right one, use gaussian). gaussian: g = exp(-z^2 / waist^2) (a Gaussian illumination spot of 1/e^2 intensity radius waist), S = integral dq/2pi |g~(q - q0)|^2 S_2D(q) by axial_points-point Gauss-Hermite (exact for any waist).

#### `heat.thermorefractive_noise.axial_points`

Gauss-Hermite nodes of the q integral (gaussian profile); each costs one factorisation per frequency (nodes with equal |q| are merged, so q0 = 0 halves the cost). 6-12 typical.

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.geometry`

planar: A = A_z of currents along z, per unit z length (energy J/m, flux linkage Wb/m, inductance H/m). axisymmetric: a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z): currents J_phi circle the axis; the solve is for the flux function psi = r A_phi on a planar operator with coefficients nu / r (2 pi psi = the flux through the circle of radius r), field A reports A_phi = psi / r, totals are whole rings (energy J, flux linkage Wb, inductance H). x_lo is the axis (r = 0: symmetry, psi = 0 there with the exact half-cell conductance of the axis cell; any face feature selecting x_lo is a validation error). Field derived values of the whole model are weighted by the ring volume 2 pi r dx dy ('integral' a whole-body total, 'mean' a volume mean; also for fields of other physics). A coupled physics that is planar (its type has no geometry setting, e.g. EM, or it is set to planar) solves the drawing as a planar cut per unit z length, so its fields are applied per cell as rings (validation warns); a partner with geometry axisymmetric too is consistent.

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.mu_dc`

Isotropic static relative permeability (> 0): sets mu_dc_xx and mu_dc_yy (component entries override it); unset = 1 (vacuum), so every cell takes part in the solve. NOT the optical mu_r of the wave physics (kept 1 there). Typical: air, copper, aluminium 1; ferrite 1e3 - 1e4; electrical steel 4e3; Metglas (amorphous Co / Fe) 1e4 - 1e5; mu-metal 5e4. A large contrast is solved exactly by the finite volumes but slows Jacobi-PCG (iterations grow with the contrast): tighten the tolerance (1e-10). With saturation_polarization it is the initial (small-field) permeability of the B-H curve.

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.magnetic_insulation`

Magnetic insulation A = 0 on the selected outer faces (the default of every face no feature sets): the normal flux density is 0, field lines run along the face. It is the mirror image of an ODD current distribution (J_z changes sign across the plane, e.g. the midplane between a conductor and its return current) and stands in for a distant boundary far from the sources. Axisymmetric: psi = r A_phi = 0, so no net flux crosses the circle of an x_hi face (the return flux lies inside it); x_lo is the axis (psi = 0 already; selecting it is a validation error). Anchors the solve.

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.symmetry`

Symmetry dA/dn = 0 (Neumann) on the selected outer faces: the tangential flux density is 0, field lines cross the face at right angles.
