It is the mirror image of an EVEN current distribution (J_z the same on both sides, e.g. the midplane of two parallel conductors carrying the same current) and models a face next to an ideal iron yoke. Does not anchor the solve: a model whose four faces are all symmetry needs an external_field or fixed_potential. Axisymmetric: not allowed on x_lo (the axis).

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.external_field`

Uniform applied flux density (B_x, B_y) [T], selection 'all' only, at most one per physics: the outermost window cells are held at the external potential (planar A = B_x y - B_y x evaluated at their faces toward the free cells, so a uniform field is reproduced exactly; axisymmetric psi = B_y r^2 / 2 on the z faces and the exact half-cell value on x_hi, B_x must be 0; exact on uniform r cells only: graded r cells add a first-order error where the radial width changes). Inside, objects perturb the field; keep them several object sizes away from the domain edges, since the ring holds the undisturbed field there. The ring cells leave the solve: B and H read 0 in them, and face conditions of the outer faces have no effect (the axis stays psi = 0). Anchors the solve. Typical: the Earth field ~5e-5 T, a Helmholtz coil 1e-4 - 1e-2 T.

#### `magnetic_fields_ac.fixed_potential`

Holds the vector potential on the selected cells for the whole run (they leave the solve; B and H read 0 in them): planar A_z [T m], axisymmetric the flux function psi = r A_phi [T m^2] (2 pi psi = the flux through the circle of radius r). A region held at one value excludes all flux, like a perfect diamagnet or superconductor; two regions held at A_1 and A_2 carry the flux (A_1 - A_2) per m of depth between them (planar). Anchors the solve.

#### `magnetostatics.nonlinear_tolerance`

Stop of the saturation loop of materials with saturation_polarization > 0 or a bh_curve. Tensor mesh: converged when one proposal changes ln of the secant reluctivity nu = H / B of every cell by at most this value (a relative change); each iteration is one assembly and one CG solve warm-started at the previous A, so keep it above the CG accuracy. Triangle mesh (Newton): converged when the last step changes A by at most this fraction of max |A| and the largest free residual of the weak form is at most this fraction of the largest load or internal force. Ignored without a saturating material.

#### `magnetostatics.nonlinear_max_iterations`

Saturation iteration (tensor: fixed-point proposals, triangles: Newton steps) limit per solve of a saturating model; an unconverged loop keeps the fields of its last iterate and logs a warning (study log). Ignored without a saturating material.

#### `magnetostatics.nonlinear_method`

Solver of materials with saturation_polarization > 0 or a bh_curve. 'auto' (default): 'anderson' on a tensor mesh, 'newton' on a triangle mesh. Tensor mesh: a fixed point on ln nu; 'anderson' mixes the last 5 iterates (Anderson acceleration with the fixed relaxation below), which converges also where plain Picard oscillates (currents imposing H on iron past the knee); 'picard' applies the damped proposal with automatic halving. Triangle mesh: 'newton' minimises the convex magnetic energy with the exact element tangent (symmetric positive definite for any increasing B-H curve) and a backtracking line search on the energy, globally convergent and quadratic near the solution (piecewise-linear bh_curve tables: superlinear across their rows); one factorisation per step. 'newton' on a tensor mesh and 'anderson' / 'picard' on a triangle mesh are validation errors.

#### `magnetostatics.nonlinear_relaxation`

Fraction of each proposed change of ln nu applied, [1/64, 1] (tensor mesh only; Newton on triangles finds its step by the energy line search). 'picard': it halves automatically (down to 1/64) while the change grows and recovers up to this value once it shrinks; Picard converges without damping where the flux is imposed (an air gap, an applied field) but oscillates where the current imposes H on iron past the knee of the curve: it needs a value below 2 / (1 + d ln nu / d ln B) (about 0.5 at B ~ 0.7 J_s), lower it (0.2) deep into saturation. 'anderson': the fixed mixing factor (0.5 - 1).

#### `magnetostatics.bh_curve`

Tabulated anhysteretic B-H curve (magnetostatics only): rows [H, B] with H [A/m] and B [T] both strictly increasing, H, B > 0 except an optional first row [0, 0] (the curve always starts at the origin), e.g. [[100, 0.5], [300, 1.0], [1000, 1.4], [5000, 1.7]]. H(B) is interpolated linearly between the rows; beyond the last row B = B_n + mu0 (H - H_n) (fully saturated), so end the table well into saturation. The cells follow the secant reluctivity nu = |H| / B(|H|) on both axes (isotropic; mu_dc / mu_dc_xx / mu_dc_yy are ignored there), solved by the same fixed point on ln nu as saturation_polarization (settings nonlinear_*; each proposal reads the cell-centre |H|, which stays stable also beyond the last row); the first iterate is the first segment's slope B_1 / H_1. Energy and inductances are secant values on a tensor mesh. On a triangle mesh Newton reads the curve B-indexed (H(B) linear per segment, the segment slope as tangent, the exact energy integral). Not combinable with saturation_polarization or a remanence in the same material (validation error); ignored by magnetic_fields_ac. A constant table per material (no x, y or field dependence; entries may be parameter expressions).

#### `membrane.squeeze_film_damping.gap`

Height H of the gas gap between the vibrating surface and the fixed wall facing it [m], uniform; the film equation assumes H much smaller than the footprint (typical MEMS 0.5-10 um). The damping scales as 1 / H^3.

#### `membrane.squeeze_film_damping.ambient_pressure`

Ambient gas pressure p_a [Pa] (1 atm = 101325): sets the gas compressibility H / p_a of the film; 0 = an incompressible film (pure damping, no gas stiffness; needs vents). Compressibility matters at squeeze numbers sigma = 12 mu omega L^2 / (p_a H^2) of order 1 and above (L the distance to a vent): the damping falls and a gas spring appears. The mean free path is not rescaled with it: set both.

#### `membrane.squeeze_film_damping.slip`

veijola: the slip-flow viscosity mu_eff = mu / (1 + 9.638 Kn^1.159), Kn = mean_free_path / gap (Veijola et al. 1995, 0 <= Kn <= 880, about 5 %); none: mu_eff = mu (continuum, Kn << 0.01).

#### `membrane.squeeze_film_damping.mean_free_path`

Molecular mean free path of the gas at the ambient pressure [m] (air: 68e-9 at 101325 Pa, scaling as 1 / p_a: 6.8e-6 at 1013 Pa); used by slip veijola.

#### `solid_mechanics.stress_stiffening`

Triangle and tetrahedron meshes: the prestressed (linear perturbation) form of the eigenfrequency, frequency_response and optomechanics studies. On: the study first solves the static state (eigenfrequency: every load, prescribed displacement, initial_stress, thermal strain and coupled input, as a stationary solve; frequency_response: the initial_stress and thermal strain alone, held supports at 0, since the loads are its harmonic drive) and adds the geometric stiffness K_sigma = int grad N . sigma grad N dV of that total stress to K in every pencil (stress stiffening of strings, membranes, buckling-softening under compression); K_sigma carries no loss. A free body, a Bloch cell or an elastic PML cannot be solved statically: K_sigma then comes from the initial_stress alone (unrelaxed). Off (default): the modes and responses of the unstressed solid, loads and initial_stress play no part in the pencil. Not available with piezoelectric or on a rectangular-cell mesh.

#### `solid_mechanics.geometric_nonlinearity`

Triangle and tetrahedron meshes: large deflections and rotations in every static solve (stationary and time_dependent studies, the static state of the eigenfrequency / frequency_response studies). Total-Lagrangian form on the reference geometry: Green-Lagrange strain E = (H + H^T + H^T H) / 2 (H the displacement gradient), second Piola-Kirchhoff stress S = C E + sigma0 - beta dT (Saint Venant-Kirchhoff material: valid for small strains with large rotations), solved by Newton iterations with the tangent K_T = int (B + B_NL)^T C (B + B_NL) dV + K_sigma(S), refactorised every iteration, damped (the step halves while the change grows) and over load_steps equal load increments. Boundary loads and body forces are dead loads (fixed direction and reference area: nominal tractions); load steps scale them, prescribed displacements and coupled body forces, while the initial stress and the thermal strain enter at full strength in every step. Outputs: strain_* are Green-Lagrange strains, stress_* the second Piola-Kirchhoff stress (equal to the Cauchy stress to first order in the strain); support reactions are the nominal forces of the internal force int (B + B_NL)^T S dV - f at the held dofs (not K u - f). The eigenfrequency study linearises about the nonlinear static state (its pencil stiffness is K_T, stress stiffening included, whether or not the stress_stiffening setting is on); frequency_response about the nonlinear state of the initial stress alone (holds at 0). A Bloch cell, an elastic PML or a free body has no static solve: their pencils take K + K_sigma of the initial stress. Not available with piezoelectric or on a rectangular-cell mesh, and on a triangle mesh not with azimuthal_order >= 1, an elastic PML or generalized plane strain. Cost: one tangent assembly and factorisation per Newton iteration (typically 3 to 6 per load step; setting tangent_update when_slow keeps the factor while the residual falls fast).

#### `solid_mechanics.load_steps`

Geometric nonlinearity: the applied loads and prescribed displacements are ramped in this many equal steps, each converged by Newton iterations from the previous one (raise it when a large load does not converge; the initial stress and thermal strain are not ramped). Default 1.

#### `solid_mechanics.nonlinear_tolerance`

Geometric nonlinearity: a load step has converged when the largest Newton correction is at most this fraction of the largest displacement (quadratic convergence: the error after the last step is about its square). Default 1e-8.

#### `solid_mechanics.nonlinear_max_iterations`

Geometric nonlinearity: Newton iterations per load step before it stops unconverged (a warning; the damped state is kept and the next step continues from it). Default 25.

#### `solid_mechanics.tangent_update`

Geometric nonlinearity: when the tangent K_T is reassembled and refactorised. every_iteration (default): full Newton, one factorisation per iteration, quadratic convergence. when_slow: modified Newton, the factorised tangent is kept (only the internal force is assembled, one back substitution) while each iteration cuts the largest free residual below 0.25 x the previous one, and refactorised at the current state otherwise; the first iteration of a load step keeps the factor of the previous step when that step ended fast. Saves factorisations when they dominate an iteration (large 3D meshes), at the price of linear convergence near the end (a few more, cheaper iterations; the remaining error is at most about a third of the nonlinear_tolerance correction). Work counters tangent_factorizations / tangent_reuses.

#### `solid_mechanics.pml_reflection`

Theoretical round-trip reflection of the elastic PML for the fastest wave at the target frequency (sets beta = 3 ln(1 / R) c / (2 omega_t w)); slower waves are absorbed more. A very small value makes the profile steep, which the discretisation reflects instead: 1e-4 to 1e-8 typical.

#### `solid_mechanics.alpha_zz`

Expansion coefficient along z, read only by solid_mechanics and solid_mechanics_3d; overrides alpha for this axis. 2D plane strain holds eps_zz = 0, so alpha_zz dT becomes out-of-plane stress and, through the Poisson effect, in-plane strain (plane stress: a free expansion along z; generalized plane strain: part of the uniform eps_zz balance; axisymmetric 2D: the hoop expansion); in 3D it is an ordinary expansion along z.

#### `solid_mechanics.rho`

Mass density; solid_mechanics and solid_mechanics_3d read it only in an eigenfrequency (or optomechanics) study (consistent mass of the solid cells; every solid cell, youngs_modulus or c11 > 0, needs rho > 0 there). Shared with heat / elastic_waves. Typical: silica 2200, silicon 2329, gold 19300.

#### `solid_mechanics.piezo_e11`

Piezoelectric stress constant e_11 [C/m^2] of the in-plane block in model axes (reduced Voigt: T_J = c_JK S_K - e_kJ E_k, D_k = e_kJ S_J + eps0 eps_dc E_k with k = 1 x / 2 y and J = 1 xx, 2 yy, 6 xy, engineering shear S_6 = 2 strain_xy); default 0; the same arrays as elastic_waves. solid_mechanics reads them only with its setting piezoelectric on, and only in solid cells (youngs_modulus or c11 > 0). A {'model': 'crystal'} entry sets them together with the c_ij, which solid_mechanics reads (2D).

#### `solid_mechanics.piezo_e12`

Piezoelectric stress constant e_12 [C/m^2] of the in-plane block in model axes (reduced Voigt: T_J = c_JK S_K - e_kJ E_k, D_k = e_kJ S_J + eps0 eps_dc E_k with k = 1 x / 2 y and J = 1 xx, 2 yy, 6 xy, engineering shear S_6 = 2 strain_xy); default 0; the same arrays as elastic_waves. solid_mechanics reads them only with its setting piezoelectric on, and only in solid cells (youngs_modulus or c11 > 0). A {'model': 'crystal'} entry sets them together with the c_ij, which solid_mechanics reads (2D).

#### `solid_mechanics.piezo_e13`

Out-of-plane piezoelectric constant e_13 [C/m^2] (D_1 versus the strain S_zz, model axes); default 0. Plane strain holds S_zz = 0, so it enters only the out-of-plane stress: stress_zz -= e_13 E_x (2D solid_mechanics with piezoelectric on). A {'model': 'crystal'} entry sets it.

#### `solid_mechanics.piezo_e23`

Out-of-plane piezoelectric constant e_23 [C/m^2] (D_2 versus the strain S_zz, model axes); default 0. Plane strain holds S_zz = 0, so it enters only the out-of-plane stress: stress_zz -= e_23 E_y (2D solid_mechanics with piezoelectric on). A {'model': 'crystal'} entry sets it.

#### `solid_mechanics.eps_dc_xy`

Off-diagonal static permittivity of a rotated anisotropic material; keep eps_dc_xy^2 < eps_dc_xx * eps_dc_yy (else the solid_mechanics build fails). Default 0.

#### `solid_mechanics.c11`

Anisotropic stiffness entry c11 [Pa] (xx-xx) of the Voigt matrix in model axes (1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 6 xy; engineering shear g = 2 strain_xy): T_I = c_IJ S_J - beta_I dT with beta_I = c_IJ alpha_J. solid_mechanics (2D) reads all ten (industry-standard plane strain: the full law with S_zz = S_xz = S_yz = 0, stress_zz = T_3); plane stress condenses T_3 = 0, generalized plane strain takes a uniform S_3, axisymmetric reads 3 as the hoop direction (orthotropic only: c16 = c26 = c36 = 0, else the build fails). Unset (NaN) = the isotropic value lambda + 2 mu of youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio per component (Lame constants), so a cell with only c_ij entries needs c11, c12, c22, c66 (plane stress / axisymmetric / generalized: also c13, c23, c33); any entry set allocates the eight arrays besides c16 / c26, which (as in elastic_waves) only c16 or c26 allocates. The set the formulation reads must be positive definite (build error). A cell is solid when its c11 > 0. Usually set by a {'model': 'crystal'} entry (rotated crystal data, with piezo_e* and eps_dc*). Not for guided (2.5D) modes (axial_wavenumber: isotropic only). solid_mechanics_3d on a tetrahedron mesh reads it too, as one of its 21 entries (see c44).

#### `solid_mechanics.mechanical_loss_factor`

Isotropic structural loss factor eta (industry-standard isotropic loss factor eta_s), read by the frequency_response study of solid_mechanics (2D) and solid_mechanics_3d (tetrahedron meshes) and by their eigenfrequency study on triangle / tetrahedron meshes (damped complex modes, Q = Re omega / (2 Im omega) in the resonance table; not with piezoelectric): every stiffness of the cell becomes c (1 + j eta) (exp(+j omega t)), so a resonance has Q ~ 1 / eta; the geometric stiffness of stress_stiffening stays lossless (dissipation dilution: Q above 1 / eta). Default 0 (lossless); typical 1e-4 (quartz, LN) to 1e-2 (metals, polymers higher).

#### `solid_mechanics.dielectric_loss_tangent`

Dielectric loss tangent tan delta (industry-standard dielectric loss factor eta_epsilon), read only by the frequency_response study of a piezoelectric solid_mechanics (2D) or solid_mechanics_3d (tetrahedron meshes, every window element): the static permittivity becomes eps0 eps_dc (1 - j tan delta) (exp(+j omega t)), a conductance omega C tan delta in parallel with the electrode capacitance. Default 0; typical 1e-4 to 1e-3 for lithium niobate, ~1e-2 for PZT.

#### `solid_mechanics.initial_stress_xx`

Initial (residual) stress sigma0_xx [Pa] of the cell, e.g. the deposition stress of a film (tension > 0): the total stress is sigma0 + C eps - beta dT, so a stationary solve relaxes it (a released structure contracts until the total stress balances the supports); default 0. Triangle and tetrahedron meshes only (a rectangular-cell mesh refuses it). In 3D a Voigt row (xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy); in 2D the in-plane row xx (axisymmetric: rr). With the stress_stiffening setting the eigenfrequency / frequency_response / optomechanics studies add the geometric stiffness K_sigma of the static state (a tensioned string or membrane rises in frequency). Constant per element (an x / y / z expression is evaluated at the centroids).

#### `solid_mechanics.initial_stress_yy`

Initial (residual) stress sigma0_yy [Pa] of the cell, e.g. the deposition stress of a film (tension > 0): the total stress is sigma0 + C eps - beta dT, so a stationary solve relaxes it (a released structure contracts until the total stress balances the supports); default 0. Triangle and tetrahedron meshes only (a rectangular-cell mesh refuses it). In 3D a Voigt row; in 2D the in-plane row yy (axisymmetric: zz, along the axis). With the stress_stiffening setting the eigenfrequency / frequency_response / optomechanics studies add the geometric stiffness K_sigma of the static state (a tensioned string or membrane rises in frequency). Constant per element (an x / y / z expression is evaluated at the centroids).

#### `solid_mechanics.initial_stress_xy`

Initial (residual) stress sigma0_xy [Pa] of the cell, e.g. the deposition stress of a film (tension > 0): the total stress is sigma0 + C eps - beta dT, so a stationary solve relaxes it (a released structure contracts until the total stress balances the supports); default 0. Triangle and tetrahedron meshes only (a rectangular-cell mesh refuses it). In 3D a Voigt row; in 2D the in-plane shear xy (axisymmetric: rz). With the stress_stiffening setting the eigenfrequency / frequency_response / optomechanics studies add the geometric stiffness K_sigma of the static state (a tensioned string or membrane rises in frequency). Constant per element (an x / y / z expression is evaluated at the centroids).

#### `solid_mechanics.initial_stress_zz`

Initial (residual) stress sigma0_zz [Pa] of the cell, e.g. the deposition stress of a film (tension > 0): the total stress is sigma0 + C eps - beta dT, so a stationary solve relaxes it (a released structure contracts until the total stress balances the supports); default 0. Triangle and tetrahedron meshes only (a rectangular-cell mesh refuses it). In 3D a Voigt row; in 2D plane strain the out-of-plane stress (stress_zz only, no in-plane effect), axisymmetric the hoop stress; plane stress (sigma_zz = 0) and generalized plane strain refuse it. With the stress_stiffening setting the eigenfrequency / frequency_response / optomechanics studies add the geometric stiffness K_sigma of the static state (a tensioned string or membrane rises in frequency). Constant per element (an x / y / z expression is evaluated at the centroids).

#### `solid_mechanics.temperature_change`

Applied temperature change [K] for thermal strain, without a heat physics: added to temperature_rise_ext, which adds to the coupled temperature_rise of heat_solid_thermal_strain.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling`

Vacuum optomechanical coupling between one optical mode and every vibration mode of the optomechanics study (2D plane strain, guided 2.5D modes with scattering backward; rho needed in every solid cell). g_om = d omega_optical / d alpha for the displacement alpha Q, Q = the mode shape scaled to |Q| = 1 at the reference node; moving boundary: each interior cell face whose cells differ in permittivity contributes Q_n [eps0 (eps_lo - eps_hi) |E_par|^2 - (1/eps_lo - 1/eps_hi) |D_n|^2 / eps0] times its length (Q_n = mean of its two corner nodes; staircase interfaces); photoelastic: eps0 E* d eps E dA per solid cell with d eps_ii = -eps_ii^2 (p11 S_ii + p12 (S_jj + S_kk)) and the shear d eps_xy = -eps_xx eps_yy 2 p44 S_xy (photoelastic_p44, unset = (p11 - p12) / 2), S the mode strain (tensor shear S_xy), S_zz = S_xz = S_yz = 0; the shear term pairs E_x and E_y averaged to the cell centres (2 Re(E_x* E_y)) and is the continuum form (the optical solvers hold diagonal eps), so em_fdfd_ez has none. A material with a {"model": "crystal"} entry with photoelastic data and no photoelastic_* property of its own uses the full p of the crystal rotated into model axes (as the entry expands): Delta(1/eps)_I = p_IJ S_J (Nye, Voigt xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy, engineering shear), d eps_ij = -eps_ii eps_jj Delta(1/eps)_ij, whose xz / yz rows pair E_x / E_y with E_z at the centres (2 Re(E_x* E_z), em_modes only; continuum form like xy); its stiffness stays the isotropic youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio. Subpixel smoothing: the face jumps and the photoelastic eps are the unsmoothed cell values (the build's material assignment), the fields, D_n and the mode energy those of the smoothed solve. em_fdfd_ez resonance: g_om = -(omega / 2) Re[(I_mb + I_pe) / sum eps0 eps |E_z|^2 dA]; em_fdfd_hz resonance: the same over sum mu0 mu |H_z|^2 dA, E_par on the Yee face itself, |D_n|^2 the mean over the four nearest normal-E faces, the photoelastic sum over the E_x / E_y faces (face-averaged d eps_xx / d eps_yy); em_modes cross-section mode (needs group_index): d beta / d alpha = omega (I_mb + I_pe) / (4 P) (1 W, the whole mode) and the ring conversion at fixed azimuthal order g_om = -(C0 / n_group) d beta / d alpha (column dn_eff_dx = d n_eff / d alpha at fixed omega; a bent em_modes uses its bend-mapped eps components, exact for bend_model 'exact'). m_eff = length x the consistent-mass Q^T M Q (x 2 per EM mirror face), x_zpf = sqrt(hbar / (2 m_eff Omega)), g0 = g_om x_zpf. Result 'table', one row per vibration mode: mechanical_mode, frequency, effective_mass, zero_point_motion, g_om_moving_boundary, g_om_photoelastic, g_om, dn_eff_dx, g0_moving_boundary, g0_photoelastic, g0, brillouin_gain (Hz, kg, m, rad/s/m, 1/m; g0 columns are g0 / 2 pi in Hz, signed: total = moving boundary + photoelastic; brillouin_gain [1/(W m)] = the forward intramodal G_B = 2 Q_m (d beta / d alpha)^2 / (omega m' Omega^2), m' = m_eff / length, em_modes with mechanical_quality_factor only, else NaN). scattering backward (em_modes): the vibration modes are the guided modes at k_z = 2 Re beta (set by the study), |Q| and m_eff include u_z, the overlap is kappa = omega (I_mb + I_pe) / (4 P) between the mode and its counter-propagating twin (E_x, E_y, -E_z) with the conjugated phonon strain (S_zz = k_z u_z, shears S_xz / S_yz with p44 pairing E_x / E_y and E_z; the E_z terms flip sign), g_om = -(C0 / n_group) Re kappa and g0 the forward-backward coupling rate, brillouin_gain = 2 Q_m |kappa|^2 / (omega m' Omega^2) (bulk limit: g_B / area). Extras optical_physics, optical_mode, optical_frequency, optical_wavelength, n_eff, n_group, length, mirror_factor, scattering, axial_wavenumber (None forward), normalisation, reference_node. Lossy or open optical modes use |E|^2 forms and the real part (no quasi-normal-mode correction). An EM mirror face needs a solid roller on the same face (even vibration modes; the odd ones do not couple). The solid field om_integrand (optomechanics study only) maps the moving-boundary g_om density of the shown vibration mode (first coupling) in rad/s/m^3: each face term half to each of its cells over the cell area, summing to g_om_moving_boundary. em_fdfd_bor optics (a resonance ~ exp(-j m phi) on a triangles mesh; the solid axisymmetric on a triangles mesh, or a solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra): every integral carries 2 pi r over the window elements (PML ring, PEC and interfaces touching them left out); moving boundary on the curved element edges between permittivities (the eps_phiphi component, isotropic), n out of the first element, q . n [eps0 Delta eps |E_par|^2 - Delta(1/eps) |D_n|^2 / eps0], |E_par|^2 = |E_phi|^2 + |E_t|^2 and |D_n|^2 the means of both sides, q . n of the solid side; photoelastic eps0 E* d eps E with the cylindrical strains (rr, phiphi = u_r / r, zz, rz) and isotropic p11 / p12 / p44 (crystal tensors are not used); U = sum eps0 eps |E|^2 2 pi r dA. An axisymmetric solid of azimuthal_order m >= 1 couples through the ring mean of cos(m phi) (zero to round-off); a 3D solid is sampled on 64 angles per (r, z) point about the axis through (axis_x, axis_y) and phi-averaged (its crown parts drop out). m_eff = Q^T M Q in kg (whole rings or the 3D body; length and mirror factors unused, a pec / pmc z face used as a mirror plane counts the drawn half), normalisation point: the solid dof nearest (reference_x, reference_y) (triangles only), no om_integrand, dn_eff_dx and brillouin_gain NaN. Extras optical_azimuthal_order, optical_q_factor, solid_mesh, mechanical_azimuthal_order, prescribed_normal_displacement and prescribed_g_om (setting prescribed_normal_displacement: the rate of that uniform outward motion of the solid surface).

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.optical_physics`

Name of the em_modes (cross-section mode at its wavelength, group_index on), em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz (in-plane resonance of its eigen-solve near its wavelength setting) or em_fdfd_bor (body-of-revolution resonance on a triangles mesh; the solid axisymmetric on a triangles mesh or a solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra) physics whose mode couples to the vibration modes; the optomechanics study solves it before the solid.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.optical_mode`

1-based mode number of the em_modes solve (descending Re beta^2), or resonance number of the em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz / em_fdfd_bor eigen-solve (nearest its wavelength first).

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.length`

Length L along z that turns the per-metre mass into kg: the ring circumference 2 pi R or waveguide length for a cross-section (em_modes), the thickness of the device for an in-plane resonator (em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz). m_eff = L x the 2D modal mass; g_om does not depend on it, g0 scales as 1 / sqrt(L). Default 2 pi x 10 um. Unused with em_fdfd_bor optics (whole rings / the 3D body: m_eff in kg).

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.photoelastic`

Include the photoelastic part (photoelastic_p11 / _p12 / _p44 of the solid cells, p44 unset = isotropic (p11 - p12) / 2; a material with a crystal entry that has photoelastic data and sets no photoelastic_* property itself: the full rotated p tensor of the crystal).

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.normalisation`

Node where the mode shape is scaled to |u| = 1 for g_om and m_eff: 'max' the peak node, 'point' the solid node nearest (reference_x, reference_y). g0 does not depend on it; g_om and m_eff do.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.mechanical_quality_factor`

Q_m of every vibration mode for the brillouin_gain column (em_modes only): Brillouin gain G_B = 2 Q_m |kappa|^2 / (omega m' Omega^2) [1/(W m)], m' = m_eff / length, kappa = d beta / d alpha (forward intramodal: pump and Stokes in the optical mode, k_z = 0 vibration; its real part) or the coupling to the counter-propagating twin (scattering backward). Empty: the column reads NaN (the modal analysis is undamped). Typical 100-1000 (silicon wires at room temperature).

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.scattering`

forward: the plane-strain (k_z = 0) vibration modes, g0 = the frequency shift of the optical mode, brillouin_gain the forward intramodal gain. backward (em_modes only): the study sets the solid's k_z to 2 Re beta of the optical mode before its modal solve (the guided 2.5D modes with u_z, as the axial_wavenumber setting, which stays empty; supports optional) and the overlap pairs the mode with its counter-propagating twin (E_x, E_y, -E_z) and the conjugated phonon strain: S_zz = k_z u_z enters the p11 / p12 terms, the shears S_xz, S_yz (p44) pair E_x, E_y with E_z, the E_z terms of the moving boundary and photoelastic sums flip sign. The g_om / g0 / dn_eff_dx columns then hold the forward-backward coupling rate (a ring: between the counter-propagating modes), brillouin_gain the backward gain. Every optomechanical_coupling of one solid needs the same scattering (backward: the same optical physics and mode). The guided modes near 2 v_L n_eff / lambda (tens of GHz) need the solid target_frequency set (0 finds the lowest, flexural ones).

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.prescribed_normal_displacement`

em_fdfd_bor optics only: a uniform outward motion q . n [m] of every optical permittivity interface bordering the solid (its stiff elements) without a mechanical mode; the table extra prescribed_g_om [rad/s/m] is the moving-boundary d omega / d alpha of it (q . n = 1 on a sphere: -omega / R). Empty: prescribed_g_om None. The vibration-mode rows are computed as usual.

#### `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.axis_x`

solid_mechanics_3d with em_fdfd_bor optics: x of the 3D point (axis_x, axis_y, 0) the body-of-revolution axis passes through, parallel to z; the optical drawing (r, z) = (x - its x_lo edge, y) maps to (axis_x + r cos phi, axis_y + r sin phi, z), and q . n is averaged over 64 ring angles.

#### `solid_mechanics.electrode.connection`

voltage: phi = voltage on every node of the electrode (0 = ground; the eigenfrequency study holds it at 0: short circuit, the resonance frequencies). floating: one shared, unknown potential carrying the net free charge of the charge setting (0 = an isolated electrode; the eigenfrequency study uses 0: open circuit, the antiresonance frequencies). At least one voltage electrode is required (the reference of phi).

#### `solid_mechanics.electrode.voltage`

Potential of a voltage electrode in a static (stationary or time-dependent) solve; ignored by floating electrodes and by the eigenfrequency study (0 there).

#### `solid_mechanics.electrode.charge`

Net free charge per m of depth on a floating electrode in a static solve (its voltage follows); ignored by voltage electrodes and by the eigenfrequency study (0 there).

#### `solid_mechanics.admittance`

frequency_response study, piezoelectric only. Result 'xy' versus frequency [Hz] of Y = I / V = j omega Q / V of the electrode (Q = the complex charge, the discrete Gauss law of D including the dielectric loss): series abs, re, im, phase, bvd_abs (|Y|, Re Y, Im Y in S/m per m of depth, or S with the thickness setting and in solid_mechanics_3d; phase in deg; bvd_abs = |Y| of the fitted model, NaN without a fit). Extras (derived values read them with operation last): the Butterworth-Van Dyke fit Y = j omega C0 (1 - j tan_delta_0) + 1 / (R1 + j omega L1 + 1 / (j omega C1)) over the fit band (least squares on the relative complex residual from a closed-form start: f_s = the sample of max |Y|, f_p = the sample of min |Y| above it): f_s, f_p, k_eff2, Q_s, C0, C1, L1, R1, tan_delta_0, f_peak, f_dip, fit_error, fit_points (f_s = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L1 C1)), f_p = f_s sqrt(1 + C1 / C0) the lossless antiresonance, k_eff2 = (f_p^2 - f_s^2) / f_p^2 = C1 / (C0 + C1), Q_s = 2 pi f_s L1 / R1, f_peak / f_dip the sampled max / min of |Y|, fit_error the rms relative residual), kappa_e = load_impedance / L1 [rad/s] (the external coupling rate into a resistive load in series with the motional branch, internal R1 / L1 = 2 pi f_s / Q_s) and omega_C0_Z = 2 pi f_s C0 load_impedance (kappa_e holds while it is << 1; both NaN per m of depth, kappa_e_warning), load_impedance, bvd_units, electrode; when the band holds fewer than 6 points or no peak with a dip above it, the fit values are NaN and fit_warning says why. One resonance per band: resolve it with a step well below f_s / Q_s.

#### `solid_mechanics.admittance.electrode`

Name of the driven Electrode / Electrode (domain) feature (connection voltage, voltage != 0) whose admittance Y = I / V is reported; empty = the only voltage electrode with a non-zero voltage (an error when there are several).

#### `solid_mechanics.admittance.fit_frequency_min`

Lowest frequency of the Butterworth-Van Dyke fit; empty = the lowest solved frequency. Choose a band around one resonance / antiresonance pair (other modes in the band bias the fit).

#### `solid_mechanics.admittance.load_impedance`

Resistive load Z of the external circuit for the extra kappa_e = Z / L1 [rad/s], the energy decay rate the load adds to the fitted motional branch (valid while the extra omega_C0_Z = omega_s C0 Z << 1). Needs C0 / L1 in F / H: a 3D model, or the thickness setting in 2D (per m of depth kappa_e is NaN). Default 50 Ohm.

#### `solid_mechanics_3d.electrode.connection`

voltage: phi = voltage on every node of the electrode (0 = ground; the eigenfrequency study holds 0: short circuit, the resonance frequencies). floating: one shared, unknown potential carrying the net free charge of the charge setting (0 = an isolated electrode; the eigenfrequency study uses 0: open circuit, the antiresonance frequencies). resistive_load: one shared potential V tied to ground through load_resistance R, j omega Q = -V / R (exp(+j omega t)); eigenfrequency study (target_frequency > 0): damped complex modes, the Resonance table adds frequency_imag, q_factor and energy_decay_rate = 2 Im omega = kappa_e of a line of impedance R (the pencil is frozen at the target and each mode refined by Newton on its Rayleigh functional: exact for the mode on the target, second order for the others); frequency_response: the resistor loads the response of the driven electrode; static studies refuse it. At least one voltage electrode is required (the reference of phi).

#### `solid_mechanics_3d.electrode.voltage`

Potential of a voltage electrode in a static (stationary or time-dependent) solve; ignored by floating electrodes and by the eigenfrequency study (0 V).

#### `eigenfrequency.relaxation`

Relaxation w of the loop-back couplings (those writing a physics solved earlier in the iteration, e.g. heat_em_thermo_optic in an FDFD + heat loop): each injects previous + w (new - previous); 1 = plain Picard. For a loop gain g (about the ratio of successive relative changes, negative when the fields alternate) w ~ 1/(1 - g): w > 1 speeds a slow monotone loop (plain Picard needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) iterations), w < 1 damps an oscillating one (e.g. a thermo-optic shift past a resonance). Nothing cures a physical runaway (monotone g > 1). The relative change compared with the tolerance is divided by w. With anderson_depth > 0 it is the Anderson mixing parameter instead (the change is then divided by w only when w < 1).

#### `eigenfrequency.warm_start`

Parameter sweeps only: start each sweep value from the previous value's solution when the mesh is unchanged (heat T and Q, potential V and its source, magnetic potentials; the couplings reading only these are applied first), which cuts coupling iterations and CG iterations. drift_diffusion ramps its contact / gate voltages and generation from the previous value's converged state instead of from equilibrium (an I-V sweep then takes about one continuation step per value). A geometrically nonlinear solid (solid_mechanics on triangles, solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra) starts its Newton solve from the displacement of the previous value, linearly extrapolated in the swept parameter from the last two values (at most one previous step ahead), and ramps its load_steps from that state's loads and held values; a start that does not converge falls back to the cold ramp from u = 0. Results then differ from a cold start within the tolerance; off, every value starts cold (T0, V = 0, u = 0) and is reproducible on its own.

#### `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

Symmetry 2.6: run the study once per symmetric / antisymmetric combination of the model's mirror faces (2^k sector runs for k faces with a bc_<face> symmetric / antisymmetric or a membrane symmetry / antisymmetry face feature, swapped per sector; each solves the drawn sources plus their images on the drawn half (quarter, ...) at that parity) and merge them. stationary / frequency_domain / time_dependent / frequency_response: the response of the drawn sources alone (no images) on the unfolded domain: per stored snapshot one combined snapshot (its label, 'combined' for a stationary one) holding the mean of the unfolded sector fields of every linear signed stored field (Re / Im phasors, raw components such as the FDTD E_z; |E|, intensities, losses and phases are left out), then the unfolded sector snapshots labelled '<label> [<sector>]'; derived values are combined by their form: integrals / means quadratic in the fields (power, flux, absorbed power, intensity, w_re^2 + w_im^2 over regions and surfaces symmetric about every mirror plane) as quadratic totals, mean / 2^k; integrals, means and point values linear in signed fields (Re / Im phasors, raw components) as the sector mean; feature-sourced values from the combined feature results below; values of earlier derived values and parameters only, such as ratios, are re-evaluated from the combined ones; anything else (max / min, mode volumes, phases, scalar outputs) is NaN with a warning; far_field results combined per angle (the mean of the complex amplitudes) and flux_spectrum results whose line / plane / box reaches every mirror plane (quadratic totals), membrane field_probe phasors (the sector mean) and port / mode_projection guide modes (renumbered to the unfolded guide: a free mirror wall gives modes 2k - 1, a held one 2k; amplitudes the signed sector mean, port powers and fractions recomputed from them) are stored with the run: Results.sector_result(physics, feature, combined=True). A membrane port incident mode on a guide ending on a mirror face is driven at twice its amplitude in the sector of its parity only. The combination assumes a linear model: couplings out of the wave physics (Joule heat, thermo-optic shifts) see each sector's own field, so their combined values are not the drawn source's (validation warns). mode_analysis / eigenfrequency: the modes or resonances of every sector, sector by sector, labelled with their parity ('mode k [x_lo symmetric]: ...'); derived values NaN. Every run: per-sector derived values and result digests in summary parity_sectors (labels, derived, results, combined_results, snapshot_sectors), the feature results per sector by Results.sector_result; the live state (Results.field, feature results) is the last sector, the one with the model's own mirror signs. With a parameter sweep every sweep value runs its sectors (cold starts): sweep derived = the combined values per value, sweep results = the last sector's, sweep sector_derived the per-sector values, parity_sectors the last value's. Needs a mirror face.

## Physics type `drift_diffusion` - Semiconductor (drift-diffusion, 2D)

2D stationary drift-diffusion per unit z length, or of a body of revolution (setting geometry axisymmetric: x = r from the x_lo window edge, whole-ring contact currents and gate charges), on the physical window (finite volumes): Poisson -div(eps0 eps_dc grad psi) = q (p - n + N_D - N_A) and the steady electron / hole continuity div J_n = q (R - G), div J_p = q (G - R) with Scharfetter-Gummel face currents (exact for an exponential carrier profile between cell centres; D = mu V_T, Boltzmann statistics), solved fully coupled by Newton (sparse direct solves of the unsymmetric Jacobian by the linear solver role, Automatic = sparse_direct) in scaled variables, potential updates log-damped. psi (output V) is the electrostatic potential referred to the intrinsic level, with the equilibrium Fermi level at 0 V: in neutral n-type silicon at 1e22 1/m^3 V = V_T asinh(N_D / 2 n_i) = +0.36 V, at an ohmic contact V = that value plus the contact voltage. Cells with n_intrinsic > 0 are semiconductor; the others are insulators (Poisson only, eps_dc, no carriers, e.g. an oxide or the air). Outer faces are insulating (zero normal D and current). Doping comes from doping features (they add), contacts and gates from ohmic_contact / gate features (at least one ohmic contact); recombination is SRH with a mid-gap trap (lifetime_n / _p) plus radiative (B) plus Auger (auger_recombination features: (C_n n + C_p p) (n p - n_i^2)); generation is the sum of the generation features and the coupled slot generation (em_semiconductor_generation: G = absorbed optical power / photon energy). Each solve continues from the last solution, ramping every applied voltage (at most max_bias_step per step) and the generation, the first one from equilibrium (nonlinear Poisson at 0 V); a step that fails is halved, and a solve that cannot converge raises. Outputs: V, N, P, E, the Scharfetter-Gummel currents J (= Jn + Jp; face currents averaged to the cell centres, outer faces counting 0), the quasi-Fermi potentials phi_n = V - V_T ln(N / n_i), phi_p = V + V_T ln(P / n_i), net doping, space charge q (P - N + N_D - N_A) and the net recombination R (0 in contacts and insulators), all copied edge-extended into an EM PML ring. The contact currents are exact face sums (table results); the electron currents into all contacts sum to q times the integral of G - R. Coupling to optics: semiconductor_em_plasma_dispersion (free carriers -> EM index, an E13 index contributor) and em_semiconductor_generation (EM absorption -> G); a stationary study iterates them with the EM solve. LIMITS: homojunctions (no band offsets, no heterojunctions), constant mobilities (an expression may make them field- or state-dependent), no Fermi-Dirac statistics or incomplete ionisation, no transient (the time-dependent study re-solves the steady state when an input changed). The window needs about 1-3 cells per Debye length near junctions (Debye length sqrt(eps V_T / (q N)): 13 nm at 1e23 1/m^3). The instance is usually named semiconductor. On a triangle mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles; planar or axisymmetric) it is the box method on the linear (P1) nodes of the window elements: each mesh edge carries the Scharfetter-Gummel current with the coefficient sum of its two elements (cot / 2 edge weight of the linear stiffness times eps or mobility: edge-averaged finite elements), control volumes are the lumped node shares; curved outlines are faceted at the nodes. Doping, contacts, gates and generation select elements: a node takes the volume-weighted mean of its semiconductor elements (a pn junction on element edges has mixed doping at its nodes), an ohmic contact holds every node of its semiconductor elements, a gate every node of its elements (potential only, an ordinary edge conductance; no current enters); generation acts on the free semiconductor elements. V, N, P and the quasi-Fermi potentials are nodal fields (linear across an insulator element next to the semiconductor), E is -grad V per element and J the least-squares vector of the element's own edge currents; every state slot holds one value per element (centroid means, carriers 0 in insulators). Mesh edges with a negative coefficient (non-Delaunay, e.g. an obtuse triangle at a material interface) are reported once as a run warning. Linear solver host SuperLU or cuDSS (back_end 'cusolver_qr' needs a tensor mesh); Automatic is cuDSS on the GPU backend with nvmath-python (a Jacobian cuDSS refuses switches the run to host SuperLU for good, with a warning), else host SuperLU. A sparse_direct node with back_end 'cudss' / 'cudss_mixed' (GPU backend, nvmath-python) factorises every Newton Jacobian on the GPU as a real LU, reusing the cuDSS plan (ordering and symbolic phase) across Newton iterations and continuation steps while the contacts, gates and insulator cells stay the same; cudss_mixed factorises in single precision with float64 refinement and falls back to double when that misses 1e-12.

- PhysicsSpec.type `drift_diffusion`; default instance name `semiconductor`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): V
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `drift_diffusion.<feature>`): doping, ohmic_contact, gate, auger_recombination, generation

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "planar"; choices planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: 2D drift-diffusion per unit z length (contact currents A/m, gate charges C/m). axisymmetric: a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z): (r, z) drift-diffusion; every Poisson conductance, Scharfetter-Gummel face coefficient, face and cell volume is weighted by 2 pi r (x-faces at their own r, y-faces and volumes at the cell-centre r; 2 pi r_c dr dz is the exact ring volume), so densities and rates (N, P 1/m^3, J A/m^2, generation and recombination 1/(m^3 s)) keep their units, while contact currents and gate charges (table results, scalar outputs current_ / charge_<feature>) are those of the whole ring in A and C (a resistance V / I in Ohm, a capacitance Q / V in F). x_lo is the axis (r = 0: symmetry, no radial current or D flux, like the insulating outer faces). Field derived values of the whole model are weighted by the ring volume 2 pi r dx dy ('integral' a whole-body total, 'mean' a volume mean; also for fields of other physics). A coupled physics that is planar (its type has no geometry setting, e.g. EM, or it is set to planar) solves the drawing as a planar cut per unit z length, so its fields are applied per cell as rings (validation warns); a partner with geometry axisymmetric too is consistent.
- `temperature` (float; unit K; default 300; range (0, inf)) - Temperature
  Lattice temperature setting the thermal voltage V_T = k_B T / q (25.85 mV at 300 K) of the Einstein relation D = mu V_T and the Boltzmann statistics. n_intrinsic is NOT rescaled with it: give a temperature-dependent n_intrinsic yourself (it may depend on heat_T). Default 300 K, the temperature of the library semiconductor data (silicon n_intrinsic 1e16 1/m^3), deliberately not heat T0 (293.15 K, where the optical indices apply): with a heat physics in the model set both to the same value (one parameter) if they should agree.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-08; range (0, inf)) - Newton tolerance
  Newton stops when the largest potential update is <= tolerance * V_T and the largest carrier update |dn| / (n + n_i) (holes alike) is <= tolerance over the free unknowns; quadratic convergence makes the final error far smaller. 1e-8 suits float64.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf)) - Newton iteration limit
  Newton iterations per continuation step (and for the equilibrium start); a step that does not converge is halved, down to 1/64 of the first step, then the solve fails (run error).
- `max_bias_step` (float; unit V; default 0.1; range (0, inf)) - Largest bias step
  Largest change of any contact or gate voltage per continuation step (the solve ramps every applied voltage and the generation from the previous solution, the first time from equilibrium at 0 V); about 4 V_T keeps Newton safe for forward-biased junctions.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_dc` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_xx, eps_dc_yy) - Static relative permittivity
  Isotropic static relative permittivity (>= 1) of the Poisson equation: sets eps_dc_xx and eps_dc_yy (component entries override it); unset = 1. Silicon 11.7, silica 3.9.
- `eps_dc_xx` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_xx) - Static relative permittivity along x
  Static relative permittivity along x (>= 1); overrides eps_dc for this axis.
- `eps_dc_yy` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_yy) - Static relative permittivity along y
  Static relative permittivity along y (>= 1); overrides eps_dc for this axis.
- `n_intrinsic` (float; unit 1/m^3; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays n_intrinsic) - Intrinsic carrier density
  Intrinsic carrier density n_i [1/m^3]: cells with n_i > 0 are semiconductor (Poisson + carriers), the rest insulators (Poisson only, no carriers). Silicon 1.0e16 at 300 K (1e10 cm^-3), GaAs 2.1e12, germanium 2.0e19. Homojunctions only: one band structure, no heterojunction band offsets.
- `mobility_n` (float; unit m^2/(V s); range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mobility_n) - Electron mobility
  Electron mobility [m^2/(V s)], constant (no doping or field dependence; give an expression for that). Lightly doped silicon 0.135 (1350 cm^2/Vs), at 1e24 1/m^3 ~0.03.
- `mobility_p` (float; unit m^2/(V s); range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mobility_p) - Hole mobility
  Hole mobility [m^2/(V s)], constant. Lightly doped silicon 0.048 (480 cm^2/Vs).
- `lifetime` (float; unit s; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays lifetime_n, lifetime_p) - Carrier lifetime
  Shockley-Read-Hall lifetime (mid-gap trap) of both carriers: sets lifetime_n and lifetime_p; unset = 1e-6 s. Silicon 1e-9 (heavily doped) .. 1e-3 (float zone).
- `lifetime_n` (float; unit s; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays lifetime_n) - Electron lifetime
  SRH electron lifetime tau_n [s]; overrides lifetime.
- `lifetime_p` (float; unit s; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays lifetime_p) - Hole lifetime
  SRH hole lifetime tau_p [s]; overrides lifetime.
- `radiative_recombination` (float; unit m^3/s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays radiative_recombination) - Radiative recombination coefficient
  Band-to-band coefficient B [m^3/s] of R_rad = B (n p - n_i^2); unset = 0. Silicon 1.1e-20, GaAs 7.2e-16.

### Fields

State fields:
- `V` - Electric potential (V)
- `N` - Electron density (1/m^3)
- `P` - Hole density (1/m^3)
- `E_x` - Electric field x (V/m)
- `E_y` - Electric field y (V/m)
- `J_x` - Current density x (A/m^2)
- `J_y` - Current density y (A/m^2)
- `Jn_x` - Electron current density x (A/m^2)
- `Jn_y` - Electron current density y (A/m^2)
- `Jp_x` - Hole current density x (A/m^2)
- `Jp_y` - Hole current density y (A/m^2)
- `phi_n` - Electron quasi-Fermi potential (V)
- `phi_p` - Hole quasi-Fermi potential (V)
- `net_doping` - Net doping (1/m^3)
- `space_charge` - Space charge density (C/m^3)
- `recombination` - Net recombination rate (1/(m^3 s))
- `generation` - Coupled generation rate (1/(m^3 s))
- `generation_ext` - Applied generation rate (1/(m^3 s))

Output fields (primary V):
- `V` - Electric potential (V)
- `N` - Electron density (1/m^3)
- `P` - Hole density (1/m^3)
- `E_x` - Electric field x (V/m)
- `E_y` - Electric field y (V/m)
- `J_x` - Current density x (A/m^2)
- `J_y` - Current density y (A/m^2)
- `Jn_x` - Electron current density x (A/m^2)
- `Jn_y` - Electron current density y (A/m^2)
- `Jp_x` - Hole current density x (A/m^2)
- `Jp_y` - Hole current density y (A/m^2)
- `phi_n` - Electron quasi-Fermi potential (V)
- `phi_p` - Hole quasi-Fermi potential (V)
- `net_doping` - Net doping (1/m^3)
- `space_charge` - Space charge density (C/m^3)
- `recombination` - Net recombination rate (1/(m^3 s))
- `generation` - Coupled generation rate (1/(m^3 s))
- `generation_ext` - Applied generation rate (1/(m^3 s))

Scalar outputs: current_<contact> (A/m) per enabled ohmic_contact feature: its total current (electron + hole) per m of depth of the last solve, as the contact table result (positive = conventional current leaving the contact into the device); charge_<gate> (C/m) per enabled gate feature: its free charge per m of depth, as the gate table result; with geometry 'axisymmetric' both are whole-ring values in A and C. Example derived value {"name": "I_anode", "expression": "semiconductor_current_anode"} (operation mean of a constant is the value itself); a parameter sweep of a contact voltage then gives the I-V curve (with the sweep setting reuse_build the build is kept and each point continues from the previous converged state).

### Source slots

- `generation` (1/(m^3 s)): Coupled electron-hole pair generation rate (field generation, written by em_semiconductor_generation), added to the generation features (field generation_ext); acts on the free semiconductor cells only.

### Feature `drift_diffusion.doping` - Doping

Adds N_D - N_A to the net doping of the selected cells (several features add; fully ionised; ignored in insulating cells). A step between two features at a rectangle edge is an abrupt junction on a cell edge (triangle meshes: on element edges, the nodes there take the mean of both sides).

- FeatureSpec.type `doping`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `donors` (float; unit 1/m^3; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y) - Donor density
  Ionised donor density N_D [1/m^3] (1e22 = 1e16 cm^-3); may depend on x, y (e.g. a Gaussian implant profile).
- `acceptors` (float; unit 1/m^3; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y) - Acceptor density
  Ionised acceptor density N_A [1/m^3]; may depend on x, y.

### Feature `drift_diffusion.ohmic_contact` - Ohmic contact

Holds every selected semiconductor cell (n_intrinsic > 0; other selected cells stay ordinary insulators) at charge-neutral equilibrium with its own doping, shifted by the voltage: n p = n_i^2, n - p = N_D - N_A, V = voltage + V_T asinh((N_D - N_A) / 2 n_i). The held values sit at the cell centres, so the voltage drop starts at the centres of the outermost held cells. A later contact or gate takes shared cells (validation warns on possible overlaps). At least one ohmic contact is required. Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, voltage, current, electron_current, hole_current] (units '', V, A/m, A/m, A/m; A with geometry axisymmetric) and the same extras: the current per m of depth (the whole ring when axisymmetric) flowing out of the contact into the device (positive = conventional current leaving the contact), summed over the Scharfetter-Gummel face currents between its held cells and their neighbours (float64, from the converged state; on a triangle mesh plus the net generation in the held nodes' control volumes, i.e. the current through the contact outline).

- FeatureSpec.type `ohmic_contact`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `voltage` (float; unit V; default 0) - Voltage
  Applied voltage of the contact [V] (the Fermi level of its cells sits at -voltage in energy, so the contact potential is V = voltage + V_T asinh(net doping / 2 n_i)).

### Feature `drift_diffusion.gate` - Gate

Holds the potential of every selected cell at voltage - work_function_difference (an ideal conductor: the value sits on its faces toward the other cells, half-cell conductance 2 eps0 eps_dc / dx of the neighbour). The cells must be insulating (n_intrinsic 0; run error otherwise): put the gate on an oxide. No current flows into a gate. Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, voltage, charge] (units '', V, C/m; C with geometry axisymmetric) and the extras voltage and charge: the free charge per m of depth (the whole ring when axisymmetric) on the gate, its outward D flux (Gauss).

- FeatureSpec.type `gate`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `voltage` (float; unit V; default 0) - Voltage
  Applied gate voltage [V]; a reused sweep build (sweep reuse_build) follows it without rebuilding.
- `work_function_difference` (float; unit V; default 0) - Work-function difference
  phi_ms [V]: gate work function minus the intrinsic-level work function of the semiconductor (electron affinity + E_g / 2 q); the held potential is V = voltage - phi_ms. 0 = a mid-gap gate; n+ polysilicon on silicon ~ -0.56, p+ ~ +0.56. Referred to the intrinsic level, not the Fermi level: the flat-band voltage is phi_ms + V_bulk with V_bulk = V_T asinh(net doping / 2 n_i) (p-type silicon at N_A = 1e23 1/m^3: V_bulk = -0.42 V), and the textbook work-function difference (to the Fermi level) is phi_ms + V_bulk.

### Feature `drift_diffusion.auger_recombination` - Auger recombination

Sets the Auger coefficients of the selected semiconductor cells (a later feature takes shared cells; unselected cells have none): R_Auger = (C_n N + C_p P) (N P - n_i^2) adds to the SRH and radiative recombination (output recombination, the continuity rows and the contact currents). The coefficients are float64 constants (about 1e-43 m^6/s: a float32 subnormal, so they are no material property). On a triangle mesh a node takes the semiconductor-volume mean of its elements.

- FeatureSpec.type `auger_recombination`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `electron_coefficient` (float; unit m^6/s; default 2.8e-43; range [0, inf)) - Electron Auger coefficient
  C_n [m^6/s] of R_Auger = (C_n n + C_p p) (n p - n_i^2) (eeh process); silicon 2.8e-43 (2.8e-31 cm^6/s), GaAs ~1e-42. A constant per feature (no x, y dependence): kept in float64 outside the material grid.
- `hole_coefficient` (float; unit m^6/s; default 9.9e-44; range [0, inf)) - Hole Auger coefficient
  C_p [m^6/s] (ehh process); silicon 9.9e-44 (9.9e-32 cm^6/s).

### Feature `drift_diffusion.generation` - Generation

Adds the rate to generation_ext on the selected cells (several features add); it acts on the free semiconductor cells only. The coupled slot generation (from an EM physics) adds to it.

- FeatureSpec.type `generation`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `rate` (float; unit 1/(m^3 s); default 1e+27; range [0, inf); may use x, y) - Generation rate
  Electron-hole pair generation rate [1/(m^3 s)]; may depend on x, y (e.g. G0 * exp(-alpha * (y0 - y)) for light entering from the top). 1 W/m^2 absorbed at 1.55 um is 7.8e18 pairs / (m^2 s).

## Physics type `elastic_waves` - Elastic and Acoustic Waves, time domain (2D, in-plane)

2D velocity-stress finite-difference time-domain solver (Virieux staggered grid, plane strain, in-plane motion; or axisymmetric (r, z) with the hoop stress, setting geometry): vx / vy [m/s] on the +x / +y cell faces at half steps, sxx / syy [Pa] at the cell centres and sxy on the +x +y cell corners, tension positive, pressure = -(sxx + syy) / 2 (the pressure of a fluid). Fluids (shear_speed unset) and isotropic (sound_speed / shear_speed, or the youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio of solid_mechanics and the library solids), in-plane orthotropic (c11, c12, c22, c66) or monoclinic solids (+ c16, c26: a rotated crystal, the energy-conserving corner / centre averages of the shear coupling) share one grid; a face takes the width-weighted mean density of its two cells, a corner the harmonic mean of the four shear moduli (0 at fluid-solid and vacuum corners), so interfaces need no special treatment and vacuum cells (no density, no stiffness) give traction-free surfaces; the effective stiffness must be positive definite. dt = courant x the stability limit of the staggered grid (anisotropic c_ij included, see courant) derived from the materials at the build (the physics sets dt_sync when alone; with another time-stepping physics the shorter step wins). Boundaries per face: absorbing (CPML in the outermost pml_cells cells of the grid, inside the domain unless an EM physics pads it), rigid (slip wall) or periodic. Sources: point force, point volume source, traction sheet on a line, thermoelastic heating pulse, and the coupled heating_power slot; probes record pressure, stresses or velocities, and the resonance finder fits their ring-down (frequency band). Use a uniform or nonuniform mesh (auto mode meshes by the optical index). The state fields (pressure, stresses, velocities) can drive a state-dependent material property or a field_transfer of another time-stepped physics. elastic_strain_xx / _yy = the in-plane stiffness inverted on the centre stresses (fluids: half the volumetric strain each; thermoelastic stress counts as minus the thermal strain). Optics: acoustics_em_acousto_optic (photoelastic index of an em_fdfd_* physics that re-solves on the frozen strain every k acoustic steps; isotropic photoelastic_p11 / _p12, or the in-plane tensor photoelastic_p16 .. _p66 of a crystal with the centre shear strain, which also drives the eps_xy of em_fdfd_hz) and em_acoustics_photoacoustic (absorbed light power of an em_fdfd_* physics into the heating_power slot). Piezoelectric: piezo_e* material arrays (usually from a crystal entry) and electrostatics_acoustics_piezo (the stress -e^T E of the electrostatics field; two-way by default: the bound charge -div(e S) of the accumulated strain re-solves the electrostatics after every step, so the waves are piezoelectrically stiffened and dt uses c^D); with piezo or c16 / c26 arrays elastic_strain_xx / _yy are the accumulated total strain (also what acoustics_em_acousto_optic sees; thermoelastic heating then shows as expansion, not as minus the thermal strain). geometry axisymmetric adds the output field and probe component stt (hoop stress). Stepper solver (role stepper, explicit_kernels): precision single, or half_storage = the fields stored as fp16 (10 B per cell less, ~1e-3 relative noise floor) in units scaled from the peak stress of the sources and heating pulses (stress) and the largest impedance (velocity), read back in Pa and m/s; half_storage refuses the resonance finder, piezoelectric and monoclinic (c16 / c26) materials and every coupling into this physics (heating_power, electric fields). Runs on the gpu and cpu backends (cpu: numpy twins of every kernel, numba for the velocity / stress updates when installed, single precision only, several times slower: small 2D models and tests).

- PhysicsSpec.type `elastic_waves`; default instance name `acoustics`
- Supported studies: time_dependent
- Default study: {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 2e-05}}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): pressure
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `elastic_waves.<feature>`): force_source, volume_source, traction_line_source, heat_pulse_source, rigid_domain, initial_velocity, field_probe, resonance_monitor

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "planar"; choices planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: plane strain per unit z length (point forces N/m, volume rates m^2/s). axisymmetric: a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z): (r, z) waves without torsion (v_phi = 0). The hoop stress s_tt is stepped too, with c_tt = c11 and c_rt = c_zt = c12 (exact for isotropic solids and fluids, an approximation for c_ij crystals: validation warns); the velocity updates use the ring-volume forms (1/r) d(r s_rr)/dr - s_tt / r and (1/r) d(r s_rz)/dr, an x-face density is the ring-volume mean of its two cells; the stiffness must be positive definite in 3D (isotropic: shear_speed < 0.866 sound_speed). Point forces and volume rates are per unit length of the ring the point stands for (the ring total is 2 pi r_c times it; a point in the axis cell is a ring of radius dx / 2), traction sheets per area (a vertical line is a cylinder, a horizontal one a disc or annulus), pressure = -(s_rr + s_zz + s_tt) / 3, the hoop stress is the output field stt and a probe component, and the stable step is a few % shorter (see courant). An absorbing x_hi stretches the radial derivatives only (the hoop terms are not stretched). x_lo is the axis (r = 0: symmetry, bc_x_lo must be rigid there, and no other physics may pad the grid at x_lo; validation errors otherwise). Field derived values of the whole model are weighted by the ring volume 2 pi r dx dy ('integral' a whole-body total, 'mean' a volume mean; also for fields of other physics). A coupled physics that is planar (its type has no geometry setting, e.g. EM, or it is set to planar) solves the drawing as a planar cut per unit z length, so its fields are applied per cell as rings (validation warns); a partner with geometry axisymmetric too is consistent.
- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "absorbing"; choices absorbing | rigid | periodic) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  absorbing: a CPML layer in the outermost pml_cells cells of the grid, backed by a rigid wall; those cells lie inside the domain unless another physics (an EM CPML) pads the grid there, so keep sources, probes and objects of interest out of them (validation warns). rigid: a slip wall on the domain edge (normal velocity and shear stress 0: the rigid wall of a fluid, a frictionless wall of a solid, and also a mirror symmetry plane), also where another physics pads the grid (the padding cells behind it stay idle). periodic: wraps to the opposite face (set both faces of the axis; an error where another physics pads the grid, since the period would include the padding). A traction-free (vacuum) surface is a material boundary instead: cells without density and stiffness are vacuum. geometry axisymmetric: bc_x_lo must be rigid, which is the axis condition (v_r = 0, s_rz = 0); a rigid x_hi is a slip wall on the cylinder r = r_max, an absorbing one a radial CPML.
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 20; range [2, inf)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Cells of each absorbing layer (CPML, polynomial grading of order 2, kappa 1); typically 10-30, about one wavelength or more at the lowest frequency of interest.
- `pml_reflection` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, 0.5]) - Absorbing layer reflection
  Target normal-incidence reflection R of the CPML: peak damping d0 = 3 c ln(1 / R) / (2 L), c the largest longitudinal speed of the grid, L the layer thickness. 1e-3..1e-6 typical; thin layers with very small R reflect from their own grading.
- `courant` (float; unit 1; default 0.9; range (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  dt = courant / (c_bound sqrt(1 / dx_min^2 + 1 / dy_min^2)), c_bound^2 = the largest stability stiffness S of a cell times the largest 1 / rho of its faces (a face density is the mean of its two cells, so a solid next to vacuum has rho / 2 there), derived from the materials at the build. S = the largest eigenvalue of [[c11 wx + c66 wy, |c12 + c66| sqrt(wx wy)], [same, c66 wx + c22 wy]], wx = (1 / dx_min^2) / (1 / dx_min^2 + 1 / dy_min^2), wy = 1 - wx, and at least max(c11, c22): c11 for isotropic solids and fluids, more for anisotropic crystals (silicon along [100]: 194 GPa on square cells, not c11 = 166 GPa), so courant 1 is the exact limit of a uniform material. Monoclinic c16 / c26 enter by absolute value (diagonals + 2 |c16| s, + 2 |c26| s, off-diagonal + |c16| wx + |c26| wy, s = sqrt(wx wy)): a bound, so dt is shorter than the exact limit (~2 % for YZ lithium niobate, ~8 % with c16 / c26 of 10 % of c11). With the two-way piezoelectric coupling (electrostatics_acoustics_piezo, back_action bound_charge) S is that of the stiffened c^D = c^E + e^T (eps0 eps_dc)^-1 e, its c16 / c26 added to the material ones before the absolute value (a bound: the grid-scale stiffening is smaller). geometry axisymmetric: 1 / dx_min^2 is multiplied by F >= 1, the largest ratio of the Gershgorin bounds of the radial (r, z) and planar operators (~1.047 on uniform cells, from the cells next to the axis); a bound, not the exact limit, so keep courant <= 0.95 there. Runtime material rewrites (state-dependent speeds) are not stability-checked: keep their speeds below the build values.
- `heating_envelope` (choice; default "instantaneous"; choices instantaneous | gaussian) - Coupled heating envelope
  Time dependence of the coupled 'heating_power' slot: instantaneous = the delivered array is the heating rate itself (held until the next transfer); gaussian = the array (e.g. a cw absorbed power map) times exp(-((t - heating_pulse_delay) / heating_pulse_width)^2), a laser pulse of energy density array x sqrt(pi) width.
- `heating_pulse_width` (float; unit s; default 1e-08; range (0, inf); visible when heating_envelope in (gaussian)) - Heating pulse width
  1/e half-width w of the gaussian heating envelope; the pressure rise resolves only if c w spans a few cells.
- `heating_pulse_delay` (float; unit s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when heating_envelope in (gaussian)) - Heating pulse delay
  Centre time of the gaussian heating envelope; empty = 3 x heating_pulse_width.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `rho` (float; unit kg/m^3; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays rho) - Density
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.rho`
- `sound_speed` (float; unit m/s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sound_speed) - Sound speed (longitudinal)
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.sound_speed`
- `shear_speed` (float; unit m/s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays shear_speed) - Shear speed
  Transverse (shear, S) wave speed: c66 = rho shear_speed^2 and c12 = rho (sound_speed^2 - 2 shear_speed^2) unless the c_ij entries are set; unset = 0 = a fluid (no shear stress). Must be below sound_speed. Typical: silica 3760, aluminium 3040, silicon ~5840.
- `c11` (float; unit Pa; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays c11) - Stiffness c11
  In-plane plane-strain stiffness component c11 [Pa] (Voigt, x = 1, y = 2, xy = 6); overrides the value derived from sound_speed / shear_speed and rho (or from youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio). Isotropic: c11 = c22 = lambda + 2 mu, c12 = lambda, c66 = mu (Lame constants); silicon along [100] / [010]: c11 = c22 = 165.7e9, c12 = 63.9e9, c66 = 79.6e9. The effective set, with c16 / c26, must be positive definite (c11 > 0, c22 > 0, c66 > 0, c12^2 < c11 c22 and det [[c11, c12, c16], [c12, c22, c26], [c16, c26, c66]] > 0; a fluid: c66 = c16 = c26 = 0, c12 = c11 = c22), else validation errors.
- `c12` (float; unit Pa; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays c12) - Stiffness c12
  In-plane plane-strain stiffness component c12 [Pa] (Voigt, x = 1, y = 2, xy = 6); overrides the value derived from sound_speed / shear_speed and rho (or from youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio). Isotropic: c11 = c22 = lambda + 2 mu, c12 = lambda, c66 = mu (Lame constants); silicon along [100] / [010]: c11 = c22 = 165.7e9, c12 = 63.9e9, c66 = 79.6e9. The effective set, with c16 / c26, must be positive definite (c11 > 0, c22 > 0, c66 > 0, c12^2 < c11 c22 and det [[c11, c12, c16], [c12, c22, c26], [c16, c26, c66]] > 0; a fluid: c66 = c16 = c26 = 0, c12 = c11 = c22), else validation errors.
- `c22` (float; unit Pa; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays c22) - Stiffness c22
  In-plane plane-strain stiffness component c22 [Pa] (Voigt, x = 1, y = 2, xy = 6); overrides the value derived from sound_speed / shear_speed and rho (or from youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio). Isotropic: c11 = c22 = lambda + 2 mu, c12 = lambda, c66 = mu (Lame constants); silicon along [100] / [010]: c11 = c22 = 165.7e9, c12 = 63.9e9, c66 = 79.6e9. The effective set, with c16 / c26, must be positive definite (c11 > 0, c22 > 0, c66 > 0, c12^2 < c11 c22 and det [[c11, c12, c16], [c12, c22, c26], [c16, c26, c66]] > 0; a fluid: c66 = c16 = c26 = 0, c12 = c11 = c22), else validation errors.
- `c66` (float; unit Pa; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays c66) - Stiffness c66
  In-plane plane-strain stiffness component c66 [Pa] (Voigt, x = 1, y = 2, xy = 6); overrides the value derived from sound_speed / shear_speed and rho (or from youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio). Isotropic: c11 = c22 = lambda + 2 mu, c12 = lambda, c66 = mu (Lame constants); silicon along [100] / [010]: c11 = c22 = 165.7e9, c12 = 63.9e9, c66 = 79.6e9. The effective set, with c16 / c26, must be positive definite (c11 > 0, c22 > 0, c66 > 0, c12^2 < c11 c22 and det [[c11, c12, c16], [c12, c22, c26], [c16, c26, c66]] > 0; a fluid: c66 = c16 = c26 = 0, c12 = c11 = c22), else validation errors.
- `c16` (float; unit Pa; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays c16) - Stiffness c16
  In-plane monoclinic stiffness c16 [Pa] (Voigt: T_xx = c11 S_xx + c12 S_yy + c16 g, T_yy = c12 S_xx + c22 S_yy + c26 g, T_xy = c16 S_xx + c26 S_yy + c66 g, g = 2 S_xy the engineering shear); default 0 (no value from the speeds or E / nu). Non-zero when the model axes are not crystal symmetry axes in the plane, e.g. YZ lithium niobate c26 = c14 (a {'model': 'crystal'} entry sets both when either is non-zero). Staggered grid: a cell takes c16 / c26 x the mean shear rate of its 4 corners, a corner the mean of c16 S_xx + c26 S_yy over its 4 cells (an energy-conserving pair; corners without shear stiffness, at fluids, vacuum and slip walls, carry none). The set [[c11, c12, c16], [c12, c22, c26], [c16, c26, c66]] must be positive definite (a fluid: c16 = c26 = 0), else validation errors; dt takes |c16|, |c26| as bounds (see courant). Either one set allocates both arrays, the strain accumulator and three rate buffers (8 float32 grids); elastic_strain_xx / _yy then show the accumulated total strain. Planar geometry and single-precision stepper only. Absorbing layers (CPML) can be unstable in some strongly anisotropic media (Becache, Fauqueux and Joly 2003): check long runs for growth near the layers.
- `c26` (float; unit Pa; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays c26) - Stiffness c26
  In-plane monoclinic stiffness c26 [Pa] (Voigt: T_xx = c11 S_xx + c12 S_yy + c16 g, T_yy = c12 S_xx + c22 S_yy + c26 g, T_xy = c16 S_xx + c26 S_yy + c66 g, g = 2 S_xy the engineering shear); default 0 (no value from the speeds or E / nu). Non-zero when the model axes are not crystal symmetry axes in the plane, e.g. YZ lithium niobate c26 = c14 (a {'model': 'crystal'} entry sets both when either is non-zero). Staggered grid: a cell takes c16 / c26 x the mean shear rate of its 4 corners, a corner the mean of c16 S_xx + c26 S_yy over its 4 cells (an energy-conserving pair; corners without shear stiffness, at fluids, vacuum and slip walls, carry none). The set [[c11, c12, c16], [c12, c22, c26], [c16, c26, c66]] must be positive definite (a fluid: c16 = c26 = 0), else validation errors; dt takes |c16|, |c26| as bounds (see courant). Either one set allocates both arrays, the strain accumulator and three rate buffers (8 float32 grids); elastic_strain_xx / _yy then show the accumulated total strain. Planar geometry and single-precision stepper only. Absorbing layers (CPML) can be unstable in some strongly anisotropic media (Becache, Fauqueux and Joly 2003): check long runs for growth near the layers.
- `youngs_modulus` (float; unit Pa; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays youngs_modulus) - Young's modulus
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.youngs_modulus`
- `poisson_ratio` (float; unit 1; range (-1, 0.499]; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays poisson_ratio) - Poisson ratio
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.poisson_ratio`
- `acoustic_damping` (float; unit 1/s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays acoustic_damping) - Acoustic damping rate
  Mass-proportional damping g of the particle velocity (rho dv/dt = div s - rho g v, semi-implicit): a wave of angular frequency omega >> g decays as exp(-g t / 2). Default 0.
- `gruneisen` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays gruneisen) - Grueneisen parameter
  Thermoelastic (photoacoustic) Grueneisen parameter G = beta c^2 / cp (beta the volumetric expansion): a heating rate q [W/m^3] adds -G q to d(sxx)/dt and d(syy)/dt, so an instantly absorbed energy density H raises the pressure by G H. Read by heat_pulse_source and the 'heating_power' slot; default 0. Typical: water 0.11 at 20 C, soft tissue ~0.2.
- `photoelastic_p11` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays photoelastic_p11) - Photoelastic coefficient p11
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p11`
- `photoelastic_p12` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays photoelastic_p12) - Photoelastic coefficient p12
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p12`
- `photoelastic_p16` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays photoelastic_p16) - Photoelastic coefficient p16
  In-plane photoelastic tensor entry photoelastic_p16 [1] in model axes, read only by acoustics_em_acousto_optic: Delta(1/n^2)_I = p_I1 S_xx + p_I2 S_yy + p_I6 g with the index-ellipsoid row I = 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz (the diagonal permittivity slots) or 6 xy (the eps_xy slot of em_fdfd_hz: Delta eps_xy = -n0_xx^2 n0_yy^2 Delta(1/n^2)_xy) and g = 2 S_xy the engineering shear at the cell centre (the 4-corner mean); photoelastic_p11 / _p12 are p_11 / p_12 of row 1. Unset = 0 (the isotropic value). Usually set by a {'model': 'crystal'} entry (rotated crystal p, written only when the cut is not isotropic in these rows); YZ lithium niobate (model x = crystal Z, y = -Y): p11 = p33, p12 = p31, p16 = 0, p21 = p13, p22 = p11, p26 = p14, p31 = p13, p32 = p12, p36 = -p14, p61 = 0, p62 = p41, p66 = p44 (crystal constants). Any one set allocates all ten arrays (default unset).
