- `piezo_e11` (float; unit C/m^2; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays piezo_e11) - Piezoelectric e11
  Piezoelectric stress constant e_11 [C/m^2] of the in-plane block in model axes (reduced Voigt: D_k = e_kJ S_J + eps0 eps_dc E, T_J = c_JK S_K - e_kJ E_k with k = 1 x / 2 y and J = 1 xx, 2 yy, 6 xy, engineering shear S_6 = 2 S_xy); default 0. Read through electrostatics_acoustics_piezo: the stress -e^T E of the electrostatics field (electric_field_x / _y slots) and, two-way (default), the bound charge -div(e S) of the accumulated strain back into the electrostatics plus the stiffened time step. Usually set by a {'model': 'crystal'} entry of the material's dispersion list (rotated crystal data; it also sets the c_ij, rho and the clamped eps_dc_xx / _yy / _xy); YZ lithium niobate (euler_deg 0, 90, 90; model x = crystal Z, y = -Y) gives piezo_e11 = e33 = 1.3, piezo_e12 = e31 = 0.2, piezo_e22 = -e22 = -2.5, piezo_e26 = e15 = 3.7 (crystal constants). Any one set allocates all six arrays and the strain accumulator (9 float32 grids; elastic_strain_xx / _yy then show the accumulated total strain). Planar geometry only.

### Fields

State fields:
- `pressure` - Pressure (Pa)
- `sxx` - Normal stress xx (Pa)
- `syy` - Normal stress yy (Pa)
- `sxy` - Shear stress xy (Pa)
- `vx` - Particle velocity x (m/s)
- `vy` - Particle velocity y (m/s)

Output fields (primary pressure):
- `pressure` - Pressure (Pa)
- `sxx` - Normal stress xx (Pa)
- `syy` - Normal stress yy (Pa)
- `sxy` - Shear stress xy (Pa)
- `stt` - Hoop stress (axisymmetric) (Pa)
- `vx` - Particle velocity x (m/s)
- `vy` - Particle velocity y (m/s)
- `v_abs` - Particle speed |v| (m/s)
- `elastic_strain_xx` - Elastic strain xx (1)
- `elastic_strain_yy` - Elastic strain yy (1)

### Source slots

- `heating_power` (W/m^3): Coupled heating rate q (em_acoustics_photoacoustic contributions, summed, or one field_transfer from another physics), kept by reference; adds -gruneisen q x the heating_envelope to d(sxx)/dt and d(syy)/dt every step.
- `electric_field_x` (V/m): Coupled electric field x component at the cell centres (electrostatics_acoustics_piezo): each transfer adds -e^T (E - E_last) of this component to the stresses at once (sxx, syy at the centres; sxy at the corners from the 4-cell mean, not where the corner has no shear stiffness), so T = c S - e^T E with E of the transfer time; the field of the first transfer counts as already present (no stress: the initial state is the equilibrium of that field). Ignored without piezo_e* arrays.
- `electric_field_y` (V/m): Coupled electric field y component at the cell centres (electrostatics_acoustics_piezo): each transfer adds -e^T (E - E_last) of this component to the stresses at once (sxx, syy at the centres; sxy at the corners from the 4-cell mean, not where the corner has no shear stiffness), so T = c S - e^T E with E of the transfer time; the field of the first transfer counts as already present (no stress: the initial state is the equilibrium of that field). Ignored without piezo_e* arrays.

### Feature `elastic_waves.force_source` - Point force

Line force along z (a 2D point) in the cell containing the point: force * waveform(t) in the direction angle, half on each of the two x faces (x component) and y faces (y component) of the cell, as force density over each face dual cell, at the start of each step (the time of the stresses it acts on). A point in the outermost cell of a non-periodic face loses the half on its outer face.

- FeatureSpec.type `force_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "ricker"; choices ricker | gaussian | cw) - Waveform
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.waveform`
- `frequency` (float; unit Hz; default 1e+06; range (0, inf)) - Frequency
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.frequency`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency of the gaussian pulse (1/e of the amplitude spectrum at f (1 +- bandwidth)).
- `force` (float; unit N/m; default 1) - Line force
  Peak force per unit z length (a 2D point is a line along z; geometry axisymmetric: per unit length of the ring through the point, total 2 pi r_c force), in the cell containing the point and split over its two faces per axis; results scale linearly with it.
- `angle` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Force direction
  Direction of the force, counter-clockwise from +x (0 = +x, 90 = +y).

### Feature `elastic_waves.volume_source` - Point volume source

Monopole (pulsating line source along z) in the cell containing the point: the injected volume per second volume_rate * waveform(t) acts as an isotropic in-plane strain rate on the cell (sampled half a step after the velocity forces, at the time of the velocities it acts with). In a fluid it radiates |p| = rho omega Q / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)|; in a solid it sends mainly compression waves.

- FeatureSpec.type `volume_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "ricker"; choices ricker | gaussian | cw) - Waveform
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.waveform`
- `frequency` (float; unit Hz; default 1e+06; range (0, inf)) - Frequency
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.frequency`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency of the gaussian pulse (1/e of the amplitude spectrum at f (1 +- bandwidth)).
- `volume_rate` (float; unit m^2/s; default 0.001) - Volume injection rate
  Peak volume injected per second and per unit z length (a monopole line source): an isotropic in-plane strain rate in the cell, d(sxx)/dt -= (c11 + c12) / 2 q, d(syy)/dt -= (c12 + c22) / 2 q, q = rate / cell area. In a fluid the cw pressure is |p| = rho omega Q / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)|, independent of the mesh. geometry axisymmetric: per unit length of the ring through the point (total 2 pi r_c rate), an isotropic 3D strain rate q / 3 per axis (a fluid again gets p += K q dt).

### Feature `elastic_waves.traction_line_source` - Line source (traction sheet)

Sheet of traction (force per area) traction * waveform(t) at the centres of the cells under an axis-aligned line, covering [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) and continuing through any padding where an end touches the domain edge: the normal component split over the two faces around each line cell, the tangential one on the faces along the line. A sheet across the whole domain (periodic or absorbing ends) launches plane waves of stress amplitude traction / 2 to each side; a shorter one diffracts.

- FeatureSpec.type `traction_line_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "ricker"; choices ricker | gaussian | cw) - Waveform
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.waveform`
- `frequency` (float; unit Hz; default 1e+06; range (0, inf)) - Frequency
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.force_source.frequency`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency of the gaussian pulse (1/e of the amplitude spectrum at f (1 +- bandwidth)).
- `traction` (float; unit Pa; default 1000) - Traction
  Peak force per unit area of the sheet; a sheet spanning the domain sends a plane wave of stress amplitude traction / 2 and velocity traction / (2 rho c) to each side (fluid: pressure traction / 2 for a normal traction).
- `direction` (choice; default "x"; choices x | y) - Force direction
  Component of the traction: normal to the line launches longitudinal (P) waves, along the line shear (S) waves (a vertical line: x = P, y = S).

### Feature `elastic_waves.heat_pulse_source` - Heating pulse (photoacoustic)

Thermoelastic source: q = power_density exp(-((t - delay) / pulse_width)^2) [W/m^3] on the selected cells adds -gruneisen q to d(sxx)/dt and d(syy)/dt (sampled at the half step), so a short pulse raises the pressure by gruneisen H, H = power_density sqrt(pi) pulse_width the absorbed energy density; cells without gruneisen ignore it. For heating computed by another time-stepped physics use the 'heating_power' slot (field_transfer, optionally with the gaussian heating_envelope setting).

- FeatureSpec.type `heat_pulse_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `power_density` (float; unit W/m^3; default 1e+12; may use x, y) - Peak heating power density
  Peak absorbed power q0 per unit volume; q = q0 exp(-((t - delay) / pulse_width)^2), absorbed energy density H = q0 sqrt(pi) pulse_width, and with a short pulse (c pulse_width << the heated size) the pressure rises by gruneisen H. May depend on x and y (e.g. Beer-Lambert exp(-mu_a (y1 - y))).
- `pulse_width` (float; unit s; default 1e-08; range (0, inf)) - Pulse width
  1/e half-width of the gaussian heating envelope; keep c pulse_width >= ~5 cells (validation warns below 2), else the pressure front is under-resolved and rings.
- `delay` (float; unit s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Pulse delay
  Time of the envelope maximum; empty = 3 x pulse_width.

### Feature `elastic_waves.rigid_domain` - Rigid domain

Every face of each selected cell keeps zero velocity (staircased to the mesh): an immovable obstacle; a fluid slides along it, a solid sticks to it.

- FeatureSpec.type `rigid_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `elastic_waves.initial_velocity` - Initial velocity

Initial particle velocity: v_x / v_y [m/s] are written into the staggered velocity fields before the first step (the state the leap-frog starts from: v^(-1/2), with the stresses at 0), on the +x / +y faces of the selected cells (several features: a later one wins its faces). Faces the scheme pins (rigid walls, rigid_domain, the axis) drop it at the first step. Single-precision stepper only (validation error for half_storage, whose storage scale comes from the sources).

- FeatureSpec.type `initial_velocity`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Stepper precisions single only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `v_x` (float; unit m/s; default 0; may use x, y) - Initial velocity x
  Particle velocity along x at t = 0 on the +x face of every selected cell, an expression of x, y evaluated at that face centre (the staggered vx position: exact for a discrete mode). Geometry axisymmetric: v_r.
- `v_y` (float; unit m/s; default 0; may use x, y) - Initial velocity y
  Particle velocity along y at t = 0 on the +y face of every selected cell, evaluated at that face centre. Geometry axisymmetric: v_z.

### Feature `elastic_waves.field_probe` - Field probe

Time series of one quantity in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell), sampled after every step; pressure and stresses in Pa at t, velocities in m/s at t - dt / 2 (their own time).

- FeatureSpec.type `field_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result kind `timeseries`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "pressure"; choices pressure | vx | vy | sxx | syy | sxy | stt) - Recorded quantity
  pressure = -(sxx + syy) / 2 (geometry axisymmetric: -(s_rr + s_zz + s_tt) / 3) and the stresses [Pa] at the cell centre (sxy on its +x +y corner) after each step; stt = the hoop stress s_tt at the cell centre (geometry axisymmetric only, else a validation error); vx / vy [m/s] on the +x / +y face of the cell, stamped half a step earlier (their own time).

### Feature `elastic_waves.resonance_monitor` - Resonance finder

Resonance finder (harmonic inversion, like Harminv / the matrix-pencil method): records one component in the cell containing each selected point (1 to 16 points) every step; when the result is read (CPU, about a second per point) the traces from the analysis start t_s on are mixed down to the band centre, low-pass filtered (Kaiser FIR, 100 dB), decimated to a sample rate of about 8 band half-widths (in Hz) and fitted by sums of damped sinusoids a exp(-gamma (t - t_s)) cos(omega (t - t_s) + phi). Several points share one joint fit (the same poles, each trace scaled to unit peak, amplitudes per point), so a mode on a nodal line of one point is still found through the others. Result 'table', one row per resonance inside the band, strongest (largest a) first, with the eigenfrequency resonance_table names: resonance_number (1, 2, ... in that order), frequency = omega / (2 pi) [Hz], frequency_imag = gamma / (2 pi) [Hz] (Im of the complex frequency, exp(+j omega t): > 0 decays; the amplitude decay rate is gamma = 2 pi frequency_imag), q_factor = omega / (2 gamma) (inf when it does not decay), amplitude a [unit of the component] and phase phi [rad] at t_s at the point where the resonance is largest, error = |difference of the complex pole -gamma + j omega between two pencil sizes| / omega (a noise / resolution estimate). Poles with error above 0.01, resonances below 0.0001 of the strongest at every point and poles growing by more than 2x over the window are dropped. Extras: component, unit, dt [s], start_time t_s and end_time [s] of the analysed window, sample_interval [steps], n_samples (at most 2000: the earliest decimated samples), model_order, frequency_min, frequency_max, note ('' or why no resonance was found), points (the point names in selection order), point_amplitudes / point_phases (per row, one value per point). Q far above pi f T_window is resolved as long as the ring-down stays above the float32 noise (~1e-7 of the signal). A mode with zero amplitude at every point is missed: select points off the nodal lines (with one point) or points that no mode of interest has as common node; a cw source drives an undamped line at its own frequency. A coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell. Velocities carry their own time stamps (t - dt / 2), so no sample delay applies. dt is the acoustic step of the run.

- FeatureSpec.type `resonance_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count 1 to 16
- Stepper precisions single, double only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "pressure"; choices pressure | vx | vy | sxx | syy | sxy | stt) - Recorded quantity
  pressure = -(sxx + syy) / 2 (geometry axisymmetric: -(s_rr + s_zz + s_tt) / 3) and the stresses [Pa] at the cell centre (sxy on its +x +y corner) after each step; stt = the hoop stress s_tt at the cell centre (geometry axisymmetric only, else a validation error); vx / vy [m/s] on the +x / +y face of the cell, stamped half a step earlier (their own time). Pressure misses the shear (S) modes of a solid; a stress or velocity component sees both kinds.
- `frequency_min` (float; unit Hz; default 500000; range (0, inf)) - Lowest frequency
  Lowest frequency of the analysed band. Keep the band inside the source spectrum; a narrower band gives a coarser decimation and a faster, better conditioned fit.
- `frequency_max` (float; unit Hz; default 2e+06; range (0, inf)) - Highest frequency
  Highest frequency of the analysed band; must exceed frequency_min and stay below the Nyquist frequency 1 / (2 dt).
- `start_time` (float; unit s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Analysis start
  Start t_s of the analysed window [s]; empty = the end of the latest pulsed source (ricker / gaussian waveform: 2 t0; heat_pulse_source and a gaussian heating_envelope: delay + 4.5 width) (0 with only cw sources). The fit assumes a free ring-down, so a start inside a pulse adds spurious poles; the amplitudes and phases refer to t_s.

## Physics type `electric_currents` - Electric Currents

2D electric currents per unit z length: quasi-static solve of -div(sigma_dc grad V) = s, s the volumetric current source [A/m^3] (current_source features plus the coupled slot current_source), on the physical window (finite volumes, Jacobi-PCG on V), V and every output copied edge-extended into an EM PML ring (so a field-dependent material property sees no step there). Unreferenced outer faces are insulated (zero normal current), and a later boundary feature on the same face wins (validation warning). Material properties are unset unless a material or its library entry sets them: cells without sigma_dc carry no current and keep their potential. The solve needs an anchor: a voltage or a terminal touching every conducting region (a pure Neumann problem is singular whatever the sources). Units are per unit z length: terminal currents A/m, conductances S and capacitances F per m of depth, resistances Ohm m (geometry axisymmetric: an (r, z) body of revolution about x_lo, held totals of the whole ring). Outputs: E_x / E_y and J_x / J_y from the face fluxes averaged to the cell centres (E = 0 in non-conducting cells, E and J = 0 in held cells; J_x / J_y include the xy cross flux, E stays -grad V); q_joule [W/m^3] = the dissipation of every face split between its two cells by their half-cell resistances (outer Dirichlet faces to their cell; the sigma_dc_xy power of each 2x2 block by area), so its integral over the window equals the sum over the voltage / terminal features of V * current, plus V times the current_source and the inward current_density it feeds in (currents_heat_joule hands it to heat). A stationary study iterates it with the couplings and the state-dependent material properties (sigma_dc of heat_T); in a time-dependent study it re-solves only when sigma_dc, a boundary condition, a held potential or a source changed (a sigma_dc(T) property is rewritten right after each heat step: leave every at 1 so the currents re-solve on the next tick, before the Joule power goes to heat). The instance is usually named currents. On a triangle mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles; 2D, planar or axisymmetric) finite elements of the discretization order (quadratic default): V is nodal, a voltage on objects holds their outline edges, a terminal every node of its elements, current_density / surface_charge on objects is an edge source on the outline (both sides), a probe reads the point's node; held currents / charges are the reactions of the un-eliminated system (exact Gauss balance); E, J / D and q_joule are element means (q_joule integrates to the stiffness energy, so to V * I) and every state slot holds one value per element (V at the centroid); electrostatics electrolytes with model linear only (a volumetric loss k (V - V_bulk) per element, none in terminal elements; rho_ion and c_ion_k from the element mean V, so the integral of rho_ion balances the held charges exactly; the inside of a voltage object solves to its voltage and carries ions when selected); no nonlinear electrolytes, waveforms or azimuthal_order. 3D models (size_z set) run on a tetrahedron mesh only (MeshSpec kind tetrahedra, 3D Cartesian; a 3D tensor mesh is a validation error): Lagrange elements of the discretization order (affine tetrahedra) on the window elements with the diagonal tensor sigma_dc_xx / _yy / _zz (sigma_dc_zz: set by the isotropic sigma_dc; sigma_dc_xy is a validation error), V nodal; outer faces act on the window faces, a voltage on objects holds their interface faces (Dirichlet), a terminal every node of its elements, current_density on objects is a sheet source on the interface faces (both sides), a probe evaluates V at the point; held currents are the reactions of the un-eliminated system in A (whole totals, exact Gauss balance; the integral of q_joule equals the sum of V * I); E, J_x / J_y and q_joule are element means, plus the 3D-only output fields E_z, J_z and sigma_dc_zz (not usable in expressions); fields are sampled on the uniform lattice of the mesh; Automatic linear solver: sparse_direct (cuDSS on the gpu backend with nvmath-python, else host SuperLU). Not in 3D: electrolytes, voltage waveforms, Stern layers, geometry axisymmetric / azimuthal_order and mirror faces of the model (validation errors).

- PhysicsSpec.type `electric_currents`; default instance name `currents`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): V
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `electric_currents.<feature>`): voltage, terminal, current_density, current_source, potential_probe

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "planar"; choices planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: 2D currents per unit z length (terminal currents A/m). axisymmetric: a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z): (r, z) currents; every conductance, face and cell volume is weighted by 2 pi r (x-faces at their own r, y-faces and volumes at the cell-centre r; 2 pi r_c dr dz is the exact ring volume; object-perimeter current_density likewise), so densities (sigma_dc S/m, current_source A/m^3, current_density A/m^2, J A/m^2, q_joule W/m^3) keep their units, while the current of a voltage / terminal (table result, scalar output current_<feature>) is that of the whole ring in A (a resistance V / I in Ohm), and the 'integral' of q_joule is the total power in W; sigma_dc_xy is not available (validation error); azimuthal_order m != 0 weights by pi r instead. x_lo is the axis (r = 0: symmetry, any feature there does nothing; validation warns). Field derived values of the whole model are weighted by the ring volume 2 pi r dx dy ('integral' a whole-body total, 'mean' a volume mean; also for fields of other physics). A coupled physics that is planar (its type has no geometry setting, e.g. EM, or it is set to planar) solves the drawing as a planar cut per unit z length, so its fields are applied per cell as rings (validation warns); a partner with geometry axisymmetric too is consistent.
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when geometry in (axisymmetric)) - Azimuthal order
  Help: shared `electric_currents.azimuthal_order`
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `sigma_dc` (float; unit S/m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_dc_xx, sigma_dc_yy, sigma_dc_zz) - Static conductivity
  Isotropic static (DC) conductivity: sets sigma_dc_xx, sigma_dc_yy and sigma_dc_zz (component entries override it; zz is read only on a tetrahedron mesh in 3D); unset = 0 = insulator: cells without sigma_dc carry no current and keep their potential (as k = 0 for heat), so every conducting region needs a voltage or terminal. NOT the optical sigma_e, the loss proxy at the solve wavelength (water: sigma_e 4.22 S/m at 1.55 um but sigma_dc 5.5e-6 S/m). Typical gold 4.1e7, silver 6.3e7, aluminium 3.8e7, water 5.5e-6; may depend on x, y and state fields, e.g. gold 4.1e7 / (1 + 0.0034 * (heat_T - 293.15)) (a stationary study iterates). 2D quantities are per unit z length: currents A/m, conductances S and capacitances F per m of depth, resistances Ohm m (geometry axisymmetric and 3D: whole totals, A, S, F, Ohm).
- `sigma_dc_xx` (float; unit S/m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_dc_xx) - Static conductivity along x
  DC conductivity along x; overrides sigma_dc for this axis.
- `sigma_dc_yy` (float; unit S/m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_dc_yy) - Static conductivity along y
  DC conductivity along y; overrides sigma_dc for this axis.
- `sigma_dc_zz` (float; unit S/m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_dc_zz) - Static conductivity along z
  DC conductivity along z (3D on a tetrahedron mesh only; 2D ignores it); overrides sigma_dc for this axis.
- `sigma_dc_xy` (float; unit S/m; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_dc_xy) - Static conductivity, cross term
  Off-diagonal component of sigma_dc (cross conduction of a rotated anisotropic material); keep sigma_dc_xy^2 < sigma_dc_xx * sigma_dc_yy (validation error for plain numbers); uniform or graded meshes (on strongly graded cells keep it clearly below that bound: the discrete operator is guaranteed positive below it times 4 r / (1 + r)^2 per axis, r = width ratio of neighbouring cells). Cross flux flows only inside 2x2 cell blocks whose xx and yy components are all > 0 (area-weighted mean sigma_dc_xy of the block), never through the outer faces. E stays -grad V; the current density J include the cross part -sigma_dc_xy (dV/dy, dV/dx), the block values averaged over each cell's blocks, and q_joule includes each block's cross power (so its integral equals V * I).

### Fields

State fields:
- `V` - Electric potential (V)
- `E_x` - Electric field x (V/m)
- `E_y` - Electric field y (V/m)
- `J_x` - Current density x (A/m^2)
- `J_y` - Current density y (A/m^2)
- `q_joule` - Joule heating density (W/m^3)
- `current_source` - Coupled current source (A/m^3)
- `current_source_ext` - Applied current source (A/m^3)
- `sigma_dc_xx` - DC conductivity xx (S/m)
- `sigma_dc_yy` - DC conductivity yy (S/m)

Output fields (primary V):
- `V` - Electric potential (V)
- `E_x` - Electric field x (V/m)
- `E_y` - Electric field y (V/m)
- `J_x` - Current density x (A/m^2)
- `J_y` - Current density y (A/m^2)
- `q_joule` - Joule heating density (W/m^3)
- `current_source` - Coupled current source (A/m^3)
- `current_source_ext` - Applied current source (A/m^3)
- `sigma_dc_xx` - DC conductivity xx (S/m)
- `sigma_dc_yy` - DC conductivity yy (S/m)
- `E_z` - Electric field z (V/m)
- `J_z` - Current density z (A/m^2)
- `sigma_dc_zz` - DC conductivity zz (S/m)

Scalar outputs: current_<feature> (A/m; geometry axisymmetric: A, the whole ring; 3D: A) per enabled voltage / terminal feature: the current per m of depth it feeds into the domain in the last solve, the current of its table result (same sign). Example derived value {"name": "I_anode", "expression": "currents_current_anode"} (operation mean of a constant is the value itself); a parameter sweep of a voltage then gives the I-V curve, voltage / current the resistance (Ohm m). A feature whose scalar would be named like an output field (a terminal named source: current_source) gets none. Under a mirror face of an EM physics of the model the value is the unfolded structure's: x 2 per mirror plane the voltage face or terminal touches (its image joins it; a face on the opposite side does not touch).

### Source slots

- `current_source` (A/m^3): Coupled volumetric current source (field current_source), added to the current_source features (field current_source_ext); each transfer replaces it.

### Feature `electric_currents.voltage` - Voltage

Fixed potential (Dirichlet). On outer faces V is imposed at the face (half-cell conductance 2 sigma_dc / dx); on object perimeters the boundary cells inside the object are held at V, imposed on their faces toward the free cells as on an outer face (the window edge is no perimeter: select the outer face there). Unreferenced outer faces are insulated, and a later boundary feature on the same face wins (validation warning). Anchors the solve. Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, voltage, current] (units '', V, A/m; axisymmetric and 3D A) and the extras voltage (V) and current (A/m; axisymmetric and 3D A): positive = current (charge) per m of depth (geometry axisymmetric: of the whole ring) flowing out of the held faces / cells into the domain (the face conductance times V_face - V_cell summed along a held outer face; for held cells the sum over them of (A V - b) of the un-eliminated system, so an injected source inside the terminal is subtracted); electrostatics: the free charge on the terminal (its outward D flux, Gauss). A cell held by two features is attributed to each (the later voltage holds it; validation warns when held objects may overlap); an outer face whose condition a later feature replaced (the last one wins) counts only for that feature. E and J / D read 0 inside held cells (an ideal conductor): the surface current / charge is this result.

- FeatureSpec.type `voltage`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `voltage` (float; unit V; default 1) - Voltage
  Held at the selected outer faces (on the face itself) or in the boundary cells inside the selected objects.

### Feature `electric_currents.terminal` - Terminal

Holds every selected cell at the voltage for the whole run (the cells leave the solve; current flows in or out freely); the voltage sits on their faces toward the free cells (half-cell conductance 2 sigma_dc / dx of the free neighbour, whatever the held cells' own coefficient); anchors the solve. A metal body with its own sigma_dc is equipotential anyway: a terminal is for feeding current in and reading it out (its cells need no sigma_dc: they act as an ideal conductor). Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, voltage, current] (units '', V, A/m; axisymmetric and 3D A) and the extras voltage (V) and current (A/m; axisymmetric and 3D A): positive = current (charge) per m of depth (geometry axisymmetric: of the whole ring) flowing out of the held faces / cells into the domain (the face conductance times V_face - V_cell summed along a held outer face; for held cells the sum over them of (A V - b) of the un-eliminated system, so an injected source inside the terminal is subtracted); electrostatics: the free charge on the terminal (its outward D flux, Gauss). A cell held by two features is attributed to each (the later voltage holds it; validation warns when held objects may overlap); an outer face whose condition a later feature replaced (the last one wins) counts only for that feature. E and J / D read 0 inside held cells (an ideal conductor): the surface current / charge is this result.

- FeatureSpec.type `terminal`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `voltage` (float; unit V; default 1) - Voltage
  Voltage every selected cell is held at for the whole run (times the waveform when one is set).

### Feature `electric_currents.current_density` - Current density

Prescribed normal current density, > 0 into the domain or the object. On outer faces a Neumann condition (the normal current through the face); on object perimeters it feeds the boundary cells inside the object with current_density * perimeter length / cell area [A/m^3] (each exposed cell face weighted by its normal component, so slanted and curved perimeters get their true length to ~2 %). Does not anchor the solve: the current must leave through a voltage or terminal. Polar / spherical domains weight each exposed face by its metric area. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (2D: Cartesian, (r, z), polar, spherical) each cut cell feeds current_density * its chord of the drawn outline into the object cell owning it (exact for straight edges).

- FeatureSpec.type `current_density`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `current_density` (float; unit A/m^2; default 10000) - Inward current density
  inward: > 0 injects current into the domain (outer faces) or into the object's boundary cells as value * perimeter length / cell area [A/m^3], < 0 extracts it; does not anchor the solve.

### Feature `electric_currents.current_source` - Current source

Applied volumetric current source: density is added to current_source_ext on the selected cells (several sources add; the coupled slot and field current_source are separate). The injected current leaves through the voltage / terminal features; non-conducting cells ignore it.

- FeatureSpec.type `current_source`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `density` (float; unit A/m^3; default 1e+12; may use x, y) - Injected current per volume
  Volumetric current injection; in 2D density * area is the line current per m of depth (A/m; geometry axisymmetric: density * ring volume, A). May depend on x and y; must be finite on the selected cells. A steady solve ignores it in non-conducting cells (sigma_dc 0).

### Feature `electric_currents.potential_probe` - Potential probe

Help: shared `electric_currents.potential_probe`

- FeatureSpec.type `potential_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result kind `timeseries`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

## Physics type `electrostatics` - Electrostatics

2D electrostatics per unit z length: quasi-static solve of -div(eps0 eps_dc grad V) = rho_free + rho_ion, rho_free the charge_density source [C/m^3], rho_ion the ionic space charge of the electrolyte features (field rho_ion; linearised, or Boltzmann by damped Newton), on the physical window (finite volumes, Jacobi-PCG on V), V and every output copied edge-extended into an EM PML ring (so a field-dependent material property sees no step there). Unreferenced outer faces are insulated (zero normal D), and a later boundary feature on the same face wins (validation warning). eps_dc is 1 (vacuum) unless a material or its library entry sets it, so every cell takes part in the solve. The solve needs an anchor: one voltage, terminal or electrolyte anywhere (every cell is a dielectric, so it reaches all of them) (a pure Neumann problem is singular whatever the sources). Units are per unit z length: terminal charges C/m, capacitances F per m of depth (charge / voltage of a terminal with the other one held at 0 V) (geometry axisymmetric: an (r, z) body of revolution about x_lo, held totals of the whole ring). Outputs: E_x / E_y and D_x / D_y from the face fluxes averaged to the cell centres (E = D / (eps0 eps_dc) without eps_dc_xy, both 0 in held cells; D_x / D_y include the xy cross flux, E stays -grad V). A stationary study iterates it with the couplings and the state-dependent material properties (eps_dc of heat_T); in a time-dependent study it re-solves only when eps_dc, a boundary condition, a held potential or a source changed (a state-dependent eps_dc re-solves at the cadence of the physics it reads; with a voltage or terminal waveform every step instead writes the superposition of static basis solves at the end time of the step, no re-solve). The instance is usually named electrostatics. On a triangle mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles; 2D, planar or axisymmetric) finite elements of the discretization order (quadratic default): V is nodal, a voltage on objects holds their outline edges, a terminal every node of its elements, current_density / surface_charge on objects is an edge source on the outline (both sides), a probe reads the point's node; held currents / charges are the reactions of the un-eliminated system (exact Gauss balance); E, J / D and q_joule are element means (q_joule integrates to the stiffness energy, so to V * I) and every state slot holds one value per element (V at the centroid); electrostatics electrolytes with model linear only (a volumetric loss k (V - V_bulk) per element, none in terminal elements; rho_ion and c_ion_k from the element mean V, so the integral of rho_ion balances the held charges exactly; the inside of a voltage object solves to its voltage and carries ions when selected); no nonlinear electrolytes, waveforms or azimuthal_order. 3D models (size_z set) run on a tetrahedron mesh only (MeshSpec kind tetrahedra, 3D Cartesian; a 3D tensor mesh is a validation error): Lagrange elements of the discretization order (affine tetrahedra) on the window elements with the diagonal tensor eps_dc_xx / _yy / _zz (eps_dc_zz: set by the isotropic eps_dc; eps_dc_xy is a validation error), V nodal; outer faces act on the window faces, a voltage on objects holds their interface faces (Dirichlet), a terminal every node of its elements, surface_charge on objects is a sheet source on the interface faces (both sides), a probe evaluates V at the point; held charges are the reactions of the un-eliminated system in C (whole totals, exact Gauss balance); E, D_x / D_y are element means, plus the 3D-only output fields E_z, D_z and eps_dc_zz (not usable in expressions); fields are sampled on the uniform lattice of the mesh; Automatic linear solver: sparse_direct (cuDSS on the gpu backend with nvmath-python, else host SuperLU). Not in 3D: electrolytes, voltage waveforms, Stern layers, geometry axisymmetric / azimuthal_order and mirror faces of the model (validation errors).

- PhysicsSpec.type `electrostatics`; default instance name `electrostatics`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): V
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `electrostatics.<feature>`): voltage, terminal, surface_charge, charge_density, potential_probe, electrolyte

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "planar"; choices planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: 2D electrostatics per unit z length (terminal charges C/m). axisymmetric: a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z): (r, z) electrostatics; every conductance, face and cell volume is weighted by 2 pi r (x-faces at their own r, y-faces and volumes at the cell-centre r; 2 pi r_c dr dz is the exact ring volume; object-perimeter surface_charge likewise), so densities (charge_density C/m^3, surface_charge C/m^2, D C/m^2) keep their units, while the charge of a voltage / terminal (table result, scalar output charge_<feature>) is that of the whole ring in C (a capacitance Q / V in F); eps_dc_xy is not available (validation error); azimuthal_order m != 0 weights by pi r instead. x_lo is the axis (r = 0: symmetry, any feature there does nothing; validation warns). Field derived values of the whole model are weighted by the ring volume 2 pi r dx dy ('integral' a whole-body total, 'mean' a volume mean; also for fields of other physics). A coupled physics that is planar (its type has no geometry setting, e.g. EM, or it is set to planar) solves the drawing as a planar cut per unit z length, so its fields are applied per cell as rings (validation warns); a partner with geometry axisymmetric too is consistent.
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when geometry in (axisymmetric)) - Azimuthal order
  Help: shared `electric_currents.azimuthal_order`
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`
- `nonlinear_tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-06; range (0, inf)) - Electrolyte iteration tolerance
  Stop of the damped Newton loop of nonlinear electrolytes (feature electrolyte, model nonlinear): converged when one Newton step changes V by at most this times kB T / (e max |z_i|) (the smallest over the nonlinear electrolytes; 25.7 mV for 1:1 at 298.15 K) anywhere. Each step is one CG solve warm-started at the previous V, so keep it above the CG accuracy in V (the linear pcg solver tolerance times the condition number, relative to the drive). Ignored without a nonlinear electrolyte.
- `nonlinear_max_iterations` (int; default 100; range [1, inf)) - Electrolyte iteration limit
  Newton iteration limit per solve of a nonlinear electrolyte; an unconverged loop keeps its damped V and logs a warning (study log). Steps are capped at 4 x kB T / (e max |z_i|) (the smallest over the nonlinear electrolytes; 25.7 mV for 1:1 at 298.15 K), so a surface or electrode potential of P such units needs at least P / 4 iterations. Ignored without a nonlinear electrolyte.
- `nonlinear_relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [0.015625, 1]) - Electrolyte iteration damping
  Fraction of each Newton update applied, [1/64, 1]; it halves automatically (down to 1/64) while the update grows and recovers once it shrinks. 1 (full Newton steps) suits the convex Boltzmann charge; lower it only when the loop oscillates. Ignored without a nonlinear electrolyte.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_dc` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_xx, eps_dc_yy, eps_dc_zz) - Static relative permittivity
  Isotropic static relative permittivity (>= 1): sets eps_dc_xx, eps_dc_yy and eps_dc_zz (component entries override it; zz is read only on a tetrahedron mesh in 3D); unset = 1 (vacuum), so every cell takes part in the solve and one voltage / terminal anchors everything. NOT the optical eps_r = n^2: lithium niobate eps_dc 43 (eps_a) / 28 (eps_c, along the optic axis) vs eps_r 4.9 / 4.6; silicon 11.7 vs 12.08; silica 3.9 vs 2.085; water 80.1 vs 1.73. 2D: charges C/m, capacitances F per m of depth (geometry axisymmetric and 3D: whole totals, C, F).
- `eps_dc_xx` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_xx) - Static relative permittivity along x
  Static relative permittivity along x (>= 1); overrides eps_dc for this axis.
- `eps_dc_yy` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_yy) - Static relative permittivity along y
  Static relative permittivity along y (>= 1); overrides eps_dc for this axis.
- `eps_dc_zz` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_zz) - Static relative permittivity along z
  Static relative permittivity along z (>= 1; electrostatics in 3D on a tetrahedron mesh, solid_mechanics_3d with piezoelectric on; 2D ignores it); overrides eps_dc for this axis.
- `eps_dc_xy` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_xy) - Static relative permittivity, cross term
  Off-diagonal component of eps_dc (cross polarisation of a rotated anisotropic material); keep eps_dc_xy^2 < eps_dc_xx * eps_dc_yy (validation error for plain numbers); uniform or graded meshes (on strongly graded cells keep it clearly below that bound: the discrete operator is guaranteed positive below it times 4 r / (1 + r)^2 per axis, r = width ratio of neighbouring cells). Cross flux flows only inside 2x2 cell blocks whose xx and yy components are all > 0 (area-weighted mean eps_dc_xy of the block), never through the outer faces. E stays -grad V; the displacement D include the cross part -eps0 eps_dc_xy (dV/dy, dV/dx), the block values averaged over each cell's blocks.
- `r` (float; unit m/V; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays r_xx, r_yy, r_zz) - Electro-optic coefficient
  Isotropic Pockels (linear electro-optic) coefficient: sets r_xx, r_yy and r_zz (component entries override it), read only by the electrostatics_em_pockels coupling: dn_ii = -1/2 n0_ii^3 r_ii E_k with E_k the applied field component chosen by its field_component. The diagonal of the Pockels tensor for one applied direction; unset = 0 (no effect). Typical: x-cut lithium niobate with the field along the optic axis r33 = 31e-12 on the optic-axis component and r13 = 10e-12 on the others (library lithium_niobate_x_cut); 0 for centrosymmetric silicon and silica. A crystal entry sets the tensor entries pockels_r11 .. _r62 instead.
- `r_xx` (float; unit m/V; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays r_xx) - Electro-optic coefficient along x
  Pockels coefficient of n_xx (the index seen by light with its electric field along x); overrides r for this component.
- `r_yy` (float; unit m/V; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays r_yy) - Electro-optic coefficient along y
  Pockels coefficient of n_yy (the index seen by light with its electric field along y); overrides r for this component.
- `r_zz` (float; unit m/V; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays r_zz) - Electro-optic coefficient along z
  Pockels coefficient of n_zz (the index seen by light with its electric field along z); overrides r for this component.
- `pockels_r11` (float; unit m/V; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays pockels_r11) - Electro-optic tensor r11
  In-plane Pockels tensor entry pockels_r11 [m/V] of a crystal in model axes: Delta(1/n^2)_I = r_I1 E_x + r_I2 E_y with the index-ellipsoid row I = 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz (the diagonal permittivity slots) or 6 xy (the eps_xy slot of em_fdfd_hz: Delta eps_xy = -n0_xx^2 n0_yy^2 Delta(1/n^2)_xy; other EM types drop it, validation warns for crystals), read only by electrostatics_em_pockels, which adds -1/2 n0_ii^3 (r_i1 E_x + r_i2 E_y) from both field components whatever its field_component (on top of r_ii E_k: set either these or r / r_ii on a material, not both). Usually set by a {'model': 'crystal'} entry: the clamped (strain-free) r^S rotated into model axes, so a piezoelectric strain computed by elastic_waves adds its own index change through acoustics_em_acousto_optic without double counting; YZ lithium niobate (model x = crystal Z, y = -Y): r11 = r33, r12 = 0, r21 = r13, r22 = -r22, r31 = r13, r32 = r22, r61 = 0, r62 = r51 (crystal constants). Default 0; any one set allocates all eight arrays.
- `pockels_r12` (float; unit m/V; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays pockels_r12) - Electro-optic tensor r12
  In-plane Pockels tensor entry pockels_r12 [m/V] of a crystal in model axes: Delta(1/n^2)_I = r_I1 E_x + r_I2 E_y with the index-ellipsoid row I = 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz (the diagonal permittivity slots) or 6 xy (the eps_xy slot of em_fdfd_hz: Delta eps_xy = -n0_xx^2 n0_yy^2 Delta(1/n^2)_xy; other EM types drop it, validation warns for crystals), read only by electrostatics_em_pockels, which adds -1/2 n0_ii^3 (r_i1 E_x + r_i2 E_y) from both field components whatever its field_component (on top of r_ii E_k: set either these or r / r_ii on a material, not both). ### Fields

State fields:
- `V` - Electric potential (V)
- `E_x` - Electric field x (V/m)
- `E_y` - Electric field y (V/m)
- `D_x` - Electric displacement x (C/m^2)
- `D_y` - Electric displacement y (C/m^2)
- `rho_free` - Coupled charge density (C/m^3)
- `rho_free_ext` - Applied charge density (C/m^3)
- `rho_ion` - Ionic space charge (C/m^3)
- `eps_dc_xx` - DC relative permittivity xx (1)
- `eps_dc_yy` - DC relative permittivity yy (1)

Output fields (primary V):
- `V` - Electric potential (V)
- `E_x` - Electric field x (V/m)
- `E_y` - Electric field y (V/m)
- `D_x` - Electric displacement x (C/m^2)
- `D_y` - Electric displacement y (C/m^2)
- `rho_free` - Coupled charge density (C/m^3)
- `rho_free_ext` - Applied charge density (C/m^3)
- `rho_ion` - Ionic space charge (C/m^3)
- `c_ion_1` - Ion concentration, species 1 (mol/L)
- `c_ion_2` - Ion concentration, species 2 (mol/L)
- `c_ion_3` - Ion concentration, species 3 (mol/L)
- `c_ion_4` - Ion concentration, species 4 (mol/L)
- `eps_dc_xx` - DC relative permittivity xx (1)
- `eps_dc_yy` - DC relative permittivity yy (1)
- `E_z` - Electric field z (V/m)
- `D_z` - Electric displacement z (C/m^2)
- `eps_dc_zz` - DC relative permittivity zz (1)

Scalar outputs: charge_<feature> (C/m; geometry axisymmetric: C, the whole ring; 3D: C) per enabled voltage / terminal feature: its free charge per m of depth (outward D flux) in the last solve, the charge of its table result. Example derived value {"name": "C_top", "expression": "electrostatics_charge_top / V_top"} = the capacitance per m of depth (F/m) with every other electrode at 0 V (operation mean of a constant is the value itself). Per enabled electrolyte feature also ionic_strength_<feature> (mol/L, 1/2 sum z_i^2 c_i) and debye_length_<feature> (m, at the mean static eps_dc of its selected cells), constants of the build. Under a mirror face of an EM physics of the model the charges are the unfolded structure's: x 2 per mirror plane the voltage face or terminal touches.

### Source slots

- `charge_density` (C/m^3): Coupled free charge density (field rho_free), added to the charge_density features (field rho_free_ext); each transfer replaces it.

### Feature `electrostatics.voltage` - Voltage

Fixed potential (Dirichlet). On outer faces V is imposed at the face (half-cell conductance 2 eps0 eps_dc / dx); on object perimeters the boundary cells inside the object are held at V, imposed on their faces toward the free cells as on an outer face (the window edge is no perimeter: select the outer face there). Unreferenced outer faces are insulated, and a later boundary feature on the same face wins (validation warning). Anchors the solve. stern_thickness > 0 (electrostatics, outer faces): a compact Stern layer of capacitance eps0 stern_permittivity / stern_thickness per area between the face voltage and the first cells (Robin face). Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, voltage, charge] (units '', V, C/m; axisymmetric and 3D C) and the extras voltage (V) and charge (C/m; axisymmetric and 3D C): positive = current (charge) per m of depth (geometry axisymmetric: of the whole ring) flowing out of the held faces / cells into the domain (the face conductance times V_face - V_cell summed along a held outer face; for held cells the sum over them of (A V - b) of the un-eliminated system, so an injected source inside the terminal is subtracted); electrostatics: the free charge on the terminal (its outward D flux, Gauss). A cell held by two features is attributed to each (the later voltage holds it; validation warns when held objects may overlap); an outer face whose condition a later feature replaced (the last one wins) counts only for that feature. E and J / D read 0 inside held cells (an ideal conductor): the surface current / charge is this result.

- FeatureSpec.type `voltage`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `voltage` (float; unit V; default 1) - Voltage
  Held at the selected outer faces (on the face itself) or in the boundary cells inside the selected objects.
- `waveform` (choice; default "none"; choices none | ricker | gaussian | cw) - Voltage waveform
  Help: shared `electrostatics.voltage.waveform`
- `frequency` (float; unit Hz; default 1e+08; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (ricker, gaussian, cw)) - Frequency
  Centre (gaussian, cw) or peak (ricker) frequency of the waveform.
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency of the gaussian waveform (1/e of the amplitude spectrum at f (1 +- bandwidth)).
- `stern_thickness` (float; unit m; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Stern layer thickness
  Thickness d_S of a compact (Stern / Helmholtz) layer between the electrode and the first cells: 0 = none (V held on the face). > 0: the face is a Robin condition h = C_S = eps0 stern_permittivity / d_S [F/m^2], external = voltage, i.e. the layer in series with the half-cell conductance 2 eps0 eps_dc / dx, so V drops by sigma / C_S across it (sigma = D.n into the domain = the electrode charge per area; Gouy-Chapman-Stern: voltage = psi_d + sigma / C_S, psi_d the diffuse-layer potential at the face). The layer holds no ions and no cells (it is not drawn; the electrolyte begins at the face). Outer faces only (validation error with objects selected); charge_<feature> and the table charge are the D flux through it. Typical 0.2 to 0.5 nm.
- `stern_permittivity` (float; unit 1; default 10; range [1, inf)) - Stern layer permittivity
  Relative permittivity eps_S of the Stern layer (oriented water: 6 to 30); used only with stern_thickness > 0.

### Feature `electrostatics.terminal` - Terminal

Holds every selected cell at the voltage for the whole run (the cells leave the solve; charge flows in or out freely); the voltage sits on their faces toward the free cells (half-cell conductance 2 eps0 eps_dc / dx of the free neighbour, whatever the held cells' own coefficient); anchors the solve. Electrostatics has no conductors of its own (every cell is a dielectric), so a terminal is the conductor: its cells are held at the voltage (their eps_dc does not matter, so a gold electrode needs none) and its free charge is read out. Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, voltage, charge] (units '', V, C/m; axisymmetric and 3D C) and the extras voltage (V) and charge (C/m; axisymmetric and 3D C): positive = current (charge) per m of depth (geometry axisymmetric: of the whole ring) flowing out of the held faces / cells into the domain (the face conductance times V_face - V_cell summed along a held outer face; for held cells the sum over them of (A V - b) of the un-eliminated system, so an injected source inside the terminal is subtracted); electrostatics: the free charge on the terminal (its outward D flux, Gauss). A cell held by two features is attributed to each (the later voltage holds it; validation warns when held objects may overlap); an outer face whose condition a later feature replaced (the last one wins) counts only for that feature. E and J / D read 0 inside held cells (an ideal conductor): the surface current / charge is this result.

- FeatureSpec.type `terminal`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `voltage` (float; unit V; default 1) - Voltage
  Voltage every selected cell is held at for the whole run (times the waveform when one is set).
- `waveform` (choice; default "none"; choices none | ricker | gaussian | cw) - Voltage waveform
  Help: shared `electrostatics.voltage.waveform`
- `frequency` (float; unit Hz; default 1e+08; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (ricker, gaussian, cw)) - Frequency
  Centre (gaussian, cw) or peak (ricker) frequency of the waveform.
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / frequency of the gaussian waveform (1/e of the amplitude spectrum at f (1 +- bandwidth)).

### Feature `electrostatics.surface_charge` - Surface charge

Prescribed surface charge. On outer faces a Neumann condition D.n = surface_charge into the domain (a charged sheet with nothing beyond the face); on object perimeters the charge is placed in the boundary cells inside the object as surface_charge * perimeter length / cell area [C/m^3] (each exposed cell face weighted by its normal component, so slanted and curved perimeters get their true length to ~2 %; polar / spherical domains: the metric face areas). Does not anchor the solve. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (2D: Cartesian, (r, z), polar, spherical) each cut cell places surface_charge * its chord of the drawn outline in the object cell owning it.

- FeatureSpec.type `surface_charge`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `surface_charge` (float; unit C/m^2; default 1e-06) - Surface charge
  charge on the selected outer faces (the D flux into the domain equals it: a charged face with nothing beyond) or on the exposed faces of the objects (placed in their boundary cells as a density); > 0 raises V. Does not anchor the solve.

### Feature `electrostatics.charge_density` - Charge density

Applied volumetric free charge: density is added to rho_free_ext on the selected cells (several sources add; the coupled slot charge_density, field rho_free, is separate).

- FeatureSpec.type `charge_density`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `density` (float; unit C/m^3; default 0.001; may use x, y) - Charge density
  rho in div(eps0 eps_dc grad V) = -rho; positive charge raises V. In 2D density * area is the line charge per m of depth (C/m; geometry axisymmetric: density * ring volume, C). May depend on x and y; must be finite on the selected cells.

### Feature `electrostatics.electrolyte` - Electrolyte

Mobile ions screening the field (Poisson-Boltzmann): on the selected cells the ionic space charge rho_ion enters the solve, -div(eps0 eps_dc grad V) = rho_free + rho_ion. model linear (Debye-Hueckel, default): rho_ion = -k (V - bulk_potential), k = sum_i z_i^2 e^2 n_i / (kB T) [F/m^3] with n_i = 1000 N_A c_i, a diagonal term, so V decays over the Debye length lambda_D = sqrt(eps0 eps_dc / k) (water, eps_dc 80, 298.15 K: 0.307 nm / sqrt(I [mol/L]), 9.7 nm at 1 mM NaCl); valid for |V - V_bulk| << kB T / (|z| e) = 25.7 mV / |z| at 298 K (larger potentials overestimate the screening charge). model nonlinear: point-charge Boltzmann ions, rho_ion = sum_i z_i e n_i exp(-z_i e (V - V_bulk) / (kB T)), solved by damped Newton: each iteration replaces the diagonal term by the tangent of rho_ion at the current V and runs one CG solve warm-started there (the first iteration from V = 0 is the linear solution), steps capped at 4 kB T / (e max |z_i|), converged when a step changes V by at most nonlinear_tolerance x kB T / (e max |z_i|) (physics settings nonlinear_tolerance / nonlinear_max_iterations / nonlinear_relaxation; iterations in the study summary solvers (the physics counters) as nonlinear_iterations; an unconverged loop keeps the damped V and logs a warning). It has no ion size: counter-ion concentrations above a few mol/L (|V - V_bulk| beyond ~0.2 V / |z| at 1 mM salt) are unphysical, and the Boltzmann exponent is clipped at 80. Both models anchor the solve: no voltage or terminal is needed (e.g. a charged surface given by surface_charge). Held cells (terminals, voltage perimeters) are ideal conductors without ions; overlapping electrolytes add (one Newton loop when any of them is nonlinear). Field rho_ion [C/m^3] (nonlinear: the Boltzmann charge of the solved V); fields c_ion_1 .. c_ion_4 [mol/L] = the local concentration of species k (the k-th entry of concentrations / valences) at the solved V, c_k exp(-z_k e (V - V_bulk) / (kB T)) (nonlinear) or its linearisation c_k (1 - z_k e (V - V_bulk) / (kB T)) (linear: the concentrations of its rho_ion, negative beyond kB T / (|z_k| e)), so sum_k z_k e 1000 N_A c_ion_k = rho_ion; 0 outside the electrolytes and on held cells, overlapping electrolytes add their k-th species; listed up to the longest species list, at most 4 (more species: validation warning); output fields only (not usable in expressions). Scalar outputs ionic_strength_<feature> [mol/L] = 1/2 sum z_i^2 c_i and debye_length_<feature> [m] (the bulk, linearised value in both models) at the mean eps_dc of the selected cells at build (the static material value). Resolve lambda_D with several cells (cells of lambda_D / 3 or finer at charged surfaces and electrodes): the screening layer there is lambda_D thick, and with model nonlinear thinner at high potentials (1:1: lambda_D / cosh(e (V - V_bulk) / (2 kB T))), so refine further. Validation reports the ionic strength and lambda_D (info). geometry axisymmetric: ring volumes, as for every density. Triangle meshes: model linear only, the terms per element (rho_ion and c_ion_k from the element mean V; mean eps_dc area-weighted).

- FeatureSpec.type `electrolyte`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `concentrations` (float_list; unit mol/L; default [0.001, 0.001]; range [0, inf)) - Ion concentrations
  Bulk molar concentration c_i of each ion species (1 mM = 1e-3 mol/L), in the order of valences; the bulk must be neutral, sum z_i c_i = 0 (validation error). Uniform over the selection; parameter expressions allowed (e.g. a concentration sweep).
- `valences` (float_list; unit 1; default [1, -1]) - Ion valences
  Charge number z_i of each species, one per concentration, none 0: Na+ / K+ 1, Cl- -1, Ca2+ 2, SO4 2- -2 (CaCl2: valences 2, -1 with concentrations c, 2 c).
- `temperature` (float; unit K; default 298.15; range (0, inf)) - Temperature
  Temperature of the Boltzmann factor kB T (the screening coefficient scales as 1 / T). Typical 298.15 K.
- `bulk_potential` (float; unit V; default 0) - Bulk potential
  Potential V_bulk of the bulk electrolyte, where every species has its bulk concentration (e.g. that of a reference electrode in it): rho_ion = -k (V - V_bulk), so V relaxes to it away from charges and electrodes.
- `model` (choice; default "linear"; choices linear | nonlinear) - Electrolyte model
  linear (Debye-Hueckel, one solve): rho_ion = -k (V - V_bulk), valid for |V - V_bulk| << kB T / (|z| e); nonlinear (Poisson-Boltzmann, damped Newton over the physics settings nonlinear_tolerance / nonlinear_max_iterations / nonlinear_relaxation): rho_ion = sum_i z_i e n_i exp(-z_i e (V - V_bulk) / (kB T)), for surface and electrode potentials of several kB T / e.

## Physics type `em_eme` - Electromagnetic Waves, eigenmode expansion (2D)

Bidirectional eigenmode expansion (EME) of a 2D in-plane device along propagation_axis (x or y), for devices long along that axis (tapers, MMIs, couplers, gratings) where em_fdfd_* would be large. Every cell layer normal to the axis is a slice; consecutive equal slices (section_tolerance) form a section, so tapers are staircases at the mesh resolution. Each section line is solved once for n_modes slab modes (the em_fdfd_ez / _hz line stencil along the other axis, transverse bc_* faces, complex PML stretch with the PML modes kept as radiation; the same material rows repeated reuse their modes). Modes are normalised to the unconjugated product <e, h> = sum u (g u) w s = 1 (orthogonal also for lossy lines); interfaces are mode-matched by these overlaps (tangential u and its transverse partner continuous: R = (I + P P^T)^-1 (I - P P^T), T = P^T (I + R)) and the S-matrices cascaded by Redheffer star products (stable with evanescent modes). Exact for a complete basis (n_modes = 0), otherwise converging in n_modes (section table reciprocity_defect). The faces along propagation_axis are semi-infinite ports at the window planes: their bc is not read. Outputs of the excitation (eme_ports): the reconstructed phasor at the cell centres, sum over modes of a_n e^{-j k_n s} + b_n e^{-j k_n (L - s)} per section (<pol>_re / _im / _abs / _phase of the out-of-plane field; the other polarisation reads 0), e_abs (primary), e_intensity and h_abs (the in-plane component along the axis from the line differences, face mean), absorbed_power = 1/2 omega eps0 (-Im eps) times the cell mean of |E|^2 along the axis (3-point Gauss, so its integral is the exact absorbed power of the continuum propagation: 1 - T - R of a lossy guide between lossless ports), and the materials. Scalar outputs transmission_<k>, transmission, reflection. em_heat_joule reads absorbed_power (the time average of the last solve); heat_em_thermo_optic / Pockels write eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy. eme_bend makes a range a circular bend (exact cylindrical line operator), eme_periodic repeats a drawn period n times (star powers) and lists its Bloch modes. Optimization study (ez or hz): design_region features write eps_r (ez) or eps_xx and eps_yy (hz) and adjoint_objective features weight port power fractions; dJ/d eps (output field eps_sensitivity) comes from the cascade adjoint without extra mode solves (exact for n_modes 0). Exact identities: a complete basis with the discrete propagation of the self-tests solves the em_fdfd_ez / _hz lattice of the sectioned guide (both polarisations). Studies: stationary (a solve whenever materials changed), frequency_domain (one solve per wavelength; the line solves are direct) and optimization. Bloch k is not supported; cannot share the model with another EM type. The instance is usually named 'eme'.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_eme`; default instance name `eme`
- Supported studies: stationary, frequency_domain, optimization
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): e_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_eme.<feature>`): eme_ports, eme_section_table, eme_length_sweep, eme_periodic, eme_bend, pec_domain, adjoint_objective, design_region

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `polarization` (choice; default "ez"; choices ez | hz) - Polarisation
  Field out of the xy plane: 'ez' (E_z, H_x, H_y; reads eps_r = eps_zz) or 'hz' (H_z, E_x, E_y; reads eps_xx / eps_yy). The mode lines and interfaces are those of em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz.
- `propagation_axis` (choice; default "x"; choices x | y) - Propagation axis
  Axis along which the device is cut into sections: every cell layer normal to it is a slice, consecutive equal slices form one section (so a taper is a staircase at the mesh resolution along this axis: refine the mesh there to smooth it), and its lo / hi faces are the ports.
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda0 of a stationary solve (omega = 2 pi C0 / lambda0); a frequency_domain study solves its own wavelengths instead (one cold solve each). Materials enter at omega (sigma_e and Drude / Lorentz poles complex). The line modes need >= 10 cells per lambda0 / |n| along the line (validation checks it). Typical 1.31e-6 or 1.55e-6 m.
- `n_modes` (int; default 20; range [0, inf)) - Modes per section
  Modes of each section line (slab_modes ranking: descending Re(k_t^2), evanescent last, PML modes kept); 0 = every active cell of the line, a complete basis: the mode matching is then exact for the discretised line (reciprocal S and, lossless, power conserved) but each section costs O(m^3) for m line cells. A truncated basis leaves a projection error that the section table reports as the interfaces' reciprocity defect (a run-log warning above 1e-3); raise n_modes until the port results converge. 10-40 typical, more for radiating (cpml) lines.
- `section_tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Section tolerance
  Slices whose material rows (permittivity, sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m, pole regions, PEC) differ from the first slice of the current section by at most this fraction of each row's largest |value| join that section (solved once, on its first slice); 0 = identical slices only. A value > 0 merges smoothly varying (e.g. heated) regions at the cost of a staircase in the material.
- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  The two faces along propagation_axis are the ports: the first and last cell layers of the domain continue to infinity, so their bc is not read (pec or pmc avoids the unused padding of cpml; periodic and mirrors are refused there). The two other (transverse) faces bound every section line as in the em_fdfd_* types: cpml absorbs outgoing waves in pml_cells extra cells added outside the domain. In the mode solve it is the complex coordinate stretch of the pml_* settings and the modes localised in it are kept (unlike em_modes and the mode ports): they stand for the radiation, so a radiating structure converges in n_modes more slowly. periodic must be set on both faces of the axis and wraps the field with the meshed window as period (uniform mesh: the size rounded up to whole cells) and no phase step (k = 0 along that axis, e.g. normal incidence); the em_fdtd_*, em_fdfd_* and em_modes types add a Bloch phase with bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear per input harmonic_channel; em_eme / em_eme_3d: k = 0 only). pec, pmc and the mirrors (symmetric / antisymmetric) pin the outermost cell as the em_fdfd_* walls do.
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic relative permittivity (>= 1): sets eps_zz (polarization ez) and eps_xx, eps_yy (hz) unless the material sets those components; may depend on x, y and physics fields. The mode solves use the complex permittivity at omega: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus every Drude / Lorentz pole chi(omega). For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf.
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (along the guide)
  z component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the one E_z sees (polarization ez); overrides eps_r for E_z.
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, x
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, y
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Help: shared `em_eme.sigma_e`
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1), 1 for practically every optical material; mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0) in the solve.
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss in Ohm/m, default 0: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0) (artificial absorbers only).

- `ez_im` - Im E_z (V/m)

- `hz_im` - Im H_z (A/m)

Output fields (primary e_abs):

- `ez_im` - Im E_z (V/m)
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (V/m)

- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (1)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `eps_sensitivity` - Objective sensitivity dJ/d eps_r (1/m^2)
- `design_density` - Design density (1)
- `hz_re` - Re H_z (A/m)
- `hz_im` - Im H_z (A/m)
- `hz_abs` - |H_z| (A/m)
- `hz_phase` - arg H_z (rad)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1)
- `eps_xy` - Relative permittivity xy (off-diagonal) (1)

Scalar outputs: Power fractions (unit 1) of the excitation (eme_ports, else mode 1 from lo) of the last solve: transmission_<k> into port mode k of the output face (k = 1 .. n_port_modes, modes found only), transmission and reflection summed over every mode of the output / input face (|S|^2 p_out / p_in; lossless: 1 = transmission + reflection, radiation into kept PML modes included). A missing value (an evanescent input mode, too few modes) gives NaN plus a run-log warning. Example derived value {"name": "T1", "expression": "eme_transmission_1"}.

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_eme.eme_ports` - Ports

Ports of the EME device and its excitation. Result 'table' (one row per reported port mode of each face, the input face first = reflection, then the output face = transmission): output_face, mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag (of that port mode, Im < 0 lossy), s_abs2 = |S|^2 of the bilinear-normalised amplitudes, phase_deg = arg S (the reference planes are the window faces along propagation_axis; each mode is real > 0 at its peak cell), power_fraction = |S|^2 p_out / p_in (p = the flux one unit of amplitude carries: power fractions are |S|^2 for lossless propagating modes). Port mode k = the k-th mode of the first / last section, the PML modes of cpml faces listed last. Extras: wavelength, input_face, input_mode, input_power, transmission and reflection (power fractions summed over every mode of the face), s_matrix_real / s_matrix_imag = the port S-matrix [[S11, S12], [S21, S22]] over the reported modes (lo modes first; S21 = lo -> hi) and s_matrix_modes {'lo': n, 'hi': n}. Without this feature the excitation is mode 1 at 1 W/m from lo. At most one per physics.

- FeatureSpec.type `eme_ports`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `input_face` (choice; default "lo"; choices lo | hi) - Input face
  Port face of the incident mode: lo = x_lo / y_lo of propagation_axis (travelling toward +axis), hi the opposite one.
- `input_mode` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Input mode
  Help: shared `em_eme.eme_ports.input_mode`
- `input_power` (float; unit W/m; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Input power
  Power per unit length in z of the incident mode; scales only the reconstructed fields (the S-matrix and power fractions do not depend on it).
- `n_port_modes` (int; default 4; range [1, inf)) - Reported port modes
  Port modes per face listed in the result table and the S-matrix extras, and the number of transmission_<k> scalar outputs.

### Feature `em_eme.eme_section_table` - Section table

Sections of the last solve. Result 'table', one row per section from lo to hi: section (1-based), start and length in m along propagation_axis, n_slices (cell layers), n_modes (modes found on its line), n_eff_1 / n_eff_2 (Re n_eff of its first two modes), power_defect and reciprocity_defect of the interface to the next section (NaN for the last): power = max over the propagating incident modes of |1 - power reflected and transmitted into propagating modes| (meaningful for lossless lines without cpml only), reciprocity = max |S12 - S21^T| / max |S21| (0 for a complete basis; the convergence measure in n_modes). Extra wavelength.

- FeatureSpec.type `eme_section_table`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none
