### Feature `em_eme.eme_bend` - Bend

Circular bend: the sections whose centre lies in [start, stop] along propagation_axis are a bend of radius R about the line coordinate reference, drawn straightened (the range length = the arc length at the reference, the angle = length / |R|). Exact for the 2D line: each bent section solves the cylindrical operator (r / R^2) d/dr (r du/dr) + k0^2 q (r / R)^2 (r = R + line coordinate - reference; ez q = eps mu, hz with the eps weights of the em_fdfd_hz line), so its n_eff = beta / k0 at r = R, propagation e^{-j beta R theta}, and the straight - bent interfaces are mode-matched like any other (radiation of a tight bend goes into the PML modes of cpml line faces). The field plot shows the straightened bend (the in-plane component along the axis is H_theta / E_theta); absorbed_power is the physical density, so its integral over the straightened drawing misses the factor r / R. Ranges must not overlap.

- FeatureSpec.type `eme_bend`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `start` (float; unit m; default 0) - Range start
  Lower end of the bend along propagation_axis [m, model coordinates]: the sections (cell layers) whose centre lies in [start, stop] belong to it.
- `stop` (float; unit m; default 1e-06) - Range stop
  Upper end of the bend along propagation_axis [m], > start.
- `radius` (float; unit m; default 1e-05) - Bend radius
  Radius R [m] of the reference line (the coordinate along the line axis (the other in-plane axis)); > 0 bends toward lower coordinates (the centre of curvature at reference - R), < 0 the other way. The bend angle is the range length / |R|; the centre of curvature must lie outside the section line or cross-section.
- `reference` (float; unit m; default 0) - Reference position
  the coordinate along the line axis (the other in-plane axis) [m, model coordinates] of the line whose radius is R: the drawn range length is its arc length and the section n_eff its beta / k0.

### Feature `em_eme.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor: the cells whose centre lies in the selected domains are inactive in every section line (u = 0 for ez; hz faces next to them carry no tangential E), staircased to the mesh.

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_eme.adjoint_objective` - Optimization objective

Objective term of the EME cascade adjoint: weight times a port power fraction of the excitation. Every solve records the quantity; the output field eps_sensitivity is dJ/d eps per unit area [1/m^2] of J = the sum of weight * quantity (ez: eps_r; hz: the sum of the eps_xx and eps_yy terms, both differentiated: the line cells and the face means along the line), from the forward and one adjoint cascade field (Lorentz reciprocity of the section equation: no extra mode solve; computed on the slices of the design regions, on every slice without one, when the field is read). Exact for a complete basis (n_modes 0), otherwise the same formula on the truncated fields (converging with n_modes). The drawn cell of an eme_periodic block stands for all its n_periods periods: its gradient sums the field products of every period. The port modes (first and last cell layer along propagation_axis) are held fixed; sigma_e, poles and mu_r are not differentiated. An optimization study maximises J by the design_region densities. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength: series value and weighted (unit 1); extras frequency, wavelength, quantity, mode_number, weight.

- FeatureSpec.type `adjoint_objective`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `quantity` (choice; default "transmission_mode"; choices transmission_mode | reflection_mode | transmission | reflection) - Quantity
  Help: shared `em_eme.adjoint_objective.quantity`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when quantity in (transmission_mode, reflection_mode)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_eme.adjoint_objective.mode_number`
- `weight` (float; unit 1; default 1) - Weight
  Factor of this term in J: 1 to maximise the quantity, -1 to minimise it, 0 to record it only.

### Feature `em_eme.design_region` - Design region

Density design region on the selected domains: each window cell carries a density rho in [0, 1], filtered by a conic filter of filter_radius and projected by a tanh of projection_beta / projection_eta to rho_bar, and gets eps = eps_min + rho_bar (eps_max - eps_min) (polarization ez: eps_r; hz: eps_xx and eps_yy, an isotropic change), overwriting the material permittivity there (sigma_e, poles and mu_r stay the material's). The same map and chain rule as the em_fdfd_* design_region. The optimization study varies rho to maximise the adjoint_objective sum J; any other study solves the initial_density design. Keep the region off the first and last cell layer along propagation_axis (the port sections: the build refuses it). Every distinct slice of the region becomes its own section (one mode solve each per evaluation). Design regions of one physics must not share cells. Output field design_density = rho_bar (0 outside every region). Result 'xy' versus iteration (0 = initial design): series objective (J of the whole model, unit 1: power fractions) and grayness (mean 4 rho_bar (1 - rho_bar), 0 = binary); extras n_cells, eps_min, eps_max, mean_density, final_grayness, note.

- FeatureSpec.type `design_region`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `eps_min` (float; unit 1; default 2.085; range [1, inf)) - Permittivity at density 0
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.eps_min`
- `eps_max` (float; unit 1; default 12.08; range [1, inf)) - Permittivity at density 1
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.eps_max`
- `initial_density` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range [0, 1]) - Initial density
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.initial_density`
- `filter_radius` (float; unit m; default 1e-07; range [0, inf)) - Filter radius
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.filter_radius`
- `projection_beta` (float; unit 1; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Projection sharpness
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.projection_beta`
- `projection_eta` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range [0, 1]) - Projection threshold
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.projection_eta`

## Physics type `em_eme_3d` - Electromagnetic Waves, eigenmode expansion (3D)

Bidirectional eigenmode expansion (EME) of a 3D device along z, for waveguide devices long along z (tapers, phase shifters, couplers) where em_fdtd_3d would be large. Every z cell layer is a slice; consecutive equal layers (section_tolerance) form a section, so z variations are staircases at the z mesh (refine or grade it). Each section is solved once for n_modes full-vector cross-section modes (the em_modes discretisation of the xy plane with the transverse bc_* faces; complex PML stretch with the PML modes kept as radiation; repeated layers reuse their modes). Modes are normalised to the unconjugated product <e, h> = sum (E x H).z dA = 1 (stretched dual areas; degenerate modes recombined orthogonal); interfaces are mode-matched by these overlaps and the S-matrices cascaded by Redheffer star products (stable with evanescent modes), converging in n_modes (section table reciprocity_defect). The z faces are semi-infinite ports at the window planes (no z padding). Outputs of the excitation (eme_ports): the reconstructed E phasor at the cell centres (sum over modes of a_n e^{-j beta_n s} + b_n e^{-j beta_n (L - s)} per section; E_z of the backward waves with the opposite sign): ex / ey / ez _re / _im, e_abs (primary), e_intensity, absorbed_power (1/2 omega eps0 (-Im eps) times the 3-point Gauss z mean of |E|^2 per cell, on lossy sections), and the permittivity arrays, shown as cut planes (an x or y cut shows the propagation). Scalar outputs transmission_<k>, transmission, reflection. pec_domain cells; eme_bend (bend map of cross_section_modes), eme_periodic (a drawn period repeated n times, its Bloch modes), adjoint_objective (port power fractions; output field eps_sensitivity = dJ/d eps from the cascade adjoint, no extra mode solve; no optimization study in 3D yet). em_heat_joule reads absorbed_power; heat_em_thermo_optic writes eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy. Host memory dominates (one cross-section factorisation at a time, the cached mode sets, the partial cascades); GPU: 28 B per cell of fields and q_abs plus the material arrays (an eigen solver node with factorization 'cudss' factorises each cross-section on the GPU instead, a general LU: the operator is not complex symmetric). Studies: stationary and frequency_domain (each wavelength starts every section's shift-invert from the summed physical modes of its previous solve, when cached). Cannot share the model with another EM type. The instance is usually named 'eme'.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_eme_3d`; default instance name `eme`
- Supported studies: stationary, frequency_domain
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): e_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_eme_3d.<feature>`): eme_ports, eme_section_table, eme_length_sweep, eme_periodic, eme_bend, pec_domain, adjoint_objective

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda0 of a stationary solve (omega = 2 pi C0 / lambda0); a frequency_domain study solves its own wavelengths instead (one cold solve each). Materials enter at omega (sigma_e and Drude / Lorentz poles complex). Typical 1.31e-6 or 1.55e-6 m.
- `n_modes` (int; default 20; range [1, inf)) - Modes per section
  Cross-section modes of each section (shift-invert near (k0 n_eff_guess)^2, ranked by descending Re(beta^2) with the PML modes kept and listed after the others). A truncated basis leaves a projection error that the section table reports as the interfaces' reciprocity defect (a run-log warning above 1e-3); raise n_modes until the port results converge. Each section costs one sparse factorisation of 2 nx ny unknowns plus about 2 n_modes + 10 Arnoldi vectors. 10-40 typical.
- `n_eff_guess` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Effective index guess
  Effective index around which the modes of every section are sought (shift-invert target (k0 n_eff_guess)^2). Empty: the largest Re sqrt(eps mu) of each cross-section, which finds its most strongly guided modes first.
- `section_tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Section tolerance
  z layers whose material rows (eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_r, sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m, pole regions) differ from the first layer of the current section by at most this fraction of each array's largest |value| over the window join that section (solved once, on its first layer); 0 = identical layers only. A value > 0 merges smoothly varying (e.g. heated) regions at the cost of a staircase in the material: with a heat coupling every heated layer differs, so set e.g. 1e-5.
- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  Transverse faces of every cross-section (the xy plane of each z layer), as in em_modes. The two z faces are the ports: the first and last z cell layers of the domain continue to infinity (no z padding). cpml absorbs outgoing waves in pml_cells extra cells added outside the domain. In the mode solves it is the complex coordinate stretch of the pml_* settings and the modes localised in it are kept (unlike em_modes): they stand for the radiation, so a radiating structure converges in n_modes more slowly. periodic must be set on both faces of the axis and wraps the field with the meshed window as period (uniform mesh: the size rounded up to whole cells) and no phase step (k = 0 along that axis, e.g. normal incidence); the em_fdtd_*, em_fdfd_* and em_modes types add a Bloch phase with bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear per input harmonic_channel; em_eme / em_eme_3d: k = 0 only). pec, pmc and the mirrors (symmetric / antisymmetric) make the outermost cell a ghost outside the wall plane, as em_modes does.
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic relative permittivity (>= 1): sets eps_zz (the E_z array eps_r) and eps_xx, eps_yy unless the material sets those components; may depend on x, y, z and physics fields. The mode solves use the complex permittivity at omega: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus every Drude / Lorentz pole chi(omega). For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf.
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (along the guide)
  z component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the one E_z (along the propagation axis) sees.
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, x
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, y
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Help: shared `em_eme.sigma_e`
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1); mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0) in the solve.
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss in Ohm/m, default 0: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0) (artificial absorbers only).

### Fields

State fields:
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (eps_zz) (1)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity (eps_xx) (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity (eps_yy) (1)

Output fields (primary e_abs):
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `ex_re` - Re E_x (phasor, centre) (V/m)
- `ex_im` - Im E_x (phasor, centre) (V/m)
- `ey_re` - Re E_y (phasor, centre) (V/m)
- `ey_im` - Im E_y (phasor, centre) (V/m)
- `ez_re` - Re E_z (phasor, centre) (V/m)
- `ez_im` - Im E_z (phasor, centre) (V/m)
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (eps_zz) (1)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity (eps_xx) (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity (eps_yy) (1)
- `eps_sensitivity` - Objective sensitivity dJ/d eps (isotropic) (1/m^3)

Scalar outputs: Power fractions (unit 1) of the excitation (eme_ports, else mode 1 from lo) of the last solve: transmission_<k> into port mode k of the output face (k = 1 .. n_port_modes, modes found only), transmission and reflection summed over every mode of the output / input face (|S|^2 p_out / p_in; lossless: 1 = transmission + reflection, radiation into kept PML modes included). A missing value (an evanescent input mode, too few modes) gives NaN plus a run-log warning. Example derived value {"name": "T1", "expression": "eme_transmission_1"}.

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_eme_3d.eme_ports` - Ports

Ports of the 3D EME device (the z_lo / z_hi window planes) and its excitation. Result 'table' (one row per reported port mode of each face, the input face first = reflection, then the output face = transmission): output_face, mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag (of that port mode, Im < 0 lossy), s_abs2 = |S|^2 of the bilinear-normalised amplitudes, phase_deg = arg S (reference planes = the window z faces; each mode is phased with its dominant transverse E real > 0 at its peak), power_fraction = |S|^2 p_out / p_in (p = the power one unit of amplitude carries). Port mode k = the k-th mode of the first / last section with the PML modes listed last. Extras: wavelength, input_face, input_mode, input_power, transmission and reflection (summed over every mode of the face), s_matrix_real / s_matrix_imag over the reported modes (lo first) and s_matrix_modes. Without this feature the excitation is mode 1 at 1 W from z_lo. At most one per physics.

- FeatureSpec.type `eme_ports`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `input_face` (choice; default "lo"; choices lo | hi) - Input face
  Port face of the incident mode: lo = z_lo (travelling toward +z), hi = z_hi.
- `input_mode` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Input mode
  Help: shared `em_eme.eme_ports.input_mode`
- `input_power` (float; unit W; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Input power
  Power of the incident mode [W]; scales only the reconstructed fields (the S-matrix and power fractions do not depend on it).
- `n_port_modes` (int; default 4; range [1, inf)) - Reported port modes
  Port modes per face listed in the result table and the S-matrix extras, and the number of transmission_<k> scalar outputs.

Circular bend in the xz plane: the sections whose centre lies in [start, stop] along z are a bend of radius R about x = reference, drawn straightened (the range length = the arc length at the reference, the angle = length / |R|). Each bent section is solved with the cross_section_modes bend map (model 'exact': the transformation-optics image of the curved guide, eps and mu scaled by the radial factor), so its n_eff = beta / k0 at the reference radius and the straight - bent interfaces are mode-matched like any other (bend radiation goes into the PML modes of cpml x faces: raise n_modes). The bend angle is the range length / |R|; the centre of curvature must lie outside the section line or cross-section.
- `reference` (float; unit m; default 0) - Reference position
  the x coordinate (the bend lies in the xz plane, about an axis along y) [m, model coordinates] of the line whose radius is R: the drawn range length is its arc length and the section n_eff its beta / k0.

### Feature `em_eme_3d.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor cells of every section cross-section (the em_modes rule: E_z = 0 at the centres of the selected cells, E_x / E_y = 0 on faces between two of them, the normal E on a conductor surface stays free), staircased to the mesh; in the absorbed power they count as lossless. Select objects: 'all' is refused.

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_eme_3d.adjoint_objective` - Optimization objective

Objective term of the EME cascade adjoint: weight times a port power fraction of the excitation. Every solve records the quantity; the output field eps_sensitivity is dJ/d eps per unit volume [1/m^3] of J = the sum of weight * quantity for an isotropic change (the sum of the eps_xx, eps_yy and eps_r terms; scripts read each component from EMEPhysics3D.eps_sensitivity().cell_gradients), from the forward and one adjoint cascade field (Lorentz reciprocity of the Yee cross-section: no extra mode solve; every window z layer, computed when the field is read). Exact for a complete basis of every cross-section; the em_eme_3d bases are truncated (n_modes), so it is the same formula on the truncated fields, converging with n_modes. The drawn cell of an eme_periodic block stands for all its n_periods periods (its gradient sums every period). The port modes (first and last z cell layer) are held fixed; sigma_e, poles and mu_r are not differentiated. em_eme_3d has no design_region and no optimization study yet: the field shows where a small material change raises or lowers J. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength: series value and weighted (unit 1); extras frequency, wavelength, quantity, mode_number, weight.

- FeatureSpec.type `adjoint_objective`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `quantity` (choice; default "transmission_mode"; choices transmission_mode | reflection_mode | transmission | reflection) - Quantity
  Help: shared `em_eme.adjoint_objective.quantity`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when quantity in (transmission_mode, reflection_mode)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_eme.adjoint_objective.mode_number`
- `weight` (float; unit 1; default 1) - Weight
  Factor of this term in J: 1 to maximise the quantity, -1 to minimise it, 0 to record it only.

## Physics type `em_fdfd_3d` - Electromagnetic Waves, frequency domain (3D)

3D finite-difference frequency-domain eigensolver on the em_fdtd_3d Yee grid: E_x, E_y, E_z on the +x / +y / +z faces of each cell in V/m, H_x, H_y, H_z on its (+y +z) / (+x +z) / (+x +y) edges in A/m. The eigenfrequency study solves curl (mu^-1 curl E) = (omega / C0)^2 eps E for the resonances nearest the target wavelength setting (host SuperLU shift-invert of the operator assembled there, ARPACK on the squared Cayley map, which sends the static gradient solutions to 0; materials and PML frozen at the target), on the live E faces only (PEC faces, mirror planes and ghost cells dropped, Bloch phases in the wrap entries). Materials as em_fdtd_3d: eps_r or the diagonal eps_xx / eps_yy / eps_zz, sigma_e and Drude / Lorentz poles as eps(omega_t) = eps - j sigma_e / (omega_t eps0) + chi(omega_t) (face means of the two cells; solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing replaces the background eps of interface faces by the em_fdtd_3d anisotropic average, so curved surfaces converge smoothly), mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega_t mu0) of the lower cell per H edge. Boundaries per face: cpml (complex stretch at omega_t), pec, pmc, periodic (Bloch k), symmetric / antisymmetric mirror. Features: pec_domain, resonance_table. Outputs of the selected resonance (each scaled to 1 V/m real at its largest E sample): the raw components ex / ey / ez / hx / hy / hz _re / _im / _abs (H = j curl E / (omega mu0 mu) at the complex resonance omega), e_abs (primary), e_intensity, h_abs (cell centres), w_e = eps0 / 4 sum eps_c |E_c|^2 and eps_r, shown as cut planes. Host memory dominates: the 3D factor grows ~ n^(4/3) with n = the E unknowns (~3 per cell; a solver size rule warns above 1e6 and refuses 4e6); device: 48 B per cell of fields plus the material arrays. heat_em_thermo_optic writes eps_r (+ eps_xx / eps_yy) as a background coupling. On a 'tetrahedra' mesh (finite elements): Nedelec edge elements of the discretization setting (quadratic default), materials one value per element, the cpml faces a PML shell of pml_cells x the maximum element size meshed with the window (complex stretch tensor), the same eigen solve (squared Cayley map, sparse mass) and outputs sampled at points (cut planes on a uniform sample lattice, derived values at quadrature points); periodic faces (Bloch k: hi-side unknowns identified with the lo side times the phase, a nonsymmetric LU factor) need the builtin mesher; subpixel smoothing does not apply there. The instance is usually named 'em'.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdfd_3d`; default instance name `em`
- Supported studies: eigenfrequency
- Default study: {"type": "eigenfrequency", "settings": {"n_resonances": 6}}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): e_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdfd_3d.<feature>`): pec_domain, resonance_table

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi`, `bc_z_lo`, `bc_z_hi` (choice; default "pec"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge / Lower z face / Upper z face
  Boundary of this face of the 3D box, the em_fdtd_3d faces on the same Yee grid: cpml = the complex coordinate stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0) of the pml_* settings in pml_cells extra cells outside the domain, evaluated at the target wavelength (frozen: the resonances near it see the right stretch); pec = tangential E 0 at the centres of the outermost domain cell layer (that layer becomes perfect conductor); pmc = tangential H 0 on the outer face of the outermost cell (the grid edge: pec and pmc walls lie half a cell apart); periodic on both faces of an axis, with the Bloch phase bloch_k<axis> (0 = plain periodic). Mirror planes (any face, E parity as em_fdtd_3d): symmetric = E mirror-even (tangential H and normal E 0 on the plane, a PMC mirror), antisymmetric = E mirror-odd (tangential E odd: a PEC mirror), on the domain edge itself (one ghost cell is added outside it); each mirror halves the unknowns of the direct solve, and the eigenfrequency study setting parity_sectors solves every parity of the mirror faces in turn. Unknowns are the live E faces only: faces between two PEC cells, the normal E on a symmetric plane and the ghost cells are dropped.
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Target wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda_t of the target (omega_t = 2 pi C0 / lambda_t): the eigenfrequency study returns the resonances nearest it. The operator is assembled there: sigma_e and the Drude / Lorentz poles enter as eps(omega_t), the PML as its stretch at omega_t, so a resonance is exact for non-dispersive, PML-free models and accurate to first order in |omega / omega_t - 1| otherwise: for an accurate Q of an open or dispersive resonator set it near the resonance and re-run. It may coincide with a resonance (the shift-invert shift sits 1e-4 above lambda_t^-2). The mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda_t / n. Typical 0.4e-6 to 2e-6 m.
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Bloch wave vector along x in rad/m, used only when bc_x_lo and bc_x_hi are periodic: the fields repeat with the phase exp(-j kx L) per period L (the meshed period, exp(+j omega t)); kx and kx + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. The resonances at fixed k are the bands of the lattice at that k (sweep a parameter for a band diagram); the operator becomes complex (no extra unknowns). Typical: pi / L at the zone edge.
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Bloch wave vector along y in rad/m, used only when bc_y_lo and bc_y_hi are periodic: the fields repeat with the phase exp(-j ky L) per period L (the meshed period, exp(+j omega t)); ky and ky + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. The resonances at fixed k are the bands of the lattice at that k (sweep a parameter for a band diagram); the operator becomes complex (no extra unknowns). Typical: pi / L at the zone edge.
- `bloch_kz` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_z_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector z
  Bloch wave vector along z in rad/m, used only when bc_z_lo and bc_z_hi are periodic: the fields repeat with the phase exp(-j kz L) per period L (the meshed period, exp(+j omega t)); kz and kz + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. The resonances at fixed k are the bands of the lattice at that k (sweep a parameter for a band diagram); the operator becomes complex (no extra unknowns). Typical: pi / L at the zone edge.
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Nedelec (edge element, first kind) degree on a tetrahedron mesh (MeshSpec kind tetrahedra; ignored on tensor meshes): quadratic (degree 2, 20 unknowns per element: 2 per edge and face) or linear (degree 1, one per edge); straight-sided elements (curved surfaces are faceted at the mesh size).

- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
