### Feature `em_fdfd_3d.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor cells: every E face between two selected cells is dropped from the unknowns (E = 0 there; the surface lies at the centres of the outermost conductor cells), a face between a conductor and another cell takes the other cell's permittivity (the normal E on the surface stays free), as em_fdtd_3d. Select objects: 'all' is refused. Staircased (no conformal option yet).

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_3d.resonance_table` - Resonance table

Resonances of the last eigenfrequency solve, nearest the target (the wavelength setting) first. Result 'table', one row per resonance: resonance_number (1-based rank by |omega - omega_target|), wavelength = 2 pi C0 / Re(omega) in m, frequency = Re(omega) / (2 pi) and frequency_imag = Im(omega) / (2 pi) in Hz (exp(+j omega t): > 0 decays), q_factor = Re(omega) / (2 Im(omega)) (inf when |Im omega| < 1e-12 Re omega: lossless and closed; negative = a growing, non-physical solution, usually a PML artefact), pml_fraction (share of the electric energy sum |Re eps| |E|^2 dV of the E faces in PML and padding cells: resonances above 0.5 are dropped, above ~1e-2 the PML shapes the resonance: widen the cladding); extras target_wavelength (m) and selected_resonance. With parity_sectors each sector has its own table (Results.sector_result). Optional domain selection = a region (e.g. a box around the cavity core): the table then ends with the column region_energy_fraction (share of the same energy weights on the E faces of the selected cells (each cell owns its +x / +y / +z faces; a mirror plane face counts with the ghost cell, so a region on a mirror face reads a little low), on tetrahedra in the dofs of the selected elements), and resonances below min_region_fraction are dropped from the solve like PML modes (table rows, snapshots and resonance numbers all skip them): a localised cavity mode passes, slab, rim, band-edge and cladding modes do not. One region per physics (one resonance_table with a selection); 'all' is refused.

- FeatureSpec.type `resonance_table`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 0
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `min_region_fraction` (float; unit 1; default 0; range [0, 1]) - Minimum region fraction
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.resonance_table.min_region_fraction`

## Physics type `em_fdfd_bor` - Electromagnetic Waves, frequency domain (axisymmetric, azimuthal order m)

Body-of-revolution (BOR) finite-difference frequency-domain solver: the drawing is the (r, z) half plane of a rotationally symmetric structure about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z), the fields of one azimuthal order m. Fields vary as exp(j (omega t - m phi)): the phasors shown are those of that travelling wave at phi = 0; a standing wave (the +m and -m modes, degenerate in a rotationally invariant structure) has E_r, E_z ~ cos(m phi) and E_phi ~ sin(m phi) with the same profiles. All six components are solved (they couple for m != 0) on the 3D cylindrical Yee cell projected onto the half plane (finite-integration form, exact ring areas and volumes): E_phi, H_r at the cell centres (H_r on the +z edge), E_r, H_z on the +r cell edges, E_z on the +z edges, H_phi at the +r+z corner; the axis carries only the m = 0 H_z unknown (|m| = 1: E_r, H_phi there recovered from cell 0 by regularity; larger |m|: none). True 3D results of disks, rings, pillars, spheres (staircased), lenses, vertical cavities and on-axis dipoles at 2D cost. Solved on the host: solver role 'linear' = sparse_direct (host SuperLU; a 'cusolver_qr' node is a validation error), one factor per wavelength and material state, reused as GMRES preconditioner after a material change at the same wavelength (thermo-optic iteration); with back_end 'cudss' / 'cudss_mixed' (GPU backend, nvmath-python) a cuDSS LDL^T on the GPU instead, without the host size limit, every later factorisation of the same sparsity (other wavelengths, material states, orders of an order sum) reusing the first one's cuDSS plan; role 'eigen' = arpack_shift_invert (eigenfrequency study: its tolerance / subspace_size; the finite-integration operator is complex symmetric, so factorization cudss is a cuDSS LDL^T on the GPU without the host size limit and cudss_mixed its complex64 form: loose solves, then the float64 Rayleigh quotient of every resonance); role 'shifted' (every study): Automatic (sparse_direct) changes nothing, a line_block node factors every driven system and every shift-invert operator on its backend instead (unknowns ordered by z rows or r columns, whichever is cheaper; the orders of an azimuthal_orders list with |m| >= 2 in one batch of A(m) = K0 + m K1 + m^2 K2 - k0^2 M; in a frequency_domain study of one order up to 8 wavelengths in one batch of whole operators, as many as 60 % of the free memory holds; mixed or double precision, refined against the complex128 operator), and a solve it rejects (residual above its accept tolerance, e.g. a nearly singular indefinite system) goes to host SuperLU with a run-log warning. Needs scipy; 3 unknowns per cell incl. PML, so validation warns near and refuses beyond the factor size limit. Studies: stationary (one driven solve at the wavelength setting, iterated with heat through heat_em_thermo_optic / em_heat_joule; the heat physics should be axisymmetric too), frequency_domain (one driven solve per wavelength; with an azimuthal_orders list both driven studies sum the orders of off-axis point sources into the 3D field, see that setting) and eigenfrequency (shift-invert resonances nearest the wavelength setting: complex omega, Q from material loss and radiation into the PML, whispering-gallery modes of disks and rings from one 2D solve) and optomechanics (as the optical physics an optomechanical_coupling of an axisymmetric solid_mechanics names: the same eigen-solve with n_optical_resonances, then the g0 table; triangles mesh only, an em_fdfd_bor no coupling names solves as a stationary background physics). Outputs at the cell centres: er, ephi, ez, hr, hphi, hz (Re of the phasors at phi = 0, V/m and A/m), their moduli <component>_abs, e_abs, e_intensity (|E|^2, the primary field), h_abs, absorbed_power (state q_abs = 1/2 omega eps0 sum_c (-Im eps_c) |E_c|^2 in W/m^3, the cell mean over the component points; em_heat_joule hands it to heat) and the permittivity arrays eps_r (eps_phiphi), eps_xx (eps_rr), eps_yy (axial eps_zz) / sigma_e. Diagonal anisotropy in cylindrical components (rotationally invariant): see the eps_* material properties. A resonance is scaled to 1 real at its largest component (V/m). Field derived values weight by the ring volume 2 pi r dr dz (the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave: |F|^2 does not depend on phi; a standing cos(m phi) wave has half the integral), and so do powers. Features: point_source (current elements), mode_source / mode_monitor (vector guided modes of a guide along the axis at the azimuthal order, horizontal lines from the axis or annular ones from an inner radius), field_probe, flux_monitor (W through a disc, annulus or cylinder, exactly conserved), far_field (W/sr in the meridional plane), pec_domain, resonance_table. Cannot share a model with in-plane EM types (validation error). heat_em_thermo_optic writes all three permittivity arrays (slots eps_r_update, eps_xx_update, eps_yy_update). On a triangles mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles) the eigenfrequency and optomechanics studies run on mixed axisymmetric finite elements instead (see discretization: curved outlines followed, materials and state fields one value per element, the same resonance_table); driven studies and the source / monitor features stay on tensor meshes. The instance is usually named 'em'.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdfd_bor`; default instance name `em`
- Supported studies: eigenfrequency, stationary, frequency_domain, optomechanics
- Default study: {"type": "eigenfrequency"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): e_intensity
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdfd_bor.<feature>`): point_source, field_probe, pec_domain, mode_source, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, far_field, resonance_table

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "axisymmetric"; choices axisymmetric) - Geometry
  Always axisymmetric: the drawing is the (r, z) half plane of a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z). The setting exists so that coupled physics with a geometry setting (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics) recognise a consistent axisymmetric partner (no planar-partner warning).
- `bc_x_lo` (choice; default "axis"; choices axis) - Left edge
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.bc_x_lo`
- `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc) - Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.bc_x_lo`
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda0 of the solve in a stationary study (omega = 2 pi C0 / lambda0); an eigenfrequency study searches the resonances nearest it (the target); a frequency_domain study solves its own wavelengths and ignores it (validation info when it is not the default). The mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / |n| in every material and >= 2 per skin depth in lossy ones (validation checks both). Typical 0.4e-6 to 2e-6 m.
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; range [0, 10000]) - Azimuthal order
  Azimuthal order m >= 0: fields ~ exp(-j m phi), one (r, z) solve per order (+m and -m are degenerate in a rotationally invariant structure: the same resonances and |fields|). m = 0: the rotationally symmetric fields (TE-like E_phi, H_r, H_z and TM-like E_r, E_z, H_phi decouple: on-axis dipoles, radial modes of disks and pillars); m = 1: the fields of an on-axis focused or plane wave and the fundamental modes of fibres and vertical cavities (E_r, E_phi, H_phi are non-zero on the axis); larger m: whispering-gallery modes of disks, rings and spheres, m ~ 2 pi R n_eff / lambda. For the free spectral range or the m of a resonance in an eigenfrequency study, list the orders in azimuthal_orders instead (one run, one assembly); likewise for an off-axis point source in a driven study (the sum over m of its Fourier terms).
- `azimuthal_orders` (float_list; unit 1; range [0, 10000]; optional (null allowed)) - Azimuthal order list
  Distinct integer orders m >= 0 solved in one run; a non-empty list replaces azimuthal_order. The materials are read and the operator parts K0, K1, K2 assembled once (A(m) = K0 + m K1 + m^2 K2 - k0^2 M). Eigenfrequency study: n_resonances resonances are searched per order near the wavelength setting; resonance numbers run order by order in list order (nearest the target first within each), snapshot labels read 'resonance k: m = <m>, lambda = ...', and the resonance_table has a column azimuthal_order (a curve with x column azimuthal_order plots lambda versus m: the free spectral range). Stationary / frequency_domain study: the driven order sum of off-axis sources: every point_source is then a 3D point current element at phi = 0 (see point_source) expanded into its Fourier terms exp(-j m phi); each listed m > 0 is solved together with -m (one factor per order: A(-m) is the phi mirror of A(m)) and the terms are summed. Shown fields and field_probe values are the phi = 0 half plane of the summed 3D field (the source side; ring-weighted field integrals of them are no 3D integrals), absorbed_power (q_abs, what em_heat_joule hands to heat) is its phi average; flux_monitor and far_field add the orders exactly and report each order too. List every order 0, 1, ..., M: the far field and powers converge once M exceeds k rho_s by a few (rho_s = source radius, k = n omega / c), fields near the source need more. mode_source / mode_monitor need a single order (validation error); each order costs one factorisation per wavelength (nothing is kept between solves). With a line_block shifted solver the orders of one axis class (|m| >= 1) are factorised in one batch. null or [] = azimuthal_order alone.
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Element order on a triangles mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles; tensor meshes ignore it and use the Yee cell). Eigenfrequency study only: the mixed axisymmetric elements, Nedelec edge elements for E_r, E_z and Lagrange elements for r E_phi of the same degree (discrete gradients are exact static solutions, so no spurious modes), elements with a curved edge mapped isoparametrically (quadratic), so disks, toroids and spheres follow the drawn outline instead of a staircase. quadratic (default) or linear (Whitney / P1: cheaper, error ~h^2 instead of ~h^4 in k^2, and the layer of elements on the axis is stiff for m = 0 / |m| = 1 fields there). About 7 (quadratic) or 2 (linear) unknowns per element, one assembly per solve (K0 + m K1 + m^2 K2 for every listed order), shift-invert by the eigen solver: host SuperLU, or with its factorization cudss a cuDSS LDL^T on the GPU (complex symmetric pencil), cudss_mixed its complex64 form with float64 Rayleigh quotients. Materials are one value per element; a cpml face gets a ring of mesh pml_layers element layers with the stretch of the pml_* settings (the stretched radius in every metric factor) and a pec outer side; pec_domain removes its elements and holds tangential E = 0 on their outline. Not available on triangles (validation errors): stationary and frequency_domain studies (driven solves) and every source / monitor feature (point_source, field_probe, flux_monitor, far_field, mode ports); resonance_table and pec_domain work.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic relative permittivity (>= 1) of all three components (eps_rr, eps_phiphi, eps_zz); n^2 of a lossless dielectric (silicon ~12.1, silica ~2.1 at 1.55 um); may depend on r (x), z (y) and physics fields; a component property wins over it. Diagonal anisotropy in cylindrical components is rotationally invariant: the drawing-plane names map as eps_xx = eps_rr (E_r, radial), eps_yy = eps_zz of the rotation axis (E_z, axial; the drawing y is z) and eps_zz = eps_phiphi (E_phi, out of the drawing plane; it writes the eps_r array). A crystal with its optic axis along the rotation axis (z-cut, uniaxial) sets eps_r = n_o^2 and eps_yy = n_e^2; a radially anisotropic shell sets eps_xx. E_phi sees the cell value, E_r and E_z (on the cell edges) the ring-volume / length weighted mean of their two cells (no subpixel smoothing). The solve uses the complex permittivity at the solve wavelength: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus the susceptibility chi(omega) of every Drude / Lorentz pole (exp(+j omega t): loss has Im < 0).
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, phi (azimuthal)
  eps_phiphi: the azimuthal component, the only one E_phi sees (the out-of-plane component of the drawing, stored in the eps_r array: it overrides eps_r for E_phi only). Not the axial component: that is eps_yy. Diagonal anisotropy in cylindrical components is rotationally invariant: the drawing-plane names map as eps_xx = eps_rr (E_r, radial), eps_yy = eps_zz of the rotation axis (E_z, axial; the drawing y is z) and eps_zz = eps_phiphi (E_phi, out of the drawing plane; it writes the eps_r array). A crystal with its optic axis along the rotation axis (z-cut, uniaxial) sets eps_r = n_o^2 and eps_yy = n_e^2; a radially anisotropic shell sets eps_xx.
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, r (radial)
  eps_rr: the radial component, the only one E_r sees (ring-volume weighted mean of the two cells of its r edge). Diagonal anisotropy in cylindrical components is rotationally invariant: the drawing-plane names map as eps_xx = eps_rr (E_r, radial), eps_yy = eps_zz of the rotation axis (E_z, axial; the drawing y is z) and eps_zz = eps_phiphi (E_phi, out of the drawing plane; it writes the eps_r array). A crystal with its optic axis along the rotation axis (z-cut, uniaxial) sets eps_r = n_o^2 and eps_yy = n_e^2; a radially anisotropic shell sets eps_xx.
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, z (axial, drawing y)
  Axial eps_zz (along the rotation axis = the drawing y): the only component E_z sees (length weighted mean of the two cells of its z edge). Diagonal anisotropy in cylindrical components is rotationally invariant: the drawing-plane names map as eps_xx = eps_rr (E_r, radial), eps_yy = eps_zz of the rotation axis (E_z, axial; the drawing y is z) and eps_zz = eps_phiphi (E_phi, out of the drawing plane; it writes the eps_r array). A crystal with its optic axis along the rotation axis (z-cut, uniaxial) sets eps_r = n_o^2 and eps_yy = n_e^2; a radially anisotropic shell sets eps_xx.
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss in S/m, default 0: every permittivity component gains -j sigma_e / (omega eps0); a weak absorber of index n and extinction kappa has sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0. Model metals with a Drude pole (it adds to all three components).
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1), 1 for optical materials; H_r, H_phi and H_z take the mean of the cells around their points. The solve uses mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0).
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss in Ohm/m, default 0: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0) (artificial absorbers only).

### Fields

State fields:
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity phi phi (1)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity rr (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity zz (axial) (1)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)
- `q_abs` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)

Output fields (primary e_intensity):
- `er` - Re E_r (V/m)
- `ephi` - Re E_phi (V/m)
- `ez` - Re E_z (V/m)
- `hr` - Re H_r (A/m)
- `hphi` - Re H_phi (A/m)
- `hz` - Re H_z (A/m)
- `er_abs` - |E_r| (V/m)
- `ephi_abs` - |E_phi| (V/m)
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (V/m)
- `hr_abs` - |H_r| (A/m)
- `hphi_abs` - |H_phi| (A/m)
- `hz_abs` - |H_z| (A/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity phi phi (1)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity rr (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity zz (axial) (1)

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdfd_bor.point_source` - Point source

Current element in the cell containing the point (x = r, y = z), a ring in 3D with the exp(-j m phi) dependence of the azimuthal order; see component. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "z"; choices r | phi | z) - Direction
  Current direction: 'phi' J_phi = I / (w h) in the cell (m = 0: a current loop of radius r carrying I, a magnetic dipole on the axis); 'z' / 'r': the current I through the ring cross-section of the cell, 2 pi r w (axial) / 2 pi r h (radial), split onto its two edge points (m = 0: the total current; in the axis cell 'z' is an on-axis electric dipole of moment I h, h = cell height; 'r' in the axis cell at |m| = 1 is the rotating transverse dipole of moment I w / 2). For m != 0, I is the amplitude of the exp(-j m phi) current distribution. In a driven order sum (azimuthal_orders in a stationary / frequency_domain study) the element is instead a 3D point current at phi = 0 (in the drawing plane; 'phi' points out of it) of dipole moment I d, d = the cell height for z, its width for r and phi: every order then carries the ring current I (r, z) or I d / (2 pi r) (phi), and in free space it radiates eta0 k^2 (I d)^2 / (12 pi) wherever it sits.
- `current` (float; unit A; default 0.001) - Current
  Current I [A] of the element (see component); fields scale linearly with it. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phasor phase of the current in degrees (0 = cos carrier, as the em_fdfd_* sources).

### Feature `em_fdfd_bor.field_probe` - Field probe

Phasor of one field component in the cell containing the point at every driven solve (a driven order sum: of the summed field at phi = 0). Result 'xy' versus wavelength: series abs (unit of the component) and phase (rad); extras frequency, wavelength, component, unit.

- FeatureSpec.type `field_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "ez"; choices er | ephi | ez | hr | hphi | hz) - Field component
  Component recorded: its complex phasor at the centre of the cell containing the point (edge points averaged there), per driven solve (stationary, frequency_domain).

### Feature `em_fdfd_bor.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor (rings in 3D): E_phi = 0 at the centre of every cell whose centre lies in the selected domains and E_r / E_z = 0 on the edges between two such cells, staircased to the mesh. On a triangles mesh its elements leave the unknowns and tangential E (E_phi included) is held 0 on their outline (exact on curved outlines with discretization quadratic).

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source` - Mode source

Port source launching one guided mode of a waveguide along the axis (fibre, pillar, metal pipe, coaxial guide) from a horizontal line in one direction: a one-sided total-field / scattered-field interface between the line row and the row upstream, the mode entering the right-hand side through the operator rows on both sides, so the launch is exact and one-sided on a straight guide. The port line must be horizontal (z = const). It starts on the axis (x0 = 0) or at an inner radius x0 > 0, an annular line whose start is a metal (pec) end on that cell edge (coaxial guides with the line from the inner conductor surface, ring-shaped cores whose field is small toward the axis); it ends either on the last window cell (then it continues through the r_hi cpml cells, or ends on the pec / pmc r_hi wall) or inside the domain, again a metal end on that cell edge (extend the line well into the cladding: the run log warns when the mode still has 1% of its peak field at a metal end; exact when the cells beyond a metal end are pec in the model, e.g. a pec_domain inner conductor). Vertical (r = const) port lines are not supported. The guided modes ~ exp(-j beta z) of the line at the azimuthal order are full-vector solutions of the body-of-revolution operator itself on a straight guide (all six components; the line cells and their row width), re-solved at every solved wavelength and after every material change, so the launch / decomposition is exact for a guide invariant along z with uniform rows for a cell on each side of the line (the run log warns otherwise). Modes are ranked by descending Re n_eff (mode 1 = the highest), radiation modes with more than half of their energy in the PML dropped; each carries 1 W (the exactly conserved discrete flux of flux_monitor) in the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave. Result 'table' of the latest port solve (a frequency_domain study: its last solved wavelength), one row per mode found (up to max(mode_number + 2, 4)): mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss), loss_db_per_cm, n_group (from the pencil derivative, without material dispersion), edge_field (largest |field| at the line end / peak) and selected; extras wavelength (m), power (W), direction, mode_number and phase (deg).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `power` (float; unit W; default 1; range [0, inf)) - Power
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.power`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, 50]) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (choice; default "positive"; choices positive | negative) - Direction
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.direction`
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phase of the launched mode amplitude sqrt(P) e^{j phase} on the line row (each mode is phased with its largest field sample real and positive).

### Feature `em_fdfd_bor.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Time-averaged power [W] through an axis-aligned line at every driven solve, with the 2 pi ring weights of the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave (a cos(m phi) standing wave carries half for m != 0): a horizontal line (z = const) gives the flux along +z through the annulus it sweeps, pi sum [A Re(E_r H_phi*) - r w Re(E_phi H_r*)], a vertical line (r = const) the flux along +r through the cylinder, pi sum [r h Re(E_phi H_z*) - r L Re(E_z H_phi*)]; E of the line cells, H on their hi face (Yee points, no averaging: the pairing the discrete Poynting theorem conserves exactly through lossless cells, and that the port modes are normalised with), span ends by their share. A line from the axis across the whole field measures the full power; a closed box of lines the radiated power. Result 'flux_spectrum' with unit 'W', one entry per solved wavelength sorted by wavelength. In a driven order sum (azimuthal_orders) power is the total of the 3D field (the orders are orthogonal in phi, so their powers add exactly), extras power_orders (n_wavelengths x n_orders: each listed m with its -m) and azimuthal_orders. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell; its hi face must be inside the grid.

- FeatureSpec.type `flux_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_bor.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on a horizontal line into the upward (positive) and downward (negative) amplitudes of one guided mode at every solved wavelength. The port line must be horizontal (z = const). It starts on the axis (x0 = 0) or at an inner radius x0 > 0, an annular line whose start is a metal (pec) end on that cell edge (coaxial guides with the line from the inner conductor surface, ring-shaped cores whose field is small toward the axis); it ends either on the last window cell (then it continues through the r_hi cpml cells, or ends on the pec / pmc r_hi wall) or inside the domain, again a metal end on that cell edge (extend the line well into the cladding: the run log warns when the mode still has 1% of its peak field at a metal end; exact when the cells beyond a metal end are pec in the model, e.g. a pec_domain inner conductor). Vertical (r = const) port lines are not supported. The guided modes ~ exp(-j beta z) of the line at the azimuthal order are full-vector solutions of the body-of-revolution operator itself on a straight guide (all six components; the line cells and their row width), re-solved at every solved wavelength and after every material change, so the launch / decomposition is exact for a guide invariant along z with uniform rows for a cell on each side of the line (the run log warns otherwise). Modes are ranked by descending Re n_eff (mode 1 = the highest), radiation modes with more than half of their energy in the PML dropped; each carries 1 W (the exactly conserved discrete flux of flux_monitor) in the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength: power_positive / power_negative = |a|^2 in W, the power of the mode toward +z / -z (separated by the discrete reciprocity form of the line row and the row above, so other modes drop out); with exactly one enabled mode_source in the physics also fraction_positive / fraction_negative = |a / (sqrt(P) e^{j phase})|^2 (transmission / reflection into this mode) and phase_positive / phase_negative (rad, not de-embedded); extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag, mode_number, normalized. Keep the line and the row above off the line rows of a mode_source.

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, 50]) - Mode number
  Guided mode measured (ranking as mode_source); later wavelengths follow it by overlap.

### Feature `em_fdfd_bor.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Near-to-far-field transform of the driven solution on the closed surface of a rectangle in the (r, z) drawing: its two z faces and its outer cylinder (and an inner cylinder when x0 > 0); a box bottom at y0 = 0 on a pec / pmc z_lo mirror is closed by the mirror images instead (E_r, E_phi, H_z even for pmc, odd for pec). Equivalent currents J = n x H, M = -n x E (H on its Yee points, tangential E interpolated onto the face), integrated over phi with the exp(-j m phi) dependence in closed form (Bessel functions J_(m-1), J_m, J_(m+1)), vacuum outside the box (enclose every scatterer and source). Result 'far_field', one row per solved wavelength: power = radiated power per steradian r^2 |E|^2 / (2 eta0) in W/sr versus angle in the drawing (meridional) plane, counter-clockwise from +r (0 = equator, pi/2 = +z along the axis; angles with cos < 0 are the phi = pi side, the same power since the travelling wave has a phi-independent |E|); its solid-angle integral 2 pi int power cos(angle) d angle over the cos >= 0 half (-pi/2 .. pi/2) is the radiated power (flux_monitor box); extras power_theta / power_phi (E_theta / E_phi parts), angle_axes, azimuthal_order. In a driven order sum (azimuthal_orders) power is the pattern of the summed 3D field in the meridional plane through the sources (angles with cos >= 0 at phi = 0, the others at phi = pi: no longer the same power), the order amplitudes added with exp(-j m phi); extras power_azimuthal_mean (its phi average, the sum over the orders: 2 pi int power_azimuthal_mean cos(angle) d angle over the cos >= 0 half is the radiated power), power_orders (n_wavelengths x n_orders x n_angles: the phi average per listed m with its -m) and azimuthal_orders instead of azimuthal_order. Needs one cell beyond x1 / y1 and below y0 inside the domain; the box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `far_field`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result kind `far_field`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; range [1, inf)) - Number of angles
  Far-field angles evenly spaced over 360 degrees in the drawing (meridional) plane, counter-clockwise from +r (0 = +r = the equatorial plane, pi/2 = +z along the axis, pi = the equator on the other side, phi = pi); 360 gives 1-degree steps.

### Feature `em_fdfd_bor.resonance_table` - Resonance table

Resonances of the last eigenfrequency study solve at the azimuthal order setting (or per order of azimuthal_orders, order by order), nearest the target (the wavelength setting) first. Result 'table', one row per resonance: resonance_number, wavelength = 2 pi C0 / Re(omega) in m, frequency / frequency_imag = Re / Im(omega) / (2 pi) in Hz (> 0 decays), q_factor = Re(omega) / (2 Im(omega)) (inf when lossless and closed), pml_fraction (share of the |E|^2 ring volume in PML cells; above 0.5 dropped), azimuthal_order (m of the row); extras target_wavelength (m), selected_resonance and azimuthal_orders (the solved list). Accurate only near the target (see the eigenfrequency study). For Q versus a parameter add a derived value with source '<physics>.<this feature>', expression q_factor, operation at and at = 0.

- FeatureSpec.type `resonance_table`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

## Physics type `em_fdfd_conical` - Electromagnetic Waves, frequency domain (out-of-plane wave number k_z)

Conical (out-of-plane wave number) finite-difference frequency-domain solver of a z-invariant structure: the drawing is its xy cross-section, the fields vary as exp(j (omega t - k_z z)) with the k_z setting (2D frequency domain with an out-of-plane wave number), so E_x, E_y, E_z and H_x, H_y, H_z all couple. Projected 3D Yee cell (the em_modes layout and wall rules): E_z at the cell centres, E_x and H_y on the +x faces, E_y and H_x on the +y faces, H_z at the +x+y corner; unknowns E (3 per cell, PML included), curl-curl operator (k0^2 eps - curl mu^-1 curl) E = -j omega mu0 J with d/dz = -j k_z, solved on the host (solver role linear = sparse_direct: host SuperLU, a 'cusolver_qr' node is a validation error; one factor per wavelength, k_z and material state, reused as GMRES preconditioner after a material change at the same wavelength and k_z; back_end cudss / cudss_mixed: a cuDSS LDL^T of the dual-area-symmetrized operator on the GPU (an LU with a Bloch phase), no host size limit, later factorisations of the same sparsity reusing the first one's cuDSS plan). Needs scipy; validation warns near and refuses beyond the factor size limit. Studies: stationary (one driven solve at the wavelength setting, iterated with heat through heat_em_thermo_optic / em_heat_joule), frequency_domain (one driven solve per wavelength at the same k_z) and eigenfrequency (role eigen = arpack_shift_invert: squared-Cayley shift-invert resonances at k_z nearest the wavelength setting, complex omega and Q; static curl-free solutions dropped; at k_z = beta they are the guided modes, so a k_z sweep gives the dispersion; PML and dispersion frozen at the target; factorization auto (the default: cudss on the gpu backend with nvmath-python, falling back to superlu if cuDSS refuses the operator; else superlu), superlu (host), cudss (GPU, no host size limit: an LDL^T of the operator symmetrized by the dual areas, an LU with a Bloch phase) or cudss_mixed (complex64 factor, loose solves, float64 Rayleigh quotients; with a Bloch phase a refined LU)). Walls / mirrors / Bloch phases / CPML as em_modes plus bloch_kx / bloch_ky; at k_z = 0 the problem splits into the em_fdfd_ez and em_fdfd_hz ones (walls half a cell apart from theirs). Outputs at the cell centres: ex, ey, ez, hx, hy, hz (Re of the phasors at z = 0, V/m and A/m), their moduli <component>_abs, e_abs, e_intensity (|E|^2, the primary field), h_abs, sz = 1/2 Re(E_x H_y* - E_y H_x*) (power flow along z, W/m^2), absorbed_power (state q_abs = 1/2 omega eps0 sum_c (-Im eps_c) |E_c|^2 in W/m^3, cell means; em_heat_joule hands it to heat) and the permittivity arrays eps_r (eps_zz), eps_xx, eps_yy, sigma_e; scalar output source_power. A resonance is scaled to 1 real at its largest E sample (V/m). Features: point_source and line_source (currents along x, y or z), field_probe, flux_monitor (W/m through a line), pec_domain, resonance_table. Material vocabulary of em_modes (eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_zz diagonal). heat_em_thermo_optic writes all three permittivity arrays (slots eps_r_update, eps_xx_update, eps_yy_update). Not yet: a conical TFSF plane wave, far field, mode ports, conformal PEC. On a triangles mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles) the eigenfrequency study runs on mixed finite elements instead (see discretization: curved outlines followed, materials and state fields one value per element, the same resonance_table); driven studies, the source / probe / flux features and periodic faces stay on tensor meshes. The instance is usually named 'em'.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdfd_conical`; default instance name `em`
- Supported studies: stationary, frequency_domain, eigenfrequency
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): e_intensity
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdfd_conical.<feature>`): point_source, line_source, field_probe, flux_monitor, pec_domain, resonance_table

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  cpml absorbs outgoing waves in pml_cells extra cells added outside the domain. In the frequency domain the CPML is the complex coordinate stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0) with the FDTD grading of the pml_* settings. periodic must be set on both faces of the axis and wraps the field with the meshed window as period (uniform mesh: the size rounded up to whole cells) and no phase step (k = 0 along that axis, e.g. normal incidence); the em_fdtd_*, em_fdfd_* and em_modes types add a Bloch phase with bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear per input harmonic_channel; em_eme / em_eme_3d: k = 0 only). Walls and mirrors sit on the planes of em_modes (the same projected 3D Yee cell): a pec / pmc wall is the inner face of the outermost domain cell (that cell is a ghost holding the mirror image), half a cell off the em_fdfd_ez pec and em_fdfd_hz pmc walls; a symmetric (E mirror-even, a PMC plane) / antisymmetric (E mirror-odd, a PEC plane) mirror adds its ghost cell outside the domain, so its plane is the domain edge. At k_z != 0 a mirror plane normal to x or y stays a symmetry (k_z points along it) and halves the unknowns.
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda0 of the solve in a stationary study (omega = 2 pi C0 / lambda0); an eigenfrequency study searches the resonances nearest it at the k_z setting (the target); a frequency_domain study solves its own wavelengths and ignores it (validation info when it is not the default). The mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / |n| in every material and >= 2 per skin depth in lossy ones (validation checks both). Typical 0.4e-6 to 2e-6 m.
- `k_z` (float; unit rad/m; default 0) - Out-of-plane wave number
  Out-of-plane wave number k_z in rad/m of every solve: the fields vary as exp(j (omega t - k_z z)) along the z-invariant structure (the industry-standard out-of-plane wave number), so all six components couple. k_z = 0 gives the decoupled em_fdfd_ez (E_z, H_x, H_y) and em_fdfd_hz (H_z, E_x, E_y) problems at once (walls half a cell apart from theirs). Uses: conical / oblique incidence on gratings and other z-invariant structures (k_z = k0 n sin(theta) of the z share of the incident wave vector, the in-plane share from bloch_kx / bloch_ky along a periodic axis), a waveguide cross-section driven at a given propagation constant beta = k_z (a source excites the guided modes resonantly where omega meets the mode dispersion), and in an eigenfrequency study the dispersion omega(k_z): the resonances at fixed k_z are the guided modes with beta = k_z (same discrete problem as em_modes, read the other way; sweep k_z for the band / dispersion diagram). k_z stays fixed over the wavelengths of a frequency_domain study (the incidence angle then changes with wavelength). |k_z| above k0 n in a material makes the field evanescent in it. A real number (no leaky / complex k_z through the model).
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Element order on a triangles mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles; tensor meshes ignore it and use the Yee cell). Eigenfrequency study only: the em_modes mixed elements (Nedelec edge elements for E_x, E_y, Lagrange elements for E_z of the same degree; discrete gradients are exact static solutions, so no spurious modes), the k_z terms in the curl, elements with a curved edge mapped isoparametrically (quadratic), so round guides follow the drawn outline instead of a staircase. quadratic (default) or linear (Whitney / P1: cheaper, error ~h^2 instead of ~h^4 in k0^2). About 7 (quadratic) or 2 (linear) unknowns per element, one assembly per solve, squared-Cayley shift-invert by the eigen solver: host SuperLU, or with its factorization cudss a cuDSS LDL^T on the GPU (complex symmetric pencil), cudss_mixed its complex64 form with float64 Rayleigh quotients. Materials are one value per element; a cpml face gets a ring of mesh pml_layers element layers with the stretch of the pml_* settings and a pec outer side; pec_domain removes its elements and holds tangential E = 0 on their outline; pec / pmc / mirror faces as em_modes. Not available on triangles (validation errors): stationary and frequency_domain studies (driven solves) with every source / probe / flux feature, periodic and Bloch faces (no periodic mesh); resonance_table and pec_domain work.
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Bloch wave vector along x in rad/m, used only when bc_x_lo and bc_x_hi are periodic: the solution is the Bloch wave F(x + L) = F(x) exp(-j kx L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t)); kx and kx + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. The phase sits on the wrap entries of the operator (no extra cost). Point sources repeat in every period image with that phase (a phased array); a line source along the periodic axis carries exp(-j kx s) (s = cell centres from the grid lo corner), so with k_z it launches the conical plane wave of wave vector (kx, k_normal, k_z). Results are those of the Bloch wave at +k.
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Bloch wave vector along y in rad/m, used only when bc_y_lo and bc_y_hi are periodic: the solution is the Bloch wave F(x + L) = F(x) exp(-j ky L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t)); ky and ky + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. The phase sits on the wrap entries of the operator (no extra cost). Point sources repeat in every period image with that phase (a phased array); a line source along the periodic axis carries exp(-j ky s) (s = cell centres from the grid lo corner), so with k_z it launches the conical plane wave of wave vector (ky, k_normal, k_z). Results are those of the Bloch wave at +k.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic relative permittivity (>= 1): sets eps_xx, eps_yy and eps_zz unless the material sets those components (a component wins over eps_r). n^2 of a lossless dielectric: silica ~2.085, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um; may depend on x, y and physics fields. E_z sees the cell value, E_x on the +x and E_y on the +y cell faces the width-weighted mean of the two cells sharing that face (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically). The solve uses the complex permittivity at the solve wavelength: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus the susceptibility chi(omega) of every Drude / Lorentz pole (exp(+j omega t): loss has Im < 0).
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (out of plane)
  z component (out of plane, along the invariant direction) of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the one E_z sees at the cell centres; overrides eps_r for E_z (it writes the eps_r array).
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, x
  x component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the one E_x sees on the +x cell faces (the width-weighted mean of the two cells sharing that face (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically)); overrides eps_r for E_x.
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, y
  y component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the one E_y sees on the +y cell faces (the width-weighted mean of the two cells sharing that face (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically)); overrides eps_r for E_y.
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss in S/m on all three E components, default 0: the permittivity at the solve wavelength gains -j sigma_e / (omega eps0); a weak absorber of index n and extinction kappa has sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0. Model metals with a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1) of H_x, H_y and H_z, each taking the value of the cell it belongs to (H_x on the +y face, H_y on the +x face, H_z at the +x+y corner of that cell); 1 for optical materials. The solve uses mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0).
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss on H_x, H_y, H_z in Ohm/m, default 0: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0).

### Fields

State fields:
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity zz (1)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)
- `q_abs` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)

Output fields (primary e_intensity):
- `ex` - Re E_x (V/m)
- `ey` - Re E_y (V/m)
- `ez` - Re E_z (V/m)
- `hx` - Re H_x (A/m)
- `hy` - Re H_y (A/m)
- `hz` - Re H_z (A/m)
- `ex_abs` - |E_x| (V/m)
- `ey_abs` - |E_y| (V/m)
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (V/m)
- `hx_abs` - |H_x| (A/m)
- `hy_abs` - |H_y| (A/m)
- `hz_abs` - |H_z| (A/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `sz` - S_z (power flow along z) (W/m^2)
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity zz (1)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)

Scalar outputs: source_power (W/m): the time-averaged power per unit z length the enabled point / line sources deliver in the last driven solve, 1/2 Re sum E . J* dA over their current points (the drawn part: a mirror image is not counted). Equal to the net flux out of a closed set of lossless flux lines around the sources without a mirror face; with one the flux results are unfolded (x mirror_factor) while this stays the drawn part. Missing (NaN plus a run-log warning) before a driven solve, e.g. in an eigenfrequency study. Derived value expression <physics>_source_power.

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdfd_conical.point_source` - Point source

Current element of any direction in the cell containing the point, modulated as exp(-j k_z z) along the invariant direction; see component and current. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "z"; choices x | y | z) - Direction
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_conical.point_source.component`
- `current` (float; unit A; default 0.001) - Current
  Current I [A] = the integral of the current density J over the cell cross-section: J = I / (dx dy) for 'z' (a filament I exp(-j k_z z), at k_z = 0 the em_fdfd_ez point source), a line of x / y current elements of moment I per unit z length otherwise. Fields scale linearly with it. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phase of the source phasor in degrees (0 = cos carrier, as the em_fdfd_* sources); with a single source it only rotates every phasor.

### Feature `em_fdfd_conical.line_source` - Line source

Uniform current sheet of any direction on the cells of an axis-aligned line (see amplitude): across a periodic period with bloch_k along it and k_z it launches the conical plane waves of that wave vector on both sides. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.

- FeatureSpec.type `line_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "z"; choices x | y | z) - Direction
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_conical.point_source.component`
- `amplitude` (float; unit A/m; default 1) - Surface current
  Uniform surface current density K [A/m] of the sheet: each line cell carries a current element of K times its length along the line (J = K / width across the line), along a periodic Bloch axis times exp(-j k s). A sheet across a whole periodic period (or ending on cpml edges, where it continues through the PML) launches plane waves of wave vector (k along the line, +-k_normal, k_z) on both sides, k_normal^2 = k0^2 n^2 - k_along^2 - k_z^2 (evanescent when negative). Fields scale linearly with it. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phase of the source phasor in degrees (0 = cos carrier, as the em_fdfd_* sources); with a single source it only rotates every phasor.

### Feature `em_fdfd_conical.field_probe` - Field probe

Phasor of one field component in the cell containing the point at every driven solve. Result 'xy' versus wavelength: series abs (unit of the component) and phase (rad); extras frequency, wavelength, component, unit.

- FeatureSpec.type `field_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "ez"; choices ex | ey | ez | hx | hy | hz) - Field component
  Component recorded: its complex phasor at the centre of the cell containing the point (face / corner points averaged there, Bloch phases included), per driven solve (stationary, frequency_domain), at z = 0 of the exp(-j k_z z) dependence.

### Feature `em_fdfd_conical.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Time-averaged power per unit length along z [W/m] through an axis-aligned line at every driven solve, 1/2 Re (E x H*) . n: a horizontal line gives the flux along +y, sum [dx E_z H_x* - dx_dual E_x H_z*] / 2, a vertical line the flux along +x, sum [dy_dual E_y H_z* - dy E_z H_y*] / 2, with E of the line cells and H on their hi face (the boundary term of the discrete Poynting theorem: through lossless cells a line across a whole period, or wall to wall, carries the same power on every row, so the difference of two such lines is exactly the source power minus the absorption between them); the face pairs along the line take the two end faces half. A line reaching a mirror face counts its image (x mirror_factor, 2 per face). The z flux of the field is the output field sz. Result 'flux_spectrum' with unit 'W/m', one entry per solved wavelength sorted by wavelength. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell; its hi face must be inside the grid (or wrap on a periodic axis).

- FeatureSpec.type `flux_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_conical.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor: in every cell whose centre lies in the selected domains E_z = 0 at the centre and E_x / E_y = 0 on the faces between two such cells, staircased to the mesh (as em_modes; no conformal option).

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_conical.resonance_table` - Resonance table

Resonances of the last eigenfrequency study solve at the k_z setting, nearest the target (the wavelength setting) first. Result 'table', one row per resonance: resonance_number, wavelength = 2 pi C0 / Re(omega) in m, frequency / frequency_imag = Re / Im(omega) / (2 pi) in Hz (> 0 decays), q_factor = Re(omega) / (2 Im(omega)) (inf when lossless and closed), pml_fraction (share of |E|^2 dA in PML cells; above 0.5 dropped); extras target_wavelength (m) and selected_resonance. At k_z = beta the resonances are the guided modes of propagation constant beta: a parameter sweep of k_z with a derived value of the frequency column gives the dispersion. Accurate only near the target (see the eigenfrequency study). For Q versus a parameter add a derived value with source '<physics>.<this feature>', expression q_factor, operation at and at = 0.

- FeatureSpec.type `resonance_table`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

## Physics type `em_fdfd_ez` - Electromagnetic Waves, frequency domain (2D, electric field out of plane)

2D finite-difference frequency-domain (FDFD) solver for the E_z polarisation: E_z out of plane in V/m, H_x and H_y in plane in A/m, x to the right and y up, on the Yee grid of em_fdtd_ez (E_z at cell centres, H_x / H_y on the +y / +x cell faces); outputs ez_re, ez_im, ez_abs, ez_phase and the polarisation-agnostic e_abs, e_intensity and h_abs (|E|, |E|^2, |H| at the cell centres, in-plane face phasors averaged there before the modulus; phasor moduli = peak amplitudes, the FDTD types give instantaneous values under the same names). Each solve is one sparse direct solve of the discrete Helmholtz equation at one vacuum wavelength in the time convention exp(+j omega t): fields are complex phasors F (the real field is Re(F e^{j omega t})), and every source is a phasor with a phase in degrees (0 = cos carrier, -90 = the sin carrier of the FDTD sources) and the current-calibrated, mesh-independent amplitude of the matching FDTD source. Materials enter with their complex values at the solve wavelength: eps - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus the susceptibility chi(omega) of every Drude / Lorentz pole, and mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0); the CPML is a complex coordinate stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0) with the FDTD grading. absorbed_power (state field q_abs) = the time-averaged loss density 1/2 omega eps0 (-Im eps) |E|^2 in W/m^3 (magnetic loss not counted, as in FDTD) that em_heat_joule hands to heat. Solver roles (PhysicsSpec.solvers, see solvers): linear = sparse_direct (back_end scipy_splu: host SuperLU, one factorisation per wavelength and material state reused for every source, ~1e6 unknowns nx * ny incl. PML; cusolver_qr: GPU sparse QR, one factorisation per solve, ~1e5 unknowns; validation warns near these sizes and refuses beyond them; cudss / cudss_mixed (GPU backend, nvmath-python): a cuDSS factor on the GPU, the LDL^T of D A with D the stretched cell areas (a general LU with a Bloch phase or H_z eps_xy couplings, whose adjoint solves then factor the transpose too), one per wavelength and material state, later ones reusing the analysis of the first (about 20 x faster than SuperLU per factorisation at 1e5 - 5e5 unknowns; prefer cudss: the cudss_mixed refinement makes its solves slower), no host size limit, the factor outside the GPU memory budget) or a line_block node (block Thomas factor on the GPU / CPU, one per wavelength and material state, cost lines x b^3 with b the cells across a line: suits elongated grids; the periodic axis lies inside the blocks, two periodic axes are an error; a rejected solve and the adjoint solves use a host SuperLU), eigen (eigenfrequency / optomechanics study) = arpack_shift_invert (its shift-invert factor: host SuperLU, or the line_block factor of the operator at the target when that is the linear solver; a rejected solve redoes the eigen-solve on SuperLU). Studies: stationary solves once at the wavelength setting (with heat, em_heat_joule and heat_em_thermo_optic iterate FDFD and heat solves to a fixed point, each FDFD solve with the latest permittivity; this loop is plain Picard by default and oscillates once the self-heating shift exceeds about one resonance linewidth: set the study relaxation < 1); frequency_domain solves a list of wavelengths (with em_heat_joule from it: each wavelength that coupled fixed point, continued from the previous one), one labelled snapshot each, with probe, flux and mode results versus wavelength and one far-field pattern per wavelength; eigenfrequency finds the source-free resonances (complex omega, Q) nearest the wavelength setting, one labelled snapshot each and the resonance_table result; optomechanics eigen-solves it the same way as the optical physics a solid_mechanics optomechanical_coupling names (else it solves as a stationary background physics there; either way no coupling or material may read it); optimization varies the design_region densities to maximise the adjoint_objective sum J (L-BFGS-B on the adjoint gradient); time_dependent (beside a time-stepped physics such as elastic_waves, never beside an em_fdtd_* one) re-solves at the wavelength setting on the frozen state every k steps of the run (k = its every), only when an input changed (stroboscopic, e.g. acousto-optics); monitors then keep the last solve. Boundaries: cpml, periodic (with a Bloch phase bloch_kx / bloch_ky: oblique incidence, band diagrams from an eigenfrequency study swept over k), pec / pmc walls and symmetric / antisymmetric mirror planes on the domain edge, with the outer-cell rows of the matching FDTD type. Features: point, line and gaussian-beam sources, a +x TFSF plane wave (uniform or graded mesh, incident wave in the uniform medium on its outline), mode (port) sources and monitors whose port modes are re-solved at every solved wavelength and after material changes (exact one-sided launch, mode powers in W/m), PEC domains, conducting sheets (2D materials such as graphene), field probes, flux monitors in W/m and the near-to-far-field transform. TFSF and mode sources enter only the right-hand side, so the field jumps across their interface: keep monitors off it. On a triangles mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles) the field is solved on Lagrange finite elements instead (see discretization: curved outlines followed, materials and state fields one value per element, the same output names on a display raster): stationary, frequency_domain, time_dependent and eigenfrequency studies with point sources, field probes, pec_domain and resonance_table; the line / beam / TFSF / mode sources, flux / mode / far-field monitors, conducting sheets, the adjoint and design features and periodic faces stay on tensor meshes. The instance is usually named 'em'.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdfd_ez`; default instance name `em`
- Supported studies: stationary, frequency_domain, eigenfrequency, optimization, time_dependent, optomechanics
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): ez_re
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdfd_ez.<feature>`): point_source, line_source, gaussian_beam, plane_wave_tfsf, mode_source, pec_domain, conducting_sheet, effective_index, phase_change_medium, field_probe, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, far_field, adjoint_objective, design_region, resonance_table

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bc_x_lo`
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.wavelength`
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.discretization`
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bloch_ky`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity
  Real relative permittivity (>= 1), n^2 of a lossless dielectric: glass ~2.1-2.25, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um; may depend on x, y and physics fields. E_z sees eps_zz instead when the material sets it. The solve uses the complex permittivity at the solve wavelength: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus the susceptibility chi(omega) of every Drude / Lorentz pole (exp(+j omega t): loss has Im < 0). For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf: an explicit permittivity wins over the Drude eps_inf, which applies only when none is set. A state-dependent value (e.g. of T) is rewritten at every coupling update of a stationary study (once, after the background solve, in a frequency_domain study) and the next solve reassembles the operator. A tabulated complex eps = eps1 + j eps2 (eps2 <= 0) at one angular frequency omega: for eps1 >= 1 set this value to eps1 and sigma_e = -eps2 omega eps0; a metal (eps1 < 1; the >= 1 bound is shared with em_fdtd_ez / em_fdtd_hz) takes a Drude pole with eps_inf 1, no permittivity property, a = 1 - eps1, omega_p = omega sqrt((a^2 + eps2^2) / a) and gamma = -omega eps2 / a, exact at that omega only (gold -115 - 11j at 1.55 um: omega_p 1.31e16, gamma 1.15e14 rad/s).
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (out of plane)
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.eps_zz`
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss in S/m, default 0: the permittivity at the solve wavelength gains -j sigma_e / (omega eps0) (exact, no time stepping). A weak absorber with index n and extinction coefficient kappa at angular frequency omega has sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0; model metals with a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1); 1 for practically every optical material. The solve uses mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0) on the H_x / H_y faces, each face taking the value of the cell it is the +y / +x face of; it also sets the local impedance of line sources.
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss on H_x, H_y in Ohm/m, default 0: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0); sigma_m / (mu0 mu_r) = sigma_e / (eps0 eps_r) gives an impedance-matched absorber without reflection at normal incidence.

### Fields

State fields:
- `ez_re` - Re E_z (V/m)
- `ez_im` - Im E_z (V/m)
- `q_abs` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (1)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)

Output fields (primary ez_re):
- `ez_re` - Re E_z (V/m)
- `ez_im` - Im E_z (V/m)
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (V/m)
- `ez_phase` - arg E_z (rad)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (1)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `eps_sensitivity` - Objective sensitivity dJ/d eps_r (W/m^3)
- `design_density` - Design density (1)
- `crystallinity` - Crystallinity (1)

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdfd_ez.point_source` - Point source

z-directed filament current phasor I e^{j phase} in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell). It radiates a cylindrical wave whose field does not depend on the mesh: |E_z| = omega mu0 I / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| in a homogeneous non-magnetic medium of wavenumber k.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `current` (float; unit A; default 0.001) - Electric line current
  Peak z-directed filament current I. The radiated field does not depend on the mesh: in a homogeneous non-magnetic medium of wavenumber k, |E_z| = omega mu0 I / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| (1 mA at wavelength 1 um: ~2e5 V/m at r = 1 um). Fields are linear, so results scale with I. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_ez.line_source` - Line source

Sheet current phasor on an axis-aligned line radiating amplitude V/m of E_z to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) sends waves along +x and -x, a horizontal one along +y and -y. For a plane wave, span the whole domain: an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML (on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `line_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  E_z radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); the calibration uses the complex eps_r (sigma_e and dispersion included) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength, so it is exact in any homogeneous medium. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so on a line crossing several media (e.g. a high-index core and its cladding) the current steps at the interfaces, the steps diffract and the field there is not the amplitude (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Each recalibration (e.g. a thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n of the line cells (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2). Typical 1 V/m.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so on a line crossing several media (e.g. a high-index core and its cladding) the current steps at the interfaces, the steps diffract and the field there is not the amplitude (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Each recalibration (e.g. a thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n of the line cells (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2). Typical 1 V/m.
