### Feature `em_fdfd_ez.plane_wave_tfsf` - Plane wave box (+x)

Plane wave travelling along +x only, injected on the outline of a total-field box: the unknown is the total E_z in the box cells and only the scattered field outside; amplitude = incident E_z, its phase referred to the centres of the first (lo-x) column of box cells; the jump enters the right-hand side through the operator rows on both sides of the outline. The incident wave is the discrete plane wave of the FDFD stencil in the background medium, the complex eps and mu_r at the solve wavelength of the outline cell just before the lo-x edge (uniform cells: numerical wavenumber k from (2 / dx) sin(k dx / 2) = n k0, n = sqrt(eps mu_r); graded x cells: the wave is marched cell by cell on the solved stencil from the lo-x edge, so it stays an exact discrete solution on any widths, starting as the uniform wave of the two cells at the lo-x edge (a grading there adds a small backward part); a lossy background attenuates it), so a box in a uniform medium (vacuum, a cladding) is exactly transparent on uniform and graded meshes alike: the box edges must lie in one uniform medium (warning otherwise: incident light leaks into the scattered field), and the box needs one scattered-field cell inside the domain on every side, except along a periodic y axis, where it may instead cover every y cell (y0 = 0, y1 = the domain height: no y edges, so a grating or a layered stack may cross it), and at a y mirror face of the wave's parity (ez: symmetric, hz: antisymmetric), where it may reach the plane: the box opens there and its mirror image completes it (the other parity, or an x mirror face, is an error). With bloch_ky != 0 (periodic y) the wave is oblique, exp(-j (k_x x + ky y)) with ky = bloch_ky, its phase referred to y = 0, and k_x from (2 / dx)^2 sin^2(k_x dx / 2) = (n k0)^2 - (2 / dy)^2 sin^2(ky dy / 2) (refused when that is not positive: evanescent); it needs uniform y cells (validation error on a graded y axis: exp(-j ky y) is no Bloch wave of graded rows; x may be graded). Enclose the scatterers with the box and put a far_field box outside it; flux and mode monitors must not straddle its outline (inside: total field, outside: scattered field). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `plane_wave_tfsf`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak incident E_z of the +x plane wave (computed for the uniform medium on the box outline); the scattered field outside the box is relative to it. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Typical 1 V/m.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source` - Mode source

Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction: a vertical line (x = const) launches toward +x (direction positive) or -x (negative), a horizontal one toward +y or -y. It is a one-sided total-field / scattered-field line: the unknown is the total field from the line cells downstream and only the scattered field (what comes back) upstream; the mode profile enters the right-hand side through the operator rows of the line cells and of their upstream neighbours, whose shared face is the interface (the lo face of the line cells for positive, their hi face for negative). The launch is exact and one-sided at every solved wavelength of a straight guide (no band-edge leakage as with a pulsed em_fdtd mode source). Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. The 1D eigenmodes along the line use the FDFD discretisation (Yee cell widths, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at the solve wavelength with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are re-solved at every solved wavelength and whenever the materials changed since the previous solve (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity), so the port always matches the current guide. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec domain edge takes E_z = 0, one on a pmc or symmetric edge dE_z/dn = 0 and one on an antisymmetric edge E_z odd about the plane, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E_z = 0 in the next cell), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'table' of the latest port solve (a frequency_domain study: its last solved wavelength), one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss in the exp(+j omega t) convention), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the two ends of the solved line / its peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode) and selected (True for the launched mode); extras wavelength (m), power (W/m), direction, mode_number and phase (deg).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (choice; default "positive"; choices positive | negative) - Direction
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.direction`
- `power` (float; unit W/m; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Mode power
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.power`
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

Perfect electric conductor: E_z = 0 in every cell whose centre lies in the selected domains (those unknowns are pinned and decoupled from their neighbours), staircased to the mesh; with solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries the H links from free cells into it put E_z = 0 at the drawn wall instead (exact wall distance t d, t >= 0.02).

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_ez.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Time-averaged Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line at every solved wavelength: S_x = -1/2 Re(E_z H_y*) through a vertical line, S_y = 1/2 Re(E_z H_x*) through a horizontal one, with E_z of the line cells and H from the discrete curl of E_z on their hi face; > 0 toward +x / +y. Keep its measuring face (the hi face of the line cells) off the interface face of a mode_source (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or on the line of a negative one), and keep the line with its measuring face entirely inside or entirely outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: those sources enter only the right-hand side, so the field jumps across their interface and a monitor there mixes total and scattered field (validation warns). Result 'flux_spectrum' with unit 'W/m': power per unit z length, summed over the line cells, absolute (no source-spectrum normalisation: a line source of amplitude A spanning the period L of a periodic axis in vacuum sends A^2 L / (2 eta0) to each side), one entry per solved wavelength sorted by wavelength. The discrete flux is conserved exactly through lossless cells; a transmission is the device power over the power of a reference run with the same source. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `flux_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on an axis-aligned line into the forward (positive: toward +x for a vertical line, +y for a horizontal one) and backward (negative) amplitudes a of one guided mode at every solved wavelength: E_z in the line cells and H_y (vertical line) / H_x (horizontal line) from the discrete curl of E_z on their hi face are projected on the mode solved at that wavelength, so each direction is measured separately, unlike a flux_monitor. The 1D eigenmodes along the line use the FDFD discretisation (Yee cell widths, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at the solve wavelength with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are re-solved at every solved wavelength and whenever the materials changed since the previous solve (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity), so the port always matches the current guide. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec domain edge takes E_z = 0, one on a pmc or symmetric edge dE_z/dn = 0 and one on an antisymmetric edge E_z odd about the plane, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E_z = 0 in the next cell), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. Keep its measuring face (the hi face of the line cells) off the interface face of a mode_source (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or on the line of a negative one), and keep the line with its measuring face entirely inside or entirely outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: those sources enter only the right-hand side, so the field jumps across their interface and a monitor there mixes total and scattered field (validation warns). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength (x in m, ascending; one point per solved wavelength): power_positive / power_negative = |a|^2 in W/m, the time-averaged power of the mode in each direction (every mode is normalised to carry 1 W/m); with exactly one enabled mode_source in the physics also fraction_positive / fraction_negative (unit 1) = |a / (sqrt(P) e^{j phase})|^2 with the source power P and phase (|S|^2: transmission into this mode downstream of the source, reflection upstream) and phase_positive / phase_negative (rad) = the phase of that S-parameter: the mode amplitude relative to the amplitude the source launches on its own line, not de-embedded (each mode profile is phased with its largest field sample real and positive, the lowest-coordinate one of mirror-equal peaks); extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (per wavelength), mode_number and normalized (True when the fractions are present).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`

### Feature `em_fdfd_ez.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Near-to-far-field transform of the solved phasors on the outline of a rectangle: E_z and H from the discrete curl of E_z (averaged onto the centres) at the sample points of the em_fdtd_ez far_field, so normalised patterns of the two types compare directly; radiated power per unit length and angle rho |E_z|^2 / (2 eta0) in W/(m rad) (its angle integral is the power through a closed flux box) versus angle, counter-clockwise from +x, one row per solved wavelength (ascending). The transform assumes vacuum outside the box (vacuum wavenumber and impedance): enclose every scatterer with the box; with a plane_wave_tfsf keep it outside the TFSF box, in the scattered field (inside, the incident plane wave would dominate the pattern): its x0 / y0 edges at least two cells before those of the TFSF box and its x1 / y1 edges in or beyond the first cell past it (each sample averages the faces on both sides of its cell, and a face on the TFSF outline mixes total and scattered field; validation warns otherwise, and for a box edge sampling across a mode_source interface face). Graded meshes work: the samples sit on the actual cell centres with trapezoid weights of their spacing (the faces on both sides of a sample cell average onto its centre); the closed contour runs through the centres of the first box cells and of the cells one beyond x1 / y1 (keep the box one cell off the x_hi / y_hi edges), and the box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `far_field`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result kind `far_field`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; range [1, inf)) - Number of angles
  Far-field angles evenly spaced over 360 degrees, counter-clockwise from +x (0 = +x, pi/2 = +y); 360 gives 1-degree steps.

## Physics type `em_fdfd_hz` - Electromagnetic Waves, frequency domain (2D, magnetic field out of plane)

2D finite-difference frequency-domain (FDFD) solver for the H_z polarisation: H_z out of plane in A/m, E_x and E_y in plane in V/m, x to the right and y up, on the Yee grid of em_fdtd_hz (H_z at cell centres, E_x on the +y and E_y on the +x cell faces, each face with the mean complex permittivity, conductivity and pole susceptibility of its two cells; solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages the permittivity of interface faces anisotropically); outputs hz_re, hz_im, hz_abs, hz_phase and the polarisation-agnostic e_abs, e_intensity and h_abs (|E|, |E|^2, |H| at the cell centres, in-plane face phasors averaged there before the modulus; phasor moduli = peak amplitudes, the FDTD types give instantaneous values under the same names). Each solve is one sparse direct solve of the discrete Helmholtz equation at one vacuum wavelength in the time convention exp(+j omega t): fields are complex phasors F (the real field is Re(F e^{j omega t})), and every source is a phasor with a phase in degrees (0 = cos carrier, -90 = the sin carrier of the FDTD sources) and the current-calibrated, mesh-independent amplitude of the matching FDTD source. Materials enter with their complex values at the solve wavelength: eps - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus the susceptibility chi(omega) of every Drude / Lorentz pole, and mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0); the CPML is a complex coordinate stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0) with the FDTD grading. absorbed_power (state field q_abs) = the time-averaged loss density 1/2 omega eps0 (-Im eps) |E|^2 in W/m^3 (magnetic loss not counted, as in FDTD) that em_heat_joule hands to heat. Solver roles (PhysicsSpec.solvers, see solvers): linear = sparse_direct (back_end scipy_splu: host SuperLU, one factorisation per wavelength and material state reused for every source, ~1e6 unknowns nx * ny incl. PML; cusolver_qr: GPU sparse QR, one factorisation per solve, ~1e5 unknowns; validation warns near these sizes and refuses beyond them; cudss / cudss_mixed (GPU backend, nvmath-python): a cuDSS factor on the GPU, the LDL^T of D A with D the stretched cell areas (a general LU with a Bloch phase or H_z eps_xy couplings, whose adjoint solves then factor the transpose too), one per wavelength and material state, later ones reusing the analysis of the first (about 20 x faster than SuperLU per factorisation at 1e5 - 5e5 unknowns; prefer cudss: the cudss_mixed refinement makes its solves slower), no host size limit, the factor outside the GPU memory budget) or a line_block node (block Thomas factor on the GPU / CPU, one per wavelength and material state, cost lines x b^3 with b the cells across a line: suits elongated grids; the periodic axis lies inside the blocks, two periodic axes are an error; a rejected solve and the adjoint solves use a host SuperLU), eigen (eigenfrequency / optomechanics study) = arpack_shift_invert (its shift-invert factor: host SuperLU, or the line_block factor of the operator at the target when that is the linear solver; a rejected solve redoes the eigen-solve on SuperLU). Studies: stationary solves once at the wavelength setting (with heat, em_heat_joule and heat_em_thermo_optic iterate FDFD and heat solves to a fixed point, each FDFD solve with the latest permittivity; this loop is plain Picard by default and oscillates once the self-heating shift exceeds about one resonance linewidth: set the study relaxation < 1); frequency_domain solves a list of wavelengths (with em_heat_joule from it: each wavelength that coupled fixed point, continued from the previous one), one labelled snapshot each, with probe, flux and mode results versus wavelength and one far-field pattern per wavelength; eigenfrequency finds the source-free resonances (complex omega, Q) nearest the wavelength setting, one labelled snapshot each and the resonance_table result; optomechanics eigen-solves it the same way as the optical physics a solid_mechanics optomechanical_coupling names (else it solves as a stationary background physics there; either way no coupling or material may read it); optimization varies the design_region densities to maximise the adjoint_objective sum J (L-BFGS-B on the adjoint gradient); time_dependent (beside a time-stepped physics such as elastic_waves, never beside an em_fdtd_* one) re-solves at the wavelength setting on the frozen state every k steps of the run (k = its every), only when an input changed (stroboscopic, e.g. acousto-optics); monitors then keep the last solve. Boundaries: cpml, periodic (with a Bloch phase bloch_kx / bloch_ky: oblique incidence, band diagrams from an eigenfrequency study swept over k), pec / pmc walls and symmetric / antisymmetric mirror planes on the domain edge, with the outer-cell rows of the matching FDTD type. Features: point, line and gaussian-beam sources, a +x TFSF plane wave (uniform or graded mesh, incident wave in the uniform medium on its outline), mode (port) sources and monitors whose port modes are re-solved at every solved wavelength and after material changes (exact one-sided launch, mode powers in W/m), PEC domains, conducting sheets (2D materials such as graphene), field probes, flux monitors in W/m and the near-to-far-field transform. TFSF and mode sources enter only the right-hand side, so the field jumps across their interface: keep monitors off it. On a triangles mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles) the field is solved on Lagrange finite elements instead (see discretization: curved outlines followed, materials and state fields one value per element, the same output names on a display raster): stationary, frequency_domain, time_dependent and eigenfrequency studies with point sources, field probes, pec_domain and resonance_table; the line / beam / TFSF / mode sources, flux / mode / far-field monitors, conducting sheets, the adjoint and design features and periodic faces stay on tensor meshes. A model with an em_fdfd_ez physics too (e.g. unpolarised light as one physics per polarisation) needs another instance name (e.g. em_hz) and the same bc_* / pml_* settings: both share one boundary configuration.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdfd_hz`; default instance name `em`
- Supported studies: stationary, frequency_domain, eigenfrequency, optimization, time_dependent, optomechanics
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): hz_re
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdfd_hz.<feature>`): point_source, line_source, gaussian_beam, plane_wave_tfsf, mode_source, pec_domain, conducting_sheet, effective_index, phase_change_medium, field_probe, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, far_field, adjoint_objective, design_region, resonance_table

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bc_x_lo`
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.wavelength`
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.discretization`
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bloch_ky`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic in-plane relative permittivity (>= 1): sets eps_xx and eps_yy unless the material sets those components (a component wins over eps_r). n^2 of a lossless dielectric: glass ~2.1-2.25, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um; may depend on x, y and physics fields. E_x / E_y sit on cell faces and each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells (of the complex values; solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages the real permittivity of interface faces anisotropically). The solve uses the complex permittivity at the solve wavelength: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus the susceptibility chi(omega) of every Drude / Lorentz pole (exp(+j omega t): loss has Im < 0). For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf: an explicit permittivity wins over the Drude eps_inf, which applies only when none is set. A state-dependent value (e.g. of T) is rewritten at every coupling update of a stationary study (once, after the background solve, in a frequency_domain study) and the next solve reassembles the operator. A tabulated complex eps = eps1 + j eps2 (eps2 <= 0) at one angular frequency omega: for eps1 >= 1 set this value to eps1 and sigma_e = -eps2 omega eps0; a metal (eps1 < 1; the >= 1 bound is shared with em_fdtd_ez / em_fdtd_hz) takes a Drude pole with eps_inf 1, no permittivity property, a = 1 - eps1, omega_p = omega sqrt((a^2 + eps2^2) / a) and gamma = -omega eps2 / a, exact at that omega only (gold -115 - 11j at 1.55 um: omega_p 1.31e16, gamma 1.15e14 rad/s).
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, x
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, y
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss on E_x and E_y in S/m, default 0 (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells): the permittivity at the solve wavelength gains -j sigma_e / (omega eps0) (exact, no time stepping). A weak absorber with index n and extinction coefficient kappa at angular frequency omega has sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0; model metals with a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1); H_z sees mu_zz = mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0) of its cell. 1 for practically every optical material; it also sets the local impedance of line sources.
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss on H_z in Ohm/m, default 0: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0); sigma_m / (mu0 mu_r) = sigma_e / (eps0 eps_r) gives an impedance-matched absorber without reflection at normal incidence.
- `eps_xy` (float; unit 1; default 0; may use x, y; writes arrays eps_xy) - Relative permittivity, xy (off-diagonal)
  Off-diagonal in-plane relative permittivity eps_xy = eps_yx (real, default 0) of a crystal whose in-plane axes are turned against x / y: a uniaxial crystal with its optic axis in the plane at angle theta from x has eps_xx = n_o^2 + (n_e^2 - n_o^2) cos^2 theta, eps_yy = n_o^2 + (n_e^2 - n_o^2) sin^2 theta, eps_xy = (n_e^2 - n_o^2) sin theta cos theta; eps_xx eps_yy > eps_xy^2 is required. The solve uses eta = eps^-1 per cell: an E_x (E_y) face takes the mean of eps_xx - eps_xy^2 / eps_yy (eps_yy - eps_xy^2 / eps_xx) of its two cells and couples to the other component through eta_xy averaged over the four faces around it (so at normal incidence on a layer only eps_yy - eps_xy^2 / eps_xx matters, and D_x = 0 gives E_x = -eps_xy / eps_xx E_y). The operator then has 9 points per row, which makes the direct solve dearer; the array is allocated only when a material sets it. Taken as 0 in PEC cells and in the outer two cell rows of a wall or mirror face. Mode ports, line-source / beam calibrations and the TFSF background do not see it (the build warns for a port or source line on cells with a material eps_xy: keep them in isotropic or unrotated cells). The adjoint (eps_sensitivity, optimization study) differentiates the face couplings with eps_xy held fixed; the output field eps_xy_sensitivity is dJ / d eps_xy. The acousto-optic and Pockels couplings add their change to it (source slot eps_xy_update); em_fdtd_hz and em_modes have no eps_xy.

### Source slots

- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xy_update` (1): Off-diagonal relative permittivity change Delta eps_xy over the whole grid (PML ring included), added to the material eps_xy at each transfer (a sum slot: the acousto-optic and Pockels couplings add their -n0_xx^2 n0_yy^2 Delta(1/n^2)_xy); see the eps_xy material property for how the solve uses it.

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.point_source` - Point source

Current-calibrated point excitation phasor in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell); its field does not depend on the mesh. magnetic_current: a z-directed magnetic line current K_m [V] at the cell centre, radiating |H_z| = omega eps0 eps_r K_m / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)|. electric_dipole: an in-plane electric current element of strength M [A] along orientation, split over the two E_x faces (+y / -y) and the two E_y faces (+x / -x) of the cell, radiating |H_z| = k M / 4 |H1^(2)(k r)| |sin(phi - orientation)|.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `excitation` (choice; default "magnetic_current"; choices magnetic_current | electric_dipole) - Excitation
  magnetic_current: z-directed magnetic line current at the cell centre (radiates the same in every direction). electric_dipole: in-plane electric current element along orientation, spread over the four E faces of the cell (radiates most broadside, nothing along its axis).
- `magnetic_current` (float; unit V; default 1; visible when excitation in (magnetic_current)) - Magnetic line current
  Peak z-directed magnetic line current K_m in V (the dual of a filament current). The radiated field does not depend on the mesh: in a homogeneous medium of relative permittivity eps_r and wavenumber k, |H_z| = omega eps0 eps_r K_m / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| (1 V at wavelength 1 um in vacuum: |H_z| ~ 1.3e3 A/m at r = 1 um). Fields are linear, so results scale with K_m. A fixed K_m radiates power ~ n^2 of its cell, so it drifts when eps there changes (e.g. thermo-optic); a filament current or dipole radiates n-independent power. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `dipole_moment` (float; unit A; default 0.001; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole strength
  Peak in-plane electric dipole strength M in A: the integral of the current density J over the cross-section, i.e. A*m of current moment per m of z, along orientation. The radiated field does not depend on the mesh: in a homogeneous medium of wavenumber k, |H_z| = k M / 4 |H1^(2)(k r)| |sin(phi - orientation)| at the angle phi counter-clockwise from +x (1 mA at wavelength 1 um in vacuum: |H_z| ~ 5e2 A/m at r = 1 um broadside). Fields are linear, so results scale with M. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `orientation` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole orientation
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_hz.point_source.orientation`
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.line_source` - Line source

Electric sheet current phasor on an axis-aligned line radiating amplitude V/m of tangential E to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) drives E_y and sends waves along +x and -x, a horizontal one drives E_x and sends them along +y and -y. The sheet sits on the hi face of the line cells (+x face of a vertical line, +y face of a horizontal one), and the local impedance uses that face permittivity (width-weighted mean of its two cells). For a plane wave, span the whole domain: an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML (on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `line_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  Tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); the calibration uses the complex face permittivity (the mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, sigma_e and dispersion included) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength, so it is exact in any homogeneous medium. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so on a line crossing several media (e.g. a high-index core and its cladding) the current steps at the interfaces, the steps diffract and the field there is not the amplitude (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). Each recalibration (e.g. a thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n of the line cells (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2). Typical 1 V/m.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.gaussian_beam` - Gaussian beam

Line source with the profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line, radiating a beam of peak tangential E = amplitude V/m to each side in the local medium (vertical line: E_y, along +x and -x; horizontal: E_x, along +y and -y); the waist lies on the line and the sheet on the hi face of the line cells. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `gaussian_beam`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) at the beam centre on the waist line, radiated to each side in the local medium; the calibration uses the complex face permittivity (the mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, sigma_e and dispersion included) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength, so it is exact in any homogeneous medium. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so on a line crossing several media (e.g. a high-index core and its cladding) the current steps at the interfaces, the steps diffract and the field there is not the amplitude (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). Each recalibration (e.g. a thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n of the line cells (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2). Typical 1 V/m.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`
- `waist` (float; unit m; default 1e-06; range (0, inf)) - Waist radius
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.waist`
- `center` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Beam centre
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.center`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.plane_wave_tfsf` - Plane wave box (+x)

Plane wave travelling along +x only (E_y, H_z = n E_y / (eta0 mu_r)), injected on the outline of a total-field box: the unknown is the total H_z in the box cells and only the scattered field outside; amplitude = incident E_y, its phase referred to the centres of the first (lo-x) column of box cells; the jump enters the right-hand side through the operator rows on both sides of the outline. The incident wave is the discrete plane wave of the FDFD stencil in the background medium, the complex eps and mu_r at the solve wavelength of the outline cell just before the lo-x edge (uniform cells: numerical wavenumber k from (2 / dx) sin(k dx / 2) = n k0, n = sqrt(eps mu_r); graded x cells: the wave is marched cell by cell on the solved stencil from the lo-x edge, so it stays an exact discrete solution on any widths, starting as the uniform wave of the two cells at the lo-x edge (a grading there adds a small backward part); a lossy background attenuates it), so a box in a uniform medium (vacuum, a cladding) is exactly transparent on uniform and graded meshes alike: the box edges must lie in one uniform medium (warning otherwise: incident light leaks into the scattered field), and the box needs one scattered-field cell inside the domain on every side, except along a periodic y axis, where it may instead cover every y cell (y0 = 0, y1 = the domain height: no y edges, so a grating or a layered stack may cross it), and at a y mirror face of the wave's parity (ez: symmetric, hz: antisymmetric), where it may reach the plane: the box opens there and its mirror image completes it (the other parity, or an x mirror face, is an error). With bloch_ky != 0 (periodic y) the wave is oblique, exp(-j (k_x x + ky y)) with ky = bloch_ky, its phase referred to y = 0, and k_x from (2 / dx)^2 sin^2(k_x dx / 2) = (n k0)^2 - (2 / dy)^2 sin^2(ky dy / 2) (refused when that is not positive: evanescent); it needs uniform y cells (validation error on a graded y axis: exp(-j ky y) is no Bloch wave of graded rows; x may be graded). Enclose the scatterers with the box and put a far_field box outside it; flux and mode monitors must not straddle its outline (inside: total field, outside: scattered field). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `plane_wave_tfsf`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak incident in-plane |E| of the +x plane wave, E_y at normal incidence (computed for the uniform medium on the box outline, H_z = n |E| / (eta0 mu_r) with n = sqrt(eps_yy mu_r) there, also for the oblique wave of a Bloch ky); the scattered field outside the box is relative to it. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Typical 1 V/m.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.mode_source` - Mode source

Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction: a vertical line (x = const) launches toward +x (direction positive) or -x (negative), a horizontal one toward +y or -y. It is a one-sided total-field / scattered-field line: the unknown is the total field from the line cells downstream and only the scattered field (what comes back) upstream; the mode profile enters the right-hand side through the operator rows of the line cells and of their upstream neighbours, whose shared face is the interface (the lo face of the line cells for positive, their hi face for negative). The launch is exact and one-sided at every solved wavelength of a straight guide (no band-edge leakage as with a pulsed em_fdtd mode source). Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. The 1D eigenmodes along the line use the FDFD discretisation (Yee cell widths, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at the solve wavelength with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are re-solved at every solved wavelength and whenever the materials changed since the previous solve (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity), so the port always matches the current guide. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The in-plane E faces use the permittivity of the operator (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the mean of core and cladding there. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'table' of the latest port solve (a frequency_domain study: its last solved wavelength), one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss in the exp(+j omega t) convention), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the two ends of the solved line / its peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode) and selected (True for the launched mode); extras wavelength (m), power (W/m), direction, mode_number and phase (deg).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (choice; default "positive"; choices positive | negative) - Direction
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.direction`
- `power` (float; unit W/m; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Mode power
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.power`
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor: tangential E = 0 on every face of each cell whose centre lies in the selected domains (E_x on its +y and -y faces, E_y on its +x and -x faces; those faces drop out of the operator, so H_z inside is 0), staircased to the mesh. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra) only faces wholly inside the drawn metal are PEC and each cut cell takes its free face lengths in the operator and its free area (>= 0.02 of the cell) in the k0^2 mu term, which keeps the operator reciprocal; mode ports, sources and eps_xy couplings keep the cell mask.

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Time-averaged Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line at every solved wavelength: S_x = 1/2 Re(E_y H_z*) through a vertical line, S_y = -1/2 Re(E_x H_z*) through a horizontal one, with H_z of the line cells and E on their hi face from Ampere's law (the discrete curl of H_z plus a source current on that face); > 0 toward +x / +y. Keep the line off the line cells of a line source or gaussian beam: their sheet sits on the same face, where the flux jumps by the radiated power, and the monitor reads the line-cell side (minus the power sent toward -x / -y). Keep its measuring face (the hi face of the line cells) off the interface face of a mode_source (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or on the line of a negative one), and keep the line with its measuring face entirely inside or entirely outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: those sources enter only the right-hand side, so the field jumps across their interface and a monitor there mixes total and scattered field (validation warns). Result 'flux_spectrum' with unit 'W/m': power per unit z length, summed over the line cells, absolute (no source-spectrum normalisation: a line source of amplitude A spanning the period L of a periodic axis in vacuum sends A^2 L / (2 eta0) to each side), one entry per solved wavelength sorted by wavelength. The discrete flux is conserved exactly through lossless cells; a transmission is the device power over the power of a reference run with the same source. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `flux_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on an axis-aligned line into the forward (positive: toward +x for a vertical line, +y for a horizontal one) and backward (negative) amplitudes a of one guided mode at every solved wavelength: H_z in the line cells and E_y (vertical line) / E_x (horizontal line) from Ampere's law on their hi face are projected on the mode solved at that wavelength, so each direction is measured separately, unlike a flux_monitor. The 1D eigenmodes along the line use the FDFD discretisation (Yee cell widths, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at the solve wavelength with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are re-solved at every solved wavelength and whenever the materials changed since the previous solve (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity), so the port always matches the current guide. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The in-plane E faces use the permittivity of the operator (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the mean of core and cladding there. Keep its measuring face (the hi face of the line cells) off the interface face of a mode_source (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or on the line of a negative one), and keep the line with its measuring face entirely inside or entirely outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: those sources enter only the right-hand side, so the field jumps across their interface and a monitor there mixes total and scattered field (validation warns). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength (x in m, ascending; one point per solved wavelength): power_positive / power_negative = |a|^2 in W/m, the time-averaged power of the mode in each direction (every mode is normalised to carry 1 W/m); with exactly one enabled mode_source in the physics also fraction_positive / fraction_negative (unit 1) = |a / (sqrt(P) e^{j phase})|^2 with the source power P and phase (|S|^2: transmission into this mode downstream of the source, reflection upstream) and phase_positive / phase_negative (rad) = the phase of that S-parameter: the mode amplitude relative to the amplitude the source launches on its own line, not de-embedded (each mode profile is phased with its largest field sample real and positive, the lowest-coordinate one of mirror-equal peaks); extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (per wavelength), mode_number and normalized (True when the fractions are present).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`

### Feature `em_fdfd_hz.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Near-to-far-field transform of the solved phasors on the outline of a rectangle: H_z and E from Ampere's law (the discrete curl of H_z, averaged onto the centres) at the sample points of the em_fdtd_hz far_field, so normalised patterns of the two types compare directly; radiated power per unit length and angle rho |eta0 H_z|^2 / (2 eta0) (|eta0 H_z| = the far-field |E| in vacuum) in W/(m rad) (its angle integral is the power through a closed flux box) versus angle, counter-clockwise from +x, one row per solved wavelength (ascending). The transform assumes vacuum outside the box (vacuum wavenumber and impedance): enclose every scatterer with the box; with a plane_wave_tfsf keep it outside the TFSF box, in the scattered field (inside, the incident plane wave would dominate the pattern): its x0 / y0 edges at least two cells before those of the TFSF box and its x1 / y1 edges in or beyond the first cell past it (each sample averages the faces on both sides of its cell, and a face on the TFSF outline mixes total and scattered field; validation warns otherwise, and for a box edge sampling across a mode_source interface face). Graded meshes work: the samples sit on the actual cell centres with trapezoid weights of their spacing (the faces on both sides of a sample cell average onto its centre); the closed contour runs through the centres of the first box cells and of the cells one beyond x1 / y1 (keep the box one cell off the x_hi / y_hi edges), and the box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `far_field`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result kind `far_field`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; range [1, inf)) - Number of angles
  Far-field angles evenly spaced over 360 degrees, counter-clockwise from +x (0 = +x, pi/2 = +y); 360 gives 1-degree steps.

## Physics type `em_fdfd_nonlinear` - Nonlinear optics, frequency domain (2D, harmonic channels)

2D frequency-domain chi2 / chi3 mixing between harmonic channels (nonlinear_optics_plan stages 1-4): every harmonic_channel feature is one em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz solve (E_z or H_z polarisation, both = two channels) at its own frequency on the shared mesh and materials, each material evaluated at that frequency, so phase matching comes from the material dispersion. chi2_medium / chi3_medium features add the nonlinear polarisation as a phasor source of the target channels (exp(+j omega t), P = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi : E..E; SHG P(2w) = eps0 d E^2, THG P(3w) = (1/4) eps0 chi3 E^3); surface_chi2 (the interface of a selection) and sheet_nonlinearity (a 2D material on a line) add surface polarisations on cell faces / line cells. coupling_mode undepleted: solved once per channel in rank order from the lower ranks (no pump back-action, no SPM / XPM), valid while the conversion stays small; pump_depleted: every term (depletion, parametric gain, SPM / XPM, steady-state free carriers of chi3 media) solved self-consistently, by block Gauss-Seidel sweeps with relaxation and Anderson acceleration (iteration_method picard; the Kerr diagonal lagged in the channel operator; high-gain parametric or bistable cavities may not converge) or by Newton-Krylov (newton: exact Jacobian, GMRES preconditioned by the channel factors), with optional source continuation, until the fields change by <= tolerance. Sources and monitors are the em_fdfd_ez / _hz features with a channel setting; fields and powers are absolute and per unit length in z, so nonlinear results scale with the source amplitudes (a 2D SHG efficiency P_2w / P_w^2 has unit m/W). Each channel factorises its own operator (host SuperLU memory adds up per channel). Study: nonlinear_frequency_domain (one snapshot per channel). Output fields of the shown channel: the phasor quartets of both polarisations (the other polarisation reads 0), e_abs (primary), e_intensity, h_abs, absorbed_power, nonlinear_polarization_abs |P_NL|, the chi2 poling sign and carrier_density (0 without free carriers), eps_sensitivity (the cascade adjoint of the adjoint_objective features) and design_density. Couplings: thermo-optic and other permittivity writers act on every channel; em_heat_joule reads the absorbed power of every channel (linear q_abs plus the exact two-photon and free-carrier absorption of the applied terms, the same for picard and newton) back into a background heat physics (solution feedback rounds of the study). Studies: nonlinear_frequency_domain, and optimization (coupling_mode undepleted, or pump_depleted with the fixed-point adjoint, iteration_method newton when a chi3 medium is present: design_region on the shared permittivity, adjoint_objective features on the channels). Periodic faces carry a Bloch phase per channel (harmonic_channel bloch_kx / bloch_ky of the inputs; generated channels the combination of their inputs' k), mirror faces a parity per channel (harmonic_channel). The instance is usually named 'nl'.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdfd_nonlinear`; default instance name `nl`
- Supported studies: nonlinear_frequency_domain, optimization
- Default study: {"type": "nonlinear_frequency_domain"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): e_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdfd_nonlinear.<feature>`): harmonic_channel, chi2_medium, chi3_medium, surface_chi2, sheet_nonlinearity, pec_domain, conducting_sheet, design_region, point_source, line_source, gaussian_beam, plane_wave_tfsf, mode_source, field_probe, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, far_field, adjoint_objective

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.bc_x_lo`
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `coupling_mode` (choice; default "undepleted"; choices undepleted | pump_depleted) - Coupling mode
  undepleted: every channel solved once in rank order, fed only by lower-rank channels (no back-action, no SPM / XPM, no free carriers; valid at small conversion). pump_depleted: every mixing term (back-action, parametric gain, SPM / XPM) and the chi3 free carriers, solved self-consistently by iteration_method until the stored channel fields change by <= tolerance.
- `iteration_method` (choice; default "picard"; choices picard | newton; visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Iteration method
  pump_depleted solver. picard: block Gauss-Seidel sweeps over the channels in rank order with relaxation and Anderson acceleration, the SPM / XPM / free-carrier diagonal lagged in the channel operator (those channels reassemble and solve by GMRES on the recycled factor every sweep); cheap per sweep, converges while the conversion per pass is moderate. newton: Newton-Krylov on the coupled channels, the exact real-linear (Wirtinger) Jacobian of the polynomial mixing and carrier terms, GMRES (restart 20, at most 60 products per Newton step) left-preconditioned by the channels' own factors (every channel solved from the same iterate), Eisenstat-Walker forcing and backtracking on the scaled residual; each GMRES product costs one back-substitution per nonlinear channel, and it converges quadratically near the solution (high conversion, parametric gain near threshold, cavities, strong Kerr phase). Kerr and carriers stay in the rhs (no reassembly; q_abs then holds only the linear losses); relaxation and anderson_depth are ignored. cusolver_qr refactorises every solve, which newton multiplies.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-08; range (0, inf); visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Iteration tolerance
  pump_depleted stops when the largest relative channel change ||G_k - x_k|| / ||G_k|| is <= tolerance, G = the channel fields solved from the stored fields x (picard: over one sweep; newton: one solve of every channel from the Newton iterate); the fixed-point update, not the operator residual. The recycled GMRES solves of picard reach 1e-10, so stay above ~1e-9.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf); visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Iteration limit
  Sweeps (picard) or Newton steps (newton) per continuation step at most; not converged then: warning, the last iterate is kept (snapshot labels say so, summary nonlinear_solve converged false).
- `relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, 1]; visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Relaxation
  picard only: under-relaxation beta of the mixing x + beta f (1 = plain sweeps); lower it (0.3-0.7) for an oscillating iteration (high conversion, cavities).
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 5; range [0, inf); visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Anderson depth
  picard only: history m of the Anderson acceleration between sweeps (0 = relaxed Picard); costs 2 m stacked copies of every channel field on the GPU.
- `continuation_steps` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when coupling_mode in (pump_depleted)) - Continuation steps
  Ramp every linear source amplitude through k / steps, k = 1..steps, each step warm-started from the previous (1 = none). Helps near bistability; a Kerr S-curve has several solutions and the branch reached depends on the ramp.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic relative permittivity (>= 1): sets eps_zz (E_z channels) and eps_xx, eps_yy (H_z channels) unless the material sets those components. n^2 of a lossless dielectric; may depend on x, y and physics fields. Each channel uses the complex permittivity at its own frequency: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus every Drude / Lorentz pole chi(omega), so the material dispersion sets the phase mismatch between channels (non-dispersive materials are phase matched by construction). For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf.
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (along the guide)
  z component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the one E_z channels see; overrides eps_r for E_z. z-cut lithium niobate: eps_r = n_o^2, eps_zz = n_e^2.
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, x
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, y
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss in S/m on every E component, default 0. Each channel uses the complex permittivity at its own frequency: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus every Drude / Lorentz pole chi(omega), so the material dispersion sets the phase mismatch between channels (non-dispersive materials are phase matched by construction).
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1), 1 for practically every optical material; mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0) per channel.
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss in Ohm/m, default 0: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0) (artificial absorbers only).

- `eps_sensitivity` - Objective sensitivity dJ/d eps_r (W/m^3)
- `design_density` - Design density (1)
- `hz_re` - Re H_z (A/m)
- `hz_im` - Im H_z (A/m)
- `hz_abs` - |H_z| (A/m)
- `hz_phase` - arg H_z (rad)
- `ex_re` - Re E_x (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `ex_im` - Im E_x (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `ey_re` - Re E_y (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `ey_im` - Im E_y (phasor, cell centres) (V/m)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1)
- `eps_xy` - Relative permittivity xy (off-diagonal) (1)
- `nonlinear_polarization_abs` - |P_NL| (shown channel) (C/m^2)
- `poling` - Poling sign (chi2 media) (1)
- `carrier_density` - Free-carrier density (chi3 media) (1/m^3)

Scalar outputs: power_exchange_<channel> in W/m: time-averaged power the nonlinear polarisation of the applied mixing terms (and the free carriers) delivers to that channel, W_k = (omega_k / 2) sum_cells A Im(conj(E_k) . P_k), per unit length in z (2D); > 0 = the channel gains power (a generated channel), < 0 = it loses power (a depleted pump, pump_depleted only), 0 on input channels in the undepleted mode (no back-action). power_exchange_imbalance (1): |sum_k W_k| / sum_k |W_k| over every term of the mixing table on the current fields, ~1e-12 for real tensors with Kleinman symmetry whatever the fields: an implementation check, not a convergence measure (larger for general / non-Kleinman d values, per-process or Miller factors, with Im chi3 and carriers, where the sum is the nonlinear loss). nonlinear_absorption in W/m: -W of the applied SPM / XPM terms of chi3 media and sigma3 sheets (two-photon absorption; 0 undepleted). free_carrier_absorption in W/m: -W of the free-carrier polarisation over every channel (> 0 absorbs; 0 without carriers). peak_carrier_density in 1/m^3: the largest steady-state N. iterations (1): sweeps (picard) or Newton steps (newton) of the last solve (1 undepleted, summed over continuation steps); residual (1): the last iterate's largest relative channel field change (0 undepleted).

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.harmonic_channel` - Harmonic channel

One frequency (and polarisation) solved by the nonlinear physics; the feature name is the channel name (an identifier). Input channels have a wavelength, generated ones an integer combination of other channels (the frequency matches exactly). Every channel is its own em_fdfd_ez / _hz solve on the shared mesh and materials, each material evaluated at the channel frequency (phase matching comes from the material dispersion). The mixing table lists every chi2 / chi3 process landing on a declared channel; products off the channel set are not computed (no automatic closure, validation info). Undepleted mode: channels are solved once in rank order (inputs 0, a combination 1 + the highest rank it names), each with the nonlinear polarisation of lower-rank channels as its source; back-action on the pump and SPM / XPM are neglected (pump_depleted includes them). At least one input channel is needed; sources and monitors name their channel. Mirror faces (symmetric / antisymmetric bc_*): the input channels have that E parity, a generated channel the parity of its combination, s^(sum of its coefficients) (2 p and p - s are even, 3 p and p + s - i odd), so under an antisymmetric face an even channel solves with that face symmetric (its unfolded fields follow); an input reached by frequency only must have the parity of the process (validation error otherwise). The image half holds the mirror image of the drawn crystal. Bloch k: bloch_kx / bloch_ky of the inputs, the combination for generated channels.

- FeatureSpec.type `harmonic_channel`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `definition` (choice; default "wavelength"; choices wavelength | combination) - Defined by
  wavelength: an input channel at a given vacuum wavelength (rank 0). combination: a generated channel whose frequency is an integer combination of other channels (rank 1 + the highest rank it names), so mixing products land on it exactly.
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf); visible when definition in (wavelength)) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength of an input channel [m] (omega = 2 pi C0 / wavelength); a parameter sweep over it gives spectra (e.g. SHG versus pump wavelength). Typical 0.8e-6 to 2e-6 m.
- `combination` (str; default "2 p"; visible when definition in (combination)) - Combination
  Integer combination of other channel names (their feature names), e.g. '2 p' (second harmonic of p), 'p + s' (sum frequency), 'p - s' (difference frequency), '2 p - s' (four-wave mixing idler); '*' between count and name is optional. Parsed, not evaluated; the frequency must be > 0 and no cycle is allowed. Name the frequency name of a polarization both channel (without _ez / _hz).
- `polarization` (choice; default "ez"; choices ez | hz | both) - Polarisation
  ez: the channel carries E_z (an em_fdfd_ez solve); hz: E_x, E_y (an em_fdfd_hz solve); both: two channels <name>_ez and <name>_hz at the same frequency (two factorisations: memory doubles). Chi2 tensors couple the polarisations (d31 E_z^2 -> P_x, GaAs d14 E_x E_y -> P_z), so a generated channel may need the other polarisation than its pump.
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when definition in (wavelength)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Input channels: Bloch wave vector along x in rad/m, used only when bc_x_lo / bc_x_hi are periodic (validation warns otherwise): the channel solves the Bloch wave F(x + L) = F(x) exp(-j kx L) per meshed period L, as em_fdfd_* bloch_kx (oblique incidence on a grating or photonic crystal: k0 sin(theta) of that input). A generated channel carries the same combination of its inputs' k (2 p: 2 k_p), which keeps every polarisation a Bloch wave of its target; an input that a process reaches by frequency only must have the matching k modulo 2 pi / L (validation error otherwise). With k != 0 on any channel: no surface_chi2 / sheet_nonlinearity (error) and no port line spanning that Bloch period. 0 = plain periodic.
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when definition in (wavelength)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Input channels: Bloch wave vector along y in rad/m, used only when bc_y_lo / bc_y_hi are periodic (validation warns otherwise): the channel solves the Bloch wave F(y + L) = F(y) exp(-j ky L) per meshed period L, as em_fdfd_* bloch_ky (oblique incidence on a grating or photonic crystal: k0 sin(theta) of that input). A generated channel carries the same combination of its inputs' k (2 p: 2 k_p), which keeps every polarisation a Bloch wave of its target; an input that a process reaches by frequency only must have the matching k modulo 2 pi / L (validation error otherwise). With k != 0 on any channel: no surface_chi2 / sheet_nonlinearity (error) and no port line spanning that Bloch period. 0 = plain periodic.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium` - Second-order nonlinear medium

Bulk chi2 of the selected domains: the crystal-class tensor rotated into model axes, times the poling sign per cell (stored as int8 on the selection bounding box). Response (exp(+j omega t) phasors): P(w3) = eps0 2^(1-n) sum over ordered source tuples chi2 : E E, so SHG P(2w) = eps0 d E^2, SFG P(w1 + w2) = 2 eps0 d E1 E2, DFG P(w1 - w2) = eps0 chi2 E1 conj(E2) (d = chi2 / 2). Products are formed at the cell centres (hz E_x / E_y collocated by the face mean C, the polarisation returned to the faces by its area-weighted adjoint, which keeps the discrete power exchange exact). One tensor for every process, or Miller's rule (miller_scaling) relative to the SHG of reference_wavelength. Overlapping media add. Fields and powers are 2D: per unit length in z, so a conversion efficiency P_2w / P_w^2 has unit m/W (multiply by an effective height to compare with a 3D guide).

- FeatureSpec.type `chi2_medium`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `crystal_class` (choice; default "3m"; choices 3m | -43m | 6mm | mm2 | 32 | general) - Crystal class
  Point group fixing the non-zero d_il (Kleinman symmetry assumed, except general): 3m (LiNbO3, LiTaO3, BBO: d22, d31 = d15 = d24, d33, with d16 = d21 = -d22; LN |d33| ~ 2.5e-11, |d31| ~ 4.6e-12, |d22| ~ 2.1e-12 m/V at 1.06 um), -43m (GaAs, GaP, InP, ZnS: d14 = d25 = d36; GaAs ~ 1.2e-10 m/V at 1.55 um SHG), 6mm (AlN, GaN, ZnO: d15 = d24, d31 = d32, d33), mm2 (KTP: d15, d24, d31, d32, d33), 32 (quartz: d11, d12 = d26 = -d11, d14, d25 = -d14), general (all 18 d_il; the power exchange identity is then exact only for Kleinman-symmetric values). Signs follow the crystal axes of the orientation setting.
- `d11` (float; unit m/V; default 0; visible when crystal_class in (32, general)) - d11
  Second-order coefficient d11 in m/V of the crystal axes (1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V; d = chi2 / 2), Voigt index pair il: i = polarisation component (1 x, 2 y, 3 z of the crystal axes), l = field pair (1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy); used by the classes 32, general. P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).
- `d12` (float; unit m/V; default 0; visible when crystal_class in (general)) - d12
  Second-order coefficient d12 in m/V of the crystal axes (1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V; d = chi2 / 2), Voigt index pair il: i = polarisation component (1 x, 2 y, 3 z of the crystal axes), l = field pair (1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy); used by the classes general. P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).

P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).

P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).
- `d31` (float; unit m/V; default 0; visible when crystal_class in (3m, 6mm, mm2, general)) - d31

P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).

P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).

P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).

P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).
- `d35` (float; unit m/V; default 0; visible when crystal_class in (general)) - d35
