P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).
- `d36` (float; unit m/V; default 0; visible when crystal_class in (general)) - d36
  Second-order coefficient d36 in m/V of the crystal axes (1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V; d = chi2 / 2), Voigt index pair il: i = polarisation component (1 x, 2 y, 3 z of the crystal axes), l = field pair (1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy); used by the classes general. P(2 omega) = eps0 d E^2 for SHG with one field component (exp(+j omega t) phasors).
- `orientation` (choice; default "z_cut"; choices z_cut | x_cut | y_cut | euler) - Orientation
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.orientation`
- `euler_alpha` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when orientation in (euler)) - Euler alpha
  z-x-z Euler angle alpha in degrees (rotation crystal -> model axes Rz(alpha) Rx(beta) Rz(gamma)).
- `euler_beta` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when orientation in (euler)) - Euler beta
  z-x-z Euler angle beta in degrees (rotation crystal -> model axes Rz(alpha) Rx(beta) Rz(gamma)).
- `euler_gamma` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when orientation in (euler)) - Euler gamma
  z-x-z Euler angle gamma in degrees (rotation crystal -> model axes Rz(alpha) Rx(beta) Rz(gamma)).
- `poling` (float; unit 1; default 1; may use x, y) - Poling
  Domain sign per cell, an expression of x, y and parameters: values >= 0 keep the tensor, < 0 invert it (chi2 -> -chi2). Periodic poling for quasi phase matching: sign(sin(2 * pi * x / Lambda)) with the period Lambda = 2 pi / |k(2 omega) - 2 k(omega)| = lambda / (2 |n(2 omega) - n(omega)|) of the guided modes; 1 = unpoled. Chirped gratings and domain walls work the same way.
- `miller_scaling` (bool; default false) - Miller's rule
  Scale every process of this medium by Miller's rule, chi(n)(w; w1..wn) proportional to chi1(w) chi1(w1)..chi1(wn), chi1 = Re eps_r - 1 averaged over the medium cells at each channel frequency (poles included, evaluated once at build; the run log lists the scaled factors), normalised so that the given coefficients hold for SHG of reference_wavelength, d(2 w_r; w_r, w_r). Off: one frequency-independent tensor. Validation estimates use the unscaled values; Miller-scaled tensors are not fully permutation symmetric, so power_exchange_imbalance is no longer ~0.
- `reference_wavelength` (float; unit m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when miller_scaling in (true)) - Reference wavelength
  Vacuum pump wavelength [m] of the SHG process the d coefficients are given for (Miller's rule reference); empty (None, the default) = the first input channel.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi3_medium` - Third-order nonlinear medium

Bulk chi3 of the selected domains (tensor rotated into model axes, n2 / beta scaled by n0^2 per cell). Response (exp(+j omega t) phasors): THG P(3w) = (1/4) eps0 chi3 E^3, SPM P(w) = (3/4) eps0 chi3 |E|^2 E, XPM P(w1) = (6/4) eps0 chi3 |E2|^2 E1, degenerate FWM P(2 wp - ws) = (3/4) eps0 chi3 Ep^2 conj(Es). Undepleted mode keeps only THG / FWM-type terms feeding higher-rank channels (SPM / XPM act on a channel from itself: pump_depleted, where with the picard iteration their diagonal enters the channel operator lagged per sweep). Per-process factors thg_scale / fwm_scale or Miller's rule relative to SPM at reference_wavelength; optional steady-state free carriers from two-photon absorption (pump_depleted). Products formed at the cell centres as for chi2_medium; overlapping chi3 media add. Fields and powers are 2D: per unit length in z.

- FeatureSpec.type `chi3_medium`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `tensor` (choice; default "isotropic"; choices isotropic | cubic) - Tensor
  isotropic: chi_xxyy = chi_xyxy = chi_xyyx = chi_xxxx / 3 (glasses, amorphous films, a common approximation); cubic: chi_iijj = chi_ijij = chi_ijji = anisotropy chi_xxxx / 3 in the crystal axes (m3m: Si, Ge, GaAs Kerr), rotated by the orientation setting.
- `anisotropy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [0, inf); visible when tensor in (cubic)) - Anisotropy
  rho = 3 chi_xxyy / chi_xxxx of the cubic tensor (1 = isotropic; silicon ~1.27 at 1.55 um).
- `orientation` (choice; default "z_cut"; choices z_cut | x_cut | y_cut | euler; visible when tensor in (cubic)) - Orientation
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium.orientation`
- `euler_alpha` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when orientation in (euler)) - Euler alpha
  z-x-z Euler angle alpha in degrees (rotation crystal -> model axes Rz(alpha) Rx(beta) Rz(gamma)).
- `euler_beta` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when orientation in (euler)) - Euler beta
  z-x-z Euler angle beta in degrees (rotation crystal -> model axes Rz(alpha) Rx(beta) Rz(gamma)).
- `euler_gamma` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when orientation in (euler)) - Euler gamma
  z-x-z Euler angle gamma in degrees (rotation crystal -> model axes Rz(alpha) Rx(beta) Rz(gamma)).
- `strength` (choice; default "n2_beta"; choices n2_beta | chi3) - Strength given by
  n2_beta: chi_xxxx = (4 eps0 c n0^2 / 3) (n2 - j c tpa_beta / (2 omega_ref)) (the em_fdtd_* nonlinear_medium vocabulary); chi3: chi_xxxx = chi3_real + j chi3_imag directly. One frequency-independent chi3 serves every process (THG, SPM / XPM, FWM), although real materials differ per process.
- `n2` (float; unit m^2/W; default 0; visible when strength in (n2_beta)) - Kerr index n2
  Kerr coefficient: dn = n2 I, I = n0 c eps0 |E|^2 / 2 for a linearly polarised plane wave (SPM P = (3/4) eps0 chi3 |E|^2 E with exp(+j omega t) phasors). Silicon ~4.5e-18 to 6e-18, Si3N4 ~2.5e-19, silica ~2.6e-20 m^2/W at 1.55 um.
- `tpa_beta` (float; unit m/W; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when strength in (n2_beta)) - Two-photon absorption
  Two-photon absorption dI/dz = -beta I^2 (Im chi3 < 0 in exp(+j omega t)); silicon ~8e-12 m/W at 1.55 um. Its power is the scalar nonlinear_absorption (pump_depleted).
- `background_index` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when strength in (n2_beta) or free_carriers in (true)) - Background index
  n0 of the n2 / beta conversion and of the free-carrier permittivity; empty (None, the default) = Re sqrt(eps_r(omega_ref)) of each cell (poles included), evaluated once at build.
- `reference_wavelength` (float; unit m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when strength in (n2_beta) or any of miller_scaling, free_carriers in (true)) - Reference wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength [m] at which n2 and tpa_beta are given (omega_ref of the TPA term and of n0), the Miller's-rule reference (SPM at it) and the wavelength of the free-carrier coefficients; empty = the first input channel.
- `chi3_real` (float; unit m^2/V^2; default 0; visible when strength in (chi3)) - chi3 real part
  Re chi_xxxx [m^2/V^2] (P = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi3 E E E; silicon ~2.5e-19 at 1.55 um).
- `chi3_imag` (float; unit m^2/V^2; default 0; range (-inf, 0]; visible when strength in (chi3)) - chi3 imaginary part
  Im chi_xxxx [m^2/V^2], <= 0 (loss in exp(+j omega t)).
- `thg_scale` (float; unit 1; default 1) - Third-harmonic factor
  Factor on chi3 for the sum-frequency processes THG (3 w) and TFG (w1 + w2 + w3) of this medium (per-process chi3: the THG susceptibility of real materials differs from the Kerr one, which n2 / tpa_beta set); 1 = the Kerr chi3, 0 drops these terms. A factor != 1 breaks the full permutation symmetry (power_exchange_imbalance no longer ~0).
- `fwm_scale` (float; unit 1; default 1) - Four-wave mixing factor
  Factor on chi3 for the FWM processes of this medium (w1 + w2 - w3 onto a channel, other than SPM / XPM of a channel on itself); 1 = the Kerr chi3, 0 drops these terms.
- `miller_scaling` (bool; default false) - Miller's rule
  Scale every process of this medium by Miller's rule, chi(n)(w; w1..wn) proportional to chi1(w) chi1(w1)..chi1(wn), chi1 = Re eps_r - 1 averaged over the medium cells at each channel frequency (poles included, evaluated once at build; the run log lists the scaled factors), normalised so that the given coefficients hold for SPM at reference_wavelength (the n2 / tpa_beta process). Off: one frequency-independent tensor. Validation estimates use the unscaled values; Miller-scaled tensors are not fully permutation symmetric, so power_exchange_imbalance is no longer ~0.
- `free_carriers` (bool; default false) - Free carriers
  Steady-state free carriers from two-photon absorption (coupling_mode pump_depleted only; ignored undepleted, with a warning): N = carrier_lifetime G per cell, G = the TPA power density of the applied SPM / XPM terms / (2 hbar omega) (one electron-hole pair per two photons; no diffusion, so N follows the local intensity squared), and every channel sees dn = -fcd_coefficient N and alpha = fca_cross_section N, both x (lambda / reference_wavelength)^2 (Drude scaling), as delta eps = 2 n0 dn - j n0 c alpha / omega (n0 = background_index or Re sqrt eps_r(omega_ref) per cell). Linear in N (the Soref-Bennett N^0.8 hole term is linearised into fcd_coefficient). Field carrier_density, scalars free_carrier_absorption and peak_carrier_density.
- `carrier_lifetime` (float; unit s; default 1e-09; range [0, inf); visible when free_carriers in (true)) - Carrier lifetime
  Effective free-carrier lifetime tau [s]: silicon wires ~0.5-3 ns, with carrier sweep-out by a reverse-biased junction ~10-100 ps; 0 = no carriers.
- `fcd_coefficient` (float; unit m^3; default 1.35e-27; range [0, inf); visible when free_carriers in (true)) - Carrier index coefficient
  Free-carrier dispersion dn = -fcd_coefficient N at reference_wavelength [m^3]; silicon at 1.55 um ~1.35e-27 (equal electron and hole densities, a linear fit of Soref-Bennett).
- `fca_cross_section` (float; unit m^2; default 1.45e-21; range [0, inf); visible when free_carriers in (true)) - Carrier absorption cross-section
  Free-carrier absorption alpha = fca_cross_section N at reference_wavelength [m^2]; silicon at 1.55 um ~1.45e-21 (equal electron and hole densities).

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.surface_chi2` - Surface second-order nonlinearity

Surface chi2 sheet on the interface of the selected domains (nonlinear_optics_plan 3.3): surface polarisation P_s [C/m] = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E with the isotropic-surface tensor (chi_s_nnn; chi_s_ntt = chi_s_nzz; chi_s_tnt = chi_s_ttn = chi_s_znz = chi_s_zzn) in the local frame of the outward normal n, the in-plane tangent t = z x n and z; SHG of one channel P_s,n = (1/2) eps0 (chi_s_nnn E_n^2 + chi_s_ntt (E_t^2 + E_z^2)), P_s,t = eps0 chi_s_tnt E_n E_t, P_s,z = eps0 chi_s_tnt E_n E_z. Sites are the cell faces between a selected and an unselected cell: the face samples its own tangential E exactly, E_z as the mean of its two cells and E_n at the selvedge cell (face mean), and returns P_s by the exact adjoint (the tangential parts as a sheet current on the face, z split half and half onto the two cells, the normal part as a one-cell dipole layer), so the discrete power exchange stays exact. Its mixing terms join the chi2 media in the table (SHG / SFG / DFG onto the declared channels; hz channels carry E_n / E_t, ez channels E_z). Normal-incidence SHG of a flat interface vanishes by symmetry: curvature, corners or oblique fields are needed. Powers are 2D: per unit length in z.

- FeatureSpec.type `surface_chi2`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `chi_s_nnn` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0) - chi_s nnn
  Surface susceptibility chi_s_nnn [m^2/V] (chi_perp,perp,perp) of the isotropic (C_inf_v) surface: the normal polarisation from the normal field, P_s,n = (1/2) eps0 chi_s_nnn E_n^2 for SHG of one channel; n = the outward normal of the selection. Noble metals: of order 1e-19 to 1e-18 m^2/V (literature values spread by an order of magnitude and depend on the selvedge convention).
- `chi_s_ntt` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0) - chi_s ntt
  chi_s_ntt = chi_s_nzz [m^2/V] (chi_perp,par,par): normal polarisation from the tangential fields, P_s,n = (1/2) eps0 chi_s_ntt (E_t^2 + E_z^2) for SHG; t = z x n is the in-plane tangent. A normal polarisation sheet is a dipole layer: it jumps the tangential E across the interface (it does not radiate at normal incidence on a flat interface).
- `chi_s_tnt` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0) - chi_s tnt
  chi_s_tnt = chi_s_ttn = chi_s_znz = chi_s_zzn [m^2/V] (chi_par,perp,par): tangential polarisation from the normal times a tangential field, P_s,t = eps0 chi_s_tnt E_n E_t and P_s,z = eps0 chi_s_tnt E_n E_z for SHG of one channel. chi_s_ntt = chi_s_tnt makes the tensor fully permutation symmetric (power_exchange_imbalance ~0).
- `selvedge` (choice; default "inside"; choices inside | outside) - Normal field side
  Cell row whose normal E the sheet samples and whose normal-E faces carry the normal polarisation P_s,n / w (a one-cell dipole layer): inside = the selected cell at each interface face, outside = its unselected neighbour. E_n jumps by eps_out / eps_in across the interface, so this is the field (and permittivity) convention of chi_s_nnn; the tangential E and E_z are sampled on the interface itself (the face / the mean of the two cells). The tangential jump then sits half a cell off the interface: first order in the mesh.
- `interface` (choice; default "staircase"; choices staircase | smoothed) - Interface shape
  staircase: the sites are the cell faces between selected and unselected cells with normal +-x / +-y and the face length: exact for axis-aligned sides, but a curve is up to 4 / pi too long (mean 4 / pi) and its normals point along the axes. smoothed: the same faces, with the normal of the drawn shape where it crosses the line between the two cells of the face (point tests at build) and the length face x |n . face normal|, so a curve has its true length and normal (the sites stay on the faces: first order in the mesh; flat axis-aligned sides stay exact, corners are rounded over about a cell).
- `interface_with` (names: geometry names; default []) - Only facing
  Domain objects: only the interface faces whose unselected cell lies in one of them carry the sheet (e.g. the metal / air side of a ridge on a substrate); empty (the default) = every unselected neighbour.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.sheet_nonlinearity` - Nonlinear sheet

Nonlinear 2D-material sheet on an axis-aligned line (nonlinear_optics_plan 3.4): a surface polarisation P_s [C/m] (chi_s(2): D3h monolayer or general) or a sheet current K [A/m] (sigma3, entered as P_s = K / (j omega)) from the tangential fields of the sites the conducting_sheet feature uses: E_z at the line-cell centres, the in-plane tangential E on their hi faces; the result goes back to the same sites (E_z as a density over the line-cell width, the tangential E as a face current over the face spacing), exact for the discrete equations. Its terms join the mixing table (sigma3 as up to two media: the THG / TFG value under the feature name, the SPM / XPM / FWM value as '<name>:kerr'). Combine it with conducting_sheet on the same line for the linear sheet response. pump_depleted: sheet SPM / XPM stay in the rhs (no lagged operator term); their absorption (Re sigma3 > 0) is in nonlinear_absorption and in absorbed_power (deposited in the line cells, so em_heat_joule heats them). The adjoint (eps_sensitivity, optimization) differentiates the sheet terms. The line covers the cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) along it; a span end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML.

- FeatureSpec.type `sheet_nonlinearity`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `sheet_model` (choice; default "D3h"; choices D3h | chi2_general | sigma3) - Nonlinearity
  D3h: a transition-metal-dichalcogenide monolayer chi_s(2) (MoS2, WS2, ...): chi_aaa = chi_s, chi_abb = chi_bab = chi_bba = -chi_s with the armchair axis a at armchair_angle in the sheet plane (t, z); chi2_general: the six chi_s_<ijk> of (t, z); sigma3: the in-plane isotropic third-order sheet conductivity of graphene, K = 2^(1-n) sum sigma3 : E E E [A/m] (THG K = sigma3 E^3 / 4, SPM K = (3/4) sigma3 |E|^2 E), entered as P_s = K / (j omega) of the target channel; the THG / TFG value and the SPM / XPM / FWM value are separate (they differ by orders of magnitude in graphene; no Cheng-Vermeulen-Sipe model here).
- `chi_s` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (D3h)) - chi_s
  D3h sheet susceptibility chi_s = chi_aaa [m^2/V] (P_s = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E [C/m]); MoS2 / WS2 monolayers ~1e-20 to 1e-19 m^2/V at near-infrared SHG (bulk-equivalent d times the 0.65 nm layer thickness; literature values span an order of magnitude).
- `armchair_angle` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (D3h)) - Armchair angle
  Angle of the D3h armchair axis a from t toward z [deg] in the sheet frame: t = along the line (+x for a horizontal, +y for a vertical line), z out of the plane; the normal field does not enter; 0 = armchair along the line (E_z alone then drives P_t = -(1/2) eps0 chi_s E_z^2), 90 = armchair out of the plane (E_t alone drives P_z = -(1/2) eps0 chi_s E_t^2). The response has a 120 degree period.
- `chi_s_ttt` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (chi2_general)) - chi_s ttt
  Sheet susceptibility chi_s_ttt [m^2/V] of a general 2D chi_s(2) in the sheet frame: t = along the line (+x for a horizontal, +y for a vertical line), z out of the plane; the normal field does not enter (ttz = tzt, zzt = ztz); P_s = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E [C/m].
- `chi_s_tzz` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (chi2_general)) - chi_s tzz
  Sheet susceptibility chi_s_tzz [m^2/V] of a general 2D chi_s(2) in the sheet frame: t = along the line (+x for a horizontal, +y for a vertical line), z out of the plane; the normal field does not enter (ttz = tzt, zzt = ztz); P_s = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E [C/m].
- `chi_s_ttz` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (chi2_general)) - chi_s ttz
  Sheet susceptibility chi_s_ttz [m^2/V] of a general 2D chi_s(2) in the sheet frame: t = along the line (+x for a horizontal, +y for a vertical line), z out of the plane; the normal field does not enter (ttz = tzt, zzt = ztz); P_s = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E [C/m].
- `chi_s_ztt` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (chi2_general)) - chi_s ztt
  Sheet susceptibility chi_s_ztt [m^2/V] of a general 2D chi_s(2) in the sheet frame: t = along the line (+x for a horizontal, +y for a vertical line), z out of the plane; the normal field does not enter (ttz = tzt, zzt = ztz); P_s = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E [C/m].
- `chi_s_zzz` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (chi2_general)) - chi_s zzz
  Sheet susceptibility chi_s_zzz [m^2/V] of a general 2D chi_s(2) in the sheet frame: t = along the line (+x for a horizontal, +y for a vertical line), z out of the plane; the normal field does not enter (ttz = tzt, zzt = ztz); P_s = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E [C/m].
- `chi_s_zzt` (float; unit m^2/V; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (chi2_general)) - chi_s zzt
  Sheet susceptibility chi_s_zzt [m^2/V] of a general 2D chi_s(2) in the sheet frame: t = along the line (+x for a horizontal, +y for a vertical line), z out of the plane; the normal field does not enter (ttz = tzt, zzt = ztz); P_s = eps0 2^(1-n) sum chi_s : E E [C/m].
- `sigma3_real` (float; unit S m^2/V^2; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (sigma3)) - sigma3 (Kerr) real part
  Re sigma3 [S m^2/V^2] of the SPM / XPM / FWM processes (in-plane isotropic: sigma_tttt = sigma_zzzz, sigma_ttzz = sigma_tztz = sigma_tzzt = sigma / 3); exp(+j omega t) phasors, Re > 0 absorbs. Graphene values depend strongly on the Fermi energy and the photon energies (literature ~1e-24 to 1e-20).
- `sigma3_imag` (float; unit S m^2/V^2; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (sigma3)) - sigma3 (Kerr) imaginary part
  Im sigma3 [S m^2/V^2] of the SPM / XPM / FWM processes (exp(+j omega t): opposite sign to the exp(-i omega t) literature).
- `thg_sigma3_real` (float; unit S m^2/V^2; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (sigma3)) - sigma3 (THG) real part
  Re sigma3 [S m^2/V^2] of the third-harmonic and three-frequency sum processes (THG, TFG), same tensor form as sigma3_real.
- `thg_sigma3_imag` (float; unit S m^2/V^2; default 0; visible when sheet_model in (sigma3)) - sigma3 (THG) imaginary part
  Im sigma3 [S m^2/V^2] of THG / TFG (exp(+j omega t) phasors).

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor in every channel. E_z channels: Perfect electric conductor: E_z = 0 in every cell whose centre lies in the selected domains (those unknowns are pinned and decoupled from their neighbours), staircased to the mesh; with solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries the H links from free cells into it put E_z = 0 at the drawn wall instead (exact wall distance t d, t >= 0.02). H_z channels: Perfect electric conductor: tangential E = 0 on every face of each cell whose centre lies in the selected domains (E_x on its +y and -y faces, E_y on its +x and -x faces; those faces drop out of the operator, so H_z inside is 0), staircased to the mesh. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra) only faces wholly inside the drawn metal are PEC and each cut cell takes its free face lengths in the operator and its free area (>= 0.02 of the cell) in the k0^2 mu term, which keeps the operator reciprocal; mode ports, sources and eps_xy couplings keep the cell mask.

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.conducting_sheet` - Conducting sheet

Conducting sheet in every channel, sigma_s evaluated at each channel frequency (the linear response; sheet_nonlinearity on the same line adds the nonlinear one). Zero-thickness conducting sheet (2D material: graphene, a TMD monolayer in its linear response, a metal film much thinner than a cell) on an axis-aligned line: the tangential E drives the surface current K = sigma_s E_t [A/m], the normal E does not conduct. E_z (em_fdfd_ez): E_z of the line cells is tangential to any line, the delta enters the operator diagonal as -j omega mu0 sigma_s / w (w = the line-cell width across the line), exact for the 3-point stencil. H_z (em_fdfd_hz): the tangential E is E_x (horizontal line) or E_y (vertical line) on the hi face of the line cells (as an H_z line source), whose face permittivity gains -j sigma_s / (omega eps0 w) with w the face spacing; the line may not lie in the last grid cell before a non-periodic outer face. A sheet in vacuum at normal incidence transmits |1 / (1 + eta0 sigma_s / 2)|^2 (exactly 1 / |1 + omega mu0 sigma_s w / (2 sin(k w))|^2 on the grid, k the discrete wavenumber). Loss 1/2 Re sigma_s |E_t|^2 per unit area of sheet is added to absorbed_power (q_abs) of the line cells as a density over the line-cell width, so q_abs integrates to the sheet loss and em_heat_joule heats those cells. The sheet enters only the operator: line-source and TFSF calibrations, mode-port solves and the material maps do not see it (keep source lines, port lines and the TFSF outline off it; enclose it in the TFSF box as a scatterer). A span end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML (as a line source: a domain-wide sheet has no end). Several sheets on one line add. In an eigenfrequency study sigma_s stays at its value at the target wavelength (first-order error away from it). The line covers the cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1) along it. No result (absorbed_power and the monitors show its effect).

- FeatureSpec.type `conducting_sheet`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `model` (choice; default "constant"; choices constant | graphene_kubo) - Conductivity model
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.model`
- `sigma_real` (float; unit S; default 6.08534e-05; visible when model in (constant)) - Conductivity (real part)
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.sigma_real`
- `sigma_imag` (float; unit S; default 0; visible when model in (constant)) - Conductivity (imaginary part)
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.sigma_imag`
- `fermi_energy` (float; unit eV; default 0.2; visible when model in (graphene_kubo)) - Fermi energy
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.fermi_energy`
- `scattering_time` (float; unit s; default 1e-13; range (0, inf); visible when model in (graphene_kubo)) - Scattering time
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.conducting_sheet.scattering_time`
- `temperature` (float; unit K; default 300; range (0, inf); visible when model in (graphene_kubo)) - Temperature
  Electron temperature T [K] of the Fermi functions (intraband weight and the smeared interband edge, width ~4 kT).

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.design_region` - Design region

Density design region on the selected domains (window cells only): each cell carries a density rho in [0, 1], filtered by a conic filter of filter_radius and projected by a tanh of projection_beta / projection_eta to rho_bar, and gets eps = eps_min + rho_bar (eps_max - eps_min) in its permittivity arrays (em_fdfd_ez: eps_r; em_fdfd_hz: eps_xx and eps_yy, an isotropic change), overwriting the material permittivity there (sigma_e, poles and mu_r stay the material's). The optimization study varies rho to maximise the adjoint_objective sum J; any other study solves the initial_density design. Design regions of one physics must not share cells. Keep the region off every source, port and objective line and the cells beyond their hi faces (the adjoint gradient is not exact there). Output field design_density = rho_bar (0 outside every design region). Result 'xy' versus iteration (0 = initial design, one point per accepted L-BFGS-B iteration): series objective (J of the whole model, W/m) and grayness (mean 4 rho_bar (1 - rho_bar) of this region, 0 = binary); extras n_cells, eps_min, eps_max, mean_density and final_grayness of the current design, and note (non-empty outside an optimization study, whose result is one point: iteration 0 with objective NaN). In em_fdfd_nonlinear one region writes eps_r, eps_xx and eps_yy (every channel sees the design, each at its own frequency); the chi2 / chi3 media and their poling stay where they are drawn. The optimization study runs coupling_mode 'undepleted' (cascade adjoint) or 'pump_depleted' (fixed-point adjoint; iteration_method 'newton' with a chi3 medium).

- FeatureSpec.type `design_region`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `eps_min` (float; unit 1; default 2.085; range [1, inf)) - Permittivity at density 0
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.eps_min`
- `eps_max` (float; unit 1; default 12.08; range [1, inf)) - Permittivity at density 1
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.eps_max`
- `initial_density` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range [0, 1]) - Initial density
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.initial_density`
- `filter_radius` (float; unit m; default 1e-07; range [0, inf)) - Filter radius
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.filter_radius`
- `projection_beta` (float; unit 1; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Projection sharpness
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.projection_beta`
- `projection_eta` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range [0, 1]) - Projection threshold
  Help: shared `em_eme.design_region.projection_eta`

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source` - Point source

The em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz feature point_source on one harmonic channel (setting channel): its polarisation picks the E_z or H_z form, the channel frequency is the solve frequency. E_z channels: z-directed filament current phasor I e^{j phase} in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell). It radiates a cylindrical wave whose field does not depend on the mesh: |E_z| = omega mu0 I / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| in a homogeneous non-magnetic medium of wavenumber k. H_z channels: Current-calibrated point excitation phasor in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell); its field does not depend on the mesh. magnetic_current: a z-directed magnetic line current K_m [V] at the cell centre, radiating |H_z| = omega eps0 eps_r K_m / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)|. electric_dipole: an in-plane electric current element of strength M [A] along orientation, split over the two E_x faces (+y / -y) and the two E_y faces (+x / -x) of the cell, radiating |H_z| = k M / 4 |H1^(2)(k r)| |sin(phi - orientation)|. Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales with them (P ~ E^n), unlike a linear FDFD result.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `current` (float; unit A; default 0.001) - Electric line current
  E_z channels only: Peak z-directed filament current I. The radiated field does not depend on the mesh: in a homogeneous non-magnetic medium of wavenumber k, |E_z| = omega mu0 I / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| (1 mA at wavelength 1 um: ~2e5 V/m at r = 1 um). Fields are linear, so results scale with I. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`
- `excitation` (choice; default "magnetic_current"; choices magnetic_current | electric_dipole) - Excitation
  H_z channels only: magnetic_current: z-directed magnetic line current at the cell centre (radiates the same in every direction). electric_dipole: in-plane electric current element along orientation, spread over the four E faces of the cell (radiates most broadside, nothing along its axis).
- `magnetic_current` (float; unit V; default 1; visible when excitation in (magnetic_current)) - Magnetic line current
  H_z channels only: Peak z-directed magnetic line current K_m in V (the dual of a filament current). The radiated field does not depend on the mesh: in a homogeneous medium of relative permittivity eps_r and wavenumber k, |H_z| = omega eps0 eps_r K_m / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| (1 V at wavelength 1 um in vacuum: |H_z| ~ 1.3e3 A/m at r = 1 um). Fields are linear, so results scale with K_m. A fixed K_m radiates power ~ n^2 of its cell, so it drifts when eps there changes (e.g. thermo-optic); a filament current or dipole radiates n-independent power. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `dipole_moment` (float; unit A; default 0.001; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole strength
  H_z channels only: Peak in-plane electric dipole strength M in A: the integral of the current density J over the cross-section, i.e. A*m of current moment per m of z, along orientation. The radiated field does not depend on the mesh: in a homogeneous medium of wavenumber k, |H_z| = k M / 4 |H1^(2)(k r)| |sin(phi - orientation)| at the angle phi counter-clockwise from +x (1 mA at wavelength 1 um in vacuum: |H_z| ~ 5e2 A/m at r = 1 um broadside). Fields are linear, so results scale with M. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `orientation` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole orientation
  H_z channels only: Direction of the dipole current in degrees counter-clockwise from +x: 0 drives only the E_x faces, 90 only the E_y faces. It radiates most broadside (perpendicular to it) and nothing along it.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.line_source` - Line source

The em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz feature line_source on one harmonic channel (setting channel): its polarisation picks the E_z or H_z form, the channel frequency is the solve frequency. E_z channels: Sheet current phasor on an axis-aligned line radiating amplitude V/m of E_z to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) sends waves along +x and -x, a horizontal one along +y and -y. For a plane wave, span the whole domain: an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML (on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. H_z channels: Electric sheet current phasor on an axis-aligned line radiating amplitude V/m of tangential E to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) drives E_y and sends waves along +x and -x, a horizontal one drives E_x and sends them along +y and -y. The sheet sits on the hi face of the line cells (+x face of a vertical line, +y face of a horizontal one), and the local impedance uses that face permittivity (width-weighted mean of its two cells). For a plane wave, span the whole domain: an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML (on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales with them (P ~ E^n), unlike a linear FDFD result.

- FeatureSpec.type `line_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  E_z channels: E_z radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); the calibration uses the complex eps_r (sigma_e and dispersion included) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength, so it is exact in any homogeneous medium. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so on a line crossing several media (e.g. a high-index core and its cladding) the current steps at the interfaces, the steps diffract and the field there is not the amplitude (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Each recalibration (e.g. a thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n of the line cells (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2). Typical 1 V/m. H_z channels: Tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); the calibration uses the complex face permittivity (the mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, sigma_e and dispersion included) and mu of the line cells at the solved wavelength, so it is exact in any homogeneous medium. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so on a line crossing several media (e.g. a high-index core and its cladding) the current steps at the interfaces, the steps diffract and the field there is not the amplitude (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). Each recalibration (e.g. a thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n of the line cells (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2). Typical 1 V/m.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.point_source.phase`

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.gaussian_beam` - Gaussian beam

The em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz feature gaussian_beam on one harmonic channel (setting channel): its polarisation picks the E_z or H_z form, the channel frequency is the solve frequency. E_z channels: Line source with the profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line, radiating a beam of peak E_z = amplitude V/m to each side in the local medium (vertical line: along +x and -x; horizontal: along +y and -y); the waist lies on the line. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. H_z channels: Line source with the profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line, radiating a beam of peak tangential E = amplitude V/m to each side in the local medium (vertical line: E_y, along +x and -x; horizontal: E_x, along +y and -y); the waist lies on the line and the sheet on the hi face of the line cells. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales with them (P ~ E^n), unlike a linear FDFD result.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.plane_wave_tfsf` - Plane wave box (+x)

The em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz feature plane_wave_tfsf on one harmonic channel (setting channel): its polarisation picks the E_z or H_z form, the channel frequency is the solve frequency. E_z channels: Plane wave travelling along +x only, injected on the outline of a total-field box: the unknown is the total E_z in the box cells and only the scattered field outside; amplitude = incident E_z, its phase referred to the centres of the first (lo-x) column of box cells; the jump enters the right-hand side through the operator rows on both sides of the outline. The incident wave is the discrete plane wave of the FDFD stencil in the background medium, the complex eps and mu_r at the solve wavelength of the outline cell just before the lo-x edge (uniform cells: numerical wavenumber k from (2 / dx) sin(k dx / 2) = n k0, n = sqrt(eps mu_r); graded x cells: the wave is marched cell by cell on the solved stencil from the lo-x edge, so it stays an exact discrete solution on any widths, starting as the uniform wave of the two cells at the lo-x edge (a grading there adds a small backward part); a lossy background attenuates it), so a box in a uniform medium (vacuum, a cladding) is exactly transparent on uniform and graded meshes alike: the box edges must lie in one uniform medium (warning otherwise: incident light leaks into the scattered field), and the box needs one scattered-field cell inside the domain on every side, except along a periodic y axis, where it may instead cover every y cell (y0 = 0, y1 = the domain height: no y edges, so a grating or a layered stack may cross it), and at a y mirror face of the wave's parity (ez: symmetric, hz: antisymmetric), where it may reach the plane: the box opens there and its mirror image completes it (the other parity, or an x mirror face, is an error). With bloch_ky != 0 (periodic y) the wave is oblique, exp(-j (k_x x + ky y)) with ky = bloch_ky, its phase referred to y = 0, and k_x from (2 / dx)^2 sin^2(k_x dx / 2) = (n k0)^2 - (2 / dy)^2 sin^2(ky dy / 2) (refused when that is not positive: evanescent); it needs uniform y cells (validation error on a graded y axis: exp(-j ky y) is no Bloch wave of graded rows; x may be graded). Enclose the scatterers with the box and put a far_field box outside it; flux and mode monitors must not straddle its outline (inside: total field, outside: scattered field). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. H_z channels: Plane wave travelling along +x only (E_y, H_z = n E_y / (eta0 mu_r)), injected on the outline of a total-field box: the unknown is the total H_z in the box cells and only the scattered field outside; amplitude = incident E_y, its phase referred to the centres of the first (lo-x) column of box cells; the jump enters the right-hand side through the operator rows on both sides of the outline. The incident wave is the discrete plane wave of the FDFD stencil in the background medium, the complex eps and mu_r at the solve wavelength of the outline cell just before the lo-x edge (uniform cells: numerical wavenumber k from (2 / dx) sin(k dx / 2) = n k0, n = sqrt(eps mu_r); graded x cells: the wave is marched cell by cell on the solved stencil from the lo-x edge, so it stays an exact discrete solution on any widths, starting as the uniform wave of the two cells at the lo-x edge (a grading there adds a small backward part); a lossy background attenuates it), so a box in a uniform medium (vacuum, a cladding) is exactly transparent on uniform and graded meshes alike: the box edges must lie in one uniform medium (warning otherwise: incident light leaks into the scattered field), and the box needs one scattered-field cell inside the domain on every side, except along a periodic y axis, where it may instead cover every y cell (y0 = 0, y1 = the domain height: no y edges, so a grating or a layered stack may cross it), and at a y mirror face of the wave's parity (ez: symmetric, hz: antisymmetric), where it may reach the plane: the box opens there and its mirror image completes it (the other parity, or an x mirror face, is an error). With bloch_ky != 0 (periodic y) the wave is oblique, exp(-j (k_x x + ky y)) with ky = bloch_ky, its phase referred to y = 0, and k_x from (2 / dx)^2 sin^2(k_x dx / 2) = (n k0)^2 - (2 / dy)^2 sin^2(ky dy / 2) (refused when that is not positive: evanescent); it needs uniform y cells (validation error on a graded y axis: exp(-j ky y) is no Bloch wave of graded rows; x may be graded). Enclose the scatterers with the box and put a far_field box outside it; flux and mode monitors must not straddle its outline (inside: total field, outside: scattered field). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales with them (P ~ E^n), unlike a linear FDFD result.

- FeatureSpec.type `plane_wave_tfsf`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  E_z channels: Peak incident E_z of the +x plane wave (computed for the uniform medium on the box outline); the scattered field outside the box is relative to it. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Typical 1 V/m. H_z channels: Peak incident in-plane |E| of the +x plane wave, E_y at normal incidence (computed for the uniform medium on the box outline, H_z = n |E| / (eta0 mu_r) with n = sqrt(eps_yy mu_r) there, also for the oblique wave of a Bloch ky); the scattered field outside the box is relative to it. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Typical 1 V/m.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.mode_source` - Mode source

The em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz feature mode_source on one harmonic channel (setting channel): its polarisation picks the E_z or H_z form, the channel frequency is the solve frequency. E_z channels: Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction: a vertical line (x = const) launches toward +x (direction positive) or -x (negative), a horizontal one toward +y or -y. It is a one-sided total-field / scattered-field line: the unknown is the total field from the line cells downstream and only the scattered field (what comes back) upstream; the mode profile enters the right-hand side through the operator rows of the line cells and of their upstream neighbours, whose shared face is the interface (the lo face of the line cells for positive, their hi face for negative). The launch is exact and one-sided at every solved wavelength of a straight guide (no band-edge leakage as with a pulsed em_fdtd mode source). Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. The 1D eigenmodes along the line use the FDFD discretisation (Yee cell widths, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at the solve wavelength with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are re-solved at every solved wavelength and whenever the materials changed since the previous solve (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity), so the port always matches the current guide. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec domain edge takes E_z = 0, one on a pmc or symmetric edge dE_z/dn = 0 and one on an antisymmetric edge E_z odd about the plane, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E_z = 0 in the next cell), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'table' of the latest port solve (a frequency_domain study: its last solved wavelength), one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss in the exp(+j omega t) convention), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the two ends of the solved line / its peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode) and selected (True for the launched mode); extras wavelength (m), power (W/m), direction, mode_number and phase (deg). H_z channels: Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction: a vertical line (x = const) launches toward +x (direction positive) or -x (negative), a horizontal one toward +y or -y. It is a one-sided total-field / scattered-field line: the unknown is the total field from the line cells downstream and only the scattered field (what comes back) upstream; the mode profile enters the right-hand side through the operator rows of the line cells and of their upstream neighbours, whose shared face is the interface (the lo face of the line cells for positive, their hi face for negative). The launch is exact and one-sided at every solved wavelength of a straight guide (no band-edge leakage as with a pulsed em_fdtd mode source). Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. The 1D eigenmodes along the line use the FDFD discretisation (Yee cell widths, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at the solve wavelength with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are re-solved at every solved wavelength and whenever the materials changed since the previous solve (thermo-optic coupling, state-dependent permittivity), so the port always matches the current guide. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side, on a locally uniform mesh (validation warns when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line and when its face lies inside a CPML layer, i.e. the line is in the outermost window cell). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The in-plane E faces use the permittivity of the operator (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the mean of core and cladding there. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'table' of the latest port solve (a frequency_domain study: its last solved wavelength), one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss in the exp(+j omega t) convention), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the two ends of the solved line / its peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode) and selected (True for the launched mode); extras wavelength (m), power (W/m), direction, mode_number and phase (deg). Amplitudes are absolute: the nonlinear response scales with them (P ~ E^n), unlike a linear FDFD result.

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `table`

- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (choice; default "positive"; choices positive | negative) - Direction

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.field_probe` - Field probe

The em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz feature field_probe on one harmonic channel (setting channel): its polarisation picks the E_z or H_z form, the channel frequency is the solve frequency. Phasor of one field component in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell) at every solved wavelength. The face components (ez hx / hy, hz ex / ey) come from neighbouring cells, so keep them off a plane_wave_tfsf outline and a mode_source interface face, where the solved field jumps between total and scattered field (validation warns). Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength (x in m, ascending; one point per solved wavelength, so a stationary study gives one, and a wavelength solved again keeps its latest solve): series abs = |phasor| in the unit of the component and phase = its argument in rad (exp(+j omega t): the field is abs cos(omega t + phase)); y_label the component label (e.g. E_z); extras frequency (Hz), wavelength (m), component (e.g. ez) and unit.

- FeatureSpec.type `field_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `component` (choice; choices ez | hx | hy | hz | ex | ey; optional (null allowed)) - Field component
  Empty (None, the default) = the channel's out-of-plane field (ez or hz). E_z channels: ez in V/m at the centre of the cell containing the point; hx / hy in A/m on the +y / +x face of that cell (the FDTD probe positions), from the discrete curl of E_z. H_z channels: hz in A/m at the centre of the cell containing the point; ex / ey in V/m from Ampere's law on the faces (the discrete curl of H_z plus the current of a line source, gaussian beam or electric dipole on that face), averaged over the two faces of that cell that carry the component (collocated at the centre, unlike the raw face samples of the FDTD probe).

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

The em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz feature flux_monitor on one harmonic channel (setting channel): its polarisation picks the E_z or H_z form, the channel frequency is the solve frequency. E_z channels: Time-averaged Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line at every solved wavelength: S_x = -1/2 Re(E_z H_y*) through a vertical line, S_y = 1/2 Re(E_z H_x*) through a horizontal one, with E_z of the line cells and H from the discrete curl of E_z on their hi face; > 0 toward +x / +y. Keep its measuring face (the hi face of the line cells) off the interface face of a mode_source (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or on the line of a negative one), and keep the line with its measuring face entirely inside or entirely outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: those sources enter only the right-hand side, so the field jumps across their interface and a monitor there mixes total and scattered field (validation warns). Result 'flux_spectrum' with unit 'W/m': power per unit z length, summed over the line cells, absolute (no source-spectrum normalisation: a line source of amplitude A spanning the period L of a periodic axis in vacuum sends A^2 L / (2 eta0) to each side), one entry per solved wavelength sorted by wavelength. The discrete flux is conserved exactly through lossless cells; a transmission is the device power over the power of a reference run with the same source. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. H_z channels: Time-averaged Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line at every solved wavelength: S_x = 1/2 Re(E_y H_z*) through a vertical line, S_y = -1/2 Re(E_x H_z*) through a horizontal one, with H_z of the line cells and E on their hi face from Ampere's law (the discrete curl of H_z plus a source current on that face); > 0 toward +x / +y. Keep the line off the line cells of a line source or gaussian beam: their sheet sits on the same face, where the flux jumps by the radiated power, and the monitor reads the line-cell side (minus the power sent toward -x / -y). Keep its measuring face (the hi face of the line cells) off the interface face of a mode_source (the line one cell upstream of a positive source, or on the line of a negative one), and keep the line with its measuring face entirely inside or entirely outside a plane_wave_tfsf box: those sources enter only the right-hand side, so the field jumps across their interface and a monitor there mixes total and scattered field (validation warns). Result 'flux_spectrum' with unit 'W/m': power per unit z length, summed over the line cells, absolute (no source-spectrum normalisation: a line source of amplitude A spanning the period L of a periodic axis in vacuum sends A^2 L / (2 eta0) to each side), one entry per solved wavelength sorted by wavelength. The discrete flux is conserved exactly through lossless cells; a transmission is the device power over the power of a reference run with the same source. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

  Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.far_field` - Far-field pattern

The em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz feature far_field on one harmonic channel (setting channel): its polarisation picks the E_z or H_z form, the channel frequency is the solve frequency. E_z channels: Near-to-far-field transform of the solved phasors on the outline of a rectangle: E_z and H from the discrete curl of E_z (averaged onto the centres) at the sample points of the em_fdtd_ez far_field, so normalised patterns of the two types compare directly; radiated power per unit length and angle rho |E_z|^2 / (2 eta0) in W/(m rad) (its angle integral is the power through a closed flux box) versus angle, counter-clockwise from +x, one row per solved wavelength (ascending). The transform assumes vacuum outside the box (vacuum wavenumber and impedance): enclose every scatterer with the box; with a plane_wave_tfsf keep it outside the TFSF box, in the scattered field (inside, the incident plane wave would dominate the pattern): its x0 / y0 edges at least two cells before those of the TFSF box and its x1 / y1 edges in or beyond the first cell past it (each sample averages the faces on both sides of its cell, and a face on the TFSF outline mixes total and scattered field; validation warns otherwise, and for a box edge sampling across a mode_source interface face). Graded meshes work: the samples sit on the actual cell centres with trapezoid weights of their spacing (the faces on both sides of a sample cell average onto its centre); the closed contour runs through the centres of the first box cells and of the cells one beyond x1 / y1 (keep the box one cell off the x_hi / y_hi edges), and the box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. H_z channels: Near-to-far-field transform of the solved phasors on the outline of a rectangle: H_z and E from Ampere's law (the discrete curl of H_z, averaged onto the centres) at the sample points of the em_fdtd_hz far_field, so normalised patterns of the two types compare directly; radiated power per unit length and angle rho |eta0 H_z|^2 / (2 eta0) (|eta0 H_z| = the far-field |E| in vacuum) in W/(m rad) (its angle integral is the power through a closed flux box) versus angle, counter-clockwise from +x, one row per solved wavelength (ascending). The transform assumes vacuum outside the box (vacuum wavenumber and impedance): enclose every scatterer with the box; with a plane_wave_tfsf keep it outside the TFSF box, in the scattered field (inside, the incident plane wave would dominate the pattern): its x0 / y0 edges at least two cells before those of the TFSF box and its x1 / y1 edges in or beyond the first cell past it (each sample averages the faces on both sides of its cell, and a face on the TFSF outline mixes total and scattered field; validation warns otherwise, and for a box edge sampling across a mode_source interface face). Graded meshes work: the samples sit on the actual cell centres with trapezoid weights of their spacing (the faces on both sides of a sample cell average onto its centre); the closed contour runs through the centres of the first box cells and of the cells one beyond x1 / y1 (keep the box one cell off the x_hi / y_hi edges), and the box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

  Far-field angles evenly spaced over 360 degrees, counter-clockwise from +x (0 = +x, pi/2 = +y); 360 gives 1-degree steps.

### Feature `em_fdfd_nonlinear.adjoint_objective` - Optimization objective

The em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz feature adjoint_objective on one harmonic channel (setting channel): its polarisation picks the E_z or H_z form, the channel frequency is the solve frequency. Objective term for the adjoint sensitivity: a flux_monitor or mode_monitor quantity on an axis-aligned line times weight. Every solve records the quantity; the output field eps_sensitivity is dJ/d eps_r per unit area [W/m^3] of J = sum of weight * quantity over the enabled objectives, from one extra sparse solve with the transposed operator on the forward factorisation (no new factorisation with scipy_splu), computed when the field is read (snapshot, derived value). A small permittivity change d eps in a region R changes J by the integral of eps_sensitivity * d eps over R; for em_fdfd_hz it is the sum of the eps_xx and eps_yy terms (an isotropic change, an off-diagonal eps_xy held fixed), and its output field eps_xy_sensitivity is dJ/d eps_xy per unit area from the same solve (zero where the solve drops eps_xy: PEC cells, the outer two rows of a wall or mirror face). For em_fdfd_hz the face fields an objective reads and the right-hand side of dipole and line source face currents are differentiated with the face permittivity; line source calibrations, port modes and a mode monitor's mode are held fixed, so the gradient is exact only in cells off every line source, port and mode monitor line and off the cells beyond their hi faces (they depend on the permittivity there too); sigma_e, poles and mu_r are not differentiated. An optimization study maximises J, summed over every physics, by varying the densities of the design_region features. Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength: series value (the quantity, W/m) and weighted (weight * value, W/m); extras frequency, wavelength, quantity and weight. Keep the line off a TFSF outline and a mode_source interface face, as for the monitors. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. In em_fdfd_nonlinear the output field eps_sensitivity is dJ/d eps of J summed over the objectives of every channel through the coupled channels (undepleted: one transposed solve per channel in reverse solve order; pump_depleted: the transposed fixed point (I - T) nu = T(c) by real GMRES to the physics tolerance, each product one transposed solve per channel, then one gradient sweep; the nonlinear sources back-propagated exactly, back-action and SPM / XPM included, the surface_chi2 / sheet_nonlinearity sites and the free carriers (newton) too; an isotropic change: the eps_r, eps_xx and eps_yy terms added); pump_depleted picard with a chi3 medium (lagged Kerr / carrier operator: use newton) and an em_fdfd_hz eps_xy are not differentiated (error when the field is read with a weighted objective; validation error in an optimization study); the chi2 / chi3 / sheet tensors, poling, the sheet sites and the chi3 n0^2 / Miller factors are held fixed (free carriers: where generation is > 0). The pump_depleted gradient is that of the converged fixed point: it is as accurate as the tolerance.

- FeatureSpec.type `adjoint_objective`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`
