- `channel` (str; default "") - Channel
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_nonlinear.point_source.channel`
- `quantity` (choice; default "flux"; choices flux | mode_power_positive | mode_power_negative) - Quantity
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.quantity`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when quantity in (mode_power_positive, mode_power_negative)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.mode_number`
- `weight` (float; unit 1; default 1) - Weight
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective.weight`

## Physics type `em_fdtd_3d` - Electromagnetic Waves, time domain (3D)

3D finite-difference time-domain solver (Yee): E_x, E_y, E_z on the +x / +y / +z faces of each cell in V/m, H_x, H_y, H_z on its (+y +z) / (+x +z) / (+x +y) edges in A/m, H half a time step earlier. Materials eps_r or the diagonal eps_xx / eps_yy / eps_zz, sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m plus Drude / Lorentz poles (on the bounding box of their material), stored as a uint16 material index with coefficient tables (at most 65534 distinct combinations; continuously varying values, e.g. thermo-optic, are re-quantised to fit). Boundaries per face: cpml (z faces too), pec, pmc, periodic (optional Bloch wave vector: a second, imaginary field set), symmetric / antisymmetric mirror. Sources: electric point dipole, TFSF plane wave, mode source (A5 cross-section modes); monitors: field probe, resonance finder, flux plane, flux box, DFT field-map layer, mode monitor, far-field pattern; outputs the raw components, e_abs, e_intensity, h_abs (cell centres), eps_r (the eps_zz array E_z sees) and absorbed_power, shown as z cut planes. Couplings: heat_em_thermo_optic (index slots of the allocated permittivity arrays) and em_heat_joule into 3D heat. Memory ~26 B per cell plus 12 B of material arrays (+8 B with eps_xx / eps_yy, +4 B with sigma_m, +8 B while tracking absorption); a stepper solver with precision half_storage stores the fields as fp16 (14 B per cell; time_dependent only, no dispersion poles, plane wave, mode ports or resonance finder; ~1e-3 relative noise floor, fields stored in units scaled from the dipole moments and read back in V/m, A/m). It advances one 3D Courant step per runner tick (every must be 1); the instance is usually named 'em'. Runs on the gpu and the cpu backend (cpu: numpy twins of every kernel, numba for the Yee updates, CPML and ohmic loss when installed, far slower: small models and tests; half_storage gpu only). In a frequency_domain study it runs one pulse and gives phasor fields per study wavelength (harmonic FDTD, see that study): every enabled source must share one gaussian or ricker waveform (same wavelength and bandwidth), the study wavelengths should lie inside its band, and no coupling may read this physics.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdtd_3d`; default instance name `em`
- Supported studies: time_dependent, frequency_domain
- Default study: {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 5e-14}}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): ez
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdtd_3d.<feature>`): dipole_source, field_probe, resonance_monitor, flux_plane, flux_box, dft_plane, pec_domain, plane_wave_source, mode_source, mode_monitor, far_field

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi`, `bc_z_lo`, `bc_z_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge / Lower z face / Upper z face
  Boundary of this face of the 3D box: cpml absorbs outgoing waves in pml_cells extra cells added outside the domain (the z faces too); pec = tangential E 0 at the centres of the outermost domain cell layer (that layer becomes perfect conductor); pmc = tangential H 0 on the outer face of the outermost cell (the grid edge: pec and pmc walls lie half a cell apart, so a cavity differs in width by one cell between them); periodic must be set on both faces of the axis (with the Bloch phase bloch_k<axis>, 0 = plain periodic). Mirror planes (any face, E parity as the 2D types): symmetric = E mirror-even (tangential H and normal E 0 on the plane, a PMC mirror), antisymmetric = E mirror-odd (tangential E odd: a PEC mirror), on the domain edge itself: one ghost cell is added outside it (its material copied from the edge cell; on a graded z axis its width follows the PML grading, so a z mirror wants uniform z cells near it), so draw the structure about the edge; heat in the model has its face on the same plane. Each mirror halves memory and time. Flux planes and boxes reaching a mirror face count their image (x 2 per face, result extra mirror_factor), mode ports solve the whole mirrored mode (powers of the full structure), the far field adds the images of its box currents (the unfolded pattern; mirrors on both faces of one axis are then an error); a dipole half a cell from the plane is mirrored with it.
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi, bc_z_lo, bc_z_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Bloch wave vector along x in rad/m (symmetry 2.8), used only when bc_x_lo and bc_x_hi are periodic: the fields repeat with the phase exp(-j kx L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t), so kx > 0 for a wave travelling toward +x); kx and kx + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. Any k != 0 steps a second (imaginary) field set: field and CPML memory, pole states and time per step double. Dipoles and mode sources drive the real set only (every period image repeats them with the Bloch phase: a dipole and a resonance monitor per swept k give the bands of a photonic-crystal slab or metasurface); the TFSF plane wave is refused (normal incidence only); mode ports solve their cross-section modes at the Bloch k of the port plane's periodic transverse axes (the Bloch mode; the mode source drives it into the real set like a dipole). DFT monitors (flux, field map, mode monitor, far field, harmonic FDTD) accumulate F_re + j F_im, the response at +k for every positive frequency; probes, field plots, expressions and couplings read the real set only. Absorbed power (track_absorption, q_accum, em_heat_joule) is refused. Typical: kx = k0 sin(theta) of the incidence angle in vacuum, or pi / L at the zone edge.
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Bloch wave vector along y in rad/m (symmetry 2.8), used only when bc_y_lo and bc_y_hi are periodic: the fields repeat with the phase exp(-j ky L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t), so ky > 0 for a wave travelling toward +y); ky and ky + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. Any k != 0 steps a second (imaginary) field set: field and CPML memory, pole states and time per step double. Dipoles and mode sources drive the real set only (every period image repeats them with the Bloch phase: a dipole and a resonance monitor per swept k give the bands of a photonic-crystal slab or metasurface); the TFSF plane wave is refused (normal incidence only); mode ports solve their cross-section modes at the Bloch k of the port plane's periodic transverse axes (the Bloch mode; the mode source drives it into the real set like a dipole). DFT monitors (flux, field map, mode monitor, far field, harmonic FDTD) accumulate F_re + j F_im, the response at +k for every positive frequency; probes, field plots, expressions and couplings read the real set only. Absorbed power (track_absorption, q_accum, em_heat_joule) is refused. Typical: ky = k0 sin(theta) of the incidence angle in vacuum, or pi / L at the zone edge.
- `bloch_kz` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_z_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector z
  Bloch wave vector along z in rad/m (symmetry 2.8), used only when bc_z_lo and bc_z_hi are periodic: the fields repeat with the phase exp(-j kz L) per period L (the meshed period; exp(+j omega t), so kz > 0 for a wave travelling toward +z); kz and kz + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. Any k != 0 steps a second (imaginary) field set: field and CPML memory, pole states and time per step double. Dipoles and mode sources drive the real set only (every period image repeats them with the Bloch phase: a dipole and a resonance monitor per swept k give the bands of a photonic-crystal slab or metasurface); the TFSF plane wave is refused (normal incidence only); mode ports solve their cross-section modes at the Bloch k of the port plane's periodic transverse axes (the Bloch mode; the mode source drives it into the real set like a dipole). DFT monitors (flux, field map, mode monitor, far field, harmonic FDTD) accumulate F_re + j F_im, the response at +k for every positive frequency; probes, field plots, expressions and couplings read the real set only. Absorbed power (track_absorption, q_accum, em_heat_joule) is refused. Typical: kz = k0 sin(theta) of the incidence angle in vacuum, or pi / L at the zone edge.
- `courant_factor` (float; unit 1; default 0.99; range (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  Time step as a fraction of the 3D CFL limit: dt = factor / (C0 sqrt(1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2 + 1/dz^2)) of the finest cells; 0.99 default. Dispersive poles need eps_r mu_r >= factor^2 + mu_r (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 per Drude pole (about delta_eps (omega_0 dt)^2 / 4 per Lorentz pole); the build checks every material (with the finest widths) and names the largest stable factor.
- `track_absorption` (bool; default false) - Track absorption
  Accumulate J.E losses (output absorbed_power in W/m^3, state q_accum in J/m^3: sigma_e on the faces split between the two cells by their half-cell conductance, Drude / Lorentz work time-centred on the pole faces and split to the dispersive cells) also without an em_heat_joule coupling; costs a pass over the box of the conducting cells and the pole boxes per step plus 8 B per cell (q_accum and the last window).

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.eps_r`
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.eps_zz`
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, x
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, y
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.sigma_e`
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1); each H edge takes the value of its lower cell (i, j, k).
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_3d.sigma_m`

### Fields

State fields:
- `ex` - E_x (+x face) (V/m)
- `ey` - E_y (+y face) (V/m)
- `ez` - E_z (+z face) (V/m)
- `hx` - H_x (+y +z edge) (A/m)
- `hy` - H_y (+x +z edge) (A/m)
- `hz` - H_z (+x +y edge) (A/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (eps_zz) (1)
- `q_accum` - Absorbed energy density (J/m^3)

Output fields (primary ez):
- `ex` - E_x (+x face) (V/m)
- `ey` - E_y (+y face) (V/m)
- `ez` - E_z (+z face) (V/m)
- `hx` - H_x (+y +z edge) (A/m)
- `hy` - H_y (+x +z edge) (A/m)
- `hz` - H_z (+x +y edge) (A/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity (eps_zz) (1)
- `absorbed_power` - Absorbed power density (W/m^3)
- `e_abs_harmonic` - |E| (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `e_intensity_harmonic` - |E|^2 (phasor) (V^2/m^2) [frequency_domain study only]
- `absorbed_power_harmonic` - Absorbed power density (time average) (W/m^3) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ex_re` - Re E_x (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ex_im` - Im E_x (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ex_abs` - |E_x| (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ex_phase` - arg E_x (phasor, centre) (rad) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ey_re` - Re E_y (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ey_im` - Im E_y (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ey_abs` - |E_y| (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ey_phase` - arg E_y (phasor, centre) (rad) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_re` - Re E_z (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_im` - Im E_z (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (phasor, centre) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_phase` - arg E_z (phasor, centre) (rad) [frequency_domain study only]

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source` - Dipole source

Electric point dipole (current element) along x, y or z on the E face nearest the point (point z param = height, mid-height when unset); calibrated to the live face coefficient, so the moment holds in any medium. A dipole in the outermost cell layer of a pec face parallel to it is refused (its tangential E is pinned there); normal to a pec face it may sit next to it (e.g. a monopole on a ground plane).

- FeatureSpec.type `dipole_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `dipole_axis` (choice; default "z"; choices x | y | z) - Dipole direction
  Direction of the current element: it drives the one E face of that direction nearest the point (the containing cell on the other two axes); radiates most broadside, nothing along its axis.
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `current_moment` (float; unit A m; default 1e-12) - Current moment
  Peak current moment I l in A m, injected as J = I l / V on the cell volume V of its E face (dual length along the dipole times the two cell widths across it), so the radiated field does not depend on the mesh: a cw dipole in vacuum radiates eta0 k^2 (I l)^2 / (12 pi) W (1e-12 A m at 1 um: ~4e-10 W). Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.field_probe` - Field probe

Time series of one raw field component in the cell containing the point (t in s, V/m or A/m), sampled after every step.

- FeatureSpec.type `field_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result kind `timeseries`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "ez"; choices ex | ey | ez | hx | hy | hz) - Field component
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.field_probe.component`

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor` - Resonance finder

Resonance finder (harmonic inversion, like Harminv / the matrix-pencil method): records one component in the cell containing each selected point (1 to 16 points) every step; when the result is read (CPU, about a second per point) the traces from the analysis start t_s on are mixed down to the band centre, low-pass filtered (Kaiser FIR, 100 dB), decimated to a sample rate of about 8 band half-widths (in Hz) and fitted by sums of damped sinusoids a exp(-gamma (t - t_s)) cos(omega (t - t_s) + phi). Several points share one joint fit (the same poles, each trace scaled to unit peak, amplitudes per point), so a mode on a nodal line of one point is still found through the others. Result 'table', one row per resonance inside the band, strongest (largest a) first, with the eigenfrequency resonance_table names: resonance_number (1, 2, ... in that order), wavelength [m, vacuum C0 / frequency], frequency = omega / (2 pi) [Hz], frequency_imag = gamma / (2 pi) [Hz] (Im of the complex frequency, exp(+j omega t): > 0 decays; the amplitude decay rate is gamma = 2 pi frequency_imag), q_factor = omega / (2 gamma) (inf when it does not decay), amplitude a [unit of the component] and phase phi [rad] at t_s at the point where the resonance is largest, error = |difference of the complex pole -gamma + j omega between two pencil sizes| / omega (a noise / resolution estimate). Poles with error above 0.01, resonances below 0.0001 of the strongest at every point and poles growing by more than 2x over the window are dropped. Extras: component, unit, dt [s], start_time t_s and end_time [s] of the analysed window, sample_interval [steps], n_samples (at most 2000: the earliest decimated samples), model_order, wavelength_min, wavelength_max, note ('' or why no resonance was found), points (the point names in selection order), point_amplitudes / point_phases (per row, one value per point). Q far above pi f T_window is resolved as long as the ring-down stays above the float32 noise (~1e-7 of the signal). A mode with zero amplitude at every point is missed: select points off the nodal lines (with one point) or points that no mode of interest has as common node; a cw source drives an undamped line at its own wavelength. A coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell. 3D: the raw Yee sample of the field_probe (point z param = height, mid-height when unset); H samples are dt/2 older, which the reference time accounts for.

- FeatureSpec.type `resonance_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count 1 to 16
- Stepper precisions single, double only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "ez"; choices ex | ey | ez | hx | hy | hz) - Field component
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.field_probe.component`
- `wavelength_min` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.wavelength_min`
- `wavelength_max` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the analysed band; must exceed wavelength_min.
- `start_time` (float; unit s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Analysis start
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.start_time`

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane` - Flux plane

Spectral power through a plane across the whole physical window at the cell edge nearest position, > 0 toward +normal. Result 'flux_spectrum': power a.u. (dt-weighted spectra, Re(E x H*) without the 1/2, E averaged across the plane and over two time steps as the 2D flux monitor), power_per_cw in W = power / (2 |S|^2) when every source shares one waveform (the cw time-averaged power at unit source amplitude). With a half_storage stepper the spectra carry the fp16 field noise (~1e-3 of the peak field, ~-60 dB in power): integrated powers keep ~1e-3, deep spectral nulls are not resolved.

- FeatureSpec.type `flux_plane`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `normal` (choice; default "z"; choices x | y | z) - Plane normal
  Axis normal to the plane; power > 0 flows toward +normal.
- `position` (float; unit m; default 0) - Plane position
  Coordinate [m] along the normal; the plane snaps to the nearest cell edge of the physical window and must have a cell on both sides (an edge on a non-PML outer face is refused). The plane spans the whole physical window across.
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.n_wavelengths`

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.flux_box` - Flux box

Net outward spectral power through the six faces of a box object, each face snapped to the nearest cell edge (trapezoid weights along the face edges, corners shared); every face needs a cell on both sides. Result 'flux_spectrum': power a.u. (dt-weighted spectra, Re(E x H*) without the 1/2, E averaged across the plane and over two time steps as the 2D flux monitor), power_per_cw in W = power / (2 |S|^2) when every source shares one waveform (the cw time-averaged power at unit source amplitude). With a half_storage stepper the spectra carry the fp16 field noise (~1e-3 of the peak field, ~-60 dB in power): integrated powers keep ~1e-3, deep spectral nulls are not resolved. Enclose a source to get its radiated power.

- FeatureSpec.type `flux_box`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds box; count exactly 1
- Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.n_wavelengths`

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.dft_plane` - Field map layer

Running DFT of E_x, E_y, E_z averaged to the cell centres of one window layer (cells containing z). Result 'dft_fields': x / y centres and the extra 'z' [m]; quantity 'abs(E_x)^2 + abs(E_y)^2 + abs(E_z)^2'; intensity (a.u.) with freq_index; intensity_per_cw_factor as the 2D DFT monitor.

- FeatureSpec.type `dft_plane`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result kind `dft_fields`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `position` (float; unit m; default 0) - Layer height
  Height z [m] of the recorded window layer (the cell containing it, an edge goes to the upper cell); the layer is always normal to z.
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. Each wavelength stores three complex64 window layers (24 B per window xy cell).

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor cells: every E face between two selected cells is pinned to 0 (the surface lies at the centres of the outermost conductor cells; the normal E on the surface stays free). Select objects: 'all' is refused. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra) every H face between four cell centres that the drawn surface cuts takes the free lengths of its four E edges (bisected along the links from the free centre) over its free area, floored so the unchanged time step stays stable; E faces between two conductor cells stay pinned, faces touching a pec wall layer, the window edge or another pec_domain without the option stay staircased, and sources, ports, poles and the stability check keep the cell mask.

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.plane_wave_source` - Plane wave

Total-field / scattered-field plane wave along one axis on a box object: total field inside the box (incident + scattered), only the scattered field outside, fed by a 1D incident line in the background medium (read from the cell before the upstream face), on uniform or graded meshes (the line runs on the grid's own cell widths along the propagation axis, so grading leaks nothing). Every box face needs one scattered-field cell inside the domain, except: on a periodic axis the box spans the whole period (its extent there is ignored), and with both transverse axes periodic a downstream face on the domain edge opens the box into the CPML (a one-sided plane-wave source: everything downstream is total field, upstream only what comes back), and a transverse face may reach a mirror face about which the incident wave is even (symmetric when the plane is normal to the third axis, antisymmetric when normal to the polarization; the other parity is an error): the box opens there and its image completes it. Keep the box faces in one uniform lossless medium (the build warns otherwise).

- FeatureSpec.type `plane_wave_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds box; count exactly 1
- Stepper precisions single only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `direction` (choice; default "+z"; choices +x | -x | +y | -y | +z | -z) - Direction
  Propagation direction of the plane wave along one axis (normal incidence on the box faces); it may not run along a periodic axis.
- `polarization` (choice; default "x"; choices x | y | z) - Electric field direction
  Axis of the incident E (linear polarisation), perpendicular to the propagation axis; H = k x E / (eta) lies along the third axis.
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak incident E [V/m] of the waveform envelope in the background medium (exact at the centre wavelength: the 1D incident line is calibrated there); the cw intensity is amplitude^2 / (2 eta), eta = eta0 sqrt(mu_r / eps_r) of the background.

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.mode_source` - Mode source

Guided mode of the cross-section (full-vector A5 solve with scipy at build, on the whole grid layer containing the position, PML included, at the FDTD numerical frequency) injected as a one-sided total-field / scattered-field plane: total field from that layer downstream. The mode is solved once before the first step; later material changes keep it. pec / pmc domain faces are approximate for modes that reach them. Result 'table' at the source wavelength: mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag, loss_db_per_cm, te_fraction, effective_area [m^2], pml_fraction, selected; extras wavelength, power, direction, mode_number.

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Stepper precisions single only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `normal` (choice; default "z"; choices x | y | z) - Propagation axis
  Normal of the port plane (the waveguide axis); the plane spans the whole grid cross-section (PML included) and must cut a straight guide.
- `position` (float; unit m; default 0) - Plane position
  Coordinate [m] of the plane along the normal: a source takes the cell containing it (its first total-field layer), a monitor the nearest cell edge.
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  1-based mode index in descending Re(beta^2) of the cross-section solve (1 = the fundamental, most strongly guided mode); a symmetric guide has near-degenerate pairs (square cores, fibres) that come back as arbitrary mixtures: make the cross-section asymmetric to select one. The source result table lists the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes.
- `direction` (choice; default "positive"; choices positive | negative) - Direction
  positive launches toward +normal (total field from the plane cell downstream), negative toward -normal; one-sided at the source wavelength.
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw) - Waveform
  gaussian (sin carrier under a gaussian envelope) or cw; the complex mode profile is driven by the carrier and its quadrature (cos) partner, so ricker is not offered.
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda0 = C0 / f0 of the carrier, the only wavelength at which the mode is solved (profile, n_eff): the launch is exact and one-sided there.
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.3; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Spectral width / f0 of the gaussian pulse; away from f0 the dispersing guide makes the launch leak backward and into radiation, and above 0.6 the build warns (quadrature partner, DC part).
- `power` (float; unit W; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Mode power
  Mode power [W] as a flux plane on the guide reads it at the source wavelength (the discrete Yee flux; cw: time-averaged after the ramp, gaussian: at the envelope peak).

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Mode decomposition on the cell-edge plane nearest the position across the physical window: running DFTs of the tangential E (averaged across the plane) and H, projected on the cross-section mode solved per wavelength at build. Result 'xy' versus wavelength: power_positive / power_negative (a.u., the flux-plane convention, so comparable with a flux plane), power_per_cw_* [W] when every source shares one waveform, fraction_* = mode power / source power with exactly one mode source (transmission downstream, reflection upstream; NaN where its spectrum is below 1e-6 of the peak); extras n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag, mode_number, normalized.

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Stepper precisions single only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `normal` (choice; default "z"; choices x | y | z) - Propagation axis
  Normal of the port plane (the waveguide axis); the plane spans the whole grid cross-section (PML included) and must cut a straight guide.
- `position` (float; unit m; default 0) - Plane position
  Coordinate [m] of the plane along the normal: a source takes the cell containing it (its first total-field layer), a monitor the nearest cell edge.
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  1-based mode index in descending Re(beta^2) of the cross-section solve (1 = the fundamental, most strongly guided mode); a symmetric guide has near-degenerate pairs (square cores, fibres) that come back as arbitrary mixtures: make the cross-section asymmetric to select one. It picks the mode at the middle wavelength; the others follow it by overlap (a build warning lists wavelengths where that overlap stays below 0.9).
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. Each wavelength costs one cross-section mode solve at build (host scipy) and four complex128 window planes; 3-11 typical, so the default is 5 (21 for the 2D mode_monitor).

### Feature `em_fdtd_3d.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Near-to-far-field transform of the tangential E and H on the six faces of a closed box object (each face snapped to the nearest cell edge; the box must enclose every source and scatterer, with vacuum outside). Result 'far_field' in one cut plane: angles [rad] from its first axis, power (n_f, n_angles) = radiated power per steradian of the dt-weighted spectra (a.u., no 1/2), power_per_cw [W/sr] when every source shares one waveform (its integral over the sphere is the flux box power_per_cw / cos(omega dt / 2): the flux spectra carry that re-timing factor, the far field does not; ~0.3 % at 25 cells per wavelength), quantity 'abs(E)^2', extras cut_plane, angle_axes. Mirror faces: the pattern of the unfolded structure (the images of the box currents are added and a box face on a mirror plane is dropped, so the box and its images must enclose the unfolded sources; at most one mirror per axis).

- FeatureSpec.type `far_field`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds box; count exactly 1
- Result kind `far_field`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. Each wavelength stores four complex128 spectra on the six box faces (64 B per face cell), so the default is 5 (21 for the 2D far_field).
- `cut_plane` (choice; default "xz"; choices xz | yz | xy) - Cut plane
  Plane of the observation directions: angles run counter-clockwise from its first axis (+x for xz and xy, +y for yz) toward its second (+z, +z, +y).
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; range [1, inf)) - Number of angles
  Directions evenly spaced over 360 degrees in the cut plane.

## Physics type `em_fdtd_bor` - Electromagnetic Waves, time domain (axisymmetric, azimuthal order m)

Body-of-revolution (BOR) finite-difference time-domain solver: the drawing is the (r, z) half plane of a rotationally symmetric structure about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z), the fields of one azimuthal order m stepped in time on the em_fdfd_bor finite-integration operator (same Yee layout, ring metric and axis rules: m = 0 H_z on the axis, |m| = 1 E_r and H_phi there recovered from cell 0, larger |m| none). The fields are the real time-domain amplitudes of one azimuthal order m: the standing wave whose E_r, E_z, H_phi vary as cos(m phi) and E_phi, H_r, H_z as sin(m phi) (m = 0: the TM fields E_r, E_z, H_phi and the TE fields E_phi, H_r, H_z themselves). Its DFT phasors divided by the source spectrum are the em_fdfd_bor phasors of the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave (E_phi, H_r, H_z times j), up to the leap-frog dispersion: they solve the em_fdfd_bor system at omega_tilde = (2 / dt) sin(omega dt / 2) exactly, so an em_fdfd_bor resonance omega rings at (2 / dt) asin(omega dt / 2). Leap-frog with the exact time-step limit of the order (courant_factor), CPML faces (cylindrical on r_hi: the em_fdfd_bor radius stretch), pec / pmc walls on the grid edge; real eps components (diagonal in cylindrical components, the em_fdfd_bor vocabulary: eps_xx = eps_rr, eps_r = eps_phiphi, eps_yy = axial eps_zz), mu_r, sigma_e, sigma_m and Drude / Lorentz dispersion poles (stepped in velocity form on all three components; DFT phasors then solve em_fdfd_bor at omega_tilde with the pole evaluated at omega_tilde and damping gamma cos(omega dt / 2)). With an azimuthal_orders list the driven order sum of off-axis point sources (true 3D point currents, the orders stepped in lockstep and summed; see that setting). Features: point_source (current elements with the FDTD waveforms), field_probe (time traces), resonance_monitor (harmonic inversion of a probe: resonances and Q of a ring-down), flux_monitor (spectral power through a disc, annulus or cylinder), far_field (W/sr in the meridional plane), mode_source / mode_monitor (vector guided modes of a guide along the axis on a horizontal line, one-sided TFSF launch and reciprocity decomposition; single order only), pec_domain. Outputs at the cell centres: er, ephi, ez, hr, hphi, hz (instantaneous, H half a step earlier), e_abs, e_intensity (primary), h_abs and the permittivity arrays; derived values weight by the ring volume 2 pi r dr dz. Runs on the GPU or the CPU backend (operators built on the host, sparse products per step). Cannot share a model with another EM type. heat_em_thermo_optic writes the three permittivity arrays (slots eps_r_update, eps_xx_update, eps_yy_update). In a frequency_domain study it runs one pulse and gives phasor fields per study wavelength (harmonic FDTD, see that study): every enabled source must share one gaussian or ricker waveform (same wavelength and bandwidth), the study wavelengths should lie inside its band, and no coupling may read this physics. Its phasor fields are <component>_re / <component>_abs and e_abs_harmonic (em_fdfd_bor convention). The instance is usually named 'em'.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdtd_bor`; default instance name `em`
- Supported studies: time_dependent, frequency_domain
- Default study: {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 2e-13}}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): e_intensity
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdtd_bor.<feature>`): point_source, field_probe, resonance_monitor, pec_domain, flux_monitor, far_field, mode_source, mode_monitor

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "axisymmetric"; choices axisymmetric) - Geometry
  Always axisymmetric: the drawing is the (r, z) half plane of a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z). The setting exists so that coupled physics with a geometry setting (heat, electric_currents, electrostatics) recognise a consistent axisymmetric partner.
- `bc_x_lo` (choice; default "axis"; choices axis) - Left edge
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_bor.bc_x_lo`
- `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc) - Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_bor.bc_x_lo`
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; range [0, 10000]) - Azimuthal order
  Azimuthal order m >= 0 of the fields (one (r, z) run per order; +m and -m are degenerate). m = 0: on-axis dipoles and the radial modes of disks and pillars (TE and TM decouple); m = 1: the fields of an on-axis focused or plane wave; larger m: whispering-gallery modes, m ~ 2 pi R n_eff / lambda. The time step shrinks with |m|: the m / r terms near the axis set dt ~ dr / (C0 (|m| + 1)), so large m costs steps (em_fdfd_bor eigenfrequency is cheaper for whispering-gallery resonances). For an off-axis point source (the sum over m of its Fourier terms) list the orders in azimuthal_orders instead.
- `azimuthal_orders` (float_list; unit 1; range [0, 10000]; optional (null allowed)) - Azimuthal order list
  Distinct integer orders m >= 0 of a driven order sum; a non-empty list replaces azimuthal_order (the em_fdfd_bor order sum in the time domain). Every point_source is then a 3D point current element at phi = 0 (see point_source) expanded into its Fourier terms exp(-j m phi); each listed m > 0 stands for +m and -m (their sum is a cos(m phi) standing wave), stepped by one (r, z) stepper per order and source kind (one for r / z currents, one for phi currents, a quarter period apart; m = 0 one for both), all in lockstep at courant_factor x the limit of the largest order and summed. Shown fields, field_probe and resonance_monitor traces and the frequency_domain phasors are the phi = 0 half plane of the summed 3D field (the source side; physical phasors, without the j of single-order runs on E_phi, H_r, H_z; ring-weighted field integrals of them are no 3D integrals); flux_monitor and far_field add the orders exactly and report each order too. List every order 0, 1, ..., M: powers and far field converge once M exceeds k rho_s by a few (rho_s = source radius, k = n omega / c). Cost: up to 2 M + 1 steppers, each at the time step of order M. Sources must exist at the build (no scripted sources added later of a new kind); mode_source / mode_monitor need a single order. null or [] = azimuthal_order alone.
- `courant_factor` (float; unit 1; default 0.99; range (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  Time step as a fraction of the exact leap-frog limit 2 / omega_max of this grid and azimuthal order (omega_max of the vacuum operator, computed at the build by a host eigen-solve), not of the 2D CFL rule; cells with eps >= 1 and mu_r >= 1 are then stable (the build refuses a field point below 1). Dispersive poles need eps_inf - P >= courant_factor^2 at every field point, P = (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 per Drude pole and delta_eps (omega_0 dt)^2 / (4 - (omega_0 dt)^2) per Lorentz pole (the build checks it and stops otherwise: refine the mesh or lower this factor). 0.99 default.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic relative permittivity (>= 1) of all three components (eps_rr, eps_phiphi, eps_zz); n^2 of a lossless dielectric (silicon ~12.1, silica ~2.1 at 1.55 um); may depend on r (x), z (y) and physics fields (rewritten coefficients at each change); a component property wins over it. Diagonal anisotropy in cylindrical components is rotationally invariant: the drawing-plane names map as eps_xx = eps_rr (E_r, radial), eps_yy = eps_zz of the rotation axis (E_z, axial; the drawing y is z) and eps_zz = eps_phiphi (E_phi, out of the drawing plane; it writes the eps_r array). A crystal with its optic axis along the rotation axis (z-cut, uniaxial) sets eps_r = n_o^2 and eps_yy = n_e^2; a radially anisotropic shell sets eps_xx. E_phi sees the cell value, E_r and E_z (on the cell edges) the ring-volume / length weighted mean of their non-PEC cells (no subpixel smoothing). Real values only; a value below 1 at a field point stops the build (the time step assumes eps >= 1). Dispersive materials (Drude / Lorentz poles of the material dispersion list) are stepped in time on all three components (velocity form as the 2D FDTD; an E_r / E_z point sees the pole times the share of its cells that carry it), this value or the first Drude eps_inf being the background; see courant_factor for the pole time-step bound.
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, phi (azimuthal)
  eps_phiphi: the azimuthal component, the only one E_phi sees (stored in the eps_r array: it overrides eps_r for E_phi only). Not the axial component: that is eps_yy. Diagonal anisotropy in cylindrical components is rotationally invariant: the drawing-plane names map as eps_xx = eps_rr (E_r, radial), eps_yy = eps_zz of the rotation axis (E_z, axial; the drawing y is z) and eps_zz = eps_phiphi (E_phi, out of the drawing plane; it writes the eps_r array). A crystal with its optic axis along the rotation axis (z-cut, uniaxial) sets eps_r = n_o^2 and eps_yy = n_e^2; a radially anisotropic shell sets eps_xx.
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, r (radial)
  eps_rr: the radial component, the only one E_r sees. Diagonal anisotropy in cylindrical components is rotationally invariant: the drawing-plane names map as eps_xx = eps_rr (E_r, radial), eps_yy = eps_zz of the rotation axis (E_z, axial; the drawing y is z) and eps_zz = eps_phiphi (E_phi, out of the drawing plane; it writes the eps_r array). A crystal with its optic axis along the rotation axis (z-cut, uniaxial) sets eps_r = n_o^2 and eps_yy = n_e^2; a radially anisotropic shell sets eps_xx.
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, z (axial, drawing y)
  Axial eps_zz (along the rotation axis = the drawing y): the only component E_z sees. Diagonal anisotropy in cylindrical components is rotationally invariant: the drawing-plane names map as eps_xx = eps_rr (E_r, radial), eps_yy = eps_zz of the rotation axis (E_z, axial; the drawing y is z) and eps_zz = eps_phiphi (E_phi, out of the drawing plane; it writes the eps_r array). A crystal with its optic axis along the rotation axis (z-cut, uniaxial) sets eps_r = n_o^2 and eps_yy = n_e^2; a radially anisotropic shell sets eps_xx.
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss J = sigma_e E in S/m, default 0, on every component (semi-implicit update; E_r / E_z take the mean of their cells as eps); a weak absorber of index n and extinction kappa has sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0.
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1), 1 for optical materials; H_r, H_phi and H_z take the mean of the cells around their points.
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss in Ohm/m on H (semi-implicit), default 0 (artificial absorbers only).

- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)

- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity rr (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity zz (axial) (1)

Output fields (primary e_intensity):
- `er` - E_r (cos m phi wave) (V/m)
- `ephi` - E_phi (sin m phi wave) (V/m)

- `hphi` - H_phi (cos m phi wave) (A/m)
- `hz` - H_z (sin m phi wave) (A/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity phi phi (1)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity rr (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity zz (axial) (1)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)

- `er_abs` - |E_r| (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ephi_re` - Re E_phi (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ephi_abs` - |E_phi| (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_re` - Re E_z (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `hr_re` - Re H_r (phasor) (A/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `hr_abs` - |H_r| (phasor) (A/m) [frequency_domain study only]

- `hphi_abs` - |H_phi| (phasor) (A/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `hz_re` - Re H_z (phasor) (A/m) [frequency_domain study only]

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.point_source` - Point source

Current element in the cell containing the point (x = r, y = z), a ring in 3D with the azimuthal dependence of the order, driven by the waveform; see component. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `component` (choice; default "z"; choices r | phi | z) - Direction
  Current direction, normalised as the em_fdfd_bor point source: 'phi' J_phi = I / (w h) in the cell (m = 0: a current loop of radius r carrying I); 'z' / 'r': the current I through the ring cross-section of the cell, split onto its two edge points (in the axis cell 'z' is an on-axis electric dipole of moment I h). For m != 0, I is the amplitude of the cos(m phi) (z, r) / sin(m phi) (phi) current of the standing wave; compared with em_fdfd_bor phasors a 'phi' current is that of phase +90 deg (the same power). In a driven order sum (azimuthal_orders) the element is instead a 3D point current at phi = 0 (in the drawing plane; 'phi' points out of it) of dipole moment I d, d = the cell height for z, its width for r and phi, as the em_fdfd_bor order sum (in free space it radiates eta0 k^2 (I d)^2 / (12 pi) wherever it sits).
- `current` (float; unit A; default 0.001) - Current
  Peak current I [A] of the element times the waveform; fields scale linearly with it. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.field_probe` - Field probe

Time series of one field component on its Yee point of the cell containing the point, sampled after every time step (t in s, values in V/m or A/m); a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `field_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result kind `timeseries`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "ez"; choices er | ephi | ez | hr | hphi | hz) - Field component
  Component recorded every step on its Yee point of the cell containing the point: E_phi at the centre, E_r / H_z on the +r edge, E_z / H_r on the +z edge, H_phi on the +r +z corner (raw samples, not averaged); H half a time step before the recorded time.

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.resonance_monitor` - Resonance finder

Help: shared `em_fdtd_bor.resonance_monitor`

- FeatureSpec.type `resonance_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count 1 to 16
- Stepper precisions single, double only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "ez"; choices er | ephi | ez | hr | hphi | hz) - Field component
  Recorded field: Component recorded every step on its Yee point of the cell containing the point: E_phi at the centre, E_r / H_z on the +r edge, E_z / H_r on the +z edge, H_phi on the +r +z corner (raw samples, not averaged); H half a time step before the recorded time.
- `wavelength_min` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.wavelength_min`
- `wavelength_max` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the analysed band; must exceed wavelength_min.
- `start_time` (float; unit s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Analysis start
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor.start_time`

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor (rings in 3D): E_phi = 0 at the centre of every cell whose centre lies in the selected domains and E_r / E_z = 0 on the edges between two such cells, staircased to the mesh (the points leave the operator: fixed at the build).

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Spectral power through an axis-aligned line, with the pairing of the em_fdfd_bor flux_monitor (E of the line cells, H on their hi face; exactly conserved through lossless cells): a horizontal line (z = const) gives the flux along +z through the annulus it sweeps, a vertical one (r = const) the flux along +r through the cylinder, with the 2 pi ring weights of the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave. Result 'flux_spectrum' in monitor order: power = pi sum Re(E H*) of the dt-weighted DFT spectra (unit 'a.u.'); power_per_cw = power / |S(omega)|^2 is the power [W] of the cw source of the same current (em_fdfd_bor at omega_tilde). The per_cw values exist only when every source feature of the physics shares one waveform (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives are not counted); S(omega) = the dt-weighted spectrum of that waveform over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength (cw: also outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)). They equal the em_fdfd_* values at the same source amplitudes, exactly only at the source wavelength (sources are calibrated there). In a driven order sum (azimuthal_orders) both are the totals of the 3D field (the orders are orthogonal in phi, so their powers add exactly), extras power_orders / power_orders_per_cw (n_wavelengths x n_orders: each listed m with its -m) and azimuthal_orders. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell; its hi face must be inside the grid.

- FeatureSpec.type `flux_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.n_wavelengths`

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Near-to-far-field transform of the DFT phasors on the closed surface of a rectangle in the (r, z) drawing, as the em_fdfd_bor far_field (its z faces and outer cylinder, an inner cylinder when x0 > 0, a box bottom at y0 = 0 on a pec / pmc z_lo mirror closed by the images; vacuum outside the box). Result 'far_field' in monitor order: power per steradian r^2 |E|^2 / (2 eta0) [W/sr] of the cw source of the same current when every source shares one waveform (NaN outside its spectrum), else of the raw dt-weighted spectra ('a.u.'), versus angle in the meridional plane counter-clockwise from +r; extras power_theta / power_phi, angle_axes, azimuthal_order. In a driven order sum (azimuthal_orders) power is the pattern of the summed 3D field in the meridional plane through the sources (angles with cos >= 0 at phi = 0, the others at phi = pi), the order amplitudes added with exp(-j m phi); extras power_azimuthal_mean (its phi average), power_orders (n_wavelengths x n_orders x n_angles: the phi average per listed m with its -m) and azimuthal_orders instead of azimuthal_order. Needs one cell beyond x1 / y1 and below y0 inside the domain; the box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `far_field`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result kind `far_field`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 21; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. Each wavelength accumulates complex128 spectra of the E / H rows and columns around the box faces (little memory); 1-41 typical.
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; range [1, inf)) - Number of angles
  Far-field angles evenly spaced over 360 degrees, counter-clockwise from +x (0 = +x, pi/2 = +y); 360 gives 1-degree steps.

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.mode_source` - Mode source

Port source launching one guided mode of a waveguide along the axis (fibre, pillar, metal pipe, coaxial guide) from a horizontal line in one direction: a one-sided total-field / scattered-field interface between the line row and the row upstream in time, the mode at the carrier frequency on the two rows (Re and Im of its profile driven by the waveform and its quadrature; as industry-standard transient ports, the mode of one frequency). At the carrier the launch is exact and one-sided; at other frequencies of a pulse the carrier profile launches a somewhat different power and leaks a little backward (both grow with the change of n_eff over the band, strongest near a cutoff), so for spectra divide by the forward power of a mode_monitor between the source and the device. The port line must be horizontal (z = const), from the axis (x0 = 0) or annular (x0 > 0: a metal end on that cell edge), ending on the last window cell (then continuing through the r_hi cpml, or ending on its pec / pmc wall) or inside the domain (a metal end), as the em_fdfd_bor ports; the line row and its neighbour rows must lie outside the z cpml layers. Its guided modes ~ exp(-j beta z) are full-vector solutions of the stepped body-of-revolution operator on a straight guide at omega_tilde = (2 / dt) sin(omega dt / 2) (the leap-frog frequency of omega, with the stepped poles and conductivities), solved once on the materials at the build (later material changes are not followed); exact for a guide invariant along z with uniform rows for a cell on each side of the line. Modes are ranked by descending Re n_eff (mode 1 = the highest) and carry 1 W in the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave. Not in a driven order sum (azimuthal_orders). Result 'table' of the carrier solve, one row per mode found (up to max(mode_number + 2, 4)): mode_number, n_eff, n_eff_imag, loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field, selected; extras wavelength (the carrier, m), power (W), direction, mode_number and phase (deg).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw) - Waveform
  gaussian: sin carrier of f0 = C0 / wavelength under exp(-((t - t0) / tau)^2), tau = 1 / (pi * bandwidth * f0), centred at t0 = 4.5 tau, so it lasts about 9 / (pi * bandwidth * f0) (550 nm, bandwidth 0.5: ~10 fs). The amplitude / current is the envelope peak: the carrier is 0 at t0, so the source peaks lower (~0.87 at bandwidth 0.5, ~0.66 at 1). cw: sin(2 pi f0 t) ramped in by 1 - exp(-t / (3 T)), T = 1 / f0, steady after ~15 periods. ricker: Ricker wavelet whose spectrum peaks at f0, delayed by 4 / f0 (broadband, up to ~2.5 f0: 3 % of the spectral peak there, 1 % at 2.76 f0). A mode_source takes gaussian or cw only: the launch drives the imaginary part of the mode profile with the quadrature (cos) partner of the waveform (keep a gaussian bandwidth <= 0.6).
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `power` (float; unit W; default 1; range [0, inf)) - Power
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.power`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, 50]) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (choice; default "positive"; choices positive | negative) - Direction
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_bor.mode_source.direction`
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phase of the launched mode amplitude sqrt(P) e^{j phase} on the line row (each mode is phased with its largest field sample real and positive).

### Feature `em_fdtd_bor.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on a horizontal line into the upward (positive) and downward (negative) amplitudes of one guided mode at each monitor wavelength, from DFT spectra of the line row and the row above (the discrete reciprocity form, so other modes drop out). The modes are solved per wavelength (mode_number at the centre one, followed outward by overlap). The port line must be horizontal (z = const), from the axis (x0 = 0) or annular (x0 > 0: a metal end on that cell edge), ending on the last window cell (then continuing through the r_hi cpml, or ending on its pec / pmc wall) or inside the domain (a metal end), as the em_fdfd_bor ports; the line row and its neighbour rows must lie outside the z cpml layers. Its guided modes ~ exp(-j beta z) are full-vector solutions of the stepped body-of-revolution operator on a straight guide at omega_tilde = (2 / dt) sin(omega dt / 2) (the leap-frog frequency of omega, with the stepped poles and conductivities), solved once on the materials at the build (later material changes are not followed); exact for a guide invariant along z with uniform rows for a cell on each side of the line. Modes are ranked by descending Re n_eff (mode 1 = the highest) and carry 1 W in the travelling exp(-j m phi) wave. Not in a driven order sum (azimuthal_orders). Result 'xy' versus vacuum wavelength: power_positive / power_negative = |a|^2 of the dt-weighted DFT spectra (a.u.); with one shared source waveform power_per_cw_* = |a / S(omega)|^2 [W] (the power of the cw source), and with exactly one enabled mode_source fraction_positive / fraction_negative = |a / (S sqrt(P) e^{j phase})|^2 (transmission / reflection into this mode) and phase_positive / phase_negative (rad, not de-embedded). The per_cw values exist only when every source feature of the physics shares one waveform (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives are not counted); S(omega) = the dt-weighted spectrum of that waveform over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength (cw: also outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)). They equal the em_fdfd_* values at the same source amplitudes, exactly only at the source wavelength (sources are calibrated there). Extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag, mode_number, normalized. Keep the line and the row above off the rows of a mode_source.

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.n_wavelengths`
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, 50]) - Mode number
  Guided mode measured (ranking as mode_source); later wavelengths follow it by overlap.

## Physics type `em_fdtd_ez` - Electromagnetic Waves, time domain (2D, electric field out of plane)

2D finite-difference time-domain solver for the E_z polarisation: E_z out of plane in V/m, H_x and H_y in plane in A/m, x to the right and y up. On the Yee grid E_z sits at cell centres and H_x / H_y on the +y / +x cell faces, half a time step earlier. gaussian and cw sources use a sin carrier (ricker is a real wavelet), DFT-based monitors accumulate exp(-i omega t) at the actual sample times, and every wavelength is a vacuum wavelength. Boundaries: CPML (cells added outside the domain), PEC, PMC, periodic and mirror planes on the domain edge; materials: eps_r (eps_zz wins for E_z), sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m plus Drude / Lorentz poles; current-calibrated sources and mode (port) sources; probe, flux, mode, DFT and far-field monitors. Outputs e_abs, e_intensity and h_abs (|E|, |E|^2, |H| at the cell centres; instantaneous values, the FDFD types give phasor moduli under the same names). It advances one Courant step per runner tick, so every must be 1; the instance is usually named 'em'. In a frequency_domain study it runs one pulse and gives phasor fields per study wavelength (harmonic FDTD, see that study): every enabled source must share one gaussian or ricker waveform (same wavelength and bandwidth), the study wavelengths should lie inside its band, and no coupling may read this physics. Stepper solver (role stepper, explicit_kernels): precision single (float32 fields, default) or double (float64 fields, coefficients, CPML and pole arrays: ~2x the field memory and time, for long or high-Q ring-downs where float32 coefficient rounding, ~1e-7 of a mode frequency, accumulates into phase drift); materials, absorbed power, probe traces and field-map spectra stay float32, and nonlinear_medium / gain_medium need single.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdtd_ez`; default instance name `em`
- Supported studies: time_dependent, frequency_domain
- Default study: {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 2e-13}}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): ez
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdtd_ez.<feature>`): point_source, line_source, gaussian_beam, plane_wave_tfsf, mode_source, pec_domain, effective_index, nonlinear_medium, gain_medium, phase_change_medium, field_probe, resonance_monitor, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, dft_monitor, far_field

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  cpml absorbs outgoing waves in pml_cells extra cells added outside the domain. pec (E_z = 0 at the centre of the outermost domain cell) and pmc (tangential H = 0 on the inner face of that cell) are perfect electric / magnetic walls up to one cell inside the domain edge. periodic must be set on both faces of the axis and wraps the field with the meshed window as period (uniform mesh: the size rounded up to whole cells) and no phase step (k = 0 along that axis, e.g. normal incidence); the em_fdtd_*, em_fdfd_* and em_modes types add a Bloch phase with bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear per input harmonic_channel; em_eme / em_eme_3d: k = 0 only). Mirror planes, on any face: symmetric = E mirror-even (a PMC mirror plane), antisymmetric = E mirror-odd (a PEC mirror plane), on the domain edge itself: one ghost cell is added outside it (the width of the edge cell, its material copied from it) to hold the mirror image, so draw the structure about the edge (x = 0 for x_lo); heat, potential and the other physics of the model have their faces on the same plane. The same plane and parity hold for the ez and hz types, so one setting imposes the same symmetry on both. A source half a cell from the plane (in the outermost domain cell) is mirrored with it. Results count the unfolded structure: a flux line reaching a mirror face and a derived integral whose selection reaches one are doubled per such face (result extra mirror_factor; integrands assumed mirror-even, e.g. powers and losses), far fields add the image contour (a box touching the plane drops its face there; at most one mirror per axis), Results.field(unfold=True) and the GUI show the mirrored field; mode-port powers, source powers and the probes stay those of the drawn part. pec and pmc walls of the two polarisations are half a cell apart (E_z pec and H_z pmc at the centre of the outermost domain cell, E_z pmc and H_z pec on its inner face), so a cavity simulated in both polarisations differs in width by one cell. For E_z: symmetric = E_z even about the plane (E_z of the ghost cell copied from its neighbour, as pmc: a PMC plane), antisymmetric = E_z odd (copied negated, so E = 0 on the plane: a PEC plane). These walls are re-applied after the sources are injected, so a source value in the outermost cell of a pec or pmc face is overwritten every step and radiates nothing, while a source next to a mirror plane sees its exact image.
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `courant_factor` (float; unit 1; default 0.99; range (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  Time step as a fraction of the 2D CFL limit: dt = factor / (C0 sqrt(1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2)) on a uniform mesh (factor * dx / (C0 sqrt(2)) for square cells; on a graded mesh the limit of the finest cells); 0.99 default. Stable only where eps_r * mu_r >= (C0 dt)^2 (1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2) (= factor^2 on a uniform mesh; coarser cells of a graded mesh have margin) + mu_r P, P = (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 per Drude pole and delta_eps (omega_0 dt)^2 / (4 - (omega_0 dt)^2) per Lorentz pole: plain eps_r and mu_r values must be >= 1, but an eps_inf ~1 metal needs a lower factor at coarse cells. The build checks every cell (field-dependent values, Drude eps_inf < 1, poles), names the worst one and the largest stable factor, but runtime eps_r rewrites (thermo-optic) are not checked.
- `track_absorption` (bool; default false) - Track absorption
  Accumulate J.E losses (output absorbed_power in W/m^3, state q_accum in J/m^3) also without an em_heat_joule coupling; costs about one extra GPU pass per step over the bounding boxes of the conducting and dispersive cells. The state q_accum exists only while accumulation runs (jz_total only with a Drude pole). It is switched on automatically when a material expression, a derived value, a field_transfer, em_heat_joule or em_semiconductor_generation reads q_accum, or a derived value reads absorbed_power (else absorbed_power is 0 everywhere). absorbed_power shows the current accumulation window, else the last completed one; em_heat_joule resets q_accum at each transfer, otherwise the window spans the whole run.
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_ky`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity
  Real relative permittivity (>= 1), n^2 of a lossless dielectric: glass ~2.1-2.25, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um; may depend on x, y and physics fields. E_z sees eps_zz instead when the material sets it. For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf: an explicit eps_r (or eps_zz) wins over the Drude eps_inf, which applies only when neither is set. A state-dependent eps_r (e.g. of T) is rewritten once per step of the physics it reads, not every EM step.
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (out of plane)
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.eps_zz`
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss J = sigma_e E_z in S/m, default 0. A weak absorber with index n and extinction coefficient kappa at angular frequency omega has sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0; model metals with a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1); 1 for practically every optical material. It enters the Courant check (eps_r * mu_r) and the local impedance of line sources.
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss on H_x, H_y in Ohm/m, default 0; sigma_m / (mu0 mu_r) = sigma_e / (eps0 eps_r) gives an impedance-matched absorber without reflection at normal incidence.

Output fields (primary ez):

- `hx` - H_x (+y face) (A/m)
- `hy` - H_y (+x face) (A/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)

- `ez_im` - Im E_z (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_abs` - |E_z| (phasor) (V/m) [frequency_domain study only]
- `ez_phase` - arg E_z (phasor) (rad) [frequency_domain study only]
