### Source slots

- `ez_source` (V/m per EM step): Added to E_z once per EM step (after the sources) until the next transfer: a raw field increment, not a calibrated source. A constant buffer b acts like a current density of about -eps0 eps_r b / dt, so its effect scales with 1/dt (mesh, courant_factor); not counted in the DFT decimation bound.
- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.point_source` - Point source

z-directed filament current I in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell). It radiates a cylindrical wave whose field does not depend on the mesh: |E_z| = omega mu0 I / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| in a homogeneous non-magnetic medium.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `current` (float; unit A; default 0.001) - Electric line current
  Peak z-directed filament current I. The radiated field does not depend on the mesh: for cw in a homogeneous non-magnetic medium of wavenumber k, |E_z| = omega mu0 I / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| (1 mA at wavelength 1 um: ~2e5 V/m at r = 1 um). Fields are linear, so results scale with I. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.line_source` - Line source

Sheet current on an axis-aligned line radiating amplitude V/m of E_z to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) sends waves along +x and -x, a horizontal one along +y and -y. For a plane wave, span the whole domain: an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML (on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `line_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  E_z radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a cw plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); the calibration uses |eta| of the line cells at the centre frequency (sigma_e and dispersion included), so other frequencies of a pulse in a dispersive medium deviate. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so on a line crossing several media (e.g. a high-index core and its cladding) the current steps at the interfaces, the steps diffract and the field there is not the amplitude (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Each recalibration (e.g. a thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n of the line cells (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2). Typical 1 V/m.

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.plane_wave_tfsf` - Plane wave box (+x)

Plane wave travelling along +x only, injected on the outline of a total-field box: total field inside the box, only the scattered field outside; amplitude = incident E_z. Uniform or graded meshes (the 1D incident line runs on the grid's own x widths, so graded x and y cells leak nothing); the incident field is computed for vacuum, so the box edges must lie in vacuum (warning otherwise), and the box needs one scattered-field cell inside the domain on every side, except at a y mirror face of the wave's parity (ez: symmetric, hz: antisymmetric), where it may reach the plane: the box opens there and its mirror image completes it (the other parity, or an x mirror face, is an error). Keep flux and mode monitors entirely inside the box (their hi face too) or outside it (validation warns). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `plane_wave_tfsf`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak incident E_z of the +x plane wave (computed for vacuum); the scattered field outside the box is relative to it. Typical 1 V/m.

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source` - Mode source

Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction: a vertical line (x = const) launches toward +x (direction positive) or -x (negative), a horizontal one toward +y or -y. The mode drives E_z in the line cells and H_y (vertical line) / H_x (horizontal line) on their upstream face, i.e. the lo face of the line cells for positive and their hi face for negative. The mode is injected as a one-sided total-field / scattered-field line (discrete equivalent currents): total field from the line cells downstream, while upstream only what comes back (reflections) remains. The launch is exact and one-sided at the source wavelength; toward the band edges of a gaussian pulse some power leaks upstream or into radiation because the profile and impedance of the mode change with wavelength, so keep the bandwidth modest in dispersive guides. Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. Its interface face holds scattered field, so a flux or mode monitor on the line of a negative source (total-field line cells, interface on their hi face) mixes both (validation warns). The 1D eigenmodes along the line are FDTD-consistent (kernel cell widths, numerical frequency and dispersion of the Yee scheme, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at that frequency with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are solved at build (finalize) on the final materials; during the run they are re-solved, following the selected mode by overlap, whenever the line materials drifted by more than 1e-3 relative since the last solve (thermo-optic or Pockels coupling, state-dependent permittivity; one host transfer of the line per material update). A mode monitor then decomposes its whole-run spectra with the latest modes (the run log notes it), which fits only light that passed after the medium settled. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side and a locally uniform mesh (validation refuses a line whose face falls on the outer grid wall and warns when a wall boundary pins the line cell or its face every step, when its face lies inside a CPML layer (line in the outermost window cell) or when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec domain edge takes E_z = 0, one on a pmc or symmetric edge dE_z/dn = 0 and one on an antisymmetric edge E_z odd about the plane, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E_z = 0 in the next cell), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'table' at the source wavelength, one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss in the exp(+j omega t) convention), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the two ends of the solved line / its peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode) and selected (True for the launched mode); extras wavelength, power, direction, mode_number and tracked_mode_number (the rank of the launched mode in the latest solve: mode_number until a re-solve during the run finds it at another rank; the selected row follows it).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (choice; default "positive"; choices positive | negative) - Direction
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.direction`
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.3; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.bandwidth`
- `power` (float; unit W/m; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Mode power
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.power`

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor: E_z = 0 (and no dispersive current) in every cell whose centre lies in the selected domains, staircased to the mesh; with solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries the H links from free cells into it put E_z = 0 at the drawn wall instead (exact wall distance, floored per cell so the time step stays stable).

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium` - Nonlinear medium

chi2 (d_eff, poling), Kerr, two-photon absorption (TPA) and TPA free carriers on the selected cells (later features win on overlaps), on top of the linear material (eps, sigma_e, poles). Each step corrects E_z at the cell centres, n0^2 = eps_r of the cell after the linear update by solving D = eps0 (eps + chi2 E + chi3 E^2 + delta eps(N)) E with the TPA + FCA conductivity implicitly (one fused kernel on the bounding box of the selection; n0 is read live, so thermo-optic eps changes carry over). The carrier density N follows dN/dt = TPA power / (2 hbar omega) - N / tau (output field carrier_density, 1/m^3) and adds the absorption sigma_fca N and the index change -k N. TPA and FCA power count as absorbed power. Nonlinear media break superposition: time_dependent study only (the frequency_domain harmonic FDTD and the FDFD / em_modes types are linear), and not with a Bloch wave vector k != 0. Resolve the harmonics it generates (>= 10 cells per wavelength at wavelength / 2 with d_eff, / 3 for a strong Kerr medium) or expect them to alias; the DFT monitors then sample often enough for up to three times the source band (no harmonic folds into a monitor band in time). Single-precision stepper only (its kernels and state are float32; a double stepper solver is a validation error).

- FeatureSpec.type `nonlinear_medium`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Stepper precisions single only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `n2` (float; unit m^2/W; default 0) - Kerr index n2
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.n2`
- `tpa_beta` (float; unit m/W; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Two-photon absorption
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.tpa_beta`
- `carrier_lifetime` (float; unit s; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Carrier lifetime
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.carrier_lifetime`
- `fca_cross_section` (float; unit m^2; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Free-carrier absorption cross-section
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fca_cross_section`
- `fcd_coefficient` (float; unit m^3; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Free-carrier index change
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fcd_coefficient`
- `pump_wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Pump wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.pump_wavelength`
- `d_eff` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - Second-order coefficient d
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.d_eff`
- `poling` (float; unit 1; default 1; may use x, y) - Poling
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.poling`

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium` - Gain medium

Four-level two-electron gain medium (Chang and Taflove, Opt. Express 12, 3827, 2004) on the selected cells, acting on E_z at the cell centres: a Lorentz polarisation d2P/dt2 + gamma dP/dt + omega_a^2 P = kappa (N1 - N2) E, kappa = 6 pi eps0 c^3 / (omega_a^2 tau_21), coupled to the rate equations of the populations N0..N3 (pump W_p N0 -> N3, decays N3 -> N2 -> N1 -> N0, stimulated transitions (E . dP/dt) / (hbar omega_a)); N2 > N1 amplifies, N1 > N2 absorbs. Regions add (overlaps are two species); the polarisation and populations live on the bounding box of the selection. Output field population_inversion = N2 - N1 (1/m^3). Not counted in absorbed power; not part of the build Courant check (keep |delta eps| (omega_a dt)^2 / 4 << 1). Time_dependent study only, Bloch k = 0 only and single-precision stepper only (as nonlinear_medium).

- FeatureSpec.type `gain_medium`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Stepper precisions single only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Transition wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.wavelength`
- `linewidth` (float; unit rad/s; default 1e+14; range [0, inf)) - Gain linewidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.linewidth`
- `density` (float; unit 1/m^3; default 1e+24; range (0, inf)) - Active ion density
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.density`
- `pump_rate` (float; unit 1/s; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Pump rate
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.pump_rate`
- `tau_32` (float; unit s; default 1e-13; range (0, inf)) - Lifetime level 3 -> 2
  Non-radiative lifetime of level 3 into level 2 [s]; >= 10 time steps (explicit rate step).
- `tau_21` (float; unit s; default 1e-09; range (0, inf)) - Lifetime level 2 -> 1
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.tau_21`
- `tau_10` (float; unit s; default 1e-13; range (0, inf)) - Lifetime level 1 -> 0
  Lifetime of the lower lasing level into the ground state [s]; >= 10 time steps.
- `initial_upper_fraction` (float; unit 1; default 0; range [0, 1]) - Initial upper-level fraction
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.initial_upper_fraction`

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Spectral Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line: the Yee discrete flux through the hi face of the line cells, > 0 toward +x for a vertical line and toward +y for a horizontal one. power is in a.u. per unit z length and not normalised by the source spectrum, so compare runs by ratios (transmission = device run / reference run with the same source); power_per_cw = power / (2 |S(omega)|^2) is the cw power in W/m. The per_cw values exist only when every source feature of the physics shares one waveform (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives are not counted); S(omega) = the dt-weighted spectrum of that waveform over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength (cw: also outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)). They equal the em_fdfd_* values at the same source amplitudes, exactly only at the source wavelength (sources are calibrated there). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `flux_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.n_wavelengths`

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on an axis-aligned line into the forward (positive: toward +x for a vertical line, +y for a horizontal one) and backward (negative) amplitudes a of one guided mode at every monitor wavelength: running DFTs of E_z in the line cells and of H_y (vertical line) / H_x (horizontal line) on their hi face are projected on the mode solved at that wavelength, so each direction is measured separately, unlike a flux_monitor. The 1D eigenmodes along the line are FDTD-consistent (kernel cell widths, numerical frequency and dispersion of the Yee scheme, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at that frequency with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are solved at build (finalize) on the final materials; during the run they are re-solved, following the selected mode by overlap, whenever the line materials drifted by more than 1e-3 relative since the last solve (thermo-optic or Pockels coupling, state-dependent permittivity; one host transfer of the line per material update). A mode monitor then decomposes its whole-run spectra with the latest modes (the run log notes it), which fits only light that passed after the medium settled. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side and a locally uniform mesh (validation refuses a line whose face falls on the outer grid wall and warns when a wall boundary pins the line cell or its face every step, when its face lies inside a CPML layer (line in the outermost window cell) or when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec domain edge takes E_z = 0, one on a pmc or symmetric edge dE_z/dn = 0 and one on an antisymmetric edge E_z odd about the plane, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E_z = 0 in the next cell), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'xy' versus wavelength: power_positive / power_negative = 2 |a|^2 in a.u. (dt-weighted spectral power per unit z length in the flux_monitor convention, so comparable with its power); power_per_cw_positive / power_per_cw_negative = |a|^2 / |S|^2 in W/m (the cw mode power, as em_fdfd_* power_*); with exactly one enabled mode_source in the physics also fraction_positive / fraction_negative (unit 1) = mode power / source power at that wavelength (|S|^2: transmission into this mode downstream of the source, reflection upstream; NaN where |S(omega)|^2 of the source is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength, and for a cw source outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)) and phase_positive / phase_negative (rad) = the phase of that S-parameter: the mode amplitude relative to the amplitude the source launches on its own line, not de-embedded (each mode profile is phased with its largest field sample real and positive, the lowest-coordinate one of mirror-equal peaks); extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (per wavelength), mode_number, tracked_mode_number (rank of the followed mode at the middle wavelength in the latest solve) and normalized (True when the fractions are present). The source spectrum covers the steps run, so run until the pulse has passed every monitor; the fractions inherit the off-centre leakage of the source, so they are most accurate near its wavelength. The per_cw values exist only when every source feature of the physics shares one waveform (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives are not counted); S(omega) = the dt-weighted spectrum of that waveform over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength (cw: also outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)). They equal the em_fdfd_* values at the same source amplitudes, exactly only at the source wavelength (sources are calibrated there).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 21; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.n_wavelengths`

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor` - Field map monitor

Running DFT of E_z over a rectangle, accumulating exp(-i omega t) at the actual sample times: |E_z(omega)|^2 per wavelength in a.u., not normalised by the source spectrum (one wavelength per freq_index); intensity x intensity_per_cw_factor[freq_index] (1 / |S(omega)|^2 per wavelength) is the cw |E_z|^2 in (V/m)^2. The per_cw values exist only when every source feature of the physics shares one waveform (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives are not counted); S(omega) = the dt-weighted spectrum of that waveform over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength (cw: also outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)). They equal the em_fdfd_* values at the same source amplitudes, exactly only at the source wavelength (sources are calibrated there). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `dft_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result kind `dft_fields`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. GPU memory: 2 * n_wavelengths * box cells * 4 B / downsample^2 (1000 x 1000 cells at 10 wavelengths: 80 MB), and every wavelength adds work per time step (validation warns above 1 GiB); 1-21 typical.
- `downsample` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Record every n-th cell
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor.downsample`

### Feature `em_fdtd_ez.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Near-to-far-field transform of E_z / H on the outline of a rectangle: radiated power per angle rho |E_z|^2 / eta0 (a.u.: dt-weighted spectra without the 1/2, so its angle integral matches a closed flux box) versus angle, counter-clockwise from +x, per wavelength. Enclose every scatterer with the box; with a TFSF source keep it outside the TFSF box, in the scattered field: its x0 / y0 edges at least one cell before those of the TFSF box and its x1 / y1 edges in the last TFSF cell or beyond (the TFSF outline faces hold scattered field; validation warns otherwise). The closed contour runs through the centres of the first box cells and of the cells one beyond x1 / y1 (keep the box one cell off the x_hi / y_hi edges), H averaged from the faces on both sides onto the centres; graded meshes work (actual centres, trapezoid weights of their spacing); the box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `far_field`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result kind `far_field`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 21; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. Each wavelength accumulates E_z / H spectra along the box outline (little memory); 1-41 typical.
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; range [1, inf)) - Number of angles
  Far-field angles evenly spaced over 360 degrees, counter-clockwise from +x (0 = +x, pi/2 = +y); 360 gives 1-degree steps.

## Physics type `em_fdtd_hz` - Electromagnetic Waves, time domain (2D, magnetic field out of plane)

2D finite-difference time-domain solver for the H_z polarisation: H_z out of plane in A/m, E_x and E_y in plane in V/m, x to the right and y up. On the Yee grid H_z sits at cell centres half a time step before the recorded time, E_x on the +y and E_y on the +x cell faces. Each face takes the arithmetic mean of the permittivity, conductivity and dispersive susceptibility of its two cells, weighted by their widths across the face (yee_grid.face_average; solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages the permittivity of interface faces anisotropically instead): curved interfaces are otherwise staircased and plasmon resonances shift on coarse meshes, so use cells of a few nm for plasmonics. In-plane E is what gives particle plasmons and guided modes whose E lies in the propagation plane (e.g. surface plasmon polaritons on metal films). gaussian and cw sources use a sin carrier (ricker is a real wavelet), DFT-based monitors accumulate exp(-i omega t) at the actual sample times, and every wavelength is a vacuum wavelength. Boundaries: CPML (cells added outside the domain), PEC, PMC, periodic and mirror planes on the domain edge; materials: eps_r (or eps_xx, eps_yy), sigma_e, mu_r, sigma_m plus Drude / Lorentz poles; current-calibrated sources (magnetic line current, electric dipole, sheet currents, TFSF plane wave) and mode (port) sources; probe, flux, mode, DFT and far-field monitors. Outputs e_abs, e_intensity and h_abs (|E|, |E|^2, |H| at the cell centres; instantaneous values, the FDFD types give phasor moduli under the same names). It advances one Courant step per runner tick, so every must be 1. A model with an em_fdtd_ez physics too (e.g. unpolarised light as one physics per polarisation) needs another instance name (e.g. em_hz) and the same bc_* / pml_* settings: both share one boundary configuration. In a frequency_domain study it runs one pulse and gives phasor fields per study wavelength (harmonic FDTD, see that study): every enabled source must share one gaussian or ricker waveform (same wavelength and bandwidth), the study wavelengths should lie inside its band, and no coupling may read this physics. Stepper solver (role stepper, explicit_kernels): precision single (float32 fields, default) or double (float64 fields, coefficients, CPML and pole arrays: ~2x the field memory and time, for long or high-Q ring-downs where float32 coefficient rounding, ~1e-7 of a mode frequency, accumulates into phase drift); materials, absorbed power, probe traces and field-map spectra stay float32, and nonlinear_medium / gain_medium need single.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_fdtd_hz`; default instance name `em`
- Supported studies: time_dependent, frequency_domain
- Default study: {"type": "time_dependent", "settings": {"duration": 2e-13}}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): hz
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_fdtd_hz.<feature>`): point_source, line_source, gaussian_beam, plane_wave_tfsf, mode_source, pec_domain, effective_index, nonlinear_medium, gain_medium, phase_change_medium, field_probe, resonance_monitor, flux_monitor, mode_monitor, dft_monitor, far_field

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  cpml absorbs outgoing waves in pml_cells extra cells added outside the domain. pec (tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost domain cell, H_z mirrored into that cell) and pmc (H_z = 0 at the centre of that cell) are perfect electric / magnetic walls up to one cell inside the domain edge. periodic must be set on both faces of the axis and wraps the field with the meshed window as period (uniform mesh: the size rounded up to whole cells) and no phase step (k = 0 along that axis, e.g. normal incidence); the em_fdtd_*, em_fdfd_* and em_modes types add a Bloch phase with bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear per input harmonic_channel; em_eme / em_eme_3d: k = 0 only). Mirror planes, on any face: symmetric = E mirror-even (a PMC mirror plane), antisymmetric = E mirror-odd (a PEC mirror plane), on the domain edge itself: one ghost cell is added outside it (the width of the edge cell, its material copied from it) to hold the mirror image, so draw the structure about the edge (x = 0 for x_lo); heat, potential and the other physics of the model have their faces on the same plane. The same plane and parity hold for the ez and hz types, so one setting imposes the same symmetry on both. A source half a cell from the plane (in the outermost domain cell) is mirrored with it. Results count the unfolded structure: a flux line reaching a mirror face and a derived integral whose selection reaches one are doubled per such face (result extra mirror_factor; integrands assumed mirror-even, e.g. powers and losses), far fields add the image contour (a box touching the plane drops its face there; at most one mirror per axis), Results.field(unfold=True) and the GUI show the mirrored field; mode-port powers, source powers and the probes stay those of the drawn part. pec and pmc walls of the two polarisations are half a cell apart (E_z pec and H_z pmc at the centre of the outermost domain cell, E_z pmc and H_z pec on its inner face), so a cavity simulated in both polarisations differs in width by one cell. For H_z: symmetric = H_z odd about the plane; antisymmetric = H_z even with tangential E = 0 on the plane (the same as pec on that face). These walls are re-applied after the sources are injected, so a source value on a pinned row or face is overwritten every step and radiates nothing (validation warns): H_z in the outermost cell of a pec or pmc face (a magnetic_current point source there), and the tangential E on the inner face of that cell of a pec face or on the plane of an antisymmetric one (a line source / gaussian beam sheet on that face, and the current parallel to the face of an electric_dipole in one of the two outermost cells).
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `courant_factor` (float; unit 1; default 0.99; range (0, 1]) - Time step factor
  Time step as a fraction of the 2D CFL limit: dt = factor / (C0 sqrt(1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2)) on a uniform mesh (factor * dx / (C0 sqrt(2)) for square cells; on a graded mesh the limit of the finest cells); 0.99 default. Stable only where min(eps_xx, eps_yy) * mu_r >= (C0 dt)^2 (1/dx^2 + 1/dy^2) (= factor^2 on a uniform mesh; coarser cells of a graded mesh have margin) + mu_r P, P = (omega_p dt)^2 / 4 per Drude pole and delta_eps (omega_0 dt)^2 / (4 - (omega_0 dt)^2) per Lorentz pole: plain permittivity and mu_r values must be >= 1, but an eps_inf ~1 metal needs a lower factor at coarse cells. The build checks every cell (field-dependent values, Drude eps_inf < 1, poles), names the worst one and the largest stable factor, but runtime eps_xx / eps_yy rewrites (thermo-optic) are not checked.
- `track_absorption` (bool; default false) - Track absorption
  Accumulate J.E losses J_x E_x + J_y E_y + sigma_e |E|^2 on the cell faces (output absorbed_power in W/m^3, state q_accum in J/m^3) also without an em_heat_joule coupling; costs about one extra full-grid GPU pass per step. The conductivity loss of a face goes to each of its two cells by that cell's own sigma_e; the loss of a pole current goes to the cells of the dispersive material (half / half between two different dispersive cells). The state q_accum exists only while accumulation runs; it is switched on automatically when a material expression, a derived value, a field_transfer, em_heat_joule or em_semiconductor_generation reads q_accum, or a derived value reads absorbed_power (else absorbed_power is 0 everywhere). absorbed_power shows the current accumulation window, else the last completed one; em_heat_joule resets q_accum at each transfer, otherwise the window spans the whole run.
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_kx`
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.bloch_ky`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic in-plane relative permittivity (>= 1): sets eps_xx and eps_yy unless the material sets those components (a component wins over eps_r). n^2 of a lossless dielectric: glass ~2.1-2.25, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um; may depend on x, y and physics fields. E_x / E_y sit on cell faces and each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically). For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf: an explicit permittivity wins over the Drude eps_inf, which applies only when none is set. A state-dependent eps_r (e.g. of T) is rewritten once per step of the physics it reads, not every EM step.
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, x
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_xx`
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, y
  Help: shared `em_eme.eps_yy`
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss J = sigma_e E on E_x and E_y in S/m, default 0 (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells). A weak absorber with index n and extinction coefficient kappa at angular frequency omega has sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0; model metals with a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1); H_z sees mu_zz = mu_r. 1 for practically every optical material. It enters the Courant check (min(eps_xx, eps_yy) * mu_r) and the local impedance of line sources.
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss on H_z in Ohm/m, default 0; sigma_m / (mu0 mu_r) = sigma_e / (eps0 eps_r) gives an impedance-matched absorber without reflection at normal incidence.

### Source slots

- `hz_source` (A/m per EM step): Added to H_z once per EM step (after the magnetic sources) until the next transfer: a raw field increment, not a calibrated source. A constant buffer b acts like a magnetic current density of about -mu0 mu_r b / dt, so its effect scales with 1/dt (mesh, courant_factor); not counted in the DFT decimation bound.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.point_source` - Point source

Current-calibrated point excitation in the cell containing the point (a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the upper cell); its field does not depend on the mesh. magnetic_current: a z-directed magnetic line current K_m [V] added to H_z at the cell centre, radiating |H_z| = omega eps0 eps_r K_m / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)|. electric_dipole: an in-plane electric current element of strength M [A] along orientation, split over the two E_x faces (+y / -y) and the two E_y faces (+x / -x) of the cell, radiating |H_z| = k M / 4 |H1^(2)(k r)| |sin(phi - orientation)|. The wall boundaries overwrite some values every step (warning): a magnetic_current in the outermost cell of a pec, pmc, symmetric or antisymmetric face radiates nothing, and so does the current parallel to a pec or antisymmetric face of an electric_dipole in one of the two outermost cells.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `excitation` (choice; default "magnetic_current"; choices magnetic_current | electric_dipole) - Excitation
  magnetic_current: z-directed magnetic line current added to H_z at the cell centre (radiates the same in every direction). electric_dipole: in-plane electric current element along orientation, spread over the four E faces of the cell (radiates most broadside, nothing along its axis).
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `magnetic_current` (float; unit V; default 1; visible when excitation in (magnetic_current)) - Magnetic line current
  Peak z-directed magnetic line current K_m in V (the dual of a filament current). The radiated field does not depend on the mesh: for cw in a homogeneous medium of relative permittivity eps_r and wavenumber k, |H_z| = omega eps0 eps_r K_m / 4 |H0^(2)(k r)| (1 V at wavelength 1 um in vacuum: |H_z| ~ 1.3e3 A/m at r = 1 um). Fields are linear, so results scale with K_m. A fixed K_m radiates power ~ n^2 of its cell, so it drifts when eps there changes (e.g. thermo-optic); a filament current or dipole radiates n-independent power. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `dipole_moment` (float; unit A; default 0.001; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole strength
  Peak in-plane electric dipole strength M in A: the integral of the current density J over the cross-section, i.e. A*m of current moment per m of z, along orientation. The radiated field does not depend on the mesh: for cw in a homogeneous medium of wavenumber k, |H_z| = k M / 4 |H1^(2)(k r)| |sin(phi - orientation)| at the angle phi counter-clockwise from +x (1 mA at wavelength 1 um in vacuum: |H_z| ~ 5e2 A/m at r = 1 um broadside). Fields are linear, so results scale with M. Sign: the current is added to the field update as given, i.e. it is minus the textbook impressed current, so absolute phases (and a source power computed from probe fields) differ by pi from textbook formulas such as E_z = -(omega mu0 I / 4) H0^(2)(k r); moduli and fluxes do not.
- `orientation` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when excitation in (electric_dipole)) - Dipole orientation
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_hz.point_source.orientation`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.line_source` - Line source

Electric sheet current on an axis-aligned line radiating amplitude V/m of tangential E to each side in the local medium: a vertical line (x = const) drives E_y and sends waves along +x and -x, a horizontal one drives E_x and sends them along +y and -y. The sheet sits on the hi face of the line cells (+x face of a vertical line, +y face of a horizontal one), and the local impedance uses that face permittivity (width-weighted mean of its two cells). For a plane wave, span the whole domain: an end on a cpml domain edge continues through the PML (on a periodic axis span the whole period); a shorter line diffracts like a slit. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. The line must not lie in the last cell row / column before a non-periodic hi face without PML: its hi face is then the outer grid wall. Next to a pec or antisymmetric face the sheet must not be the inner face of the outermost cell either (the line in the outermost lo cell or the last-but-one hi cell): the wall pins that E face to 0 every step, so the line radiates nothing (warning).

- FeatureSpec.type `line_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  Tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) radiated to each side of the line in the local medium (a cw plane wave of this amplitude when the line spans a periodic axis); the calibration uses |eta| of the line faces at the centre frequency (sigma_e and dispersion included), so other frequencies of a pulse in a dispersive medium deviate. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so on a line crossing several media (e.g. a high-index core and its cladding) the current steps at the interfaces, the steps diffract and the field there is not the amplitude (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). Each recalibration (e.g. a thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n of the line cells (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2). Typical 1 V/m.

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.gaussian_beam` - Gaussian beam

Line source with the profile exp(-((s - center) / waist)^2) along the line, radiating a beam of peak tangential E = amplitude V/m to each side in the local medium (vertical line: E_y, along +x and -x; horizontal: E_x, along +y and -y); the waist lies on the line and the sheet on the hi face of the line cells, so the line must not lie in the last cell row / column before a non-periodic hi face without PML (the outer grid wall), nor, next to a pec or antisymmetric face, put the sheet on the inner face of the outermost cell, which the wall pins to 0 every step (warning: the beam radiates nothing). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `gaussian_beam`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak tangential E (E_x for a horizontal line, E_y for a vertical one) at the beam centre on the waist line, radiated to each side in the local medium; the calibration uses |eta| of the line faces at the centre frequency (sigma_e and dispersion included), so other frequencies of a pulse in a dispersive medium deviate. Fields are linear, so results scale with it. Each line cell is calibrated to its own medium, so on a line crossing several media (e.g. a high-index core and its cladding) the current steps at the interfaces, the steps diffract and the field there is not the amplitude (validation warns); keep the line in one medium. Its medium is the face mean of the line cell and the cell past its hi face, so on an interface sqrt(mean eps) is not the mean index (Si / air: ~14% off). Each recalibration (e.g. a thermo-optic eps change in the line cells) keeps the amplitude, so the launched power ~ amplitude^2 n / (2 eta0) follows n of the line cells (~0.5% for dn = 0.01 at n = 2.2). Typical 1 V/m.
- `waist` (float; unit m; default 1e-06; range (0, inf)) - Waist radius
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.waist`
- `center` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Beam centre
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam.center`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.plane_wave_tfsf` - Plane wave box (+x)

Plane wave travelling along +x only (E_y, H_z = E_y / eta0), injected on the outline of a total-field box: total field inside the box (its H_z cells), only the scattered field outside (the E faces on the outline included); amplitude = incident E_y. Uniform or graded meshes (the 1D incident line runs on the grid's own x widths, so graded x and y cells leak nothing); the incident field is computed for vacuum, so the box edges must lie in vacuum (warning otherwise), and the box needs one scattered-field cell inside the domain on every side, except at a y mirror face of the wave's parity (ez: symmetric, hz: antisymmetric), where it may reach the plane: the box opens there and its mirror image completes it (the other parity, or an x mirror face, is an error). Keep flux and mode monitors entirely inside the box (their hi face too) or outside it (validation warns). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `plane_wave_tfsf`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw | ricker) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source.bandwidth`
- `amplitude` (float; unit V/m; default 1) - Amplitude
  Peak incident E_y of the +x plane wave (computed for vacuum, H_z = E_y / eta0); the scattered field outside the box is relative to it. Typical 1 V/m.

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.mode_source` - Mode source

Port source launching one guided mode of the cross-section under an axis-aligned line in one direction: a vertical line (x = const) launches toward +x (direction positive) or -x (negative), a horizontal one toward +y or -y. The mode drives H_z in the line cells and E_y (vertical line) / E_x (horizontal line) on their upstream face, i.e. the lo face of the line cells for positive and their hi face for negative. The mode is injected as a one-sided total-field / scattered-field line (discrete equivalent currents): total field from the line cells downstream, while upstream only what comes back (reflections) remains. The launch is exact and one-sided at the source wavelength; toward the band edges of a gaussian pulse some power leaks upstream or into radiation because the profile and impedance of the mode change with wavelength, so keep the bandwidth modest in dispersive guides. Mode monitors normalise by it when it is the only enabled mode source of the physics. Its interface face holds scattered field, so a flux or mode monitor on the line of a negative source (total-field line cells, interface on their hi face) mixes both (validation warns). The 1D eigenmodes along the line are FDTD-consistent (kernel cell widths, numerical frequency and dispersion of the Yee scheme, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at that frequency with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are solved at build (finalize) on the final materials; during the run they are re-solved, following the selected mode by overlap, whenever the line materials drifted by more than 1e-3 relative since the last solve (thermo-optic or Pockels coupling, state-dependent permittivity; one host transfer of the line per material update). A mode monitor then decomposes its whole-run spectra with the latest modes (the run log notes it), which fits only light that passed after the medium settled. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side and a locally uniform mesh (validation refuses a line whose face falls on the outer grid wall and warns when a wall boundary pins the line cell or its face every step, when its face lies inside a CPML layer (line in the outermost window cell) or when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The in-plane E faces use the permittivity the engine uses (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the mean of core and cladding there. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'table' at the source wavelength, one row per mode for the first max(mode_number + 2, 4) modes: mode_number, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (< 0 = loss in the exp(+j omega t) convention), loss_db_per_cm, n_group, edge_field (largest |field| at the two ends of the solved line / its peak; above 1e-2 at a metal end the line cuts the mode) and selected (True for the launched mode); extras wavelength, power, direction, mode_number and tracked_mode_number (the rank of the launched mode in the latest solve: mode_number until a re-solve during the run finds it at another rank; the selected row follows it).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdfd_ez.mode_source.mode_number`
- `direction` (choice; default "positive"; choices positive | negative) - Direction
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.direction`
- `waveform` (choice; default "gaussian"; choices gaussian | cw) - Waveform
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.waveform`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 5.5e-07; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.wavelength`
- `bandwidth` (float; unit 1; default 0.3; range (0, inf); visible when waveform in (gaussian)) - Relative bandwidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.bandwidth`
- `power` (float; unit W/m; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Mode power
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_source.power`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor: tangential E = 0 on every face of each cell whose centre lies in the selected domains (E_x on its +y and -y faces, E_y on its +x and -x faces), with no dispersive current on those faces; staircased to the mesh. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra) only faces wholly inside the drawn metal are PEC and each cut cell updates H_z from its free face lengths and free area (enlarged where needed so the time step stays stable).

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.nonlinear_medium` - Nonlinear medium

chi2 (d_eff, poling), Kerr, two-photon absorption (TPA) and TPA free carriers on the selected cells (later features win on overlaps), on top of the linear material (eps, sigma_e, poles). Each step corrects each in-plane component on its own faces (E_x and E_y, face mean of the cell values as for eps), n0^2 = the face permittivity; |E|^2 is taken per component (E_x^2 on E_x faces, E_y^2 on E_y faces) and the carriers live on the faces of the component whose TPA generated them; chi2 acts per component too (P_x = eps0 chi2 E_x^2 on E_x faces, P_y = eps0 chi2 E_y^2 on E_y faces): exact for a field along one in-plane axis (slab modes, plane waves), approximate for mixed in-plane polarisation (the cross-component chi2, Kerr and TPA terms are dropped) after the linear update by solving D = eps0 (eps + chi2 E + chi3 E^2 + delta eps(N)) E with the TPA + FCA conductivity implicitly (one fused kernel on the bounding box of the selection; n0 is read live, so thermo-optic eps changes carry over). The carrier density N follows dN/dt = TPA power / (2 hbar omega) - N / tau (output field carrier_density, 1/m^3) and adds the absorption sigma_fca N and the index change -k N. TPA and FCA power count as absorbed power. Nonlinear media break superposition: time_dependent study only (the frequency_domain harmonic FDTD and the FDFD / em_modes types are linear), and not with a Bloch wave vector k != 0. Resolve the harmonics it generates (>= 10 cells per wavelength at wavelength / 2 with d_eff, / 3 for a strong Kerr medium) or expect them to alias; the DFT monitors then sample often enough for up to three times the source band (no harmonic folds into a monitor band in time). Single-precision stepper only (its kernels and state are float32; a double stepper solver is a validation error).

- FeatureSpec.type `nonlinear_medium`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Stepper precisions single only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `n2` (float; unit m^2/W; default 0) - Kerr index n2
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.n2`
- `tpa_beta` (float; unit m/W; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Two-photon absorption
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.tpa_beta`
- `carrier_lifetime` (float; unit s; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Carrier lifetime
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.carrier_lifetime`
- `fca_cross_section` (float; unit m^2; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Free-carrier absorption cross-section
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fca_cross_section`
- `fcd_coefficient` (float; unit m^3; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Free-carrier index change
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.fcd_coefficient`
- `pump_wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Pump wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.pump_wavelength`
- `d_eff` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - Second-order coefficient d
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.d_eff`
- `poling` (float; unit 1; default 1; may use x, y) - Poling
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium.poling`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.gain_medium` - Gain medium

Four-level two-electron gain medium (Chang and Taflove, Opt. Express 12, 3827, 2004) on the selected cells, acting on each in-plane E face set separately (E_x and E_y faces, weight = face mean of the selected cells; each face set keeps its own populations, so a field along one in-plane axis depletes only that set): a Lorentz polarisation d2P/dt2 + gamma dP/dt + omega_a^2 P = kappa (N1 - N2) E, kappa = 6 pi eps0 c^3 / (omega_a^2 tau_21), coupled to the rate equations of the populations N0..N3 (pump W_p N0 -> N3, decays N3 -> N2 -> N1 -> N0, stimulated transitions (E . dP/dt) / (hbar omega_a)); N2 > N1 amplifies, N1 > N2 absorbs. Regions add (overlaps are two species); the polarisation and populations live on the bounding box of the selection. Output field population_inversion = N2 - N1 (1/m^3). Not counted in absorbed power; not part of the build Courant check (keep |delta eps| (omega_a dt)^2 / 4 << 1). Time_dependent study only, Bloch k = 0 only and single-precision stepper only (as nonlinear_medium).

- FeatureSpec.type `gain_medium`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Stepper precisions single only (see solvers): another precision of the physics' resolved stepper solver is a validation error at the feature
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Transition wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.wavelength`
- `linewidth` (float; unit rad/s; default 1e+14; range [0, inf)) - Gain linewidth
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.linewidth`
- `density` (float; unit 1/m^3; default 1e+24; range (0, inf)) - Active ion density
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.density`
- `pump_rate` (float; unit 1/s; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Pump rate
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.pump_rate`
- `tau_32` (float; unit s; default 1e-13; range (0, inf)) - Lifetime level 3 -> 2
  Non-radiative lifetime of level 3 into level 2 [s]; >= 10 time steps (explicit rate step).
- `tau_21` (float; unit s; default 1e-09; range (0, inf)) - Lifetime level 2 -> 1
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.tau_21`
- `tau_10` (float; unit s; default 1e-13; range (0, inf)) - Lifetime level 1 -> 0
  Lifetime of the lower lasing level into the ground state [s]; >= 10 time steps.
- `initial_upper_fraction` (float; unit 1; default 0; range [0, 1]) - Initial upper-level fraction
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.gain_medium.initial_upper_fraction`
