### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.flux_monitor` - Flux monitor

Spectral Poynting flux through an axis-aligned line: S_x = Re(E_y H_z*) through a vertical line, S_y = -Re(E_x H_z*) through a horizontal one, > 0 toward +x / +y. E is taken on the hi face of the line cells and H_z at their centres (time-centred, not interpolated in space). power is in a.u. per unit z length and not normalised by the source spectrum, so compare runs by ratios (transmission = device run / reference run with the same source); power_per_cw = power / (2 |S(omega)|^2) is the cw power in W/m. The per_cw values exist only when every source feature of the physics shares one waveform (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives are not counted); S(omega) = the dt-weighted spectrum of that waveform over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength (cw: also outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)). They equal the em_fdfd_* values at the same source amplitudes, exactly only at the source wavelength (sources are calibrated there). The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `flux_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `flux_spectrum`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 100; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.n_wavelengths`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.mode_monitor` - Mode monitor

Port monitor splitting the field on an axis-aligned line into the forward (positive: toward +x for a vertical line, +y for a horizontal one) and backward (negative) amplitudes a of one guided mode at every monitor wavelength: running DFTs of H_z in the line cells and of E_y (vertical line) / E_x (horizontal line) on their hi face are projected on the mode solved at that wavelength, so each direction is measured separately, unlike a flux_monitor. The 1D eigenmodes along the line are FDTD-consistent (kernel cell widths, numerical frequency and dispersion of the Yee scheme, PML stretch, complex permittivity and permeability of the line cells at that frequency with poles, sigma_e and sigma_m) and are solved at build (finalize) on the final materials; during the run they are re-solved, following the selected mode by overlap, whenever the line materials drifted by more than 1e-3 relative since the last solve (thermo-optic or Pockels coupling, state-dependent permittivity; one host transfer of the line per material update). A mode monitor then decomposes its whole-run spectra with the latest modes (the run log notes it), which fits only light that passed after the medium settled. Put the line across a straight guide with the same cross-section a few cells on either side and a locally uniform mesh (validation refuses a line whose face falls on the outer grid wall and warns when a wall boundary pins the line cell or its face every step, when its face lies inside a CPML layer (line in the outermost window cell) or when the cell widths along the normal change by more than 1% around the line). Span ends, as at an industry-standard port boundary: an end on a cpml domain edge continues the solve through the PML cells (open: radiation is absorbed); an end on a pec or antisymmetric domain edge takes tangential E = 0 on the inner face of the outermost cell (dH_z/dn = 0), one on a pmc edge H_z = 0 and one on a symmetric edge H_z odd, as those walls do; an end inside the domain, or a partial span of a periodic axis, is metal (E along the propagation direction = 0 on the face beyond the end, so dH_z/dn = 0), so extend the line well into the cladding (the build warns when the mode still exceeds 1% of its peak at a metal end); a span over a whole periodic axis is periodic. The in-plane E faces use the permittivity the engine uses (each face takes the width-weighted mean of its two cells), so a guide edge on a face line takes the mean of core and cladding there. The line covers cells [cell(start), cell(end) + 1), so an end exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell. Result 'xy' versus wavelength: power_positive / power_negative = 2 |a|^2 in a.u. (dt-weighted spectral power per unit z length in the flux_monitor convention, so comparable with its power); power_per_cw_positive / power_per_cw_negative = |a|^2 / |S|^2 in W/m (the cw mode power, as em_fdfd_* power_*); with exactly one enabled mode_source in the physics also fraction_positive / fraction_negative (unit 1) = mode power / source power at that wavelength (|S|^2: transmission into this mode downstream of the source, reflection upstream; NaN where |S(omega)|^2 of the source is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength, and for a cw source outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)) and phase_positive / phase_negative (rad) = the phase of that S-parameter: the mode amplitude relative to the amplitude the source launches on its own line, not de-embedded (each mode profile is phased with its largest field sample real and positive, the lowest-coordinate one of mirror-equal peaks); extras frequency, wavelength, n_eff (real part), n_eff_imag (per wavelength), mode_number, tracked_mode_number (rank of the followed mode at the middle wavelength in the latest solve) and normalized (True when the fractions are present). The source spectrum covers the steps run, so run until the pulse has passed every monitor; the fractions inherit the off-centre leakage of the source, so they are most accurate near its wavelength. The per_cw values exist only when every source feature of the physics shares one waveform (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives are not counted); S(omega) = the dt-weighted spectrum of that waveform over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength (cw: also outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)). They equal the em_fdfd_* values at the same source amplitudes, exactly only at the source wavelength (sources are calibrated there).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count exactly 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.mode_number`
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 21; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.mode_monitor.n_wavelengths`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.dft_monitor` - Field map monitor

Running DFT of H_z, E_x and E_y over a rectangle, accumulating exp(-i omega t) at the actual sample times (H_z half a step earlier), with E_x / E_y averaged onto the cell centres: intensity = |E_x(omega)|^2 + |E_y(omega)|^2 and hz_intensity = |H_z(omega)|^2 per wavelength in a.u., not normalised by the source spectrum (one wavelength per freq_index); intensity x intensity_per_cw_factor[freq_index] (1 / |S(omega)|^2 per wavelength) is the cw |E|^2 in (V/m)^2. The per_cw values exist only when every source feature of the physics shares one waveform (type, wavelength, bandwidth; coupling drives are not counted); S(omega) = the dt-weighted spectrum of that waveform over the steps run; NaN where |S|^2 is below 1e-6 of its value at the source wavelength (cw: also outside |f - f0| < 1 / (steps run x dt)). They equal the em_fdfd_* values at the same source amplitudes, exactly only at the source wavelength (sources are calibrated there). The box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `dft_monitor`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result kind `dft_fields`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 5; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. GPU memory: 6 * n_wavelengths * box cells * 4 B / downsample^2 (H_z, E_x and E_y spectra; 1000 x 1000 cells at 10 wavelengths: 240 MB), and every wavelength adds work per time step (validation warns above 1 GiB); 1-21 typical.
- `downsample` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Record every n-th cell
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor.downsample`

### Feature `em_fdtd_hz.far_field` - Far-field pattern

Near-to-far-field transform of H_z / E on the outline of a rectangle: radiated power per angle rho |eta0 H_z|^2 / eta0 (the far-field |E|^2 in vacuum; a.u.: dt-weighted spectra without the 1/2, so its angle integral matches a closed flux box) versus angle, counter-clockwise from +x, per wavelength. Enclose every scatterer with the box; with a TFSF source keep it outside the TFSF box, in the scattered field: its x0 / y0 edges at least one cell before those of the TFSF box and its x1 / y1 edges in the last TFSF cell or beyond (the TFSF outline faces hold scattered field; validation warns otherwise). The closed contour runs through the centres of the first box cells and of the cells one beyond x1 / y1 (keep the box one cell off the x_hi / y_hi edges), E averaged from the faces on both sides onto the centres; graded meshes work (actual centres, trapezoid weights of their spacing); the box covers cells [cell(lo), cell(hi) + 1) per axis, so an edge exactly on a cell edge takes one extra cell.

- FeatureSpec.type `far_field`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; object kinds rectangle; count exactly 1
- Result kind `far_field`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 4e-07; range (0, inf)) - Shortest wavelength
  Help: shared `em_fdtd_3d.flux_plane.wavelength_start`
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 8e-07; range (0, inf)) - Longest wavelength
  Longest vacuum wavelength of the monitor spectrum; it must exceed wavelength_start (equal only with n_wavelengths = 1).
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 21; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Wavelengths evenly spaced in wavelength (not frequency) from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop; 1 = the centre of the range. Each wavelength accumulates H_z / E spectra along the box outline (little memory); 1-41 typical.
- `n_angles` (int; default 360; range [1, inf)) - Number of angles
  Far-field angles evenly spaced over 360 degrees, counter-clockwise from +x (0 = +x, pi/2 = +y); 360 gives 1-degree steps.

## Physics type `em_modes` - Electromagnetic Waves, cross-section modes

Full-vector finite-difference eigenmode solver of a waveguide cross-section: the xy plane is the cross-section, the guide runs along z (out of plane), x to the right and y up; fields vary as exp(j (omega t - beta z)) (time convention exp(+j omega t)) with n_eff = beta / k0, k0 = omega / C0, so a lossy or leaky mode has Im n_eff < 0. Yee cross-section (a 3D Yee cell projected, transverse-H formulation after Fallahkhair, Li and Murphy, JLT 2008): E_z at the cell centres, E_x and H_y on the +x cell faces, E_y and H_x on the +y faces, H_z at the +x+y corner; eps_zz (array eps_r) is the cell value, eps_xx on a +x face and eps_yy on a +y face the width-weighted mean of the two cells, mu the cell value (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing replaces the background eps at interface locations: E_x / E_y faces 1 / (n^2 <1/eps> + (1 - n^2) / <eps>) with n the in-plane interface normal component, E_z cells the area mean <eps>); all complex at the solve wavelength (sigma_e, Drude / Lorentz chi, sigma_m). The generalised eigenproblem A h = beta^2 B h for h = eta0 (H_x, H_y) is solved on the host by shift-invert Arnoldi (scipy eigs on a SuperLU factor: needs scipy; 2 unknowns per cell, PML included, so validation warns near and refuses beyond the factor size limit) around (k0 n_eff_guess)^2. Solver roles: eigen = arpack_shift_invert (tolerance, subspace_size, factorization: superlu, cudss = a cuDSS LU on the GPU without the host size limit, guarded by the free device memory; cudss_mixed only on a triangles mesh, since this operator is not complex symmetric); shifted: Automatic (sparse_direct) = that SuperLU factor, a line_block node factors the shift-invert operators on its backend instead (unknowns ordered by grid rows or columns, a periodic axis inside the blocks, two periodic axes an error; mixed or double precision, refined against the complex128 operator), batched: the omega and, with group_index, omega (1 +- 1e-3) operators of a solve and, in a frequency_domain study, those of the next wavelengths, up to 8 operators per batch, as many as 60 % of the free memory holds; a rejected solve redoes that eigen-solve on SuperLU (run-log warning); shg_overlap / bend_overlap solves stay SuperLU. Modes with more than half of their |H|^2 in PML cells are dropped, the rest ranked by descending Re(beta^2) (ties by Im; = descending Re n_eff for low-loss guided modes, evanescent ones last), up to n_modes kept. Each mode carries 1 W, P = 1/2 Re integral (E x H*).z dA (E_x / H_y and E_y / H_x share their points), phased so its dominant transverse E component is real and positive at its peak (the lowest-index cell of mirror-equal peaks). Degenerate pairs (the two HE11 polarisations of a round fibre, TE11 / TM11 of a metal pipe) come back as arbitrary, not necessarily orthogonal, combinations. Outputs (the displayed mode: the mode_number setting after a study, at the cell centres with the face / corner components averaged there): ex, ey, ez, hx, hy, hz = the real parts in V/m and A/m, e_abs, e_intensity (|E|^2, the primary field), h_abs and sz = 1/2 Re(E_x H_y* - E_y H_x*) in W/m^2 (time-averaged power flow along z; its integral over the window equals the 1 W only to discretisation order and misses any PML share); state fields e_intensity and sz of the displayed mode; scalar outputs n_eff_1 .. n_eff_<n_modes> (derived values: <physics>_n_eff_<k>). No absorbed power: em_modes is not an em_heat_joule source. Features: mode_table, mode_dispersion, shg_overlap (coupled-mode SHG efficiency of a mode pair at omega / 2 omega), bend_overlap (straight-to-bend junction loss of a bent guide), pec_domain. Periodic faces may carry a Bloch phase (bloch_kx / bloch_ky: Bloch modes of a periodic cross-section). Studies: mode_analysis (one solve at the wavelength setting after any background heat / current solve, one snapshot per mode) and frequency_domain (one solve per wavelength). heat_em_thermo_optic rewrites eps_zz, eps_xx and eps_yy (slots eps_r_update, eps_xx_update, eps_yy_update). The xy plane here is a cross-section, not a propagation plane, so em_modes cannot share a model with em_fdtd_* or em_fdfd_* (validation error). On a triangles mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles) the same physics is a finite-element solve: Nedelec edge elements for E_x, E_y and Lagrange elements for E_z of the discretization setting (Lee-Sun-Cendes mixed form for beta^2, complex symmetric with PML / loss), materials one value per element, a structured PML ring; the same outputs on a display raster of the window (state fields one value per element) and the same table / dispersion results; details and refusals under discretization. The instance is usually named 'modes'.

- PhysicsSpec.type `em_modes`; default instance name `modes`
- Supported studies: mode_analysis, frequency_domain, thermal_noise, optomechanics
- Default study: {"type": "mode_analysis"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): e_intensity
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): used
- Features (topics `em_modes.<feature>`): mode_table, mode_dispersion, shg_overlap, bend_overlap, pec_domain

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `bc_x_lo`, `bc_x_hi`, `bc_y_lo`, `bc_y_hi` (choice; default "cpml"; choices cpml | pec | pmc | periodic | symmetric | antisymmetric) - Left edge / Right edge / Bottom edge / Top edge
  cpml absorbs outgoing waves in pml_cells extra cells added outside the domain. In the mode solve it is the complex coordinate stretch s = kappa + sigma / (alpha + j omega eps0) with the FDTD grading of the pml_* settings: a mode whose tail reaches it gains a small artificial loss (Im n_eff, see pml_fraction), and modes with more than half of their |H|^2 in PML cells are dropped. periodic must be set on both faces of the axis and wraps the field with the meshed window as period (uniform mesh: the size rounded up to whole cells) and no phase step (k = 0 along that axis, e.g. normal incidence); the em_fdtd_*, em_fdfd_* and em_modes types add a Bloch phase with bloch_kx / bloch_ky (em_fdfd_nonlinear per input harmonic_channel; em_eme / em_eme_3d: k = 0 only). Walls and mirrors all sit on one plane, the inner face of the outermost cell (the outermost cell is a ghost: each field component centred along that axis takes -1 (pec, antisymmetric) or +1 (pmc, symmetric) times its inner neighbour, the components on the plane are free (pec) or 0 (pmc)); that is half a cell off the em_fdtd_ez pec and em_fdtd_hz pmc walls, so a guide between two pec walls of a domain n cells wide is n - 2 cells wide. Mirrors, on any face, add their ghost cell outside the domain, so their plane is the domain edge: symmetric = E mirror-even (a PMC plane), antisymmetric = E mirror-odd (a PEC plane). A mirror through a symmetric guide halves the unknowns and keeps one parity: on x_lo, antisymmetric keeps the modes whose E_x is even about the plane (quasi-TE, e.g. TE0 of a strip), symmetric those whose E_y is even (quasi-TM).
- `pml_cells` (int; unit cells; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_cells`
- `pml_order` (int; default 3; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer grading
  Polynomial order m of the CPML sigma / kappa grading with depth into the layer; 3-4 typical.
- `pml_sigma_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer strength
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_sigma_factor`
- `pml_kappa_max` (float; unit 1; default 15; range [1, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer stretch
  Peak real coordinate stretching of the CPML (1 = none); larger values damp evanescent and grazing waves better. 5-15 typical.
- `pml_alpha_max` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when any of bc_x_lo, bc_x_hi, bc_y_lo, bc_y_hi in (cpml)) - Absorbing layer low-frequency damping
  Help: shared `em_eme.pml_alpha_max`
- `wavelength` (float; unit m; default 1.55e-06; range (0, inf)) - Wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength lambda0 of the mode solve in a mode_analysis study (omega = 2 pi C0 / lambda0; k0 = omega / C0). The materials enter at that omega (sigma_e and every Drude / Lorentz pole as a complex permittivity). A frequency_domain study solves its own wavelengths instead (validation info when this is not the default) and gives n_eff versus wavelength (mode_dispersion). The mesh needs >= 10 (better 20) cells per lambda0 / |n| in every material and, in metals, >= 2 (better 4) per skin depth lambda0 / (2 pi |Im n|); validation checks both. A 220 nm silicon core needs ~20 nm cells (or a refinement) for n_eff to ~1e-2. Typical 1.31e-6 or 1.55e-6 m.
- `n_modes` (int; default 4; range [1, 100]) - Number of modes
  Modes kept per solve: the eigen-solve finds the 2 n_modes + 10 eigenvalues beta^2 nearest the target (k0 n_eff_guess)^2, drops the modes with more than half of their |H|^2 in PML cells, ranks the rest by descending Re(beta^2), ties by descending Im(beta^2) (= descending Re n_eff for low-loss guided modes; evanescent modes, Re(beta^2) < 0, come last) and keeps up to n_modes (fewer may come back, e.g. near cutoff or when most candidates are PML modes). More modes cost more eigensolver work; 2-10 typical.
- `n_eff_guess` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Effective index guess
  Effective index around which modes are sought: the shift-invert target is sigma = (k0 n_eff_guess)^2, so the modes whose n_eff^2 lies nearest n_eff_guess^2 are found. Empty: the largest Re sqrt(eps mu) over the non-PEC cells and the three permittivity components at the solve wavelength (before any bend map), which finds the most strongly guided modes. Set it lower to reach higher-order modes, or near the expected value for a surface plasmon or a mode far below the core index.
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Displayed mode
  Mode number (1-based rank, descending Re(beta^2), see n_modes; as every mode_number) of the mode shown after the study: Results.field and the GUI field view, the state fields e_intensity / sz, and selected = True in mode_table. A frequency_domain study shows the mode of that rank at every wavelength (no tracking; mode_dispersion follows a mode by overlap). Must not exceed n_modes (validation error); when fewer modes are found the last one is shown (run-log warning).
- `group_index` (bool; default false) - Compute group index
  Also compute the group index n_g = C0 d(Re beta) / d(omega) of every mode by a central difference in omega (relative step 1e-3) with the materials re-evaluated at both frequencies (Drude / Lorentz chi and sigma_e: material dispersion included; plain eps_r values have none). Tensor meshes: two more eigen-solves per wavelength, each mode followed by overlap (about 3x the time); triangles meshes: the first-order perturbation of the complex symmetric pencil, two more assemblies and no eigen-solve. Off: n_group is NaN in the results.
- `bend_radius` (float; unit m; default 0) - Bend radius
  Signed radius R of a waveguide bent in the xz plane (0 = straight). R > 0 puts the centre of curvature at x = x_ref - R (the outer side of the bend is +x), R < 0 at x_ref + |R| (outer side -x), x_ref = bend_reference_x; the guide runs around the y axis (rings in the chip plane: y vertical), radius r = |R| s with s = 1 + (x - x_ref) / R at the x of each field point. bend_model sets the form (exact metric or the conformal map). n_eff is referred to the radius at x_ref: the angular propagation constant (azimuthal order of a ring) is nu = beta R = k0 n_eff R. Bend modes radiate toward the outer side, which shows as Im n_eff < 0 / loss_db_per_cm: keep a cpml face and enough cladding there (validation warns otherwise). s must stay > 0 over the whole grid, PML included, and the x axis must not be periodic (validation errors). Typical 5e-6 to 1e-4 m.
- `bend_reference_x` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Bend reference x
  x coordinate in m (physical frame) where s = 1 (bend_radius): the radius to which n_eff is referred, usually the guide centre. Empty: the domain centre size_x / 2. Unused when bend_radius = 0.
- `bend_model` (choice; default "exact"; choices exact | conformal) - Bend model
  Form of the bend (unused when bend_radius = 0). 'exact': the bent guide written exactly as a straight one in (x, y, R phi): eps and mu become eps diag(s, s, 1/s), mu diag(s, s, 1/s) (x, y, z components, each at its own field point), so the result is the true bend mode to discretisation order whenever the centre of curvature lies outside the grid; E_x, E_y, H_x, H_y are the physical E_r, E_y, H_r, H_y and E_z, H_z = s x the physical E_phi, H_phi; power and overlaps use the straight formulas. 'conformal': the approximate map of the bend-loss literature, every permittivity component times s^2, mu untouched: an error second order in w / R (w the mode width; e.g. -5e-4 relative in n_eff for the whispering-gallery mode of a 50 um metal-rimmed ring at 1.55 um). Both need s > 0 over the grid, PML included.
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Element order on a triangles mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles; tensor meshes ignore it and use the Yee cross-section). quadratic (default, the industry standard): second-order Nedelec edge elements for E_x, E_y and P2 Lagrange for E_z (Lee-Sun-Cendes mixed form, free of spurious modes), elements with a curved edge mapped isoparametrically, so circles and ellipses are followed to the mesh; linear: Whitney edge elements and P1 on straight elements, cheaper, error ~h^2 instead of ~h^4 in beta^2. About 7 (quadratic) or 2 (linear) unknowns per element, solved by the shift-invert of the eigen solver: host SuperLU, or with its factorization cudss a cuDSS LDL^T on the GPU (the pencil is complex symmetric), cudss_mixed its complex64 form: one float64 refinement step per solve, ARPACK to 1e-6, then beta^2 from the float64 Rayleigh quotient of each eigenvector (error ~ the square of the vector error). Materials are one value per element (an element takes the material at its centroid; the mesh follows every drawn outline). On triangles: pec / antisymmetric faces fix tangential E on the window edge, pmc / symmetric faces are natural (mirror planes are the window edge, no ghost cell); a cpml face gets a ring of mesh pml_layers structured element layers, pml_cells x the maximum element size thick, with the stretch of the pml_* settings and a pec outer side (pml_kappa_max 1 suits radiating leaky modes, the default 15 evanescent tails); pec_domain removes its elements and holds E = 0 on their outline. Not available on triangles (validation errors): periodic faces, bend_radius, shg_overlap, bend_overlap, a line_block shifted solver and the thermal_noise / optomechanics studies; subpixel smoothing and conformal boundaries do not apply.
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_x_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Bloch wave vector along x in rad/m, used only when bc_x_lo and bc_x_hi are periodic: the modes are Bloch waves of the periodic cross-section, F(x + L) = F(x) exp(-j kx L) per period L (the meshed period; fields ~ exp(j (omega t - beta z))), e.g. one supercell of a photonic-crystal fibre or of a waveguide array at a transverse phase step kx L per cell; kx and kx + 2 pi / L are the same state, 0 = plain periodic. The phase sits on the wrap entries of the operator (same unknowns and cost; the operator is no longer symmetric, which the shift-invert solve handles); the displayed centre fields take it across the wrap. Not with shg_overlap (its 2 omega modes would need 2 kx) and not in thermal_noise or optomechanics studies (their overlaps assume k = 0): validation errors. Typical: pi / L at the edge of the first zone.
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when bc_y_lo in (periodic)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Bloch wave vector along y in rad/m, used only when bc_y_lo and bc_y_hi are periodic: the modes are Bloch waves of the periodic cross-section, F(y + L) = F(y) exp(-j ky L) per period L (the meshed period; fields ~ exp(j (omega t - beta z))), e.g. one supercell of a photonic-crystal fibre or of a waveguide array at a transverse phase step ky L per cell; ky and ky + 2 pi / L are the same state, 0 = plain periodic. The phase sits on the wrap entries of the operator (same unknowns and cost; the operator is no longer symmetric, which the shift-invert solve handles); the displayed centre fields take it across the wrap. Not with shg_overlap (its 2 omega modes would need 2 ky) and not in thermal_noise or optomechanics studies (their overlaps assume k = 0): validation errors. Typical: pi / L at the edge of the first zone.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `eps_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r, eps_xx, eps_yy) - Relative permittivity
  Isotropic relative permittivity (>= 1): sets eps_xx, eps_yy and eps_zz unless the material sets those components (a component wins over eps_r). n^2 of a lossless dielectric: silica ~2.085, silicon ~12.1 at 1.55 um; may depend on x, y and physics fields. E_z sees the cell value, E_x on the +x and E_y on the +y cell faces the width-weighted mean of the two cells sharing that face (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically). The solve uses the complex permittivity at the solve wavelength: this value - j sigma_e / (omega eps0) plus the susceptibility chi(omega) of every Drude / Lorentz pole (exp(+j omega t): loss has Im < 0, giving Im n_eff < 0). For a dispersive material it is the background eps_inf (an explicit permittivity wins over the Drude eps_inf). A state-dependent value (e.g. of T) is rewritten once after the background solve, before the mode solve.
- `eps_zz` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_r) - Relative permittivity, z (along the guide)
  z component (along the guide) of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the one E_z sees at the cell centres; overrides eps_r for E_z. Uniaxial crystal with its optic axis along the guide: eps_zz = n_e^2, eps_r = n_o^2.
- `eps_xx` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_xx) - Relative permittivity, x
  x component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the one E_x sees on the +x cell faces (the width-weighted mean of the two cells sharing that face (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically)); overrides eps_r for E_x. E.g. x-cut lithium niobate at 1.55 um (optic axis along x): eps_xx 4.571 = n_e^2 with eps_r 4.889 = n_o^2 for the other components.
- `eps_yy` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_yy) - Relative permittivity, y
  y component of the relative permittivity (>= 1), the one E_y sees on the +y cell faces (the width-weighted mean of the two cells sharing that face (solver_defaults.subpixel_smoothing averages interface faces anisotropically)); overrides eps_r for E_y. For a uniaxial crystal with its optic axis along y set eps_yy = n_e^2.
- `sigma_e` (float; unit S/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_e) - Electric conductivity
  Ohmic loss in S/m on all three E components, default 0: the permittivity at the solve wavelength gains -j sigma_e / (omega eps0), so the guide gets Im n_eff < 0 and loss_db_per_cm > 0. A weak absorber with index n and extinction coefficient kappa at angular frequency omega has sigma_e = 2 n kappa omega eps0; model metals with a Drude pole, not their DC conductivity.
- `mu_r` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_r) - Relative permeability
  Real relative permeability (>= 1) of H_x, H_y and H_z, each taking the value of the cell it belongs to (H_x on the +y face, H_y on the +x face, H_z at the +x+y corner of that cell); 1 for practically every optical material. The solve uses mu_r - j sigma_m / (omega mu0).
- `sigma_m` (float; unit Ohm/m; default 0; range [0, inf); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_m) - Magnetic conductivity
  Magnetic loss on H_x, H_y, H_z in Ohm/m, default 0: mu_r gains -j sigma_m / (omega mu0) (artificial absorbers only).

### Fields

State fields:
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `sz` - S_z (power flow along z) (W/m^2)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity zz (1)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)

Output fields (primary e_intensity):
- `ex` - Re E_x (V/m)
- `ey` - Re E_y (V/m)
- `ez` - Re E_z (V/m)
- `hx` - Re H_x (A/m)
- `hy` - Re H_y (A/m)
- `hz` - Re H_z (A/m)
- `e_abs` - |E| (V/m)
- `e_intensity` - |E|^2 (V^2/m^2)
- `h_abs` - |H| (A/m)
- `sz` - S_z (power flow along z) (W/m^2)
- `eps_r` - Relative permittivity zz (1)
- `eps_xx` - Relative permittivity xx (1)
- `eps_yy` - Relative permittivity yy (1)
- `sigma_e` - Electric conductivity (S/m)

Scalar outputs: n_eff_<k> for k = 1 .. n_modes (unit 1): Re n_eff of mode k of the last solve, ranked as mode_table (a frequency_domain study: its last wavelength). A mode that was not found has no value: its derived value is NaN plus a run-log warning. Example derived value {"name": "n_eff_te0", "expression": "modes_n_eff_1"} (operation mean of a constant is the value itself); in a parameter sweep it gives n_eff per value.

### Source slots

- `eps_r_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_r: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_xx_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_xx: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.
- `eps_yy_update` (1): Relative permittivity eps_yy: each transfer replaces the whole array, PML ring included; index couplings (heat_em_thermo_optic) add their dn: eps = (n0 + sum dn)^2.

### Feature `em_modes.mode_table` - Mode table

Mode table of the last solve (a frequency_domain study: its last wavelength). Result 'table', one row per mode found, by descending Re(beta^2) (see n_modes): mode_number (1-based rank), n_eff (Re n_eff = Re beta / k0), n_eff_imag (Im n_eff < 0 = loss in the exp(+j omega t), exp(-j beta z) convention), loss_db_per_cm = -20 log10(e) Im(beta) / 100 (power loss in dB/cm, > 0 for a lossy or leaky mode), n_group (C0 d(Re beta) / d(omega), NaN unless group_index or when the mode could not be followed to the shifted frequencies, with a run-log warning), te_fraction = integral |E_x|^2 dA / integral (|E_x|^2 + |E_y|^2) dA (the industry-standard TE polarisation fraction: 1 = E along x, e.g. the quasi-TE mode of a strip on a substrate parallel to the xz plane, 0 = E along y), effective_area = (integral |E|^2 dA)^2 / integral |E|^4 dA in m^2 (all three components at the cell centres; the nonlinear-optics definition; like the 1 W normalisation it covers the whole mode, mirror images included) and pml_fraction (share of the mode's |H|^2 in PML cells: kept modes have < 0.5, and above ~1e-2 the PML shapes the mode: widen the cladding), and selected (True for the mode of the mode_number setting); extras wavelength (m) and selected_mode. For n_eff in a parameter sweep the scalar output <physics>_n_eff_<k> is simplest; any other column needs a derived value with source '<physics>.<this feature>', the column name as expression, operation at and at = mode_number - 1 (the row index).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_table`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `em_modes.mode_dispersion` - Mode dispersion

Scalars of one mode versus vacuum wavelength. Result 'xy' (x = wavelength in m, ascending; one point per solved wavelength, so a mode_analysis study gives one; a wavelength solved again keeps its latest solve), series n_eff (Re n_eff = Re beta / k0), n_eff_imag (Im n_eff < 0 = loss in the exp(+j omega t), exp(-j beta z) convention), loss_db_per_cm = -20 log10(e) Im(beta) / 100 (power loss in dB/cm, > 0 for a lossy or leaky mode), n_group (C0 d(Re beta) / d(omega), NaN unless group_index or when the mode could not be followed to the shifted frequencies, with a run-log warning), te_fraction = integral |E_x|^2 dA / integral (|E_x|^2 + |E_y|^2) dA (the industry-standard TE polarisation fraction: 1 = E along x, e.g. the quasi-TE mode of a strip on a substrate parallel to the xz plane, 0 = E along y), effective_area = (integral |E|^2 dA)^2 / integral |E|^4 dA in m^2 (all three components at the cell centres; the nonlinear-optics definition; like the 1 W normalisation it covers the whole mode, mirror images included) and pml_fraction (share of the mode's |H|^2 in PML cells: kept modes have < 0.5, and above ~1e-2 the PML shapes the mode: widen the cladding), and overlap (|overlap| of the followed mode with the one followed at the previous solve, 1 at the first; a value well below 1 means the mode changed character or crossed another); extras frequency (Hz), wavelength (m) and mode_number. The first solve that finds at least mode_number modes picks the mode of that rank; every later solve follows the mode of largest overlap with the previous one, so it keeps its identity where modes swap order in n_eff (solve order: the frequency_domain wavelengths list, else wavelength_start to wavelength_stop). Rows are NaN while the mode is not found.

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_dispersion`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_number` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Mode number
  1-based rank (descending Re(beta^2), as mode_table) of the followed mode at the first solve that finds that many modes; later solves follow it by overlap.

### Feature `em_modes.shg_overlap` - Second-harmonic overlap

Coupled-mode second-harmonic generation of a 3D waveguide from its cross-section modes. Result 'xy' versus pump vacuum wavelength (x, m; one point per solve: mode_analysis one, frequency_domain one per wavelength): after every em_modes solve at omega the feature solves the modes at 2 omega itself (same materials, walls, bend and eigen solver; a second eigen-solve of the same size, so about twice the time) and pairs mode pump_mode (omega) with mode harmonic_mode (2 omega), both by rank as in mode_table (no tracking across wavelengths). Series: n_eff_pump, n_eff_harmonic, delta_beta = Re beta(2 omega) - 2 Re beta(omega) [1/m], coherence_length = pi / |delta_beta| and poling_period = 2 pi / |delta_beta| [m] (NaN at delta_beta = 0), overlap = |kappa| [V^2/W^1.5], kappa = integral conj(e_2w) . (d : e_w e_w) dA over the selected domains (1 W modes, fields at the cell centres by face means), efficiency = (omega eps0 / 2)^2 |kappa|^2 in %/(W cm^2) (P_2w = efficiency P_w^2 L^2 when phase matched; times sinc^2(delta_beta L / 2) otherwise; a plane-wave mode of area A gives 8 pi^2 d^2 / (eps0 c n_w^2 n_2w lambda^2 A)) and efficiency_qpm = (2 / pi)^2 efficiency (first-order quasi phase matching, 50 % duty). Convention: exp(j (omega t - beta z)), SHG P(2 omega)_i = eps0 sum_jk d_ijk E_j E_k with d = chi2 / 2 given as Voigt d_il in MODEL axes (x, y = cross-section, z = along the guide; l = 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy): rotate crystal values yourself, e.g. x-cut lithium niobate with its c axis along model x and TE modes (E along x): d11 = d33(LN) ~ 2.5e-11 m/V, plus d12 = d13 = d31(LN) ~ -4.6e-12 m/V for the minor field components. The mesh must resolve the 2 omega modes (>= 10 cells per lambda / (2 n)); no mirror faces (the overlap integrand has no single parity) and Bloch k = 0 (validation errors); loss enters only through Re beta. With a bend (bend_radius) kappa is the physical overlap per length of arc at bend_reference_x (where delta_beta and L are measured too): bend_model exact integrates s dA with E_phi = E_z / s, conformal s^2 dA with the fields taken as physical (exact for E along y, approximate otherwise like the map), s = 1 + (x - x_ref) / R. ring_crystal local: d stays in the local frame (x radial, y vertical, z along the guide), i.e. it turns with the guide: right for terms unchanged by rotations about y (e.g. d33, d31, d15 of a z-cut crystal, c axis along y). ring_crystal fixed (bend only; an x- or y-cut ring): d is given at the reference cross-section (azimuth phi = 0) and the crystal stays fixed while the guide turns about y, so the local d(phi) = Q(phi) Q Q : d with Q rows (cos phi, 0, sin phi), (0, 1, 0), (-sin phi, 0, cos phi) and phi = z / R (signed R as bend_radius, z the arc at x_ref). kappa(phi) = sum over m = -3..3 of kappa_m exp(j m phi) (exact from 8 azimuths), and order m is phase matched when delta_beta R + m = 0. Extra series: azimuthal_mismatch = delta_beta R [1] (the azimuthal-order mismatch nu_2w - 2 nu_w of a ring), ring_order m* = round(-delta_beta R) (NaN when |m*| > 3: no ring harmonic supplies it), ring_mismatch = delta_beta + m* / R [1/m], ring_overlap = |kappa_m*| and ring_efficiency = (omega eps0 / 2)^2 |kappa_m*|^2 in %/(W cm^2) (0 when |m*| > 3; P_2w = ring_efficiency P_w^2 L^2 sinc^2(ring_mismatch L / 2) over an arc L), and ring_overlap_minus3 .. ring_overlap_plus3 = |kappa_m| [V^2/W^1.5]; the plain overlap / efficiency series stay those of the reference cross-section (phi = 0). E.g. x-cut lithium niobate, TE modes: d11 = d33(LN) gives kappa(phi) ~ cos^3 phi, i.e. orders +-1 (3/8) and +-3 (1/8) of kappa(0).

- FeatureSpec.type `shg_overlap`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `pump_mode` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Pump mode
  1-based rank (as mode_table) of the pump mode of each em_modes solve; must not exceed n_modes.
- `harmonic_mode` (int; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Second-harmonic mode
  1-based rank (descending Re(beta^2)) of the second-harmonic mode among the n_harmonic_modes modes of the 2 omega solve; must not exceed n_harmonic_modes.
- `n_harmonic_modes` (int; default 4; range [1, 100]) - Modes at the second harmonic
  Modes kept by the 2 omega solve (as n_modes of the physics).
- `harmonic_n_eff_guess` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Second-harmonic index guess
  Effective index around which the 2 omega modes are sought (as n_eff_guess); empty = the largest index of the cross-section at 2 omega.
- `ring_crystal` (choice; default "local"; choices local | fixed) - Crystal around the ring
  Bent guides only (bend_radius != 0 for 'fixed', validation error otherwise). 'local': the d_il hold in the guide's local frame everywhere. 'fixed': the d_il hold at the reference cross-section and the crystal stays fixed while the guide turns about y, so the coupling varies around the ring and phase matching picks an azimuthal order m = -3..3 (series azimuthal_mismatch, ring_order, ring_mismatch, ring_overlap, ring_efficiency, ring_overlap_minus3 .. _plus3; feature help).
- `d11` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d11
  Second-order coefficient d11 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 1 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 1); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d12` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d12
  Second-order coefficient d12 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 1 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 2); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d13` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d13
  Second-order coefficient d13 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 1 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 3); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d14` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d14
  Second-order coefficient d14 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 1 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 4); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d15` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d15
  Second-order coefficient d15 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 1 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 5); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d16` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d16
  Second-order coefficient d16 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 1 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 6); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d21` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d21
  Second-order coefficient d21 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 2 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 1); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d22` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d22
  Second-order coefficient d22 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 2 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 2); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d23` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d23
  Second-order coefficient d23 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 2 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 3); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d24` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d24
  Second-order coefficient d24 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 2 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 4); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d25` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d25
  Second-order coefficient d25 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 2 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 5); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d26` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d26
  Second-order coefficient d26 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 2 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 6); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
- `d31` (float; unit m/V; default 0) - d31
  Second-order coefficient d31 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 3 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 1); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.

  Second-order coefficient d32 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 3 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 2); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.

  Second-order coefficient d33 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 3 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 3); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.

  Second-order coefficient d34 in m/V in model axes (Voigt: polarisation component 3 = x, y, z for 1, 2, 3; field pair l = 4); d = chi2 / 2, 1 pm/V = 1e-12 m/V.
