### Feature `em_modes.bend_overlap` - Straight-to-bend overlap

Straight-to-bend junction of a bent guide (bend_radius != 0, validation error otherwise). Result 'table' of the last solve (a frequency_domain study: its last wavelength): after every em_modes solve the feature solves the same cross-section straight (same materials, walls and eigen solver, n_straight_modes modes near straight_n_eff_guess; a second eigen-solve of the same size) and pairs each bent mode with the straight mode of largest power coupling overlap = |c_bs c_sb| / |c_bb c_ss|, c_ab = 1/2 integral (E_a x H_b*).z dA over the junction plane (the transverse fields of the bent mode are the physical E_r, E_y, H_r, H_y in both bend models). Columns: mode_number (bent rank), n_eff, n_eff_imag (bent, referred to bend_reference_x), straight_mode (rank of the best-matching straight mode), n_eff_straight, overlap (1 = a perfect match), junction_loss_db = -10 log10(overlap) (the power lost into other modes and radiation at one straight-bend junction, ~1 / R^2 for large R: a ring coupler or an S-bend has two junctions per transition) and overlap_same_rank (with the straight mode of the same rank, NaN when fewer were found); extras wavelength (m) and n_straight_found. Both guides share the cross-section, so the junction is centred: the outward shift of the bent mode, which a lateral offset of the straight guide compensates, is part of the loss.

- FeatureSpec.type `bend_overlap`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `n_straight_modes` (int; default 4; range [1, 100]) - Straight modes
  Modes kept by the straight solve (as n_modes of the physics).
- `straight_n_eff_guess` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Straight index guess
  Effective index around which the straight modes are sought (as n_eff_guess); empty = the largest index of the cross-section.

### Feature `em_modes.pec_domain` - Perfect electric conductor

Perfect electric conductor: in every cell whose centre lies in the selected domains E_z = 0 at the centre and E_x / E_y = 0 on the faces between two such cells (eps^-1 = 0 there), staircased to the mesh. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (Dey-Mittra on the projected Yee cell) the drawn outline is used instead: E_z = 0 at the bisected wall distance along each centre link into the metal, and H_z takes the free lengths of its E_x / E_y edges over the free area of its dual cell (free fractions >= 0.02); links and dual cells crossing a pec / pmc / mirror wall plane stay staircased. On a triangles mesh the elements whose centroid lies in the selected domains leave the unknowns and E_t tangential and E_z are 0 on their outline, which the mesh follows (curved outlines isoparametric with discretization quadratic).

- FeatureSpec.type `pec_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

## Physics type `heat` - Heat Transfer in Solids

Anisotropic heat conduction (finite volumes on the rise T - T0; Automatic linear solver: multigrid PCG on the gpu backend and on 3D meshes, host SuperLU on the cpu in 2D, banded Cholesky in 1D, the sparse direct solver on triangle / tetrahedron meshes: a double cuDSS Cholesky on the gpu backend when nvmath-python is installed, host SuperLU otherwise or after a cuDSS refusal), 2D per unit z length or 3D (7-point stencil with k_zz; boundary features on outer faces x_lo ... z_hi only, no k_xy, no out_of_plane_convection; fields are shown as z cuts): steady state (quasi-static) or implicit-Euler transient (time_mode). Solves on the physical window only (no PML; T is copied edge-extended into an EM PML ring). Unreferenced outer faces are insulated (a later boundary feature on the same face wins), material properties are unset unless a material or its library entry sets them (cells without k do not conduct), and a steady solve needs an anchor: a temperature, h > 0 convection, a fixed-temperature domain or out-of-plane convection. With EM in a time-dependent study set every to a few hundred EM steps (one CG solve costs far more than an EM step; validation warns below 100). On a triangle mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles; 2D, planar or axisymmetric) finite elements of the discretization order (quadratic default) on the conducting window elements: object perimeters are their outline edges (temperature = Dirichlet there, convection = Robin, heat_flux = an edge source heating both sides), a point is its mesh node, field T is nodal (other fields and every state slot one value per element, T at the element centroid); no azimuthal_order, noise features or thermal_noise study. On a tetrahedron mesh (MeshSpec kind tetrahedra; 3D Cartesian) the same with Lagrange elements on tetrahedra (affine, diagonal k_xx / k_yy / k_zz): outer faces act on the window faces, object boundaries are their interface faces (temperature = Dirichlet, convection = Robin, heat_flux = a sheet source heating both sides), a point_heat_source is the exact point load at its (x, y, z), probes evaluate T at the point; fields are sampled on the uniform lattice of the mesh (field derived values are not available there yet); Automatic linear solver: sparse_direct (cuDSS on the gpu backend with nvmath-python; host SuperLU otherwise, ~1e5 unknowns P2 before its 3D size warning).

- PhysicsSpec.type `heat`; default instance name `heat`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent, thermal_noise
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): T
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `heat.<feature>`): temperature, heat_flux, convection, radiation, heat_source, point_heat_source, fixed_temperature_domain, out_of_plane_convection, initial_temperature, temperature_probe, thermorefractive_noise, particle_noise

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `time_mode` (choice; default "stationary"; choices stationary | transient) - Time dependence
  stationary: a steady solve at every heat step (quasi-static, no heat capacity); transient: implicit Euler with rho*cp in steps <= time_step. Only a time_dependent study runs transient heat: every other study (stationary, frequency_domain) solves the steady state (transient is ignored there); with EM in a time-dependent study each heat step spans every * dt_EM.
- `T0` (float; unit K; default 293.15; range (0, inf)) - Reference temperature
  Initial temperature of every cell and reference of the thermo-optic change n = n0 + dndT (T - T0). Cells that neither conduct, lose heat nor (transient, rho and cp set) store heat keep T0 (or their initial temperature) and ignore heat sources. Typical 293.15 K.
- `time_step` (float; unit s; default 0.001; range (0, inf); visible when time_mode in (transient)) - Time step
  Largest implicit-Euler step (the heat dt_limit). Heat alone steps by time_step (every must be 1); with EM each heat step is every * dt_EM, which must not exceed time_step. Implicit Euler is stable for any step but first-order accurate: keep it well below the diffusion time rho*cp*L^2/k of interest. T is the temperature at the end of the step just taken, so the heat time label and probe times run up to (every - 1) * dt_EM ahead of the snapshot time (the last may exceed the duration).
- `geometry` (choice; default "planar"; choices planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: 2D conduction per unit z length (W/m). axisymmetric: a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z): (r, z) conduction; every conductance, face and cell volume is weighted by 2 pi r (x-faces at their own r, y-faces and volumes at the cell-centre r; 2 pi r_c dr dz is the exact ring volume; object-perimeter heat_flux / convection likewise), so densities (Q W/m^3, heat flux W/m^2, h W/(m^2 K)) keep their units, a point_heat_source P is the ring's total power in W (on the axis cell a point source) and the 'integral' of Q the body's total power in W; k_xy is not available (validation error); out_of_plane_convection stays a volumetric loss h * sides / thickness; azimuthal_order m != 0 weights by pi r instead. x_lo is the axis (r = 0: symmetry, any feature there does nothing; validation warns). Field derived values of the whole model are weighted by the ring volume 2 pi r dx dy ('integral' a whole-body total, 'mean' a volume mean; also for fields of other physics). A coupled physics that is planar (its type has no geometry setting, e.g. EM, or it is set to planar) solves the drawing as a planar cut per unit z length, so its fields are applied per cell as rings (validation warns); a partner with geometry axisymmetric too is consistent.
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when geometry in (axisymmetric)) - Azimuthal order
  Help: shared `electric_currents.azimuthal_order`
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `k` (float; unit W/(m K); range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays k_xx, k_yy, k_zz) - Thermal conductivity
  Isotropic conductivity: sets k_xx, k_yy and k_zz (component entries override it; k_zz acts only in 3D models); unset (no library value) means 0, so those cells do not conduct. May depend on x, y (z in 3D) and state fields such as T (e.g. k_300*(300/T)**1.3; a stationary study then iterates). Typical: silica 1.38, silicon 130, aluminium 237, gold 317, silver 429, water 0.6.
- `k_xx` (float; unit W/(m K); range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays k_xx) - Thermal conductivity along x
  Conductivity along x; overrides k for this axis.
- `k_yy` (float; unit W/(m K); range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays k_yy) - Thermal conductivity along y
  Conductivity along y; overrides k for this axis.
- `k_zz` (float; unit W/(m K); range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays k_zz) - Thermal conductivity along z
  Conductivity along z (3D models only; a 2D model has no z conduction); overrides k for this axis.
- `k_xy` (float; unit W/(m K); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays k_xy) - Thermal conductivity, cross term
  Off-diagonal conductivity (cross conduction, e.g. a rotated anisotropic crystal); keep k_xy^2 < k_xx*k_yy (validation error for plain numbers). Needs a 2D Cartesian planar model (validation error otherwise); uniform or graded meshes. Cross heat flows only inside 2x2 cell blocks that all conduct (area-weighted mean k_xy of the block), never through the outer faces; the heat_flux_abs field includes it (block values averaged over each cell's blocks). On strongly graded cells keep k_xy^2 clearly below k_xx*k_yy: the discrete operator is guaranteed positive for k_xy^2 < k_xx*k_yy * 4 r_x / (1 + r_x)^2 * 4 r_y / (1 + r_y)^2 (r = width ratio of neighbouring cells; each factor 0.99 at r = 1.2).
- `rho` (float; unit kg/m^3; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays rho) - Density
  Density; used only by transient heat (heat capacity rho*cp). Unset = 0: no heat capacity, so transient heat treats those cells quasi-statically (conducting ones follow their neighbours, non-conducting ones keep their temperature and ignore heat sources; validation warns when heat is transient). Typical: silica 2200, silicon 2329, water 998.
- `cp` (float; unit J/(kg K); range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays cp) - Specific heat capacity
  Specific heat capacity; used only by transient heat (heat capacity rho*cp). Unset = 0: no heat capacity (see rho). Typical: silica 746, silicon 700, water 4182.
- `dndT` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays dndT_xx, dndT_yy, dndT_zz) - Thermo-optic coefficient
  Isotropic thermo-optic coefficient dn/dT: sets dndT_xx, dndT_yy and dndT_zz (component entries override it), read by heat_em_thermo_optic (n = n0 + dndT (T - T0)). Use the measured dn/dT of the free material: it already contains the density change of expansion; alpha adds only the growth of the structure. On a dispersive (Drude / Lorentz) material it shifts only the background permittivity, not the pole part (see heat_em_thermo_optic). Typical: silica 1e-5, silicon 1.8e-4, water -9e-5.
- `dndT_xx` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays dndT_xx) - Thermo-optic coefficient along x
  dn/dT of n_xx: em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz and em_modes use it for eps_xx; overrides dndT for this component.
- `dndT_yy` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays dndT_yy) - Thermo-optic coefficient along y
  dn/dT of n_yy: em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz and em_modes use it for eps_yy; overrides dndT for this component.
- `dndT_zz` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays dndT_zz) - Thermo-optic coefficient along z
  dn/dT of n_zz, the out-of-plane index E_z sees (eps_zz of em_fdtd_ez, em_fdfd_ez and em_modes); set by dndT, which this entry overrides. Without dndT and dndT_zz it is 0, so the E_z types see no thermo-optic change even when dndT_xx / dndT_yy are set. Typical: z-cut lithium niobate (dn_e/dT) 3.3e-5.
- `alpha` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays alpha_xx, alpha_yy) - Thermal expansion coefficient
  Linear thermal expansion coefficient: sets alpha_xx and alpha_yy (and alpha_zz when a solid_mechanics or solid_mechanics_3d physics is present, which turns alpha dT into thermal strain and stress through heat_solid_thermal_strain). heat_em_thermo_optic scales eps by (1 + alpha_xx dT)(1 + alpha_yy dT), i.e. n by about (1 + alpha dT): the in-plane growth of the structure on the fixed grid (dropped when solid_em_strain_optic maps the solid strain instead; a film clamped to a substrate grows with the substrate's alpha: library values are free-crystal, so override them, e.g. LN on Si 2.6e-6 instead of 1.5e-5). Per cell this is first-order, exact only for an alpha uniform over the mode. Leave 0 for liquids: their region is the container's. Typical: silica 5.5e-7, silicon 2.6e-6, gold 1.4e-5.
- `alpha_xx` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays alpha_xx) - Thermal expansion along x
  Expansion coefficient along x (see alpha).
- `alpha_yy` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays alpha_yy) - Thermal expansion along y
  Expansion coefficient along y (see alpha).

### Fields

State fields:
- `T` - Temperature (K)
- `Q` - Coupled heat source (W/m^3)
- `Q_ext` - Applied heat source (W/m^3)
- `k_xx` - Thermal conductivity xx (W/(m K))
- `k_yy` - Thermal conductivity yy (W/(m K))
- `k_zz` - Thermal conductivity zz (W/(m K))

Output fields (primary T):
- `T` - Temperature (K)
- `T_rise` - Temperature rise (K)
- `Q` - Coupled heat source (W/m^3)
- `Q_ext` - Applied heat source (W/m^3)
- `heat_flux_abs` - Conductive heat flux magnitude (W/m^2)

### Source slots

- `volumetric_power` (W/m^3): Heat source Q: each transfer replaces Q (copied; the PML ring is ignored) with the sum of the additive heating couplings (em_heat_joule, currents_heat_joule, fluid_heat_convection).

### Feature `heat.temperature` - Temperature

Fixed temperature (Dirichlet). On outer faces T is imposed at the face (half-cell conductance 2 k / dx); on object perimeters the boundary cells inside the object are held at T, imposed on their faces toward the free cells as on an outer face (the window edge is no perimeter: select the outer face there). Unreferenced outer faces are insulated, and a later boundary feature on the same face wins (validation warning); on cells held by two features the later one wins, and held cells ignore heat flux / convection (validation warns when their objects may overlap). Anchors a steady solve. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (2D) a perimeter holds T on the drawn outline instead (conductance k / (t d) along each link from outside, t >= 0.02).

- FeatureSpec.type `temperature`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `temperature` (float; unit K; default 293.15; range (0, inf); may use t) - Temperature
  Held at the selected outer faces (on the face itself) or in the boundary cells inside the selected objects. May depend on time t [s] (parameters and t only), re-set at the start of every heat step of a time_dependent study (the implicit step from t_n to t_n + dt sees the value at t_n; t = 0 in other studies). A temperature of t acts on outer faces only (validation error for objects in the selection).

### Feature `heat.heat_flux` - Heat flux

Prescribed heat flux, > 0 into the domain or the object. On outer faces a Neumann condition; on object perimeters it heats the boundary cells inside the object by flux * perimeter length / cell area (each exposed cell face weighted by its normal component, so slanted and curved perimeters get their true length to ~2 %). Does not anchor a steady solve. Polar / spherical domains weight each exposed face by its metric area. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (2D: Cartesian, (r, z), polar, spherical) the drawn outline is used instead: each cut cell feeds flux * its chord of the outline into the object cell owning it (exact for straight edges; arcs about a polar origin too), whatever the cut-cell volumes.

- FeatureSpec.type `heat_flux`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `flux` (float; unit W/m^2; default 10000; may use t) - Inward heat flux
  > 0 heats the domain (outer faces) or the object (perimeters), < 0 extracts heat. Typical 1e3-1e6 (sunlight ~1e3). May depend on time t [s] (parameters and t only), re-set at the start of every heat step of a time_dependent study (the implicit step from t_n to t_n + dt sees the value at t_n; t = 0 in other studies).

### Feature `heat.convection` - Convective cooling

Convective loss h (T - T_ext) per unit area. On outer faces a Robin condition in series with the half cell; on object perimeters the boundary cells inside the object lose h * perimeter length / cell area * (T - T_ext) (each exposed cell face weighted by its normal component, so slanted and curved perimeters get their true length to ~2 %), on top of conduction to neighbouring cells (polar / spherical domains: the metric face areas). Anchors a steady solve when h > 0. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (2D: Cartesian, (r, z), polar, spherical) on the drawn outline instead: each cut cell loses h L / (1 + h delta / k_n) * (T - T_ext) from the object cell owning it, L its chord of the outline, delta the distance from that cell centre to the chord, k_n the normal conductivity at build time.

- FeatureSpec.type `convection`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `h` (float; unit W/(m^2 K); default 10; range [0, inf)) - Heat transfer coefficient
  Help: shared `heat.convection.h`
- `T_ext` (float; unit K; default 293.15; range (0, inf)) - Ambient temperature
  Temperature of the surrounding fluid that the loss h (T - T_ext) drives toward; typically room temperature, 293.15 K.

### Feature `heat.radiation` - Surface-to-ambient radiation

Grey-body radiation to an ambient enclosure: a loss eps sigma (T^4 - T_amb^4) per unit area (sigma = 5.67e-8 W/(m^2 K^4)) from the boundary cells of the selected outer faces (their face area) and object perimeters (staircase perimeter weights, also under conformal_boundaries). It adds to the face condition (Convective cooling on the same face: both act; on a Temperature face it is pointless) and uses the boundary cell temperature (error ~ h_r dx / (2 k), h_r = 4 eps sigma T^3 ~ 5 W/(m^2 K) at 300 K). Newton-linearised at the current temperature: a steady solve re-linearises and re-solves until the radiating temperatures change by < 1e-7 (relative; at most 50 solves, then a run warning), a transient step uses the temperature at its start. Anchors a steady solve when the emissivity is > 0. On triangles / tetrahedra: a Robin term per boundary edge / face linearised at its midpoint / centroid temperature (each re-linearisation re-assembles and refactorises). No view factors or surface-to-surface exchange.

- FeatureSpec.type `radiation`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `emissivity` (float; unit 1; default 0.9; range [0, 1]) - Surface emissivity
  Hemispherical emissivity eps of the surface (grey body): oxidised metals and most dielectrics 0.8-0.95, silicon ~0.6, polished metals 0.02-0.1.
- `T_amb` (float; unit K; default 293.15; range (0, inf)) - Ambient temperature
  Temperature of the surroundings the surface exchanges radiation with (a large enclosure, e.g. the vacuum chamber walls).

### Feature `heat.heat_source` - Heat source

Applied volumetric heat source: Q is added to Q_ext on the selected cells (several sources add; the coupled source Q of em_heat_joule is separate). A steady solve ignores it on cells that neither conduct nor lose heat.

- FeatureSpec.type `heat_source`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `Q` (float; unit W/m^3; default 1e+12; may use x, y; may use t) - Power density
  Heat per unit volume; in 2D, Q times the area is the power per unit z length (W/m). May depend on x and y (3D models: also z); must be finite on the selected cells. Or (not both) on time t: May depend on time t [s] (parameters and t only), re-set at the start of every heat step of a time_dependent study (the implicit step from t_n to t_n + dt sees the value at t_n; t = 0 in other studies).

### Feature `heat.point_heat_source` - Point heat source

Line heat source along z (a point in 2D): P deposited in the cell containing each point; a coordinate exactly on a cell edge goes to the cell on its +x / +y side. Points outside the physical domain are an error.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_heat_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `P` (float; unit W/m, W axisymmetric, W 3d; default 1; may use t) - Power
  Planar 2D: power per unit z length in W/m (a 2D point is a line source along z), deposited in the cell containing the point (Q_ext += P / cell area; a point exactly on a cell edge goes to the cell on its +x / +y side). The temperature of that cell rises as the cell shrinks (logarithmic singularity of a line source). With geometry 'axisymmetric' P is the ring's total power in W instead (a point on the axis cell: a point source); in a 3D model P is the total power in W of a point source at the point's height (Q_ext += P / cell volume). May depend on time t [s] (parameters and t only), re-set at the start of every heat step of a time_dependent study (the implicit step from t_n to t_n + dt sees the value at t_n; t = 0 in other studies).

### Feature `heat.fixed_temperature_domain` - Fixed temperature (domain)

Holds every selected cell at a fixed temperature for the whole run (the cells leave the solve, heat flows in or out freely): an ideal reservoir whose temperature sits on its faces toward the free cells (half-cell conductance 2 k / dx of the free neighbour, whatever the held cells' own k, so a k = 0 sink still conducts); the heat_flux_abs field reads 0 inside it. Anchors a steady solve. With solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries (2D) the temperature sits on the drawn edge instead: conductance k / (t d) of the free neighbour, t d the distance from its centre to the edge along the link (t >= 0.02).

- FeatureSpec.type `fixed_temperature_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `temperature` (float; unit K; default 293.15; range (0, inf)) - Temperature
  Temperature every selected cell is held at for the whole run.

### Feature `heat.out_of_plane_convection` - Out-of-plane convection

Convective loss through the top / bottom faces of a thin slab (2D model of a membrane or chip layer): volumetric loss h * sides / thickness * (T - T_ext) on the selected cells. Anchors a steady solve when h > 0.

- FeatureSpec.type `out_of_plane_convection`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `h` (float; unit W/(m^2 K); default 10; range [0, inf)) - Heat transfer coefficient
  Help: shared `heat.convection.h`
- `T_ext` (float; unit K; default 293.15; range (0, inf)) - Ambient temperature
  Temperature of the surrounding fluid that the loss h (T - T_ext) drives toward; typically room temperature, 293.15 K.
- `thickness` (float; unit m; default 1e-06; range (0, inf)) - Layer thickness
  Out-of-plane (z) thickness of the slab the 2D model represents; the loss per unit volume scales as 1 / thickness, so thin slabs cool strongly.
- `sides` (int; default 2; range [1, 2]) - Cooled sides
  Number of cooled slab faces: 1 = one face (the other insulated), 2 = top and bottom.

### Feature `heat.initial_temperature` - Initial temperature

Temperature of the selected cells at t = 0 for transient heat. A steady solve uses it only as the starting guess and as the temperature of cells that neither conduct nor lose heat (validation info).

- FeatureSpec.type `initial_temperature`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `temperature` (float; unit K; default 293.15; range (0, inf)) - Temperature
  Temperature of the selected cells at t = 0; other cells start at T0.

### Feature `heat.temperature_probe` - Temperature probe

Temperature (K) of the cell containing the point, one sample after every heat solve (time-dependent study: every heat step; stationary study and the background stage of a frequency-domain study: one per fixed-point iteration, all at t = 0).

- FeatureSpec.type `temperature_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles, tetrahedra
- Result kind `timeseries`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `heat.thermorefractive_noise` - Thermorefractive noise

One-sided power spectral density of X = integral w(x, y) g(z) exp(-j q0 z) dT dV over the selected cells (thermal_noise study only; elsewhere the result stays empty): S_X(f) = 4 k_B T0^2 integral dq/2pi |g~(q - q0)|^2 Re sum conj(w) u dA, (j 2 pi f rho cp + k_zz q^2 - div k grad) u = w on the heat window. Assumptions: uniform temperature T0, z-invariant cross-section, dT of the isobaric (entropy) fluctuations only (pressure / Brillouin fluctuations and the sound speed are not modelled), dndT the measured isobaric coefficient. Held cells (temperature on objects, fixed_temperature_domain) and Dirichlet faces do not fluctuate; insulated faces act as mirrors. mode_pair / illumination: an em mirror face lies on the window edge (keep the heat face there insulated: the even mirror) and doubles the result (the whole mirrored cross-section counts); w = 0 on the ghost cells outside em pec / pmc wall planes, which keep the heat boundary condition of that face. Every selected cell with w != 0 needs rho and cp > 0 (infinite variance otherwise: validation and run error). mode_pair: X = complex amplitude scattered into the collected mode per incident amplitude, both modes normalised to 1 W, so S is the PSD of the scattered field in (power fraction) / Hz and |X|^2 the scattered power per incident power; a heterodyne beat with a local oscillator of power P_LO carries 4 P_LO P_in S per Hz of optical power squared. illumination: X = amplitude [W^0.5] scattered into the collected mode by the FDFD illumination as solved (its source amplitude sets the scale; g(z) multiplies it along the waveguide), S in W/Hz: the PSD of the collected scattered field; the static (mean) scattering of the structure is not part of it. Units of S: 1/Hz (mode_pair), W/Hz (illumination) or (w K m^3)^2 / Hz. Result: xy over the study frequencies, series psd (all selected cells combined) and psd_db (10 log10 psd). When the selection covers several materials, also psd_<material> (self term: w on that material's cells alone; psd_other for weighted cells in no material), psd_cross = psd - sum of the self terms (interference between materials, may be negative; its integral over all f is 0) and psd_<material>_db; a material name that makes two series collide is a run error. Extra keys variance (exact integral of psd over all f: k_B T0^2 integral |w g|^2 / (rho cp) dV, the equal-time variance of X), contribution_variances (the same per material, summing to variance), static_variance (the part of variance that never relaxes: at q = 0 the mean dT of a connected region without temperature anchor (no Dirichlet / h > 0 face, held cell or volumetric loss) is conserved, a delta at f = 0 outside every band; 0 otherwise), band_fraction (share of the relaxing part variance - static_variance inside the solved band, trapezoid in ln f), axial_wavenumber q0 [1/m], mirror_factor, axial_norm (integral |g|^2 dz [m]) and, for mode_pair / illumination, wavelength [m] and the resolved collected_mode (number), collected_n_eff, collected_te_fraction (and incident_mode). collected_selection te_and_tm solves both fundamental modes in one run: every series gets the prefix psd_te / psd_tm instead of psd (psd_te_<material>, psd_tm_cross, ...) and every extra key the suffix _te / _tm. Cost: one host SuperLU of the window per frequency, axial sample and collected mode (each material adds one back substitution).

- FeatureSpec.type `thermorefractive_noise`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `weighting` (choice; default "mode_pair"; choices mode_pair | illumination | expression) - Weighting
  mode_pair: X = amplitude scattered into collected_mode per incident amplitude (1 W modes of mode_physics, Lorentz reciprocity): w = omega eps0 / 4 sum_i 2 n_i dndT_i E_inc,i E_partner,i with the partner mode travelling against the collected direction (backward collection of a forward mode: E_t . E_t + E_z E_z of the same forward mode, i.e. |E_t|^2 - |E_z|^2; forward collection of the same mode: |E|^2, then X is the thermorefractive phase noise in rad), q0 = |beta_inc +- beta_coll|; n_i = sqrt(Re eps_ii) (eps_xx, eps_yy, eps_r = eps_zz), dndT_xx / _yy / _zz of the heat materials. illumination: the same with E_inc = the field [V/m] of illumination_physics (an em_fdfd_ez / _hz physics solving the same cross-section at k_z = 0, e.g. a gaussian_beam from the top): X = amplitude [W^0.5] scattered into collected_mode for that illumination, q0 = beta_coll, S in W/Hz (scales with the source amplitude squared). expression: w = weight (x, y), q0 = axial_wavenumber.
- `illumination_physics` (ref: physics name; optional (null allowed); visible when weighting in (illumination)) - Illumination physics
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.illumination_physics`
- `mode_physics` (ref: physics name; optional (null allowed); visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Mode physics
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.mode_physics`
- `incident_selection` (choice; default "collected"; choices collected | te | tm | number; visible when weighting in (mode_pair)) - Incident mode
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.incident_selection`
- `incident_mode` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when incident_selection in (number)) - Incident mode number
  Mode number (em_modes rank, 1 = highest Re n_eff) of the incident light when incident_selection is number; <= n_modes of mode_physics.
- `incident_direction` (choice; default "forward"; choices forward | backward; visible when weighting in (mode_pair)) - Incident direction
  Travel direction of the incident mode along z (backward: E_z sign flipped, beta -> -beta).
- `collected_selection` (choice; default "te"; choices te | tm | te_and_tm | number; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Collected mode
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_selection`
- `collected_mode` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when collected_selection in (number)) - Collected mode number
  Mode number (em_modes rank, 1 = highest Re n_eff) of the collected light when collected_selection is number; <= n_modes of mode_physics.
- `collected_direction` (choice; default "backward"; choices forward | backward; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Collected direction
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_direction`
- `weight` (float; unit 1/(K m^3); default 1; may use x, y; visible when weighting in (expression)) - Weighting function
  w(x, y): X = integral w dT dV (per unit z length times the axial profile); X has the units of w times K m^3, the PSD those squared per Hz. Evaluated at the cell centres; may depend on x and y.
- `axial_wavenumber` (float; unit 1/m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when weighting in (expression)) - Axial wavenumber
  q0 of the weighting phase exp(-j q0 z) along the waveguide axis; 0 = uniform along z.
- `axial_profile` (choice; default "uniform"; choices uniform | gaussian) - Axial profile
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.axial_profile`
- `interaction_length` (float; unit m; default 0.0001; range (0, inf); visible when axial_profile in (uniform)) - Interaction length
  Length L along z over which the weighting acts (uniform profile); the PSD scales with L.
- `waist` (float; unit m; default 1e-05; range (0, inf); visible when axial_profile in (gaussian)) - Spot radius
  w0 of g(z) = exp(-z^2 / w0^2) (gaussian profile); integral |g|^2 dz = w0 sqrt(pi / 2).
- `axial_points` (int; default 8; range [1, 64]; visible when axial_profile in (gaussian)) - Axial samples
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.axial_points`

### Feature `heat.particle_noise` - Diffusing particle scattering

Scattering spectrum of dilute particles (e.g. proteins) diffusing in the liquid on the selected cells (thermal_noise study only; hosted by heat for its noise solver, independent of the heat materials): one-sided PSD of X = integral w(x, y) g(z) exp(-j q0 z) dc dV, dc the number-density fluctuation of independent particles (Poisson, <dc dc'> = n0 delta, n0 = c N_A). S_X(f) = 4 n0 integral dq/2pi |g~(q - q0)|^2 Re sum conj(w) u dA with (j 2 pi f + D q^2 - div D grad) u = w on the selected cells, which the particles cannot leave (no flux through the selection edge or the window faces, which an em mirror plane shares). w is the mode-pair / illumination weighting of thermorefractive_noise with dndT_i -> dn/dc * M / N_A, i.e. the scattered amplitude of one particle at (x, y) (first Born / dipole approximation, isotropic polarisability, local field of the liquid). Lineshape: about D (q0^2 + 1/d^2) / (2 pi), d the evanescent decay length (BSA, q0 = beta: ~1 kHz). The coherent mean signal n0 integral w g exp(-j q0 z) dV (zero for a spot much longer than 1/q0) is not part of S. Not modelled: hindered diffusion near walls, adsorption / binding, particle interactions. Result: xy as thermorefractive_noise (psd, psd_db; prefix psd_te / psd_tm and key suffix _te / _tm with collected_selection te_and_tm) plus psd_single = psd / (n0 V_s): the time-averaged PSD of one particle diffusing within the sensing volume V_s = (integral |w g|^2 dV)^2 / integral |w g|^4 dV. Extra keys as thermorefractive_noise plus bound_signal_max (|w|^2 of one particle held at the strongest cell at the spot centre: the static signal of a bound particle, W or power fraction) at (bound_signal_x, bound_signal_y) [m], sensing_volume [m^3], particles_in_sensing_volume (n0 V_s), index_increment [m^3] and number_density [1/m^3]. Cost: one host SuperLU of the selected cells per frequency and axial sample.

- FeatureSpec.type `particle_noise`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `weighting` (choice; default "illumination"; choices illumination | mode_pair) - Weighting
  As thermorefractive_noise, with dndT_i replaced by the isotropic index increment per particle dn/dc * M / N_A: illumination: X = amplitude [W^0.5] scattered into collected_mode, S in W/Hz; mode_pair: X = amplitude per incident amplitude (1 W modes), S in 1/Hz.
- `illumination_physics` (ref: physics name; optional (null allowed); visible when weighting in (illumination)) - Illumination physics
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.illumination_physics`
- `mode_physics` (ref: physics name; optional (null allowed); visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Mode physics
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.mode_physics`
- `incident_selection` (choice; default "collected"; choices collected | te | tm | number; visible when weighting in (mode_pair)) - Incident mode
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.incident_selection`
- `incident_mode` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when incident_selection in (number)) - Incident mode number
  Mode number (em_modes rank, 1 = highest Re n_eff) of the incident light when incident_selection is number; <= n_modes of mode_physics.
- `incident_direction` (choice; default "forward"; choices forward | backward; visible when weighting in (mode_pair)) - Incident direction
  Travel direction of the incident mode along z (backward: E_z sign flipped, beta -> -beta).
- `collected_selection` (choice; default "te"; choices te | tm | te_and_tm | number; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Collected mode
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_selection`
- `collected_mode` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when collected_selection in (number)) - Collected mode number
  Mode number (em_modes rank, 1 = highest Re n_eff) of the collected light when collected_selection is number; <= n_modes of mode_physics.
- `collected_direction` (choice; default "backward"; choices forward | backward; visible when weighting in (mode_pair, illumination)) - Collected direction
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.collected_direction`
- `refractive_increment` (float; unit m^3/kg; default 0.000185; range (0, inf)) - Refractive index increment
  dn/dc of the particle in the liquid [m^3/kg] (1 mL/g = 1e-3 m^3/kg); proteins ~1.85e-4 (0.185 mL/g). With molar_mass it sets the index increment per particle dn/dc * M / N_A [m^3] (the excess polarisability alpha / eps0 = 2 n_liquid times it).
- `molar_mass` (float; unit kg/mol; default 66.5; range (0, inf)) - Molar mass
  Molar mass M of the particle [kg/mol] (= kDa); BSA 66.5.
- `diffusivity` (float; unit m^2/s; default 5.9e-11; range (0, inf)) - Diffusion coefficient
  Translational diffusion coefficient D of the particle in the liquid; Stokes-Einstein k_B T / (6 pi eta R_h). BSA in water at 20-25 C: 5.9e-11 to 6.1e-11 m^2/s.
- `concentration` (float; unit mol/m^3; default 1e-06; range (0, inf)) - Concentration
  Mean molar concentration c of the particles [mol/m^3] (1 nM = 1e-6 mol/m^3); n0 = c N_A per m^3. The PSD scales with c; psd_single does not depend on it.
- `axial_profile` (choice; default "uniform"; choices uniform | gaussian) - Axial profile
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.axial_profile`
- `interaction_length` (float; unit m; default 0.0001; range (0, inf); visible when axial_profile in (uniform)) - Interaction length
  Length L along z over which the weighting acts (uniform profile); the PSD scales with L.
- `waist` (float; unit m; default 1e-05; range (0, inf); visible when axial_profile in (gaussian)) - Spot radius
  w0 of g(z) = exp(-z^2 / w0^2) (gaussian profile); integral |g|^2 dz = w0 sqrt(pi / 2).
- `axial_points` (int; default 8; range [1, 64]; visible when axial_profile in (gaussian)) - Axial samples
  Help: shared `heat.thermorefractive_noise.axial_points`

## Physics type `laminar_flow` - Laminar Flow (2D)

2D incompressible laminar flow per unit z length by a D2Q9 lattice-Boltzmann method (TRT collision with the magic parameter 3/16, He-Luo incompressible equilibrium, Guo forcing) on the physical window, which needs a uniform mesh of square cells (no PML; outputs edge-extended into an EM PML ring). Cells with viscosity > 0 are fluid (they also need rho), the others solid no-slip walls (halfway bounce-back on their faces; with solver_defaults.conformal_boundaries interpolated Bouzidi bounce-back at the drawn wall position along each link); unreferenced outer faces are fixed no-slip walls. Steady flow is exact for Poiseuille channels and second-order accurate otherwise, valid at low Mach number (lattice Mach < 0.2) and laminar Reynolds numbers; a steady solve needs ~ L^2 lattice steps (L = longest window axis in cells), each a single GPU kernel (on the cpu backend its numba twin when numba is installed, else the far slower numpy twin: small models; half_storage stays GPU only). Outputs: the flow velocity u_x, u_y and its magnitude u_abs [m/s] (u is the velocity here, the displacement in solid_mechanics), gauge pressure [Pa], vorticity [1/s]. Couple it to heat with fluid_heat_convection; buoyancy is a field_transfer of heat T into body_force_y. The instance is usually named fluid.

- PhysicsSpec.type `laminar_flow`; default instance name `fluid`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): u_x, u_y
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `laminar_flow.<feature>`): wall, slip_wall, inlet_velocity, pressure, periodic, body_force, initial_velocity, flow_probe

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `time_mode` (choice; default "stationary"; choices stationary | transient) - Time dependence
  stationary: each solve marches the lattice to a steady state (re-solved only when a material, force or face changed; quasi-static, dt_limit inf); transient: one or more lattice steps per runner step (dt_limit = dt_lbm). Only a time_dependent study runs transient flow; every other study solves the steady state (transient is ignored there). Transient flow cannot share a time-dependent study with an FDTD wave physics (its femtosecond step is far below dt_lbm: validation error), nor with elastic_waves when the acoustic step gives the least viscous fluid tau < 1/2 + 1e-3 (3 nu dt / dx^2, e.g. water on 10 um cells; validation error, a warning below 1/2 + 0.02).
- `relaxation_time` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0.5, 5]) - Lattice relaxation time
  TRT relaxation time tau+ of the most viscous fluid: dt_lbm = (tau - 1/2) dx^2 / (3 nu_max), nu = viscosity / rho; other fluids get tau = 1/2 + 3 nu dt_lbm / dx^2. The lattice Mach number sqrt(3) u dt_lbm / dx must stay small (validation warns above 0.2 for numeric inlet velocities, the run warns above 0.2 and fails above 0.7): lower tau for fast flow, raise it (up to ~2) to reach a steady state in fewer steps. Steady results do not depend on tau (TRT with the magic parameter 3/16). Typical 1.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-06; range (0, inf)) - Steady-state tolerance
  Steady march stops when the remaining velocity change, extrapolated from the geometric decay between check intervals (rate r: change * r / (1 - r)), is <= tolerance * peak lattice speed on two checks in a row, or when the change stops decreasing below 1e-5 of the peak (float32 rounding noise, ~1e-7..1e-6: a tolerance below that floor stops there, never better). Typical 1e-6, error ~ tolerance.
- `max_steps` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Lattice step limit
  Lattice step limit per steady march; 0 = auto: 30 decay times L^2 / (pi^2 nu_lat) of the slowest diffusive mode (L = longest window axis in cells, doubled on an axis with exactly one slip / pressure face such as a free-surface film, halved on a periodic axis; nu_lat the smallest lattice viscosity), at least 10 of the largest check intervals (checks start every max(100, 3.5 L) steps and double while one sees less than 5 % of a decay). A steady march needs ~ L^2 lattice steps (a 500-cell axis ~1e6 steps). A march that hits the limit keeps its result and logs a warning.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `viscosity` (float; unit Pa s; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays viscosity) - Dynamic viscosity
  Dynamic viscosity mu of a fluid. Cells with viscosity > 0 are fluid; unset or 0 = solid (a no-slip obstacle: its boundary is a halfway bounce-back wall). Fluid cells also need rho. May depend on x, y and state fields (e.g. water 2.414e-5 * 10**(247.8 / (heat_T - 140)); a stationary study iterates). Typical: water 1.0e-3 (20 C), air 1.81e-5, glycerol 1.4, silicone oil 1e-2.
- `rho` (float; unit kg/m^3; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays rho) - Density
  Mass density. Heat: transient heat capacity rho*cp (unset = 0: no heat capacity, those cells follow their neighbours; validation warns when heat is transient). Laminar flow: required on fluid cells (kinematic viscosity viscosity / rho, inertia, pressure scale). Typical: silica 2200, silicon 2329, water 998, air 1.2.

### Fields

State fields:
- `u_x` - Velocity x (m/s)
- `u_y` - Velocity y (m/s)
- `u_abs` - Flow speed |u| (m/s)
- `pressure` - Pressure (Pa)

Output fields (primary u_abs):
- `u_abs` - Flow speed |u| (m/s)
- `u_x` - Velocity x (m/s)
- `u_y` - Velocity y (m/s)
- `pressure` - Pressure (Pa)
- `vorticity` - Vorticity (1/s)
- `body_force_x` - Coupled body force x (N/m^3)
- `body_force_y` - Coupled body force y (N/m^3)
- `viscosity` - Dynamic viscosity (Pa s)

### Source slots

- `body_force_x` (N/m^3): Coupled body force density along x (e.g. buoyancy), added to the body_force features; each transfer replaces it.
- `body_force_y` (N/m^3): Coupled body force density along y, e.g. Boussinesq buoyancy +rho g beta (T - T0) from heat T by field_transfer (g = 9.81 the magnitude, gravity along -y: warm fluid is pushed along +y); each transfer replaces it.

### Feature `laminar_flow.wall` - Wall

No-slip wall on outer faces: halfway bounce-back (the wall sits on the face), moving along itself at tangential_velocity. Unreferenced outer faces are fixed walls, and solid cells (no viscosity) are walls on their faces; a later boundary feature on the same face wins (validation warning).

- FeatureSpec.type `wall`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Requires a uniform mesh (see mesh)
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `tangential_velocity` (float; unit m/s; default 0; may use x, y; may use t) - Wall velocity
  Velocity of the wall along itself: +x on y_lo / y_hi, +y on x_lo / x_hi (a lid-driven cavity); 0 = a fixed wall. May depend on x, y (evaluated at the centres of the cells along the face). Or (not both) of time t [s] with parameters, re-set at the start of every runner step (t = 0 outside a time_dependent study; stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change).

### Feature `laminar_flow.slip_wall` - Slip wall (symmetry)

Free-slip face (specular reflection of the lattice populations): zero normal velocity and zero shear stress, i.e. a symmetry plane.

- FeatureSpec.type `slip_wall`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Requires a uniform mesh (see mesh)
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `laminar_flow.inlet_velocity` - Velocity inlet

Prescribed velocity on outer faces (moving-wall bounce-back with the face velocity, normal to the face; solid cells along the face stay solid). Combine with a pressure face elsewhere (validation warning otherwise: without one the inflow must balance the outflow exactly).

- FeatureSpec.type `inlet_velocity`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Requires a uniform mesh (see mesh)
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `velocity` (float; unit m/s; default 0.001; may use x, y; may use t) - Inflow velocity
  Normal velocity into the domain (> 0 inflow, < 0 outflow); with profile 'parabolic' the mean over each run of fluid cells along the face. May depend on x, y (evaluated at the centres of the cells along the face). Typical microfluidics 1e-4 - 1e-2. Or (not both) of time t [s] with parameters, re-set at the start of every runner step (t = 0 outside a time_dependent study; stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change).
- `profile` (choice; default "uniform"; choices uniform | parabolic) - Profile
  uniform: the velocity value per cell; parabolic: the value times the discrete Poiseuille shape s (w - s) of each run of fluid cells along the face, normalised to mean 1 (fully developed channel inflow, peak 1.5 x the value).

### Feature `laminar_flow.pressure` - Pressure

Prescribed pressure on outer faces (anti-bounce-back with the velocity of the boundary cell), an open inlet or outlet. The pressure field is gauge pressure: a model without a pressure face keeps a zero mean.

- FeatureSpec.type `pressure`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Requires a uniform mesh (see mesh)
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `pressure` (float; unit Pa; default 0; may use x, y; may use t) - Pressure
  Gauge pressure on the face (pressure is relative: 0 at an open outlet). May depend on x, y (evaluated at the centres of the cells along the face). Or (not both) of time t [s] with parameters, re-set at the start of every runner step (t = 0 outside a time_dependent study; stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change).

### Feature `laminar_flow.periodic` - Periodic pair

Periodic pair: both faces of one axis (['x_lo', 'x_hi'] or ['y_lo', 'y_hi']); the lattice wraps around. Drive such a channel with a body_force. Only the flow is periodic (heat and the other physics keep their own face conditions).

- FeatureSpec.type `periodic`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count exactly 2; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Requires a uniform mesh (see mesh)
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `laminar_flow.body_force` - Body force

Applied body force density on the selected cells (several add; held in the solver state body_force_x_ext / _y_ext, not an output field; the coupled slots body_force_x / body_force_y and their output fields are separate, e.g. a buoyancy field_transfer from heat T). Solid cells ignore it. The same feature as the solid_mechanics body_force.

- FeatureSpec.type `body_force`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `f_x` (float; unit N/m^3; default 0; may use x, y; may use t) - Body force x
  Body force per volume along x (Guo forcing); a pressure gradient dp/dx of a periodic channel is f_x = -dp/dx (an oscillating one, e.g. F cos(omega t), gives Womersley flow). May depend on x, y. Or (not both) of time t [s] with parameters, re-set at the start of every runner step (t = 0 outside a time_dependent study; stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change).
- `f_y` (float; unit N/m^3; default 0; may use x, y; may use t) - Body force y
  Body force per volume along y, e.g. gravity -rho g = -9.79e3 for water (a hydrostatic pressure gradient builds up against it). May depend on x, y. Or (not both) of time t [s] with parameters, re-set at the start of every runner step (t = 0 outside a time_dependent study; stationary flow re-marches to a steady state after each change).

### Feature `laminar_flow.initial_velocity` - Initial values

Initial values of transient flow: the lattice populations of the selected fluid cells start at the equilibrium of (u_x, u_y, pressure) at the cell centres instead of rest (several features: a later one wins its cells; solid cells stay at rest). The velocity should be divergence free (an incompressible flow): a divergent start relaxes through sound waves. A stationary flow only starts its first steady march from it.

- FeatureSpec.type `initial_velocity`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `u_x` (float; unit m/s; default 0; may use x, y) - Initial velocity x
  Velocity along x at t = 0 on the selected cells; may depend on x, y (cell centres). E.g. the Taylor-Green vortex U sin(k x) cos(k y).
- `u_y` (float; unit m/s; default 0; may use x, y) - Initial velocity y
  Velocity along y at t = 0 on the selected cells; may depend on x, y.
- `pressure` (float; unit Pa; default 0; may use x, y) - Initial pressure
  Gauge pressure at t = 0 on the selected cells; may depend on x, y. 0 is fine for slow flow (an inconsistent start pressure only launches weak sound waves that the viscosity damps).

### Feature `laminar_flow.flow_probe` - Flow probe

Samples the chosen quantity of the cell containing the point: stationary flow once per steady solve and at every stationary iteration (t = 0); transient flow after every runner step, at its end time.

- FeatureSpec.type `flow_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Result kind `timeseries`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "u_abs"; choices u_abs | u_x | u_y | pressure) - Quantity
  Field sampled: u_abs (flow speed |u|), u_x, u_y [m/s] or pressure [Pa].

## Physics type `magnetic_fields_ac` - Magnetic Fields, AC (2D)

2D time-harmonic magnetic fields (eddy currents) at one frequency (setting frequency), quasi-static: curl(nu curl A) + j omega sigma_dc A = J with nu = 1 / (mu0 (mu_dc - j mu_dc_loss)), phasors exp(+j omega t) of peak amplitude; planar A_z of currents along z, or axisymmetric the flux function psi = r A_phi of currents J_phi on the planar operator with coefficients nu / r (setting geometry), as magnetostatics. Solved on the host by one complex SuperLU factorisation of the finite-volume system (scipy required; solid conductors with a prescribed current add one bordered circuit row each); a later operator change (sigma_dc(heat_T), mu_dc) first tries GMRES preconditioned with the old factor, refactorising only when it misses. Fields: A, B (re / im parts and magnitudes; B from the complex face fluxes), J_conduction = sigma_dc E with E = -j omega A (+ v of solid conductors), J_total, q_eddy, q_magnetic and w_mag (time averages), J_applied, J_coupled. Faces default to magnetic insulation (A = 0); external_field holds the outer ring at a uniform applied field amplitude (phase 0, the phase reference of held values). No remanence (a permanent magnet is static: magnetostatics). A time-dependent study re-solves only when a material, a source or a held value changed. Fields are edge-extended into an EM PML ring. On a triangle mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles) complex finite elements of the discretization setting (P2 default, P1) solve for planar A_z or axisymmetric A_phi itself (not psi) in B-space, with the magnetostatics conditions on triangles (faces on the window edge, external_field on the window-edge nodes, fixed_potential psi / r on the element nodes) and the same coils, circuit rows, scalars and results; state fields are per element (A at the centroid, element means of B and the loss / energy densities; plots show A and B on the nodes); a solid conductor touching the axis is a run error (its applied field v / r is singular there). There the Automatic linear solver is a double cuDSS LDL^T on the gpu backend with nvmath-python (back_end 'auto' = 'cudss'; an operator change refactorises on the kept analysis instead of GMRES; a cuDSS refusal switches to host SuperLU with a warning), else host SuperLU. The instance is usually named magnetic.

- PhysicsSpec.type `magnetic_fields_ac`; default instance name `magnetic`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): B_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `magnetic_fields_ac.<feature>`): magnetic_insulation, symmetry, external_field, fixed_potential, current_source, coil, probe

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "planar"; choices planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  Help: shared `magnetic_fields_ac.geometry`
- `frequency` (float; unit Hz; default 50; range (0, inf)) - Frequency
  Frequency f of the time-harmonic solve (omega = 2 pi f, phasors exp(+j omega t), peak amplitudes). One frequency per build: sweep it with a parameter (each value refactorises). Skin depth delta = sqrt(2 / (omega mu0 mu_dc sigma_dc)): copper 9.3 mm at 50 Hz, 0.66 mm at 10 kHz, 66 um at 1 MHz; resolve delta with >= 3 cells near conductor surfaces. Quasi-static: displacement current neglected (sizes << the wavelength c / f).
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `mu_dc` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_xx, mu_dc_yy) - Static relative permeability
  Help: shared `magnetic_fields_ac.mu_dc`
- `mu_dc_xx` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_xx) - Static relative permeability along x
  Static relative permeability along x (axisymmetric: r), > 0; overrides mu_dc for this axis.
- `mu_dc_yy` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_yy) - Static relative permeability along y
  Static relative permeability along y (axisymmetric: z), > 0; overrides mu_dc for this axis.
- `mu_dc_loss` (float; unit 1; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_loss) - Magnetic loss (imaginary permeability)
  Magnetic loss: imaginary part of the relative permeability, mu = mu_dc - j mu_dc_loss (exp(+j omega t)); >= 0, unset = 0 (the array is allocated only when a material sets it). Dissipates q_magnetic = omega Im(nu) |B|^2 / 2 with nu = 1 / (mu0 mu). Tabulated data (mu', mu'') at the solve frequency: an expression of the swept frequency parameter covers a dispersive material. Typical: soft ferrite mu_dc 2000, mu_dc_loss 10 - 200 (rising with f); Metglas ~1e4 / 1e3 at 100 kHz.
- `sigma_dc` (float; unit S/m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_dc_xx, sigma_dc_yy) - Static conductivity
  Isotropic static conductivity [S/m] carrying the eddy and solid-conductor currents (out of the plane: magnetic_fields_ac needs sigma_dc_xx = sigma_dc_yy, else a run error); the same arrays as electric_currents, so a sigma_dc(heat_T) expression reaches both. Unset = 0 (no induced current). Ignored inside stranded coils (no eddy currents in a stranded winding; there it sets the wire conductivity of the coil resistance). Typical copper 5.8e7, aluminium 3.8e7, stainless steel 1.4e6, electrical steel 2e6 (laminations: use the stack value or a lower effective one), sea water 4.8.
- `sigma_dc_xx` (float; unit S/m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_dc_xx) - Static conductivity along x
  DC conductivity along x; overrides sigma_dc for this axis (magnetic_fields_ac: must equal sigma_dc_yy).
- `sigma_dc_yy` (float; unit S/m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays sigma_dc_yy) - Static conductivity along y
  DC conductivity along y; overrides sigma_dc for this axis (magnetic_fields_ac: must equal sigma_dc_xx).

### Fields

State fields:
- `B_abs` - Magnetic flux density amplitude (T)
- `B_x_re` - Magnetic flux density x (axisymmetric: r), real part (T)
- `B_x_im` - Magnetic flux density x (axisymmetric: r), imaginary part (T)
- `B_y_re` - Magnetic flux density y (axisymmetric: z), real part (T)
- `B_y_im` - Magnetic flux density y (axisymmetric: z), imaginary part (T)
- `A_abs` - Magnetic vector potential amplitude (T m)
- `A_re` - Magnetic vector potential (z; axisymmetric: phi), real part (T m)
- `A_im` - Magnetic vector potential (z; axisymmetric: phi), imaginary part (T m)
- `J_total_abs` - Total current density amplitude (A/m^2)
- `J_total_re` - Total current density, real part (A/m^2)
- `J_total_im` - Total current density, imaginary part (A/m^2)
- `J_conduction_re` - Conduction current density (eddy and solid conductors), real part (A/m^2)
- `J_conduction_im` - Conduction current density (eddy and solid conductors), imaginary part (A/m^2)
- `q_eddy` - Ohmic loss density (time average) (W/m^3)
- `q_magnetic` - Magnetic loss density (time average) (W/m^3)
- `w_mag` - Magnetic energy density (time average) (J/m^3)
- `J_coupled` - Coupled current density (A/m^2)
- `J_applied_re` - Applied current density, real part (A/m^2)
- `J_applied_im` - Applied current density, imaginary part (A/m^2)
- `mu_dc_xx` - Static relative permeability xx (1)
- `mu_dc_yy` - Static relative permeability yy (1)
- `sigma_dc_xx` - Static conductivity (S/m)

Output fields (primary B_abs):
- `B_abs` - Magnetic flux density amplitude (T)
- `B_x_re` - Magnetic flux density x (axisymmetric: r), real part (T)
- `B_x_im` - Magnetic flux density x (axisymmetric: r), imaginary part (T)
- `B_y_re` - Magnetic flux density y (axisymmetric: z), real part (T)
- `B_y_im` - Magnetic flux density y (axisymmetric: z), imaginary part (T)
- `A_abs` - Magnetic vector potential amplitude (T m)
- `A_re` - Magnetic vector potential (z; axisymmetric: phi), real part (T m)
- `A_im` - Magnetic vector potential (z; axisymmetric: phi), imaginary part (T m)
- `J_total_abs` - Total current density amplitude (A/m^2)
- `J_total_re` - Total current density, real part (A/m^2)
- `J_total_im` - Total current density, imaginary part (A/m^2)
- `J_conduction_re` - Conduction current density (eddy and solid conductors), real part (A/m^2)
- `J_conduction_im` - Conduction current density (eddy and solid conductors), imaginary part (A/m^2)
- `q_eddy` - Ohmic loss density (time average) (W/m^3)
- `q_magnetic` - Magnetic loss density (time average) (W/m^3)
- `w_mag` - Magnetic energy density (time average) (J/m^3)
- `J_coupled` - Coupled current density (A/m^2)
- `J_applied_re` - Applied current density, real part (A/m^2)
- `J_applied_im` - Applied current density, imaginary part (A/m^2)
- `mu_dc_xx` - Static relative permeability xx (1)
- `mu_dc_yy` - Static relative permeability yy (1)
- `sigma_dc_xx` - Static conductivity (S/m)

Scalar outputs: energy: time-averaged magnetic energy (1/4) Re(A^H K A) of the free cells (J/m planar, J axisymmetric); eddy_loss: time-averaged ohmic loss, the integral of q_eddy = sigma_dc |E|^2 / 2 over the conducting cells (induced and solid-conductor currents; stranded coils excluded) in W/m or W; magnetic_loss: (omega / 2) Im(A^H K A), the mu_dc_loss dissipation (W/m, W; the integral of q_magnetic only approximately at material interfaces); per enabled coil feature <coil>_current_re, <coil>_current_im, <coil>_voltage_re, <coil>_voltage_im, <coil>_resistance, <coil>_inductance, <coil>_power as its table result.

### Source slots

- `current_density` (A/m^2): Coupled current density J_z (axisymmetric J_phi; field J_coupled), a real amplitude at phase 0 added to the current_source and coil features; each transfer replaces it.

- `B_y` (float; unit T; default 0.0001) - Applied flux density y

### Feature `magnetic_fields_ac.current_source` - Current density

Applied current density amplitude J [A/m^2] at phase 0 on the selected cells, added to field J_applied_re (several sources and coils add; the coupled slot current_density, field J_coupled, is separate): planar J_z out of the drawing, axisymmetric J_phi circling the axis. May depend on x and y. It is an impressed current: conducting material under it still carries eddy currents (use a stranded coil for a winding).

- FeatureSpec.type `current_source`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `density` (float; unit A/m^2; default 1e+06; may use x, y) - Current density amplitude
  J_z (planar) or J_phi (axisymmetric) amplitude at phase 0; may depend on x and y.

### Feature `magnetic_fields_ac.coil` - Coil or conductor

Coil or conductor carrying a time-harmonic current. conductor 'stranded': many thin insulated turns, J = turns * I / area uniform over the selected cells (I = current at phase deg), no eddy currents in its cells (their sigma_dc is the wire conductivity of the coil resistance, times fill_factor); always current-driven. conductor 'solid': one massive conductor (turns ignored) with J = sigma_dc (v - j omega A) / r, the applied field v uniform over it (planar v = voltage per m of length; axisymmetric the loop voltage around the ring / (2 pi r)): drive 'current' prescribes the total current (one circuit row; the solve finds v, skin and proximity effects included), drive 'voltage' the loop voltage [V/m planar, V axisymmetric] (the solve finds the current). Its cells need sigma_dc > 0. Go / return pairs: two coil features with currents +I / -I (or phase 180). Result 'table': one row [feature, current_re, current_im, voltage_re, voltage_im, resistance, inductance, power] of the latest solve and the same extras: the complex current and loop voltage (stranded: R_dc I + j omega flux linkage), Z = V / I: resistance Re Z, inductance Im Z / omega, power Re(V I*) / 2; planar per m of length (A, V/m, Ohm/m, H/m, W/m), axisymmetric whole rings (A, V, Ohm, H, W). With several conductors each Z includes the mutual terms (for series +I / -I the resistances and inductances add to the loop values). Scalars <feature>_<key> carry the same numbers.

- FeatureSpec.type `coil`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `conductor` (choice; default "stranded"; choices stranded | solid) - Conductor
  'stranded': uniform J = turns I / area, no eddy currents in it; 'solid': one massive conductor with its own skin and proximity effects (circuit row).
- `drive` (choice; default "current"; choices current | voltage; visible when conductor in (solid)) - Drive
  Solid conductors: 'current' prescribes the total current, 'voltage' the loop voltage (stranded coils are always current-driven).
- `current` (float; unit A; default 1; visible when conductor in (stranded) or drive in (current)) - Current amplitude
  Peak current per turn (solid: the total current), > 0 along +z (axisymmetric: counter-clockwise seen from +z), at the given phase.
- `voltage` (float; unit V/m, V axisymmetric; default 0.001; visible when drive in (voltage)) - Voltage amplitude
  Solid conductor with drive 'voltage': peak loop voltage, in V per m of length (planar) or V around the ring (axisymmetric).
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phase of the current (or voltage) phasor in degrees; held potentials and the external field are at phase 0.
- `turns` (int; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when conductor in (stranded)) - Turns
  Number of turns spread over the selected cross-section (stranded only).
- `fill_factor` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, 1]; visible when conductor in (stranded)) - Copper fill factor
  Stranded only: conducting share of the cross-section; the coil resistance is turns^2 / (fill_factor area^2) times the sum of (path length / sigma_dc) area over its cells (0 where sigma_dc is unset: an ideal winding).

## Physics type `magnetostatics` - Magnetostatics (2D)

2D magnetostatics on the physical window (finite volumes, Jacobi-PCG): -div(nu grad A) = J with nu = 1 / (mu0 mu_dc) (planar A_z [T m] of currents J_z along z; c_xx = nu_yy, c_yy = nu_xx, since B_y = -dA/dx sees mu_yy), or axisymmetric the flux function psi = r A_phi of currents J_phi on the planar operator with coefficients nu / r (setting geometry). B = curl A (planar B_x = dA/dy, B_y = -dA/dx; axisymmetric B_r = -(1/r) dpsi/dz, B_z = (1/r) dpsi/dr) and H = nu (B - B_r) from the face fluxes averaged to the cell centres; w_mag = (nu_xx B_x^2 + nu_yy B_y^2) / 2. Every outer face is magnetic insulation (A = 0) unless a feature sets it; sources are current_source and coil features, the coupled slot current_density and material remanence; external_field holds the outer ring at a uniform applied field. mu_dc may depend on x, y and state fields (a stationary study iterates); a material with saturation_polarization (analytic) or a bh_curve (table) follows an anhysteretic B-H curve, solved by an Anderson-accelerated (or damped Picard) fixed point on ln nu (settings nonlinear_*; iterations in the study summary as nonlinear_iterations, an unconverged loop logs a warning). A time-dependent study re-solves only when mu_dc, remanence, a source or a held value changed. Fields are edge-extended into an EM PML ring. Scalars: energy and per coil flux linkage and inductance. On a triangle mesh (MeshSpec kind triangles) finite elements of the discretization setting (P2 default, P1) solve for planar A_z or axisymmetric A_phi itself (not psi) in B-space: B = curl A at quadrature points, H = diag(nu) (B - B_r) (no xx / yy swap there), saturating materials isotropic H = nu(|B|) B by exact-tangent Newton with an energy line search (nonlinear_method auto = newton); faces act on the window edge, external_field holds A_ext on the window-edge nodes (the whole window is free), fixed_potential holds psi / r on the element nodes, state fields are per element (A at the centroid, B / H / w_mag element means; plots show B and H averaged to the nodes), the energy scalar is the integral of H dB, and an axisymmetric radial remanence is allowed. The instance is usually named magnetic.

- PhysicsSpec.type `magnetostatics`; default instance name `magnetic`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): B_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `magnetostatics.<feature>`): magnetic_insulation, symmetry, external_field, fixed_potential, current_source, coil, probe

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "planar"; choices planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  Help: shared `magnetic_fields_ac.geometry`
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`
- `nonlinear_tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-06; range (0, inf)) - Saturation iteration tolerance
  Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_tolerance`
- `nonlinear_max_iterations` (int; default 100; range [1, inf)) - Saturation iteration limit
  Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_max_iterations`
- `nonlinear_method` (choice; default "auto"; choices auto | anderson | picard | newton) - Saturation iteration method
  Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_method`
- `nonlinear_relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 0.5; range [0.015625, 1]) - Saturation iteration damping
  Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_relaxation`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `mu_dc` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_xx, mu_dc_yy) - Static relative permeability
  Help: shared `magnetic_fields_ac.mu_dc`
- `mu_dc_xx` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_xx) - Static relative permeability along x
  Static relative permeability along x (axisymmetric: r), > 0; overrides mu_dc for this axis.
- `mu_dc_yy` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_yy) - Static relative permeability along y
  Static relative permeability along y (axisymmetric: z), > 0; overrides mu_dc for this axis.
- `remanence_x` (float; unit T; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays remanence_x) - Remanence along x
  Remanent flux density B_r [T] along x of a permanent magnet: H = (B - B_r) / (mu0 mu_dc), entered as face sources at the magnet boundary (exact for a uniformly magnetised region, also across its edges). Typical: NdFeB 1.2 - 1.4 T with mu_dc 1.05, SmCo 1.0 T, ferrite 0.4 T with mu_dc 1.1. Unset = 0 (the remanence arrays are allocated only when a material sets one). Axisymmetric geometry: not available (validation error; magnetise along z with remanence_y).
- `remanence_y` (float; unit T; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays remanence_y) - Remanence along y
  Remanent flux density B_r [T] along y (axisymmetric: along the axis z) of a permanent magnet: H = (B - B_r) / (mu0 mu_dc), entered as face sources at the magnet boundary (exact for a uniformly magnetised region, also across its edges). Typical: NdFeB 1.2 - 1.4 T with mu_dc 1.05, SmCo 1.0 T, ferrite 0.4 T with mu_dc 1.1. Unset = 0 (the remanence arrays are allocated only when a material sets one).
- `saturation_polarization` (float; unit T; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays saturation_polarization) - Saturation polarisation
  Saturation polarisation J_s [T] (> 0) of an anhysteretic B-H curve (magnetostatics only): the Frohlich-Kennelly curve B = mu0 H + J_s a H / (1 + a H) with a = mu0 (mu_dc - 1) / J_s, i.e. initial permeability mu_dc, B -> mu0 H + J_s in strong fields, no hysteresis. Tensor mesh: per axis the same curve with mu_dc_xx / mu_dc_yy and the cell-centre |B|, solved by a fixed point on ln of the secant reluctivity nu = H(|B|) / |B|, Anderson-accelerated (settings nonlinear_method, nonlinear_tolerance, nonlinear_max_iterations, nonlinear_relaxation); the energy scalar and coil inductances are then secant values ((1/2) A^T K A, flux linkage / current), not the integral of H dB. Triangle mesh: H = nu(|B|) B at every quadrature point (isotropic: mu_dc_xx must equal mu_dc_yy, validation error otherwise), solved by Newton; the energy scalar is the integral of H dB. Unset = linear (the array is allocated only when a material sets it); mu_dc <= 1 stays linear. Not combinable with a remanence in the same material (validation error); ignored by magnetic_fields_ac. Typical: iron 2.15, electrical steel 2.0, Metglas 0.6 - 1.6, Mn-Zn ferrite 0.4 - 0.5, NiFe (mu-metal) 0.8.
- `bh_curve` (table; columns H [A/m], B [T]; >= 2 rows, every column strictly increasing; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - B-H curve
  Help: shared `magnetostatics.bh_curve`

### Fields

State fields:
- `B_abs` - Magnetic flux density magnitude (T)
- `B_x` - Magnetic flux density x (axisymmetric: r) (T)
- `B_y` - Magnetic flux density y (axisymmetric: z) (T)
- `A` - Magnetic vector potential (z; axisymmetric: phi) (T m)
- `H_x` - Magnetic field x (axisymmetric: r) (A/m)
- `H_y` - Magnetic field y (axisymmetric: z) (A/m)
- `w_mag` - Magnetic energy density (J/m^3)
- `J_coupled` - Coupled current density (A/m^2)
- `J_applied` - Applied current density (A/m^2)
- `mu_dc_xx` - Static relative permeability xx (1)
- `mu_dc_yy` - Static relative permeability yy (1)

Output fields (primary B_abs):
- `B_abs` - Magnetic flux density magnitude (T)
- `B_x` - Magnetic flux density x (axisymmetric: r) (T)
- `B_y` - Magnetic flux density y (axisymmetric: z) (T)
- `A` - Magnetic vector potential (z; axisymmetric: phi) (T m)
- `H_x` - Magnetic field x (axisymmetric: r) (A/m)
- `H_y` - Magnetic field y (axisymmetric: z) (A/m)
- `w_mag` - Magnetic energy density (J/m^3)
- `J_coupled` - Coupled current density (A/m^2)
- `J_applied` - Applied current density (A/m^2)
- `mu_dc_xx` - Static relative permeability xx (1)
- `mu_dc_yy` - Static relative permeability yy (1)

Scalar outputs: energy: magnetic field energy of the free cells, (1/2) A^T K A of the discrete solution = integral of B^2 / (2 mu0 mu_dc) (J/m planar, J axisymmetric; with remanence the energy of B alone, not the magnet's co-energy; held cells and the external-field ring excluded, held-free faces count their free half cell; with saturating materials the secant value at the converged nu, not the integral of H dB; on a triangle mesh the integral of the energy density w(B) over the window elements outside fixed_potential regions, i.e. the integral of H dB also when saturating); <coil>_flux_linkage (Wb/m planar, Wb axisymmetric) and <coil>_inductance (H/m, H) of every enabled coil feature, as its table result.

### Source slots

- `current_density` (A/m^2): Coupled current density J_z (axisymmetric J_phi; field J_coupled), added to the current_source and coil features (field J_applied); each transfer replaces it.
