### Feature `magnetostatics.coil` - Coil

Stranded coil (many thin insulated turns): J = turns * current / area spread uniformly over the selected cells (area = their x-y, axisymmetric r-z, cross-section; skin and proximity effects need the solid conductors of magnetic_fields_ac). current [A] > 0 along +z (axisymmetric +phi). A planar coil without a return is a net current per m of depth that returns through the insulation faces; model a go / return pair as two coil features with opposite currents. Result 'table': one row [feature, current, turns, flux_linkage, inductance] of the latest solve and the same extras: flux_linkage = turns / area * integral of A over the coil (axisymmetric 2 pi psi: the flux through each turn) in Wb/m (planar) or Wb, inductance = flux_linkage / current in H/m or H (nan at zero current). For coils in series carrying +I and -I the inductances of the features add up to the loop inductance 2 W / I^2 (W the energy scalar); with several independent currents a coil's value includes the flux of the others (mutual terms). Scalars <feature>_flux_linkage and <feature>_inductance carry the same numbers.

- FeatureSpec.type `coil`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `current` (float; unit A; default 1) - Current
  Current per turn, > 0 along +z (axisymmetric: counter-clockwise seen from +z).
- `turns` (int; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Turns
  Number of turns spread over the selected cross-section (stranded winding).

## Physics type `magnetostatics_3d` - Magnetostatics (3D)

3D magnetostatics by the reduced magnetic scalar potential (finite volumes, 7-point stencil on the physical window of a 3D model): H = T - grad phi_m with T the coil fields, B = mu0 mu_dc H + B_r, div B = 0, solved for u = mu0 phi_m [T m] with the coefficients c = mu_dc per axis (mu_dc_xx, mu_dc_yy, mu_dc_zz; no cross terms) and the face drive w = mu0 T + B_r / mu_dc, so the face flux is B itself: B is taken from the face fluxes averaged to the cell centres (accurate in high-mu cells and iron cores too), H = (B - B_r) / (mu0 mu_dc) per axis, w_mag = sum of B^2 / (2 mu0 mu_dc) per axis (the density of the energy scalar, as in 2D; not B . H / 2 inside magnets), phi_m [A], J = curl T [A/m^2]. Every outer face is magnetic insulation (B.n = 0) unless a symmetry feature sets phi_m = 0 there; sources are coils, an external_field (held outer ring), ideal_iron regions at a potential and material remanence; with none of the anchors (symmetry face, ring, ideal iron) the type holds the window corner cell at 0. Saturating materials (saturation_polarization or a bh_curve, isotropic) run a fixed point on ln of their secant permeability, each iteration one assembly and one warm-started solve (settings nonlinear_*; 'newton' is not available on this grid); field mu_eff shows the assembled permeability. Scalars: energy and per coil flux linkage and inductance. The Lorentz force is not available yet (magnetostatics_3d_plan stage 4); eddy currents in 3D are out of scope. Linear solver: pcg (Automatic: multigrid on the gpu, host SuperLU on the cpu). A time-dependent study re-solves only when mu_dc, a saturation or a remanence changed. Fields are edge-extended into an EM PML shell. On a tetrahedron mesh (MeshSpec kind tetrahedra; 3D Cartesian) the same model by finite elements (setting discretization: quadratic or linear Lagrange phi_m on affine tetrahedra), solved by the sparse direct solver (Automatic: cuDSS on the gpu backend with nvmath-python, else host SuperLU; one factorisation per saturation iteration, cuDSS refreshing its plan): the external field holds phi_m on the window faces (no held ring: every element stays free and wins over face features there), the corner anchor is the window node nearest the lower corner, B, H, w_mag, J and mu_eff are element means (constant per element on the display), phi_m is the element field, energy and flux linkage exact integrals of the element fields; field derived values are not available on tetrahedra yet (use probes and the coil table). The instance is usually named magnetic.

- PhysicsSpec.type `magnetostatics_3d`; default instance name `magnetic`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): B_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `magnetostatics_3d.<feature>`): magnetic_insulation, symmetry, external_field, ideal_iron, coil, probe

  Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_max_iterations`

  Help: shared `magnetostatics.nonlinear_method`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `mu_dc` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_xx, mu_dc_yy, mu_dc_zz) - Static relative permeability
  Isotropic static relative permeability (> 0): sets mu_dc_xx, mu_dc_yy and mu_dc_zz (component entries override it); unset = 1 (vacuum). NOT the optical mu_r of the wave physics. Typical: air, copper, aluminium 1; ferrite 1e3 - 1e4; electrical steel 4e3; Metglas 1e4 - 1e5; mu-metal 5e4. The finite volumes solve a large contrast exactly; the pcg multigrid (Automatic on the gpu) keeps the iteration count moderate (a few hundred at 1e5). With saturation_polarization it is the initial (small-field) permeability of the B-H curve.
- `mu_dc_xx` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_xx) - Static relative permeability along x
  Static relative permeability along x, > 0; overrides mu_dc for this axis.
- `mu_dc_yy` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_yy) - Static relative permeability along y
  Static relative permeability along y, > 0; overrides mu_dc for this axis.
- `mu_dc_zz` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays mu_dc_zz) - Static relative permeability along z
  Static relative permeability along z, > 0; overrides mu_dc for this axis.
- `remanence_x` (float; unit T; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays remanence_x) - Remanence along x
  Remanent flux density B_r [T] along x of a permanent magnet: B = mu0 mu_dc H + B_r, entered as face drives B_r / mu_dc at the magnet faces (exact for a uniformly magnetised region, also across its edges). Typical: NdFeB 1.2 - 1.4 T with mu_dc 1.05, SmCo 1.0 T, ferrite 0.4 T with mu_dc 1.1. Unset = 0 (the remanence arrays are allocated only when a material sets one).
- `remanence_y` (float; unit T; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays remanence_y) - Remanence along y
  Remanent flux density B_r [T] along y of a permanent magnet: B = mu0 mu_dc H + B_r, entered as face drives B_r / mu_dc at the magnet faces (exact for a uniformly magnetised region, also across its edges). Typical: NdFeB 1.2 - 1.4 T with mu_dc 1.05, SmCo 1.0 T, ferrite 0.4 T with mu_dc 1.1. Unset = 0 (the remanence arrays are allocated only when a material sets one).
- `remanence_z` (float; unit T; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays remanence_z) - Remanence along z
  Remanent flux density B_r [T] along z of a permanent magnet: B = mu0 mu_dc H + B_r, entered as face drives B_r / mu_dc at the magnet faces (exact for a uniformly magnetised region, also across its edges). Typical: NdFeB 1.2 - 1.4 T with mu_dc 1.05, SmCo 1.0 T, ferrite 0.4 T with mu_dc 1.1. Unset = 0 (the remanence arrays are allocated only when a material sets one).
- `saturation_polarization` (float; unit T; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays saturation_polarization) - Saturation polarisation
  Saturation polarisation J_s [T] (> 0) of an anhysteretic B-H curve: the Frohlich-Kennelly curve B = mu0 H + J_s a H / (1 + a H) with a = mu0 (mu_dc - 1) / J_s, i.e. initial permeability mu_dc, B -> mu0 H + J_s in strong fields, no hysteresis. Isotropic: mu_dc_xx, mu_dc_yy and mu_dc_zz must be equal in the material (validation error). Solved by a fixed point on ln of the secant permeability mu = B(|H|) / (mu0 |H|) at the cell-centre |H| of each solve, Anderson-accelerated (settings nonlinear_*); energy and coil inductances are then secant values, not the integral of H dB. Unset = linear (the array is allocated only when a material sets it); mu_dc <= 1 stays linear. Not combinable with a remanence or a bh_curve in the same material (validation error). Typical: iron 2.15, electrical steel 2.0, Metglas 0.6 - 1.6, Mn-Zn ferrite 0.4 - 0.5, NiFe (mu-metal) 0.8.
- `bh_curve` (table; columns H [A/m], B [T]; >= 2 rows, every column strictly increasing; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - B-H curve
  Help: shared `magnetostatics.bh_curve`

### Fields

State fields:
- `B_abs` - Magnetic flux density magnitude (T)
- `B_x` - Magnetic flux density x (T)
- `B_y` - Magnetic flux density y (T)
- `B_z` - Magnetic flux density z (T)
- `phi_m` - Magnetic scalar potential (A)
- `H_x` - Magnetic field x (A/m)
- `H_y` - Magnetic field y (A/m)
- `H_z` - Magnetic field z (A/m)
- `w_mag` - Magnetic energy density (J/m^3)
- `J_x` - Coil current density x (A/m^2)
- `J_y` - Coil current density y (A/m^2)
- `J_z` - Coil current density z (A/m^2)
- `mu_eff` - Effective relative permeability (1)
- `mu_dc_xx` - Static relative permeability xx (1)
- `mu_dc_yy` - Static relative permeability yy (1)
- `mu_dc_zz` - Static relative permeability zz (1)

Output fields (primary B_abs):
- `B_abs` - Magnetic flux density magnitude (T)
- `B_x` - Magnetic flux density x (T)
- `B_y` - Magnetic flux density y (T)
- `B_z` - Magnetic flux density z (T)
- `phi_m` - Magnetic scalar potential (A)
- `H_x` - Magnetic field x (A/m)
- `H_y` - Magnetic field y (A/m)
- `H_z` - Magnetic field z (A/m)
- `w_mag` - Magnetic energy density (J/m^3)
- `J_x` - Coil current density x (A/m^2)
- `J_y` - Coil current density y (A/m^2)
- `J_z` - Coil current density z (A/m^2)
- `mu_eff` - Effective relative permeability (1)
- `mu_dc_xx` - Static relative permeability xx (1)
- `mu_dc_yy` - Static relative permeability yy (1)
- `mu_dc_zz` - Static relative permeability zz (1)

Scalar outputs: energy [J]: magnetic field energy of the free cells, the sum over faces of B_n^2 / (2 mu0 mu_face) times the face volume (held cells and the external-field ring excluded, held-free faces count their free half cell; with remanence the energy of B alone, not the magnet's co-energy; with saturating materials the secant value at the converged mu, not the integral of H dB); <coil>_flux_linkage [Wb] and <coil>_inductance [H] of every enabled coil feature, as its table result (secant values when saturating).

### Source slots

- none

### Feature `magnetostatics_3d.magnetic_insulation` - Magnetic insulation

Magnetic insulation B.n = 0 on the selected outer faces (z_lo / z_hi included; the default of every face no feature sets): field lines run along the face (Neumann on phi_m). It is the mirror plane of a field parallel to it, and stands in for a distant boundary far from the sources. Does not anchor phi_m: with insulation on every face, no external field, symmetry face or ideal iron the type holds the window corner cell at phi_m = 0 (the problem is then unique up to that constant; the corner cell reads B = 0).

- FeatureSpec.type `magnetic_insulation`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `magnetostatics_3d.symmetry` - Symmetry (field normal)

Symmetry (field normal) on the selected outer faces: phi_m = 0 there (Dirichlet), so the tangential H is 0 and field lines cross the face at right angles; the mirror plane of a field normal to it (the midplane between a magnet and its mirror image), or a face next to ideal iron. The opposite face kinds of 2D magnetostatics (there A = 0 is insulation): this type solves for the scalar potential. Anchors the solve.

- FeatureSpec.type `symmetry`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `magnetostatics_3d.external_field` - External magnetic field

Uniform applied flux density (B_x, B_y, B_z) [T], selection 'all' only, at most one per physics: the outermost window cells (all six faces) are held at the applied potential phi_m = -B . r / mu0 evaluated at their faces toward the free cells (r from the window corner), so a uniform field is exact on any cell widths. Inside, objects perturb the field; keep them several object sizes from the window edges (the ring holds the undisturbed field: error ~ (object size / distance)^3 of a dipole). The ring cells leave the solve (B, H read 0 there) and face features have no effect under it. Anchors the solve. Typical: the Earth field ~5e-5 T, a Helmholtz coil 1e-4 - 1e-2 T.

- FeatureSpec.type `external_field`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `B_x` (float; unit T; default 0) - Applied flux density x
  x component of the uniform applied flux density.
- `B_y` (float; unit T; default 0) - Applied flux density y
  y component of the uniform applied flux density.
- `B_z` (float; unit T; default 0.0001) - Applied flux density z
  z component of the uniform applied flux density.

### Feature `magnetostatics_3d.ideal_iron` - Ideal iron (fixed magnetic potential)

Holds the magnetic scalar potential phi_m on the selected cells for the whole run: ideal iron (mu -> infinity), H = 0 inside and B normal to its surface; the cells leave the solve (B and H read 0 in them). Two regions at different potentials drive the flux between them like the poles of a yoke (the magnetomotive force is their difference in A). The opposite of the 2D fixed vector potential (a flux excluder). Anchors the solve.

- FeatureSpec.type `ideal_iron`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `potential` (float; unit A; default 0) - Magnetic scalar potential
  Held phi_m [A] (magnetomotive force against phi_m = 0); 0 for a single iron region.

### Feature `magnetostatics_3d.coil` - Coil

Stranded coil (many thin insulated turns) wound around the axis 'x', 'y' or 'z' (setting axis) on the selected winding objects, e.g. a circle prism along that axis minus a smaller one (difference): every window slice normal to the axis that holds winding cells must close around a hole inside the window, else the build fails naming the coil. current [A] > 0 circulates counter-clockwise seen from +axis (B along +axis inside). The drive is the coil field T along the axis (T-Omega, H = T - grad phi_m): T = turns current / h in the enclosed hole, ramping to 0 across the winding by the distances to the hole and to the outside (uniform J in a circular ring), 0 outside; h = the winding's axial length. J = curl T is shown in fields J_x / J_y / J_z (its total through a half plane from the axis is turns current). Result 'table': one row [feature, current, turns, flux_linkage, inductance] of the latest solve and the same extras: flux_linkage [Wb] = the integral of T . B / current over the coil's support (the flux through each turn, summed), inductance = flux_linkage / current [H] (nan at zero current); with several coils a coil's value includes the flux of the others (mutual terms). Exact energy identity W = flux_linkage current / 2 for one coil with no held cells (no ring, ideal iron or symmetry face); held cells add their boundary term. Scalars <feature>_flux_linkage and <feature>_inductance carry the same numbers. With a core of mu_dc above ~1e3 in the hole, use pcg precision 'double' or 'mixed' (T - grad phi_m cancels to a few digits there; validation warns for 'single'). On a tetrahedron mesh T is held as edge integrals (lowest-order edge elements; the hole / winding / outside ramp from a fine lattice over the winding), so the current through the coil is exactly turns current and J is constant per element; the winding must be one piece along the axis and its axial length h is the extent of its elements.

- FeatureSpec.type `coil`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `axis` (choice; default "z"; choices x | y | z) - Coil axis
  Axis the winding circles; every slice normal to it through the winding must close around a hole inside the window.
- `current` (float; unit A; default 1) - Current
  Current per turn, > 0 counter-clockwise seen from +axis (B along +axis inside).
- `turns` (int; unit 1; default 1; range [1, inf)) - Turns
  Number of turns spread over the winding (stranded).

### Feature `magnetostatics_3d.probe` - Magnetic probe

B_abs [T] or phi_m [A] (setting component) of the cell containing the point (its z, mid-height when unset; a tetrahedron mesh: evaluated at the point), one sample per re-solve plus one at the end of the run (stationary: all at t = 0).

- FeatureSpec.type `probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra
- Result kind `timeseries`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "B_abs"; choices B_abs | phi_m) - Quantity
  Field sampled at the point: B_abs [T] or phi_m [A].

## Physics type `membrane` - Membrane

Tensioned film (the industry-standard membrane), optionally with plate bending (a tensioned Kirchhoff plate), time-harmonic (exp(+j omega t)): D (1 + j eta) del^4 w - div(T (1 + j eta) grad w) - rho_s omega^2 w = p, w the out-of-plane displacement [m], T the tension tensor [[tension_xx, tension_xy], [tension_xy, tension_yy]] [N/m] (film stress x thickness; material + the coupled_tension_* slots), D = bending_stiffness [N m] (unset: no bending), rho_s = areal_density [kg/m^2], eta = loss_factor, p = pressure [Pa]. Waves travel at c = sqrt(T / rho_s). 2D models on a triangle mesh (complex Lagrange P2 / P1, isoparametric on curved outlines; fem.harmonic; with D the C0 interior penalty plate form on P2: slope jumps between elements penalised, clamps hold dw/dn = 0 weakly); 1D models on line elements over the cells (Hermite cubic with D; a string / plate strip or the cross-section of a guide along y with the axial_wavenumber setting k_y: + T_yy (1 + j eta) k_y^2, with D also 2 D k_y^2 w'' and D k_y^4 terms). An element with no tension, areal_density or bending_stiffness is a hole (not solved; its outline is a free edge). Bloch cells: periodic_x / _y with bloch_kx / _ky on a periodic triangle mesh (eigenfrequency). Ports: exact semi-infinite clamped strip guides on outer faces with analytic modes (plates: numeric strip modes), incident modes and power fractions (frequency_response); mode_projection gives guide mode amplitudes along a film guide. Studies: eigenfrequency (resonances nearest target_frequency by shift-invert on the host, eigen solver role arpack_shift_invert; complex omega with Im > 0 for a decaying resonance, Q = Re omega / (2 Im omega) from the loss factor and the PML; one snapshot per resonance labelled "resonance k: f = <Hz> Hz[, Q = ...]", each resonance scaled to 1 m real at its peak dof; resonance_table feature) and frequency_response (the driven response to the pressure_load / line_force / point_force phasors at each frequency in Hz, one complex sparse factorisation per frequency on the 'linear' sparse_direct solver (back_end 'cudss' / 'cudss_mixed' on the gpu backend factorises on the device, triangle meshes only, its plan kept over the sweep since the pattern is fixed; Automatic / 'auto': cudss_mixed there when nvmath-python is installed, else host SuperLU, up to ~1e6 unknowns practical, 2e6 refused); one snapshot per frequency (study setting snapshots); field_probe, port and mode_projection record per frequency). Edges are free unless clamped (w = 0); clamped_line / simply_supported_line hold drawn line objects inside the membrane (zero-thickness walls, irises); symmetry / antisymmetry make faces even / odd mirror planes of a half or quarter model; squeeze_film_damping adds the gas damping of a thin gap under the film per resonance (eigenfrequency). PML (triangles): pml_<face> settings grow a ring of pml_cells x dx beyond those faces with a fixed complex stretch (fem.pml, set at pml_frequency or the eigenfrequency target / the first response frequency), outer side clamped; resonances with most of their energy in the ring are dropped. Fields w_re, w_im, w_abs, w_phase (nodal on triangles, cell centres in 1D), tension_xx / tension_yy / tension_xy (material + coupled), areal_density; state() holds w_re / w_im / w_abs per element (1D: per cell). The instance is usually named membrane.

- PhysicsSpec.type `membrane`; default instance name `membrane`
- Supported studies: eigenfrequency, frequency_response
- Default study: {"type": "eigenfrequency"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): w_re
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `membrane.<feature>`): clamped, clamped_line, simply_supported_line, simply_supported, symmetry, antisymmetry, pressure_load, line_force, point_force, field_probe, resonance_table, squeeze_film_damping, port, mode_projection

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Lagrange order of w: quadratic (P2, default) or linear (P1), on the triangles of a 2D model (P2 elements with an edge on a circle / ellipse follow the drawn curve, isoparametric) and on the cells of a 1D model (line elements on the cell edges). Resonance errors fall as (k h)^4 for P2 and (k h)^2 for P1 (k = 2 pi f / c, c = sqrt(T / rho_s)).
- `target_frequency` (float; unit Hz; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Eigenfrequency target
  Eigenfrequency study only: the resonances nearest this frequency are searched (shift-invert about (2 pi target_frequency)^2, moved 1e-4 above it so a target on a resonance still factors); 0 = the lowest ones, which needs a clamped boundary (a free membrane moves without strain at 0 Hz). With a PML it also sets the PML strength unless pml_frequency is given, so it must then be > 0. Ignored by frequency_response.
- `axial_wavenumber` (float; unit rad/m; default 0) - Axial wavenumber
  1D models only: w ~ W(x) exp(-j k_y y), the line being the cross-section of a membrane guide along y; adds T_yy (1 + j eta) k_y^2 to the operator, so a strip of width W clamped at both ends has the branches omega_n = c sqrt((n pi / W)^2 + k_y^2), c = sqrt(T / rho_s) (sweep a parameter for the dispersion; below the cut-off n pi c / W a guided wave of frequency f has imaginary k_y). With a bending_stiffness D the plate strip operator D (1 + j eta) (W'''' - 2 k_y^2 W'' + k_y^4 W) is added. 0 (default) = a line uniform along y (a string or a strip). A 2D model refuses a nonzero value (its y is drawn; use periodic_y with bloch_ky there).
- `pml_x_lo` (bool; default false) - PML on x_lo
  Triangle meshes only: a perfectly matched layer beyond x_lo. The mesh grows a ring of pml_cells x the mesh dx there (the MeshSpec pml_layers element layers across), its material continued from the window edge, with the fem.pml stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (d the depth, w the thickness); beta is set by pml_reflection for the fastest wave of the ring at the reference frequency omega_r (pml_frequency, else: eigenfrequency target_frequency, frequency_response the first frequency solved): c = sqrt(T / rho_s), with bending_stiffness D the propagating plate wave c^2 = (T + sqrt(T^2 + 4 D rho_s omega_r^2)) / (2 rho_s) (its evanescent partner needs no extra strength); its outer side is clamped (w = 0, with bending also dw/dn = 0). With bending the ring must resolve the boundary layer sqrt(D / T) like the window and needs one element layer per cell (MeshSpec pml_layers >= pml_cells; coarser layers reflect strongly, validation warns). Waves leaving through x_lo are absorbed: resonances get frequency_imag > 0 and a radiation Q, resonances with more than half of their energy in the layer are dropped as PML modes. Waves far below the reference frequency are absorbed less. Keep clamps, line forces and probes off x_lo; every physics sharing the mesh must ring the same faces.
- `pml_x_hi` (bool; default false) - PML on x_hi
  Triangle meshes only: a perfectly matched layer beyond x_hi. The mesh grows a ring of pml_cells x the mesh dx there (the MeshSpec pml_layers element layers across), its material continued from the window edge, with the fem.pml stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (d the depth, w the thickness); beta is set by pml_reflection for the fastest wave of the ring at the reference frequency omega_r (pml_frequency, else: eigenfrequency target_frequency, frequency_response the first frequency solved): c = sqrt(T / rho_s), with bending_stiffness D the propagating plate wave c^2 = (T + sqrt(T^2 + 4 D rho_s omega_r^2)) / (2 rho_s) (its evanescent partner needs no extra strength); its outer side is clamped (w = 0, with bending also dw/dn = 0). With bending the ring must resolve the boundary layer sqrt(D / T) like the window and needs one element layer per cell (MeshSpec pml_layers >= pml_cells; coarser layers reflect strongly, validation warns). Waves leaving through x_hi are absorbed: resonances get frequency_imag > 0 and a radiation Q, resonances with more than half of their energy in the layer are dropped as PML modes. Waves far below the reference frequency are absorbed less. Keep clamps, line forces and probes off x_hi; every physics sharing the mesh must ring the same faces.
- `pml_y_lo` (bool; default false) - PML on y_lo
  Triangle meshes only: a perfectly matched layer beyond y_lo. The mesh grows a ring of pml_cells x the mesh dx there (the MeshSpec pml_layers element layers across), its material continued from the window edge, with the fem.pml stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (d the depth, w the thickness); beta is set by pml_reflection for the fastest wave of the ring at the reference frequency omega_r (pml_frequency, else: eigenfrequency target_frequency, frequency_response the first frequency solved): c = sqrt(T / rho_s), with bending_stiffness D the propagating plate wave c^2 = (T + sqrt(T^2 + 4 D rho_s omega_r^2)) / (2 rho_s) (its evanescent partner needs no extra strength); its outer side is clamped (w = 0, with bending also dw/dn = 0). With bending the ring must resolve the boundary layer sqrt(D / T) like the window and needs one element layer per cell (MeshSpec pml_layers >= pml_cells; coarser layers reflect strongly, validation warns). Waves leaving through y_lo are absorbed: resonances get frequency_imag > 0 and a radiation Q, resonances with more than half of their energy in the layer are dropped as PML modes. Waves far below the reference frequency are absorbed less. Keep clamps, line forces and probes off y_lo; every physics sharing the mesh must ring the same faces.
- `pml_y_hi` (bool; default false) - PML on y_hi
  Triangle meshes only: a perfectly matched layer beyond y_hi. The mesh grows a ring of pml_cells x the mesh dx there (the MeshSpec pml_layers element layers across), its material continued from the window edge, with the fem.pml stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (d the depth, w the thickness); beta is set by pml_reflection for the fastest wave of the ring at the reference frequency omega_r (pml_frequency, else: eigenfrequency target_frequency, frequency_response the first frequency solved): c = sqrt(T / rho_s), with bending_stiffness D the propagating plate wave c^2 = (T + sqrt(T^2 + 4 D rho_s omega_r^2)) / (2 rho_s) (its evanescent partner needs no extra strength); its outer side is clamped (w = 0, with bending also dw/dn = 0). With bending the ring must resolve the boundary layer sqrt(D / T) like the window and needs one element layer per cell (MeshSpec pml_layers >= pml_cells; coarser layers reflect strongly, validation warns). Waves leaving through y_hi are absorbed: resonances get frequency_imag > 0 and a radiation Q, resonances with more than half of their energy in the layer are dropped as PML modes. Waves far below the reference frequency are absorbed less. Keep clamps, line forces and probes off y_hi; every physics sharing the mesh must ring the same faces.
- `pml_cells` (int; unit 1; default 8; range [1, 100]) - PML thickness (elements)
  Thickness of the PML ring in multiples of the mesh dx (h_max) on every pml_<face> face; the stretch profile wants the ring a fair part of the longest wavelength c / f there (6-12 typical).
- `pml_reflection` (float; unit 1; default 1e-06; range (0, 1]) - PML reflection
  Theoretical round-trip reflection of the PML for a normally incident wave of the fastest speed c of the ring (pml_<face>) at the reference frequency (beta = 3 ln(1 / R) c / (2 omega_r w)); oblique and slower waves are absorbed more in depth, less at grazing incidence. A very small value makes the profile steep, which the discretisation reflects instead: 1e-4 to 1e-8 typical.
- `pml_frequency` (float; unit Hz; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - PML reference frequency
  Frequency [Hz] at which the PML strength is set (fixed for the whole study, so a resonance pencil stays linear in omega^2). Empty: the eigenfrequency target_frequency, or in a frequency_response study the first frequency solved (put the lowest first for the strongest absorption over the sweep).
- `periodic_x` (bool; default false) - Periodic x
  Triangle mesh, eigenfrequency study only: x_lo and x_hi are one Bloch-periodic pair, w on x_hi equals w on x_lo times exp(-j bloch_kx L) (L = the window size along x, exp(+j omega t)); the mesh is built with matching nodes on the two sides (no PML ring on them). The modes come from the reduced pencil P^H K P, P^H M P (complex Hermitian; real when every k L is a multiple of pi) and are complex: w_re / w_im / w_abs show them. With bending the slope jump across the seam is penalised like any interior edge. Clamps, supports, line forces and ports must stay off the periodic faces; with every bloch_k 0 a cell without any clamp moves at 0 Hz: set target_frequency > 0.
- `periodic_y` (bool; default false) - Periodic y
  Triangle mesh, eigenfrequency study only: y_lo and y_hi are one Bloch-periodic pair, w on y_hi equals w on y_lo times exp(-j bloch_ky L) (L = the window size along y, exp(+j omega t)); the mesh is built with matching nodes on the two sides (no PML ring on them). The modes come from the reduced pencil P^H K P, P^H M P (complex Hermitian; real when every k L is a multiple of pi) and are complex: w_re / w_im / w_abs show them. With bending the slope jump across the seam is penalised like any interior edge. Clamps, supports, line forces and ports must stay off the periodic faces; with every bloch_k 0 a cell without any clamp moves at 0 Hz: set target_frequency > 0.
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when periodic_x in (true)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Bloch wave vector along x [rad/m], used only when periodic_x is on: the phase step exp(-j kx L) per period L; kx and kx + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. Swept through a parameter, one eigenfrequency study per k gives the band diagram (a strip clamped on two faces and periodic along the third: the guide dispersion f_n(k)). Typical: pi / L at the zone edge.
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when periodic_y in (true)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Bloch wave vector along y [rad/m], used only when periodic_y is on: the phase step exp(-j ky L) per period L; ky and ky + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. Swept through a parameter, one eigenfrequency study per k gives the band diagram (a strip clamped on two faces and periodic along the third: the guide dispersion f_n(k)). Typical: pi / L at the zone edge.

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `tension` (float; unit N/m; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays tension_xx, tension_yy) - Tension
  In-plane tension of the film [N/m] = film stress x thickness (sigma h; e.g. 1 GPa x 50 nm silicon nitride = 50 N/m), isotropic: writes tension_xx and tension_yy. The wave speed is c = sqrt(T / areal_density). An element with no tension and no areal_density is a hole (not solved, its outline a free edge); the coupled tension slots add to it. Negative (compressive) values make the membrane unstable (no restoring force): resonances with Re omega <= 0 are dropped.
- `tension_xx` (float; unit N/m; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays tension_xx) - Tension xx
  Tension component N_xx [N/m]; overrides tension along x (an anisotropic or coupled prestress).
- `tension_yy` (float; unit N/m; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays tension_yy) - Tension yy
  Tension component N_yy [N/m]; overrides tension along y. 1D models: the tension along the guide, read only by the axial_wavenumber term.
- `tension_xy` (float; unit N/m; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays tension_xy) - Tension xy
  In-plane shear tension N_xy [N/m] (unset = 0; the array is allocated only when a material sets it); the tensor [[N_xx, N_xy], [N_xy, N_yy]] should be positive definite. Ignored in 1D models.
- `areal_density` (float; unit kg/m^2; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays areal_density) - Areal density
  Mass per area rho_s = rho h [kg/m^2] (e.g. 3100 kg/m^3 x 50 nm silicon nitride = 1.55e-4). Unset = 0: with no tension either the element is a hole.
- `loss_factor` (float; unit 1; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays loss_factor) - Loss factor
  Isotropic structural loss factor eta: the tension becomes T (1 + j eta) (exp(+j omega t)), so a resonance has Q = 1 / eta (exactly Re s / (2 Im s), s = sqrt(1 + j eta)). Unset = 0 (the array is allocated only when a material sets it). Typical 1e-6 to 1e-3.
- `bending_stiffness` (float; unit N m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays bending_stiffness) - Bending stiffness
  Plate bending stiffness D = E h^3 / (12 (1 - nu^2)) [N m] (e.g. 250 GPa, 80 nm, nu 0.23: 1.13e-11 N m), adding D (1 + j eta) del^4 w to the membrane equation (a tensioned Kirchhoff plate). Setting it in any material (0 included) switches the whole physics to plate elements: Hermite cubic line elements in 1D (w and w'), on triangles the C0 interior penalty form on quadratic elements (discretization quadratic; a PML stretches the plate form too; a port on a face with D > 0 takes the numeric plate strip modes; mode_projection is refused). Then clamped also holds the slope dw/dn = 0, simply_supported (and antisymmetry) holds w only, symmetry the slope only. The clamped boundary layer sqrt(D / T) (0.38 um for the example at 80 N/m) must be resolved by the mesh near clamps.
- `plate_poisson_ratio` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays plate_poisson_ratio) - Plate Poisson ratio
  Poisson ratio nu of the plate bending moments M = D [(1 - nu) H(w) + nu tr H(w) I] (triangle meshes; unset = 0). It changes free and simply supported plate edges only (the moment there), not clamped ones or the interior equation; D already holds its 1 / (1 - nu^2). 1D models ignore it (exact for clamped and simply supported ends). Must lie in (-1, 0.5].

### Fields

State fields:
- `w_re` - Out-of-plane displacement (real part) (m)
- `w_im` - Out-of-plane displacement (imaginary part) (m)
- `w_abs` - Out-of-plane displacement amplitude (m)

Output fields (primary w_re):
- `w_re` - Out-of-plane displacement (real part) (m)
- `w_im` - Out-of-plane displacement (imaginary part) (m)
- `w_abs` - Out-of-plane displacement amplitude (m)
- `w_phase` - Out-of-plane displacement phase (rad)
- `tension_xx` - Tension xx (N/m)
- `tension_yy` - Tension yy (N/m)
- `tension_xy` - Tension xy (N/m)
- `areal_density` - Areal density (kg/m^2)

### Source slots

- `coupled_tension_xx` (N/m): Coupled tension N_xx per element (1D: per cell), e.g. the relaxed prestress h sigma_xx of a solid; added to the material tension_xx; each transfer replaces it.
- `coupled_tension_yy` (N/m): Coupled tension N_yy, as coupled_tension_xx.
- `coupled_tension_xy` (N/m): Coupled shear tension N_xy, as coupled_tension_xx (ignored in 1D models).

### Feature `membrane.clamped` - Clamped

w = 0 on the selected outer faces (the window edge) and object outlines (triangle meshes; a 1D model: its ends x_lo / x_hi); with a bending_stiffness also the slope dw/dn = 0 (1D: w' = 0; triangles: weakly, Nitsche, on each side of an outline). Edges without a clamp are free (zero transverse force and moment). A clamp beats a line force on the same face; not on a periodic face. Line objects (a zero-thickness iris or wall): clamped_line.

- FeatureSpec.type `clamped`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `membrane.clamped_line` - Clamped line

w = 0 on the mesh edges of the selected line objects (triangle meshes: the mesher puts element edges on every line; any direction, the part inside the window); with a bending_stiffness also dw/dn = 0 weakly (Nitsche) on each side of the line. The two sides stay one membrane otherwise: a line across a strip splits it into two clamped strips. Validation warns for a line end on a periodic side (unless the line spans the period: its image must be held too) and for a line reaching beyond the window.

- FeatureSpec.type `clamped_line`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `membrane.simply_supported_line` - Simply supported line

w = 0 on the mesh edges of the selected line objects (triangle meshes, as clamped_line), the slope free: with a bending_stiffness the slope stays continuous across the line (the interior penalty acts there as on any interior edge: a line support of a continuous plate). Without bending_stiffness the same as clamped_line.

- FeatureSpec.type `simply_supported_line`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `membrane.simply_supported` - Simply supported

w = 0 on the selected outer faces and object outlines (1D: the ends), the slope free (zero bending moment: M_nn = 0 with plate_poisson_ratio). Without bending_stiffness the same as clamped. Not on a periodic face. Line objects: simply_supported_line.

- FeatureSpec.type `simply_supported`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `membrane.symmetry` - Symmetry

Even mirror plane: w(mirrored) = w. A film: the free edge (T dw/dn = 0, nothing is held; needs tension_xy = 0 there, as a mirrored shear tension changes sign). With a bending_stiffness: the slope dw/dn = 0 (1D: w' = 0; triangles: weakly, Nitsche, as a clamp) with w free and zero transverse shear. On outer faces (1D: x_lo / x_hi) and straight object outlines; not on a PML or periodic face. A face also held by clamped / simply_supported / antisymmetry is held (warning). With the antisymmetry feature on the same plane in a second run it gives every mode of the full structure: the even modes here, the odd ones there. A port or mode_projection guide ending on a symmetry face takes that wall as free (half-guide profiles, see port). Its outer faces are model mirror planes (core.mirror): fields unfold w even across them, integrals touching them count twice (the unfolded structure), and the study setting parity_sectors swaps symmetry / antisymmetry on them per sector run.

- FeatureSpec.type `symmetry`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `membrane.antisymmetry` - Antisymmetry

Odd mirror plane: w(mirrored) = -w. w = 0 on the selected faces, the slope free (with a bending_stiffness: zero bending moment M_nn = 0), the same hold as simply_supported. On outer faces (1D: x_lo / x_hi) and straight object outlines; not on a PML or periodic face. Its outer faces are model mirror planes (core.mirror): fields unfold w odd across them, integrals touching them count twice, parity_sectors swaps the feature per sector run. A squeeze_film_damping film vents on its faces (odd pressure).

- FeatureSpec.type `antisymmetry`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

Complex pressure p e^(j phase) [Pa] on the selected elements (cells in 1D), int p v dA; read by the frequency_response study only.

Complex transverse force per length F e^(j phase) [N/m] on the selected outer faces (the window edge) and object outlines (both sides of an interior outline share it); a 1D model: at its ends. Read by the frequency_response study only; not on a PML face.

Complex transverse point force F e^(j phase) [N] at each selected point (exact delta load of the element holding it); 1D models: a line across the strip, N/m. Read by the frequency_response study only.

Result 'xy' versus frequency [Hz]: series w_re, w_im, w_abs [m] and w_phase [rad] (a repeated frequency replaces its sample); a two_wave_fit derived value pairs w_re with w_im, a lorentz_fit of w_abs*w_abs gives the quality factor. Frequency response only.

### Feature `membrane.resonance_table` - Resonance table

Resonances of the last eigenfrequency solve, nearest target_frequency first. Result 'table' with columns resonance_number, frequency [Hz], frequency_imag [Hz, > 0 decays], q_factor (inf when lossless), pml_fraction (energy share in the PML); extras target_frequency, selected_resonance. For a frequency versus a parameter add a derived value with source '<physics>.<this feature>', expression frequency, operation at and at = 0. With squeeze_film_damping features (triangle meshes) the table appends gas_damping, gas_stiffness, gamma_gas, q_gas: the totals of every enabled film (c, k and gamma add over the films; see that feature).

- FeatureSpec.type `resonance_table`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `membrane.squeeze_film_damping` - Squeeze-film damping

Gas damping of a thin film (gap H) between the selected membrane domains (the footprint) and a fixed parallel wall, evaluated per resonance after the eigenfrequency solve (triangle meshes; it does not change the modes; c and k are quadratic in w, so the side of the wall does not matter). On the footprint elements (holes excluded) the linearised compressible Reynolds equation div(H^3 / (12 mu_eff) grad p) - j omega (H / p_a) p = j omega w is solved per mode on the membrane's own elements and order (fem.squeeze_film), w the mode shape (peak 1 m), p = 0 on vented footprint edges (vents), no flux on sealed ones. Result 'table', one row per mode: resonance_number, frequency [Hz], effective_mass [kg], per mode for the mode shape of the eigenfrequency study (peak |w| = 1 m): gas_damping c = -Re F [kg/s] and gas_stiffness k = omega Im F [N/m] of the modal gas force F = int p conj(w) dA per unit modal velocity (both scale with the square of the shape normalisation), gamma_gas = c / m_eff [1/s] (the energy decay rate, the linewidth in rad/s) and q_gas = omega m_eff / c, with m_eff = int rho_s |w|^2 dA of the same shape (independent of it); extras area [m^2], gap [m], film_elements, vent_edges. The Resonance table appends the totals over every enabled film. Complex modes (PML, loss) use Re omega and m_eff = Re(w^H M w). Refused: Bloch cells, a footprint reaching a PML ring (build error), 1D models. Only the eigenfrequency study evaluates it (a frequency_response is not damped by it).

- FeatureSpec.type `squeeze_film_damping`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `gap` (float; unit m; default 2e-06; range (0, inf)) - Gap height
  Help: shared `membrane.squeeze_film_damping.gap`
- `viscosity` (float; unit Pa s; default 1.81e-05; range (0, inf)) - Gas viscosity
  Dynamic viscosity mu of the gas [Pa s] (air at 20 C: 1.81e-5), independent of pressure; slip reduces it to mu_eff in the gap.
- `ambient_pressure` (float; unit Pa; default 101325; range [0, inf)) - Ambient pressure
  Help: shared `membrane.squeeze_film_damping.ambient_pressure`
- `slip` (choice; default "veijola"; choices none | veijola) - Gas slip
  Help: shared `membrane.squeeze_film_damping.slip`
- `mean_free_path` (float; unit m; default 6.8e-08; range [0, inf); visible when slip in (veijola)) - Mean free path
  Help: shared `membrane.squeeze_film_damping.mean_free_path`
- `vents` (choice; default "open_edges"; choices open_edges | all | none) - Vented edges
  Which footprint boundary edges vent to the ambient (p = 0; the others are sealed, no gas flux). open_edges: free edges, hole outlines, footprint edges inside the membrane and antisymmetry faces (odd pressure) vent; window edges of clamped / simply_supported / symmetry faces, symmetry outlines and held edges with membrane on both sides (clamped_line / simply_supported_line, clamped / supported object outlines inside the film) are sealed (a clamped outline with a hole outside vents as a hole outline). all: every footprint edge vents; none: a closed film (needs ambient_pressure > 0: a trapped gas spring). Holes vent without the flow resistance of a perforation.

### Feature `membrane.port` - Port

Exact semi-infinite termination of a straight clamped strip guide on one outer face (triangle meshes, frequency_response only; a plate face: last paragraph): the analytic profiles sin(n pi s / W) (s from the first wall, W = the span of membrane elements on the face, clamped at both ends) with beta_n^2 = (rho_s omega^2 - T_ss (n pi / W)^2) / T_nn, Im beta <= 0, give the Dirichlet-to-Neumann term sum_n j beta_n T_nn (2 / W) (int phi_n w)(int phi_n v) per mode (no numeric mode solve); incident_mode m > 0 adds the load of A phi_m entering. A guide wall on a window face with the symmetry feature (and no hold there) is a free mirror wall: phi_n = sin(k_n s) (free at s = W) or cos(k_n s) (free at s = 0), k_n = (n - 1/2) pi / W in beta_n, i.e. the even modes 2n - 1 of the unfolded guide of width 2 W (same amplitudes; powers and power_fraction of the half; the incident mode 1 of the full guide is mode 1 here); symmetry on both walls is refused. The guide must be uniform at the face (density and loss to 1e-6; the tension and tension_xy to tension_tolerance, the mean tension of the port elements being used) and not ringed by a PML. Result 'xy' versus frequency [Hz]: per mode the outgoing amplitude b_n = a_n - A delta_nm at the face (series mode_<n>_re / _im / _abs [m], _phase [rad]), power_<n> = W omega Re(T_nn beta_n) |b_n|^2 / 4 [W] and power_fraction_<n> = power_<n> / incident_power (the incident power of every port; NaN without one), and incident_power [W]. Lossless: the outgoing powers of all ports sum to the incident power (transmission T and reflection R). Extras: tension_spread (the relative tension spread measured at the face), tension_tolerance, medium_warning (text when the spread exceeds 1e-6 but is accepted; else empty), free_walls ([at s = 0, at s = W]; None before a solve). A guide wall on a symmetry / antisymmetry face (a mirror wall): incident modes are numbered on the unfolded guide (see incident_mode; incident_modes for several), powers are those of the unfolded guide (x 2 per mirror wall; fractions unchanged), and the extras mirror_walls (+1 symmetry, -1 antisymmetry, None per wall), sector_modes / sector_signs (the unfolded number and sign of each half mode: a symmetry wall 2k - 1, an antisymmetry wall 2k, signed (-1)^(k-1) / (-1)^k when the wall is at s = 0) and sector_drive_scale give the parity_sectors combination (Results.sector_result(..., combined=True): unfolded modes, recomputed powers and fractions); series port_incident_power = this port's own incident power [W]. Plate port (bending_stiffness > 0 at the port elements, D and plate_poisson_ratio uniform there to 1e-6): the guide modes are computed per frequency from a Hermite cubic strip on the port's edge nodes (D (1 + j eta), T_nn, T_ss, rho_s, nu; walls from the holds: a clamped face / outline holds w and dw/ds, simply_supported / antisymmetry w, symmetry dw/ds, an unheld face or hole outline is a free plate edge), the quadratic eigenproblem in beta^2 solved densely (2 per free strip dof), Im beta <= 0, numbered by cut-off (Re beta^2 descending), profiles scaled to peak |w| 1 with the first lobe positive. The port absorbs all of them: the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of the strip (effective shear V_n against w, moment M_nn against dw/dn; complex symmetric by reciprocity) on every quadratic dof of the port elements. b_n = the outgoing amplitudes from the (w, dw/dn) traces, power_<n> = the modal energy flux (omega / 2) Im(V_n conj(w) + M_n conj(dw/dn)) (lossless: exact balance), series as above. Extras plate_walls (the wall kinds; None for a film port), sector_modes / sector_signs None (no parity_sectors combination: a plate port on a guide ending on a mirror face is refused under parity_sectors); mirror walls still double the powers.

- FeatureSpec.type `port`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count exactly 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `mode_count` (int; unit 1; default 10; range [1, 200]) - Modes
  Number n of strip modes phi_n (sin(n pi s / W); with a symmetry wall sin / cos((n - 1/2) pi s / W), see the feature description) the port absorbs exactly (Dirichlet-to-Neumann per mode, propagating and evanescent); higher modes see a free edge, so keep the port where their near field has decayed (exp(-n pi d / W)) or raise the count. W = the span of membrane elements along the face. A plate port (bending_stiffness > 0 at the face) absorbs every numeric strip mode of its cross-section (two per free strip dof); there mode_count is the number of modes reported and allowed as incident modes, numbered by cut-off (Re beta^2 descending: propagating modes first, then by decay; a plate guide has a second, bending-dominated evanescent family that comes late), and it must cover the propagating modes for the power balance.
- `incident_mode` (int; unit 1; default 0; range [0, 400]) - Incident mode
  Mode number m sent into the domain through this port (0 = none: the port only absorbs). Its amplitude below is the incident w profile amplitude at the port face. On a guide with a wall on a symmetry / antisymmetry face, m is numbered on the unfolded (full-width) guide: a symmetry wall admits the odd m (half mode (m + 1) / 2), an antisymmetry wall the even m (half mode m / 2); a mode of the other parity is a build error unless the study runs parity_sectors (each mode then in the run of its parity). A plate port numbers its modes on the drawn guide (by cut-off, see mode_count), also on a half guide, and has no parity_sectors combination.
- `amplitude` (float; unit m; default 1e-09) - Incident amplitude
  Amplitude A [m] of the incident mode A phi_m(s) at the port face, at the phase below.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phase of the drive phasor in degrees (exp(+j omega t)).
- `incident_modes` (float_list; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Incident modes
  Several incident modes at once (whole numbers, numbered as incident_mode); a non-empty list replaces incident_mode. Their amplitudes / phases: incident_amplitudes / incident_phases (one entry per mode; empty: amplitude / phase for each). Modes of both parities about a mirror wall (e.g. 1 and 2 on a half guide) need the study setting parity_sectors.
- `incident_amplitudes` (float_list; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Incident amplitudes
  Amplitude [m] per entry of incident_modes (empty: amplitude for each).
- `incident_phases` (float_list; unit deg; optional (null allowed)) - Incident phases
  Phase [deg] per entry of incident_modes (empty: phase for each).
- `sector_drive` (bool; default false) - Parity-sector drive
  Set by the study setting parity_sectors on its sector copies (leave it off): an incident mode of a guide ending on a mirror face is then driven at 2 A in the sector of its parity and not at all in the other, so the mean of the sectors is the drawn amplitude A.
- `tension_tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-06; range (0, 1]) - Tension tolerance
  Largest relative variation of the tension along the port cut (spread of T_nn and of T_ss over the elements at the face, |tension_xy| / T_nn) that is accepted; above it the build of the first solve fails. Default 1e-06 (a uniform guide). Raise it (e.g. 1e-2) for a guide whose tension comes from a solid (solid_membrane_tension coupling): the port then uses the mean tension of its cut, a spread above 1e-06 gives a RuntimeWarning and the result extras tension_spread / medium_warning, and the port reflects at about the level of the spread. Areal density and loss factor must stay uniform to 1e-06.

### Feature `membrane.mode_projection` - Mode projection

a_n(p) = (2 / W) int w(p, s) sin(n pi (s - cross_start) / W) ds at points positions p from start to end along guide_axis, s across from cross_start to cross_end (W = their distance; a wall on a window face with the symmetry feature is free: the port's half-guide profiles, extra free_walls; composite Gauss; the sample points are located once at build, a point outside the mesh is a build error). Result 'xy' versus position [m] of the shown solution (resonance or the last frequency): series mode_<n>_re / _im / _abs [m], _phase [rad]; a two_wave_fit or two_exp_fit derived value of mode_1_re gives beta or kappa of a mode. A frequency_response run also records a_n(p) at every solved frequency (independent of the study snapshots setting; host 16 B x points x mode_count per frequency): extras frequencies [Hz] (ascending, a repeated frequency replaces its row) and frequency_series {mode_<n>_re / _im / _abs / _phase: (n_frequencies, points) array, row i at frequencies[i], column j at x[j]} (results.npz result/<physics>.<feature>/frequency_series/<name>). result_axis 'frequency' instead gives result 'xy' versus those frequencies [Hz]: mode_<n>_power = the mean of |a_n|^2 over the sampled positions in average_start .. average_end [m^2] (a guide-averaged mode power, insensitive to standing-wave ripple), mode_<n>_rms = its square root [m] and total_power = the sum over the modes [m^2]; extras average_window [m] (first and last averaged position) and average_points; an error before a frequency_response run. An output / input ratio is a derived curve dividing the mode_<n>_power series of two such projections (that view also stores extras averaged_series {mode_<n>_re / _im: (n_frequencies, averaged points)}). Extras mirror_walls / sector_modes / sector_signs as the port (parity_sectors combines the projection on the unfolded guide). Triangle meshes; refused with bending_stiffness (the film profiles are not the plate guide modes, which are numeric per frequency: use ports or field probes).

- FeatureSpec.type `mode_projection`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `guide_axis` (choice; default "y"; choices x | y) - Guide direction
  Axis the guide runs along; the projection integrates across the other axis.
- `cross_start` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Guide wall start
  Coordinate [m] of the first guide wall across the guide (empty: the window edge; on a symmetry face the wall is free).
- `cross_end` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Guide wall end
  Coordinate [m] of the second guide wall (empty: the window edge; on a symmetry face the wall is free); W = cross_end - cross_start.
- `start` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - First position
  First sampled position [m] along the guide (empty: the window edge).
- `end` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Last position
  Last sampled position [m] along the guide (empty: the window edge).
- `points` (int; unit 1; default 101; range [2, 100000]) - Positions
  Number of equally spaced positions from start to end.
- `mode_count` (int; unit 1; default 3; range [1, 200]) - Modes
  Number of profiles phi_n, n = 1 .. mode_count, projected on (sin(n pi (s - cross_start) / W); a wall on a symmetry face: sin / cos((n - 1/2) pi (s - cross_start) / W), see the feature description).
- `result_axis` (choice; default "position"; choices position | frequency) - Result versus
  'position' (default): a_n(p) of the shown solution versus position. 'frequency' (frequency_response only): per recorded frequency the mean of |a_n|^2 over the positions in average_start .. average_end (series mode_<n>_power [m^2], mode_<n>_rms [m], total_power [m^2]; see the feature description).
- `average_start` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed); visible when result_axis in (frequency)) - Averaging start
  result_axis 'frequency': first position [m] of the averaging window along the guide (empty: start); the mean runs over the sampled positions inside the window.
- `average_end` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed); visible when result_axis in (frequency)) - Averaging end
  result_axis 'frequency': last position [m] of the averaging window (empty: end). A build error when no sampled position lies in the window.

## Physics type `pressure_acoustics` - Pressure Acoustics, frequency domain

Frequency-domain pressure acoustics (the industry-standard formulation) for the frequency_response study: -div(grad p / rho) - omega^2 p / (rho c^2) = j omega q (exp(+j omega t), peak amplitudes), p the complex pressure, rho / c the material density and sound_speed (every fluid element needs both > 0; elastic_waves shares the Params; no losses but impedance and PML), on a triangle mesh (planar, or axisymmetric (r, z) with geometry, azimuthal order 0) or a tetrahedron mesh (3D), complex Lagrange P2 (default) or P1 elements (fem.harmonic / harmonic3d). K and M are assembled once; each frequency is one complex symmetric factorisation by the linear role (sparse_direct: back_end 'cudss' / 'cudss_mixed' on the gpu backend: cuDSS LDL^T reusing its plan, the pencil kept on the device; 'auto' = cudss_mixed there when nvmath-python is installed, else host SuperLU). Outer faces default to sound hard (also mirror planes); features: sound_hard, sound_soft, prescribed_pressure, impedance, vibrating_boundary (outer faces act on their window edge, object outlines in 2D / interfaces in 3D), rigid_obstacle (excluded voids), point_source, background_pressure_field (scattered-field formulation), frequency_probe and surface_pressure (complex records per frequency, harmonic probe series <c>_re / _im / _abs / _phase). PML: settings pml_<face> grow absorbing layers (fixed complex stretch, fem.pml) of pml_cells element sizes beyond those faces, tuned at pml_frequency (default the lowest study frequency). Fields: p_abs / p_re / p_im / spl (total), p_s_* (scattered), v_* particle velocity j grad p / (omega rho) per element (v_z in 3D), rho, sound_speed; state p_abs / p_re / p_im per element. Snapshots per frequency labelled "f = <Hz> Hz". The instance is usually named pressure_acoustics.

- PhysicsSpec.type `pressure_acoustics`; default instance name `pressure_acoustics`
- Supported studies: frequency_response
- Default study: {"type": "frequency_response", "settings": {"frequency_start": 100, "frequency_stop": 1000, "n_frequencies": 10}}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): p_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `pressure_acoustics.<feature>`): background_pressure_field, rigid_obstacle, sound_hard, sound_soft, prescribed_pressure, impedance, vibrating_boundary, point_source, frequency_probe, surface_pressure

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "planar"; choices planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: the drawing is a cross-section of a fluid uniform along z; point sources are line sources (flow rate per metre of depth, m^2/s), surface results are per metre of depth. axisymmetric: a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z): the fluid is the body of revolution of the drawing and every field is independent of the angle (azimuthal order 0); a point source on the axis is a point source, off the axis a ring of that total flow rate; surface means are area-weighted and weighted integrals cover the whole ring; no PML on x_lo. 2D models only (a 3D model is solved in full: validation errors on axisymmetric there). x_lo is the axis (r = 0: symmetry, a boundary condition there does nothing; validation warns). Field derived values of the whole model are weighted by the ring volume 2 pi r dx dy ('integral' a whole-body total, 'mean' a volume mean; also for fields of other physics). A coupled physics that is planar (its type has no geometry setting, e.g. EM, or it is set to planar) solves the drawing as a planar cut per unit z length, so its fields are applied per cell as rings (validation warns); a partner with geometry axisymmetric too is consistent.
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`
- `pml_x_lo` (bool; default false) - Absorbing layer beyond the left edge
  Perfectly matched layer beyond x_lo: the mesh grows a layer of pml_cells x the mesh dx (h_max) there (triangles: the absorbing ring of pml_layers structured element layers; tetrahedra: the shell), its material continued from the window edge, with the fixed complex stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness), beta set by pml_reflection for the fastest sound speed in the layer at pml_frequency (default the lowest study frequency); its outer side is held at p = 0. Waves leave the window through it; higher frequencies and slower waves are absorbed more. No boundary feature may select x_lo (it is the inner side of the layer); z faces in 3D models only; geometry axisymmetric: not on x_lo (the axis). Another physics on the same mesh must not request layers on other faces (the run fails).
- `pml_x_hi` (bool; default false) - Absorbing layer beyond the right edge
  Perfectly matched layer beyond x_hi: the mesh grows a layer of pml_cells x the mesh dx (h_max) there (triangles: the absorbing ring of pml_layers structured element layers; tetrahedra: the shell), its material continued from the window edge, with the fixed complex stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness), beta set by pml_reflection for the fastest sound speed in the layer at pml_frequency (default the lowest study frequency); its outer side is held at p = 0. Waves leave the window through it; higher frequencies and slower waves are absorbed more. No boundary feature may select x_hi (it is the inner side of the layer); z faces in 3D models only; geometry axisymmetric: not on x_lo (the axis). Another physics on the same mesh must not request layers on other faces (the run fails).
- `pml_y_lo` (bool; default false) - Absorbing layer beyond the bottom edge
  Perfectly matched layer beyond y_lo: the mesh grows a layer of pml_cells x the mesh dx (h_max) there (triangles: the absorbing ring of pml_layers structured element layers; tetrahedra: the shell), its material continued from the window edge, with the fixed complex stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness), beta set by pml_reflection for the fastest sound speed in the layer at pml_frequency (default the lowest study frequency); its outer side is held at p = 0. Waves leave the window through it; higher frequencies and slower waves are absorbed more. No boundary feature may select y_lo (it is the inner side of the layer); z faces in 3D models only; geometry axisymmetric: not on x_lo (the axis). Another physics on the same mesh must not request layers on other faces (the run fails).
- `pml_y_hi` (bool; default false) - Absorbing layer beyond the top edge
  Perfectly matched layer beyond y_hi: the mesh grows a layer of pml_cells x the mesh dx (h_max) there (triangles: the absorbing ring of pml_layers structured element layers; tetrahedra: the shell), its material continued from the window edge, with the fixed complex stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness), beta set by pml_reflection for the fastest sound speed in the layer at pml_frequency (default the lowest study frequency); its outer side is held at p = 0. Waves leave the window through it; higher frequencies and slower waves are absorbed more. No boundary feature may select y_hi (it is the inner side of the layer); z faces in 3D models only; geometry axisymmetric: not on x_lo (the axis). Another physics on the same mesh must not request layers on other faces (the run fails).
- `pml_z_lo` (bool; default false) - Absorbing layer beyond the lower z face
  Perfectly matched layer beyond z_lo: the mesh grows a layer of pml_cells x the mesh dx (h_max) there (triangles: the absorbing ring of pml_layers structured element layers; tetrahedra: the shell), its material continued from the window edge, with the fixed complex stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness), beta set by pml_reflection for the fastest sound speed in the layer at pml_frequency (default the lowest study frequency); its outer side is held at p = 0. Waves leave the window through it; higher frequencies and slower waves are absorbed more. No boundary feature may select z_lo (it is the inner side of the layer); z faces in 3D models only; geometry axisymmetric: not on x_lo (the axis). Another physics on the same mesh must not request layers on other faces (the run fails).
- `pml_z_hi` (bool; default false) - Absorbing layer beyond the upper z face
  Perfectly matched layer beyond z_hi: the mesh grows a layer of pml_cells x the mesh dx (h_max) there (triangles: the absorbing ring of pml_layers structured element layers; tetrahedra: the shell), its material continued from the window edge, with the fixed complex stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness), beta set by pml_reflection for the fastest sound speed in the layer at pml_frequency (default the lowest study frequency); its outer side is held at p = 0. Waves leave the window through it; higher frequencies and slower waves are absorbed more. No boundary feature may select z_hi (it is the inner side of the layer); z faces in 3D models only; geometry axisymmetric: not on x_lo (the axis). Another physics on the same mesh must not request layers on other faces (the run fails).
- `pml_cells` (int; unit 1; default 8; range [1, 100]) - Absorbing layer thickness
  Thickness of every PML in element sizes (x the mesh dx, h_max); about half a wavelength or more at the lowest frequency, 6-12 typical. Triangles: MeshSpec pml_layers sets the structured element layers across it.
- `pml_reflection` (float; unit 1; default 1e-06; range (0, 0.5]) - Absorbing layer reflection
  Theoretical round-trip reflection R of a normally incident wave in the PML at pml_frequency for the fastest sound speed c of the layer: beta = 3 ln(1 / R) c / (2 omega w). A very small R makes the profile steep, which the elements reflect instead: 1e-3 to 1e-8 typical.
- `pml_frequency` (float; unit Hz; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Absorbing layer frequency
  Frequency [Hz] at which the PML strength is set (pml_reflection holds there; the stretch does not change with frequency, so K and M are assembled once); empty = the lowest frequency of the frequency_response study (absorption only grows above it).
