### Feature `pressure_acoustics.background_pressure_field` - Background pressure field

Scattered-field formulation: the unknown is p_s, the total pressure p = p_s + p_b in the window (p_s in a PML, which absorbs p_s only). p_b is assumed to solve the background medium (background_density, background_sound_speed) exactly, so the source is only where the model differs from it: elements whose material differs (the contrast), rigid_obstacle elements (their sound-hard outline: n . grad p_s = -n . grad p_b), the outer faces (every non-PML face is a total-field condition: 0 for a symmetry plane of p_b, e.g. the floor of a standing wave) and the total-field impedance / held values (p_s = given - p_b). One per physics (the last one wins). Probes and surface results add p_b exactly at their points; the p_* fields hold the nodal p_s + p_b, the p_s_* fields the scattered part.

- FeatureSpec.type `background_pressure_field`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `wave` (choice; default "plane_wave"; choices plane_wave | standing_wave | expression) - Background wave
  plane_wave: p_b = p0 exp(-j k d . x) travelling along the unit direction d, k = 2 pi f / background_sound_speed; standing_wave: the plane wave reflected by a rigid plane normal to an axis direction, p_b = 2 p0 cos(k (u - plane_position)), u the coordinate along that axis (normal incidence onto a floor: direction -y, plane_position 0 gives 2 p0 cos(k y)); expression: p_b = pressure_re + j pressure_im as expressions of x, y (z in 3D) and parameters, the same at every frequency (sweep a parameter for a frequency-dependent one; its gradient on outer faces by central differences).
- `amplitude` (float; unit Pa; default 1; visible when wave in (plane_wave, standing_wave)) - Amplitude
  Peak pressure p0 of the incident plane wave (a standing wave peaks at 2 p0).
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0; visible when wave in (plane_wave, standing_wave)) - Phase
  Phase of p0 in degrees: of the plane wave at the origin, of the standing wave everywhere.
- `direction` (choice; default "-y"; choices +x | -x | +y | -y | +z | -z | custom; visible when wave in (plane_wave, standing_wave)) - Direction of travel
  Propagation direction d of the incident wave: an axis, or custom = (direction_x, direction_y, direction_z) normalised (plane_wave only). +z / -z need a 3D model; geometry axisymmetric: +y or -y (along the axis) only.
- `direction_x` (float; unit 1; default 0; visible when direction in (custom)) - Direction x
  x component of a custom propagation direction (normalised; the z component is ignored in 2D and must be 0 there).
- `direction_y` (float; unit 1; default -1; visible when direction in (custom)) - Direction y
  y component of a custom propagation direction (normalised; the z component is ignored in 2D and must be 0 there).
- `direction_z` (float; unit 1; default 0; visible when direction in (custom)) - Direction z
  z component of a custom propagation direction (normalised; the z component is ignored in 2D and must be 0 there).
- `plane_position` (float; unit m; default 0; visible when wave in (standing_wave)) - Rigid plane position
  Coordinate of the rigid plane along the axis of direction (y = plane_position for +y / -y).
- `pressure_re` (float; unit Pa; default 0; may use x, y; visible when wave in (expression)) - Pressure, real part
  Real part of p_b [Pa]: an expression of x, y (z in 3D) and parameters; it should solve the Helmholtz equation of the background medium (else the mismatch radiates).
- `pressure_im` (float; unit Pa; default 0; may use x, y; visible when wave in (expression)) - Pressure, imaginary part
  Imaginary part of p_b [Pa] (phasors exp(+j omega t)), as pressure_re.
- `background_density` (float; unit kg/m^3; default 1.2; range (0, inf)) - Background density
  Density rho_b of the medium p_b travels in; elements whose 1 / rho and 1 / (rho c^2) differ from the background ones by more than 1e-6 (relative) are scatterers (the contrast source).
- `background_sound_speed` (float; unit m/s; default 343; range (0, inf)) - Background sound speed
  Sound speed c_b of the background medium: the wavenumber k = 2 pi f / c_b of p_b and, with background_density, the medium the contrast is taken against. Air 343, water 1480.

### Feature `pressure_acoustics.rigid_obstacle` - Rigid obstacle

The selected elements are left out of the solve (no pressure inside, fields 0 there); their outline is sound hard (n . grad p = 0), with a background the total field is. Select solids and thin plates here (structural back-action neglected).

- FeatureSpec.type `rigid_obstacle`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `pressure_acoustics.sound_hard` - Sound hard wall

n . grad p = 0 on outer faces (the default of every face without a PML or other condition; also a mirror-symmetry plane), for the total field with a background. A later feature on the same face wins, so this resets an earlier one.

- FeatureSpec.type `sound_hard`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `pressure_acoustics.sound_soft` - Sound soft boundary

p = 0 (total field; with a background p_s = -p_b) on outer faces and object outlines. Held values: the later feature wins shared nodes.

- FeatureSpec.type `sound_soft`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `pressure_acoustics.prescribed_pressure` - Pressure

p = pressure exp(j phase) (total field) on outer faces and object outlines (the window edge of an outer face; along a PML side the wall stays sound hard). Held values: the later feature wins shared nodes.

- FeatureSpec.type `prescribed_pressure`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `pressure` (float; unit Pa; default 1; may use x, y) - Pressure amplitude
  Total pressure amplitude held on the boundary (with a background: p_s = this - p_b there); may depend on x, y (z in 3D).
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phase of the complex amplitude of the held pressure in degrees (phasors exp(+j omega t)).

### Feature `pressure_acoustics.impedance` - Impedance

Robin condition n_out . grad p / rho = -j omega p / Z (Z the specific impedance; empty: rho c of the adjacent fluid, the first-order absorbing boundary) on outer faces and object outlines; with a background the total field obeys it.

- FeatureSpec.type `impedance`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `impedance` (float; unit Pa s/m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Acoustic impedance
  Specific acoustic impedance Z = p / v_n (v_n the normal velocity out of the fluid), a real number; empty = rho c of the adjacent fluid element, the plane-wave absorber (no reflection at normal incidence, a reflection growing with the angle). Air 413, water 1.48e6.

### Feature `pressure_acoustics.vibrating_boundary` - Vibrating wall

Inward normal motion: n_out . grad p / rho = j omega v_in (velocity), = a_in (acceleration), = -omega^2 d_in (displacement), on outer faces and object outlines (a load; the wall is sound hard otherwise).

- FeatureSpec.type `vibrating_boundary`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `quantity` (choice; default "velocity"; choices acceleration | velocity | displacement) - Given quantity
  Which normal motion of the wall is given (positive into the fluid): velocity v, acceleration a = j omega v or displacement d = v / (j omega); the flux n_out . grad p / rho = j omega v_in.
- `velocity` (float; unit m/s; default 0.001; may use x, y; visible when quantity in (velocity)) - Normal velocity amplitude
  Normal velocity amplitude into the fluid [m/s]; may depend on x, y (z in 3D).
- `acceleration` (float; unit m/s^2; default 1; may use x, y; visible when quantity in (acceleration)) - Normal acceleration amplitude
  Normal acceleration amplitude into the fluid [m/s^2]; may depend on x, y (z in 3D).
- `displacement` (float; unit m; default 1e-09; may use x, y; visible when quantity in (displacement)) - Normal displacement amplitude
  Normal displacement amplitude into the fluid [m]; may depend on x, y (z in 3D).
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phase of the complex amplitude of the wall motion in degrees (phasors exp(+j omega t)).

### Feature `pressure_acoustics.point_source` - Point source

Monopole of volume flow rate Q exp(j phase): the load j omega Q phi_i(x0) (axisymmetric: divided by 2 pi, the per-radian solve). Must lie in a fluid element.

- FeatureSpec.type `point_source`; category source
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `flow_rate` (float; unit m^3/s, m^2/s planar; default 1e-06) - Volume flow rate
  Peak volume flow rate Q of a monopole: the load j omega Q at the point; 3D free field p = j omega rho Q exp(-j k r) / (4 pi r). Planar 2D: per metre of depth (a line source, m^2/s); axisymmetric: a point on the axis, else a ring of total rate Q.
- `phase` (float; unit deg; default 0) - Phase
  Phase of the complex amplitude of the flow rate in degrees (phasors exp(+j omega t)).

### Feature `pressure_acoustics.frequency_probe` - Pressure probe

Complex pressure at the point per solved frequency (core.harmonic_probe 'xy' result vs frequency [Hz]): series p_re, p_im, p_abs, p_phase (total, p_b exact at the point) and p_s_re ... (scattered; = p without a background), in Pa; 0 in a rigid obstacle.

- FeatureSpec.type `frequency_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `pressure_acoustics.surface_pressure` - Surface pressure

'xy' result vs frequency [Hz]: series p_mean_re / _im / _abs / _phase = int p dA / int dA [Pa] and p_weighted_* = int p weight dA (Pa m^2; planar 2D Pa m per metre of depth; axisymmetric whole rings) over the selected outer faces (their window side) and object outlines / interfaces on side (outward normal out of the object); extras area [m^2, planar m], weight_integral (int weight dA), side. p is continuous, so a side picks faces, not a field side; p_b enters exactly (quadrature). E.g. r = |<p_top> - <p_bottom>| / p_max by a derived curve of two features (side +y, -y).

- FeatureSpec.type `surface_pressure`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles, tetrahedra
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `side` (choice; default "all"; choices all | +x | -x | +y | -y | +z | -z) - Side
  Part of the selection: 'all', or the boundary pieces whose outward normal (out of the selected object; an outer face: out of the domain) has a positive component along +x ... -z, e.g. +y = the top face of a rectangle (2D: +y = up; axisymmetric: +y = +z). +z / -z need a 3D model.
- `weight` (float; unit 1; default 1; may use x, y) - Weight
  Weight psi of the weighted integral int p psi dA (e.g. a mode shape expression of x, y, z); its unit multiplies the result (Pa m^2; planar 2D Pa m per metre of depth).

## Physics type `solid_mechanics` - Solid Mechanics (2D)

2D static linear elasticity; setting out_of_plane: plane strain (default; eps_zz = 0: the cross-section of a structure long along z, e.g. a waveguide), plane stress (sigma_zz = 0: a thin plate) or generalized plane strain (uniform eps_zz set by the net axial force); setting geometry axisymmetric: an (r, z) body of revolution with the hoop strain (whole-ring forces in N). The rest is written for plane strain. Small strain, isotropic cells (youngs_modulus, poisson_ratio) or the anisotropic c_ij entries (c11 .. c66 in Voigt model axes, NaN = the isotropic value; a crystal entry sets them) with anisotropic thermal expansion alpha_xx / alpha_yy / alpha_zz: sigma = C (eps - alpha dT), dT = temperature_rise (coupled, heat_solid_thermal_strain) + temperature_rise_ext (temperature_change features). Discretisation: bilinear elements on the cells of the physical window, displacement on the cell corners, block-Jacobi PCG; outputs at the cell centres (u = mean of the 4 corners; strain, stress and von Mises from the centre gradients), 0 in void cells (no youngs_modulus or c11 > 0: not solved, carry nothing), copied edge-extended into an EM PML ring. Units per unit z length: forces and reactions N/m. strain_xy is the tensor shear strain (half the engineering strain); stress_zz = nu (sigma_xx + sigma_yy) - E alpha_zz dT is the out-of-plane stress plane strain implies; von_mises includes it. Faces without a support or load are traction free. Every solid region (cells with stiffness joined through edges or corners) needs supports that hold u_x and u_y and stop rotation, e.g. rollers on one x and one y face (validation checks the directions, the build each region). A stationary study solves it after the physics it reads; in a time-dependent study it re-solves only when a material, support, load or coupled input changed (quasi-static, no inertia). An eigenfrequency study finds the undamped in-plane vibration modes (plane strain) nearest target_frequency instead: K u = omega^2 M u with the consistent mass of rho (needed in every solid cell) on the host (eigen solver role arpack_shift_invert: symmetric shift-invert Lanczos on a real SuperLU factor), supports held at 0, loads / thermal strain ignored (no prestress: setting stress_stiffening on a triangle mesh adds it); with the axial_wavenumber setting k_z the guided (2.5D) modes u ~ exp(i (k_z z - omega t)) instead, u_z coupled (dispersion f(k_z) of a waveguide: flexural, torsional, longitudinal branches; supports optional for k_z > 0); one snapshot per mode labelled "resonance k: f = <Hz> Hz" with the mode shape scaled to a peak node |u| of 1 m (strain and stress per that shape, no thermal part; support reactions are not available), the resonance_table feature lists the frequencies; an optomechanics study solves the same modes after an optical mode (em_modes, em_fdfd_ez, em_fdfd_hz, em_fdfd_bor) and its optomechanical_coupling feature tabulates g0. Output u_x, u_y (u_z) are the displacement [m] and u_abs its magnitude (u is the flow velocity in laminar_flow, elastic_waves names its velocity vx / vy). elastic_strain_* = strain - alpha dT (elastic_strain_zz = -alpha_zz dT), the stress-producing part. Optics: solid_em_strain_optic (strain -> EM index) and em_solid_optical_force (em_fdfd_ez -> the body_force_x / body_force_y slots). Setting piezoelectric: a nodal potential on the same elements with the piezo_e* / eps_dc_* material arrays and electrode features, static and modal (short / open circuit) coupled solves on the host. A frequency_response study solves the driven harmonic response (K (1 + j mechanical_loss_factor) - omega^2 M) u = f per frequency (host complex SuperLU; loads, prescribed displacements and electrode voltages are amplitudes at phase 0; a temperature change or coupled temperature is static, never a drive: with stress_stiffening its thermal stress joins the prestress), one snapshot per frequency with the real parts and u_abs = |u|; with piezoelectric the admittance feature gives Y(f) and a Butterworth-Van Dyke fit. A 3D model (size_z set) uses solid_mechanics_3d. The instance is usually named solid. On a triangle mesh (mesh kind 'triangles', mesh plan S7.5): Lagrange elements of the discretization setting (quadratic P2 default, isoparametric on curved boundaries) on the window elements with stiffness, one host SuperLU of K per assembly at its first static solve (linear solver sparse_direct, Automatic there), plane strain / plane stress / generalized plane strain (the same superposition, conditions exact by the same quadrature) / axisymmetric, c_ij, thermal strain, every support and load feature (Fixed (domain) holds every node of the selected elements; segment loads in any direction), probes at point nodes, the eigenfrequency study and the elastic frequency_response study (stationary, time_dependent, eigenfrequency and frequency_response; there also: initial_stress_* material entries (total stress sigma0 + C eps - beta dT, relaxed by static solves), setting stress_stiffening (K + K_sigma of the static state in the eigenfrequency / frequency_response pencils), damped modes with a mechanical_loss_factor, free bodies about a target_frequency > 0 and in frequency responses, the frequency_probe feature and complex support reactions per frequency; not yet: piezoelectric (so no admittance), guided modes, solid_em_strain_optic; the optomechanics study with geometry axisymmetric and em_fdfd_bor optics only); state() and coupled slots are one value per element (centroid), displayed fields nodal (displacement exact, strain / stress averaged over the solid elements at each node), the PML ring void unless an elastic PML. Triangle meshes, eigenfrequency study only: settings pml_<face> make the ring an elastic PML (fixed complex stretch set at target_frequency, outer side clamped, complex modes with a radiation Q, PML modes dropped; stress_stiffening sees the ring as a clamped elastic continuation in its static state), and azimuthal_order m >= 1 (geometry axisymmetric, isotropic materials) solves the modes u_r = U_r cos(m phi), u_z = U_z cos(m phi), u_phi = U_phi sin(m phi) with three amplitudes per node (fields u_x, u_y and u_z = U_phi; strain / stress outputs the cos parts at phi = 0; rings weighted by pi; the axis holds u_z = 0 and ties u_phi = -u_r at m = 1, holds all three at m >= 2; m = 1 has the sideways translation and tilt as rigid motions, m >= 2 none, so supports are optional there; stress_stiffening takes the initial stress alone). Triangle meshes, planar plane strain / plane stress or axisymmetric (azimuthal order 0), no PML: setting geometric_nonlinearity makes every static solve total-Lagrangian (Green-Lagrange strain, second Piola-Kirchhoff stress outputs, Newton over load_steps, support reactions the nominal forces of the internal force, not K u - f) and linearises the eigenfrequency / frequency_response pencils about that state (tangent K_T); the Prescribed displacement (domain) feature holds chosen components of whole domains. Display fields strain_energy_density / kinetic_energy_density (triangle meshes; J/m^3; not in state()): a static solve 1/2 sigma : eps_el (no initial stress) and 0, a shown mode or response the time averages 1/4 Re(sigma : eps_el*) and 1/4 rho omega^2 |u|^2 at the mode / drive frequency (azimuthal order: twice the phi mean, so ring integrals give the totals); in a PML ring they use the unstretched gradients (not physical there).

- PhysicsSpec.type `solid_mechanics`; default instance name `solid`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent, eigenfrequency, optomechanics, frequency_response
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): u_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `solid_mechanics.<feature>`): fixed, roller, displacement, fixed_domain, prescribed_displacement_domain, boundary_load, segment_load, body_force, temperature_change, solid_probe, frequency_probe, resonance_table, optomechanical_coupling, electrode, electrode_domain, admittance

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `geometry` (choice; default "planar"; choices planar | axisymmetric) - Geometry
  planar: the cross-section of a structure (out_of_plane decides eps_zz / sigma_zz), forces and reactions per m of depth (N/m). axisymmetric: a body of revolution about the x_lo window edge (x = r >= 0, y = z): (r, z) deformation without torsion (u_phi = 0): unknowns u_r = u_x, u_z = u_y on the cell corners, hoop strain u_r / r, element integrals weighted by 2 pi r (2 x 2 Gauss), so the operator, loads and reactions are whole rings: tractions and body forces keep their units (Pa, N/m^3), nodal forces and support reactions are in N (F_y of a support = the axial force on its ring area, F_x = the integral of its radial traction, not a net vector force). The _zz outputs are the hoop components (stress_zz = sigma_theta theta, elastic_strain_zz = u_r / r - alpha_zz dT, alpha_zz = the hoop expansion), _yy the axial ones; u_r = 0 is held on the x_lo nodes automatically. Only u_z needs a support per solid region (a z translation is the one rigid motion). out_of_plane is not used; not with piezoelectric, axial_wavenumber or the optomechanics study; an eigenfrequency study finds the axisymmetric (torsion-free) modes with the whole-ring mass. x_lo is the axis (r = 0: symmetry, u_r = 0 is held there automatically; a support or load selecting x_lo acts on a line without area: validation warns). Field derived values of the whole model are weighted by the ring volume 2 pi r dx dy ('integral' a whole-body total, 'mean' a volume mean; also for fields of other physics). A coupled physics that is planar (its type has no geometry setting, e.g. EM, or it is set to planar) solves the drawing as a planar cut per unit z length, so its fields are applied per cell as rings (validation warns); a partner with geometry axisymmetric too is consistent.
- `azimuthal_order` (int; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when geometry in (axisymmetric)) - Azimuthal order
  Help: shared `electric_currents.azimuthal_order`
- `out_of_plane` (choice; default "plane_strain"; choices plane_strain | plane_stress | generalized_plane_strain; visible when geometry in (planar)) - Out-of-plane condition
  Planar geometry only (axisymmetric ignores it): what the drawing assumes along z. plane_strain (default): eps_zz = 0, a cross-section of a structure long along z with clamped ends; stress_zz = lambda (eps_xx + eps_yy) - beta_z dT is the stress that holds eps_zz at 0 (it overestimates the thermal stress of a waveguide whose ends are free). plane_stress: sigma_zz = 0, a thin plate in the drawing plane (top view of a film or membrane): the reduced stiffness lambda -> 2 mu lambda / (lambda + 2 mu) and thermal stress beta - lambda beta_z / (lambda + 2 mu); outputs elastic_strain_zz = eps_zz - alpha_zz dT with eps_zz = (beta_z dT - lambda (eps_xx + eps_yy)) / (lambda + 2 mu) per cell, stress_zz = 0; forces per m of thickness (N/m). generalized_plane_strain (industry-standard form): eps_zz = e0 + e1 x + e2 y over the whole drawn cross-section (x, y of the drawing), e0 set by the net axial force (setting axial_force; 0 = free ends) and the bending terms e1 / e2 (setting bending, default both free) by the bending moments (bending_moment_x / _y; 0 = an unloaded, freely bending long body): the right model of thermal stress in a long waveguide or fibre; solved by superposition (one pcg solve of the eps_zz = 0 problem plus, per assembly, one per free term; on a triangle mesh back substitutions on the K factor), the force and moment conditions hold exactly in the elements; outputs stress_zz and elastic_strain_zz = eps_zz - alpha_zz dT. Piezoelectric, axial_wavenumber and the optomechanics study need plane_strain; the eigenfrequency study needs plane_strain or plane_stress.
- `thickness` (float; unit m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when geometry in (planar)) - Thickness
  Planar geometry only: the out-of-plane thickness d of the structure (a plate, or the length of a long part). Empty (default): everything per m of depth, support reactions in N/m. A value: the support reaction tables are for that thickness in N (the per-m forces times d); the solution, tractions (Pa) and body forces (N/m^3) do not change, nor do axial_force (always the total on the cross-section), electrode charges (C/m) and the optomechanical length. Typical for plane stress: the film thickness.
- `axial_force` (float; unit N; default 0; visible when out_of_plane in (generalized_plane_strain)) - Axial force
  Generalized plane strain only: the net force along +z on the drawn cross-section (integral of stress_zz over the solid cells; a mirrored model: of the drawn part only). 0 = free ends (no net axial load); a positive value pulls. Ignored by the other conditions.
- `bending` (choice; default "xy"; choices xy | x | y | none; visible when out_of_plane in (generalized_plane_strain)) - Out-of-plane bending
  Generalized plane strain only: which linear terms of eps_zz = e0 + e1 x + e2 y are solved. 'xy' (default): e1 and e2, set by bending_moment_y and bending_moment_x; 'x': e1 only (e2 = 0), 'y': e2 only (e1 = 0); 'none': uniform eps_zz = e0. A mirrored model draws half the section and the moments and force are those of the drawn part: hold the term across a mirror plane at 0 (a mirror on an x face: bending y; on a y face: bending x; on both: none), since the whole body's eps_zz is even there. Each free term adds one pcg solve per assembly.
- `bending_moment_x` (float; unit N m; default 0; visible when out_of_plane in (generalized_plane_strain)) - Bending moment about x
  Generalized plane strain with bending xy or y: M_x = integral of y stress_zz dA over the solid cells of the drawn cross-section, about the drawing origin (x = y = 0, the lower left domain corner); an axial force F through the point (x_F, y_F) gives M_x = y_F F. 0 (default) = no applied moment. Ignored otherwise.
- `bending_moment_y` (float; unit N m; default 0; visible when out_of_plane in (generalized_plane_strain)) - Bending moment about y
  Generalized plane strain with bending xy or x: M_y = -(integral of x stress_zz dA) over the solid cells of the drawn cross-section, about the drawing origin (right-hand rule: an axial force F through (x_F, y_F) gives M_y = -x_F F). 0 (default) = no applied moment. Ignored otherwise.
- `target_frequency` (float; unit Hz; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Eigenfrequency target
  Eigenfrequency study only: the vibration modes nearest this frequency are searched (shift-invert about (2 pi target_frequency)^2, moved 1e-4 above it so a target on a resonance still factors); 0 = the lowest modes (a body that moves without strain then fails: check the supports). On a triangle mesh a target > 0 also allows a free body (no supports; axisymmetric: no held u_z): its rigid-body modes (f below 1e-4 x the target) are dropped. Ignored by the other studies.
- `stress_stiffening` (bool; default false) - Stress stiffening
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.stress_stiffening`
- `geometric_nonlinearity` (bool; default false) - Geometric nonlinearity
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.geometric_nonlinearity`
- `load_steps` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when geometric_nonlinearity in (true)) - Load steps
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.load_steps`
- `nonlinear_tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-08; range (0, inf); visible when geometric_nonlinearity in (true)) - Nonlinear tolerance
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.nonlinear_tolerance`
- `nonlinear_max_iterations` (int; default 25; range [1, inf); visible when geometric_nonlinearity in (true)) - Nonlinear iteration limit
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.nonlinear_max_iterations`
- `tangent_update` (choice; default "every_iteration"; choices every_iteration | when_slow; visible when geometric_nonlinearity in (true)) - Tangent update
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.tangent_update`
- `axial_wavenumber` (float; unit rad/m; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Axial wavenumber
  Eigenfrequency study only. Empty (default): the in-plane plane-strain vibration modes (u_x, u_y). A value k_z: the guided (2.5D) modes of the structure long along z, u ~ exp(i (k_z z - omega t)) with all three components coupled (Q1 elements, exact element integrals; the complex Hermitian operator is solved in the equivalent real symmetric form u_z -> -i u_z, exact for isotropic cells): the physical displacement is (u_x cos phi, u_y cos phi, u_z sin phi), phi = k_z z - omega t, so field u_z is the amplitude of the quadrature part and the strains / stresses are the phi = 0 values (elastic_strain_zz = k_z u_z enters stress_* and von_mises; the shear strains xz / yz peak at phi = pi / 2 and are not output). k_z > 0 leaves no rigid motion: supports are optional (a free suspended wire). k_z = 0 gives the plane-strain modes plus the antiplane (pure u_z) modes; these need u_z held on every solid region: Fixed and Fixed (domain) hold u_z, Roller and Displacement leave it free. Typical: backward Brillouin scattering needs k_z = 2 beta = 4 pi n_eff / lambda (~2.5e7 rad/m for a silicon wire at 1550 nm). For a dispersion relation f(k_z) sweep a parameter used here. Ignored by the other studies; the optomechanics study refuses it (an optomechanical_coupling with scattering backward makes that study set k_z = 2 Re beta itself).
- `piezoelectric` (bool; default false) - Piezoelectric
  On: piezoelectric plane strain. A nodal electric potential phi (the same bilinear elements, every window node, void cells included as dielectric) couples to the displacement through the piezo_e* material arrays (solid cells) with the clamped permittivity eps0 eps_dc_xx / _yy / _xy (every window cell, unset = 1): T = c S - e^T E, D = e S + eps E, E = -grad phi, div D = 0 (no free volume charge). Electrode / Electrode (domain) features fix phi (connection voltage; at least one, the ground, is required) or make an isolated equipotential carrying a net charge (floating); every other outer face is insulating (D . n = 0). The coupled operator [[K_uu, K_uphi], [K_phiu, -K_phiphi]] is symmetric but indefinite, so the static solve is one host SuperLU factorisation (float64, kept while the operator is unchanged; counters piezo_* in the summary) instead of the pcg linear solver; the eigenfrequency study solves the coupled pencil (no mass on phi) with the eigen solver: voltage electrodes held at 0 give the short-circuit (resonance) frequencies, floating ones with charge 0 the open-circuit (antiresonance) frequencies; k_eff^2 = (f_a^2 - f_r^2) / f_a^2 from two runs. The frequency_response study drives the electrodes harmonically (voltages and charges as amplitudes, losses mechanical_loss_factor / dielectric_loss_tangent) and its admittance feature gives Y(f) with a Butterworth-Van Dyke fit (f_s, f_p, k_eff^2, C0, R1, L1, C1). Outputs electric_potential / electric_field_x / _y and the stress with its -e^T E part (stress_zz with piezo_e13 / _e23). Stiffness: youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio or the c_ij entries (a {'model': 'crystal'} entry sets c_ij, piezo_e* and eps_dc*). Not with axial_wavenumber or the optomechanics study; the host factor limits it to ~10^6 dofs (3 per node).
- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Triangle meshes only (mesh kind 'triangles'; a tensor mesh ignores it: bilinear cells): the displacement elements. quadratic (default, the industry standard): P2 Lagrange, isoparametric on curved boundaries (circle / ellipse edges follow the drawn curve), strain and stress linear per element; linear: P1, constant strain per element (stiff in bending, locks toward poisson_ratio 0.5). Unknowns per element and component: ~2 (quadratic) or ~0.5 (linear); one host SuperLU per assembly (sparse_direct). Displayed strain / stress are averaged at the nodes over the solid elements around them (a material interface is smeared over one element; displacements and the state() element values are not).
- `pml_x_lo` (bool; default false) - PML on x_lo
  Triangle mesh, eigenfrequency study only: an elastic perfectly matched layer beyond x_lo. The mesh grows a ring of pml_cells x the mesh dx there (the MeshSpec pml_layers element layers across), its material continued from the window edge, with the complex coordinate stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness; axisymmetric: the stretched radius r~ beyond x_hi), beta set by pml_reflection at the target frequency for the fastest wave sqrt(c_II / rho) of the ring; its outer side is clamped. Waves leaving the window through that face are absorbed, so the modes are complex: frequency_imag > 0 and the radiation Q = f / (2 frequency_imag) in the Resonance table (mode shapes shown as their real part and |u|); modes with more than half of their |u|^2 in the ring are PML modes and dropped. The pencil stays linear in omega^2 (beta is frequency independent); absorption weakens for modes far below the target. With stress_stiffening the static prestress state treats the ring as an ordinary (unstretched) elastic continuation clamped at its outer side, and its K_sigma is stretched like K. Supports and loads must stay off x_lo (the inner side of the ring); not on x_lo of an axisymmetric solid (the axis). Needs target_frequency > 0.
- `pml_x_hi` (bool; default false) - PML on x_hi
  Triangle mesh, eigenfrequency study only: an elastic perfectly matched layer beyond x_hi. The mesh grows a ring of pml_cells x the mesh dx there (the MeshSpec pml_layers element layers across), its material continued from the window edge, with the complex coordinate stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness; axisymmetric: the stretched radius r~ beyond x_hi), beta set by pml_reflection at the target frequency for the fastest wave sqrt(c_II / rho) of the ring; its outer side is clamped. Waves leaving the window through that face are absorbed, so the modes are complex: frequency_imag > 0 and the radiation Q = f / (2 frequency_imag) in the Resonance table (mode shapes shown as their real part and |u|); modes with more than half of their |u|^2 in the ring are PML modes and dropped. The pencil stays linear in omega^2 (beta is frequency independent); absorption weakens for modes far below the target. With stress_stiffening the static prestress state treats the ring as an ordinary (unstretched) elastic continuation clamped at its outer side, and its K_sigma is stretched like K. Supports and loads must stay off x_hi (the inner side of the ring); not on x_lo of an axisymmetric solid (the axis). Needs target_frequency > 0.
- `pml_y_lo` (bool; default false) - PML on y_lo
  Triangle mesh, eigenfrequency study only: an elastic perfectly matched layer beyond y_lo. The mesh grows a ring of pml_cells x the mesh dx there (the MeshSpec pml_layers element layers across), its material continued from the window edge, with the complex coordinate stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness; axisymmetric: the stretched radius r~ beyond x_hi), beta set by pml_reflection at the target frequency for the fastest wave sqrt(c_II / rho) of the ring; its outer side is clamped. Waves leaving the window through that face are absorbed, so the modes are complex: frequency_imag > 0 and the radiation Q = f / (2 frequency_imag) in the Resonance table (mode shapes shown as their real part and |u|); modes with more than half of their |u|^2 in the ring are PML modes and dropped. The pencil stays linear in omega^2 (beta is frequency independent); absorption weakens for modes far below the target. With stress_stiffening the static prestress state treats the ring as an ordinary (unstretched) elastic continuation clamped at its outer side, and its K_sigma is stretched like K. Supports and loads must stay off y_lo (the inner side of the ring); not on x_lo of an axisymmetric solid (the axis). Needs target_frequency > 0.
- `pml_y_hi` (bool; default false) - PML on y_hi
  Triangle mesh, eigenfrequency study only: an elastic perfectly matched layer beyond y_hi. The mesh grows a ring of pml_cells x the mesh dx there (the MeshSpec pml_layers element layers across), its material continued from the window edge, with the complex coordinate stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (fem.pml; d the depth, w the thickness; axisymmetric: the stretched radius r~ beyond x_hi), beta set by pml_reflection at the target frequency for the fastest wave sqrt(c_II / rho) of the ring; its outer side is clamped. Waves leaving the window through that face are absorbed, so the modes are complex: frequency_imag > 0 and the radiation Q = f / (2 frequency_imag) in the Resonance table (mode shapes shown as their real part and |u|); modes with more than half of their |u|^2 in the ring are PML modes and dropped. The pencil stays linear in omega^2 (beta is frequency independent); absorption weakens for modes far below the target. With stress_stiffening the static prestress state treats the ring as an ordinary (unstretched) elastic continuation clamped at its outer side, and its K_sigma is stretched like K. Supports and loads must stay off y_hi (the inner side of the ring); not on x_lo of an axisymmetric solid (the axis). Needs target_frequency > 0.
- `pml_cells` (int; unit 1; default 8; range [1, 100]) - PML thickness (elements)
  Thickness of the elastic PML ring in multiples of the mesh dx (h_max) on every pml_<face> face (the MeshSpec pml_layers sets the element layers across it); the profile needs about 6-10 layers, and the ring should span a fair part of the longest wavelength (c / f at the target) for a low reflection.
- `pml_reflection` (float; unit 1; default 1e-06; range (0, 1]) - PML reflection
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.pml_reflection`

### Material properties (MaterialSpec.properties)

- `youngs_modulus` (float; unit Pa; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays youngs_modulus) - Young's modulus
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.youngs_modulus`
- `poisson_ratio` (float; unit 1; range (-1, 0.499]; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays poisson_ratio) - Poisson ratio
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.poisson_ratio`
- `alpha` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays alpha_xx, alpha_yy, alpha_zz) - Thermal expansion coefficient
  Linear thermal expansion coefficient; also read by heat_em_thermo_optic (see the heat type).
- `alpha_xx` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays alpha_xx) - Thermal expansion along x
  Expansion coefficient along x (see alpha).
- `alpha_yy` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays alpha_yy) - Thermal expansion along y
  Expansion coefficient along y (see alpha).
- `alpha_zz` (float; unit 1/K; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays alpha_zz) - Thermal expansion along z
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.alpha_zz`
- `photoelastic_p11` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays photoelastic_p11) - Photoelastic coefficient p11
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p11`
- `photoelastic_p12` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays photoelastic_p12) - Photoelastic coefficient p12
  Help: shared `elastic_waves.photoelastic_p12`
- `rho` (float; unit kg/m^3; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays rho) - Density
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.rho`
- `photoelastic_p44` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays photoelastic_p44) - Photoelastic coefficient p44
  Shear strain-optic coefficient p44 (Voigt: Delta(1/n^2)_xy = p44 x the engineering shear 2 strain_xy; cubic crystal axes along x, y, z), read only by the optomechanical_coupling g0 overlap (solid_em_strain_optic and acoustics_em_acousto_optic have no shear term). Unset = the isotropic (photoelastic_p11 - photoelastic_p12) / 2 per cell. Typical: silicon -0.051 (silica isotropic, -0.075).
- `piezo_e11` (float; unit C/m^2; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays piezo_e11) - Piezoelectric e11
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.piezo_e11`
- `piezo_e12` (float; unit C/m^2; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays piezo_e12) - Piezoelectric e12
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.piezo_e12`
- `piezo_e16` (float; unit C/m^2; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays piezo_e16) - Piezoelectric e16
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.piezo_e16`
- `piezo_e21` (float; unit C/m^2; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays piezo_e21) - Piezoelectric e21
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.piezo_e21`
- `piezo_e22` (float; unit C/m^2; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays piezo_e22) - Piezoelectric e22
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.piezo_e22`
- `piezo_e26` (float; unit C/m^2; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays piezo_e26) - Piezoelectric e26
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.piezo_e26`
- `piezo_e13` (float; unit C/m^2; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays piezo_e13) - Piezoelectric e13
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.piezo_e13`
- `piezo_e23` (float; unit C/m^2; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays piezo_e23) - Piezoelectric e23
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.piezo_e23`
- `eps_dc` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_xx, eps_dc_yy) - Static relative permittivity
  Isotropic static relative permittivity (>= 1): sets eps_dc_xx and eps_dc_yy (component entries override it); unset = 1 (vacuum). The same arrays as electrostatics / drift_diffusion; solid_mechanics reads them only with piezoelectric on, as the clamped (constant-strain) permittivity eps^S of every window cell, void ones included. NOT the optical eps_r: lithium niobate eps^S 44 / 29 (along the optic axis), silica 3.9.
- `eps_dc_xx` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_xx) - Static relative permittivity along x
  Static relative permittivity along x (>= 1); overrides eps_dc for this axis.
- `eps_dc_yy` (float; unit 1; range [1, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_yy) - Static relative permittivity along y
  Static relative permittivity along y (>= 1); overrides eps_dc for this axis.
- `eps_dc_xy` (float; unit 1; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays eps_dc_xy) - Static relative permittivity, cross term
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.eps_dc_xy`
- `c11` (float; unit Pa; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays c11) - Stiffness c11
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.c11`
- `c12` (float; unit Pa; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays c12) - Stiffness c12
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.c12`
- `c13` (float; unit Pa; optional (null allowed); may use x, y; may use physics fields; writes arrays c13) - Stiffness c13
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.c13`

Output fields (primary u_abs):

- `stress_yy` - Stress yy (Pa)

- `strain_yy` - Strain yy (1)

- `elastic_strain_xx` - Elastic strain xx (1)
- `elastic_strain_yy` - Elastic strain yy (1)
- `elastic_strain_zz` - Elastic strain zz (out of plane) (1)

- `body_force_y` - Coupled body force y (N/m^3)

### Source slots

- `temperature_rise` (K): Coupled temperature above the stress-free state (heat_solid_thermal_strain: heat T - T0), added to the temperature_change features (field temperature_rise_ext); each transfer replaces it.
- `body_force_x` (N/m^3): Coupled body force density along x (an optical or Lorentz force; several such couplings add), added to the body_force features; each transfer replaces it; void cells drop it.
- `body_force_y` (N/m^3): Coupled body force density along y, as body_force_x.

### Feature `solid_mechanics.fixed` - Fixed

Clamped support: u_x = u_y = 0 (and u_z = 0 for guided modes, axial_wavenumber). Outer faces only (a support on an object boundary: Fixed (domain) on the object). Holds every node of the face, corners included. Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, F_x, F_y] (units '', N/m, N/m; with the thickness setting N, N for that thickness; geometry axisymmetric: N, N of the whole ring) and the extras F_x and F_y: the force per m of depth the support exerts on the solid (sum of K u - f over its held dofs, so components it does not hold read 0); a dof held by two supports counts in both (the later value holds it). After a frequency_response study on a triangle mesh: a table of the complex reaction per solved frequency instead, columns frequency, F_x_re, F_x_im, F_y_re, F_y_im (Hz and the force unit above).

- FeatureSpec.type `fixed`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `solid_mechanics.roller` - Roller

Roller (symmetry) support: the normal displacement is 0 (u_x on x_lo / x_hi, u_y on y_lo / y_hi), the tangential one free (zero shear traction; u_z of guided modes free too). Rollers on one x face and one y face hold a solid completely. Outer faces only (a support on an object boundary: Fixed (domain) on the object). Holds every node of the face, corners included. Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, F_x, F_y] (units '', N/m, N/m; with the thickness setting N, N for that thickness; geometry axisymmetric: N, N of the whole ring) and the extras F_x and F_y: the force per m of depth the support exerts on the solid (sum of K u - f over its held dofs, so components it does not hold read 0); a dof held by two supports counts in both (the later value holds it). After a frequency_response study on a triangle mesh: a table of the complex reaction per solved frequency instead, columns frequency, F_x_re, F_x_im, F_y_re, F_y_im (Hz and the force unit above).

- FeatureSpec.type `roller`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `solid_mechanics.displacement` - Displacement

Prescribed displacement: u_x and / or u_y [m] on every node of the selected faces; an empty component stays free (validation error when both are empty; u_z of guided modes stays free). A later support on the same face component sets its value (warning). Outer faces only (a support on an object boundary: Fixed (domain) on the object). Holds every node of the face, corners included. Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, F_x, F_y] (units '', N/m, N/m; with the thickness setting N, N for that thickness; geometry axisymmetric: N, N of the whole ring) and the extras F_x and F_y: the force per m of depth the support exerts on the solid (sum of K u - f over its held dofs, so components it does not hold read 0); a dof held by two supports counts in both (the later value holds it). After a frequency_response study on a triangle mesh: a table of the complex reaction per solved frequency instead, columns frequency, F_x_re, F_x_im, F_y_re, F_y_im (Hz and the force unit above).

- FeatureSpec.type `displacement`; category boundary_condition

### Feature `solid_mechanics.prescribed_displacement_domain` - Prescribed displacement (domain)

Triangle meshes: prescribed displacement per component on every node of the selected elements: u_x and / or u_y [m], an empty component stays free (validation error when both are empty), e.g. u_x = 0 with u_y free on a thin strip that may deflect but not slide (with geometric nonlinearity a no-slip string). Holding u_x on every node across a member also locks the rotation of its cross-sections (bending becomes shear). A later support on the same node component sets its value. Result 'table' of the latest solve with one row [feature, F_x, F_y] (units '', N/m, N/m; with the thickness setting N, N for that thickness; geometry axisymmetric: N, N of the whole ring) and the extras F_x and F_y: the force per m of depth the support exerts on the solid (sum of K u - f over its held dofs, so components it does not hold read 0); a dof held by two supports counts in both (the later value holds it). After a frequency_response study on a triangle mesh: a table of the complex reaction per solved frequency instead, columns frequency, F_x_re, F_x_im, F_y_re, F_y_im (Hz and the force unit above).

- FeatureSpec.type `prescribed_displacement_domain`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):

### Feature `solid_mechanics.boundary_load` - Boundary load

Surface traction (t_x, t_y) [Pa] on outer faces, in the model axes (not the face normal): consistent nodal forces t * half of each adjacent face segment, per m of depth (geometry axisymmetric: t times the tributary ring area, N; on x_hi the cylinder r = R, on a y face the annulus). Several loads add; on a held component it only enters the reaction.

- FeatureSpec.type `boundary_load`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `t_x` (float; unit Pa; default 0) - Traction x
  Force per area along +x on the selected outer faces (a pressure p pushing into the x_hi face is t_x = -p).
- `t_y` (float; unit Pa; default -1e+06) - Traction y
  Force per area along +y on the selected outer faces (a pressure p on y_hi is t_y = -p). Typical 1e5-1e8.

### Feature `solid_mechanics.segment_load` - Boundary load (segment)

Surface traction (t_x, t_y) [Pa] on a part of a boundary or along an interior line: each selected line must be horizontal or vertical (validation error otherwise) and acts on the node line (cell edge) nearest to it (validation warns beyond a hundredth of a cell): a line on an outer face loads that part of the face, an interior line a line force inside the solid (a traction jump across it). Consistent nodal forces: t times the integral of each node shape function over the segment, clipped to the window, so the total force is t times the segment length per m of depth, also when its ends lie inside cells (geometry axisymmetric: whole rings in N, a horizontal segment the annulus pi (r_1^2 - r_0^2), a vertical one the cylinder 2 pi r h). Several loads add. On a triangle mesh the line may run in any direction: the mesher puts element edges on it and the traction acts on them exactly (int t N ds per node).

- FeatureSpec.type `segment_load`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): line entities; object kinds line; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `t_x` (float; unit Pa; default 0) - Traction x
  Force per area along +x on the selected line segments (model axes).
- `t_y` (float; unit Pa; default -1e+06) - Traction y
  Force per area along +y on the selected line segments (a pressure p pressing down on a top face is t_y = -p). Typical 1e5-1e8.

### Feature `solid_mechanics.body_force` - Body force

Applied body force density [N/m^3], consistent nodal forces f * cell area / 4 to the four corners of each selected cell (geometry axisymmetric: f times the integral of the shape function over the ring volume, with x = r; f_x is radial); void cells (no youngs_modulus or c11 > 0) drop it. Several body forces add; the coupled slots body_force_x / body_force_y are separate.

- FeatureSpec.type `body_force`; category domain_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): domain entities; count at least 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result: none

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `f_x` (float; unit N/m^3; default 0; may use x, y) - Body force x
  Force per volume along +x; may depend on x and y.
- `f_y` (float; unit N/m^3; default -21600; may use x, y) - Body force y
  Force per volume along +y; gravity along -y is -rho g (silica -2.16e4). May depend on x and y.

### Feature `solid_mechanics.solid_probe` - Solid probe

Samples one output field in the cell containing the point (one sample per re-solve and one per stationary iteration or end-of-run flush, all at t = 0 in a stationary study); on a triangle mesh the nodal value at the point (the mesher puts a node there; strain and stress there are the node-averaged display values).

- FeatureSpec.type `solid_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `timeseries`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
- `component` (choice; default "u_abs"; choices u_x | u_y | u_z | u_abs | strain_xx | strain_yy | strain_xy | elastic_strain_xx | elastic_strain_yy | elastic_strain_zz | stress_xx | stress_yy | stress_xy | stress_zz | von_mises | electric_potential | electric_field_x | electric_field_y | strain_energy_density | kinetic_energy_density) - Quantity
  Output field sampled at the point (unit of that field); the energy densities on a triangle mesh only.

### Feature `solid_mechanics.frequency_probe` - Frequency probe

frequency_response study only (triangle and tetrahedron meshes): the complex displacement (exp(+j omega t), phase 0 = the drive) at the point per solved frequency, the nodal field evaluated there (triangles: the mesher puts a node on the point; 0 off the solid). Result 'xy' versus frequency [Hz] (core.harmonic_probe series): u_x_re / _im / _abs / _phase, u_y_re / _im / _abs / _phase (m; phase in rad, in (-pi, pi]); a derived value two_wave_fit pairs a _re series with its _im sibling. The record restarts with each frequency_response run.

- FeatureSpec.type `frequency_probe`; category probe
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): point entities; object kinds point; count exactly 1
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): triangles
- Result kind `xy`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `solid_mechanics.resonance_table` - Resonance table

Vibration modes of the last eigenfrequency study solve, nearest the target (the target_frequency setting) first, ranked by |omega - omega_target|. Result 'table', one row per mode: resonance_number, frequency, angular_frequency (1-based rank, Hz, rad/s); extras target_frequency (Hz) and selected_resonance. Undamped: every frequency is real (Q infinite), except with a resistive_load electrode (solid_mechanics_3d), which appends frequency_imag (Hz, > 0 decays), q_factor and energy_decay_rate (1/s, = 2 Im omega, the external coupling rate kappa_e). For a frequency versus a parameter add a derived value with source '<physics>.<this feature>', expression frequency, operation at and at = 0 (the first mode).

- FeatureSpec.type `resonance_table`; category monitor
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): none (a selection is ignored with a warning)
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, triangles
- Result kind `table`

Params (FeatureSpec.params):
none

### Feature `solid_mechanics.electrode` - Electrode

Electrode on outer faces (every node of the face, corners included). piezoelectric only (ignored with a validation warning otherwise): an equipotential electrode, connection voltage (held phi) or floating (one shared phi with a net charge). Two electrodes must not share a node (adjacent outer faces share their corner node: a build error; select both faces in one feature instead). Its nodes keep their mechanical supports and loads (a thin metal film without stiffness). Result 'table' of the latest static solve with one row [feature, V, Q] (units '', V, C/m) and the extras V and Q: the electrode potential and the net free charge on it per m of depth (Q = -sum of the phi rows of A x over its nodes, the discrete Gauss law; a voltage electrode: the charge its source delivered, so Q / V of a single driven electrode against ground is the capacitance per m of depth). Not available after an eigenfrequency solve.

- FeatureSpec.type `electrode`; category boundary_condition
- Selection (FeatureSpec.selection): boundary entities; count at least 1; outer faces allowed; object perimeters not allowed
- Result kind `table`

  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.electrode.connection`
- `voltage` (float; unit V; default 0) - Voltage
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.electrode.voltage`
- `charge` (float; unit C/m; default 0) - Charge
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.electrode.charge`

## Physics type `solid_mechanics_3d` - Solid Mechanics (3D)

3D static linear elasticity, small strain, isotropic cells (youngs_modulus, poisson_ratio -> Lame lambda, mu) with anisotropic thermal expansion alpha_xx / alpha_yy / alpha_zz: sigma = lambda tr(eps) I + 2 mu eps - beta dT, beta_i = 2 mu alpha_ii + lambda (alpha_xx + alpha_yy + alpha_zz), dT = temperature_rise (coupled, heat_solid_thermal_strain) + temperature_rise_ext (temperature_change features). Discretisation: trilinear bricks on the cells of the physical window, displacement on the cell corners, matrix-free stiffness product, 3 x 3 block-Jacobi PCG (about 20 iterations per cell along the longest window axis; pcg precision mixed runs them in float32 on float32 copies of the operator, refined against the float64 residual to the double answer: much cheaper per iteration on GPUs with slow float64 arithmetic); outputs at the cell centres (u = mean of the 8 corners; strain, stress and von Mises from the centre gradients), 0 in void cells (youngs_modulus 0: not solved, carry nothing), edge-extended into any PML shell. Forces and reactions in N. strain_xy / _xz / _yz are tensor shear strains (half the engineering strain); elastic_strain_* = strain - alpha dT. Faces without a support or load are traction free. Every solid region (cells with stiffness joined through faces, edges or corners) needs supports that stop all six rigid motions, e.g. rollers on one x, one y and one z face (validation checks the three directions, the build the rank per region; regions touching only along an edge or at a corner count as joined, so a hinge there shows as an unconverged solve). Bricks are stiff in bending of thin members: mesh a film with >= 4 cells through its thickness. A stationary study solves it after the physics it reads; in a time-dependent study it re-solves only when a material, support, load or coupled input changed (quasi-static, no inertia). On a tensor mesh an eigenfrequency study finds the n_resonances LOWEST undamped vibration modes K u = omega^2 M u (consistent trilinear mass of rho, needed in every solid cell; no target frequency): matrix-free shift-invert Lanczos at 0 (scipy eigsh, the eigen solver role arpack_shift_invert without a factor), each Lanczos step one block-Jacobi PCG solve of the stiffness by the 'linear' solver, which must be double or mixed; the Lanczos tolerance is at least 1000 x the CG tolerance (the inexact inner solves floor its residual), so the CG tolerance sets the frequency accuracy (1e-8: ~1e-8 relative; 1e-12 for exact checks). Cost: ~(n_resonances + 4) x a few solves of ~20 CG iterations per cell along the longest axis, no host factor (memory: a few float64 vectors on the run backend, the Lanczos basis on the host; the cpu backend runs numpy versions of the matrix-free kernels, the stiffness product numba-compiled when numba is installed, much slower per CG iteration than the GPU). Supports held at 0, loads / thermal strain ignored (no prestress); one snapshot per mode labelled "resonance k: f = <Hz> Hz" with the mode shape scaled to a peak node |u| of 1 m (strain and stress per that shape, no thermal part; support reactions are not available); the resonance_table feature lists the frequencies. Interior targets (an indefinite K - sigma M, which CG cannot solve) and free-free bodies are not available on that mesh. The strain-optic and optical-force couplings are 2D only (solid_mechanics); the optomechanics study runs on a tetrahedron mesh only, with em_fdfd_bor optics (optomechanical_coupling: the modes sampled on rings about the body-of-revolution axis; piezoelectric and periodic axes off). Output u_x, u_y, u_z are the displacement [m], u_abs its magnitude. The instance is usually named solid. On a tetrahedron mesh (MeshSpec kind 'tetrahedra', 3D Cartesian): Lagrange elements of the discretization setting (quadratic P2 default, linear P1 locks in bending and toward poisson_ratio 0.5; affine elements) on the window elements with stiffness (a PML shell is void); cells may also be anisotropic there: the 21 c_IJ material entries (Voigt 1 xx, 2 yy, 3 zz, 4 yz, 5 xz, 6 xy, engineering shear; T = c S - beta dT with beta_I = c_IJ alpha_J, shear rows included; an unset entry takes the isotropic value of youngs_modulus / poisson_ratio, a cell is solid when c11 > 0, the 6 x 6 must be positive definite; a {'model': 'crystal', 'plane': 'full'} entry sets all 21; a rectangular-cell mesh refuses them), one host SuperLU of the stiffness per assembly (linear solver sparse_direct, Automatic there; pcg does not run on tetrahedra), every support and load feature (Fixed, Displacement and Boundary load also on domain objects: their interface faces; Fixed (domain) holds every node of the selected elements), probes evaluated at the point; the eigenfrequency study then finds the n_resonances modes nearest target_frequency (0 = the lowest) by shift-invert Lanczos on a factor of K - sigma M (eigen solver factorization superlu on the host, or cudss / cudss_mixed: cuDSS LDL^T of the real symmetric pencil on the GPU, the mixed one in float32 refined to full accuracy); with target_frequency > 0 a free body (free-free: no supports, or supports that leave rigid motions free) is allowed in that study, its rigid-body modes (0 Hz) dropped, and in the frequency_response study (regular at f > 0), while static solves still need supports; a mechanical_loss_factor damps the modes there (complex frequencies, Q in the resonance table); initial_stress_* material entries prestress every static solve (total stress sigma0 + C eps - beta dT) and setting stress_stiffening adds the geometric stiffness of the static state to the eigenfrequency / frequency-response pencils; the frequency_probe feature and the support results record complex values per frequency; setting geometric_nonlinearity solves every static state by total-Lagrangian Newton iterations (Green-Lagrange strain, second Piola-Kirchhoff stress, load_steps, reactions from the internal force) and linearises the pencils about it; outputs strain_energy_density / kinetic_energy_density (time averages for a mode or a response; 0 on the rectangular-cell mesh); the Prescribed displacement (domain) feature holds chosen components of every node of a domain. state() and coupled slots are one value per element (centroid; heat on the same tetrahedron mesh couples through heat_solid_thermal_strain), displayed fields nodal (displacement exact, strain / stress averaged over the solid elements at each node: a material interface is smeared over one element). Setting piezoelectric (tetrahedra only): a potential on every window element (void ones dielectric) with the piezo_e* / eps_dc* material entries, Electrode / Electrode (domain) features (voltage or floating, charges in C), the static coupled solve by the linear sparse_direct solver, the eigenfrequency study on the coupled pencil (voltage electrodes shorted, floating ones open; each mode with its potential), outputs electric_potential, electric_field_* and electric_displacement_* (0 without it; the rectangular-cell mesh shows them as 0). The frequency_response study (tetrahedra only; elastic or piezoelectric with mechanical_loss_factor / dielectric_loss_tangent) factorises the complex symmetric K (1 + j eta) - omega^2 M once per frequency by the 'linear' sparse_direct solver (host SuperLU, or cuDSS LDL^T with back_end cudss on a GPU, its plan reused across frequencies); the Admittance feature gives Y(f) in S with the BVD fit and kappa_e. Settings periodic_x / _y / _z with bloch_kx / _ky / _kz (tetrahedra, eigenfrequency study only): Bloch / Floquet unit cells, u and phi on each hi face = the lo face values times exp(-j k L), the modes of the reduced pencil P^H K P, P^H M P (complex Hermitian, complex modes shown as their real part and |u|), a band diagram by sweeping bloch_k (template solid_bloch_band_diagram_3d). Settings pml_<face> (tetrahedra, eigenfrequency study, piezoelectric off): an elastic PML shell of pml_cells element layers beyond those faces (complex coordinate stretch, outer side clamped), complex modes with the radiation Q in the resonance table. Setting electrode_edge_size: a gmsh mesh refined along the edges of the electrode objects. The squeeze_film_damping feature (tetrahedra, eigenfrequency / optomechanics studies) adds the gas damping of a thin film under a flat face per mode (Reynolds equation on the face, vents, slip) to the resonance table. A Roller on a face of a crystal that is not mirror symmetric there gets a warning (a half model would be wrong). Sizes and estimates on tetrahedra are uncalibrated.

- PhysicsSpec.type `solid_mechanics_3d`; default instance name `solid`
- Supported studies: stationary, time_dependent, eigenfrequency, frequency_response, optomechanics
- Default study: {"type": "stationary"}
- Backends (SolverDefaultsSpec.backend): gpu, cpu
- Mesh kinds (MeshSpec.kind): tensor, tetrahedra; refinement indicator fields (when its solver has no error indicator of its own): u_abs
- Dispersion poles (MaterialSpec.dispersion): not used
- Features (topics `solid_mechanics_3d.<feature>`): fixed, roller, displacement, fixed_domain, prescribed_displacement_domain, boundary_load, body_force, temperature_change, solid_probe, frequency_probe, resonance_table, squeeze_film_damping, electrode, electrode_domain, admittance, optomechanical_coupling

### Settings (PhysicsSpec.settings)

- `discretization` (choice; default "quadratic"; choices quadratic | linear) - Discretization
  Help: shared `electric_currents.discretization`
- `target_frequency` (float; unit Hz; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Eigenfrequency target
  Eigenfrequency study on a tetrahedron mesh (MeshSpec kind 'tetrahedra') only: the vibration modes nearest this frequency are searched (shift-invert about (2 pi target_frequency)^2, moved 1e-4 above it so a target on a resonance still factors); 0 = the lowest modes. A free body (free-free: no supports, or supports that leave a rigid motion free) and a free Bloch cell (periodic axes with every bloch_k 0) need a target > 0: their rigid-body modes (f below 1e-4 x the target, six for an unsupported body) are dropped, and a target below the first elastic mode is fine. Static solves of a free body stay refused (a frequency response at f > 0 is regular). A tensor mesh finds the lowest modes only (matrix-free shift-invert at 0): a nonzero value is a validation error there. Ignored by the other studies.
- `stress_stiffening` (bool; default false) - Stress stiffening
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.stress_stiffening`
- `geometric_nonlinearity` (bool; default false) - Geometric nonlinearity
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.geometric_nonlinearity`
- `load_steps` (int; default 1; range [1, inf); visible when geometric_nonlinearity in (true)) - Load steps
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.load_steps`
- `nonlinear_tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-08; range (0, inf); visible when geometric_nonlinearity in (true)) - Nonlinear tolerance
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.nonlinear_tolerance`
- `nonlinear_max_iterations` (int; default 25; range [1, inf); visible when geometric_nonlinearity in (true)) - Nonlinear iteration limit
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.nonlinear_max_iterations`
- `tangent_update` (choice; default "every_iteration"; choices every_iteration | when_slow; visible when geometric_nonlinearity in (true)) - Tangent update
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.tangent_update`
- `piezoelectric` (bool; default false) - Piezoelectric
  On (tetrahedron mesh, MeshSpec kind 'tetrahedra', only): the full 3D piezoelectric solid. A potential phi (the Lagrange elements of the discretization setting) lives on every window element, void ones included as dielectric, and couples to the displacement through the 18 piezo_e* material entries (solid elements) with the clamped permittivity eps0 eps_dc (the six eps_dc_* entries, every window element, unset = 1): T = c S - e^T E, D = e S + eps E, E = -grad phi, div D = 0. Electrode / Electrode (domain) features fix phi (connection voltage; at least one, the ground, is required) or make an isolated equipotential carrying a net charge [C] (floating); every other boundary is insulating (D . n = 0). The coupled symmetric indefinite operator is factorised once per assembly by the 'linear' sparse_direct solver (host SuperLU, or cuDSS LDL^T with back_end cudss on a GPU), with the potential scaled to balance the blocks. With every e = 0 it is a 3D anisotropic electrostatics solve (electrode capacitance with fringing in the air around the solid). Outputs electric_potential, electric_field_x / _y / _z, electric_displacement_x / _y / _z and the stress with its -e^T E part. Studies stationary / time_dependent (static solves) and eigenfrequency: the modes of the coupled pencil (massless potential) nearest target_frequency by the 'eigen' solver, voltage electrodes held at 0 V (short circuit: resonance frequencies f_r) and floating ones at zero charge (open circuit: antiresonance frequencies f_a); their voltage / charge values are ignored there. Run the model once with the drive electrode voltage and once floating: k_eff^2 = (f_a^2 - f_r^2) / f_a^2. An electrode with connection resistive_load damps the modes (complex frequencies: kappa_e = 2 Im omega of that load). Each mode shows its potential (the voltage map) and E / D with the shape. frequency_response: the driven coupled pencil with eps (1 - j dielectric_loss_tangent), electrode voltages / charges as phase-0 amplitudes, the Admittance feature Y = j omega Q / V in S. A {'model': 'crystal', 'plane': 'full'} entry sets c_IJ, piezo_e* and eps_dc*. A rectangular-cell mesh refuses it.
- `electrode_edge_size` (float; unit m; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when piezoelectric in (true)) - Electrode edge size
  Piezoelectric on a gmsh tetrahedron mesh (mesher 'gmsh'): the element size along the edges of every domain object an enabled Electrode / Electrode (domain) feature selects (box edges, cylinder rims), growing by the mesh max_ratio away from them; 0 = off. The electric field is singular at an electrode edge, so the capacitance C0 and k_eff^2 converge slowly without it; typical a fifth to a tenth of the film thickness. Outer-face electrodes, spheres and shapes gmsh does not mesh conformally get none; the builtin mesher ignores it.
- `periodic_x` (bool; default false) - Periodic x
  Tetrahedron mesh, eigenfrequency study only: x_lo and x_hi are one Bloch-periodic pair, u and phi on x_hi equal those on x_lo times exp(-j bloch_kx L) (L = the mesh extent along x, exp(+j omega t)). The two faces must be meshed alike node for node (the builtin mesher does; mesher gmsh writes periodic surfaces for it); supports and electrodes must stay off them. The modes come from the reduced pencil P^H K P, P^H M P (complex Hermitian; real when every k L is a multiple of pi) and are complex: shown as their real part (phase 0) with u_abs = |u|, electrode tables not available. With every periodic bloch_k 0 a free cell keeps its rigid translations (and the rotation about a single periodic axis): set target_frequency > 0, which drops them, or hold the cell; a piezoelectric cell then also needs a ground electrode, while k != 0 needs none.
- `periodic_y` (bool; default false) - Periodic y
  Tetrahedron mesh, eigenfrequency study only: y_lo and y_hi are one Bloch-periodic pair, u and phi on y_hi equal those on y_lo times exp(-j bloch_ky L) (L = the mesh extent along y, exp(+j omega t)). The two faces must be meshed alike node for node (the builtin mesher does; mesher gmsh writes periodic surfaces for it); supports and electrodes must stay off them. The modes come from the reduced pencil P^H K P, P^H M P (complex Hermitian; real when every k L is a multiple of pi) and are complex: shown as their real part (phase 0) with u_abs = |u|, electrode tables not available. With every periodic bloch_k 0 a free cell keeps its rigid translations (and the rotation about a single periodic axis): set target_frequency > 0, which drops them, or hold the cell; a piezoelectric cell then also needs a ground electrode, while k != 0 needs none.
- `periodic_z` (bool; default false) - Periodic z
  Tetrahedron mesh, eigenfrequency study only: z_lo and z_hi are one Bloch-periodic pair, u and phi on z_hi equal those on z_lo times exp(-j bloch_kz L) (L = the mesh extent along z, exp(+j omega t)). The two faces must be meshed alike node for node (the builtin mesher does; mesher gmsh writes periodic surfaces for it); supports and electrodes must stay off them. The modes come from the reduced pencil P^H K P, P^H M P (complex Hermitian; real when every k L is a multiple of pi) and are complex: shown as their real part (phase 0) with u_abs = |u|, electrode tables not available. With every periodic bloch_k 0 a free cell keeps its rigid translations (and the rotation about a single periodic axis): set target_frequency > 0, which drops them, or hold the cell; a piezoelectric cell then also needs a ground electrode, while k != 0 needs none.
- `bloch_kx` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when periodic_x in (true)) - Bloch wave vector x
  Bloch wave vector along x in rad/m, used only when periodic_x is on: the phase step exp(-j kx L) per period L; kx and kx + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. Swept through a parameter, one eigenfrequency study per k gives the band diagram (template solid_bloch_band_diagram_3d). Typical: pi / L at the zone edge.
- `bloch_ky` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when periodic_y in (true)) - Bloch wave vector y
  Bloch wave vector along y in rad/m, used only when periodic_y is on: the phase step exp(-j ky L) per period L; ky and ky + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. Swept through a parameter, one eigenfrequency study per k gives the band diagram (template solid_bloch_band_diagram_3d). Typical: pi / L at the zone edge.
- `bloch_kz` (float; unit rad/m; default 0; visible when periodic_z in (true)) - Bloch wave vector z
  Bloch wave vector along z in rad/m, used only when periodic_z is on: the phase step exp(-j kz L) per period L; kz and kz + 2 pi / L are the same state; 0 = plain periodic. Swept through a parameter, one eigenfrequency study per k gives the band diagram (template solid_bloch_band_diagram_3d). Typical: pi / L at the zone edge.
- `pml_x_lo` (bool; default false) - PML on x_lo
  Tetrahedron mesh, eigenfrequency study, piezoelectric off only: an elastic perfectly matched layer beyond x_lo. The mesh grows a shell of pml_cells element layers (x the mesh dx) there, its material continued from the window edge, with the complex coordinate stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (d the depth, w the thickness), beta set by pml_reflection at the target frequency for the fastest wave (sqrt(c_II / rho)); its outer side is clamped. Waves leaving the window through that face are absorbed, so the modes are complex: frequency_imag > 0 and the radiation Q = f / (2 frequency_imag) in the Resonance table (mode shapes shown as their real part and |u|); modes with more than half of their |u|^2 in the shell are PML modes and dropped. The pencil stays linear in omega^2 (beta is frequency independent), so no iteration on the target; absorption weakens for modes far below it. Supports and loads must stay off x_lo (it is the inner side of the shell). Needs target_frequency > 0.
- `pml_x_hi` (bool; default false) - PML on x_hi
  Tetrahedron mesh, eigenfrequency study, piezoelectric off only: an elastic perfectly matched layer beyond x_hi. The mesh grows a shell of pml_cells element layers (x the mesh dx) there, its material continued from the window edge, with the complex coordinate stretch s = 1 - j beta (d / w)^2 (d the depth, w the thickness), beta set by pml_reflection at the target frequency for the fastest wave (sqrt(c_II / rho)); its outer side is clamped. The pencil stays linear in omega^2 (beta is frequency independent), so no iteration on the target; absorption weakens for modes far below it. Supports and loads must stay off x_hi (it is the inner side of the shell). Needs target_frequency > 0.
