- `reference_y` (float; unit m; default 0; visible when normalisation in (point)) - Reference y
  y of the reference point (normalisation 'point').
- `mechanical_quality_factor` (float; unit 1; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Mechanical quality factor
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.mechanical_quality_factor`
- `scattering` (choice; default "forward"; choices forward | backward) - Brillouin scattering
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.scattering`
- `prescribed_normal_displacement` (float; unit m; optional (null allowed)) - Prescribed boundary motion
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.prescribed_normal_displacement`
- `axis_x` (float; unit m; default 0) - Axis x (3D solid)
  Help: shared `solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling.axis_x`
- `axis_y` (float; unit m; default 0) - Axis y (3D solid)
  solid_mechanics_3d with em_fdfd_bor optics: y of the axis point (see axis_x).

## Coupling type `acoustics_em_acousto_optic` - Acousto-optic effect (elastic waves -> electromagnetic waves)

Acousto-optic (photoelastic) effect: each transfer writes, for every permittivity component ii of the EM physics (E_z: zz through eps_r_update; H_z: xx and yy), dn_ii = -1/2 n0_ii^3 (photoelastic_p11 e_ii + photoelastic_p12 (e_jj + e_kk)) of the elastic strain of the acoustic stresses (elastic_strain_xx / _yy: the in-plane stiffness inverted at the cell centres, fluids half the volumetric strain each, e_zz = 0 plane strain; the photoelastic math of solid_em_strain_optic without its deformation term); n0 = the E13 shared reference index. A crystal (a material with the photoelastic tensor entries photoelastic_p16 .. _p66, set by a {"model": "crystal"} entry) instead gets the in-plane row of its model-axis tensor, dn_ii = -1/2 n0_ii^3 (p_i1 e_xx + p_i2 e_yy + p_i6 g), g = 2 e_xy the engineering shear at the cell centre (mean of its 4 corners), unset entries = the isotropic values. em_fdfd_hz also gets the xy row in its eps_xy_update slot (a sum contributor): Delta eps_xy = -n0_xx^2 n0_yy^2 (p_61 e_xx + p_62 e_yy + p_66 g), isotropic p_66 = (p11 - p12) / 2 (so a shear wave in glass rotates the in-plane index ellipse; photoelastic_p44 is not read here: library silicon gets (p11 - p12) / 2 = -0.0555 instead of its p44 = -0.051: set photoelastic_p66 = p44 on the material for the cubic shear with cube axes along x, y); em_fdfd_ez needs no xy term (E_z does not see it). The anti-plane change (Delta(1/n^2)_yz, _xz) is dropped (validation warns for crystals). With piezo arrays the strain is the accumulated total strain. It is an E13 index contributor (adds to heat_em_thermo_optic / electrostatics_em_pockels on the same physics, one every). Only frequency-domain EM types: in a time_dependent study the EM physics re-solves on the frozen strain every k acoustic steps (its every, which this coupling inherits: transfer just before each re-solve), a stroboscopic sequence of optical states; an optical FDTD in the same run is refused (its step is ~1e5 times shorter). Choose k so k dt samples the acoustic period finely enough, keeping in mind each re-solve is a sparse direct solve.

- CouplingSpec.type `acoustics_em_acousto_optic`; source physics type elastic_waves; target physics type em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): not allowed (one mesh)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `currents_heat_joule` - Joule heating (electric currents -> heat)

Resistive (Joule) heating: q_joule in W/m^3 of the last electric_currents solve (J.E per cell: the dissipation of every face split between its two cells by their half-cell resistances, outer Dirichlet faces to their cell; a DC solve is time-averaged by construction) becomes the heat source Q (volumetric_power; heat ignores the edge-extended PML ring). It is an additive contribution: Q = the sum of every em_heat_joule / currents_heat_joule / fluid_heat_convection / magnetic_heat_induction coupling into that heat physics, all with the same every (validation error otherwise); a field_transfer into volumetric_power cannot be combined with them. Its integral over the window equals the sum over the voltage / terminal features of V * current exactly, so the derived integral of currents_q_joule is the electrical power per m of depth. The stationary fixed point is currents -> Q -> T -> sigma_dc(T) -> currents: a temperature-dependent conductivity is a sigma_dc expression of heat_T on the material (no coupling needed; the currents re-solve whenever it is rewritten, right after each heat step). In a time-dependent study leave every null or equal to the heat every, and the currents every at 1 (it re-solves only when something changed), so the q_joule sent before each heat step already uses the sigma_dc(T) of the previous one. Transient heat: each step uses the q_joule of the temperature at its start (explicit in the source), except the first step, which has no Joule source (the first transfer follows it).

- CouplingSpec.type `currents_heat_joule`; source physics type electric_currents; target physics type heat
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): its result moves to the target mesh (conservative)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `electrostatics_acoustics_piezo` - Piezoelectric coupling (electrostatics <-> elastic waves)

Piezoelectric coupling (planar, sagittal plane): each transfer hands the electrostatics E_x / E_y (cell centres) to the electric_field_x / _y slots of elastic_waves, which adds T = -e^T (E - E_last) to its stresses at once (piezo_e* material arrays in reduced Voigt form, usually from a crystal entry; the first transfer only records the field, the initial state being its equilibrium). Transfers right after the physics step (every 1 with both at every 1); a time-varying field comes from voltage / terminal waveforms (superposed static solves, the field at the end time of each step), so the stress at t_n uses E(t_n). back_action bound_charge (default, two-way): before the field, the bound charge rho_b = -div(e S) of the accumulated strain S (face form: the mean P = e S of the two cells per face; at a Dirichlet / Robin outer face of the electrostatics the cell P, its surface charge landing on the electrode; insulating outer faces none) goes into the electrostatics slot 'charge_density' and the electrostatics re-solves at the acoustics time, so D = eps E + e S is source-free and the waves are stiffened without lag (dt from c^D = c^E + e^T eps^-1 e). back_action none: one-way, wave speeds about K^2 / 2 low (~2 % for a YZ lithium niobate SAW). Not modelled: pyroelectric and thermal-strain charge, the anti-plane coupling of cuts whose model plane is no crystal mirror plane (validation warns).

- CouplingSpec.type `electrostatics_acoustics_piezo`; source physics type electrostatics; target physics type elastic_waves
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): not allowed (one mesh)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
- `back_action` (choice; default "bound_charge"; choices bound_charge | none) - Back-action on the field
  bound_charge (two-way): after every acoustic step the bound charge rho_b = -div(e S) of the strain goes into the electrostatics slot 'charge_density', the electrostatics re-solves (warm-started CG; with driven terminals only the DC part) and its E goes back in the same transfer, so the waves feel the piezoelectric stiffening without lag and the acoustic dt uses c^D = c^E + e^T eps^-1 e; costs one CG solve per acoustic step, needs the coupling every equal to the acoustics' every and writes charge_density alone. none (one-way): only the field is handed over (wave speeds about K^2 / 2 low, no charge back).

## Coupling type `electrostatics_em_pockels` - Pockels effect (electrostatics -> electromagnetic waves)

Pockels (linear electro-optic) effect: each transfer writes, for every permittivity component ii the EM type has (E_z types: zz through eps_r_update; H_z types: xx and yy through eps_xx_update / eps_yy_update; em_modes: all three), the index change dn_ii = -1/2 n0_ii^3 r_ii E_k with E_k = E_x or E_y of the electrostatics physics (field_component; V/m, E = -grad V) and r_xx / r_yy / r_zz the material Pockels coefficients [m/V] of the electrostatics vocabulary (isotropic r sets all three; 0 where unset). n0_ii = sqrt of the permittivity component before any coupling rewrites it (the E13 shared reference index; dispersive cells: sqrt of eps_r / eps_inf, the pole susceptibility never changes: validation warning). It is an E13 index contributor: with heat_em_thermo_optic on the same physics the slot gets eps = (n0 + dn_Pockels + dn_thermal)^2, so both couplings need the same every (validation error otherwise); an overwriting field_transfer on the slot, or a state-dependent permittivity property, cannot be combined with it. This is the diagonal of the Pockels tensor for one applied direction: x-cut lithium niobate in top view (crystal z along model x, electrodes either side of a waveguide along y, field_component x) has r_xx = r33 = 30.8e-12 (E_x of the H_z types sees n_e) and r_yy = r_zz = r13 = 8.6e-12 (clamped r^S, library lithium_niobate_x_cut); the sign follows E: a positive E_k with r > 0 lowers n. A crystal (a {"model": "crystal"} entry: the clamped r^S rotated into model axes, the tensor entries pockels_r11 .. _r62) adds -1/2 n0_ii^3 (r_i1 E_x + r_i2 E_y) from both field components whatever field_component, so the opposite-sign r22 terms of a rotated cut are included; clamped because the strain of a piezoelectric elastic_waves run adds its own index change through acoustics_em_acousto_optic (without that coupling, a slow drive of a free crystal sees r^T, larger for lithium niobate). em_fdfd_hz also gets the xy row in its eps_xy_update slot (a sum contributor): Delta eps_xy = -n0_xx^2 n0_yy^2 (r_61 E_x + r_62 E_y) (r51 of YZ lithium niobate); other in-plane EM types drop it, and every type drops the anti-plane change (Delta(1/n^2)_yz, _xz; validation warns for crystals). The applied field is the one of the last electrostatics solve: a stationary study applies it each fixed-point iteration (one iteration behind within the loop, as the thermo-optic coupling), a frequency_domain or mode_analysis study once after the background solve, before the wavelengths / modes. eps_dc differences matter: a dielectric with a high eps_dc (lithium niobate eps_c 28) between low-eps_dc cladding (silica 3.9) takes only a small share of the voltage.

- CouplingSpec.type `electrostatics_em_pockels`; source physics type electrostatics; target physics type em_eme or em_eme_3d or em_fdfd_3d or em_fdfd_bor or em_fdfd_conical or em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz or em_fdfd_nonlinear or em_fdtd_3d or em_fdtd_bor or em_fdtd_ez or em_fdtd_hz or em_modes
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): not allowed (one mesh)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
- `field_component` (choice; default "x"; choices x | y) - Applied field direction
  Component E_k of the electrostatic field (E_x or E_y of the source) that drives every index change dn_ii = -1/2 n0_ii^3 r_ii E_k; the other component is ignored, so align the material's r_ii with this direction (x-cut lithium niobate in top view: x, its optic axis). The crystal tensor entries pockels_r11 .. _r62 always use both components.

## Coupling type `em_acoustics_photoacoustic` - Photoacoustic heating (electromagnetic waves -> elastic waves)

Photoacoustic source: the absorbed power density q_abs [W/m^3] of the last solve of the EM physics (time-averaged 1/2 omega eps0 (-Im eps) |E|^2, as em_heat_joule) is added to the heating_power slot of elastic_waves, which multiplies it by its heating_envelope (gaussian: a laser pulse of energy density q sqrt(pi) heating_pulse_width; instantaneous: steady heating for the whole run, validation warns) and adds -gruneisen q to d(sxx)/dt and d(syy)/dt. It is a 'sum' contributor: several such couplings (e.g. one per wavelength) add; a field_transfer into heating_power cannot be combined with them. Time_dependent study: transferred after each re-solve of the EM physics (normally only its first, unless its permittivity changes).

- CouplingSpec.type `em_acoustics_photoacoustic`; source physics type em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz; target physics type elastic_waves
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): its result moves to the target mesh (conservative)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `em_heat_joule` - Joule heating (electromagnetic waves -> heat)

Joule heating: the absorbed power density J.E in W/m^3 (sigma_e conduction plus Drude / Lorentz currents) of an EM physics type with an absorbed_power output (em_eme, em_eme_3d, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical, em_fdfd_ez, em_fdfd_hz, em_fdfd_nonlinear, em_fdtd_3d, em_fdtd_ez, em_fdtd_hz; not em_modes, which solves eigenmodes without a source), taken through its take_absorbed_power() as the mean over the EM steps since the last transfer (an FDFD physics: the time-averaged power density of its last solve), becomes the heat source Q (volumetric_power) as an additive contribution: Q = the sum of every em_heat_joule / currents_heat_joule / fluid_heat_convection / magnetic_heat_induction coupling into that heat physics (e.g. E_z and H_z physics for unpolarised light, or optical plus resistive heating), all with the same every (validation error otherwise); a field_transfer into volumetric_power cannot be combined with them. With FDFD use a stationary study for one wavelength, or a frequency_domain study for a list (coupled wavelength scan: each wavelength a stationary fixed point of every physics, continued from the previous one in list order; no em_modes or time-domain physics beside it). em_fdtd_hz evaluates the loss on the cell faces that carry E_x / E_y and assigns each face loss to its lossy neighbour cell(s): the sigma_e part by conductivity, the Drude / Lorentz part to the dispersive cell(s); em_fdfd_hz uses each cell's own loss with |E_x|^2 and |E_y|^2 averaged over its two faces. Leave every null or equal to the heat every so each heat solve gets exactly the steps since the previous one (validation warns otherwise); runner.flush() at the end of the run sends the mean over the last partial window merged with the previous full one, so the final Q does not depend on where the run stops within a window (a study shorter than every * dt_EM has no full window and delivers its power only in that flush). A cw window W = every * dt_EM averages the cos^2 power exactly only over a whole number of half optical periods, else the mean is off by up to T_opt / (2 pi W), varying from cell to cell with the phase (validation warns above 1 % and names the nearest whole-half-period every). Transient heat lags one window: its step over [kW, (k+1)W] uses the power of [(k-1)W, kW], so the first interval has no source and the last window (and the flushed final Q) is never stepped (heat gets (K-1)/K of the energy of K windows). Pulsed (non-cw) EM sources feeding a steady heat solve, transient heat or such a short study give a validation warning.

- CouplingSpec.type `em_heat_joule`; source physics type em_eme or em_eme_3d or em_fdfd_bor or em_fdfd_conical or em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz or em_fdfd_nonlinear or em_fdtd_3d or em_fdtd_ez or em_fdtd_hz; target physics type heat
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): its result moves to the target mesh (conservative)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `em_semiconductor_generation` - Photogeneration (electromagnetic waves -> semiconductor)

Photogeneration: G = quantum_efficiency * q_abs / (hbar omega) [1/(m^3 s)], q_abs the absorbed power density [W/m^3] taken through the EM loss protocol take_absorbed_power() (em_fdfd: the time-averaged loss of the last solve; em_fdtd: the mean since the last transfer, which a second reader of the same source would reset: validation error), omega from photon_wavelength or the em_fdfd solve frequency. It overwrites the drift_diffusion slot 'generation' (one writer; the generation features add separately) and acts only on the free semiconductor cells (n_intrinsic > 0, not held by an ohmic contact). Every absorbing cell counts: the optical sigma_e / eps imaginary part of the EM material is the absorption, so give the semiconductor its band-to-band loss at the wavelength (library silicon is lossless). Use a stationary study (em_fdfd solves, then the carriers; with a plasma-dispersion coupling back to the EM physics the study iterates to the fixed point); a frequency_domain study does not feed harmonic solutions to a background physics (validation error).

- CouplingSpec.type `em_semiconductor_generation`; source physics type em_eme or em_eme_3d or em_fdfd_bor or em_fdfd_conical or em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz or em_fdfd_nonlinear or em_fdtd_3d or em_fdtd_ez or em_fdtd_hz; target physics type drift_diffusion
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): its result moves to the target mesh (conservative)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
- `photon_wavelength` (float; unit m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Photon wavelength
  Vacuum wavelength of the absorbed light, setting the photon energy hbar omega = 2 pi hbar c / wavelength; null = the solve wavelength of an em_fdfd source (its omega). Required for a time-stepped (em_fdtd) source (validation error).
- `quantum_efficiency` (float; unit 1; default 1; range [0, 1]) - Quantum efficiency
  Electron-hole pairs per absorbed photon (internal quantum efficiency); 1 for band-to-band absorption. Free-carrier or metal absorption creates no pairs: such cells are either not semiconductor cells (generation ignored there) or need a lower value.

## Coupling type `em_solid_optical_force` - Optical force (electromagnetic waves -> solid mechanics)

Optical (Maxwell-stress) force: the time-averaged force density f = -(eps0 / 4) |E_z|^2 grad eps_r (peak phasor E_z of the last em_fdfd_ez solve; non-magnetic, no electrostriction, the absorption force of lossy cells and the sigma_e / pole part of eps ignored) as a face jump: each cell face carries -(eps0 / 4) |E_z|^2 (eps_r jump across it) times its length, split between its solid cells (c11 > 0, else youngs_modulus > 0, as the solver) and divided by their area, so the force on a dielectric boundary lands in the solid next to it in full (E_z is tangential to every in-plane boundary, so |E_z|^2 is continuous there); into body_force_x / body_force_y as an additive contribution (it sums with magnetic_solid_lorentz_force, all with one every; a field_transfer into those slots cannot be combined with it). Only em_fdfd_ez: the in-plane E of em_fdfd_hz has a discontinuous normal component that this face form does not handle. Use a stationary study (a frequency_domain study does not feed harmonic solutions back).

- CouplingSpec.type `em_solid_optical_force`; source physics type em_fdfd_ez; target physics type solid_mechanics
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): its result moves to the target mesh (conservative)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `field_transfer` - Field transfer

Generic transfer: at every transfer the expression of value (source_field of the source physics), x, y (3D: z) and parameters is evaluated into one persistent float32 full-grid buffer and written into target_slot of the target physics. Slots overwrite (heat volumetric_power replaces Q; the EM permittivity slots eps_r_update / eps_xx_update / eps_yy_update replace their whole array, PML included; EM ez_source / hz_source keep the buffer and add it to E_z / H_z every EM step until the next transfer: a raw V/m or A/m increment per step, so its effect scales with 1/dt), so no other coupling may write that slot, not even an additive one (e.g. em_heat_joule, currents_heat_joule, fluid_heat_convection, magnetic_heat_induction, heat_em_thermo_optic, em_solid_optical_force). Slot units: describe, per physics type.

- CouplingSpec.type `field_transfer`; source physics type any; target physics type any
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): the source field is interpolated onto the target mesh

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
- `source_field` (str; default "") - Source field
  State field of the source physics read at every transfer (full grid, PML ring included); valid names are the source type's state fields, listed by describe (e.g. T of heat). EM q_accum is an accumulated energy density, not a power: use em_heat_joule for that.
- `target_slot` (str; default "") - Target input
  Source slot of the target physics written at every transfer; valid names are the target type's source slots, listed by describe. Every transfer overwrites the slot, so no other coupling may write it, not even an additive one such as em_heat_joule or heat_em_thermo_optic (validation error).
- `expression` (expression; default "value") - Transform expression
  Expression of value (the source field), x, y (in 3D models also z; cell centres, PML cells get the nearest window centre) and parameters, e.g. 1e-3*value; no other field names and no t. The result is written as float32 into one persistent full-grid buffer (a constant fills the grid).

## Coupling type `fluid_heat_convection` - Convective heat transport (laminar flow -> heat)

Advection of heat by the flow: each transfer evaluates q = -rho cp u . grad T [W/m^3] on the fluid cells (rho, cp of the material, u of the laminar flow, T the solve-precision temperature of the heat physics) and contributes it to the heat source volumetric_power (an additive contribution: it sums with em_heat_joule, currents_heat_joule, magnetic_heat_induction); it re-transfers whenever the flow or the temperature changed. The advective form uses face fluxes: interior faces between fluid cells with the mean of the two cell velocities and temperatures (second-order central, oscillation-free for a cell Peclet number rho cp u dx / k < 2), faces to solid cells carry nothing, outer faces only where heat holds a temperature (that face value is the inflow temperature; other outer faces carry no advective flux: an outlet with zero gradient). It vanishes for uniform T whatever the discrete divergence of u, so it conserves energy only to the accuracy of the flow. The advection is explicit (lagged): a stationary study iterates heat and this coupling (Picard, gain ~ the Peclet number rho cp U L / k over the heat diffusion length / pi; use the study relaxation < 1 when it oscillates or diverges at Pe >~ 3); transient heat steps with the source of the previous state (stable for u dt / dx < ~1). Set a Temperature condition on the inflow face of heat for the inflow temperature.

- CouplingSpec.type `fluid_heat_convection`; source physics type laminar_flow; target physics type heat
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): not allowed (one mesh)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `heat_em_phase_change` - Phase change (heat -> electromagnetic waves)

Phase change driven by temperature: right after every heat step it hands the heat temperature T (end of the step) and the heat time to every phase_change_medium feature of the EM physics, which advances its crystallinity over the elapsed heat time and rewrites eps / sigma_e on its cells (see phase_change_medium). Only in a time_dependent study with transient heat (validation errors otherwise); leave every blank (= the heat every). It overwrites the permittivity of those cells, so it cannot be combined with another coupling into the permittivity slots of the same EM physics (heat_em_thermo_optic, electrostatics_em_pockels, field_transfer: validation error), nor with a state-dependent permittivity material there. The absorbed power reaches heat through em_heat_joule as usual. With em_fdfd_* the FDFD re-solves after every update (stroboscopic, the time scale of GST switching); with em_fdtd_* every heat window of every * dt_EM advances it (femtoseconds: only very fast test kinetics or melting act). The cells are rewritten on the bounding box of each medium and the EM physics is told materials_changed once per update.

- CouplingSpec.type `heat_em_phase_change`; source physics type heat; target physics type em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz or em_fdtd_ez or em_fdtd_hz
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): the source field is interpolated onto the target mesh

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `heat_em_thermo_optic` - Thermo-optic effect (heat -> electromagnetic waves)

Thermo-optic effect: each transfer rewrites the permittivity arrays of the EM physics from the heat temperature T, with dT = T - T0 (T0 of the heat physics) and n0 = sqrt of the built permittivity component (the background eps_inf for dispersive materials), recorded before the first transfer. It is an additive index contribution: it hands dn = n - n0 per component, and eps = (n0 + the sum of dn of every index coupling into that slot)^2 (e.g. two heat physics, or later electro-optic couplings), all with the same every (validation error otherwise); alone it gives the formulas below. E_z types (em_fdtd_ez, em_fdfd_ez): eps_zz = (n0_zz + dndT_zz dT)^2 (1 + alpha_xx dT)(1 + alpha_yy dT) through eps_r_update. H_z types (em_fdtd_hz, em_fdfd_hz): eps_xx = (n0_xx + dndT_xx dT)^2 (1 + alpha_xx dT)(1 + alpha_yy dT) through eps_xx_update, and eps_yy likewise with n0_yy and dndT_yy through eps_yy_update. em_modes (a cross-section, E along x, y and z): all three, eps_zz through eps_r_update, eps_xx and eps_yy through their slots; there the plane is transverse to the propagation, and the exact image of a transverse stretch leaves eps_xx / eps_yy unchanged (isotropic alpha) and scales eps_zz and mu_zz by s_x s_y, so the alpha factor goes on eps_zz only (eps_xx = (n0_xx + dndT_xx dT)^2): mu_zz cannot be held, so the transverse expansion is only partly counted, and the axial path term (n_eff alpha_zz dT on the phase per length) is a post-processing factor. The alpha factor is the in-plane thermal expansion mapped onto the fixed grid (transformation optics: a structure stretched by s_x s_y is a medium with eps_zz s_x s_y), so n grows by about (1 + alpha dT) and the optical path as the real structure does; for H_z the exact image scales mu_zz instead, so only the phase index matches there. Applied per cell it is a first-order local approximation, exact only for an alpha uniform over the mode: cells with alpha 0 (cladding, air) miss their share of the stretch, so the expansion shift is under-counted by the mode energy fraction outside the expanding material. With an enabled solid_em_strain_optic (deformation on) into the same EM physics the alpha factor is dropped (dn = dndT dT): the solid strain then supplies the deformation, constraints and cladding included. Dispersive materials: the Drude / Lorentz susceptibility is never changed, so dndT shifts eps by 2 n0 dndT dT instead of 2 n(omega) dndT dT (too small by about n(omega) / n0; scale dndT by that ratio at the wavelength of interest) and alpha scales only the background (negligible for metals); validation warns for a dndT on them, or an alpha with a Lorentz pole. An isotropic dndT sets dndT_xx, dndT_yy and dndT_zz; off-diagonal dndT / alpha terms are not modelled. Each slot overwrites its whole array including the PML, so it cannot be combined with a field_transfer into that slot or a state-dependent permittivity property (validation error). Time-dependent study (every = the heat every): applied right after each heat step, so the EM steps of one heat interval see the temperature of the absorbed power of the previous one; stationary study: one fixed-point iteration; frequency-domain study: applied once after the heat solve, before the wavelengths (a coupled wavelength scan, e.g. with em_heat_joule from that EM physics: in every fixed-point iteration of each wavelength, as in the stationary study); mode_analysis study: applied once after the heat solve, before the mode solve.

- CouplingSpec.type `heat_em_thermo_optic`; source physics type heat; target physics type em_eme or em_eme_3d or em_fdfd_3d or em_fdfd_bor or em_fdfd_conical or em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz or em_fdfd_nonlinear or em_fdtd_3d or em_fdtd_bor or em_fdtd_ez or em_fdtd_hz or em_modes
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): the source field is interpolated onto the target mesh

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `heat_solid_thermal_strain` - Thermal expansion (heat -> solid mechanics)

Thermal strain: each transfer writes dT = T - T0 of the heat physics (its rise in solve precision, not the float32 T; T0 = the stress-free temperature) into the temperature_rise slot of a solid_mechanics (2D, with a 2D heat) or solid_mechanics_3d (3D, with a 3D heat) physics, which re-solves with the thermal load C alpha dT (alpha_xx / alpha_yy / alpha_zz; 2D plane strain turns alpha_zz dT into out-of-plane stress, in 3D it is an ordinary expansion along z). Window only (the PML ring of the slot reads 0). Stationary study: applied after the heat solve; time-dependent study: right after each heat step. One writer of the slot (a second one, or a field_transfer to temperature_rise, is a validation error); temperature_change features add to it. For the optics (2D only) add solid_em_strain_optic (solid -> EM): with its deformation on, heat_em_thermo_optic on the same EM physics drops its (1 + alpha dT) factor, as the solid strain then supplies the deformation.

- CouplingSpec.type `heat_solid_thermal_strain`; source physics type heat; target physics type solid_mechanics or solid_mechanics_3d
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): its result moves to the target mesh (interpolate)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `magnetic_heat_induction` - Induction heating (magnetic fields AC -> heat)

Induction heating: each transfer hands q_eddy + q_magnetic [W/m^3] of the last magnetic_fields_ac solve (time averages over a period: sigma_dc |E|^2 / 2 of the induced and solid-conductor currents, omega Im(nu) |B|^2 / 2 of mu_dc_loss) to the heat source volumetric_power as an additive contribution: it sums with em_heat_joule, currents_heat_joule, fluid_heat_convection, all with the same every (validation error otherwise); a field_transfer into volumetric_power cannot be combined with it. Its integral over the window is eddy_loss plus the integral of q_magnetic (magnetic_loss up to material-interface rounding; W/m planar, W axisymmetric: use the same geometry for both physics, otherwise a validation warning). Stranded coils carry no eddy current and their own resistive loss (resistance of the coil result) is not transferred. Transfers right after each magnetic solve; the magnetic solve repeats only when a material or source changed, e.g. a temperature-dependent sigma_dc expression of heat_T (no coupling needed; each change costs one host refactorisation unless the recycled factor converges, see the solve summary). Stationary study: one Picard fixed point; time-dependent: transient heat steps with the loss of the latest solve.

- CouplingSpec.type `magnetic_heat_induction`; source physics type magnetic_fields_ac; target physics type heat
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): its result moves to the target mesh (conservative)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `magnetic_solid_lorentz_force` - Lorentz force (magnetic fields -> solid mechanics)

Lorentz force density f = J x B [N/m^3] of a planar magnetic physics: f_x = -J_z B_y, f_y = J_z B_x with magnetostatics J = J_coupled + J_applied (coils, current sources) and magnetic_fields_ac the time average Re(J_total B*) / 2 of the peak phasors (the force at twice the frequency is dropped: a static solid sees the mean). Handed per cell to body_force_x / body_force_y as an additive contribution (it sums with em_solid_optical_force, all with one every; a field_transfer into those slots cannot be combined with it); solid_mechanics drops it in void cells (youngs_modulus 0), so a winding modelled as air carries no load. Only planar geometry: an axisymmetric magnetic physics is a validation error (plane strain has no image of a ring current hoop load). No magnetisation force (the force on permeable or magnetised material, Maxwell stress at mu_dc jumps) and no magnetostriction. Transfers right after each magnetic solve.

- CouplingSpec.type `magnetic_solid_lorentz_force`; source physics type magnetostatics or magnetic_fields_ac; target physics type solid_mechanics
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): its result moves to the target mesh (conservative)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
none

## Coupling type `semiconductor_em_plasma_dispersion` - Free-carrier plasma dispersion (semiconductor -> electromagnetic waves)

Free-carrier plasma dispersion: each transfer gives the index change dn = -(electron_coefficient N + hole_coefficient P^hole_exponent) from the electron / hole densities N, P [1/m^3] of the last drift_diffusion solve (0 outside the semiconductor; edge-extended into the PML ring), the same for every permittivity component the EM type has (E_z types: eps_r_update; H_z types: eps_xx_update / eps_yy_update; em_modes: all three). It is an E13 index contributor: the slot gets eps = (n0 + sum of the dn of every index coupling)^2 with n0 the unperturbed index, so it adds to heat_em_thermo_optic / electrostatics_em_pockels (all need one every); an overwriting field_transfer or a state-dependent permittivity property on the slot cannot be combined with it. The densities are absolute (dn relative to carrier-free material, as the library silicon index is undoped). Defaults: Soref-Bennett silicon at 1.55 um. The free-carrier absorption (Soref-Bennett dalpha = 8.5e-18 N + 6.0e-18 P [1/cm], N, P in 1/cm^3) is not part of it (the EM types have no loss slot): give the material a state-dependent sigma_e = n eps0 c0 dalpha, for silicon at 1.55 um (n 3.48, N, P in 1/m^3) sigma_e = 7.85e-24 * semiconductor_N + 5.54e-24 * semiconductor_P [S/m] (plus any background loss). Stationary study: one fixed-point iteration behind within the loop; mode_analysis / frequency_domain: applied once after the background solve (cross-section modulators with em_modes).

- CouplingSpec.type `semiconductor_em_plasma_dispersion`; source physics type drift_diffusion; target physics type em_eme or em_eme_3d or em_fdfd_3d or em_fdfd_bor or em_fdfd_conical or em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz or em_fdfd_nonlinear or em_fdtd_3d or em_fdtd_bor or em_fdtd_ez or em_fdtd_hz or em_modes
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): the source field is interpolated onto the target mesh

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
- `electron_coefficient` (float; unit m^3; default 8.8e-28; range [0, inf)) - Electron index coefficient
  a in dn = -(a N + b P^c), N [1/m^3]; default 8.8e-28 = Soref-Bennett silicon at 1.55 um (8.8e-22 cm^3); at 1.31 um 6.2e-28.
- `hole_coefficient` (float; unit m^2.4; default 1.34716e-22; range [0, inf)) - Hole index coefficient
  b in dn = -(a N + b P^c), P [1/m^3]; default 8.5e-18 * (1e-6)^0.8 = 1.347e-22 = Soref-Bennett silicon at 1.55 um (8.5e-18 with P in cm^-3); at 1.31 um 6.0e-18 * (1e-6)^0.8 = 9.51e-23.
- `hole_exponent` (float; unit 1; default 0.8; range [0, inf)) - Hole exponent
  c in dn = -(a N + b P^c); 0.8 for silicon (Soref-Bennett). Changing it changes the unit of hole_coefficient.

## Coupling type `solid_em_strain_optic` - Strain-optic effect (solid mechanics -> electromagnetic waves)

Strain-optic effect: each transfer writes, for every permittivity component ii of the EM type (E_z types: zz; H_z types: xx, yy; em_modes: all three), the index change dn_ii = (n0_ii + dn_pe) sqrt(1 + w (strain_xx + strain_yy)) - n0_ii with the photoelastic part dn_pe = -1/2 n0_ii^3 (photoelastic_p11 e_ii + photoelastic_p12 (e_jj + e_kk)) of the elastic strain e = elastic_strain_* (strain - alpha dT, e_zz = -alpha_zz dT: the measured dndT of a free material already contains its free thermal expansion) and w = 1 with deformation (total strain, void cells none: a first-order local image like the alpha factor of heat_em_thermo_optic; exact only for isotropic in-plane strain, see the deformation setting). Isotropic (or cubic, crystal axes along x, y, z) photoelastic coefficients p11 / p12; the shear term p44 strain_xy (an off-diagonal eps) is not modelled. It is an E13 index contributor: with heat_em_thermo_optic / electrostatics_em_pockels on the same physics the slot gets eps = (n0 + the sum of dn)^2, all with one every. Plane strain is exact for a cross-section (em_modes); an in-plane (top-view) EM target gets a validation info. Stationary study: after the solid solve; frequency_domain / mode_analysis: once after the background solve. Source solid_mechanics only: from a solid_mechanics_3d physics it is not modelled yet (the em_fdtd_3d material index cannot hold three continuous permittivity components, and the 3D deformation image is open).

- CouplingSpec.type `solid_em_strain_optic`; source physics type solid_mechanics; target physics type em_eme or em_eme_3d or em_fdfd_3d or em_fdfd_bor or em_fdfd_conical or em_fdfd_ez or em_fdfd_hz or em_fdtd_3d or em_fdtd_bor or em_fdtd_ez or em_fdtd_hz or em_modes
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): not allowed (one mesh)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
- `deformation` (bool; default true) - Include deformation
  Also map the deformation of the structure onto the fixed grid: n times sqrt(1 + strain_xx + strain_yy) (total strain, the eps_zz det F image of the in-plane stretch, the phase-index convention of heat_em_thermo_optic). On, heat_em_thermo_optic on the same EM physics drops its (1 + alpha dT) factor (the solid strain replaces it); off, only the photoelastic part. Exact for isotropic in-plane strain (thermal) only: the full image of a stretch e_xx != e_yy is anisotropic (E_z: mu_xx, mu_yy times 1 -/+ (e_xx - e_yy); H_z: eps_xx, eps_yy likewise), which no index slot holds, so the phase along a stretched axis (a strip under uniaxial tension, the hoop strain of a ring) is off to first order in e_xx - e_yy.

## Coupling type `solid_membrane_tension` - Film prestress (solid mechanics -> membrane)

Membrane tension from a plane-stress solid on the same triangle mesh: each transfer writes N_xx = h stress_xx, N_yy = h stress_yy and N_xy = h stress_xy [N/m] per element into the membrane slots coupled_tension_xx / _yy / _xy (overwriting: no other coupling may write them), which the membrane adds to its material tension (leave that unset when the solid gives the whole prestress; validation info otherwise). stress_ij is the total static stress of the solid (initial_stress + C (strain - thermal strain): the relaxed state of a prestressed film with holes) at the element centroid, the element mean for P1 / P2 on straight elements, so the cell integral of the tension is exact; void elements (no youngs_modulus) give 0, so with areal_density 0 there they are membrane holes (free edges); a void element with areal_density > 0 is mass without stiffness. h = the thickness param, else the thickness setting of the solid. The solid must be planar plane_stress on the membrane's triangle mesh (validation errors; no mesh transfer). Run order: in an eigenfrequency or frequency_response study set StudySpec.solved_physics to the membrane only: the solid then runs as a stationary background physics (validated and estimated as in a stationary study), its static solve comes first, the coupling transfers once, then the membrane resonances / responses are solved; without solved_physics the study solves the solid itself and the coupling is a validation error. A membrane PML ring gets no coupled tension (the solid is void there: warning). Linearised about the relaxed state: no stress stiffening of the solid itself and no bending.

- CouplingSpec.type `solid_membrane_tension`; source physics type solid_mechanics; target physics type membrane
- Across meshes (source and target on different meshes): not allowed (one mesh)

Params (CouplingSpec.params):
- `thickness` (float; unit m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Film thickness
  Film thickness h [m] in N_ij = h sigma_ij. Empty (default): the thickness setting of the solid (validation error when that is empty too); a value overrides it (a warning when both are set and differ).

## Study type `eigenfrequency` - Eigenfrequency

Source-free resonances (eigenfrequencies) of every physics listing eigenfrequency among its supported studies (em_fdfd_ez, em_fdfd_hz, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical, em_fdfd_3d, solid_mechanics, solid_mechanics_3d or membrane); the EM types are searched near the target = that physics' wavelength setting lambda_t (omega_t = 2 pi C0 / lambda_t). The FDFD operator is assembled at omega_t and the generalised eigenproblem L u = -(omega / C0)^2 M u (M = eps cells for E_z, mu cells for H_z) is solved on the host by shift-invert Arnoldi about omega_t (scipy eigs on a SuperLU factor: the eigen solver role, arpack_shift_invert, whatever the linear back end, so its size limit of ~1e6 unknowns applies). Accuracy limit: the material dispersion (sigma_e, Drude / Lorentz poles) and the PML stretch depend on omega but are evaluated at omega_t only, so the problem is linear in omega^2 by freezing them: a resonance far from the target carries an error of first order in |omega / omega_t - 1| (exact only for non-dispersive, PML-free models); for an accurate value set the wavelength setting near the resonance and re-run (a dispersive or open resonator converges in one or two such steps). The shift-invert shift sits 1e-4 above the target, so a target on a resonance still factors. Results: complex omega with Im > 0 for a decaying resonance (exp(+j omega t)), Q = Re(omega) / (2 Im(omega)) (radiation into the PML plus material loss), the resonance_table feature, and one snapshot per resonance number k of the stored fields (default each primary field and its _im partner) labelled "resonance k: lambda = <nm> nm, Q = <value>" (several physics: their names and values joined; mirror faces add the parity, "resonance k [x_lo symmetric]: ..."), nearest the target first; each field is scaled to 1 (V/m for E_z, A/m for H_z) real at its peak, and its in-plane fields come from the curl at omega_t. Afterwards each physics shows resonance 1 (Results.field); ticks = the number of resonance snapshots. Sources and monitors play no part (probe, flux and mode results stay empty). Every other physics must support the stationary study and runs as a background physics first (heat is always steady here), iterated to a stationary fixed point, then every coupling from background to eigen-solved physics (heat_em_thermo_optic, field_transfer, state-dependent material properties) is applied once; couplings or material properties reading an eigen-solved physics are a validation error. StudySpec.solved_physics (a list of physics names) restricts the eigen-solved physics to those listed: the others, also of an eigen-capable type, then run as stationary background physics and may feed the listed ones through couplings (e.g. a solid relaxed to its static state before the modes of another physics). For Q or the resonance wavelength versus a parameter use a parameter sweep with a derived value of the resonance_table result. solid_mechanics (2D plane strain): the undamped vibration modes K u = omega^2 M u (consistent mass of rho) nearest its target_frequency setting (0 = the lowest), host shift-invert Lanczos (scipy eigsh on a real SuperLU factor: the eigen solver role, arpack_shift_invert), exact for the discretisation (no frozen terms), Q infinite; with its axial_wavenumber setting k_z the guided (2.5D) modes u ~ exp(i (k_z z - omega t)) of the cross-section instead (u_z coupled; sweep a parameter for the dispersion f(k_z)); labels "resonance k: f = <Hz> Hz", mode shapes scaled to a peak node |u| of 1 m; loads and thermal strain play no part unless the stress_stiffening setting is on (triangle and tetrahedron meshes: the static state of every load, initial_stress and thermal strain is solved first and its geometric stiffness K_sigma joins K; a free body, Bloch cell or elastic PML takes the initial_stress alone). On triangle and tetrahedron meshes a mechanical_loss_factor eta makes the modes complex: K_el (1 + j eta) (K_sigma stays real), Q = Re omega / (2 Im omega) in the resonance table. solid_mechanics_3d: on a tensor mesh the n_resonances lowest modes only (no target), by matrix-free shift-invert Lanczos at 0 whose steps are PCG solves of its double 'linear' solver (no host factor; accuracy set by the CG tolerance); on tetrahedra the modes nearest target_frequency, with target_frequency > 0 also of a free body without supports (its rigid-body modes at 0 Hz are dropped). em_fdfd_bor (body of revolution): the same shift-invert search near its wavelength setting at its azimuthal order m, or n_resonances per order of its azimuthal_orders list from one assembly (resonance numbers run order by order, labels "resonance k: m = <m>, lambda = ..."), on the full-vector (r, z) curl-curl operator (E_r, E_phi, E_z; M = eps ring volumes); static gradient solutions (|k^2| < 1e-6 k_t^2) are dropped; each resonance is scaled to 1 V/m real at its largest component. em_fdfd_conical: the same search at its out-of-plane wave number k_z on the three-component curl-curl operator (E_x, E_y, E_z; M = eps of the E points), static solutions dropped as for em_fdfd_bor, each resonance scaled to 1 V/m real at its largest E sample; at k_z = beta the resonances are the guided modes of propagation constant beta (a k_z sweep gives the dispersion). em_fdfd_3d: the same search on the 3D curl-curl operator of the live Yee E faces (M = the face eps; squared Cayley map as em_fdfd_bor, static gradient solutions dropped), each resonance scaled to 1 V/m real at its largest E face; snapshots are its z cut planes; its host factor grows ~ n^(4/3) (size rule 1e6 / 4e6 E unknowns). membrane (triangles, 1D): resonances of -div(T (1 + j eta) grad w) = rho_s omega^2 w nearest its target_frequency (fem.harmonic_resonances on the eigen role; complex with loss_factor / PML: Q = Re omega / (2 Im omega)), labels "resonance k: f = <Hz> Hz[, Q = ...]", scaled to 1 m real at the peak; clamps held at 0, loads ignored. Setting search: nearest (the above), targets (several targets from one build: one shift each, the union in frequency order) or band (every resonance in a frequency band, inertia-counted on real symmetric pencils) for solid_mechanics, solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra and membrane; the resonance_table then has target_frequency NaN and carries targets / band / expected_count.

- StudySpec.type `eigenfrequency`; needs a physics that steps in time: no
- Background study: stationary
- Mesh refinement levels: StudySpec.adaptation allowed

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `n_resonances` (int; default 6; range [1, 100]) - Number of resonances
  Resonances kept per eigen-solved physics: the shift-invert eigen-solve finds the 2 n_resonances + 10 eigenvalues k^2 nearest the target (k0 of the wavelength setting)^2, drops those with more than half of their |field|^2 dA in PML cells (and static / non-propagating ones), ranks the rest by |omega - omega_target| and keeps up to n_resonances (fewer may come back, with a run-log warning). With PML many candidates are PML resonances, so ask for a few more than needed. solid_mechanics (plane strain or guided) and solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra: the n_resonances + 4 eigenvalues omega^2 nearest (2 pi target_frequency)^2 (a free body: + its rigid motions, whose 0 Hz modes are dropped; with a loss factor or an elastic PML 2 n_resonances + 4 complex ones), ranked by |omega - omega_target|; solid_mechanics_3d on a tensor mesh: the n_resonances + 4 lowest (each Lanczos step one PCG solve). membrane: the n_resonances + 4 (real) or 2 n_resonances + 4 (loss_factor or PML: complex) eigenvalues nearest (2 pi target_frequency)^2, PML modes dropped. 1-10 typical. search targets: kept per target; search band: the resonances per shift of the march through the band (more per shift = fewer, larger shifts).
- `search` (choice; default "nearest"; choices nearest | targets | band) - Search
  Which resonances are solved. 'nearest' (default): n_resonances nearest each solved physics' own target (wavelength or target_frequency setting). 'targets': the union of the n_resonances nearest each frequency of target_frequencies (overriding target_frequency), from one build and assembly: one shift-invert factorisation per target (a cuDSS factor keeps its plan across targets), duplicates of two targets merged. 'band': every resonance with frequency_min <= Re f <= frequency_max (at most max_resonances, the lowest): shifts march upward, each trusting the eigenvalues out to its farthest one; a real symmetric pencil (an undamped solid without Bloch phase, a lossless membrane without PML) counts the modes per interval by Sylvester inertia (the summary gives the count, a short interval gets a repair shift, a mismatch a warning); damped, PML, loaded or complex Bloch pencils march with half-overlapping shifts and no count (warning: modes may be missing). targets and band list the resonances in frequency order (resonance 1 = the lowest). Types: solid_mechanics (piezoelectric: targets only), solid_mechanics_3d on tetrahedra (piezoelectric: targets only), membrane (the PML strength at pml_frequency, else the mean target / the band centre); the EM types and solid_mechanics_3d on a tensor mesh take nearest only.
- `target_frequencies` (float_list; unit Hz; range [0, inf); optional (null allowed); visible when search in (targets)) - Target frequencies
  search 'targets': the target frequencies in Hz (>= 0; 0 = the lowest modes of a supported solid; a damped, PML or loaded pencil needs > 0); n_resonances are kept nearest each, the union in frequency order. Overrides the target_frequency setting of every solved physics.
- `frequency_min` (float; unit Hz; default 0; range [0, inf); visible when search in (band)) - Band start
  search 'band': lower band edge in Hz (>= 0; resonances with Re f >= it are kept). A free body's 0 Hz rigid-body modes are dropped.
- `frequency_max` (float; unit Hz; default 1e+06; range (0, inf); visible when search in (band)) - Band end
  search 'band': upper band edge in Hz; must exceed frequency_min.
- `max_resonances` (int; default 200; range [1, inf); visible when search in (band)) - Most resonances in the band
  search 'band': at most this many resonances (the lowest of the band); the march stops once reached (warning). Bounds the run time and the stored mode shapes (one host vector each).
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf)) - Maximum coupling iterations
  Background fixed point, before the eigen-solve over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics in a coupling loop (each solved in model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); physics only fed by the loop (sinks: they feed no coupling back) are solved once afterwards, and a model without a loop is a single pass. Typically 10-50; a warning is logged when the tolerance is not reached. The loop stops early with a warning when the change does not decrease for 3 iterations in a row (from iteration 4) and fails the run when the fields turn non-finite.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, inf)) - Relative tolerance
  Background fixed point, before the eigen-solve over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes between iterations by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (the heat temperature T is compared as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for a loop gain g (ratio of successive changes): at g = 0.9 a change of 1e-4 means an error of ~1e-3. Anderson steps (anderson_depth) approach the remaining error itself, so there it is about the change. Typically 1e-4.
- `relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Coupling relaxation
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Coupling acceleration depth
  Background fixed point, before the eigen-solve over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m = this value, mixing parameter = relaxation): each loop-back injects its new value during the sweep (later physics of the sweep see it), then before the next sweep every loop-back value is replaced by the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and their changes (each value scaled by its largest magnitude; host float64 copies, ~3 m + 3 per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9 and 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. Like any secant method it can converge to a fixed point Picard cannot reach: an unstable branch (bistable thermo-optic loops) or, past a runaway (monotone g > 1), an unphysical one, so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` (float; unit Hz; default 5; range [0, inf)) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the live field frames the GUI shows while computing; 0 disables them. Frames never change the results (the headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Study type `frequency_domain` - Frequency domain

Time-harmonic solves at a list of vacuum wavelengths (exp(+j omega t), omega = 2 pi c / wavelength). Harmonic physics (types listing frequency_domain among their supported studies: em_fdfd_ez, em_fdfd_hz, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical (at a fixed k_z), em_modes, em_eme, em_eme_3d) are solved once per wavelength in list order; the study wavelengths override the wavelength setting of an FDFD or em_modes physics (em_modes: n_modes modes per wavelength, the mode of its mode_number setting in the snapshot, mode_dispersion results versus wavelength). Time-domain types (em_fdtd_ez, em_fdtd_hz, em_fdtd_3d, em_fdtd_bor: harmonic FDTD) instead run one pulse after the background solve, accumulating a running DFT of the whole physical window at every study wavelength until the field energy fell below auto_shutoff of its peak (or max_duration), divided by the spectrum of their shared source waveform (every source of one such physics: the same gaussian or ricker waveform, wavelength and bandwidth): the phasor response to a unit source at phase 0, as the FDFD gives it (output fields: <component>_re / _im / _abs / _phase, e_abs_harmonic, e_intensity_harmonic and absorbed_power_harmonic (time average); ez / hz: the out-of-plane component, stored by default ez_abs / hz_abs; em_fdtd_3d: ex, ey, ez at the cell centres, stored by default e_abs_harmonic; em_fdtd_bor: its own set, see its description); their monitors keep their own unnormalised pulse spectra. Memory: 8 (ez) / 24 (hz, 3D) bytes per window cell and wavelength. Every other physics must support the stationary study and runs as a background physics, solved first (heat is always steady here): the background physics and the couplings among them iterate to a stationary fixed point (max_iterations, tolerance), then every coupling from background to harmonic physics (heat_em_thermo_optic, field_transfer, material properties depending on background fields such as T) is applied once, so every wavelength sees the same background state. Coupled wavelength scan: when an enabled coupling or material property reads a harmonic physics (em_heat_joule or field_transfer from an FDFD physics, a property depending on its fields; every physics must then support the stationary study, so no em_modes or time-domain type), each wavelength is instead a stationary fixed point of every physics (max_iterations, tolerance, relaxation as the stationary study), warm-started from the previous wavelength in list order: an ascending list scans blue to red (the thermal triangle of a red-shifting ring), a descending one red to blue (hysteresis); one log line per wavelength with its iteration count, a warning when one does not converge (the scan continues), summary fixed_point over all wavelengths (converged = all, iterations and relative_change the largest) and wavelength_fixed_points [{wavelength, converged, iterations, relative_change, tolerance}]; a cancel inside a wavelength leaves its monitors holding the last iterate. Needs at least one harmonic physics. Stores one snapshot per wavelength of the stored fields (default each primary field, plus <field>_im next to an FDFD <field>_re, so |field|^2 per wavelength can be rebuilt; native window cells up to 250,000 cells, else nearest-cell resampled), labelled "lambda = <nm> nm"; the last wavelength stays the live state (Results.field), and feature results (probes, flux spectra) hold every solved wavelength (sorted by wavelength; snapshot labels keep the solve order).

- StudySpec.type `frequency_domain`; needs a physics that steps in time: no
- Background study: stationary
- Coupled points: couplings and material properties may read a physics this study solves; each point of the study axis is then a stationary fixed point of every physics
- Mesh refinement levels: StudySpec.adaptation allowed

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `wavelength_start` (float; unit m; default 1.5e-06; range (0, inf)) - Start wavelength
  First vacuum wavelength in m of the range solved when wavelengths is null or empty: n_wavelengths wavelengths spaced linearly in wavelength from wavelength_start to wavelength_stop, solved in that order. The study wavelengths override the wavelength setting of every FDFD physics. Typically 0.4e-6 to 2e-6.
- `wavelength_stop` (float; unit m; default 1.6e-06; range (0, inf)) - Stop wavelength
  Last vacuum wavelength in m of the range; must be greater than wavelength_start (equal is allowed with n_wavelengths = 1). Ignored when wavelengths lists any wavelength.
- `n_wavelengths` (int; default 11; range [1, inf)) - Number of wavelengths
  Wavelengths of the range, spaced linearly in wavelength (not in frequency); 1 solves only the centre (wavelength_start + wavelength_stop) / 2. Each wavelength costs one assembly, factorisation and solve per FDFD physics (harmonic FDTD: one DFT update per sample and 8 / 24 B per window cell of GPU memory). Ignored when wavelengths lists any wavelength.
- `wavelengths` (float_list; unit m; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Wavelength list
  Explicit vacuum wavelengths in m (each > 0), solved in list order; a non-empty list overrides wavelength_start, wavelength_stop and n_wavelengths. null or [] = use the range.
- `auto_shutoff` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, 1]) - Pulse shutoff level
  em_fdtd_* physics only (harmonic FDTD): the pulse ends once t is past the source pulse (2 t0) and the EM energy 0.5 sum(eps0 eps E^2 + mu0 mu H^2) dA over the physical window (checked about 10 times per wall second) is at most auto_shutoff times its running peak, or at max_duration. The truncated ring-down errs the harmonic fields by roughly sqrt(auto_shutoff) times the ring-down share of the response (more for slowly decaying resonances); 1e-4 typical, 1e-6 for percent-level comparisons.
- `max_duration` (float; unit s; default 2e-12; range (0, inf)) - Maximum pulse duration
  em_fdtd_* physics only (harmonic FDTD): upper bound in s of the simulated pulse time; when it ends the run before the energy fell below auto_shutoff a warning is logged (high-Q resonances: raise it). Typical 1e-12 to 1e-11 s.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf)) - Maximum coupling iterations
  Background fixed point, before the wavelength loop over the background physics only (unused without background physics; a coupled wavelength scan: the fixed point of every physics at each wavelength): Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics in a coupling loop (each solved in model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); physics only fed by the loop (sinks: they feed no coupling back) are solved once afterwards, and a model without a loop is a single pass. Typically 10-50; a warning is logged when the tolerance is not reached. The loop stops early with a warning when the change does not decrease for 3 iterations in a row (from iteration 4) and fails the run when the fields turn non-finite.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, inf)) - Relative tolerance
  Background fixed point, before the wavelength loop over the background physics only (unused without background physics; a coupled wavelength scan: the fixed point of every physics at each wavelength): Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes between iterations by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (the heat temperature T is compared as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for a loop gain g (ratio of successive changes): at g = 0.9 a change of 1e-4 means an error of ~1e-3. Anderson steps (anderson_depth) approach the remaining error itself, so there it is about the change. Typically 1e-4.
- `relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Coupling relaxation
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Coupling acceleration depth
  Background fixed point, before the wavelength loop over the background physics only (unused without background physics; a coupled wavelength scan: the fixed point of every physics at each wavelength): Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m = this value, mixing parameter = relaxation): each loop-back injects its new value during the sweep (later physics of the sweep see it), then before the next sweep every loop-back value is replaced by the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and their changes (each value scaled by its largest magnitude; host float64 copies, ~3 m + 3 per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9 and 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. Like any secant method it can converge to a fixed point Picard cannot reach: an unstable branch (bistable thermo-optic loops) or, past a runaway (monotone g > 1), an unphysical one, so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` (float; unit Hz; default 5; range [0, inf)) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the live field frames the GUI shows while computing; 0 disables them. Frames never change the results (the headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Study type `frequency_response` - Frequency response

Driven time-harmonic response (exp(+j omega t), omega = 2 pi f) at a list of frequencies in Hz, the frequency-domain study of the mechanics (the EM frequency_domain study takes wavelengths). Solved physics: every type listing frequency_response among its supported studies (solid_mechanics, solid_mechanics_3d, membrane or pressure_acoustics; solid_mechanics, 2D: planar plane strain / plane stress or axisymmetric; not generalized plane strain or guided modes; solid_mechanics_3d on a tetrahedron mesh; pressure_acoustics: -div(grad p / rho) - omega^2 p / (rho c^2) = j omega q on triangles / tetrahedra, its frequency_probe / surface_pressure records): (K (1 + j eta) - omega^2 M) u = f with the consistent mass of rho (every solid cell needs rho > 0), the loss factor mechanical_loss_factor eta and, piezoelectric, the coupled potential with eps (1 - j dielectric_loss_tangent); every load, prescribed displacement, electrode voltage and floating charge is the complex amplitude (phase 0) of the drive; one complex symmetric factor per frequency of the pencil reduced once to the free dofs (2D: host SuperLU outside the solver roles, counters in the summary; solid_mechanics_3d: its 'linear' sparse_direct solver, host SuperLU or cuDSS LDL^T with the plan reused across frequencies). Results: the admittance feature (Y = I / V of an electrode versus f with a Butterworth-Van Dyke fit), one snapshot per frequency of the stored fields (setting snapshots: all, last = the last solved frequency only, none; feature records per frequency are kept either way) labelled "f = <Hz> Hz" holding the real parts (phase 0) of the response, u_abs = the amplitude |u| of the complex displacement, u_x_im / u_y_im (/ u_z_im) the imaginary parts (triangle and tetrahedron meshes; store them through stored_fields); the last frequency stays live. On triangle and tetrahedron meshes the frequency_probe feature records the complex displacement at a point per frequency (series u_x_re, u_x_im, u_x_abs, u_x_phase, ...) and every support result becomes a table of its complex reaction per frequency (F_x_re, F_x_im, ...); solid_probe samples and electrode tables are not filled. With the stress_stiffening setting the initial_stress is first relaxed by a static solve (loads stay the drive, not a preload) and its geometric stiffness K_sigma joins K (real, no loss). A free body (no supports) is allowed: K - omega^2 M is regular at f > 0. Every other physics must support the stationary study and runs as a background physics first (its couplings into the solved physics applied once); couplings reading a solved physics are a validation error; StudySpec.solved_physics restricts the solved physics to those listed (the others run as background physics). membrane (triangles, 1D): the pressure_load / line_force / point_force phasors, one complex factor per frequency on its 'linear' sparse_direct solver, field_probe, port and mode_projection records per frequency. sweep_method adaptive / modal (membrane, the solids, pressure_acoustics) replaces the factorisation per frequency by a reduced model built first (see the setting). ticks = frequencies; summary response_frequencies (+ frequency_sweep with a reduced sweep). parity_sectors runs a half (quarter) model once per mirror parity and combines the drawn drive (see the setting; membrane symmetry / antisymmetry faces are mirror planes).

- StudySpec.type `frequency_response`; needs a physics that steps in time: no
- Background study: stationary

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `frequency_start` (float; unit Hz; default 1e+06; range (0, inf)) - Start frequency
  Lowest frequency in Hz of the range (used when frequencies is empty).
- `frequency_stop` (float; unit Hz; default 2e+06; range (0, inf)) - Stop frequency
  Highest frequency in Hz of the range; must exceed frequency_start (equal is allowed with n_frequencies = 1).
- `n_frequencies` (int; default 101; range [1, inf)) - Number of frequencies
  Frequencies of the range, both ends included, spaced as log_spacing selects (1 = the arithmetic or geometric mean). Each costs one complex sparse factorisation per solved physics; resolve a resonance of quality factor Q at f0 with a step well below f0 / Q.
- `log_spacing` (bool; default false) - Logarithmic spacing
  false (default): evenly spaced in f (linspace, a resonance sweep); true: evenly in log f (geomspace, a spectrum over decades). Ignored when frequencies lists any frequency.
- `frequencies` (float_list; unit Hz; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Frequency list
  Explicit frequencies in Hz (each > 0), solved in this order; a non-empty list overrides frequency_start, frequency_stop and n_frequencies. Feature results (admittance) are sorted by frequency.
- `snapshots` (choice; default "all"; choices all | last | none) - Stored snapshots
  Which frequencies keep a snapshot of the stored fields (the industry-standard store-fields-in-output choice): 'all' (default) one per frequency, 'last' only the last solved one (also after a cancel), 'none' no snapshot. Each snapshot holds the stored fields on up to 250,000 cells (~1 MB per field for a large window), so a sweep over hundreds of frequencies may keep only the last. Feature records per frequency (probes, port / support / mode_projection records, admittance) and the live last-frequency state are the same for every choice. With 'last' / 'none' the fields are formed for the last solved frequency only (every sweep_method; the live field view is not refreshed during the sweep).
- `sweep_method` (choice; default "direct"; choices direct | adaptive | modal) - Sweep method
  How the frequencies are solved. 'direct' (default): one complex sparse factorisation per frequency. 'adaptive' (asymptotic waveform evaluation / an adaptive fast sweep): a reduced model trained on the frequency list: factorisations at the ends and the middle, each adding the solution and rom_moments frequency derivatives (back-solves on the same factor) to a Galerkin basis, then one more at the frequency of the largest estimated relative residual until it is <= rom_tolerance or rom_max_points factorisations; every listed frequency is then a small dense solve (cheap: use a fine list). Pays off in a window with a few to tens of resonances; a band holding hundreds of modes needs as many basis vectors (keep 'direct'). 'modal': the modal_count eigenmodes nearest the band centre (the membrane's 'eigen' solver; the solids and pressure_acoustics a host shift-invert of K, M) plus the direct solution at the band centre (static correction of the truncated modes); exact for a uniform loss_factor once every mode is in the basis, approximate otherwise. Both end with one verification factorisation at the worst frequency; summary frequency_sweep {method, physics: {name: {basis_size, factorizations, expansion_frequencies [Hz], max_residual, worst_frequency [Hz], verified_error (true relative error there), converged, warnings, ...}}}. With a reduced sweep, probe / projection / reaction / electrode records come from the reduced coordinates and the fields are built only for the stored snapshots (snapshots 'all': every frequency, else the last). Types: membrane (not with ports), solid_mechanics and solid_mechanics_3d (modal: not piezoelectric), pressure_acoustics (a background_pressure_field or a damping boundary: adaptive only, one snapshot per expansion, no derivatives).
- `rom_tolerance` (float; default 1e-06; range (0, inf); visible when sweep_method in (adaptive, modal)) - Reduced model tolerance
  Largest estimated relative residual ||b - A x|| / ||b|| over the frequency list ('adaptive': training stops below it; 'modal': a warning above it). Near a resonance of quality factor Q the relative error can be up to about Q times the residual, so for Q = 1e4 peaks use 1e-8 or below; the summary reports the true error at the worst frequency.
- `rom_moments` (int; default 4; range [0, 20]; visible when sweep_method in (adaptive)) - Derivatives per expansion
  Frequency derivatives of the solution added per expansion frequency (adaptive): back-solves on the factor already made, so each factorisation adds rom_moments + 1 basis vectors.
- `rom_max_points` (int; default 40; range [1, inf); visible when sweep_method in (adaptive)) - Most expansion frequencies
  Largest number of expansion frequencies (factorisations, not counting the verification) of the adaptive model; reaching it without rom_tolerance logs a warning.
- `modal_count` (int; default 20; range [1, inf); visible when sweep_method in (modal)) - Number of modes
  Eigenmodes nearest the band centre (frequency list's (min + max) / 2) in the modal basis; take every resonance of the band plus a margin on either side.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf)) - Maximum coupling iterations
  Background fixed point, before the frequency solves over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics in a coupling loop (each solved in model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); physics only fed by the loop (sinks: they feed no coupling back) are solved once afterwards, and a model without a loop is a single pass. Typically 10-50; a warning is logged when the tolerance is not reached. The loop stops early with a warning when the change does not decrease for 3 iterations in a row (from iteration 4) and fails the run when the fields turn non-finite.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, inf)) - Relative tolerance
  Background fixed point, before the frequency solves over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes between iterations by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (the heat temperature T is compared as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for a loop gain g (ratio of successive changes): at g = 0.9 a change of 1e-4 means an error of ~1e-3. Anderson steps (anderson_depth) approach the remaining error itself, so there it is about the change. Typically 1e-4.
- `relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Coupling relaxation
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Coupling acceleration depth
  Background fixed point, before the frequency solves over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m = this value, mixing parameter = relaxation): each loop-back injects its new value during the sweep (later physics of the sweep see it), then before the next sweep every loop-back value is replaced by the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and their changes (each value scaled by its largest magnitude; host float64 copies, ~3 m + 3 per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9 and 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. Like any secant method it can converge to a fixed point Picard cannot reach: an unstable branch (bistable thermo-optic loops) or, past a runaway (monotone g > 1), an unphysical one, so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` (float; unit Hz; default 5; range [0, inf)) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the live field frames the GUI shows while computing; 0 disables them. Frames never change the results (the headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Study type `mode_analysis` - Mode analysis

Cross-section eigenmode solve: every physics listing mode_analysis among its supported studies (em_modes) computes its n_modes modes at its wavelength setting (the xy plane is the waveguide cross-section, propagation along z). Every other physics must support the stationary study and runs as a background physics, solved first (heat is always steady here): the background physics and the couplings among them iterate to a stationary fixed point (max_iterations, tolerance), then every coupling from background to mode physics (heat_em_thermo_optic, field_transfer, material properties depending on background fields such as T) is applied once before the mode solve. Couplings or material properties that read a mode physics are a validation error (mode solutions are not fed back). Stores one snapshot per mode number k of the stored fields (default each primary field: em_modes e_intensity), labelled "mode k: n_eff = <value>" (a complex value when lossy; with several em_modes physics their names and values joined; mirror faces add the parity, "mode k [x_lo symmetric]: ..."), in the em_modes rank order (descending Re(beta^2)); afterwards each em_modes physics shows the mode of its mode_number setting (Results.field). ticks = the number of mode snapshots. For n_eff versus a parameter use a parameter sweep with a derived value of the mode_table result; for n_eff versus wavelength a frequency_domain study.

- StudySpec.type `mode_analysis`; needs a physics that steps in time: no
- Background study: stationary
- Mesh refinement levels: StudySpec.adaptation allowed

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf)) - Maximum coupling iterations
  Background fixed point, before the mode solve over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics in a coupling loop (each solved in model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); physics only fed by the loop (sinks: they feed no coupling back) are solved once afterwards, and a model without a loop is a single pass. Typically 10-50; a warning is logged when the tolerance is not reached. The loop stops early with a warning when the change does not decrease for 3 iterations in a row (from iteration 4) and fails the run when the fields turn non-finite.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, inf)) - Relative tolerance
  Background fixed point, before the mode solve over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes between iterations by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (the heat temperature T is compared as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for a loop gain g (ratio of successive changes): at g = 0.9 a change of 1e-4 means an error of ~1e-3. Anderson steps (anderson_depth) approach the remaining error itself, so there it is about the change. Typically 1e-4.
- `relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Coupling relaxation
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`

  Background fixed point, before the mode solve over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m = this value, mixing parameter = relaxation): each loop-back injects its new value during the sweep (later physics of the sweep see it), then before the next sweep every loop-back value is replaced by the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and their changes (each value scaled by its largest magnitude; host float64 copies, ~3 m + 3 per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9 and 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. Like any secant method it can converge to a fixed point Picard cannot reach: an unstable branch (bistable thermo-optic loops) or, past a runaway (monotone g > 1), an unphysical one, so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.

  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
