## Study type `nonlinear_frequency_domain` - Nonlinear frequency domain

Cascaded frequency-domain nonlinear optics of every physics listing nonlinear_frequency_domain among its supported studies (em_fdfd_nonlinear): its harmonic channels are solved together, not one wavelength after the other as in frequency_domain. Undepleted mode: each channel is one FDFD solve in rank order (inputs, then the channels generated from them, each driven by the nonlinear polarisation of the lower ranks); pump_depleted: sweeps (picard) or Newton steps (newton) over all channels until self-consistent (a log line per sweep / step with its residual; not converged within max_iterations: a warning, the last iterate is stored and the snapshot labels end in "(not converged)"); Progress before each channel solve, cancel between them. Every other physics must support the stationary study and runs as a background physics first (heat is always steady here), iterated to a stationary fixed point, then every coupling from background to nonlinear physics (heat_em_thermo_optic, field_transfer, state-dependent material properties) is applied once. Solution feedback: a coupling from a nonlinear physics into a background physics (em_heat_joule into heat: linear, two-photon and free-carrier absorption of every channel) makes the run alternate rounds of background solve (that coupling applied before each of its sweeps) and nonlinear solve (pump_depleted warm-started from the last fields) until every primary field changes by at most tolerance between rounds or feedback_rounds is reached (warning), with a log line per round and the summary key feedback {couplings, rounds, converged, relative_change, tolerance, history} (None without feedback); couplings into a nonlinear physics from a nonlinear physics and material properties reading one are validation errors. The run log lists the mixing terms and each channel solve summary. Stores one snapshot per channel in solve order of the stored fields (default the primary e_abs), labelled "channel <name>: lambda = <nm> nm" (several nonlinear physics: their name first, the others NaN); afterwards each shows its first input channel (Results.field). ticks = n_channels = the channel snapshots; summary nonlinear_solve = {physics: {mode, order (channel names in solve order), channel_solves, sweeps, converged, residual, tolerance, residual_history, continuation_steps, method ('picard' | 'newton', '' undepleted), gmres_iterations, backtracks}}. Spectra (a QPM tuning curve, SHG versus pump wavelength) and power curves are parameter sweeps over the poling period, the input wavelength or the source amplitude, with derived values of channel monitors or the power_exchange_<channel> scalars.

- StudySpec.type `nonlinear_frequency_domain`; needs a physics that steps in time: no
- Background study: stationary
- Solution feedback: couplings from a physics this study solves into background physics are allowed (feedback rounds)

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf)) - Maximum coupling iterations
  Background fixed point, before the nonlinear solve over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics in a coupling loop (each solved in model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); physics only fed by the loop (sinks: they feed no coupling back) are solved once afterwards, and a model without a loop is a single pass. Typically 10-50; a warning is logged when the tolerance is not reached. The loop stops early with a warning when the change does not decrease for 3 iterations in a row (from iteration 4) and fails the run when the fields turn non-finite.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, inf)) - Relative tolerance
  Background fixed point, before the nonlinear solve over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes between iterations by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (the heat temperature T is compared as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for a loop gain g (ratio of successive changes): at g = 0.9 a change of 1e-4 means an error of ~1e-3. Anderson steps (anderson_depth) approach the remaining error itself, so there it is about the change. Typically 1e-4.
- `relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Coupling relaxation
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Coupling acceleration depth
  Background fixed point, before the nonlinear solve over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m = this value, mixing parameter = relaxation): each loop-back injects its new value during the sweep (later physics of the sweep see it), then before the next sweep every loop-back value is replaced by the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and their changes (each value scaled by its largest magnitude; host float64 copies, ~3 m + 3 per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9 and 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. Like any secant method it can converge to a fixed point Picard cannot reach: an unstable branch (bistable thermo-optic loops) or, past a runaway (monotone g > 1), an unphysical one, so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` (float; unit Hz; default 5; range [0, inf)) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the live field frames the GUI shows while computing; 0 disables them. Frames never change the results (the headless api.run sets 0).
- `feedback_rounds` (int; default 20; range [1, inf)) - Feedback rounds
  Studies with solution feedback only, used when an enabled coupling reads a physics the study solves itself and writes a background physics (e.g. em_heat_joule from em_fdfd_nonlinear into heat: two-photon absorption heating): rounds of background solve (the feedback couplings applied before each of its sweeps) and study solve at most, until every primary field of these physics changes between rounds by at most the tolerance (the same relative measure as the background fixed point); a warning when not reached or when the change stops decreasing for 3 rounds (from round 4), the last round is kept. Without a coupling back into the study physics one background solve follows the study solve. No relaxation acts between rounds. Typically 5-20.

## Study type `optimization` - Optimization

Density-based topology optimisation over the design_region features of em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz physics: maximises J = the sum of weight * quantity of every adjoint_objective of every physics (use weight -1 to minimise a quantity), each physics solved at its own wavelength setting (several physics of one polarisation at different wavelengths share the permittivity arrays, so one design region serves a broadband objective). Each design cell has a density rho in [0, 1], filtered and projected to rho_bar and mapped to eps = eps_min + rho_bar (eps_max - eps_min) (see design_region). scipy L-BFGS-B with bounds [0, 1] minimises -J / |J0| (J0 = J of the initial design); every evaluation writes the densities, solves every physics (scipy_splu re-uses the previous factor as a GMRES preconditioner while the design changes little) and takes dJ/d eps of the objectives from one transposed solve (eps_sensitivity), then dJ/d rho by the transposed projection and filter. Stops at max_iterations, at the tolerance or after 5 x max_iterations evaluations, per continuation stage (continuation_stages > 1: the projection beta grows by beta_growth per stage up to the design_region value; iterations count on across stages, objective_initial is J at the first stage beta). Snapshots: the initial design (iteration 0) and every accepted iteration, labelled "iteration k: J = <value> W/m" (em_eme: no unit, J is a power fraction); with stored_fields [] they hold the primary fields plus "<physics>.design_density" of every physics with a design_region (the design per iteration), plus "final: J = ..." when the last evaluated state differs; afterwards the physics hold the returned design (Results.field, design_density). Each design_region result is J and its grayness versus iteration; summary key optimization {iterations, evaluations, design_cells, objective_initial, objective_final, continuation_stages, message}; ticks = iterations. Every physics must be em_fdfd_ez / em_fdfd_hz / em_fdfd_nonlinear / em_eme; couplings and state-dependent material properties are not supported. The gradient is exact for the discrete model except on source, port and objective lines (keep design regions off them); sigma_e, poles and mu_r of the design cells are not optimised. An em_fdfd_nonlinear physics takes part with its design_region (writing eps_r, eps_xx and eps_yy) and the adjoint_objective features of its channels: each evaluation solves the channels and their adjoint (undepleted: one transposed solve per channel in reverse solve order; pump_depleted: the transposed fixed point by GMRES, each product one transposed solve per channel; no free carriers, and iteration_method newton with a chi3 medium) (inverse-designed harmonic generation; the chi2 / chi3 tensors and poling stay fixed). An em_eme physics (polarization ez or hz, section_tolerance 0) takes part with its design_region (ez: eps_r; hz: eps_xx and eps_yy) and adjoint_objective features (port power fractions, unit 1: the labels and log lines show J without a unit, the design_region objective series has unit 1): each evaluation re-solves the changed sections and takes dJ/d eps from the cascade adjoint (one adjoint cascade field, no extra mode solve; exact for n_modes 0).

- StudySpec.type `optimization`; needs a physics that steps in time: no

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `max_iterations` (int; default 20; range [1, 10000]) - Maximum iterations
  L-BFGS-B iterations at most; each needs one or more evaluations (line-search trials, at most 5 x max_iterations in all), and one evaluation = per FDFD physics one assembly, one solve (recycled factor or a new factorisation) and one transposed (adjoint) solve. Typical 20-200. With continuation_stages > 1 it holds per stage.
- `continuation_stages` (int; unit 1; default 1; range [1, 20]) - Sharpening stages
  Beta continuation of the design_region tanh projection: L-BFGS-B runs this many times in a row, stage s (1 .. n) with projection_beta x beta_growth^(s - n), so the last stage uses the design_region value and the first ones optimise a smoother (greyer) problem. 1 = no continuation. Regions with projection_beta 0 stay unprojected. Typical 3-5 with a final beta 8-32.
- `beta_growth` (float; unit 1; default 2; range (1, inf)) - Sharpening growth
  Factor between the projection betas of consecutive continuation stages (unused at continuation_stages 1); typical 1.5-2.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 1e-05; range [0, inf)) - Relative tolerance
  L-BFGS-B ftol on the scaled objective f = -J / |J0| (J0 = J of the initial design): stop once an iteration lowers f by at most tolerance * max(|f|, 1); 0 runs all max_iterations. Typical 1e-4 to 1e-6.
- `live_update_hz` (float; unit Hz; default 5; range [0, inf)) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the live field frames the GUI shows while computing; 0 disables them. Frames never change the results (the headless api.run sets 0).

## Study type `optomechanics` - Optomechanics

Vacuum optomechanical coupling g0 between optical and mechanical eigenmodes of one model: every solid_mechanics (or solid_mechanics_3d) physics with an optomechanical_coupling feature is the mechanical physics, the physics those features name (em_modes: cross-section modes at its wavelength setting; em_fdfd_ez / _hz: in-plane resonances near its wavelength setting, n_optical_resonances of them; em_fdfd_bor on a triangles mesh: body-of-revolution resonances of its azimuthal order(s), paired with an axisymmetric solid on triangles or a 3D solid on tetrahedra) are the optical physics; every other physics runs as a stationary background physics first (as in mode_analysis / eigenfrequency: background fixed point, then the background -> solved couplings once; couplings or material properties reading a solved physics, i.e. any solid_mechanics, em_modes or em_fdfd_* physics, are a validation error; an FDFD physics no feature names solves as a background physics). Order: background, optical solves (the first coupling's optical mode is shown), the vibration modes of each solid (n_mechanical_modes nearest its target_frequency; consistent mass of rho, supports held at 0, prestressed by its static state only with the stress_stiffening setting, which the tensor-mesh solid of this study does not offer; a solid whose coupling has scattering backward solves its guided 2.5D modes at k_z = 2 Re beta of that optical mode, set here after the optical solve), the g0 table of every coupling, then one snapshot per mechanical mode number labelled "mechanical mode k: f = <Hz> Hz, g0 / 2 pi = <Hz> Hz" (the first coupling's g0) with the stored fields (default each primary field: the mode shape and the optical intensity; the solid field om_integrand, available in this study only, maps the moving-boundary g_om density of the shown mode); mode 1 stays shown. ticks = the number of mechanical snapshots, summary n_resonances. The optical physics keeps its selected mode for every snapshot.

- StudySpec.type `optomechanics`; needs a physics that steps in time: no
- Background study: stationary

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `n_mechanical_modes` (int; default 6; range [1, 100]) - Number of vibration modes
  Vibration modes of every solid_mechanics physics with an optomechanical_coupling: the n + 4 eigenvalues omega^2 nearest (2 pi target_frequency)^2 of its target_frequency setting (0 = the lowest), ranked by |omega - omega_target|; one g0 row and one snapshot each. 4-20 typical.
- `n_optical_resonances` (int; default 4; range [1, 100]) - Number of optical resonances
  em_fdfd_ez / _hz / _bor optical physics only: resonances of its eigen-solve near its wavelength setting (the eigenfrequency study rules: PML resonances dropped, nearest the target first; em_fdfd_bor per azimuthal order); optical_mode picks one. em_modes solves its n_modes modes.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf)) - Maximum coupling iterations
  Background fixed point, before the eigen-solves over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics in a coupling loop (each solved in model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); physics only fed by the loop (sinks: they feed no coupling back) are solved once afterwards, and a model without a loop is a single pass. Typically 10-50; a warning is logged when the tolerance is not reached. The loop stops early with a warning when the change does not decrease for 3 iterations in a row (from iteration 4) and fails the run when the fields turn non-finite.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, inf)) - Relative tolerance
  Background fixed point, before the eigen-solves over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes between iterations by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (the heat temperature T is compared as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for a loop gain g (ratio of successive changes): at g = 0.9 a change of 1e-4 means an error of ~1e-3. Anderson steps (anderson_depth) approach the remaining error itself, so there it is about the change. Typically 1e-4.
- `relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Coupling relaxation
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Coupling acceleration depth
  Background fixed point, before the eigen-solves over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m = this value, mixing parameter = relaxation): each loop-back injects its new value during the sweep (later physics of the sweep see it), then before the next sweep every loop-back value is replaced by the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and their changes (each value scaled by its largest magnitude; host float64 copies, ~3 m + 3 per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9 and 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. Like any secant method it can converge to a fixed point Picard cannot reach: an unstable branch (bistable thermo-optic loops) or, past a runaway (monotone g > 1), an unphysical one, so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` (float; unit Hz; default 5; range [0, inf)) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the live field frames the GUI shows while computing; 0 disables them. Frames never change the results (the headless api.run sets 0).

## Study type `stationary` - Stationary

Steady solve of every physics at t = 0; with couplings, solving and applying every coupling is repeated until the primary fields reach a fixed point (tolerance) or max_iterations. Stores the final state only. Heat is always solved as a steady state (time_mode transient is ignored). EM FDFD (em_fdfd_ez, em_fdfd_hz, em_fdfd_bor, em_fdfd_conical), em_eme and em_eme_3d are solved at their wavelength setting; with heat (em_heat_joule, heat_em_thermo_optic) every iteration re-solves them with the permittivity of the latest temperature and hands their absorbed power to heat. EM FDTD (em_fdtd_ez, em_fdtd_hz, em_fdtd_3d, em_fdtd_bor) does not support it: use time_dependent; neither does em_modes: use mode_analysis.

- StudySpec.type `stationary`; needs a physics that steps in time: no
- Mesh refinement levels: StudySpec.adaptation allowed

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf)) - Maximum coupling iterations
  Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics in a coupling loop (each solved in model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); physics only fed by the loop (sinks: they feed no coupling back) are solved once afterwards, and a model without a loop is a single pass. Typically 10-50; a warning is logged when the tolerance is not reached. The loop stops early with a warning when the change does not decrease for 3 iterations in a row (from iteration 4) and fails the run when the fields turn non-finite.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, inf)) - Relative tolerance
  Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes between iterations by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (the heat temperature T is compared as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for a loop gain g (ratio of successive changes): at g = 0.9 a change of 1e-4 means an error of ~1e-3. Anderson steps (anderson_depth) approach the remaining error itself, so there it is about the change. Typically 1e-4.
- `relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Coupling relaxation
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Coupling acceleration depth
  Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m = this value, mixing parameter = relaxation): each loop-back injects its new value during the sweep (later physics of the sweep see it), then before the next sweep every loop-back value is replaced by the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and their changes (each value scaled by its largest magnitude; host float64 copies, ~3 m + 3 per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9 and 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. Like any secant method it can converge to a fixed point Picard cannot reach: an unstable branch (bistable thermo-optic loops) or, past a runaway (monotone g > 1), an unphysical one, so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` (float; unit Hz; default 5; range [0, inf)) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the live field frames the GUI shows while computing; 0 disables them. Frames never change the results (the headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Study type `thermal_noise` - Thermal noise

Thermorefractive noise of a z-invariant cross-section (fluctuation-dissipation theorem; Levin-type direct approach). Every heat physics (always planar 2D, never CG-solved here and needing no temperature anchor) computes the one-sided PSD of X = integral w(x, y) g(z) exp(-j q0 z) dT dV of each of its thermorefractive_noise features: S_X(f) = 4 k_B T0^2 integral dq/2pi |g~(q - q0)|^2 Re sum conj(w) u dA, where (j omega rho cp + k_zz q^2 - div k grad) u = w on the heat window (k, boundary conditions, held cells and volumetric losses as assembled for a steady solve: temperature / fixed-temperature cells are ideal reservoirs and do not fluctuate, insulated faces are mirrors), one host SuperLU factorisation per (frequency, axial sample), or GPU line-block batches of them (the heat shifted solver: sparse_direct by default, or line_block). The temperature is uniform T0 (the heat T0 setting; a heated background is not supported). Every em_modes physics is solved first (its modes give the mode-pair weightings); every other physics must support the stationary study and runs as a background physics first. particle_noise features solve the same way for dilute particles diffusing in a liquid (4 n0 instead of 4 k_B T0^2, diffusivity instead of k / rho cp). Couplings reading heat or em_modes are a validation error. Results: one xy result per feature (psd versus frequency) with the exact total variance (sum rule k_B T0^2 integral |w|^2 / (rho cp) dV), its never-relaxing static part and the share of the rest inside the solved band; one snapshot per mode number after the mode solve (labelled "mode <k>: n_eff = <value>", as in mode_analysis: step through the modes with the snapshot slider) and one final snapshot labelled "thermal noise" (Displayed mode of each em_modes physics); ticks = factorisations; summary noise_frequencies.

- StudySpec.type `thermal_noise`; needs a physics that steps in time: no
- Background study: stationary

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `frequency_start` (float; unit Hz; default 1000; range (0, inf)) - Start frequency
  Lowest noise frequency in Hz of the range (used when frequencies is empty). Below the slowest thermal relaxation rate the spectrum is flat. At q_z = 0 the mean temperature of a region without temperature anchor (insulated) never relaxes: that share is the static_variance of the result, outside every band. Typical 1e2-1e4.
- `frequency_stop` (float; unit Hz; default 1e+09; range (0, inf)) - Stop frequency
  Highest noise frequency in Hz; must exceed frequency_start. Above the fastest relaxation rate D q^2 / (2 pi) of the weighting the spectrum falls as 1/f^2 (for water and q = 1.5e7 1/m about 5 MHz). Typical 1e9-1e11.
- `n_frequencies` (int; default 31; range [1, inf)) - Number of frequencies
  Frequencies of the range, spaced as log_spacing selects (both ends included; 1 = the geometric mean, or the arithmetic mean with log_spacing off). Each costs one sparse factorisation per axial sample of every thermorefractive_noise feature (host SuperLU, or batched on the GPU with a line_block solver as the heat shifted solver).
- `log_spacing` (bool; default true) - Logarithmic spacing
  true: the range frequencies are spaced evenly in log f (geomspace; suits spectra spanning decades); false: evenly in f (linspace). Ignored when frequencies lists any frequency.
- `frequencies` (float_list; unit Hz; range (0, inf); optional (null allowed)) - Frequency list
  Explicit noise frequencies in Hz (each > 0), solved and reported in ascending order; a non-empty list overrides frequency_start, frequency_stop and n_frequencies.
- `max_iterations` (int; default 50; range [1, inf)) - Maximum coupling iterations
  Background fixed point, before the mode and noise solves over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Gauss-Seidel iterations over the physics in a coupling loop (each solved in model order, each coupling applied once its sources are solved); physics only fed by the loop (sinks: they feed no coupling back) are solved once afterwards, and a model without a loop is a single pass. Typically 10-50; a warning is logged when the tolerance is not reached. The loop stops early with a warning when the change does not decrease for 3 iterations in a row (from iteration 4) and fails the run when the fields turn non-finite.
- `tolerance` (float; unit 1; default 0.0001; range (0, inf)) - Relative tolerance
  Background fixed point, before the mode and noise solves over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Converged when every primary field of the loop physics changes between iterations by at most this fraction of its range max|f| (the heat temperature T is compared as its rise T - T0). The remaining error is about change * g / (1 - g) for a loop gain g (ratio of successive changes): at g = 0.9 a change of 1e-4 means an error of ~1e-3. Anderson steps (anderson_depth) approach the remaining error itself, so there it is about the change. Typically 1e-4.
- `relaxation` (float; unit 1; default 1; range (0, inf)) - Coupling relaxation
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.relaxation`
- `anderson_depth` (int; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Coupling acceleration depth
  Background fixed point, before the mode and noise solves over the background physics only (unused without background physics): Anderson acceleration of the loop-back couplings (Walker-Ni, depth m = this value, mixing parameter = relaxation): each loop-back injects its new value during the sweep (later physics of the sweep see it), then before the next sweep every loop-back value is replaced by the least-squares combination of the last m iterates and their changes (each value scaled by its largest magnitude; host float64 copies, ~3 m + 3 per value); 0 = plain relaxation. A monotone loop of gain g needs ~ln(tolerance)/ln(g) Picard iterations (~120 at g = 0.9 and 1e-6), far fewer accelerated. Like any secant method it can converge to a fixed point Picard cannot reach: an unstable branch (bistable thermo-optic loops) or, past a runaway (monotone g > 1), an unphysical one, so it is opt-in. Typically 3-5.
- `warm_start` (bool; default false) - Sweep warm start
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.warm_start`
- `live_update_hz` (float; unit Hz; default 5; range [0, inf)) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the live field frames the GUI shows while computing; 0 disables them. Frames never change the results (the headless api.run sets 0).

## Study type `time_dependent` - Time dependent

Advances every physics in ticks of dt_sync, the smallest dt_limit of the physics (EM: its Courant step); a physics with every = n steps on every n-th tick over n * dt_sync. Couplings are applied after every tick at their own every and flushed at the end of the run, also when it is cancelled. Needs at least one physics that steps in time; snapshots at the output interval plus the final state.

- StudySpec.type `time_dependent`; needs a physics that steps in time: yes

Params (StudySpec.settings):
- `duration` (float; unit s; default 1e-13; range (0, inf)) - Duration
  Simulated time span in s; the run stops at the tick nearest the duration (less than half a time step advances nothing). EM runs typically take 100-1000 fs: the pulse (2*t0 = 9/(pi*bandwidth*f0); ricker 8/f0) plus the transit time and the ring-down (validation warns when the duration ends before the longest pulse, plus the domain diagonal * n_max / C0 with a flux, DFT, mode or far-field monitor); transient heat takes ms to s.
- `output_interval` (float; unit s; default 0; range [0, inf)) - Output interval
  Time in s between snapshots of the stored fields (study stored_fields, default each physics' primary field), from t = 0; 0 stores only the final state. Intermediate snapshots stop once they exceed 1 GB; the final state is always stored. Snapshots hold the native window cells (graded included) up to 250,000 cells, else nearest-cell values on square pixels of max(finest cell, sqrt(window area / 250,000)) (native_shape set): fine features can then be skipped.
- `live_update_hz` (float; unit Hz; default 5; range [0, inf)) - Live update rate
  Maximum rate of the live field frames the GUI shows while computing; 0 disables them. Frames never change the results (the headless api.run sets 0).
- `parity_sectors` (bool; default false) - Parity sectors
  Help: shared `eigenfrequency.parity_sectors`

## Templates

Worked examples: every template validates without errors (selftest templates_validate), and modifying the closest one is the most reliable way to write a valid model. api.template(key) returns one as a ModelSpec, python -m open_sol template KEY FILE writes its model file.

The model JSON of each template is in api_templates.md beside this file (its Contents gives each template's line range; also describe('templates')). One line per template: key - label: description, then the physics types, features (<physics>.<feature>), couplings, solver types and study it uses.

- `dielectric_cylinder` - Dielectric cylinder: EM: a 550 nm gaussian point source scatters off a glass cylinder; field probe and transmitted flux spectrum. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez; features em_fdtd_ez.point_source, em_fdtd_ez.field_probe, em_fdtd_ez.flux_monitor; study time_dependent.
- `gold_nanodisk` - Gold nanodisk: EM: TFSF plane wave on a Drude gold disk (uniform 2 nm mesh); near-field DFT and far-field pattern, 400-900 nm. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez; features em_fdtd_ez.plane_wave_tfsf, em_fdtd_ez.dft_monitor, em_fdtd_ez.far_field; study time_dependent.
- `joule_heating` - Joule heating: EM + heat: a CW gaussian beam heats a gold disk in silica; Joule and thermo-optic couplings, 293.15 K walls. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez, heat; features em_fdtd_ez.gaussian_beam, heat.temperature, heat.temperature_probe; couplings em_heat_joule, heat_em_thermo_optic; study time_dependent.
- `transient_heat_sink` - Transient heat sink: Heat (transient): a heater in a silicon block, convection on top, fixed temperature at the bottom. Uses physics heat; features heat.heat_source, heat.convection, heat.temperature, heat.temperature_probe; study time_dependent.
- `nonlinear_conduction` - Nonlinear conduction: Heat (stationary): temperature-dependent conductivity k_300*(300/T)**1.3 around a heated core. Uses physics heat; features heat.heat_source, heat.temperature; study stationary.
- `photoacoustic_disc` - Photoacoustic disc: elastic_waves (time_dependent): a 1 mm absorbing disc in water heated by a 100 ns pulse (heat_pulse_source, Grueneisen 0.2): the thermoelastic pressure (initial p0 = Grueneisen x absorbed energy density, ~35 kPa) leaves the disc as an N-shaped pulse recorded by a pressure probe 2 mm away. Uses physics elastic_waves; features elastic_waves.heat_pulse_source, elastic_waves.field_probe; study time_dependent.
- `rigid_disk_scattering` - Rigid disk scattering (pressure acoustics): Axisymmetric pressure_acoustics: a thin rigid disk in a plane wave (scattered-field background, PMLs), the mean pressure on its top and bottom faces from k a = 0.05 to 0.3 (log sweep); the low-frequency pressure difference is (8 / 3 pi) k a p0. Uses physics pressure_acoustics; features pressure_acoustics.background_pressure_field, pressure_acoustics.rigid_obstacle, pressure_acoustics.surface_pressure; study frequency_response.
- `fresnel_interface` - Fresnel interface: EM: a 1 um gaussian pulse crosses a vacuum / glass (eps_r = 4) interface in a y-periodic strip; flux spectrum 0.9-1.1 um behind it (8/9 of a vacuum run). Uses physics em_fdtd_ez; features em_fdtd_ez.line_source, em_fdtd_ez.flux_monitor; study time_dependent.
- `gold_nanodisk_hz` - Gold nanodisk (in-plane electric field): EM (H_z polarisation): TFSF plane wave with in-plane E on a Drude gold disk (uniform 2 nm mesh, 200 fs); near-field DFT of |E|^2 shows the particle plasmon, plus the far-field pattern, 400-900 nm. Uses physics em_fdtd_hz; features em_fdtd_hz.plane_wave_tfsf, em_fdtd_hz.dft_monitor, em_fdtd_hz.far_field; study time_dependent.
- `directional_coupler` - Directional coupler (in-plane electric field): EM (H_z polarisation): two 0.3 um silicon strips in silica with a 4 um long, 0.2 um gap coupling section and cosine S-bends (uniform 20 nm mesh); a 1.55 um gaussian mode source in strip A and mode monitors give the through, cross and reflected power fractions (|S|^2) and phases, 1.45-1.65 um. Uses physics em_fdtd_hz; features em_fdtd_hz.mode_monitor, em_fdtd_hz.mode_source; study time_dependent.
- `fd_joule_heating` - Joule heating of a gold nanowire (frequency domain): EM (FDFD, E_z) + heat, stationary study: a 530 nm gaussian beam heats a 30 nm gold nanowire in water by about 9 K; Joule and thermo-optic couplings, convection on the outer faces, max T and the absorbed power. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez, heat; features em_fdfd_ez.gaussian_beam, heat.convection, heat.temperature_probe; couplings em_heat_joule, heat_em_thermo_optic; study stationary.
- `effective_index_rib_waveguide` - Rib waveguide (effective index 2.5D): EM (FDFD, H_z): top view of a 0.5 um silicon rib (220 nm rib on a 90 nm slab, silica above and below) collapsed by the effective-index method (effective_index features); a 1.55 um mode source and a mode monitor give the lateral mode index and transmission. Uses physics em_fdfd_hz; features em_fdfd_hz.effective_index, em_fdfd_hz.mode_source, em_fdfd_hz.mode_monitor; study stationary.
- `disk_resonator_eigenmodes` - Disk resonator eigenmodes: EM FDFD (E_z), eigenfrequency study: the whispering-gallery resonances of a silicon disk (eps_r 12.11, radius r_disk = 1 um) in air nearest 1.55 um (6 resonances; each mode is a near-degenerate pair on the staircase disk), with wavelength, Q and field shape per resonance; derived lambda_1 and Q_1 of the nearest one. The same modes as the FDTD disk_resonator template (ring-down), without a source or a long run. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez; features em_fdfd_ez.resonance_table; study eigenfrequency.
- `cylinder_harmonic_fdtd` - Dielectric cylinder, time-domain spectrum: EM FDTD (E_z) in a frequency_domain study (harmonic FDTD): one plane-wave pulse (TFSF box, 1 um, bandwidth 0.5) scatters off a dielectric cylinder (eps_r 4, radius r_cyl = 0.3 um) and gives the complex E_z phasor of every study wavelength 0.85-1.2 um (8 values, one snapshot each) from a single time-domain run; switch the physics to em_fdfd_ez for the same maps by one frequency-domain solve per wavelength. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez; features em_fdtd_ez.plane_wave_tfsf; study frequency_domain.
- `waveguide_bend_optimization` - Waveguide bend optimization: EM FDFD (E_z) at 1.55 um, optimization study: a 0.28 um silicon strip in silica turns by 90 degrees inside a 1.2 x 1.2 um design region (density from silica to silicon, filter radius 80 nm, tanh projection reaching beta 8 by a continuation over 3 stages: beta 2, 4, 8, at most 25 L-BFGS-B iterations each). Objective: the mode 1 power leaving along +y (mode_power_positive). The design_density field is stored per iteration; the design_region result shows J and the grayness versus iteration. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez; features em_fdfd_ez.mode_source, em_fdfd_ez.adjoint_objective, em_fdfd_ez.design_region; study optimization.
- `disk_resonator` - Disk resonator ring-down: EM (E_z): a 1.55 um gaussian pulse (bandwidth 0.2) from a line current inside a silicon disk (eps_r 12.11, radius 1 um) in air excites its whispering-gallery modes; a resonance_monitor near the rim lists their wavelengths, Q and amplitudes over 1.45-1.65 um from the 2 ps ring-down. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez; features em_fdtd_ez.point_source, em_fdtd_ez.resonance_monitor; study time_dependent.
- `bloch_band_diagram` - Photonic crystal band diagram: EM (E_z): one unit cell of a square lattice of dielectric rods (eps_r 8.9, r = 0.2 a, a = 0.5 um), Bloch-periodic with bloch_kx = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0-0.5 (Gamma-X); a point-source pulse and a resonance finder per k give the band frequencies (TM gap ~1.14-1.56 um). Uses physics em_fdtd_ez; features em_fdtd_ez.point_source, em_fdtd_ez.resonance_monitor; study time_dependent.
- `fdfd_band_diagram` - Photonic crystal band diagram (frequency domain): EM (FDFD, E_z): the rod unit cell of bloch_band_diagram (eps_r 8.9, r = 0.2 a, a = 0.5 um), Bloch-periodic with bloch_kx = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0-0.5 (Gamma-X); an eigenfrequency study per k lists the 6 band frequencies nearest 1.2 um (resonance_table), without time stepping or a resonance fit. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez; features em_fdfd_ez.resonance_table; study eigenfrequency.
- `nonlinear_silicon_slab` - Nonlinear silicon slab: EM (E_z): a 1.55 um gaussian pulse of 1 GV/m peak crosses a 2 um silicon slab with Kerr (n2 6e-18 m^2/W), two-photon absorption (beta 8e-12 m/W) and TPA free carriers (lifetime 1 ns, FCA 1.45e-21 m^2, dn/dN -1.35e-27 m^3) in a y-periodic strip; transmitted flux spectrum, probe trace and the carrier_density map. Uses physics em_fdtd_ez; features em_fdtd_ez.line_source, em_fdtd_ez.nonlinear_medium, em_fdtd_ez.flux_monitor, em_fdtd_ez.field_probe; study time_dependent.
- `phase_change_gst_switch` - GST phase-change switch: EM (E_z, frequency domain at 1.55 um) + transient heat, time dependent: a cw line source (3 MV/m) heats a 100 nm GST-225 film on 0.5 um of silica over a 293 K heat sink; em_heat_joule feeds the absorbed power to heat, heat_em_phase_change crystallises the film from its temperature history (more absorbing as it crystallises), and the FDFD re-solves after every heat step; crystallinity and T maps, film temperature and crystallinity traces. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez, heat; features em_fdfd_ez.line_source, em_fdfd_ez.phase_change_medium, heat.temperature, heat.temperature_probe; couplings em_heat_joule, heat_em_phase_change; study time_dependent.
- `strip_waveguide_modes` - Strip waveguide modes: EM cross-section modes, mode_analysis: a 500 x 220 nm silicon strip in silica at 1.55 um (20 nm mesh, CPML on every side); mode table of 4 modes (n_eff, loss, TE fraction, effective area), derived n_eff_1 and te_fraction_1 (quasi-TE0: n_eff ~2.4, te_fraction ~1). Uses physics em_modes; features em_modes.mode_table; study mode_analysis.
- `thermo_optic_phase_shifter` - Thermo-optic phase shifter: Heat + EM cross-section modes, mode_analysis with a sweep over P_heater (0, 10, 20 W/m): a gold heater 1 um above a 500 x 220 nm silicon strip in silica, substrate face at 293.15 K; steady heat, heat_em_thermo_optic, then the modes on the heated permittivity; derived n_eff_1 (dn_eff ~5e-4 at 20 W/m: ~2 rad per mm) and T_core. Uses physics heat, em_modes; features heat.temperature, heat.heat_source, em_modes.mode_table; couplings heat_em_thermo_optic; study mode_analysis.
- `pn_phase_shifter_depletion` - PN phase shifter (prescribed carriers): EM cross-section modes, mode_analysis with a sweep over the reverse bias V_R (0, 2, 4 V): a 500 x 220 nm silicon rib on a 90 nm slab in silica with a lateral pn junction at its centre (N_A = N_D = 5e17 cm^-3). The carrier densities are prescribed by the depletion approximation in closed form (none inside the depletion width W(V_R), the doping outside) and enter eps_r / sigma_e of silicon through the Soref-Bennett plasma dispersion at 1.55 um; derived n_eff_1 and loss_1 (dB/cm) per bias (dn_eff ~1e-4 between 0 and 4 V). Uses physics em_modes; features em_modes.mode_table; study mode_analysis.
- `pn_phase_shifter_electrostatics` - PN phase shifter (electrostatics): Electrostatics + EM cross-section modes, mode_analysis with a sweep over V_R (0, 2, 4 V): the rib of 'pn_phase_shifter_depletion', but the electrostatics solves V of the depletion-approximation space charge between slab contacts at 0 V and V_bi + V_R, and the carriers follow V by Boltzmann statistics (n = N_D exp((V - V_bi - V_R) / V_T), p = N_A exp(-V / V_T), clamped at the doping): smooth depletion edges and the 2D field of the rib, read by eps_r / sigma_e (Soref-Bennett) as state-dependent materials; derived n_eff_1 and loss_1. Uses physics electrostatics, em_modes; features electrostatics.terminal, electrostatics.charge_density, em_modes.mode_table; study mode_analysis.
- `microdisk_bor_eigenmodes` - Microdisk whispering-gallery modes (axisymmetric): EM body-of-revolution FDFD, eigenfrequency study: the whispering-gallery resonances of azimuthal order m = 15 of a silicon microdisk (eps_r 12.11, radius r_disk = 1.5 um, 240 nm thick) in air nearest 1.55 um, solved on the (r, z) half plane above its equatorial plane (pmc mirror on z_lo: quasi-TE modes, E in the disk plane), cpml on r_hi and z_hi, 20 nm mesh. Wavelength, Q (radiation into the PML) and field per resonance; derived lambda_1 and Q_1. A full 3D answer at 2D cost; list several orders in azimuthal_orders (e.g. 14, 15, 16) for the free spectral range. Uses physics em_fdfd_bor; features em_fdfd_bor.resonance_table; study eigenfrequency.
- `dipole_radiation_3d` - Dipole radiation (3D): em_fdtd_3d: a z-oriented electric dipole (1e-12 A m, gaussian pulse at 1 um) in a 1.2 um vacuum cube with CPML on all six faces; a flux box around it gives the radiated cw power, analytically eta0 k^2 (I l)^2 / (12 pi). Uses physics em_fdtd_3d; features em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source, em_fdtd_3d.flux_box; study time_dependent.
- `photonic_crystal_slab_bands_3d` - Photonic crystal slab band diagram (3D): em_fdtd_3d: one unit cell of a square lattice of air holes (a = 0.5 um, r = 0.3 a) in a 0.275 um eps 12 slab with vacuum and CPML above and below, x / y periodic with bloch_kx = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0-0.5 (Gamma-X); an in-plane dipole on the mid-plane and a resonance finder per k give the TE-like band frequencies and Q (guided below the light line, leaky above it). Uses physics em_fdtd_3d; features em_fdtd_3d.dipole_source, em_fdtd_3d.resonance_monitor; study time_dependent.
- `pec_box_eigenmodes_3d` - PEC box cavity with a silicon cube: eigenmodes (3D): em_fdfd_3d: a 1.0 x 0.8 x 0.6 um vacuum box with pec walls on all six faces and a 0.3 um eps 12 cube at its centre; the eigenfrequency study finds the 4 resonances nearest 1.4 um (resonance table: wavelength, Q = inf for this lossless closed cavity) and their mode shapes on 40 nm cells (10 per wavelength in silicon). Uses physics em_fdfd_3d; features em_fdfd_3d.resonance_table; study eigenfrequency.
- `nanobeam_mirror_cell_bands_3d` - Nanobeam mirror cell band diagram (3D, frequency domain): em_fdfd_3d: one mirror cell of a silicon nanobeam photonic crystal in D2O (igor_experiment 4.3: period a = 394.3 nm, hole d = 279.3 nm along y through a 595.2 x 220 nm beam, n 3.47 / 1.32), quarter cross-section (x_lo antisymmetric = PEC plane, y_lo symmetric = PMC plane: the TE-like sector), 300 nm D2O and 8 CPML cells on x_hi / y_hi, z periodic with bloch_kz = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0.4-0.5 (guided, below the D2O light line); an eigenfrequency study per k lists the 4 bands nearest 1.496 um (resonance_table). At k_fraction 0.5 the dielectric (longer wavelength) and air band edges bound the TE-like gap that should contain 1.496 um; set a and d to a taper cell to follow the band-edge grading. a / 16 cells (24.6 nm) with subpixel smoothing, ~4e4 unknowns per k (one host factor each, minutes); more padding mainly raises the guided-band Q (the evanescent tail reaches the CPML). Uses physics em_fdfd_3d; features em_fdfd_3d.resonance_table; study eigenfrequency.
- `linear_taper_eme` - Linear taper (EME): EME, stationary: a 10 um linear taper from a 0.5 um to a 2 um wide guide (eps 4 in silica, ez, 1.55 um, 25 nm mesh, cpml on y, pec x faces); eme_ports with the fundamental incident from x_lo, the section table, derived T1 = transmission into the fundamental of the wide guide, and eme_length_sweep: T1 versus the taper length from 2.5 to 40 um, re-cascaded from the one solve. Uses physics em_eme; features em_eme.eme_ports, em_eme.eme_section_table, em_eme.eme_length_sweep; study stationary.
- `mmi_1x2_eme` - 1 x 2 MMI splitter (EME): EME, stationary, ez at 1.55 um: a centre-fed 1 x 2 multimode interference splitter (eps 4 in silica, 25 nm mesh, cpml on y, pec x faces): a 1 um input guide, a 3 um wide MMI section of length L_mmi (parameter, 7.3 um = 3 L_pi / 8 for the two-fold symmetric image, L_pi = 4 n_r W_e^2 / (3 lambda) with the effective width W_e ~ 3.36 um) and two 1 um output guides centred at +-0.75 um. The output port modes are the supermodes of the guide pair, so T1 (symmetric supermode) is the power split equally into both outputs and the antisymmetric one stays ~0 by symmetry. Beat-length check: the section table lists n_eff_1 / n_eff_2 of the MMI section (its two lowest, even and odd modes), and L_pi = lambda / (2 (n_eff_1 - n_eff_2)) of those modes is exact for the EME, which propagates every section mode with its own beta; set L_mmi = 3 L_pi / 8 from it to tune the splitter. Uses physics em_eme; features em_eme.eme_ports, em_eme.eme_section_table; study stationary.
- `thermo_optic_phase_shifter_eme_3d` - Thermo-optic phase shifter (EME 3D): Heat + em_eme_3d, stationary: a 0.5 x 0.2 um silicon strip in silica running 20 um along z, a 1.5 x 0.2 um heater region 1 um above it from z = 5 to 15 um dissipating P_heater (parameter, 1 mW), the substrate face y_lo at 293.15 K; steady heat, heat_em_thermo_optic, then the EME of the heated guide (pec transverse walls of the 4 x 3 um box, 50 nm cells, 10 modes, section_tolerance 1e-4: heated layers within about 1 K of a section's first layer merge into it, a staircase of a few percent of the phase shift). The transmission row of the eme_ports table gives the phase of S21 (sweep P_heater to get the phase shift, about 0.1 rad per mW here); derived T1 and the mean core temperature. Uses physics heat, em_eme_3d; features heat.temperature, heat.heat_source, em_eme_3d.eme_ports, em_eme_3d.eme_section_table; couplings heat_em_thermo_optic; solvers pcg; study stationary.
- `heated_microchannel` - Heated microchannel: Laminar flow + heat, stationary: water flows (parabolic inflow, mean U_in = 2 mm/s) through a 20 um channel in a silica chip past a 60 x 6 um heater (Q_heater, ~7 W/m) 10 um above it; fluid_heat_convection carries the heat downstream; derived T_max, T_outlet (mean water temperature at the outlet) and U_max. Uses physics laminar_flow, heat; features laminar_flow.inlet_velocity, laminar_flow.pressure, heat.temperature, heat.heat_source; couplings fluid_heat_convection; study stationary.
- `heated_slab` - Heated slab: Heat (stationary): a 1 mm slab with a uniform 1e+09 W/m^3 source between two 300 K walls; peak rise Q L^2 / (8 k) = 62.5 K. Uses physics heat; features heat.temperature, heat.heat_source; study stationary.
- `heated_chip_3d` - Heated chip (3D): Heat (stationary, 3D): a 1 x 1 x 0.5 mm silicon block (k = 130 W/(m*K)) on a 300 K heat sink (z_lo) with a 0.4 mm square chip dissipating 0.8 W in its top 50 um, convection on z_hi; derived value T_max. Uses physics heat; features heat.temperature, heat.convection, heat.heat_source; study stationary.
- `waveguide_thermal_noise` - Waveguide thermal noise: thermal_noise study of a 480 x 220 nm silicon strip in silica (library materials) at 1550 nm: em_modes on the half cross-section (x_lo antisymmetric mirror through the strip centre, quasi-TE family; em CPML on the other faces) and heat with the substrate sink T = 293.15 K on y_lo (2 um below the strip), other faces insulated. One thermorefractive_noise feature on all cells (mode_pair: the quasi-TE mode backscattered into itself, q0 = 2 beta, uniform over 1 mm): psd in 1/Hz (backscattered power per incident power per Hz) with the silica and silicon self terms and their cross term. 29 log-spaced frequencies 1000..1e+10 Hz, uniform 20 nm mesh; derived values n_eff_1 and the PSD at 1 MHz. Uses physics em_modes, heat; features heat.temperature, heat.thermorefractive_noise; study thermal_noise.
- `flux_concentrator_needle` - Flux-concentrator needle: Magnetostatics, axisymmetric, stationary sweep: a Metglas needle (r = 31 um, l = 15 mm, mu_dc 1e5) in a uniform axial field B_ext = 1e-4 T concentrates the flux at its tip; derived B_sensor (mean |B| over a 31 um disc a gap below the tip) and gain = B_sensor / B_ext (EF = 20 log10(gain) dB), swept over gap = 25 .. 400 um. Uses physics magnetostatics; features magnetostatics.external_field; solvers pcg; study stationary.
- `iron_c_core_saturation` - Iron C-core saturation: Magnetostatics on a triangle mesh, planar, stationary sweep: an iron C-core (80 x 60 mm, 10 mm limbs, mu_dc 4000, saturation_polarization 1.8 T) with a gap_width = 2 mm air gap in its right limb, driven by a 200-turn coil around the left limb (go and return sides as two coil features); I_coil swept 0.5 .. 32 A. Derived B_gap = mean |B| in the gap against the ideal mu0 N I / g (analytic curve, valid below the knee: the core reluctance takes ~3 %); Newton (nonlinear_method auto) solves the saturation. Uses physics magnetostatics; features magnetostatics.coil; study stationary.
- `busbar_proximity` - Busbar pair, proximity effect: Magnetic fields AC, planar, stationary sweep over the frequency f = 50 Hz .. 20 kHz: two copper bars 10 x 2 mm (wide faces 2 mm apart) carry +I and -I (solid conductors, prescribed current 100 A): the current crowds onto the facing surfaces. Derived R_loop, L_loop (per m of length) and the loss P per m. Uses physics magnetic_fields_ac; features magnetic_fields_ac.coil; study stationary.
- `flux_concentrator_needle_ac` - Flux-concentrator needle, AC: Magnetic fields AC, axisymmetric, stationary sweep over the frequency f = 10 Hz .. 30 kHz: the flux_concentrator_needle model (Metglas needle r = 31 um, l = 15 mm, mu_dc 1e5, applied axial field amplitude B_ext = 1e-4 T) with the needle conductivity sigma_needle = 7e5 S/m and magnetic loss mu_dc_loss = loss_tangent mu_dc: eddy currents screen the needle once the skin depth falls below its radius (~1 kHz), so the gain = B_sensor / B_ext (mean |B| over a 31 um disc a gap = 100 um below the tip; EF = 20 log10(gain) dB) drops with frequency. Uses physics magnetic_fields_ac; features magnetic_fields_ac.external_field; study stationary.
- `needle_3d` - Flux concentrator needle (3D): Magnetostatics (3D, stationary): a 15 mm x 125 um x 25 um Metglas needle (mu_dc 1e5) along z in a uniform axial field B_ext (external_field, 10 x 10 x 35 mm window held at the applied potential), the geometry of Carey et al. 2026 on coarse 25 um cells around the needle and its lower tip (graded by 1.3 to 1 mm, by 1.5 to 2 mm outside). Derived values: gain_h50 = mean |B| / B_ext over a sensor box 50 um below the tip and EF_h50 = 20 log10(gain) against the prolate-spheroid estimate (Eq. 2 with m = l / sqrt(w t)); line curve B_axis: |B| on the needle axis below the tip against Eq. 2. - `heated_chip_stress_3d` - Heated chip stress (3D): Heat + solid mechanics 3D, stationary: a 1 x 1 x 0.5 mm silicon block on a 300 K heat sink (z_lo, also clamped) with a 0.4 mm square chip dissipating 0.8 W in its top 50 um, convection on z_hi; heat_solid_thermal_strain hands the temperature rise to the solid; derived T_max, von_mises_max, u_z_max. Uses physics heat, solid_mechanics_3d; features heat.temperature, heat.convection, heat.heat_source, solid_mechanics_3d.fixed; couplings heat_solid_thermal_strain; study stationary.
- `solid_bloch_band_diagram_3d` - Phononic nanobeam band diagram (3D): Solid mechanics 3D on builtin tetrahedra: one unit cell (a = 0.5 um) of a free-standing silicon nanobeam (0.25 x 0.25 um core) with a 0.75 um wide wing over the middle half of the period, periodic along x with bloch_kx = k_fraction 2 pi / a swept over 0-0.5 (Gamma-X); an eigenfrequency study per k lists the 8 bands nearest 4 GHz (resonance_table; target > 0 drops the rigid modes at Gamma). Uses physics solid_mechanics_3d; features solid_mechanics_3d.resonance_table; study eigenfrequency.
- `heated_waveguide_stress` - Heated waveguide stress: Heat + solid mechanics (plane strain), stationary: cross-section of a 0.48 x 0.22 um silicon waveguide in silica under a 2 x 0.2 um gold heater (P_heater = 20 W/m), substrate y_lo held at 293.15 K and clamped, rollers on the sides; heat_solid_thermal_strain hands the temperature rise (~5 K at the core) to the solid; derived T_core, stress_xx_core, stress_yy_core, von_mises_max. - `silicon_ring_breathing_g0` - Silicon ring breathing g0: Optomechanics study: quasi-TE0 mode (em_modes, 1.55 um, group index) and the lowest in-plane vibration modes of a suspended 450 x 220 nm silicon strip (quarter domain with mirrors and rollers), optomechanical_coupling table of g0 / 2 pi (moving boundary, photoelastic, total) for a ring of R = 10 um (length 2 pi R). Uses physics em_fdfd_hz, solid_mechanics; features solid_mechanics.roller, solid_mechanics.optomechanical_coupling; study optomechanics.
- `silicon_nitride_membrane_modes` - Silicon nitride membrane modes: A 1 x 0.7 mm silicon nitride membrane (50 nm film at 1 GPa stress: tension 50 N/m, areal density 1.55e-4 kg/m^2) clamped on its frame: the six lowest drum modes on quadratic triangles, f_mn = (c / 2) sqrt((m / a)^2 + (n / b)^2) with c = sqrt(T / rho_s) = 568 m/s (f_11 = 495 kHz), listed by the resonance table. Uses physics membrane; features membrane.clamped, membrane.resonance_table; study eigenfrequency.
- `ppln_slab_shg` - PPLN slab waveguide SHG (QPM tuning curve): Nonlinear FDFD (undepleted): a 1550 nm mode pumps a periodically poled z-cut lithium niobate slab in silica; sweep of the poling period over the QPM peak, forward second-harmonic mode power vs the coupled-mode sinc^2 curve. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear; features em_fdfd_nonlinear.harmonic_channel, em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium, em_fdfd_nonlinear.mode_source, em_fdfd_nonlinear.mode_monitor; study nonlinear_frequency_domain.

Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear; features em_fdfd_nonlinear.harmonic_channel, em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium, em_fdfd_nonlinear.plane_wave_tfsf, em_fdfd_nonlinear.far_field; study nonlinear_frequency_domain.
- `silicon_thg_waveguide` - Silicon slab waveguide THG (absorbing silicon): Nonlinear FDFD (undepleted chi3): a guided pump mode in a silicon slab waveguide generates the third harmonic in dispersive, absorbing silicon; sweep of the pump wavelength, forward and backward third-harmonic power. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear; features em_fdfd_nonlinear.harmonic_channel, em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium, em_fdfd_nonlinear.line_source, em_fdfd_nonlinear.field_probe; study nonlinear_frequency_domain.
- `silicon_fwm_waveguide` - Silicon waveguide FWM with TPA and free carriers: Nonlinear FDFD (pump depleted, Newton-Krylov): degenerate four-wave mixing in a silicon slab waveguide with two-photon and free-carrier absorption; sweep of the pump power, idler conversion and the nonlinear losses. - `gold_ridge_surface_shg` - Gold ridge surface SHG: Nonlinear FDFD (undepleted, surface chi2): an in-plane polarised 1550 nm plane wave on a gold ridge generates second harmonic at the metal surface; sweep of the ridge width, SH power and far field. - `shg_metasurface_optimization` - Inverse-designed SHG metasurface: em_fdfd_nonlinear (E_z channels p at 1.55 um and sh = 2 p, undepleted cascade), optimization study: a y-periodic 0.5 um cell with a 0.3 um z-cut lithium niobate film (d33 25 pm/V, eps 4.58) on silica, pumped at normal incidence by a 1e7 V/m line source in air. A 0.8 um design layer on the film (density from air to silicon nitride, eps 1 .. 4, filter radius 60 nm, tanh projection reaching beta 8 over 3 continuation stages, at most 30 L-BFGS-B iterations each) is shaped to maximise the second-harmonic flux transmitted into the silica (adjoint_objective of channel sh): the layer focuses and phase-matches the pump in the film. The design_density field is stored per iteration; the design_region result shows J and the grayness versus iteration. 2D: powers per unit length in z. Uses physics em_fdfd_nonlinear; features em_fdfd_nonlinear.harmonic_channel, em_fdfd_nonlinear.chi2_medium, em_fdfd_nonlinear.line_source, em_fdfd_nonlinear.adjoint_objective, em_fdfd_nonlinear.design_region; study optimization.
- `thermo_optic_heater` - Thermo-optic heater: Electric currents + heat + EM FDFD (E_z), stationary: a gold strip heater (1 x 8.8 um, V_heater = 0.02 V, sigma_dc(T)) 1.52 um beside a 0.48 um silicon slab waveguide in silica; Joule heating (~2 kW/m), out-of-plane sink (7e5 W/(m^2 K) through 1 um: heater rise ~60-80 K, waveguide ~20 K), thermo-optic phase of the guided mode (~0.1 rad, mode_monitor phase_positive); derived P_heater, T_max, T_waveguide. Uses physics em_fdfd_ez, heat, electric_currents; features em_fdfd_ez.mode_source, em_fdfd_ez.mode_monitor, heat.out_of_plane_convection, heat.temperature_probe, electric_currents.terminal; couplings currents_heat_joule, heat_em_thermo_optic; study stationary.
- `silicon_pn_photodiode` - Silicon pin photodiode: drift_diffusion, stationary: a lateral p+ / i / n+ silicon diode (4 x 0.2 um, 10 nm cells) reverse-biased by V_reverse = 1 V, with a uniform generation G_light = 1e27 1/(m^3 s) in the 2 um intrinsic absorber (photocurrent ~ q G A = 6.4e-5 A/m, read from the contact tables); derived R_total. Uses physics drift_diffusion; features drift_diffusion.doping, drift_diffusion.ohmic_contact, drift_diffusion.generation; study stationary.
- `induction_billet` - Induction heating of a billet: Magnetic fields AC + heat, axisymmetric, time-dependent: a 20-turn coil carrying I = 300 A peak at f = 1 kHz heats an aluminium billet (r = 20 mm, 60 mm tall) by eddy currents in its skin (delta ~2.7 mm); the eddy loss feeds transient heat for 20 s through magnetic_heat_induction.
